translation: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.
interpretation: This phrase serves as an invocation of the Divine attributes of Mercy, indicating that every action, thought, or undertaking must be grounded in the recognition of God's limitless compassion, which sustains all of existence and provides the essential foundation for human moral and spiritual conduct.

translation: All praise is for Allah—Lord of all worlds.
interpretation: This verse establishes that all forms of praise, gratitude, and perfection belong exclusively to Allah, the Creator and Sustainer of the entire universe, who encompasses all of existence with His sovereignty, care, and providence.

translation: The Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.
interpretation: These two divine attributes signify that Allah encompasses all existence with His mercy; the first refers to His vast mercy that reaches all His creation in this world, while the second refers to His specific, perpetual mercy that He reserves for His believing servants in the Hereafter.

translation: The Master of the Day of Judgment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty of Allah over the Day of Resurrection, asserting that on that day, all worldly authority and human pretense will vanish, leaving only His supreme judgment to recompense every soul according to its deeds with perfect justice.

translation: You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help.
interpretation: This verse establishes that absolute sincerity in worship belongs exclusively to Allah, affirming that all acts of devotion and submission are directed solely toward Him, while simultaneously recognizing that humans are entirely dependent on His divine power and support to fulfill their obligations and navigate life's challenges.

translation: Guide us to the straight path.
interpretation: This verse is a profound supplication in which the believer asks Allah to bestow upon them the gift of guidance, specifically requesting to be directed toward the clear and unerring path of truth, which leads to His pleasure and paradise, by firming their faith, granting them the ability to follow His commandments, and keeping them away from the paths of those who have incurred His wrath or gone astray.

translation: The path of those upon whom You have bestowed favor, not of those who have evoked [Your] anger or of those who are astray.
interpretation: This verse is a supplication for guidance towards the straight path, which is defined as the way followed by the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous upon whom Allah bestowed His grace. It asks for protection from the ways of two specific groups: those who knowingly rejected the truth and earned Allah’s displeasure, and those who wandered away from the truth due to ignorance and lack of guidance, emphasizing that salvation lies in the balance of knowledge followed by righteous action.

translation: Alif, Lam, Mim.
interpretation: These are abbreviated letters (al-huruf al-muqatta'at) found at the beginning of several Surahs, and their true knowledge is known only to Allah, though many scholars interpret them as signs pointing to the miraculous nature of the Qur'an, which is composed of the same letters used in the Arabic language yet remains inimitable.

translation: This is the Book, in which there is no doubt, a guidance for the righteous.
interpretation: The verse asserts that the Qur'an is the definitive word of God, completely free of any falsehood or ambiguity, serving as a beacon of light and truth that specifically benefits those who possess Taqwa—the God-fearing individuals who safeguard themselves against disobedience and strive to align their lives with divine commands.

translation: Those who believe in the unseen, establish prayer, and spend out of what We have provided for them.
interpretation: The verse defines the attributes of the righteous by emphasizing three core aspects: spiritual faith that transcends sensory perception, a dedicated and consistent connection with the Creator through prescribed prayer, and a practical manifestation of gratitude by sharing one's God-given worldly blessings with those in need, thereby balancing the internal state of belief with external manifestations of piety and social responsibility.

translation: And who believe in what has been revealed to you, [O Muhammad], and what was revealed before you, and of the Hereafter they are certain [in faith].
interpretation: The verse highlights that the hallmark of true believers is their comprehensive faith, which includes accepting the Qur'an revealed to Prophet Muhammad, the divine scriptures previously sent to other prophets, and an unwavering certainty regarding the reality of the afterlife, where accountability and eternal life await, thereby anchoring their worldly actions in the awareness of a higher divine purpose.

translation: Those are upon [right] guidance from their Lord, and it is those who are the successful.
interpretation: This verse indicates that those who possess the aforementioned qualities—believing in the unseen, establishing prayer, and spending from what God has provided—are following a divine light and a clear path of truth bestowed upon them by their Creator, which leads them to attain the ultimate success of reaching Paradise and escaping the punishment of Hell.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve - it is all the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them - they will not believe.
interpretation: This verse describes individuals whose hearts have become so hardened and sealed by their persistent rejection of truth that the external message of guidance no longer finds a way to penetrate their consciousness; having willfully chosen disbelief, they have arrived at a state of spiritual stagnation where further warnings serve only as a confirmation of their already settled refusal to accept the divine reality.

translation: Allah has set a seal upon their hearts and upon their hearing, and over their vision is a veil. And for them is a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse describes the spiritual consequence of persistent disbelief and willful arrogance, where the hearts of the deniers become so hardened that they are no longer receptive to the truth, their hearing becomes incapable of perceiving the guidance in Allah's message, and a veil is placed over their insight so that they cannot recognize the signs of the Creator in the universe; consequently, they forfeit the possibility of faith and face a severe retribution in the afterlife.

translation: And of the people are some who say, "We believe in Allah and the Last Day," but they are not believers.
interpretation: This verse addresses the hypocrites who outwardly declare their faith in Allah and the afterlife to integrate into the Muslim community and gain protection, while their hearts remain devoid of sincere belief; it serves as a divine exposure of those whose external professions contradict their internal spiritual state, highlighting that true faith is not merely a verbal claim but an affirmation that must dwell within the heart and manifest in one's deeds.

translation: They [think to] deceive Allah and those who believe, but they deceive not except themselves and perceive [it] not.
interpretation: This verse describes the behavior of the hypocrites who manifest faith outwardly while concealing disbelief inwardly, erroneously believing that their deceit can influence Allah or harm the believers. The Quran explains that this deception ultimately rebounds upon the hypocrites themselves, as they deprive their own souls of faith, guidance, and the eternal reward, becoming victims of their own duplicity while remaining blinded to the self-inflicted spiritual destruction they are causing.

translation: In their hearts is a disease, so Allah has increased their disease; and for them is a painful punishment because they used to lie.
interpretation: The disease mentioned refers to hypocrisy and spiritual corruption that infects the hearts of the hypocrites, and Allah increases this state by allowing them to sink further into their disbelief and deception as a consequence of their persistent refusal to embrace the truth, ultimately leading to their severe torment because they willfully rejected the divine message and practiced falsehood.

translation: And when it is said to them, 'Do not cause corruption on the earth,' they say, 'We are but reformers.'
interpretation: This verse describes a psychological state common among hypocrites, where they engage in actions that undermine the moral, social, or spiritual integrity of society, yet they justify their destructive behaviors by framing them as improvements, reforms, or necessary compromises, highlighting their lack of self-awareness and their deceptive nature in prioritizing their own agendas over the true well-being of the community.

translation: Unquestionably, it is they who are the corrupters, but they perceive [it] not.
interpretation: This verse reveals the self-deception of the hypocrites who, through their hypocrisy and alliance with the enemies of faith, corrupt the moral and social order of society while believing their actions are a form of wisdom or reformation, remaining entirely unaware of the destructive impact their conduct has on their own souls and the community.

translation: And when it is said to them, 'Believe as the people have believed,' they say, 'Should we believe as the foolish have believed?' Unquestionably, it is they who are the foolish, but they do not know.
interpretation: This verse reveals the arrogance of the hypocrites who viewed the sincere early believers as intellectually inferior or 'foolish' for accepting the message of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). God responds by turning their logic back upon them, declaring that true foolishness lies in their own rejection of the truth and their spiritual blindness, which prevents them from recognizing that it is they who have traded guidance for error, even if they lack the awareness to realize their own misguided state.

translation: And when they meet those who believe, they say, 'We have believed'; but when they are alone with their devils, they say, 'Indeed, we are with you; we were only mockers.'
interpretation: This verse describes the characteristic hypocrisy of the munafiqun (hypocrites), who lead a double life by feigning faith when in the company of the believers to gain social or political safety, while revealing their true animosity and allegiance to their corrupt leaders (their 'devils') in private, where they claim their previous profession of faith was merely a deceptive act of mockery meant to ridicule the Muslims.

translation: Allah mocks them and prolongs them in their transgression, [while] they wander blindly.
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah's mockery is a form of retributive justice; as the hypocrites mocked the believers, Allah leaves them to their own devices, allowing their wickedness to increase as a punishment for their stubborn disbelief, until they are utterly lost in their confusion and error.

translation: Those are the ones who have purchased error in exchange for guidance, so their transaction has brought no profit, nor were they guided.
interpretation: This verse uses the metaphor of a failed commercial transaction to describe those who consciously abandoned the path of truth and divine guidance in exchange for worldly misguidance and disbelief, emphasizing that this exchange results in a total loss of their spiritual potential and ultimate salvation because they traded an eternal, invaluable commodity for a transient, destructive one.

translation: Their example is like that of one who kindled a fire, but when it illuminated what was around him, Allah took away their light and left them in darknesses [so] they could not see.
interpretation: This verse describes the state of hypocrites who briefly embraced the truth through the guidance of Islam, likened to a fire providing light, but because their inner intentions remained corrupt, Allah stripped them of that spiritual insight, leaving them trapped in the darkness of their own disbelief, confusion, and inability to perceive the path to salvation.

translation: Deaf, dumb, and blind; so they will not return [to the right path].
interpretation: This verse describes the state of the hypocrites who, despite being presented with the clear evidence and truth of the message of Islam, have metaphorically blocked their faculties of perception because of their deep-seated arrogance and denial, rendering them unable to hear the truth, speak it, or perceive the guidance that would lead them back from their state of disbelief.

translation: Or like a rainstorm from the sky in which is darkness, thunder, and lightning. They put their fingers in their ears against the thunderclaps in dread of death. But Allah is encompassing the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse presents a profound parable for the state of hypocrites who, when confronted with the overwhelming clarity and potential consequences of divine truth—likened here to a terrifying, dark, and thunderous rainstorm—attempt to shut out the message by plugging their ears, hoping to avoid the spiritual reality that they perceive as a threat to their ego and worldly comfort, while failing to realize that they cannot escape the comprehensive reach and ultimate judgment of Allah, who possesses absolute power over them.

translation: The lightning almost snatches away their sight. Every time it lights [the way] for them, they walk therein; but when darkness comes over them, they stand [still]. And if Allah had willed, He could have taken away their hearing and their sight. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse describes the state of the hypocrites, likening their situation to a person caught in a violent storm; the 'lightning' symbolizes the clear proofs and divine signs that occasionally illuminate the truth for them, allowing them to make fleeting progress, while the 'darkness' represents the moments of doubt and disbelief that leave them paralyzed and unable to move forward in the path of faith. The verse highlights their inability to remain steadfast in the truth because their hearts are not firmly anchored, and it serves as a reminder of Allah's absolute power and forbearance in sparing their faculties despite their persistent rejection of His guidance.

translation: O mankind, worship your Lord, who created you and those before you, that you may become righteous.
interpretation: This verse serves as a universal call to all of humanity, grounding the obligation of worship in the fundamental truth of creation. By reminding people that their existence and the existence of their predecessors originated from a single Creator, God establishes His exclusive right to be worshiped. The ultimate objective of this worship is defined as 'taqwa' (righteousness or God-consciousness), suggesting that the act of acknowledging and submitting to the Creator acts as a spiritual discipline that protects the human soul from error and aligns it with divine purpose.

translation: [He] who made for you the earth a bed [spread out] and the sky a ceiling and sent down from the sky, rain and brought forth thereby fruits as provision for you. So do not attribute to Allah equals while you know [that there is nothing similar to Him].
interpretation: This verse serves as a rational proof of Allah's Oneness by highlighting the fundamental conditions of human life: the stability of the earth, the protective canopy of the atmosphere, and the life-sustaining cycle of rain. By describing these acts as exclusive manifestations of His creative power and sustenance, the verse emphasizes that since Allah is the sole Provider and Sustainer of the universe, it is logically inconsistent and ungrateful for human beings to associate partners with Him or worship anything else, as they inherently recognize that none of these miracles could be performed by any other being.

translation: And if you are in doubt about what We have sent down upon Our Servant [Muhammad], then produce a surah the like thereof and call upon your witnesses other than Allah, if you should be truthful.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine challenge to all skeptics who deny the prophethood of Muhammad and the authenticity of the Qur'an; Allah defies them to produce even a single chapter comparable to the Qur'an in its eloquence, legislative wisdom, and spiritual depth, emphasizing that if they truly believe the Qur'an is a human fabrication, they should be able to replicate it with the assistance of their allies and deities, thereby proving the impossibility of human authorship and establishing the Qur'an as a miraculous revelation from the Creator.

translation: But if you do not - and you will never be able to - then fear the Fire, whose fuel is people and stones, prepared for the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a definitive challenge to those who deny the divine origin of the Qur'an, asserting that their inability to produce anything comparable to it is not merely a temporary state, but an eternal impossibility. By invoking the description of the Fire fueled by people and stones, the text emphasizes the gravity of persisting in disbelief, suggesting that the very entities that fueled idol worship—the statues themselves—alongside their devotees, will become instruments of the torment they once ignored, highlighting that the ultimate destination for those who reject the truth is a consequence deliberately set for those who choose to remain in opposition to it.

translation: And give glad tidings to those who believe and do righteous deeds that they will have gardens beneath which rivers flow. Whenever they are provided with a provision of fruit therefrom, they will say, 'This is what we were provided with before,' for it is given to them in resemblance. And they will have therein purified spouses, and they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: The verse illustrates the eternal bliss of the believers in Paradise, emphasizing that the delights they receive—such as the fruits—will possess a beauty and quality familiar to them from their earthly lives, yet elevated to a state of perfect, heavenly resemblance. This familiarity brings comfort to the soul, while the promise of purified companions and an everlasting residence signifies the complete removal of worldly anxieties and the attainment of ultimate, undisturbed contentment.

translation: Indeed, Allah is not timid to present an example - that of a mosquito or what is smaller than it. And as for those who have believed, they know that it is the truth from their Lord. But as for those who disbelieve, they say, 'What did Allah intend by this as an example?' He misleads many thereby and guides many thereby. And He misleads not except the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: God illustrates that the scale or nature of a parable is irrelevant to its divine purpose; whether He speaks of a mosquito or something even more minuscule, the intent is always to reveal profound truth. This highlights that spiritual guidance is not contingent upon the greatness of the subject matter, but upon the heart's receptivity. Those with faith perceive the underlying wisdom and recognize it as a manifestation of divine knowledge, while the recalcitrant use the simplicity of the example as an excuse for skepticism. Ultimately, the parable serves as a divine filter: it clarifies the path for the sincere, while those who have already chosen to rebel against moral order find in these very parables a reason to further confirm their own deviation.

translation: Those who break the covenant of Allah after its ratification, and sever that which Allah has ordered to be joined, and cause corruption on earth - it is they who are the losers.
interpretation: This verse describes the characteristics of the transgressors who destroy the foundations of social and spiritual stability; by breaking their promise with God, they abandon the fundamental obligation of faith, and by severing the ties of kinship and the bonds of unity that God commanded to be maintained, they disrupt the harmony of human relationships, ultimately leading to their own ruin as they deprive themselves of the divine guidance and mercy necessary for eternal success.

translation: How can you disbelieve in Allah when you were lifeless and He brought you to life; then He will cause you to die, then He will bring you [back] to life, and then to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse serves as a profound call to reflection for the human conscience by highlighting the undeniable phases of existence: the initial state of non-existence, the gift of life granted by the Creator, the inevitable transition of death, the subsequent resurrection, and the ultimate accountability before God. It challenges the denial of a Creator by pointing out that the very transition from non-existence to being is an empirical sign of His power, arguing that one who possesses the ability to originate life and sustain the order of death and resurrection is the only logical recipient of worship, making any denial of His sovereignty an act of deep ingratitude and intellectual inconsistency.

translation: It is He who created for you all that is on earth, then He directed Himself to the heaven, and made them seven heavens, and He is, of all things, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse establishes that Allah brought the entire earthly realm into existence for the benefit and service of humanity, demonstrating His supreme authority and wisdom in the design of the universe, where the creation of the heavens following the earth signifies a deliberate and structured process of divine command, ultimately highlighting that nothing in existence escapes the comprehensive and infinite knowledge of the Creator.

translation: And when your Lord said to the angels, 'Indeed, I will make upon the earth a successive authority.' They said, 'Will You place upon it one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood, while we declare Your praise and sanctify You?' Allah said, 'Indeed, I know that which you do not know.'
interpretation: The command to place a successor on earth marks the appointment of humanity as custodians tasked with the cultivation and moral stewardship of the world according to divine guidance, signifying that despite the potential for human transgression and conflict, the creation of mankind serves a profound purpose in the divine order that transcends the limited understanding of the angels, who base their assessment solely on the preservation of absolute purity and perpetual glorification.

translation: And He taught Adam the names - all of them. Then He showed them to the angels and said, 'Inform Me of the names of these, if you are truthful.'
interpretation: God Almighty honored Adam by granting him the unique cognitive capacity to grasp the essence and categorization of all things, a knowledge He deliberately withheld from the angels to demonstrate that human existence carries a specific purpose grounded in intellect, agency, and the ability to perceive reality, thereby proving Adam's suitability for stewardship on Earth.

translation: They said, 'Exalted are You; we have no knowledge except what You have taught us. Indeed, it is You who is the Knowing, the Wise.'
interpretation: The angels, upon being unable to name the things Allah had presented to them, acknowledged their limitations and absolute dependence on the Creator, affirming that all knowledge is a gift bestowed by Him alone according to His divine wisdom and decree, thereby demonstrating the essence of true servitude through humble recognition of His omniscience.

translation: He said, 'O Adam, inform them of their names.' And when he had informed them of their names, He said, 'Did I not tell you that I know the unseen [aspects] of the heavens and the earth? And I know what you reveal and what you have been concealing.'
interpretation: In this moment, Allah demonstrates to the angels the superiority of Adam through his divinely granted knowledge, proving that Adam possesses an understanding of the essence and nature of creation that they do not. By commanding Adam to name the objects, Allah validates that humans were granted a capacity for language, categorization, and intellectual inquiry which serves as the basis for their vicegerency on earth. The final declaration by Allah serves as a reminder to the angels of His absolute omniscience, emphasizing that He is aware of both the outward actions performed by His creatures and the innermost thoughts and hidden intentions they seek to keep secret.

translation: And when We said to the angels, 'Prostrate to Adam,' they prostrated, except for Iblis; he refused and was arrogant and became of the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights that the root of Iblis's disobedience was not a lack of knowledge regarding God's command, but rather the internal vices of pride and arrogance. By refusing to show honor to Adam as instructed, Iblis elevated his own ego above the divine decree, demonstrating that arrogance is a fundamental barrier to faith and obedience, ultimately leading one to reject the truth and distance themselves from divine mercy.

translation: And We said, 'O Adam, dwell, you and your wife, in Paradise and eat therefrom in [ease and] abundance from wherever you will. But do not approach this tree, lest you be among the wrongdoers.'
interpretation: This verse signifies the initial state of innocence and provision granted to humanity by God, setting clear boundaries for obedience. The prohibition against approaching the tree was not a restriction on enjoyment, but rather a trial to exercise free will and respect the divine covenant, emphasizing that disobedience acts as a form of self-transgression by distancing the soul from the grace and guidance of its Creator.

translation: But Satan caused them to slip out of it and removed them from that [condition] in which they had been. And We said, 'Go down, [all of you], as enemies to one another, and you will have upon the earth a place of settlement and provision for a time.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the cunning nature of Satan, who used deception to lead Adam and Eve into disobedience, resulting in their removal from the state of grace and comfort in Paradise. The command to 'go down' signifies the transition of humanity from a state of eternal bliss to a life on Earth characterized by struggle, trial, and limited duration, establishing the world as a temporary testing ground where human conflicts and the ongoing battle between good and evil will persist until the appointed time.

translation: Then Adam received from his Lord [some] words, and He accepted his repentance. Indeed, it is He who is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.
interpretation: When Adam realized his error after eating from the forbidden tree, he felt profound remorse. Allah, in His boundless grace, inspired Adam with words of supplication through which he could seek forgiveness. This demonstrates that repentance is a divine gift; it is Allah who first guides the servant to repent, and then, because of His inherent nature as the Oft-Returning and the Merciful, He accepts that repentance and restores the servant to His favor.

translation: We said, 'Go down from it, all of you. And when guidance comes to you from Me, whoever follows My guidance - there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve.'
interpretation: This verse signifies the commencement of human responsibility on Earth, establishing that the transition from a state of primordial ease to the trials of worldly life is not a abandonment, but a relocation governed by divine connection; by providing guidance, Allah guarantees that those who align their will with His revealed truth will be granted an inner tranquility and spiritual security that transcends worldly circumstances, effectively insulating them from the existential fear of the unknown and the sorrow of past worldly attachments.

translation: But those who disbelieve and deny Our verses - those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse serves as a declaration of the ultimate consequence for those who willfully reject the truth of God’s signs and revelations; by persistently choosing denial over guidance, they effectively seal their own fate, resulting in an everlasting confinement in the Fire, signifying that their persistent rejection has fundamentally transformed their inner state such that they are no longer fit for the proximity of Divine mercy.

translation: O Children of Israel, remember My favor which I have bestowed upon you and fulfill My covenant [upon you] that I will fulfill your covenant [from Me], and be afraid of none but Me.
interpretation: God calls upon the Children of Israel to reflect on the immense blessings and divine guidance bestowed upon their ancestors, reminding them that their prosperity and security are contingent upon their faithfulness to the spiritual and ethical agreement they made with God. By commanding them to fulfill their side of the covenant—which involves upholding the truth and following His messengers—God guarantees them His protection and promised rewards, while simultaneously warning that true fear and reverence must be directed solely toward Him, as He alone holds the power to reward or punish.

translation: And believe in what I have sent down, confirming that which is with you, and do not be the first to disbelieve in it. And do not exchange My signs for a small price, and fear only Me.
interpretation: Allah commands the People of the Scripture to believe in the Qur'an, which confirms the original truth revealed in the Torah and the Gospel, and warns them against being the pioneers of disbelief in this new message due to worldly attachments, emphasizing that the guidance of God is worth far more than any fleeting material gain they might acquire by suppressing the truth.

translation: And do not mix the truth with falsehood or conceal the truth while you know [it].
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning against the intellectual and moral dishonesty of obscuring divine guidance with human fabrications, urging believers and People of the Scripture to maintain integrity by openly declaring the truth they recognize, rather than suppressing it to serve personal agendas or social pressures, as conscious suppression of divine revelation constitutes a severe betrayal of one's covenant with God.

translation: And establish prayer, give zakah, and bow with those who bow.
interpretation: This verse commands the believers to perform their prayers perfectly by observing its conditions and pillars, to fulfill the obligation of giving charity to the needy as a means of purifying the soul and wealth, and to perform acts of worship collectively in congregation with the Muslim community, emphasizing the importance of communal unity and shared devotion to God.

translation: Do you enjoin righteousness upon the people and forget yourselves while you recite the Scripture? Then will you not reason?
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern rebuke to those who advocate for virtue and piety to others but fail to embody those same principles themselves, highlighting the hypocrisy of possessing religious knowledge without applying it to one's own conduct. It emphasizes that true intellect and sound reasoning require an individual to align their personal actions with the truths they preach, as ignoring one's own spiritual state while guiding others is a clear contradiction of divine guidance and rational integrity.

translation: And seek help through patience and prayer, and indeed, it is difficult except for the humbly submissive [to Allah].
interpretation: Allah commands the believers to rely on patience—specifically in enduring the hardships of life and remaining steadfast in obedience—and prayer as their primary sources of strength when facing difficulties; this path is described as heavy and burdensome to the soul because it requires abandoning desires and submitting to divine discipline, a challenge that can only be overcome by those who possess true humility, fear of Allah, and complete devotion to His presence.

translation: Those who are certain that they will meet their Lord and that they will return to Him.
interpretation: The verse describes the state of the humble believers who carry a profound and firm conviction in the reality of the afterlife; their certainty regarding the meeting with Allah and their inevitable return to Him serves as the primary motivation for them to maintain patience, prayer, and submissiveness, as they realize that all actions will be judged and all worldly matters will ultimately conclude in the presence of their Creator.

translation: O Children of Israel, remember My favor which I have bestowed upon you and that I preferred you over the worlds.
interpretation: God addresses the Children of Israel, reminding them of the historical manifestations of His grace upon their ancestors—such as deliverance from Pharaoh, the provision of Manna and Salwa, and the appointment of prophets and messengers from among them—which served as a period of divine selection intended to establish them as a beacon of guidance for humanity, contingent upon their adherence to His covenant.

translation: And fear a Day when no soul will suffice for another soul at all, nor will intercession be accepted from it, nor will compensation be taken from it, nor will they be aided.
interpretation: This verse serves as a solemn warning regarding the absolute finality and justice of the Day of Judgment, emphasizing that every individual will be held accountable solely for their own deeds. It highlights that in that ultimate moment, human connections, worldly ransom, or collective support will provide no protection; rather, the soul's fate will depend entirely on the merit of its own faith and righteous actions before God, making it imperative for the believer to prepare through piety and sincerity while they still have the opportunity.

translation: And recall when We saved you from the people of Pharaoh, who were inflicting upon you the worst of torment, slaughtering your [newborn] sons and keeping your women alive. And in that was a great trial from your Lord.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder to the Children of Israel of the immense favor God bestowed upon them by delivering them from the systemic oppression of Pharaoh, who sought to weaken their community by killing their male offspring to ensure their eventual extinction while sparing their females for servitude; the reference to this experience as a 'great trial' signifies that their liberation was not merely a physical rescue but a profound test of their faith, gratitude, and steadfastness in acknowledging God as the sole architect of their salvation.

translation: And [recall] when We parted the sea for you and saved you and drowned the people of Pharaoh while you were looking on.
interpretation: This verse serves as a profound reminder of Allah's miraculous intervention on behalf of the Children of Israel, highlighting His absolute power over the natural order by splitting the sea to provide them a path of salvation while simultaneously delivering retribution upon their oppressors, the Pharaoh and his followers, who were witnesses to their own destruction as a consequence of their persistent disbelief and tyranny.

translation: And [recall] when We made an appointment with Moses for forty nights. Then you took [for worship] the calf after him, while you were wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse recounts a moment of profound spiritual betrayal by the Children of Israel; despite the sacred covenant established during the forty nights Moses spent in communion with God on Mount Sinai, the people succumbed to their base desires and ignorance by fashioning and worshipping a golden calf, thereby committing a grave act of polytheism (shirk) and injustice against their own souls through their breach of faith.

translation: Then We forgave you after that, so that you might be grateful.
interpretation: This verse signifies that despite the people's repeated transgressions and rebellion against divine guidance, God bestowed His mercy upon them by pardoning their offenses, intending for them to recognize this immense favor and respond with sincere gratitude, obedience, and commitment to the truth.

translation: And [recall] when We gave Moses the Scripture and the criterion that you might be guided.
interpretation: This verse reminds the Children of Israel of the immense divine favor bestowed upon Moses, specifically the revelation of the Torah, which served as both a comprehensive guide and a 'Furqan'—a clear standard to distinguish between truth and falsehood, good and evil, and light and darkness, intended to lead the community out of ignorance and into the path of spiritual uprightness.

translation: And [recall] when Moses said to his people, 'O my people, indeed you have wronged yourselves by your taking of the calf [for worship]. So repent to your Creator and kill yourselves. That is best for you in the sight of your Creator.' Then He accepted your repentance; indeed, He is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse recounts the severe trial faced by the Children of Israel after they committed the grave sin of idolatry. The command for the wrongdoers to 'kill themselves' was a profound form of penance, representing the ultimate submission of the soul to God's justice and a physical manifestation of purging the idolatrous impulse from within. By enacting this repentance, they demonstrated the sincerity of their contrition, leading God to restore His mercy upon them, highlighting that no sin is too great for the door of divine forgiveness if it is met with true, transformative repentance.

translation: And [recall] when you said, 'O Moses, we will not believe you until we see Allah outright'; so the thunderbolt took you while you were looking on.
interpretation: This verse serves as a rebuke to the Children of Israel for their arrogance and excessive demands in the presence of Moses; their insistence on seeing God with their physical eyes was an act of extreme insolence that disregarded the limitations of human perception and the nature of the Divine, resulting in their immediate punishment by a celestial fire or thunderous roar, which demonstrated the gravity of their defiance and the absolute necessity of approaching faith through the submission to revelation rather than empirical physical demands.

translation: Then We revived you after your death, so that you might be grateful.
interpretation: This verse refers to the historical incident where the Children of Israel were struck by death as a consequence of their arrogance and demand to see Allah directly, after which Allah restored them to life to give them a second chance to repent, recognize His absolute power over life and death, and respond with true gratitude and obedience.

translation: And We shaded you with clouds and sent down to you manna and quails, [saying], 'Eat from the good things which We have provided for you.' And they wronged Us not - but they were [only] wronging themselves.
interpretation: This verse reminds the Children of Israel of the divine favors bestowed upon them during their wandering in the wilderness, where God provided them with shade from the intense heat and sustenance without toil. The conclusion emphasizes that when they chose to rebel against God's commands or express ingratitude for these bounties, they did not inflict any harm upon God, for He is beyond any need. Instead, they acted as their own enemies, causing their own spiritual ruin and inviting the consequences of their disobedience upon their own souls.

translation: And mention when We said, 'Enter this city and eat from it wherever you will in [ease and] abundance, and enter the gate bowing humbly and say, 'Relieve us of our burdens,' We will [then] forgive your sins for you, and We will increase the doers of good [in goodness and reward].'
interpretation: This verse serves as a historical reminder to the Children of Israel regarding the divine instruction to enter a place of safety and prosperity with a humble, repentant attitude; it illustrates that the path to God's forgiveness and increased grace is paved through the twin requirements of submission to His authority and a sincere request for the removal of one's shortcomings, emphasizing that the promise of divine favor is explicitly conditional upon the individual's commitment to being a muhsin, or one who performs deeds with excellence and sincerity.

translation: But those who did wrong changed the words to other than that which had been told to them, so We sent down upon those who did wrong a torment from the sky because they were defiantly disobeying.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the consequence of moral corruption and disobedience, specifically highlighting that when people deliberately alter divine instructions or substitute truth with falsehood, they bring upon themselves divine retribution as a direct result of their persistent rebellion and abandonment of the path of righteousness.

translation: And when Moses prayed for water for his people, We said, 'Strike the stone with your staff,' and there gushed forth from it twelve springs, and every tribe knew their drinking place. 'Eat and drink from the provision of Allah, and do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the miraculous divine care bestowed upon the Children of Israel during their wanderings, emphasizing that even in the harsh wilderness, God provided for their physical needs through supernatural means. The command to 'not commit abuse' serves as a spiritual reminder that material abundance and divine favor require human gratitude, restraint, and adherence to moral laws rather than arrogance and moral decay.

translation: And when you said, 'O Moses, we can never endure one [kind of] food. So call upon your Lord to bring forth for us from the earth its green herbs, its cucumbers, its garlic, its lentils, and its onions.' Moses said, 'Would you exchange what is better for what is less? Go down into any city, and indeed, you will have what you have asked.' And they were struck with humiliation and poverty and returned with anger from Allah; that was because they used to disbelieve in the signs of Allah and kill the prophets without right. That was because they disobeyed and were transgressing.
interpretation: This verse serves as a historical rebuke to the Children of Israel, illustrating their ingratitude for the divine provision of Manna and Salwa, which were superior spiritual and physical blessings. By demanding mundane agricultural crops over these heavenly gifts, they demonstrated a preference for the base and temporal over the sublime and eternal. The subsequent mention of their humiliation and the wrath of God highlights that this specific rebellion was not an isolated incident, but a manifestation of a deeper, persistent cycle of spiritual arrogance, the rejection of prophetic truth, and the violation of divine limits, which ultimately leads to a state of spiritual desolation.

translation: Indeed, those who believed and those who were Jews or Christians or Sabeans [before Prophet Muhammad] - those who believed in Allah and the Last Day and did righteousness - will have their reward with their Lord, and no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the criterion for salvation and reward from Allah is not restricted to a specific label or affiliation, but rather contingent upon sincere faith in the Oneness of Allah and the reality of the Hereafter, coupled with the performance of righteous deeds, acknowledging that those who followed the divine guidance of their respective prophets in their era of truth and lived righteously are promised a state of eternal peace and security in the presence of their Creator.

translation: And [recall] when We took your covenant and raised over you the mount, [saying], 'Take what We have given you with determination and remember what is in it, that you might become righteous.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine reminder to the Children of Israel regarding the solemn pact they made to uphold the Torah. The act of raising Mount Sinai above them symbolizes the weight and absolute gravity of the divine command, compelling them to accept the scripture not as a mere suggestion, but with steadfast commitment and serious resolve. By urging them to remember and internalize the teachings contained within, Allah emphasizes that constant mindfulness and active application of the law are the essential paths to achieving 'taqwa' (God-consciousness), which guards the soul against deviation and preserves the purity of faith.

translation: Then you turned away after that; and had it not been for the favor of Allah upon you and His mercy, you would have been among the losers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern reminder of the frailty of human nature and the inherent inclination to stray from divine guidance; it emphasizes that if not for the constant grace and compassionate interventions of Allah, the cumulative weight of human rebellion and neglect of covenant would inevitably lead to absolute spiritual ruin and eternal loss.

translation: And you have already known about those amongst you who transgressed in the matter of the Sabbath, so We said to them, 'Be you monkeys, despised and rejected.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine warning regarding the historical incident where a group of Israelites defied the command of Allah to abstain from fishing on the Sabbath. By overtly violating the sacred law they were bound to, they committed an act of rebellion that led to their physical and spiritual transformation. The transformation into 'monkeys' signifies the loss of their human dignity and their descent into a state of disgrace and exclusion from Allah's mercy, serving as an eternal lesson that those who consciously twist divine laws for worldly gain lose their moral stature and become objects of contempt.

translation: And We made it a deterrent punishment for those who were present and those who came after them, and a lesson for the righteous.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the punishment inflicted upon those who transgressed the Sabbath was intended to serve as a cautionary example that deters contemporaries and future generations from committing similar acts of defiance against divine law, while simultaneously acting as an enlightening exhortation for those who fear God to remain steadfast in their piety and obedience.

translation: And mention when Moses said to his people, 'Indeed, Allah commands you to slaughter a cow.' They said, 'Do you take us in ridicule?' He said, 'I seek refuge in Allah from being among the ignorant.'
interpretation: When Prophet Moses delivered the divine command to his people to slaughter a cow, they responded with suspicion and arrogance, viewing his instruction as a mockery rather than a serious religious duty. This verse highlights the danger of questioning divine commands based on human logic or cultural bias, as Moses clarifies that his role is merely to convey the truth from God, and that to mock or ignore such a command would be an act of profound ignorance—ignoring the gravity of God's authority and the wisdom inherent in His decrees.

translation: They said, 'Call upon your Lord to make clear to us what it is.' He said, '[Allah] says,
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubbornness of the Children of Israel who, by constantly questioning and demanding specific details about the cow, made a simple act of obedience complicated for themselves; the description given indicates that the cow should be of a moderate age, neither too old nor too young, which serves as a lesson that when Allah commands an act of worship, one should hasten to fulfill it with sincere submission rather than seeking unnecessary complications that may lead to hardship.

translation: They said, 'Call upon your Lord to make clear to us what its color is.' He said, 'Indeed, He says that it is a yellow cow, bright in color, pleasing to the beholders.'
interpretation: The people of Musa continued to place obstacles and ask excessive questions regarding the cow they were commanded to sacrifice, aiming to avoid the obligation. In response, Allah specified that the cow must be bright yellow—a color so vibrant and pure that it brings joy and delight to anyone who looks upon it, indicating the necessity of perfection and lack of flaws in the animal chosen for this divine command.

translation: They said, 'Call upon your Lord for us to make clear to us what it is. Indeed, all cows look alike to us. And indeed we, if Allah wills, will be guided.'
interpretation: The people of Musa expressed their confusion and hesitant nature by asking for further clarification regarding the cow's specific attributes, acknowledging that the variety of cows made it difficult for them to identify the correct one, while simultaneously expressing a commitment to follow guidance should Allah clarify the matter further.

translation: He said, 'He says, it is a cow neither trained to till the earth nor to irrigate the field, one free from fault and without any spot in her.' They said, 'Now you have brought the truth.' So they slaughtered her, though they had nearly not done so.
interpretation: The extreme specificity of the physical requirements for the cow serves as an allegorical reflection of the Israelites' psychological resistance; by imposing increasingly difficult and arbitrary constraints, the command intended to expose their profound reluctance to obey God's decree. Their exclamation that he had 'now brought the truth' only after the description became impossibly narrow reveals that their primary motivation was not the fulfillment of the divine command, but rather the hope that the task would be rendered impossible, thus granting them an excuse to evade the burden of obedience.

translation: And [recall] when you slew a man and disputed over it, but Allah was to bring out that which you were concealing.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern reminder that human attempts to obscure the truth or cover up criminal acts through mutual accusation or denial are ultimately futile, because Allah possesses absolute knowledge and perfect power to expose hidden deeds and bring the truth to light, regardless of how meticulously the perpetrators attempt to hide their involvement.

translation: Then We said, 'Strike the slain man with part of the cow.' Thus does Allah bring the dead to life, and He shows you His signs that you might use reason.
interpretation: By commanding the Israelites to strike the deceased with a part of the slaughtered cow, Allah demonstrated His absolute power over life and death, teaching them that just as He revived this body to identify its killer, He is capable of resurrecting all of humanity on the Day of Judgment, urging the human intellect to reflect upon these tangible proofs to move from doubt to certain faith.

translation: Then your hearts became hardened after that, being like stones or even harder. For indeed, there are stones from which rivers gush forth, and there are some that split open and water comes out, and there are some that fall down for fear of Allah. And Allah is not unaware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse serves as a profound metaphor for the spiritual state of the Children of Israel who, despite witnessing clear divine miracles, allowed their hearts to become insensible to the truth. By comparing their hearts to stone, Allah highlights a state of spiritual rigidity where the capacity for humility, gratitude, and awe—qualities that even inanimate objects like stones exhibit before the majesty of their Creator—has been extinguished, warning the reader that human pride and persistent rejection of truth can result in a spiritual atrophy that is even more formidable and impenetrable than the hardest rock.

translation: Do you then hope that they would believe you, while a party of them used to hear the words of Allah, then pervert it after they had understood it, while they knew?
interpretation: This verse serves as a rhetorical reprimand to the believers, emphasizing that it is futile to expect the hardened hearts of those who knowingly distorted the divine revelation to embrace the truth, as their history of willful corruption and intellectual dishonesty demonstrates a deliberate rejection of guidance despite their clear comprehension of it.

translation: And when they meet those who believe, they say, 'We have believed'; but when they are alone with one another, they say, 'Do you talk to them about what Allah has revealed to you so they can argue with you about it before your Lord? Will you not then use your reason?'
interpretation: This verse reveals the hypocritical nature of certain individuals who adopt a double-faced approach: they profess belief when in the company of the faithful to secure social or political advantages, yet behind closed doors, they caution their peers against disclosing religious knowledge or evidence from their scriptures that might eventually be used against them by the believers to prove their falsehood on the Day of Judgment, showing that their primary concern is worldly self-preservation rather than truth.

translation: Do they not know that Allah knows what they conceal and what they declare?
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern reminder of Allah’s absolute omniscience, highlighting the futility of human hypocrisy. It addresses those who harbor hidden intentions or engage in secretive wrongdoing, asserting that there is no boundary between the private, inner thoughts of the heart and the public, overt actions of the limbs in the sight of the Creator. By questioning their lack of awareness, the verse warns that since nothing is hidden from Allah, every secret intent will be accounted for just as surely as every public deed, thereby urging the believer toward sincerity and the abandonment of deceptive behavior.

translation: And among them are unlettered ones who do not know the Scripture except in wishful thinking, and they are but guessing.
interpretation: This verse addresses a segment of the People of the Scripture who were illiterate regarding the true divine revelation, lacking the ability to read or properly comprehend the scriptures, and instead relied on mere hearsay, baseless fabrications, and distorted interpretations inherited from their ancestors, treating these groundless assumptions as divine truth while they remained in a state of conjecture and uncertainty.

translation: So woe to those who write the 'Scripture' with their own hands, then say, 'This is from Allah,' in order to exchange it for a small price. Woe to them for what their hands have written and woe to them for what they earn.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning and condemnation of religious scholars or individuals who deliberately distort the divine scriptures by altering, falsifying, or inventing rulings to suit their own worldly desires and personal gain. By falsely attributing these human fabrications to Allah, they deceive the masses and compromise the truth for trivial material benefits, thereby incurring severe spiritual ruin and punishment for both their act of forgery and the illicit wealth they accumulate through this deception.

translation: And they said, 'The Fire will not touch us except for a number of days.' Say, 'Have you taken a covenant with Allah? For Allah will never break His covenant. Or do you say about Allah that which you do not know?'
interpretation: The verse exposes the arrogance and baseless claims of those who believe they are exempt from divine accountability, highlighting that their assertion of a limited punishment is a fabrication rooted in wishful thinking rather than any divine promise, thereby challenging them to produce evidence for a covenant that does not exist.

translation: Yes, whoever earns evil and his sin has encompassed him; those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse signifies that those who persist in disbelief and commit sins until their hearts are entirely overwhelmed and locked by them, leaving no room for repentance or faith, are those whose destiny is the Hellfire, where they shall remain forever because their very souls have become identified with their sinful state, rendering them incapable of returning to the truth.

translation: But they who believe and do righteous deeds - those are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the attainment of eternal paradise is contingent upon the inseparable combination of sincere faith in the heart and the outward manifestation of that faith through righteous deeds, confirming that those who harmonize their belief with obedience to God's commands are the true inhabitants of heaven who will dwell there forever in a state of permanent bliss and security.

translation: And remember when We took a covenant from the Children of Israel: 'Do not worship anyone but Allah, and show goodness to parents, relatives, orphans, and the needy, and speak kindly to people, and perform the prayer, and give the zakat.' Then you turned away, except for a few of you, and you were refusing.
interpretation: This verse serves as a historical reminder to the Children of Israel of the fundamental divine obligations that transcend time and law, emphasizing that the worship of the One God is inextricably linked to social morality and compassion. By commanding kindness toward family and the vulnerable alongside the pillars of prayer and charity, the verse teaches that a true relationship with the Creator is validated by the quality of one's treatment of fellow human beings, further highlighting that the subsequent betrayal of this covenant by the majority was not an act of mere forgetfulness, but a deliberate and persistent turning away from the clear truth despite their knowledge of it.

translation: And [recall] when We took your covenant, [saying], 'Do not shed each other’s blood or evict one another from your homes.' Then you acknowledged [this while] you were witnessing.
interpretation: This verse addresses the Children of Israel, reminding them of the solemn pledge they made to God to uphold the sanctity of human life and to respect communal property rights by not resorting to violence or forced displacement against their own kin, emphasizing that they are morally and legally bound by this agreement to which they themselves bore witness as a binding duty.

translation: Then you are those who kill one another and drive out a party of your people from their homes, assisting one another against them in sin and aggression; and if they come to you as captives, you ransom them, although their expulsion was forbidden to you. Do you believe in part of the Scripture and disbelieve in part? Then what is the recompense for those who do that among you except disgrace in worldly life; and on the Day of Resurrection they will be sent back to the severest of punishment. And Allah is not unaware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern reprimand to the Children of Israel for their hypocritical and inconsistent application of Divine Law; they selectively honored the commandment to ransom captives while brazenly violating the far more fundamental prohibition against shedding the blood of their kin and expelling them from their homes, thereby exposing the corruption of their hearts which prioritized tribal alliances and worldly interests over true obedience to God's comprehensive command.

translation: Those are the ones who have bought the life of this world with the Hereafter, so the punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be aided.
interpretation: These individuals have consciously prioritized transient worldly gains and desires over the eternal reward of the afterlife, effectively trading their salvation for temporary enjoyment; consequently, they have forfeited any grounds for mercy, ensuring that their divine chastisement will remain severe and absolute, with no intercessor or power capable of protecting them from the justice of God.

translation: And We gave Moses the Book and followed up after him with messengers. And We gave Jesus, the son of Mary, clear proofs and supported him with the Pure Spirit. But is it [not] that whenever a messenger came to you with what your souls did not desire, you were arrogant? And a party [of messengers] you denied and another party you killed.
interpretation: This verse addresses the Children of Israel, highlighting their historical pattern of rebellious behavior toward God's messengers. By reminding them that God provided them with consistent guidance through Moses, Jesus, and subsequent prophets, the verse exposes their hypocrisy: they claim to follow the Torah while simultaneously rejecting and even murdering the very messengers sent to renew that same divine truth, simply because those prophets challenged their personal desires, worldly interests, and ingrained arrogance.

translation: And they said, 'Our hearts are wrapped [in covers, preventing them from understanding].' But Allah has cursed them for their disbelief, so little is it that they believe.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubborn arrogance of the disbelievers who claim their lack of faith is due to an inherent incapacity or divine sealing of their hearts; however, the Qur'an clarifies that their state is a direct consequence of their own persistent rejection of truth, which led to them being deprived of divine grace and guidance, resulting in their inability to accept faith except in a trivial and inconsequential manner.

translation: And when there came to them a Book from Allah confirming that which was with them - although before they used to pray for victory against those who disbelieved - but when there came to them that which they recognized, they disbelieved in it; so the curse of Allah will be upon the disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse highlights the irony and obstinacy of the People of the Scripture, who had long awaited the arrival of the final Prophet described in their own sacred texts to aid them in their struggles against polytheists. However, once the Prophet Muhammad appeared and brought the Quran—which verified the core truths of their previous scriptures—they rejected him out of arrogance, envy, and the fear of losing their status, thus turning their backs on the very truth they had previously championed.

translation: How wretched is that for which they sold themselves - that they would disbelieve in what Allah has revealed through out of jealous envy that Allah would send down His bounty upon whom He wills from among His servants. So they returned with wrath upon wrath. And for the disbelievers is a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse condemns the Jews who recognized the truth of the Prophet Muhammad's message but rejected it out of pride and envy, specifically because they could not accept that Allah would bestow the honor of prophethood upon someone other than themselves; consequently, their refusal to accept this divine grace resulted in their incurring God's wrath upon wrath—the first for their past disbelief in previous revelations and the second for their rejection of the final revelation—ultimately leading to their deserved state of humiliation and spiritual loss.

translation: And when it is said to them, 'Believe in what Allah has revealed,' they say, 'We believe [only] in what was revealed to us.' And they disbelieve in what came after it, while it is the truth confirming that which is with them. Say, 'Then why did you kill the prophets of Allah before, if you are [indeed] believers?'
interpretation: This verse exposes the inconsistent hypocrisy of the People of the Scripture; they claim adherence to their own revealed laws as an excuse to reject the final revelation, yet their history of slaying the prophets sent to them contradicts their claim of true faith, proving that their rejection of the Qur'an is not based on devotion to God's law but on willful arrogance and selective obedience.

translation: And Moses had certainly come to you with clear proofs. Then you took the calf [for worship] after he had left, while you were wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a historical rebuke to the Children of Israel, highlighting the inconsistency and ingratitude of their ancestors; despite receiving undeniable evidence of God's truth through Moses, they succumbed to the temptation of idolatry by worshiping the golden calf, an act of profound spiritual injustice and moral rebellion committed knowingly after having witnessed the divine signs.

translation: And [recall] when We took your covenant and raised over you the mount, [saying], 'Take what We have given you with determination and listen.' They said, '[We] hear and disobey.' And their hearts were imbued with [the love of] the calf because of their disbelief. Say, 'How wretched is that which your faith enjoins upon you, if you should be believers.'
interpretation: This verse exposes the deep-seated hypocrisy and spiritual corruption of the Children of Israel who, despite witnessing the awe-inspiring power of Allah when Mount Sinai was raised above them as a sign of His covenant, responded with verbal compliance masking inward rebellion. Their claim to 'hear' was immediately negated by their act of 'disobedience,' revealing that their hearts had become so saturated with the love of false idols—symbolized by the golden calf—that this idolatry had displaced the true faith they claimed to possess, making their supposed belief worthless and contradictory to the commandments of God.

translation: Say, 'If the home of the Hereafter with Allah is for you exclusively and not the [other] people, then wish for death, if you should be truthful.'
interpretation: The verse serves as a divine challenge to those who falsely claim exclusive entitlement to Paradise while persisting in their disbelief; Allah commands the Prophet to demand they express a sincere desire for death as a testament to their claim, since anyone who truly believes they have secured a place of eternal bliss with the Creator would naturally yearn to leave the hardships of this transient world to attain that reward immediately.

translation: But they will never wish for it, ever, because of what their hands have put forth. And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse highlights that the hypocrites will never desire death because they are fully aware of the sins and evil deeds they have committed, which await them in the afterlife; therefore, their inner knowledge of their own transgression and the inevitable divine retribution acts as a barrier to their longing for a confrontation with the truth of the hereafter, all while God remains perfectly aware of their hidden injustices.

translation: And you will surely find them the most greedy of people for life—[even] more than those who associate others with Allah. One of them wishes that he could be granted life a thousand years, but it would not remove him in the least from the [destined] punishment that he should be granted life. And Allah is Seeing of what they do.
interpretation: This verse exposes the deep-seated attachment to worldly life felt by those who deny the truth, highlighting their fear of death and their pursuit of long life as a means to escape divine reckoning. Despite their longing for immortality, the verse serves as a stern reminder that length of life is not a currency to purchase salvation; no matter how long a person remains in this world, they cannot avoid the ultimate accountability for their actions, as Allah is fully aware of the deeds they perform and the true intentions underlying their worldly desires.

translation: Say, 'Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel - it is he who has brought the revelation down upon your heart, by permission of Allah, confirming that which was before it and as guidance and good tidings for the believers.'
interpretation: The verse serves as a stern refutation against those who claimed to believe in Allah but expressed hostility toward the angel Gabriel, arguing that Gabriel is not acting on his own authority but is merely the trusted messenger who transmits the Quran directly to the Prophet's heart by Allah's divine command; therefore, rejecting the messenger of revelation is equivalent to rejecting the revelation itself, which serves as a divine confirmation of previous scriptures and a source of guidance and joyful news for those who have faith.

translation: Whoever is an enemy to Allah and His angels and His messengers and Gabriel and Michael - then indeed, Allah is an enemy to the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse establishes that hostility towards Allah's appointed agents, such as the angels Gabriel and Michael—who are tasked with conveying revelation and providing sustenance—is essentially hostility towards Allah Himself. By naming these specific angels, the Qur'an refutes the excuses of those who claimed they accepted Allah but rejected His messengers or specific angels, clarifying that rejecting any part of Allah's divine chain of communication and authority is an act of disbelief that positions the individual as an adversary of the Creator.

translation: And We have certainly revealed to you verses of clear evidence, and none deny them except the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse asserts that the divine revelations provided to the Prophet Muhammad are self-evidently clear and logically sound, leaving no room for sincere confusion; therefore, those who persist in rejecting these signs do so not because of a lack of proof, but because they have chosen to abandon the path of obedience and moral integrity, effectively blinding themselves to the truth due to their own willful rebellion against God.

translation: Is it not that every time they made a covenant, a party of them threw it away? But most of them do not believe.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inherent perfidy and inconsistency of those who lack true faith; their hearts are not anchored by the sanctity of promises, leading them to repeatedly violate their commitments whenever their personal interests or whims dictate, demonstrating that their superficial agreements are devoid of the sincerity that true belief in God would otherwise necessitate.

translation: And when a messenger from Allah came to them confirming what was with them, a party of those who were given the Scripture threw the Book of Allah behind their backs as if they did not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy and rejection of the Jewish scholars who, despite possessing the Torah that foretold the coming of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), chose to ignore and discard the truth once it was manifest. By 'throwing the Book of Allah behind their backs,' they metaphorically abandoned the divine guidance they were entrusted with, acting out of arrogance and worldly interests rather than ignorance, thereby willfully violating their covenant with Allah.

translation: And they followed what the devils had recited during the reign of Solomon. It was not Solomon who disbelieved, but the devils disbelieved, teaching people magic and that which was revealed to the two angels at Babylon, Harut and Marut. But the two angels do not teach anyone unless they say, 'We are a trial, so do not disbelieve.' And yet they learn from them that by which they cause separation between a man and his wife. But they do not harm anyone through it except by permission of Allah. And the people learn what harms them and does not benefit them. And they certainly knew that whoever purchased it would not have any share in the Hereafter. And wretched is that for which they sold themselves, if they only knew.
interpretation: This verse clarifies that magic is a source of corruption that does not possess independent power, as all effects occur solely by the permission and decree of Allah. It highlights that the practice of magic is an act of disbelief and a spiritual ruin, where individuals seek transient harm for others at the cost of their own eternal salvation. By framing the knowledge of Harut and Marut as a test, the verse warns that true wisdom lies in seeking knowledge that benefits the soul rather than pursuing forbidden arts that sever human bonds and distance the practitioner from the mercy of God.

translation: And if they had believed and feared Allah, then the reward from Allah would have been far better, if they only knew.
interpretation: This verse underscores that the true essence of prosperity and ultimate success lies in faith combined with God-consciousness; it implies that the worldly gains or illicit advantages people often chase are trivial compared to the eternal, superior rewards that Allah grants to those who align their lives with His guidance, suggesting that if human beings truly understood the nature of eternal life versus the fleeting nature of this world, they would prioritize spiritual integrity over temporary worldly interests.

translation: O you who have believed, do not say 'Ra'ina' [listen to us], but say 'Unzurna' [look at us] and listen. And for the disbelievers is a painful punishment.
interpretation: God commands the believers to avoid using the expression 'Ra'ina,' which the Jews of Medina were misusing as a play on words to insult the Prophet Muhammad, as it carried an offensive double meaning in their language. Instead, He instructs the believers to use the word 'Unzurna,' which conveys the same request for attention without ambiguity, thereby emphasizing that the tongue should be guarded against any speech that could be distorted or perceived as disrespectful toward the Messenger.

translation: Neither those who disbelieve among the People of the Scripture nor the polytheists wish that any good should be sent down to you from your Lord. But Allah selects for His mercy whom He wills, and Allah is the possessor of great bounty.
interpretation: This verse reveals the intensity of the envy and malice harbored by the disbelievers and polytheists toward the believers; they are deeply distressed by the revelation of the Qur'an and the divine blessings bestowed upon the Prophet and his followers because they wish to see no favor or guidance reach the Muslim community. Allah consoles the believers by clarifying that prophethood and divine revelation are matters of His absolute sovereign decree and wisdom, which He bestows upon whom He chooses; therefore, the believers should not be deterred by the hostility of those who fail to recognize that Allah’s grace is limitless and cannot be contained or restricted by the resentful desires of the disbelievers.

translation: We do not abrogate a verse or cause it to be forgotten except that We bring forth [one] better than it or similar to it. Do you not know that Allah is over all things competent?
interpretation: This verse establishes the principle of divine abrogation in legislation, explaining that when Allah replaces a previous ruling with a new one, it is always done out of perfect wisdom to benefit humanity, either by providing a ruling that is more suited to the changing circumstances of the believers, easier for them to follow, or one that maintains the same spiritual benefit, thereby demonstrating His absolute power to regulate the affairs of His creation as He deems best.

translation: Do you not know that to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth? And you have not besides Allah any protector or any helper.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine reminder of Allah's absolute sovereignty and exclusive authority over all existence, intended to detach the believer's heart from seeking aid or validation from created beings, emphasizing that since He alone possesses the power to command the universe, He is the only One whose guardianship provides true security and whose assistance is effective against any adversity.

translation: Or do you intend to ask your Messenger as Moses was asked before? And whoever exchanges faith for disbelief has certainly strayed from the soundness of the way.
interpretation: The verse serves as a stern admonition to the believers against the excessive and insolent questioning of their Prophet, drawing a parallel to the Israelites who persistently demanded miracles and made impossible requests of Moses. It warns that such an attitude, rooted in doubt rather than a sincere quest for guidance, represents a dangerous spiritual exchange—trading the certainty of faith for the confusion of disbelief—thereby causing the individual to lose their path to salvation.

translation: Many of the People of the Scripture wish they could turn you back to disbelief after you have believed, out of envy from themselves even after the truth has become clear to them. So pardon and overlook until Allah delivers His command. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine warning to the believers regarding the deep-seated psychological hostility held by certain segments of the People of the Scripture. It explains that their desire to see the believers revert to disbelief does not stem from a genuine search for truth, but rather from internal jealousy and resentment because the believers embraced the faith that they themselves recognized as valid. By instructing the believers to 'pardon and overlook,' God is establishing a strategy of patience and moral superiority, advising them not to engage in reciprocal hostility but to remain steadfast in their conduct until God manifests His decree, reminding the faithful that divine power ultimately supersedes the schemes of any opposing group.

translation: And establish prayer and give zakah, and whatever good you put forward for yourselves - you will find it with Allah. Indeed, Allah, of what you do, is Seeing.
interpretation: The verse serves as a divine reminder that the acts of worship and charity performed by a believer are not lost, but rather serve as a spiritual investment. By establishing prayer, one maintains a direct connection with the Creator, and by paying zakah, one purifies their wealth and fosters compassion within the community; these deeds act as a repository stored in the presence of Allah, which will be fully manifest and rewarded on the Day of Judgment, as nothing a person does escapes His absolute and watchful vision.

translation: And they say, 'None will enter Paradise except one who is a Jew or a Christian.' That is [merely] their wishful thinking, Say, 'Produce your proof, if you should be truthful.'
