It teaches that a believer's heart must reach a state of complete contentment and inner peace with the Prophet's rulings, without any residual resistance or resentment, reflecting a total surrender to Divine guidance.

translation: And in that case, We would have given them from Our presence a great reward.
interpretation: This verse underscores the infinite generosity of Allah, suggesting that had those who were commanded to sacrifice their lives or properties actually obeyed, Allah would have bestowed upon them a recompense of immense value, originating directly from His divine presence, which surpasses any worldly gain in both quality and eternal duration.

translation: And We would have guided them to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse signifies that if those who were commanded to obey the messenger had actually submitted and acted upon the divine guidance provided to them, Allah would have granted them the grace and success of remaining firm on the path of truth that leads directly to His pleasure and paradise.

translation: And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger - those will be with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favor of the prophets, the steadfast affirmers of truth, the martyrs and the righteous. And excellent are those as companions.
interpretation: This verse establishes that true companionship in the afterlife is determined by one's allegiance to Divine guidance; those who align their will with Allah and follow the Prophet are granted a spiritual elevation that elevates them to the company of the highest souls, signifying that moral and spiritual alignment in this world directly determines the quality of one's eternal environment.

translation: That is the bounty from Allah, and sufficient is Allah as All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the blessings, wisdom, and status granted to the believers are not earned through their own power alone, but are a manifestation of Allah's grace and divine favor; since He is All-Knowing, He bestows this bounty upon those whom He knows to be deserving of it according to His perfect wisdom and comprehensive knowledge.

translation: O you who have believed, take your precaution and either go forth in small groups or go forth all together.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine directive for the believers to be vigilant and strategically prepared against potential adversaries, emphasizing that effective defense requires both caution and organized mobilization, whether by deploying forces in smaller, specialized squads or by assembling a unified, collective front, depending on the circumstances and the nature of the threat faced.

translation: And indeed, among you is he who lingers behind; and if disaster strikes you, he says, 'Allah has favored me in that I was not present with them.'
interpretation: This verse describes the mindset of the hypocrites who avoid participating in the struggles of the believers. When they see their brethren facing hardship, trial, or death, they do not view their own absence as a failure of duty or a loss of spiritual reward, but rather as a calculated stroke of good fortune. They falsely attribute their safety to a divine blessing, willfully ignoring that true success and favor from Allah lie in steadfastness, courage, and standing with the truth, rather than in the mere avoidance of worldly harm.

translation: But if bounty comes to you from Allah, he will surely say, as if there had never been between you and him any affection, 'Oh, I wish I had been with them so I could have attained a great attainment.'
interpretation: This verse describes the psychological state of the hypocrites who refrain from participating in the cause of Allah due to cowardice or lack of faith, but once they see the believers achieving victory or gaining spoils, they regret their absence not out of religious devotion, but out of greed and envy, wishing they had shared in the material gains while hiding their previous lack of genuine commitment to the believers' struggle.

translation: Those who believe fight in the cause of Allah, while those who disbelieve fight in the cause of Taghut (idolatry/tyranny). So fight against the allies of Satan. Indeed, the plot of Satan is ever weak.
interpretation: The verse highlights the fundamental divide in human struggle, asserting that the motivation behind the believer's combat is to establish justice and uphold divine truth, whereas the unbeliever's combat is driven by arrogance, injustice, and the worship of anything other than God. By labeling the disbelievers as 'allies of Satan,' the verse frames the conflict as a spiritual struggle between light and darkness, reassuring the believers that despite the outward strength of their adversaries, the influence and schemes of evil are inherently fragile and destined to fail when faced with sincere faith and divine support.

translation: Have you not seen those to whom it was said, 'Restrain your hands [from fighting], establish prayer, and give zakah'? But then, when fighting was ordained for them, at once a party of them feared people as they fear Allah or with [even] greater fear. They said, 'Our Lord, why have You decreed upon us fighting? If only You had postponed [it for] us for a short time.' Say, 'The enjoyment of this world is little, and the Hereafter is better for he who fears Allah. And injustice will not be done to you, [even] as much as a thread [inside a date seed].'
interpretation: This verse addresses the psychological transformation of the believers who were initially eager for jihad when they were weak, but became hesitant and fearful once the command to fight was formally enacted. Allah exposes the hypocrisy of those who prioritized their fear of worldly consequences over their reverence for His command, reminding them that their desire for delay is rooted in an attachment to the fleeting comforts of this life. The verse serves as a profound exhortation to shift one's focus from mortal threats to the eternal reward, emphasizing that obedience to Allah in difficult times is the true path to salvation, and assuring the faithful that perfect divine justice ensures that every deed, no matter how small, will be fully accounted for and rewarded.

translation: Wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you should be within towers of lofty construction. But if good comes to them, they say, 'This is from Allah'; and if evil befalls them, they say, 'This is from you.' Say, 'All is from Allah.' So what is [the matter] with those people that they can hardly understand any statement?
interpretation: The verse clarifies that the decree of death is absolute and unavoidable for every soul, regardless of the precautions taken or the fortification of one's surroundings, as life and death are under the ultimate command of Allah. It further rebukes those who possess a contradictory logic by attributing prosperity to Allah's favor while blaming the Prophet (or the cause of their misfortune) for their trials, affirming that both prosperity and adversity originate from the divine wisdom and decree of Allah, which these individuals fail to comprehend due to their lack of deep reflection.

translation: Whatever of good reaches you, is from Allah, but whatever of evil befalls you, is from yourself. And We have sent you, O Muhammad, as a Messenger to mankind, and Allah is sufficient as a Witness.
interpretation: This verse clarifies that every blessing, success, and favor that a person experiences comes purely from the grace and bounty of Allah, while the calamities, hardships, and sins one encounters are a consequence of one's own shortcomings, wrong choices, and disobedience; therefore, man should attribute all virtue to Allah while taking responsibility for his own failures.

translation: Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah; but whoever turns away - then We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], over them as a guardian.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the Messenger of Allah does not speak from his own desire, but rather conveys the revelation of Allah; therefore, following his guidance is identical to following the commands of Allah. It simultaneously clarifies that the Prophet is a warner and a conveyor of the message, not a controller over human choices, meaning he is not held accountable for the personal actions of those who reject the truth after it has been made clear to them.

translation: And they say, 'Obedience!' but when they leave you, a party of them devises by night something other than what you say. But Allah records what they devise by night. So turn away from them and rely upon Allah. And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning against the hypocrisy of those who profess outward agreement with the Prophet while harboring conflicting intentions in private. It highlights the divine omniscience of Allah, who is fully aware of the secret conspiracies they form when they are away from the Messenger's presence. The directive to 'turn away' instructs the believer to avoid engaging in fruitless confrontation with such insincere individuals, emphasizing that true protection, sufficiency, and the management of outcomes lie solely in trusting Allah, who is the ultimate Guardian and Trustee over all human affairs.

translation: Do they not then reflect on the Qur'an? Had it been from [any] other than Allah, they would have found within it much contradiction.
interpretation: The verse serves as a rational challenge to the authenticity of the Qur'an, positing that its perfect internal consistency, despite being revealed over twenty-three years under varying circumstances and complex life situations, is proof of its divine origin. It suggests that if a work were authored by mere human intellect, its diverse contents would inevitably contain discrepancies or contradictions over time, whereas the Qur'an maintains a unified message, confirming that such flawlessness is only possible for a source that transcends human limitations and encompasses all-encompassing knowledge.

translation: And when there comes to them information about public security or fear, they spread it around. But if they had only referred it back to the Messenger and to those of authority among them, those who are able to think and analyze it would have surely known the truth of the matter. And if not for the favor of Allah upon you and His mercy, you would have followed Satan, except for a few.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning against the dangerous habit of spreading rumors and unverified news, especially regarding matters of national security or social stability. It instructs believers that such sensitive information should not be disseminated carelessly, but rather submitted to the leadership and those with expertise, whose wisdom and insight allow them to discern the facts and determine the appropriate course of action, thereby preventing chaos and protecting the unity of the community from the divisive influence of Satan.

translation: So fight in the cause of Allah; you are not held responsible except for yourself. And encourage the believers [to fight] that perhaps Allah will restrain the [military] might of those who disbelieve. And Allah is stronger in might and stronger in [the ability to] punish.
interpretation: This verse establishes that every individual believer bears the primary burden of fulfilling their duty toward Allah and upholding the truth regardless of the actions or apathy of others; by fulfilling his own obligation and actively exhorting his brethren to righteousness, the believer serves as a catalyst for divine intervention, reminding the faithful that human efforts are but a means, whereas the ultimate power to suppress the aggression of the arrogant and impose divine justice resides solely with the Almighty.

translation: Whoever intercedes for a good cause will have a share in its reward, and whoever intercedes for an evil cause will have a portion of its burden. And Allah is ever, over all things, a Keeper.
interpretation: This verse establishes the principle of moral responsibility for one's influence on others; it asserts that any person who facilitates a righteous act, aids a needy individual, or advocates for justice will share in the spiritual merit earned by that deed. Conversely, those who encourage wrongdoing or assist in harmful actions will bear a portion of the accountability for the resulting harm, as Allah acts as the Ever-Watchful Guardian who sustains, preserves, and records every action and its consequential impact.

translation: And when you are greeted with a greeting, greet with one better than it or return it [in the same manner]. Indeed, Allah is ever, over all things, an Accountant.
interpretation: This verse serves as a fundamental principle for social interaction and moral conduct, instructing Muslims to reciprocate kindness by either exceeding the gesture or at least matching it with equivalent courtesy. It encourages a spirit of generosity, warmth, and mutual respect in community relations, while reminding believers that God keeps a precise account of every action and intent, ultimately rewarding those who demonstrate excellence in their dealings with others.

translation: Allah - there is no deity except Him. He will surely assemble you for the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt. And who is more truthful than Allah in statement?
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine proclamation of the absolute Oneness of Allah, asserting that He is the only One worthy of worship. By linking this declaration to the inevitability of the Day of Resurrection, Allah reminds humanity that their life is purposeful and that they will ultimately be gathered before their Creator to account for their deeds. The rhetorical question at the end emphasizes that Allah's promises are the absolute truth, leaving no room for skepticism regarding the afterlife, as His word is the most authoritative and trustworthy foundation for belief.

translation: Why are you divided into two parties regarding the hypocrites, while Allah has cast them back [into disbelief] for what they earned? Do you wish to guide those whom Allah has led astray? And he whom Allah leaves to stray - never will you find for him a way [of guidance].
interpretation: The verse serves as a stern admonition to the believers, questioning their confusion and division regarding how to treat the hypocrites who had abandoned the community of faith. It clarifies that these individuals have been pushed back into the depths of their own disbelief by Allah as a direct consequence of their own persistent choosing of deceit and treachery. It emphasizes that guidance is a divine prerogative granted to those who sincerely seek the truth, and once a person has fully committed to a path of persistent corruption and rejection of the truth, they have effectively sealed their own fate, making it impossible for any human effort to redirect them toward righteousness.

translation: They wish you would disbelieve as they disbelieved so you would be alike. So do not take from among them allies until they emigrate for the cause of Allah. But if they turn away, then seize them and kill them wherever you find them and take not among them any ally or helper.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to the believers regarding the inherent enmity of hypocrites and those who actively oppose the faith, highlighting that their ultimate desire is not merely disagreement, but the total abandonment of the believer's core convictions to align with their own state of disbelief. The command to withhold alliance and to treat those who reject peace and persist in hostility as combatants is intended to protect the integrity of the Muslim community from subversion and to establish clear boundaries between those who are committed to the path of truth and those who seek to undermine it through deceit and betrayal.

translation: Except for those who join a people between whom and yourselves there is a treaty, or those who come to you, their hearts constrained from fighting you or fighting their own people. And if Allah had willed, He could have given them power over you, and they would have fought you. So if they remove themselves from you and do not fight you and offer you peace, then Allah has not made for you any cause for action against them.
interpretation: This verse establishes a policy of non-aggression and restraint for the Muslim community when dealing with neutral or peace-seeking factions. It clarifies that if an enemy group has entered into a covenant with a third party that is also allied with the Muslims, or if a group chooses neutrality because they are torn by divided loyalties between their kinship and their commitment to peace, the Muslims are obligated to respect their non-combatant status. The verse emphasizes that peace is the preferred outcome and that as long as these groups maintain their neutrality, refrain from hostility, and offer terms of peace, the divine law provides no legal or moral justification for the believers to initiate aggression against them, acknowledging that it is only by Allah's grace that these potential adversaries were not allowed to become active combatants.

translation: You will find others who wish to be secure from you and secure from their own people; every time they are sent back into fitnah (tribulation/disbelief), they fall back into it. So if they do not withdraw from you, offer you peace, and restrain their hands, then seize them and kill them wherever you find them. And it is against them that We have given you a clear authority.
interpretation: This verse addresses a specific group of hypocrites who exhibit double-faced behavior, professing faith to the Muslims while maintaining their allegiance to the disbelievers to protect their own interests. Their return to 'fitnah' whenever an opportunity arises signifies that their apparent conversion is insincere and opportunistic. Therefore, God grants the believers the legal authority to take decisive military action against these individuals—who remain actively treacherous and refuse to commit to peace—to ensure the safety and security of the Muslim community.

translation: It is not for a believer to kill a believer unless by mistake. And whoever kills a believer by mistake, then the freeing of a believing slave and a compensation payment handed over to his family, unless they forgo it as charity. But if he was from a people who are enemies to you and he was a believer, then only the freeing of a believing slave. And if he was from a people with whom you have a treaty, then a compensation payment handed over to his family and the freeing of a believing slave. And whoever does not find the means, then a fast for two consecutive months as repentance from Allah. And Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse establishes the sanctity of a believer's life in Islam by unequivocally forbidding intentional homicide, while legislating strict legal and spiritual consequences for accidental killing. The ruling serves as a moral deterrent and a restorative justice mechanism: the financial compensation (Diyah) provides support to the victim's grieving family, the emancipation of a slave acts as a social contribution to rectify the loss of a life, and the mandatory fasting serves as a path for the perpetrator to seek genuine divine forgiveness. By categorizing the victim based on their political affiliation with the Muslim community, the verse balances individual justice with communal security, emphasizing that even in the case of an error, the perpetrator must perform a multi-faceted act of expiation to purify their soul and uphold the sanctity of faith.

translation: But whoever kills a believer intentionally - his recompense is Hell, wherein he will abide eternally, and Allah has become angry with him and has cursed him and has prepared for him a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse establishes the extreme gravity of taking an innocent human life, specifically that of a believer, by highlighting that the act is so heinous that it incurs the ultimate divine wrath. The severity of the stated recompense serves as a profound deterrent against shedding blood, emphasizing that such a transgression destroys the sanctity of life that God has ordained, thereby severing the perpetrator's spiritual connection to mercy and inviting a state of permanent estrangement from God's grace.

translation: O you who have believed, when you go forth in the cause of Allah, investigate; and do not say to one who gives you [a greeting of] peace, 'You are not a believer,' aspiring for the goods of worldly life; for with Allah are many spoils. You yourselves were like that before; then Allah conferred His favor upon you, so investigate. Indeed, Allah is ever, with what you do, Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine command for Muslims to exercise caution and avoid hasty judgments during times of conflict, specifically warning against accusing others of disbelief simply to seize their worldly possessions or justify aggression. It reminds the believers that they were once in a state of weakness or ignorance before Allah guided them, and therefore, they should show empathy and discernment, ensuring that the evidence for someone's faith or lack thereof is verified through careful investigation rather than driven by material greed.

translation: Not equal are those believers who sit at home—except those who have a disabling injury—and those who strive in the cause of Allah with their wealth and their lives. Allah has preferred those who strive with their wealth and their lives over those who sit at home, by a degree; and to each Allah has promised the best outcome. But Allah has distinguished the strivers over those who sit at home with a great reward.
interpretation: This verse establishes a clear hierarchy of merit within the community of believers based on their commitment to the faith. While all true believers are promised a virtuous outcome for their belief, those who actively sacrifice their wealth and physical safety to uphold and spread the message of Allah hold a higher station in His sight than those who remain passive and refrain from participation, unless they are genuinely prevented by physical infirmity. The distinction is made to emphasize that spiritual progress is not merely internal, but must be demonstrated through tangible commitment and action, as those who exhaust their resources and lives for the sake of divine justice earn a significantly greater spiritual recompense.

translation: [High] degrees from Him and forgiveness and mercy. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah elevates the ranks of those who strive for His sake and adhere to His guidance, granting them a position of honor and proximity, alongside the washing away of their past sins through His forgiveness and the bestowing of His grace through His mercy, highlighting that these divine attributes are constant and inherent to His nature, providing unending hope for those who repent and seek His bounty.

translation: Indeed, those whom the angels take [in death] while they were wronging themselves, [the angels] will ask, 'In what condition were you?' They will reply, 'We were oppressed in the land.' [The angels] will say, 'Was not the earth of Allah spacious [enough] for you to emigrate therein?' For those, their refuge is Hell – and evil it is as a destination.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning against compromising one's faith or moral integrity under the pretext of societal pressure or worldly circumstances. It emphasizes that individuals hold personal responsibility for their religious practice, and 'being oppressed' is not a valid excuse to remain in an environment where one cannot fulfill their obligations to Allah when the option to relocate to a place of greater freedom and righteousness exists. The failure to prioritize one's faith over temporary comfort or fear of persecution ultimately leads to a dire spiritual consequence.

translation: Except for the oppressed among men, women, and children who cannot devise a plan nor are they guided to a way.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine exemption for those who are physically, socially, or financially incapacitated to the point where they cannot emigrate for the sake of their faith or escape persecution. It highlights that Allah does not hold individuals accountable for their inability to act when they lack the means, resources, or knowledge of a safe path to change their circumstances, thereby emphasizing the divine principle that responsibilities are commensurate with one's capacity.

translation: For those, it is expected that Allah will pardon them, and Allah is ever Pardoning, Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse serves as a source of immense hope for believers who may have stumbled in their faith or committed errors, indicating that Allah's mercy is expansive enough to encompass those who possess a genuine inclination toward repentance and humility, suggesting that while one should never take Allah's forgiveness for granted, the divine nature of being 'The Pardoner' and 'The Forgiver' is always ready to embrace those who turn back to Him with sincerity.

translation: And when you travel throughout the land, there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer, if you fear that those who disbelieve may disrupt [or attack] you. Indeed, the disbelievers are ever to you a clear enemy.
interpretation: The verse grants a concession to travelers to shorten their obligatory prayers as a measure of ease, specifically linking this permission to the state of fear or danger from potential enemy hostilities, thereby emphasizing that while the traveler is generally vulnerable, the mandate to pray remains, adjusted to the reality of physical security concerns in a hostile environment.

translation: And when you are among them and lead them in prayer, let a group of them stand with you and let them take their weapons. Then, when they have prostrated, let them be behind you and let the other group who have not yet prayed come and pray with you, taking their precautions and their weapons. Those who disbelieve wish that you would neglect your weapons and your baggage so they could swoop down upon you in a single attack. And there is no blame upon you if you are troubled by rain or are ill that you put down your weapons, but take your precautions. Indeed, Allah has prepared a humiliating punishment for the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse establishes the 'Prayer of Fear' (Salat al-Khawf), demonstrating that the obligation of communal prayer is so vital that it is not dropped even in the heat of battle; rather, the Sharia provides a flexible methodology to ensure that the remembrance of Allah and the protection of the community are maintained simultaneously, emphasizing that physical alertness must never be compromised by the enemy who seeks to exploit any momentary lapse in defensive readiness.

translation: And when you have completed the prayer, remember Allah standing, sitting, and [lying] on your sides; but when you become secure, re-establish [regular] prayer. Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers a decree of specified times.
interpretation: The verse commands believers to maintain a state of constant mindfulness and dhikr (remembrance) of Allah in every posture and condition of life, emphasizing that the cessation of the formal prayer ritual does not signal a cessation of spiritual connection; it further clarifies that the formal prayers are a mandatory obligation tied to fixed, prescribed times that must be observed faithfully once safety and stability are restored.

translation: And do not weaken in the pursuit of the enemy. If you should be suffering, then they are suffering as you are suffering, but you expect from Allah that which they do not expect. And Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse serves as a source of psychological and spiritual fortitude for the believers, teaching them that suffering in the path of truth is a shared experience between the righteous and their opponents, yet the believers possess a superior advantage: the hope for divine reward and eternal mercy. It encourages endurance by emphasizing that the pain of the struggle is not unique to the faithful, but the ultimate outcome is exclusively in their favor due to their connection with Allah, while the opposition lacks any such transcendent hope, making the believers' resilience both rational and divinely supported.

translation: Indeed, We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], the Book in truth so you may judge between the people by that which Allah has shown you. And do not be an advocate for the deceitful.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine directive to the Prophet Muhammad, emphasizing that the authority to judge must be rooted solely in the revelation provided by Allah, which is absolute truth. It functions as a firm warning against bias or leniency toward those who act with treachery or dishonesty, establishing that justice must be impartial and unaffected by any external pressure or personal inclination to defend the wrongdoer.

translation: And ask forgiveness of Allah. Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: This verse serves as a direct command from Allah to the Prophet, and by extension to all believers, to continuously seek His pardon for any shortcomings or sins. It highlights the inherent nature of Allah's attributes, assuring the seeker that His infinite capacity to forgive and His boundless mercy are always present for those who turn to Him with sincerity, thereby providing a source of hope and spiritual restoration.

translation: And do not argue on behalf of those who deceive themselves. Indeed, Allah does not like those who are treacherous and sinful.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine prohibition against defending or advocating for individuals who engage in acts of betrayal, dishonesty, or injustice. Because such people ultimately harm their own souls by incurring the wrath of God, the believer is commanded to distance themselves from such behavior and not to use their influence or speech to shield the guilty from accountability or justice, as Allah disapproves of those who habitually commit treachery and persist in sin.

translation: They hide from the people, but they cannot hide from Allah, for He is with them when they plot by night in speech of which He does not approve; and Allah is ever encompassing of what they do.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning against hypocrisy, highlighting the foolishness of those who prioritize appearances before society over their relationship with the Divine. It underscores that while a person might successfully conceal their sins, malice, or dishonest intentions from human beings through deception or secrecy, they remain entirely exposed before the Creator. Allah’s omnipresence means that He is witness to every hidden thought and private deliberation, even those conducted in the darkness of night; therefore, true accountability lies in recognizing that one's internal reality is as visible to God as one's external actions, and nothing can escape His comprehensive knowledge.

translation: Here you are, arguing on their behalf in this worldly life; but who will argue with Allah on their behalf on the Day of Resurrection, or who will be their guardian?
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning against those who defend the treacherous or those who hide the truth to protect the guilty. It highlights the ultimate futility of human intercession on the Day of Judgment, emphasizing that while people may successfully deceive or manipulate earthly judicial systems, no advocate will have the power, standing, or authority to challenge the absolute justice of Allah when He renders His final, infallible verdict.

translation: And whoever does a wrong or wrongs himself but then seeks forgiveness of Allah will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine promise highlighting the infinite mercy of Allah; it assures the believer that no sin, whether it is a transgression against others or an act of self-harm through disobedience, is beyond the reach of divine pardon provided the individual turns to God in sincere repentance, thereby emphasizing that God's grace always surpasses His punishment for those who humbly acknowledge their faults.

translation: And whoever commits a sin, he only earns it against himself; and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse establishes the principle of individual moral responsibility, emphasizing that the burden of wrongdoing falls solely upon the transgressor rather than affecting the sanctity or divine decree of Allah; furthermore, it highlights that Allah's perfect knowledge and infinite wisdom ensure that every action is accounted for justly, as His governance is rooted in a balance between His awareness of all deeds and His precise, purposeful management of creation.

translation: And whoever commits a fault or a sin and then blames it on an innocent person, he has taken upon himself a slander and a manifest sin.
interpretation: This verse establishes a severe moral and legal warning against the act of scapegoating or false accusation. It emphasizes that shifting the burden of one's own transgressions onto the innocent is a compounded offense: it involves the original act of wrongdoing, the corruption of truth through lying, and the grave injustice of harming an blameless individual, all of which constitute a clear and inexcusable sin before God.

translation: And if it were not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, a group of them would have determined to mislead you. But they do not mislead except themselves, and they will not harm you at all. And Allah has revealed to you the Book and wisdom and has taught you that which you did not know. And ever has the favor of Allah upon you been great.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet's infallibility and immunity from the plots of the hypocrites are entirely due to Allah's divine protection and constant guidance. By revealing the Qur'an and the Sunnah, Allah granted the Prophet a comprehensive source of divine knowledge and discernment that shielded him from being deceived by those who sought to distort the truth or lead him into error, proving that any attempt to undermine the Prophet's mission would ultimately backfire only upon the perpetrators themselves.

translation: No good is in most of their private conversation, except for he who enjoins charity or that which is right or conciliation between people. And whoever does that seeking means to the pleasure of Allah - then We are going to give him a great reward.
interpretation: This verse indicates that private consultations among people are generally devoid of benefit, as they often involve sinful speech, vanity, or worldly schemes. However, it establishes an exception for speech that serves a higher moral purpose: encouraging charity, promoting righteousness, or reconciling parties in conflict. The verse emphasizes that these actions only attain divine value when they are performed with the sincere intention of seeking Allah's pleasure, thereby transforming everyday social interactions into acts of profound worship that merit a magnificent eternal reward.

translation: And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows other than the way of the believers - We will give him what he has taken and drive him into Hell, and evil it is as a destination.
interpretation: This verse warns that anyone who deliberately abandons the path of the Prophet and the consensus of the early believers, having already recognized the truth of the guidance, will be left to follow their own misguided choices. God will allow them to continue on the corrupt path they have chosen for themselves, ultimately leading them to a state of total abandonment by divine grace, which results in their ruin in Hellfire.

translation: Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. And he who associates others with Allah has certainly gone far astray.
interpretation: This verse establishes the absolute gravity of shirk (polytheism or associating partners with Allah) as the only unforgivable sin if a person dies in that state without having repented, because it constitutes a direct denial of the fundamental truth of Allah's oneness; however, for all other sins, Allah retains the sovereign right to grant His mercy and forgiveness to whomsoever He chooses, underscoring that while repentance is the key to salvation, the ultimate scope of divine forgiveness is boundless for those who remain within the fold of monotheistic belief.

translation: They call upon instead of Him none but female deities, and they [actually] call upon none but a rebellious Satan.
interpretation: The polytheists rely upon idols that lack power, life, and benefit, which they designate with feminine names, yet in reality, by worshiping these inanimate objects, they are following the whispers and the path of the rebellious Satan who has distanced himself from all good and diverted them into the depths of disbelief and arrogance against their Creator.

translation: Whom Allah has cursed. And he had said, 'I will surely take from among Your servants a specific portion.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the intense enmity of Iblis toward humanity, illustrating his vow to lead a determined segment of Allah's servants astray by employing various temptations and deceptions, thereby drawing them away from the path of obedience and into the realm of disobedience and disbelief.

translation: And I will surely mislead them, and I will surely arouse in them [sinful] desires, and I will command them so they will slit the ears of cattle, and I will command them so they will change the creation of Allah. And whoever takes Satan as an ally instead of Allah has certainly sustained a clear loss.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the manipulative tactics of Satan, who seeks to lead humanity astray by decorating falsehood as truth and inciting them to commit acts of corruption against their natural disposition and Divine Law, such as engaging in superstitious rituals and altering the God-given nature of things; ultimately, following his path results in a profound and irreparable spiritual bankruptcy, as the individual forfeits their connection to the Creator in exchange for fleeting illusions.

translation: He promises them and arouses desire in them, but Satan does not promise them except delusion.
interpretation: The verse highlights the deceptive nature of Satan, who employs false promises and empty hopes to lure humans away from the path of righteousness, convincing them that worldly pleasures and sinful actions will lead to security or benefit, when in reality, these promises are mere illusions designed to lead the soul toward its own ultimate ruin.

translation: Those—their refuge is Hell, and they will find no escape from it.
interpretation: This verse signifies that those who have willfully chosen the path of disbelief and rebellion against Allah’s guidance will ultimately face a state of permanent confinement, as the doors of divine mercy and escape from the consequences of their actions will be eternally closed to them, leaving them with no means of redemption or exit.

translation: It is not your desires, nor the desires of the People of the Scripture, that matter; whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, and he will not find for himself besides Allah any protector or helper.
interpretation: The verse clarifies that salvation and divine favor are not attained through mere wishful thinking or unfounded claims of superiority, but rather through sincere faith coupled with righteous deeds, as Allah’s system of justice is objective and applies to all people equally regardless of their self-proclaimed status.

translation: And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while being a believer - those will enter Paradise and will not be wronged, [even as much as] the speck on a date seed.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine assurance of absolute justice in the afterlife, emphasizing that faith is the indispensable foundation for deeds to be accepted by God. By explicitly mentioning both genders, the Qur'an dismantles any notion of spiritual superiority based on sex, establishing that the criteria for salvation are universal—namely, the sincerity of belief coupled with virtuous conduct. The metaphor of the 'naqir'—the tiny speck on the back of a date stone—illustrates that God's justice is so precise and meticulous that not a single atom's weight of an individual's struggle or good deed will be overlooked or diminished, ensuring that every soul receives the full recompense it has earned.

translation: And who is better in religion than one who submits his face to Allah while being a doer of good and follows the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth? And Allah took Abraham as an intimate friend.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the highest form of spiritual perfection and the ideal religious state is attained through the synthesis of two fundamental elements: complete sincerity in submission to Allah (Islam), which focuses on the heart's devotion, and the manifestation of this sincerity through righteous deeds (Ihsan). By invoking Abraham as the archetype of this path, the verse highlights that such a state is achieved by turning away from all false ideologies toward pure monotheism, a dedication so profound that it earns the believer a unique, intimate spiritual closeness with the Divine, as evidenced by Allah's selection of Abraham as His chosen confidant (Khalil).

translation: And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And ever is Allah, of all things, encompassing.
interpretation: This verse affirms the absolute sovereignty of Allah over all creation, emphasizing that everything in existence, both in the heavens and on earth, is His property, subject to His command, and under His total control; furthermore, it highlights His divine attribute of encompassing knowledge and power, meaning that nothing escapes His awareness, and His grasp extends over all things simultaneously, leaving no possibility for anything to exist or act outside of His comprehensive oversight.

translation: And they request from you a [legal] ruling concerning women. Say, 'Allah gives you a ruling about them and [about] what has been recited to you in the Book concerning the orphan girls to whom you do not give what was ordained for them while you desire to marry them and [concerning] the oppressed among children and that you maintain for orphans [their rights] in justice.' And whatever you do of good - indeed, Allah is ever Knowing of it.
interpretation: The verse serves as a divine correction regarding the treatment of marginalized groups in society, specifically orphan women and young children. It emphasizes that believers must uphold the rights and dowries of these women rather than exploiting their vulnerable status for personal gain or marriage, and it commands justice for those who lack power, reminding the community that every act of righteousness performed in their favor is fully witnessed and accounted for by Allah.

translation: And if a woman fears from her husband contempt or evasion, there is no sin upon them if they make terms of settlement between them; and settlement is best. And greed has been brought to the souls. But if you do good and fear Allah - indeed Allah is ever, with what you do, Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse establishes that when a marital relationship experiences discord or a husband begins to neglect his duties, the couple is encouraged to prioritize reconciliation and mutual compromise over separation. It acknowledges the inherent human tendency toward selfishness and possessiveness—which often hinders forgiveness—and emphasizes that acting with righteousness and mindfulness of God’s omnipresence is the true path to preserving the bond, as God is fully aware of both the hidden intentions of the heart and the outward actions taken to resolve the dispute.

translation: And you will never be able to be equal between wives, even if you should strive [to do so]. So do not incline completely [toward one] and leave another hanging. And if you amend [your affairs] and fear Allah - then indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse establishes that while complete emotional and internal impartiality between multiple wives is beyond human capacity, a husband is divinely commanded to maintain external fairness and justice in his treatment of them. It serves as a stern warning against neglecting one spouse to the point where she exists in a state of uncertainty, neither fully married nor divorced, while simultaneously offering hope that God will overlook the involuntary human shortcomings of the heart if the individual strives to maintain piety and corrective action in their conduct.

translation: But if they separate [by divorce], Allah will enrich each [of them] from His abundance. And ever is Allah Encompassing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine reassurance for both spouses that divorce is not the end of their sustenance or well-being; rather, Allah promises to provide for each individual independently through His infinite grace, encouraging them to move forward with the trust that His wisdom dictates the best outcome for their circumstances, even when a marriage must come to an end.

translation: And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And We have instructed those who were given the Scripture before you and yourselves to have taqwa of Allah. But if you disbelieve - then to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And ever is Allah Free of need and Praiseworthy.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty of Allah over all creation, asserting that His ownership of the heavens and the earth is constant regardless of human belief or rejection. By highlighting the continuity of the command to fear Allah from the previous scriptures to the present message, it underscores the universal nature of this moral obligation. Ultimately, it reveals that human disbelief does not diminish Allah’s majesty or status, for He is entirely self-sufficient, requiring no creation to serve Him, yet He remains inherently worthy of all praise due to His divine perfection.

translation: And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse establishes the absolute sovereignty of Allah over all creation, affirming that everything in the heavens and the earth is His possession, subject to His authority and management. By declaring that Allah is sufficient as a Wakil (Disposer of affairs), the verse invites the believer to relinquish reliance on worldly causes and place their absolute trust in His perfect wisdom and protective care, knowing that He oversees the interests of His servants with complete sufficiency.

translation: If He wills, He can do away with you, O mankind, and bring others in your place. And Allah is ever competent to do that.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern reminder of Allah's absolute sovereignty and His independence from His creation, emphasizing that humanity holds no special status that would prevent God from replacing them with a different, more obedient, or different creation should they fail to fulfill their purpose; it highlights that human existence is entirely dependent on His will, and He possesses the infinite power to bring about a new order without being diminished or hindered by the absence of those who previously existed.

translation: Whoever desires the reward of this world - then with Allah is the reward of this world and the Hereafter. And ever is Allah Hearing and Seeing.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder to the believer that all worldly gains and spiritual recompense ultimately reside with Allah, urging the individual to elevate their aspirations toward the eternal life rather than focusing solely on fleeting earthly benefits, while affirming that Allah is fully aware of every hidden desire and intention held within the hearts of His servants.

translation: O you who have believed, believe in Allah and His Messenger and the Book that He sent down upon His Messenger and the Scripture which He sent down before. And whoever disbelieves in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day has certainly gone far astray.
interpretation: This verse calls upon those who have already entered the fold of faith to demonstrate the perfection and sincerity of that faith by deeply internalizing the foundational pillars of belief, emphasizing that true guidance requires an unwavering, comprehensive acceptance of all of Allah's revelations and messengers; it serves as a stern warning that to reject any part of this integrated system of divine belief is to sever one's connection to the truth, leading the soul into a state of profound and distant misguidance where the path of salvation is entirely lost.

translation: Indeed, those who have believed then disbelieved, then believed, then disbelieved, and then increased in disbelief - never will Allah forgive them, nor will He guide them to a way.
interpretation: This verse addresses those who continuously fluctuate between faith and disbelief, repeatedly engaging in acts that negate their faith until their hearts become hardened and deeply entrenched in denial. Their persistent choice to return to disbelief after clear guidance indicates a willful rejection of truth that makes them ineligible for Divine forgiveness and guidance, as they have exhausted their opportunities for repentance through their own obstinate refusal to remain committed to the path of righteousness.

translation: Give tidings to the hypocrites that there is for them a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning from Allah to those who outwardly profess faith while concealing disbelief in their hearts, emphasizing that their duplicity will lead to a severe and agonizing consequence, as they are not merely mistaken but are actively deceptive and treacherous in their rejection of the truth.

translation: Those who take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. Do they seek with them honor? But indeed, all honor belongs to Allah.
interpretation: This verse addresses those who seek worldly power, protection, or prestige by aligning themselves with those who reject faith, foolishly believing that such alliances will grant them strength or status. The verse serves as a reminder that true honor, sovereignty, and authority are derived solely from Allah, and that turning away from the believers to seek favor with others is a futile endeavor that ultimately leads to spiritual humiliation, as worldly alliances are transient and lack the backing of divine support.

translation: And it has already been revealed to you in the Book that when you hear the verses of Allah being denied and mocked, do not sit with them until they engage in another conversation. Indeed, if you were to do so, you would be like them. Indeed, Allah will gather the hypocrites and the disbelievers in Hell all together.
interpretation: This verse establishes a moral imperative for believers to dissociate themselves from environments where God's truth is treated with ridicule or blasphemy, emphasizing that maintaining company with those who persist in such mockery makes one morally complicit in their wrongdoing, as true faith requires active disapproval of falsehood rather than passive or complicit presence.

translation: Those who wait and watch about you - then if there comes to you a victory from Allah, they say, 'Were we not with you?' But if the disbelievers have a success, they say [to them], 'Did we not gain the advantage over you, but we protected you from the believers?' Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection, and never will Allah give the disbelievers a way [to overcome] the believers.
interpretation: This verse addresses the hypocrites who fluctuate their loyalties based on the shifting outcomes of battles, hoping to secure worldly gains regardless of who prevails. The final assurance signifies that although the disbelievers may temporarily gain an upper hand in worldly affairs, they hold no spiritual or ultimate authority over the believers, and their perceived power will be completely nullified by divine justice on the Day of Judgment.

translation: Indeed, the hypocrites seek to deceive Allah, but He is deceiving them. And when they stand for prayer, they stand lazily, showing [themselves to] the people and not remembering Allah except a little.
interpretation: The verse highlights the fundamental lack of sincerity in the hearts of the hypocrites; because they do not truly believe in Allah or His omniscience, they attempt to conceal their disbelief under a veneer of outward worship, yet their lethargy and performative behavior during prayer expose their spiritual hypocrisy and the absence of a genuine connection with the Creator.

translation: They are wavering between that, neither belonging to the believers nor to the disbelievers, and whoever Allah leaves to stray, you will never find a way for him to the truth.
interpretation: This verse describes the state of the hypocrites who lack a firm identity or sincere conviction; they are caught in a state of perpetual vacillation, unable to commit to the path of faith because of their inner dishonesty, nor able to fully align with the disbelievers in a way that provides them stability, and because their hearts are sealed due to their persistent rejection of guidance, they have forfeited the capacity to find the right path, as guidance is a favor from Allah that is not bestowed upon those who have chosen deception.

translation: O you who have believed, do not take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. Do you wish to give Allah against yourselves a clear case?
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine prohibition against forming alliances or seeking political and spiritual protection from those who reject the faith, as such associations undermine the internal cohesion of the Muslim community and signify a lack of trust in God; by doing so, the believers provide a valid argument or proof for their own accountability and punishment, as they would be consciously acting against the clear guidance and warnings provided by their Creator.

translation: Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire - and never will you find for them a helper.
interpretation: The verse illustrates the severity of the punishment for those who outwardly profess faith while harboring disbelief and deceit within their hearts, emphasizing that because their hypocrisy is more dangerous to the community than open hostility, they are destined for the most agonizing and isolated level of Hell, cut off from any intercession or aid.

translation: Except for those who repent, correct themselves, hold fast to Allah, and are sincere in their religion for Allah; for those will be with the believers. And Allah is going to give the believers a great reward.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the path to salvation and inclusion among the righteous is not barred by past failings, provided one undergoes a genuine transformation: by abandoning disobedience, amending one's deeds through righteousness, grounding one's reliance entirely in Allah, and purifying one's intentions so that every act of worship is performed solely for His sake. By embodying these qualities, a person is granted the status and companionship of the true believers, ultimately earning the immense, eternal reward that Allah has reserved for those who remained steadfast in their faith and devotion.

translation: What would Allah gain if He punished you, if you were grateful and believed? And Allah is Ever Appreciative, All-Knowing.
interpretation: Allah indicates that He does not derive any benefit from punishing His servants, nor does He take pleasure in their suffering; rather, He desires for them to attain salvation through gratitude for His blessings and sincere faith in His oneness, as His nature is to reward those who act with gratitude and to possess complete knowledge of the sincerity residing in their hearts.

translation: Allah does not like the public mention of evil except by one who has been wronged. And ever is Allah Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse establishes that while Allah discourages backbiting, slander, and foul speech, He grants a legal and moral concession to the oppressed to speak out against the injustice they have suffered. It serves as a validation that one who has been treated unfairly is permitted to name their oppressor and describe the harm done to them in order to seek justice or defense, while acknowledging that Allah is perfectly aware of both the grievance of the victim and the transgression of the wrongdoer.

translation: Whether you reveal a good deed or conceal it or pardon an evil, indeed, Allah is ever Pardoning and Competent.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to adopt a character of excellence and forgiveness, assuring them that Allah is fully aware of both their public and private acts of goodness. By emphasizing that Allah is both 'Al-Afuww' (The Pardoner) and 'Qadeer' (The All-Powerful), the verse teaches that true strength lies not in seeking vengeance, but in exercising the power to forgive. It serves as a reminder that since Allah—despite His absolute authority and power—chooses to pardon His servants, those who emulate this divine attribute by forgiving others will find that their mercy is recognized and valued by Him.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers and wish to discriminate between Allah and His messengers and say, 'We believe in some and disbelieve in others,' and wish to adopt a way in between -
interpretation: This verse censures those who attempt to separate their devotion to Allah from obedience to His messengers, as well as those who selectively accept parts of divine revelation while rejecting others based on their personal desires, clarifying that such an approach is a path of hypocrisy and disbelief, as true faith requires total submission to Allah and the acceptance of all whom He has commissioned as His messengers without division.

translation: Those are the disbelievers truly, and We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse establishes that those who engage in selective belief—accepting parts of divine revelation while rejecting others—are categorized by Allah as true disbelievers, not because they lack knowledge of God, but because they have demonstrated an arrogant rejection of His authority by setting their own criteria for what to follow, and consequently, they face a punishment that matches their pride with profound humiliation.

translation: And those who believe in Allah and His messengers and do not make distinction between any of them - to them He will give their rewards. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true faith requires the absolute acceptance of all prophets sent by Allah without exception or prejudice, acknowledging the unity of the divine message; by embracing this comprehensive belief, the faithful prove their sincerity, which earns them divine compensation, while Allah's attributes of forgiveness and mercy ensure that He overlooks their previous shortcomings and grants them grace beyond their deeds.

translation: The People of the Scripture ask you to bring down to them a book from the heaven. But they had asked Moses for even greater than that, for they said, 'Show us Allah outright,' so the thunderbolt struck them for their wrongdoing. Then they took the calf [for worship] after the clear signs had come to them, but We pardoned that. And We gave Moses a clear authority.
interpretation: This verse serves to console the Prophet Muhammad by highlighting the historical stubbornness of the People of the Scripture; just as they demanded miracles and physical manifestations from Moses—such as seeing God directly—they now demand the same from him. By recalling how they persisted in their disbelief by worshipping the calf even after witnessing undeniable proofs and receiving divine mercy, the verse demonstrates that their demands are not born of a sincere desire for guidance, but are rather a manifestation of the same arrogant defiance that characterized their ancestors.

translation: And We raised over them the mount [Sinai] for [the acceptance of] their covenant and said to them, 'Enter the gate bowing humbly,' and We said to them, 'Do not transgress on the sabbath,' and We took from them a solemn covenant.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine reminder of the immense weight of the obligations placed upon the Children of Israel. By physically elevating Mount Sinai over them, Allah manifested His absolute power and majesty, compelling them to acknowledge the gravity of the covenant they had entered into. The command to enter the gate bowing is an instruction to demonstrate profound humility and total submission to the will of the Creator upon entering the holy site. Furthermore, the explicit prohibition against transgressing the sanctity of the Sabbath—a day specifically set aside for worship and reflection—highlighted the test of their obedience. The 'solemn covenant' emphasizes that these were not mere suggestions but binding, sacred commitments that required steadfast adherence, reflecting the profound seriousness of the relationship between God and His people.

translation: So for their breaking of the covenant, and their disbelief in the signs of Allah, and their killing of the prophets without right, and their saying, 'Our hearts are wrapped,' nay, Allah has set a seal upon them because of their disbelief, so they believe not, except a few.
interpretation: The verse explains that the spiritual blindness and hardness of heart experienced by the Children of Israel were not innate or arbitrary, but rather the direct consequence of their persistent rebellion; by repeatedly violating sacred covenants, rejecting divine guidance, and committing grave injustices, they allowed their own souls to become encased in disbelief until they reached a state where they were no longer receptive to the truth.

translation: And for their disbelief and their speaking against Mary a grave falsehood.
interpretation: This verse highlights the intensity of the transgressions committed by the people of the Book, specifically pointing to the heinous and baseless slander they directed against Mary, the mother of Jesus, thereby rejecting the truth and engaging in severe moral corruption by defaming a woman whom God had chosen and purified.

translation: And [for] their saying, 'Indeed, we have killed the Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary, the messenger of Allah.' And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him; but [another] was made to resemble him to them. And indeed, those who differ over it are in doubt about it. They have no knowledge of it except the following of assumption. And they did not kill him, for certain.
interpretation: This verse clarifies that the narrative of the Jews regarding the killing and crucifixion of Jesus is a falsehood rooted in conjecture, as Allah raised Jesus unto Himself to save him from their plot, causing someone else who resembled him to be taken and crucified in his place, leaving those who claim his death in a state of uncertainty and ignorance.

translation: Rather, Allah raised him to Himself. And ever is Allah Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah physically and spiritually elevated the Prophet Isa (Jesus) to His presence, saving him from the crucifixion intended by his enemies; this act of elevation serves as a manifestation of Allah's sovereign power and His divine wisdom in preserving His messenger to fulfill a purpose known only to Him.

translation: And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death. And on the Day of Resurrection, he will be a witness against them.
interpretation: This verse indicates that every individual from the People of the Scripture will inevitably acknowledge the truth of Jesus ('Isa) as a prophet and servant of Allah before their own death, a realization that occurs at the moment of transition when the reality of the afterlife becomes apparent to them; however, this compelled belief at the time of death does not grant them salvation, as Jesus will then stand as a witness on the Day of Judgment to testify regarding their past denials and actions against the truth he brought.

translation: So for wrongdoing on the part of the Jews, We made unlawful for them [certain] good foods which had been lawful to them, and for their averting from the way of Allah many [people].
interpretation: The verse indicates that the dietary restrictions imposed upon the Children of Israel were not originally part of their divine law, but rather a punitive measure decreed by Allah as a consequence of their persistent disobedience, their corruption, and their active efforts to hinder others from following the path of truth and righteousness.

translation: And [for] their taking of usury, while they had been forbidden from it, and their consuming of the people's wealth unjustly. And We have prepared for the disbelievers among them a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the moral and spiritual corruption of those who persisted in disobedience despite receiving clear divine prohibitions. The act of taking usury and consuming others' wealth through deceitful or unjust means represents a fundamental disregard for the rights of fellow humans and a direct defiance of God's law. By emphasizing the preparation of a painful punishment, the Quran underscores that such exploitation—which disrupts social justice and integrity—is a grave violation that leads to spiritual ruin, distinguishing those who embrace such greed as being in a state of willful disbelief and spiritual blindness.

translation: But those firm in knowledge among them and the believers believe in what has been revealed to you, [O Muhammad], and what was revealed before you. And those who establish prayer and give zakah and believe in Allah and the Last Day - those We will give a great reward.
interpretation: The verse highlights that true believers, especially those well-grounded in divine knowledge, do not differentiate between the revelations brought by Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and those brought by the prophets before him, as they recognize that all divine truth originates from the same source. By coupling this belief with righteous deeds such as regular prayer and obligatory charity, these individuals demonstrate a complete submission to the divine covenant, which guarantees them an immense and everlasting reward from Allah in the afterlife for their sincerity and steadfastness.

translation: Indeed, We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him. And We revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, the Descendants, Jesus, Job, Jonah, Aaron, and Solomon, and to David We gave the book [of Psalms].
interpretation: This verse serves to establish the continuity of divine revelation, affirming that Muhammad's prophethood is not an innovation but a continuation of the same mission entrusted to the messengers of the past; it highlights that God's message has always been consistent and that the inclusion of various prophets emphasizes the universal nature of the invitation to monotheism, while the specific mention of David receiving the Psalms honors the tradition of revealed scriptures given to humanity throughout history.

translation: And [We sent] messengers about whom We have related [their stories] to you before and messengers about whom We have not related to you. And Allah spoke to Moses with [direct] speech.
interpretation: This verse serves to emphasize the continuity of divine guidance throughout history by highlighting that while Allah sent numerous prophets to humanity, only a selected few were mentioned in the Qur'an; furthermore, the specific mention of Musa (Moses) receiving direct, unmediated speech from Allah underscores his unique rank and the profound intimacy of his communion with the Creator, distinguishing his experience from the general mode of revelation provided to other prophets.

translation: Messengers as bringers of good tidings and warners so that mankind will have no argument against Allah after the messengers. And ever is Allah Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: Allah sent prophets to convey His laws and reveal His will to humanity so that no one can claim ignorance or lack of guidance on the Day of Judgment, as the arrival of these messengers leaves no room for excuses, demonstrating that Allah's actions are governed by His perfect wisdom and irresistible power.

translation: But Allah bears witness to that which He has revealed unto you; He has sent it down with His knowledge, and the angels bear witness [as well]. And sufficient is Allah as Witness.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine reassurance to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) regarding the truthfulness and origin of the revelation he received; it declares that Allah Almighty testifies to the authenticity of the Qur'an by grounding its revelation in His infinite knowledge and absolute wisdom, while also citing the angels as additional witnesses to signify that this message is not the product of human fabrication but a supreme decree that possesses undeniable celestial validation.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieved and averted others from the way of Allah have certainly strayed far away.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the persistence of the disbelievers in their denial, coupled with their active efforts to obstruct others from following the path of guidance, places them in a state of profound and irrevocable error, far removed from the truth and any possibility of accidental repentance, as they have intentionally chosen a path that leads them deeper into darkness and away from the ultimate purpose of their existence.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieved and committed injustice - never will Allah forgive them, nor will He guide them to a path.
interpretation: This verse indicates that individuals who have entrenched themselves in disbelief and persistent injustice, to the point where they continuously reject the truth and actively oppose righteousness, effectively shut the door to divine guidance and mercy upon themselves; their hearts become so sealed by their own choices that they no longer possess the capacity to seek repentance or follow the path of truth, leaving them in a state of permanent deprivation.

translation: Except the path of Hell, in which they will abide forever; and that is easy for Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that for those who have persistently chosen disbelief and injustice despite clear warnings, their ultimate and inescapable destination is Hell, where they will remain eternally, and that executing this divine judgment of justice is effortless for Allah, as His sovereignty and power over all matters are absolute and beyond any difficulty.

translation: O mankind, the Messenger has come to you with the truth from your Lord, so believe; it is better for you. But if you disbelieve - then indeed, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. And ever is Allah Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: Allah addresses all of humanity, informing them that Muhammad has brought the absolute truth—the message of monotheism and divine guidance—which serves their ultimate interest and salvation. He warns that choosing to reject this truth does not diminish His sovereignty or majesty, for He is the owner of everything in existence, and that His judgment is rooted in His perfect omniscience regarding His creation and His profound wisdom in all His commands and decrees.

translation: O People of the Scripture, do not commit excess in your religion or say about Allah except the truth. The Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary, was but a messenger of Allah and His word which He directed to Mary and a soul from Him. So believe in Allah and His messengers. And do not say, 'Three'; desist - it is better for you. Indeed, Allah is but one God. Exalted is He above having a son. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse calls for a return to the absolute oneness of God (Tawhid), correcting the theological errors of Christians regarding the nature of Jesus. It clarifies that Jesus is a created being and a messenger, not a divine entity or part of a Trinity, and emphasizes that attributing a son to Allah contradicts His majesty and sovereign authority as the sole Creator and Sustainer of the universe.

translation: Never would the Messiah disdain to be a servant of Allah, nor would the angels near [to Him]. And whoever disdains His worship and is arrogant - He will gather them to Himself all together.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the station of servitude to Allah is the highest honor, as evidenced by the fact that even the most noble creations, such as Prophet Isa (Jesus) and the archangels, occupy this status. It serves as a refutation of those who attribute divinity to the Messiah or the angels, asserting that any creature, regardless of its rank, is fundamentally a servant of the Creator, and therefore, arrogance or refusal to acknowledge this submission is a denial of the fundamental reality of existence which will lead to a universal reckoning before Allah.

translation: As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, He will give them in full their rewards and grant them extra from His bounty. But as for those who disdained and were arrogant, He will punish them with a painful punishment, and they will not find for themselves besides Allah any protector or helper.
interpretation: This verse establishes the principle of divine justice, contrasting the fate of those who surrender to God through faith and good works with those who rely on their own pride. The promise of an increase from God's bounty beyond mere reward signifies that divine grace is not limited to strict reciprocity, while the punishment for the arrogant highlights that their refusal to submit to the Truth isolates them from the only source of protection and mercy in existence.

translation: O mankind, there has come to you a conclusive proof from your Lord, and We have sent down to you a clear light.
interpretation: This verse addresses all of humanity, declaring that Allah has provided them with an irrefutable argument and evidence in the form of Prophet Muhammad, and has revealed the Qur'an as a luminous guide that dispels the darkness of ignorance and disbelief, illuminating the path of truth so that those who seek guidance may recognize the way to salvation.

translation: As for those who believed in Allah and held fast to Him, He will admit them into mercy from Him and bounty and guide them to Himself on a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true salvation and divine guidance are reserved for those who combine sincere faith with an active, constant reliance on Allah, treating Him as their sole source of protection and support. By clinging to His commands and seeking His closeness, the believer is granted a dual reward: the encompassing grace of His mercy which shields them from harm, and the abundance of His bounty which enriches their soul. Ultimately, this divine companionship culminates in God directing the believer's inner heart and outer conduct toward the 'straight path,' which is the unified, unwavering course that leads directly to His presence and ultimate truth.

translation: They ask you for a legal ruling. Say, 'Allah gives you a ruling concerning the one who leaves neither ascendant nor descendant as heir.' If a man dies, leaving no child but [having] a sister, she will have half of what he left. And he inherits from her if she has no child. But if there are two sisters [or more], they will have two-thirds of what he left. If there are brothers and sisters, then the male will have the equivalent of the portion of two females. Allah makes clear to you [His law], lest you go astray. And Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse establishes the laws of inheritance for a deceased person who leaves no parents or children, specifically regarding siblings. It clarifies the fractional shares for sisters and the distribution between male and female siblings to ensure justice and prevent familial disputes. By providing these precise calculations, Allah protects the believers from falling into error or injustice in the division of wealth, demonstrating His comprehensive knowledge of human affairs and familial bonds.

translation: O you who have believed, fulfill [all] contracts. Lawful for you are the animals of grazing livestock except for that which is recited to you [in this Qur'an] - hunting not being permitted while you are in the state of ihram. Indeed, Allah ordains what He intends.
interpretation: This verse establishes the absolute sanctity of keeping one's promises and upholding all covenants, whether they are between man and his Creator or between individuals in societal and commercial dealings, as faithfulness to these commitments is a cornerstone of faith and social order; concurrently, it defines the boundaries of permissible sustenance by clarifying that while Allah has provided grazing livestock for human consumption, He retains the sole authority to legislate exceptions, such as the prohibition of hunting during the state of sacred pilgrimage, thereby reminding believers that human behavior is subject to the supreme and purposeful wisdom of the Divine.

translation: O you who have believed, do not violate the rites of Allah or the sacred month or the sacrificial animals or the garlanded (animals) or those repairing to the Sacred House seeking bounty from their Lord and (His) pleasure. But when you come out of ihram, then hunt. And do not let the hatred of a people for having obstructed you from al-Masjid al-Haram lead you to transgress. And cooperate in righteousness and piety, but do not cooperate in sin and aggression. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is severe in penalty.
interpretation: This verse establishes a divine mandate for believers to uphold the sanctity of religious symbols, places, and times, demanding that they refrain from aggression even against those who have previously harmed them.
