It emphasizes that justice must be maintained regardless of personal animosity, and directs the community to foster collective cooperation in virtuous deeds and God-consciousness, while strictly prohibiting any collaboration in acts of injustice or moral transgression, reminding the believers that their ultimate accountability remains with Allah, whose justice is absolute.

translation: This day are (all) good things made lawful for you. The food of those who have been given the Scripture is lawful for your food and yours is lawful for theirs. (Lawful unto you in marriage) are chaste women from the believers and chaste women from those who were given the Scripture before you (Hebrw and Christian women) when you give them their due bridal gifts, desiring chastity, not committing illegal sexual intercourse, nor taking them as girlfriends. And whoever denies the faith, his work has become worthless, and he, in the Hereafter, will be among the losers.
interpretation: This verse establishes that Allah has sanctified the sustenance and social unions of the believers by permitting the consumption of food prepared by the People of the Book and legalizing marriage with their chaste women, provided that these unions are based on formal contracts with bridal gifts and mutual modesty rather than illicit affairs. It serves as a test of the believers' commitment to Divine Law, emphasizing that while such cross-community interactions are permissible, they must be conducted within the strict moral framework defined by faith; ultimately, abandoning these divinely ordained boundaries constitutes a rejection of the faith itself, leading to the nullification of one's spiritual endeavors and eternal loss in the afterlife.

translation: O you who have believed, when you rise to prayer, wash your faces and your forearms to the elbows and wipe over your heads and wash your feet to the ankles. And if you are in a state of janabah, then purify yourselves. But if you are ill or on a journey or one of you comes from the place of relieving himself or you have contacted women and do not find water, then seek clean earth and wipe over your faces and hands with it. Allah does not intend to make difficulty for you, but He intends to purify you and complete His favor upon you that you may be grateful.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine legislative framework for ritual purity, emphasizing that the physical act of washing or performing tayammum is not an end in itself, but a spiritual preparation that reflects God's mercy; by simplifying the requirements during times of hardship, Allah ensures that the path to communion with Him through prayer remains accessible, thereby cleansing the believer of both minor and major impurities while fostering a state of constant mindfulness and gratitude toward His sustaining grace.

translation: And remember the favor of Allah upon you and His covenant with which He bound you when you said, 'We hear and we obey'; and fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of that within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine reminder to the believers to maintain a state of gratitude and accountability, emphasizing that the pledge of obedience given to Allah is not merely a verbal acknowledgment but a commitment that must manifest in their daily actions. By referencing the 'covenant' and the inner 'breasts,' the Qur'an highlights that true devotion is rooted in the heart; therefore, one must cultivate a constant awareness of God, knowing that He is fully cognizant of the hidden intentions and secret thoughts that precede any outward profession of faith.

translation: Allah has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds that for them is forgiveness and a great reward.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine covenant between Allah and the believers, emphasizing that faith is not merely an inward conviction but must be manifested through righteous actions. The promise of forgiveness serves as a divine assurance that their past shortcomings will be pardoned, while the 'great reward' refers to the eternal blessings of Paradise, signifying that the value of sincere devotion and virtuous conduct far outweighs the temporary struggles of worldly life.

translation: But those who disbelieved and denied Our verses - those are the companions of Hellfire.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern declaration of the ultimate spiritual consequence for those who persist in rejecting the divine truth revealed through God's signs. It emphasizes that the state of 'disbelief' coupled with the active 'denial' of these signs creates an unbreakable bond between such individuals and the torment of the afterlife, illustrating that persistent arrogance against divine guidance leads to a permanent separation from mercy.

translation: O you who have believed, remember the favor of Allah upon you when a people determined to extend their hands against you, but He withheld their hands from you; and fear Allah. And upon Allah let the believers rely.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder to the believers of Allah's divine protection and constant providence, specifically referring to instances where enemies plotted to harm them but were divinely restrained. It teaches that true security does not come from human strength alone but from the active oversight of Allah, urging the faithful to maintain consciousness of His presence and to place their complete, unwavering trust in Him as the ultimate source of safety and success in all their affairs.

translation: So for their breaking of the covenant We cursed them and made their hearts hard; they distort words from their [proper] usages and have forgotten a portion of that of which they were reminded. And you will still observe deceit among them, except a few of them. But pardon them and overlook [their misdeeds]. Indeed, Allah loves the doers of good.
interpretation: The verse explains that the spiritual hardening and corruption of the hearts of those who broke their covenant with God is a direct consequence of their persistent rebellion and deliberate distortion of divine revelation. Because they abandoned the truth and neglected the guidance they were given, they became prone to treachery and deceit. The instruction for the Prophet to pardon and overlook their transgressions is a divine counsel to uphold moral excellence and patience, emphasizing that responding to hostility with grace and benevolence is a virtue beloved by God, as it reflects the character of those who seek righteousness despite the betrayal of others.

translation: And from those who say, 'We are Christians,' We took their covenant; but they forgot a portion of that of which they were reminded. So We caused among them animosity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection. And Allah is going to inform them about what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse explains that because those who claimed to be followers of Jesus abandoned the core truths and divine reminders revealed to them, they lost the spirit of unity and brotherhood. As a consequence of turning away from the guidance and forgetting their obligations, they were left to be fractured by deep-seated hostility and internal discord, a state of spiritual and social fragmentation that will persist within their communities until the final judgment, at which point God will hold them fully accountable for their corruptions and deviations.

translation: O People of the Scripture, there has come to you Our Messenger, making clear to you much of what you used to conceal of the Scripture and overlooking much. There has come to you from Allah a light and a clear Book.
interpretation: This verse addresses the People of the Scripture, informing them that Muhammad (peace be upon him) has arrived as a divine messenger to unveil the truths they had intentionally hidden or distorted within their own scriptures. While he exposes these concealed teachings to restore the original divine message, he also chooses to overlook many other matters out of mercy and divine wisdom, avoiding unnecessary provocation or hardship. The 'light' refers to the Prophet himself—as he illuminates the path of truth—and the 'clear Book' refers to the Qur'an, which serves as a definitive, unambiguous guide that removes all doubt and clarifies the laws and beliefs ordained by Allah.

translation: By it, Allah guides those who seek His pleasure to the ways of peace and brings them out from darkness into the light, by His permission, and guides them to a straight path.
interpretation: Allah guides those who sincerely seek His approval and strive for His pleasure toward the paths of safety, salvation, and spiritual harmony. Through the light of the Quran and faith, He liberates their souls from the darkness of ignorance, doubt, and disbelief, leading them into the light of divine truth and steering them steadily along the clear, righteous path that reaches its ultimate destination in the presence of God.

translation: They have certainly disbelieved who say, 'Allah is the Messiah, the son of Mary.' Say, 'Then who could prevent Allah at all if He had intended to destroy the Messiah, the son of Mary, his mother and everyone on earth?' And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them. He creates what He wills, and Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse refutes the claim of those who attribute divinity to the Messiah by highlighting the absolute sovereignty and limitless power of Allah. It posits a rhetorical challenge: if the Messiah were truly divine, he would possess the power to sustain himself and his creation; however, since Allah holds the exclusive authority to bring life and death to all beings, including the Messiah and his mother, their dependency on the Creator proves that they are created beings rather than deities. The verse underscores that the totality of existence belongs to Allah, who exercises His divine will without restriction, demonstrating that the conceptual framework of incarnation contradicts the true nature of God's majesty and absolute oneness.

translation: And the Jews and the Christians say, 'We are the children of Allah and His beloved ones.' Say, 'Then why does He punish you for your sins?' Rather, you are human beings from among those He has created. He forgives whom He wills, and He punishes whom He wills. And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, and to Him is the [final] destination.
interpretation: This verse refutes the false claims of the People of the Scripture who believed they held a special, innate status as God's children or favorites that exempted them from accountability. Allah instructs the Prophet to point out that their own suffering and the punishments they face contradict this claim of immunity, asserting instead that they are subject to the same moral laws and divine judgment as any other created being. It emphasizes that divine favor is not determined by lineage or group identity, but rather by Allah's sovereign authority and wisdom, whereby He grants forgiveness or inflicts punishment based on His absolute justice and the deeds of the individuals, reminding all of mankind that ultimate return and judgment belong to Him alone.

translation: O People of the Scripture, there has come to you Our Messenger to make clear to you [the religion] after a period [of suspension] of messengers, lest you say, 'There came not to us any bringer of good tidings or a warner.' But there has come to you a bringer of good tidings and a warner. And Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: Allah addresses the Jews and Christians, informing them that Muhammad (peace be upon him) was sent to them after a long gap in the arrival of prophets—a period during which religious truths had been obscured and divine guidance had been interrupted. By sending him, Allah removed any possible excuse they might have claimed on the Day of Judgment—namely, the excuse of ignorance or the lack of a prophetic warning. With the arrival of Muhammad, the truth was made manifest, the path of guidance was illuminated, and the opportunity for salvation was clearly presented, leaving no room for those who reject the message to plead that they were left without a guide.

translation: And mention when Moses said to his people, 'O my people, remember the favor of Allah upon you when He appointed among you prophets and made you possessors and gave you that which He had not given any one among the worlds.'
interpretation: Moses is reminding the Children of Israel of the immense honor bestowed upon them by God, specifically emphasizing that they were granted sovereign independence and divine guidance through a lineage of prophets, a status of favor and distinction that was uniquely conferred upon them compared to all other nations of that era.

translation: O my people, enter the Holy Land which Allah has assigned to you and do not turn back [in flight] or you will become losers.
interpretation: This verse reflects the command of Prophet Musa to the Children of Israel to enter Jerusalem and the surrounding sacred territories, reminding them that the land was divinely decreed for them as a promise of their inheritance; the instruction not to turn back serves as a divine warning that abandoning their duty to stand firm in faith and obedience to Allah’s commands would result in their spiritual and material ruin, shifting them from a position of favored guidance to one of catastrophic loss.

translation: They said, 'O Moses, indeed within it is a people of tyrannical strength, and indeed, we will never enter it until they leave it; but if they leave it, then indeed we will enter.'
interpretation: The people of Israel displayed cowardice and a lack of faith in God's promise of victory by focusing on the physical strength and stature of the inhabitants of the land rather than relying on the divine support that had previously rescued them from Pharaoh, thereby revealing their reluctance to face hardship for the sake of their faith.

translation: Said two men from among those who feared, upon whom Allah had bestowed favor, 'Enter upon them through the gate; for when you have entered it, you will be predominant. And upon Allah rely, if you should be believers.'
interpretation: The two men, identified by tradition as Joshua and Caleb, encouraged their people by reminding them that God's grace and promise of victory are guaranteed if they obey His command to enter the land, emphasizing that true faith requires both taking the necessary physical step of confrontation and placing absolute trust in Allah's support to overcome their fears of the inhabitants.

translation: They said, 'O Moses, indeed we will never enter it, as long as they are within it; so go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting right here.'
interpretation: This verse reveals the depths of the Israelites' disobedience and lack of faith; by telling Moses to go fight alongside his Lord while they remained behind, they demonstrated a profound abandonment of their religious duty and a complete failure to fulfill the covenant of Jihad and struggle to enter the Holy Land, effectively prioritizing their own comfort over the command of Allah.

translation: He said, 'My Lord, indeed I do not possess except myself and my brother, so part us from the defiantly disobedient people.'
interpretation: Musa, peace be upon him, expressed his total helplessness before Allah, acknowledging that he had no power or authority over his people except for his own soul and his brother Harun. By asking Allah to separate them from the disobedient, he was seeking a clear distinction and deliverance from the consequences of their rebellion, effectively distancing himself and his brother from the punishment that would befall those who transgressed the limits of faith and obedience.

translation: He (Allah) said, 'Then indeed, it is forbidden to them for forty years; they will wander throughout the land. So do not grieve over the defiantly disobedient people.'
interpretation: This verse signifies that because of the Israelites' refusal to enter the Holy Land out of fear and disobedience, Allah decreed a state of exile and confusion for them for forty years. During this period, they were to wander in the wilderness, unable to reach their destination. The prohibition was a consequence of their lack of faith and their defiance against Moses and Allah's command, and Allah instructs Moses not to feel sorrow or pity for their self-inflicted plight, as their state was a direct result of their own wickedness and rejection of divine guidance.

translation: And recite to them the story of the two sons of Adam, in truth, when they both offered a sacrifice and it was accepted from one of them but was not accepted from the other. Said the latter, 'I will surely kill you.' Said the former, 'Indeed, Allah only accepts from the righteous.'
interpretation: The verse highlights that the root cause of moral failure and hostility—symbolized by Cain's threat—is the lack of taqwa (God-consciousness). It teaches that divine acceptance is not based on status, lineage, or the mere act of giving, but on the sincerity and purity of heart that accompanies one's deeds. By stating that God accepts only from the righteous, the accepted brother emphasizes that the rejection of the other's offering was not an act of divine injustice, but a direct consequence of the internal spiritual state of the offerer.

translation: If you should raise your hand against me to kill me, I shall not raise my hand against you to kill you. Indeed, I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the principle of principled non-violence and moral restraint in the face of aggression. The speaker, Habil (Abel), declares that his refusal to retaliate with lethal force is not a sign of weakness or cowardice, but rather a deliberate choice rooted in the fear of God and the preservation of sanctity of life. By choosing to submit to being the victim rather than becoming a murderer, he upholds his spiritual integrity and places his trust in the divine justice of the Lord of the worlds over the immediate, sinful instinct of self-preservation through violence.

translation: I want you to bear my sin and your sin, so that you will be among the companions of the Fire; and that is the recompense of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The speaker is expressing that the responsibility for the shedding of his blood will fall upon his brother, signifying that the brother will carry the burden of his own transgression in killing an innocent soul along with the sins that the victim might have otherwise committed, thereby sealing his fate as one of the inhabitants of Hell who have transgressed the limits set by God.

translation: Then his soul prompted him to kill his brother, so he killed him and became among the losers.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the grave consequences of succumbing to one's base instincts and desires. When Cain allowed envy and hatred to take root within his heart, his inner self gradually made the act of fratricide seem acceptable to him, eventually leading him to commit the heinous crime. By choosing to follow his ego's impulses rather than the moral dictates of his conscience, he incurred a profound loss—losing not only the life of his brother but also his own spiritual standing and peace of mind in this world and the hereafter.

translation: Then Allah sent a crow scratching in the ground to show him how to cover the corpse of his brother. He said, 'Woe to me! Have I failed to be like this crow and cover the corpse of my brother?' And he became of the regretful.
interpretation: When Cain was overwhelmed by the burden of his brother's dead body, not knowing how to handle it, Allah provided a natural lesson through the instinct of a crow. By witnessing the crow burying its dead, Cain was struck with profound regret, not out of true repentance for the act of murder itself, but out of the helplessness and shame of being incapable of even performing the basic act of burial, which highlighted the futility and horror of his sinful deed.

translation: Because of that, We ordained for the Children of Israel that if any one slew a person - unless it be for murder or for spreading mischief in the land - it would be as if he slew all mankind: and if any one saved a life, it would be as if he saved the life of all mankind. And there came to them Our messengers with clear signs, yet, even after that, many of them continued to commit excesses in the land.
interpretation: This verse underscores the profound sanctity of human life in the eyes of God, establishing that the unlawful killing of a single individual is a crime of such magnitude that it is morally equivalent to destroying the entirety of humanity, as it violates the divine right to life and threatens the social fabric of mankind. Conversely, the act of saving a life is equated to bestowing life upon all people, reflecting the immense value placed on mercy and preservation. The concluding observation regarding the Children of Israel serves as a divine warning that despite receiving clear moral guidance and evidentiary proofs from God, human nature is prone to arrogance and transgression when individuals prioritize their own desires over the sanctity of others' existence.

translation: Except for those who repent before you overpower them; so know that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse establishes that if individuals who have committed crimes warranting severe punishment—specifically those defined by rebellion or banditry—sincerely turn to Allah in repentance and abandon their harmful actions before they are apprehended by the authorities, they are exempted from the prescribed worldly penalties. Their repentance serves to bridge the gap between them and Allah's mercy, signaling that while human justice may be superseded by the cessation of their hostility, the ultimate judgment belongs to Allah, who accepts true remorse and grants forgiveness to those who rectify their path.

translation: O you who have believed, fear Allah and seek the means [of approach] to Him, and strive in His cause that you may succeed.
interpretation: The verse urges believers to cultivate God-consciousness (Taqwa) as the foundation of their faith and to actively seek closeness to Allah through righteous deeds, obedience, and spiritual devotion, as these act as the 'means' (Wasilah) that bridge the gap between the servant and the Creator, ultimately leading to success in both worlds through persistent striving for His sake.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve - if they had all that is on the earth and the like of it with it to ransom themselves with it from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, it would not be accepted from them, and for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that the gravity of disbelief in the afterlife is so immense that no worldly possession, regardless of its magnitude, can serve as a substitute or ransom to absolve the disbeliever from the divine penalty, highlighting that the moral and spiritual consequences of rejecting faith are absolute and cannot be mitigated by material wealth on the Day of Judgment.

translation: They wish to get out of the Fire, but never are they to emerge therefrom, and for them is an enduring punishment.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the absolute finality of the fate of those who have rejected faith and persisted in transgression; their desire to escape the intensity of Hellfire is met with the reality that their spiritual state has rendered them permanently confined to it, as they lack the purifying belief that would have allowed for their eventual redemption or transition from that state of suffering.

translation: As for the male thief and the female thief, cut off their hands in recompense for what they earned [as] a deterrent from Allah. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse establishes a severe penal sanction for the crime of theft, reflecting the gravity of violating the sanctity of private property in a social order. By prescribing amputation as a deterrent, the legislation aims to protect the wealth of individuals and maintain public stability, while the attributes of Allah being 'Exalted in Might' and 'Wise' suggest that this law is not merely punitive but is rooted in a profound wisdom that considers the psychological and societal impact of crime, ultimately intending to discourage corruption and uphold justice in the land.

translation: But whoever repents after his wrongdoing and reforms, indeed, Allah will turn to him in forgiveness. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine assurance that the gates of mercy remain open for any individual who sincerely regrets their transgressions, ceases their harmful actions, and rectifies their conduct through righteous deeds; it emphasizes that Allah's forgiveness is not merely a suspension of punishment, but a complete acceptance of the repentant, provided there is a genuine transformation of the heart and behavior.

translation: Do you not know that to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth? He punishes whom He wills and forgives whom He wills, and Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse establishes the absolute sovereignty of God, emphasizing that His authority over the entire universe is total and unquestioned. The mention of His power to punish or forgive serves as a reminder to the believers that divine judgment is rooted in His perfect wisdom and comprehensive knowledge; it is an assertion that His actions are not subject to human limitation, reinforcing that He alone manages the outcomes of all creation according to His justice and mercy.

translation: O Messenger, do not let those who hasten into disbelief grieve you, from among those who say, 'We believe' with their mouths, but their hearts have not believed; nor those among the Jews—they are listeners to falsehood, listeners to other people who have not come to you. They distort words from their proper meanings, saying, 'If you are given this, accept it; but if you are not given it, then beware.' And whomever Allah intends to try, you will never possess for him any power against Allah. Those are the ones for whom Allah does not intend to purify their hearts. For them in this world is disgrace, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment.
interpretation: The verse serves as a divine consolation to the Prophet Muhammad, urging him not to be distressed by the hypocrisy of those who outwardly profess faith while harboring disbelief in their hearts, nor by the corrupt leaders among the Jews who actively seek out lies and distort the scriptures to suit their own agendas. It emphasizes that such individuals, whose hearts have remained hardened and defiant against the truth, have forfeited the divine grace of purification, and their rejection of God's guidance leads them inevitably toward humiliation in this life and severe retribution in the hereafter, as no human intervention can alter the fate of those whom Allah has allowed to fall into trial due to their own deliberate persistent choices.

translation: They are avid listeners to falsehood, devourers of the illicit. So if they come to you, judge between them or turn away from them. And if you turn away from them, they will not harm you at all. But if you judge, judge between them with justice. Indeed, Allah loves the just.
interpretation: This verse addresses the moral corruption of those who habitually listen to lies and consume wealth gained through unlawful means, such as bribes or usury. Allah instructs the Prophet (peace be upon him) and the believers that when faced with such people seeking judgment, one is given the choice to either exercise justice or decline involvement entirely, as their hostility cannot harm those who rely on Allah. If one chooses to arbitrate, they are bound by the divine mandate of absolute fairness, as justice is a quality that attracts the love and favor of Allah.

translation: But how is it that they come to you for judgment, while they have the Torah, in which is the judgment of Allah? Then they turn away even after that; but those are not believers.
interpretation: This verse censures the behavior of those who seek the Prophet's judgment while simultaneously possessing the Torah—a book they claim to believe in and which contains Allah's clear rulings—yet they exhibit inconsistency by turning away from divine judgment whenever it contradicts their personal whims or desires, thereby demonstrating that their appeal to the Prophet is not born of true faith or submission to God, but rather a pursuit of convenience.

translation: Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which was guidance and light. The prophets who submitted [to Allah] judged by it for the Jews, as did the rabbis and scholars by that with which they were entrusted of the Scripture of Allah, and they were witnesses thereto. So do not fear the people but fear Me, and do not exchange My verses for a small price. And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the Torah was a divine light and a source of guidance that mandated the practice of justice according to God’s laws; it highlights that the responsibility of the spiritual leaders and scholars was to act as guardians and witnesses of this covenant, warning that any compromise of these divine rulings for worldly gain or out of fear of public opinion constitutes a fundamental denial of the authority and truth of God’s revelation.

translation: And We ordained for them therein a life for a life, an eye for an eye, a nose for a nose, an ear for an ear, a tooth for a tooth, and for wounds is legal retribution. But whoever gives [up his right as] charity, it is an expiation for him. And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed - then it is those who are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse establishes the principle of exact justice in cases of physical harm, ensuring that the punishment is proportionate to the injury, thereby preventing excessive revenge; however, the Quran emphasizes that while the victim has the right to exact this retribution, choosing to forgive the offender instead serves as a means of spiritual purification and atonement for the victim, and it serves as a stern warning that those who hold authority must uphold these divine standards of justice rather than relying on human-made laws or personal desires, as departing from God’s revealed justice constitutes a grave act of oppression against the truth and society.

translation: And We sent, following in their footsteps, Jesus, the son of Mary, confirming that which came before him in the Torah; and We gave him the Gospel, in which was guidance and light and confirming that which came before it of the Torah as a guidance and instruction for the righteous.
interpretation: This verse highlights the continuity of the divine message, illustrating how Allah sent Jesus to affirm the truth of the Torah while simultaneously providing a new scripture, the Gospel, which acted as a renewed source of divine guidance and spiritual illumination for those who fear God, ensuring that the fundamental principles of monotheism and moral rectitude remained intact and accessible to the faithful.

translation: And let the people of the Gospel judge by what Allah has revealed therein. And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed - then it is those who are the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse commands the followers of the Gospel to adhere to and implement the divine laws and guidance revealed by Allah within that scripture, emphasizing that turning away from God's established laws in favor of personal desires or human-made criteria constitutes a grave act of disobedience that alienates an individual from the path of faith and righteousness.

translation: And judge between them by what Allah has revealed and do not follow their inclinations and beware of them, lest they tempt you away from some of what Allah has revealed to you. And if they turn away - then know that Allah only intends to afflict them with some of their sins. And indeed, many among the people are defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine mandate to the Prophet Muhammad, and by extension to all leaders and believers, asserting that justice must be exclusively grounded in the laws and principles revealed by God. It warns against the human tendency to compromise eternal truth for the sake of temporary societal desires or the pressure of influential groups. The warning regarding 'temptation' highlights that political and social influence is often used as a tool to distract from divine ethics; therefore, one must maintain an uncompromising commitment to revealed morality. The final observation regarding those who turn away signifies that when people reject divine guidance, their subsequent internal and external conflicts are a natural, albeit painful, consequence of their own moral choices, reinforcing that straying from divine truth leads to spiritual and social decay.

translation: Do they then seek the judgment of the time of ignorance? And who is better in judgment than Allah for a people who have certainty?
interpretation: This verse serves as a rhetorical rebuke to those who abandon the divine laws revealed by Allah to seek guidance from man-made ideologies, customs, or worldly traditions that lack spiritual foundation. By labeling such systems as the 'judgment of ignorance,' the verse highlights that human wisdom, when disconnected from divine revelation, is inherently flawed, biased, and transient. The verse asserts that since Allah is the Creator and the All-Knowing, His legislative framework is perfectly aligned with human nature and the ultimate justice, making it the only logical and supreme authority for those who possess true conviction and intellectual discernment.

translation: O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies. They are [in fact] allies of one another. And whoever is an ally to them among you - then indeed, he is [one] of them. Indeed, Allah guides not the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This command prohibits the believers from forming intimate alliances or relying on the Jews and Christians for protection and political support against their own community, as these groups often unite based on their shared interests and opposition to the message of Islam; therefore, anyone who chooses to align their loyalty and identity with these groups effectively separates themselves from the community of believers and adopts the status of those whom they have sided with, placing themselves outside the path of divine guidance granted to the righteous.

translation: So you see those in whose hearts is a disease hastening toward them, saying, 'We are afraid that a misfortune may strike us.' But perhaps Allah will bring conquest or a command from Him, and they will become, over what they have been concealing within themselves, regretful.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the behavior of the hypocrites who align themselves with the enemies of Islam out of cowardice and fear of political or military shifts. By showing loyalty to those who oppose the faith, they hope to protect themselves if the power dynamic changes. The verse warns that these calculations are short-sighted, as Allah possesses the power to manifest His victory or judgment at any time, leaving these hypocrites to face the bitter reality of their duplicity and the subsequent shame and remorse when their true intentions are exposed and their opportunistic maneuvers fail to secure them the safety they sought.

translation: And those who have believed will say, 'Are these the ones who swore by Allah their strongest oaths that they were indeed with you?' Their deeds have become worthless, and they have become among the losers.
interpretation: This verse reflects the astonishment and realization of the believers on the Day of Resurrection, when they observe the hypocrites who had previously sworn solemn oaths to be allies of the faithful. The verse highlights that the hypocrites' outward displays of loyalty were hollow, as their internal disbelief nullified any good deeds they claimed to perform, ultimately leaving them in a state of total loss and divine rejection in the hereafter.

translation: O you who have believed, whoever of you should revert from his religion - Allah will bring forth [in place of them] a people He will love and who will love Him [who are] humble toward the believers, powerful against the disbelievers; they strive in the cause of Allah and do not fear the blame of a critic. That is the favor of Allah; He bestows it upon whom He wills. And Allah is all-Encompassing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine assurance that the truth of Islam is independent of the actions of any individual; should some choose to abandon their faith, Allah will replace them with those who embody the highest spiritual qualities, characterized by a deep mutual love between the Creator and the believer, a gentle humility toward their fellow brethren, and an unyielding, dignified strength when confronting those who oppose the truth, all while remaining steadfast in their devotion to God without being deterred by the ridicule or criticism of others.

translation: Your ally is none but Allah and His Messenger and those who have believed - those who establish prayer and give zakah, and they bow [in worship and humility].
interpretation: This verse establishes that the true source of authority, guardianship, and loyal support for a believer is Allah, followed by His Messenger, and the community of faithful believers who demonstrate their sincerity through consistent prayer and the act of charity, signifying that their allegiance and guidance are rooted in divine command rather than worldly affiliations.

translation: And whoever takes Allah and His Messenger and those who have believed as allies - indeed, the party of Allah - they are the ones who will be victorious.
interpretation: This verse establishes that true alliance and loyalty must be directed solely toward Allah, His Messenger, and the community of believers; when a person aligns themselves with these entities, they become part of the 'party of Allah' (Hizbullah), a status that guarantees spiritual and ultimate triumph, as those who remain faithful to divine guidance will inevitably prevail over falsehood and worldly opposition.

translation: O you who have believed, take not those who have taken your religion in ridicule and amusement among those who were given the Scripture before you nor the disbelievers as allies. And fear Allah, if you should be believers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine directive for the believers to establish clear boundaries in their social and political affiliations. It forbids forming intimate alliances or relying on those who mock and belittle the Islamic faith—specifically those who possess previous scriptures or those who openly reject the truth—because such individuals, by virtue of their hostility toward the divine message, cannot be trusted to act in the best interests of the community of believers. The command to 'fear Allah' serves as a reminder that a believer's ultimate loyalty must be to their faith and their Creator, and that compromising one's principles for the sake of companionship with those who disparage the truth is incompatible with the sincerity of one's belief.

translation: And when you call to prayer, they take it in mockery and amusement. That is because they are a people who do not reason.
interpretation: The verse highlights the state of those whose hearts are disconnected from divine guidance, as they view the act of calling to prayer—an invitation to spiritual connection and moral rectitude—not as a sacred summons, but as an opportunity for ridicule and triviality. This reaction stems from a profound lack of intellectual and spiritual maturity; by failing to contemplate the profound purpose behind the worship of the Creator, they remain trapped in a superficial existence, rendering them incapable of discerning the truth or understanding the gravity of their own conduct.

translation: Say, 'O People of the Scripture, do you resent us except because we believe in Allah and what was revealed to us and what was revealed before, and because most of you are defiantly disobedient?'
interpretation: The verse commands the Prophet Muhammad to confront the People of the Scripture by highlighting the illogical nature of their hostility toward the Muslims. He explains that their resentment is rooted in nothing other than the Muslims' commitment to fundamental faith—belief in the One God, the revelation of the Qur'an, and the truth of the previous scriptures—which exposes the hypocrisy of those among them who have abandoned the core principles of their own religious heritage and strayed into disobedience.

translation: Say, 'Shall I inform you of [what is] worse than that as penalty from Allah? [It is that of] those whom Allah has cursed and with whom He became angry and made of them apes and pigs and slaves of Taghut. Those are worse in position and further astray from the sound way.'
interpretation: The verse serves as a rhetorical rebuke to the People of the Scripture, highlighting that their self-righteous critique of the believers is hypocritical. Allah identifies that those who have turned away from divine truth, earned His curse through their rebellion, and descended into the basest of behaviors—symbolized by the imagery of apes and swine—are the ones truly deserving of condemnation. By comparing their spiritual corruption to the worship of false idols (Taghut), the verse emphasizes that they have strayed so far from the path of righteousness that their outward religious pretensions are nullified by the depth of their inner perversion and defiance of God's law.

translation: And when they come to you, they say, 'We have believed,' while they have certainly entered with disbelief, and they have certainly left with it. And Allah is most knowing of what they were concealing.
interpretation: This verse exposes the hypocrisy of those who outwardly proclaim faith while harboring disbelief in their hearts, emphasizing that their feigned sincerity is futile because Allah is fully aware of the hidden intentions and persistent rejection they conceal within themselves despite their verbal declarations.

translation: And you see many of them hastening into sin and aggression and the devouring of [what is] unlawful. How wretched is what they have been doing.
interpretation: The verse highlights the moral corruption of those who, despite claiming religious knowledge or status, rush toward forbidden acts and injustice. It serves as a stern warning that the normalization of greed and the consumption of ill-gotten gains constitute a grave spiritual decay, ultimately leading to a miserable outcome in the hereafter because their actions are devoid of sincerity and righteousness.

translation: Why do the rabbis and the learned men not forbid them from their saying of what is sinful and their consuming of what is unlawful? Indeed, evil is what they have been practicing.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern condemnation of the religious leaders and scholars among the People of the Book for their moral negligence; it highlights that their failure to enjoin good and forbid evil—specifically regarding the falsehoods spoken by their people and their illicit financial gains—renders these leaders complicit in the corruption, emphasizing that silence in the face of manifest sin is a grave abandonment of spiritual responsibility.

translation: The Jews said, 'Allah's hand is chained.' Chained be their own hands, and cursed be they for what they said. Rather, both His hands are outstretched; He spends how He wills. And surely that which has been revealed to you from your Lord will increase many of them in transgression and disbelief. And We have cast among them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection. Every time they kindled the fire of war, Allah extinguished it. And they strive upon the earth for corruption, and Allah does not like the corrupters.
interpretation: This verse addresses the blasphemous claim of certain Jewish groups who likened the Creator to His creation by suggesting His power or generosity was constrained. The Qur'an rejects this anthropomorphism, affirming that Allah’s grace and power are limitless and fully manifest, while the curse mentioned is a reflection of their own spiritual paralysis and the consequence of their own arrogant denials. It highlights a recurring pattern where divine guidance, instead of leading them to humility, provokes them into deeper rebellion, resulting in their social fragmentation, constant internal discord, and the repeated failure of their hostile conspiracies against the truth.

translation: And if only the People of the Scripture had believed and feared Allah, We would have removed from them their misdeeds and admitted them to Gardens of Pleasure.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the path to divine forgiveness and ultimate salvation is conditional upon internal faith and righteousness; if the People of the Book were to sincerely accept the truth of the message and align their lives with God-consciousness, Allah promises to erase the weight of their past transgressions and grant them entry into the eternal bliss of Paradise, indicating that divine grace is always accessible to those who turn away from their errors and embrace piety.

translation: And if they had upheld the Torah and the Gospel and what has been revealed to them from their Lord, they would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet. Among them is a moderate community, but many of them—evil is what they do.
interpretation: This verse signifies that if the People of the Scripture had truly implemented the laws and spiritual guidance contained in their revealed books—the Torah and the Gospel—and followed the final revelation sent to Muhammad, Allah would have opened for them the blessings of the heavens and the earth, granting them abundance, prosperity, and spiritual contentment. It emphasizes that adherence to divine law is the fundamental prerequisite for receiving both material and spiritual well-being, while simultaneously lamenting that, despite the presence of some righteous individuals among them, the majority persist in disobedience and wrongdoing, which prevents them from attaining this divine favor.

translation: O Messenger, announce that which has been revealed to you from your Lord, and if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message. And Allah will protect you from the people. Indeed, Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine mandate to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) emphasizing the absolute necessity of delivering the entirety of the divine message without omission or fear of social consequences, accompanied by a promise of spiritual and physical protection from those who might oppose his mission; it underscores that the responsibility of the messenger is purely to transmit the revelation, while the failure to do so would nullify the core purpose of his prophetic appointment, and it concludes by asserting that those who choose to reject the truth out of arrogance or disbelief are excluded from the divine guidance that leads to salvation.

translation: Say, O People of the Scripture, you are [standing] on nothing until you uphold the Torah, the Gospel, and what has been revealed to you from your Lord. And that which has been revealed to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in transgression and disbelief. So do not grieve over the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern call to the People of the Scripture, clarifying that their religious identity and claims to divine guidance are void and lack any spiritual standing as long as they neglect the fundamental tenets of their own revealed books, the Torah and the Gospel, and refuse to accept the final revelation sent to Prophet Muhammad. It highlights that true adherence to their own scriptures would naturally lead them to recognize the truth of the Qur'an, and it consoles the Prophet by explaining that the obstinacy and increased enmity of the disbelievers towards his message is a result of their own hardened hearts, advising him not to waste his sorrow on those who have chosen to persist in rejection.

translation: Indeed, those who have believed and those who were Jews, the Sabians, and the Christians - those who believed in Allah and the Last Day and did righteousness - no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse establishes the universal criterion for divine reward, clarifying that salvation is not determined by labels or tribal affiliation, but by the sincerity of one's faith in the Oneness of God and the Day of Judgment, coupled with the consistent performance of righteous deeds, thereby assuring those who uphold these core tenets that they shall be shielded from the terrors of the afterlife and the regrets of their earthly actions.

translation: We took a covenant from the Children of Israel and sent to them messengers. Whenever there came to them a messenger with what their souls did not desire, a party of them they denied, and another party they killed.
interpretation: This verse highlights the deep-seated rebellion and arrogance of the Children of Israel, who prioritized their personal whims, desires, and worldly interests over the divine truth brought by the prophets. Their rejection and killing of the messengers stemmed from a corrupted state of heart that could not endure the confrontation of their sinful behaviors or the submission required by God's commands, demonstrating how moral decay leads to the ultimate transgression of shedding innocent blood.

translation: And they thought there would be no trial, so they became blind and deaf. Then Allah turned to them in forgiveness, but again many of them became blind and deaf. And Allah is Seeing of what they do.
interpretation: The verse highlights the spiritual instability of those who mistakenly believe they will not be tested by Allah; their lack of foresight leads them to spiritual blindness and deafness, unable to perceive the truth or hear the guidance. Even when they receive divine mercy through repentance, their lack of genuine sincerity causes them to relapse into their state of heedlessness, demonstrating that Allah is fully aware of their persistent defiance and inconsistency.

translation: They have certainly disbelieved who say, 'Allah is the Messiah, son of Mary.' But the Messiah had said, 'O Children of Israel, worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord.' Indeed, he who associates others with Allah - Allah has forbidden him Paradise, and his abode is the Fire. And there are not for the wrongdoers any helpers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a definitive rejection of the doctrine of the divinity of Christ, emphasizing that Jesus himself explicitly commanded the worship of the One God alone; therefore, anyone who attributes divine status to him or others is committing the gravest injustice, resulting in the permanent forfeiture of Paradise and the incurrence of eternal punishment, as such individuals have rejected the foundational truth of Divine Oneness.

translation: They have certainly disbelieved who say, 'Allah is the third of three,' while there is no god except one God. And if they do not desist from what they are saying, there will surely afflict the disbelievers among them a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse rejects the doctrine of the Trinity, emphasizing that it contradicts the fundamental principle of Tawhid (the absolute Oneness of God) which is the core of divine message. It declares that attributing plurality to the Divine Essence is a grave form of disbelief, and it issues a stern warning that those who persist in such beliefs—which equate the Creator with created concepts or partners—will face severe consequences in the afterlife unless they repent and acknowledge the singularity and absolute transcendence of God.

translation: Do they not then repent to Allah and seek His forgiveness? And Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: This verse serves as a compassionate invitation from Allah to those who have deviated from the truth, urging them to abandon their errors and return to Him in sincere repentance. By questioning their lack of repentance, Allah highlights the accessibility of His mercy; He emphasizes that no matter the severity or frequency of their past transgressions, His nature as the Forgiving and Merciful ensures that any soul who genuinely seeks reconciliation will find an open door to His grace and a complete erasure of their previous faults.

translation: The Messiah, son of Mary, is not but a messenger; [other] messengers have passed on before him. And his mother was a supporter of truth. They both used to eat food. Look how We make clear to them the signs; then look how they are deluded.
interpretation: This verse serves as a definitive argument against the divinity of Jesus, asserting that he was a human messenger subject to the same biological necessities as all other created beings, such as the need for sustenance. By highlighting that both he and his mother were mortal and required food to survive, the Quran underscores his dependency on the Creator, thereby refuting the concept of his Godhood and emphasizing that he is a creature created by Allah, like those who preceded him in the long line of prophethood.

translation: Say, 'Do you worship other than Allah that which holds for you neither harm nor benefit while Allah is the Hearing, the Knowing?'
interpretation: The verse serves as a rational challenge to those who associate partners with God, highlighting the inherent futility of worshiping created beings or inanimate objects that lack the divine power to alter one's destiny. By contrasting the inability of false deities to effect change with Allah's absolute attribute of being 'As-Sami' (The All-Hearing) and 'Al-'Alim' (The All-Knowing), the text emphasizes that true devotion should be directed exclusively toward the Creator who possesses total awareness and sovereignty over all outcomes.

translation: Say, 'O People of the Scripture, do not exceed limits in your religion beyond the truth and do not follow the inclinations of a people who had gone astray before and misled many and have strayed from the soundness of the way.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine prohibition against extremism and religious fanaticism, specifically addressing the People of the Scripture who distorted their faith by elevating human beings to divine status or inventing innovations that lack foundation in truth. It warns the believers against imitating the behavioral patterns of those who previously deviated from divine guidance, emphasizing that such predecessors not only lost their own way but also corrupted the faith of others, thereby leading them away from the balanced, straight path of monotheism and moral rectitude.

translation: Cursed were those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel by the tongue of David and Jesus, the son of Mary. That is because they disobeyed and [habitually] transgressed.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the curse pronounced by these two noble prophets upon the disobedient among the Children of Israel was not an act of personal grievance, but a divine condemnation manifesting through their tongues as a consequence of the people's persistent rebellion, their audacity in violating God's commandments, and their repeated transgressions against the bounds of righteousness, which ultimately distanced them from the mercy of Allah.

translation: They did not prevent one another from wrongdoing that they did. Vile indeed was that which they were doing.
interpretation: This verse serves as a severe condemnation of the Children of Israel who abandoned the moral duty of enjoining good and forbidding evil, noting that their silence in the face of each other's transgressions was a sign of their spiritual decay and a direct cause of their divine punishment, as collective indifference to sin inevitably leads to the normalization and proliferation of corruption within a society.

translation: You see many of them becoming allies to those who have disbelieved. How wretched is that which they have put forth for themselves, in that Allah has become angry with them, and they will abide eternally in punishment.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern condemnation of those who forsake the bonds of faith to seek security or political alignment with disbelievers who oppose God's truth. It highlights that the root of their eternal suffering is not merely a divine decree of punishment, but the direct consequence of their own choices and actions, which have manifested as an obstruction between them and divine mercy, resulting in the permanence of their misery.

translation: And if they had believed in Allah and the Prophet and what was revealed to him, they would not have taken them as allies; but many of them are defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse establishes that true faith is incompatible with taking the enemies of Allah and His Messenger as allies. The act of forming loyal alliances with those who oppose the divine message serves as evidence that one's heart lacks the reality of belief in Allah, His Messenger, and the truth of the Quran; their outward profession of faith is contradicted by their choices, revealing that their defiance and deviation from the path of obedience are the root causes of their misguided allegiances.

translation: You will surely find the most intense of the people in animosity toward the believers to be the Jews and those who associate others with Allah; and you will find the nearest of them in affection to the believers those who say, 'We are Christians.' That is because among them are priests and monks and because they are not arrogant.
interpretation: The verse highlights the contrast in attitudes toward the early Muslim community, noting that the intensity of hostility from the Jews and polytheists stemmed from their deep-seated refusal to accept the truth of Islam, while the relative receptiveness of the Christians was attributed to the presence of humble, devoted scholars and ascetics among them, whose religious sincerity and lack of pride disposed them toward acknowledging the righteousness of the message of the Prophet Muhammad.

translation: And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of what they have recognized of the truth. They say, 'Our Lord, we have believed, so register us among the witnesses.'
interpretation: This verse describes the spiritual state of sincere seekers of truth who, upon hearing the Qur'an, experience a profound emotional and intellectual recognition of its divine origin; their tears serve as a physical manifestation of the internal impact caused by the sudden clarity of the truth, leading them to consciously profess their faith and request to be recorded among the followers of the prophets who bear witness to the oneness of God and the truth of His revelation.

translation: And why should we not believe in Allah and in what has come to us of the truth while we aspire that our Lord will admit us [to Paradise] with the righteous people?
interpretation: This verse reflects the sincere questioning of those who have perceived the truth and recognized the consistency of the divine message with the innate nature of the human soul, highlighting that faith is not merely a cognitive acceptance but a hopeful commitment to follow the path of the righteous in anticipation of Allah's mercy and admission into the company of the pious in the afterlife.

translation: So Allah rewarded them for what they said with gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide eternally. And that is the reward of the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse signifies that because these believers humbly acknowledged the truth and bore witness to the oneness of Allah and the prophethood of His Messenger with sincerity and firm conviction, Allah granted them a recompense befitting their noble testimony, which is an everlasting Paradise where they shall dwell forever; this reward serves as a manifestation of Allah’s grace toward those who strive to perfect their faith and deeds through ihsan, meaning they worship and act as if they see Allah, or are at least conscious that He sees them, thereby attaining the highest levels of spiritual excellence.

translation: But those who disbelieved and denied Our verses - those are the companions of the Hellfire.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the consequence of rejecting the signs and proofs of Allah, which are manifested in the natural world and the revealed scriptures, is an eternal habitation in the Fire, signifying that the deliberate choice to reject truth after it has been made clear is the fundamental cause of spiritual ruin and divine alienation.

translation: O you who have believed, do not prohibit the good things which Allah has made lawful to you and do not transgress. Indeed, Allah does not like transgressors.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine prohibition against self-imposed asceticism that contradicts the spirit of the Sharia, warning believers that by forbidding themselves what God has permitted—such as wholesome food, drink, or marital relations—they are essentially overstepping the boundaries established by the Creator. It emphasizes that true piety is not found in creating hardships or denying oneself the legitimate blessings of life, as such actions constitute a form of transgression against the natural order and the limits set by God.

translation: And eat of what Allah has provided for you, lawful and good. And fear Allah, in whom you are believers.
interpretation: This verse serves as both a permission and a command for the believers to consume only that which is lawful and pure, emphasizing that the sustenance provided by God is a blessing that must be approached with mindfulness of His limits. By pairing the instruction to eat with the command to fear God, the Qur'an establishes a connection between one's physical sustenance and one's spiritual integrity, reminding the believer that the state of one's faith is reflected in their adherence to divine boundaries regarding what is permitted in their daily lives.

translation: Allah will not impose blame upon you for what is unintentional in your oaths, but He will impose blame upon you for what you have intended of oaths. So its expiation is the feeding of ten needy people from the average of that which you feed your [own] families or clothing them or the freeing of a slave. But whoever cannot find [or afford it] - then a fast of three days [is required]. That is the expiation for oaths when you have sworn. But guard your oaths. Thus does Allah make clear to you His verses that you may be grateful.
interpretation: Allah establishes a distinction between oaths uttered casually without true intent—which carry no liability—and oaths made with firm resolution and sincerity, which bind the swearer to their promise. By prescribing a tiered system of expiation for breaking such vows—ranging from feeding or clothing the needy to manumission, or fasting as a final recourse—Allah emphasizes the sanctity and gravity of using His name to guarantee one’s word, teaching the believer to treat their commitments with the utmost seriousness and to avoid reckless swearing.

translation: O you who have believed, indeed, intoxicants, gambling, [sacrificing on] stone alters [to other than Allah], and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it that you may be successful.
interpretation: This verse serves as a definitive prohibition of substances and practices that cloud the human intellect or involve superstitious reliance on chance rather than God, categorizing them as spiritual impurities that corrupt the soul and hinder a person from achieving true success, which is the attainment of divine pleasure and eternal salvation.

translation: Satan only wants to cause between you animosity and hatred through intoxicants and gambling and to avert you from the remembrance of Allah and from prayer. So will you not desist?
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine warning that intoxicants and gambling are not merely personal habits but are strategic tools utilized by Satan to dismantle the social fabric of the community; by clouding the intellect and inciting base instincts, he systematically drives believers toward conflict and resentment while simultaneously severing their essential connection to the Creator through the abandonment of prayer and spiritual mindfulness.

translation: And obey Allah and obey the Messenger, and beware; but if you turn away, then know that upon Our Messenger is only the clear notification.
interpretation: The verse commands believers to adhere strictly to the laws of Allah and the guidance of His Prophet as a fundamental pillar of faith, warning that ignoring these dictates carries spiritual consequences; however, it also emphasizes that the Prophet's responsibility is limited to conveying the divine message clearly and truthfully, meaning that if people choose to reject the guidance despite its clarity, the accountability for that refusal rests solely upon them, not on the Messenger who has fulfilled his duty.

translation: There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteousness for what they have consumed [in the past] if they [now] fear Allah and believe and do righteous deeds, then fear Allah and believe, and then fear Allah and do good; and Allah loves the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse clarifies that the prohibition of certain things, such as intoxicants or gambling, does not retrospectively condemn those who consumed them before the prohibition was revealed, provided they maintain sincerity in their faith, piety, and constant striving for excellence in their worship and conduct, as Allah encompasses with His love those who perfect their deeds and demonstrate profound devotion in every stage of their spiritual growth.

translation: O you who have believed, Allah will surely test you with something of the game that your hands and your spears [can] reach, that Allah may make evident those who fear Him unseen. And whoever transgresses after that - for him is a painful punishment.
interpretation: Allah tests the faith and sincerity of the believers during the state of Ihram by placing within their easy reach animals that are prohibited to hunt; this serves as a trial to distinguish those who truly hold Allah in awe and refrain from disobedience even when there is no human authority watching them, demonstrating that their fear of Allah is rooted in their hearts rather than motivated by the fear of being seen by others.

translation: O you who have believed, do not kill game while you are in the state of ihram. And whoever of you kills it intentionally - the penalty is an equivalent from sacrificial animals to what he killed, as judged by two just men among you as an offering delivered to the Ka'bah, or an expiation: the feeding of needy people, or the equivalent of that in fasting, so that he may taste the consequence of his deed. Allah has pardoned what is past; but whoever returns to it, Allah will take retribution from him. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Owner of Retribution.
interpretation: This verse establishes a sacred boundary for the pilgrim, emphasizing that the sanctity of the state of ihram demands a respectful distance from harming living creatures, as a test of one's discipline and submission to divine law. By mandating a penalty for the intentional killing of game, the Lawgiver does not merely seek compensation, but intends for the offender to experience a profound sense of remorse and consequence, ensuring that the spiritual state of pilgrimage remains untainted by aggression or disregard for life. The provision of options for expiation highlights the divine mercy in offering avenues for rectification, while the stern warning against recidivism underscores that defiance of Allah’s commands, after having been pardoned, constitutes a grave transgression that invites divine justice.

translation: Lawful to you is game from the sea and its food as provision for you and the travelers, but forbidden to you is game from the land as long as you are in the state of Ihram. And fear Allah to whom you will be gathered.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine legislative exemption that permits the consumption and hunting of marine life for pilgrims and non-pilgrims alike, highlighting the benevolence of Allah in providing sustenance. However, it simultaneously imposes a strict prohibition on hunting terrestrial animals for those currently in the state of Ihram—the sacred state for Hajj or Umrah—to emphasize the sanctity of that spiritual condition and to test the believer's commitment to divine restrictions. The conclusion serves as a moral anchor, reminding the believers that their ultimate accountability rests with Allah, who will gather all of creation to Himself, thereby framing the adherence to these laws not merely as ritual obedience but as a prerequisite for spiritual readiness for the afterlife.

translation: Allah has made the Ka'bah, the Sacred House, a standing for the people, as well as the Sacred Month, the sacrificial animals, and the garlands. That is so you may know that Allah knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth, and that Allah is, of all things, Knowing.
interpretation: The establishment of the Sacred House and the prescribed rituals serves as a vital foundation for human society, both spiritually and worldly, ensuring peace and order among people. By designating specific times, places, and symbols of devotion as sacrosanct, Allah demonstrates His divine wisdom and absolute knowledge of all existence, reminding humanity that His legislative guidance is rooted in a comprehensive understanding of the cosmic order and the needs of His creation.

translation: Know that Allah is severe in punishment and that Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: This verse serves as a spiritual balance for the believer, urging them to maintain a state of consciousness between fear of Allah’s justice for those who persist in wrongdoing and hope in His vast mercy for those who repent and return to Him; it emphasizes that while Allah possesses the absolute power to punish the defiant, His essential nature is defined by forgiveness and mercy, inviting the servant to seek His grace rather than succumb to despair or arrogance.

translation: The Messenger is not responsible except for [the] notification. And Allah knows what you reveal and what you conceal.
interpretation: The Messenger's duty is strictly limited to conveying the divine message clearly and truthfully to humanity, leaving the acceptance or rejection of that guidance to the free will of individuals, while Allah, in His absolute omniscience, remains fully aware of both the outward actions that people manifest and the hidden intentions or secrets they keep within their hearts, ensuring that everyone will ultimately be held accountable for their choices.

translation: Say, 'Not equal are the evil and the good, although the abundance of the evil might impress you.' So fear Allah, O you of understanding, that you may be successful.
interpretation: This verse establishes that moral worth is determined by quality and purity rather than mere quantity or outward appeal. It serves as a directive to believers that they should not be deceived by the prevalence or popularity of falsehood, corruption, or vice, as these carry no intrinsic value in the eyes of God. True success and righteousness are reserved for those who possess the intellectual and spiritual depth to discern the truth and maintain piety regardless of how many people may be acting in opposition to it.

translation: O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they are shown to you, will distress you. But if you ask about them while the Qur'an is being revealed, they will be shown to you. Allah has pardoned that which is past; and Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine prohibition against excessive and inquisitive questioning regarding matters that have not been explicitly legislated, as the revelation of such answers might impose additional burdens or restrictions upon the believers that they would find difficult to fulfill. It teaches the faithful to embrace the ease provided by the silence of the Lawgiver, emphasizing that whatever God has not mentioned is an act of mercy and pardon, and that one should focus on practicing what is clear rather than speculating about the unknown.

translation: A people before you had asked such questions, then they became disbelievers in them.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning against the tendency of inquisitive minds to demand unnecessary details, miracles, or complex rulings regarding divine matters that are beyond human comprehension or practical necessity; by highlighting that past nations faced destruction or disbelief precisely because they persisted in questioning their prophets out of defiance or intellectual arrogance rather than genuine spiritual guidance, the Qur'an underscores that true faith rests on submission to God's revealed wisdom rather than speculative inquiry that leads to rejection when the answers fail to align with personal desires.

translation: Allah has not instituted [the custom of] bahirah, nor sa'ibah, nor wasilah, nor ham. But those who disbelieve invent falsehood about Allah, and most of them do not use reason.
interpretation: This verse addresses and invalidates the superstitious practices of the pre-Islamic Arabs, who would dedicate certain livestock to their idols by prohibiting their use, shearing, or consumption, falsely attributing these restrictions to divine law. Allah clarifies that He never legislated such prohibitions, thereby exposing the claims of the disbelievers as fabrications and highlighting that their persistence in these rituals stems from a failure to employ their intellect to recognize the oneness of Allah and the true purpose of their creation.

translation: And when it is said to them, 'Come to what Allah has revealed and to the Messenger,' they say, 'Sufficient for us is that upon which we found our fathers.' Even though their fathers knew nothing, nor were they guided?
interpretation: This verse censures those who reject the clear guidance of Allah and His Messenger by blindly clinging to the customs and traditions of their ancestors. It highlights the foolishness of prioritizing human precedents over divine revelation, especially when those ancestors lacked both knowledge of the truth and true guidance, thereby warning against the intellectual stagnation and spiritual blindness that come from rejecting the light of faith in favor of inherited ignorance.

translation: O you who have believed, upon you is [responsibility for] yourselves. Those who have gone astray will not harm you when you have been guided. To Allah is your return all together; then He will inform you of what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse serves as a directive for believers to prioritize their own spiritual rectitude and commitment to guidance over the failures of others. It clarifies that a person's ultimate accountability lies in their own adherence to the path of Allah, and that if a believer remains steadfast in righteousness and truth, the deviant behavior or disbelief of those around them will not impair their spiritual standing or hinder their salvation, as the final judgment rests solely with Allah who will judge every soul based on its own deeds.

translation: O you who have believed, testimony among you when death approaches one of you at the time of bequest should be two just men from among you or two from others if you are traveling through the land and the affliction of death befalls you. Detain them both after the prayer, and let them swear by Allah if you doubt, 'We will not exchange our oath for a price, even if he should be a near relative, and we will not conceal the testimony of Allah. Indeed, if we did, we would surely be among the sinful.'
interpretation: This verse establishes a legal framework for witnessing wills, emphasizing the absolute necessity of integrity and impartiality in bearing testimony. It dictates that when a person is nearing death while traveling and cannot find witnesses from their own community, they may appoint two trustworthy individuals from elsewhere. The requirement to swear an oath after prayer underscores the gravity of the act, serving as a spiritual safeguard to prevent witnesses from succumbing to nepotism, bribery, or the concealment of truth, thereby ensuring justice is upheld even in the most personal and critical matters of legacy.

translation: But if it is discovered that those two have become guilty of sin [i.e., perjury], then two others shall stand in their place from those who have a claim against the first two—the nearest [of kin]—and they shall swear by Allah, 'Our testimony is truer than their testimony, and we have not transgressed; indeed, if we did, we would then be among the wrongdoers.'
interpretation: This verse establishes a legal mechanism to prevent injustice in cases of inheritance or contested wills when there is suspicion of deceit by the witnesses. It dictates that if it later becomes apparent that the original witnesses lied, the heirs of the deceased—those most entitled to the truth of the matter—are empowered to provide counter-testimony under oath. By swearing that their account is more truthful and invoking the consequences of being among the wrongdoers if they lie, these heirs act as a secondary layer of judicial protection to ensure that the rightful inheritance is preserved and the truth is upheld before Allah.

translation: That is more likely to ensure that they give the testimony in its true form, or else they would fear that other oaths might be taken after their own oaths. And fear Allah and listen. And Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.
interpretation: This command aims to prevent the corruption of testimony by emphasizing that requiring witnesses to swear an oath before their testimony, and reminding them of the consequence that their testimony could be refuted or their integrity questioned by subsequent oaths, serves as a psychological and moral deterrent against falsehood; it compels the witness to uphold the truth out of fear that their dishonesty would be exposed and their character disgraced before the community and before Allah.

translation: On the Day when Allah will gather the messengers and say, 'What was the response you received?' They will say, 'We have no knowledge. Indeed, it is You who is the Knower of the unseen.'
