interpretation: This verse depicts the profound awe and humility of the messengers on the Day of Judgment; when asked about the response of their nations, they deflect the question back to Allah's absolute omniscience. Their answer signifies that while they witnessed the outward actions of their people, the true state of their hearts, their hidden sincerity, or their final internal rejection is known only to Allah, acknowledging that His knowledge encompasses the unseen realities that transcend human perception.

translation: When Allah will say, 'O Jesus, son of Mary, remember My favor upon you and upon your mother when I supported you with the Pure Spirit and you spoke to the people in the cradle and in maturity; and when I taught you writing and wisdom and the Torah and the Gospel; and when you designed from clay like the form of a bird with My permission, then you breathed into it, and it became a bird with My permission; and you healed the blind and the leper with My permission; and when you brought forth the dead with My permission; and when I restrained the Children of Israel from you when you brought them clear proofs and those who disbelieved among them said, 'This is not but obvious magic.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine reminder to Jesus (Isa) of the unique manifest signs and miraculous powers granted to him by Allah, emphasizing that all these extraordinary deeds—such as speaking in infancy, shaping clay into living birds, healing the incurable, and raising the dead—were performed strictly by the will and permission of God, thereby invalidating any claims of divinity for Jesus and refuting the accusations of sorcery leveled against him by the disbelievers who rejected his clear proofs.

translation: And when I inspired the disciples to believe in Me and My messenger, they said, 'We have believed, and bear witness that we are Muslims [in submission to Allah].'
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine guidance granted to the companions of Jesus, emphasizing that their faith was not merely a personal conviction but a result of Allah's inspiration, leading them to explicitly testify to their total submission and adherence to the message of monotheism.

translation: When the disciples said, 'O Jesus, son of Mary, is your Lord able to send down to us a table spread [with food] from the heaven?' [Jesus] said, 'Fear Allah, if you should be believers.'
interpretation: Jesus urges his disciples to maintain reverence for God and to refrain from demanding miracles as a condition for their belief, as asking for supernatural signs to prove God's power is an act that implies a lack of complete trust in His sovereignty and wisdom, which is the hallmark of true faith.

translation: They said, 'We wish to eat from it so that our hearts may be reassured, and we may know that you have spoken the truth to us, and that we may be among those who witness it.'
interpretation: The disciples of Jesus expressed that witnessing a divine miracle in the form of a table spread with food would elevate their faith from the level of intellectual acceptance to the certainty of direct observation, thereby strengthening their conviction in his prophethood and providing them with tangible evidence to testify to the truth before others.

translation: Said Isa, the son of Maryam, 'O Allah, our Lord, send down to us a table spread with food from the heaven to be for us a festival for the first of us and the last of us and a sign from You. And provide for us, and You are the best of providers.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the sincere supplication of Prophet Isa (Jesus) to Allah, invoking Him through His divine lordship to provide sustenance as a miraculous manifestation of His omnipotence. By asking for the table to be a 'festival' for both the early and later generations, Isa intended for the event to serve as a perpetual reminder and a tangible proof of divine support, reinforcing the faith of his followers and underscoring that all true provision comes from Allah, the Sustainer, whose generosity surpasses all others.

translation: Allah said, 'Indeed, I will send it down to you, but whoever among you disbelieves after that, I will punish him with a punishment by which I have not punished anyone among the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gravity of witnessing a direct, miraculous sign from Allah; when a community is granted an explicit divine favor or evidence they requested, the moral responsibility of that community increases significantly, such that rejecting the truth thereafter constitutes a level of arrogance and defiance so extreme that it warrants a severity of punishment unmatched in history, serving as a final warning against the ingratitude of those who turn away after receiving clear enlightenment.

translation: And [beware the Day] when Allah will say, 'O Jesus, Son of Mary, did you say to the people, Take me and my mother as deities besides Allah?' He will say, 'Exalted are You! It was not for me to say that to which I have no right. If I had said it, You would have known it. You know what is within myself, and I do not know what is within Yourself. Indeed, it is You who is Knower of the unseen.'
interpretation: In this dialogue, Jesus (peace be upon him) responds to Allah's inquiry with profound humility and absolute disavowal of divinity, clarifying that he never commanded his followers to worship him or his mother. He emphasizes that if he had uttered such a false claim, Allah, who possesses complete knowledge of all hidden matters and internal thoughts, would undoubtedly be aware of it. By stating 'You know what is within myself, and I do not know what is within Yourself,' Jesus acknowledges the infinite gulf between the created human messenger and the divine nature of the Creator, asserting that human knowledge is limited to what is manifested, whereas Allah's knowledge encompasses all that is concealed.

translation: I said not to them except what You commanded me: 'Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord.' And I was a witness over them as long as I was among them; but when You took me up, You were the Observer over them, and You are, over all things, Witness.
interpretation: In this verse, Prophet Isa (Jesus) declares his absolute fidelity to the divine mission, clarifying that his message was purely monotheistic and devoid of any claim to divinity for himself. By stating that he was a witness only during his presence among them, he places the ultimate responsibility of monitoring his followers' subsequent deviations or adherence to the truth solely upon Allah, who remains the ever-watchful Guardian and Witness over every human action, past and present.

translation: If You should punish them, indeed they are Your servants; but if You forgive them, indeed it is You who is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse represents Prophet Isa's (Jesus) final plea to Allah on the Day of Judgment. It highlights total submission to the Divine Will, emphasizing that since these people are Allah's creation, their fate rests entirely in His hands. The appeal to 'The Exalted in Might' and 'The Wise' suggests that if Allah chooses to forgive, it is not out of weakness or indifference to justice, but an act of supreme authority and perfect wisdom, acknowledging that only He possesses the absolute knowledge to judge whether His servants deserve mercy or punishment.

translation: Allah will say, 'This is the Day when the truthful will benefit from their truthfulness. For them are gardens [in Paradise] beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever, Allah being pleased with them, and they with Him. That is the great attainment.'
interpretation: This verse underscores that on the Day of Judgment, the ultimate measure of success is the integrity and sincerity (sidq) one maintained throughout their earthly life, particularly in their devotion and obedience to Allah. The reward of Paradise is not merely a physical paradise but a state of divine contentment where the relationship between the Creator and the created is perfected; Allah is pleased with their deeds, and they are fully satisfied with His judgment and generosity, which represents the highest possible achievement for a human soul.

translation: To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is within them. And He is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse establishes that Allah is the absolute Owner and Sovereign of the entire universe, encompassing both the physical heavens, the earth, and everything contained within them. It emphasizes that since all existence belongs to Him, He alone holds the authority to command, forbid, and decree. The concluding declaration of His omnipotence serves as a reminder that because He created and owns all things, there is no limitation to His power, and He is fully capable of executing His will over every aspect of creation without exception.

translation: All praise is due to Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and made the darkness and the light; yet those who disbelieve equate others with their Lord.
interpretation: The verse highlights the absolute power and unique sovereignty of Allah in creating the physical universe with all its contrasts, while simultaneously exposing the irrationality of those who reject the truth; despite witnessing the clear signs of His singular creative authority, these individuals persist in associating partners with Him, effectively placing created beings on the same level of reverence as the Creator who brought everything into existence.

translation: It is He who created you from clay and then decreed a term and a specified time with Him; then you are still in doubt.
interpretation: Allah reminds humanity of their humble physical origins from clay to emphasize His absolute power, contrasting this with the two types of appointed times: the span of an individual's life in this world and the fixed time known only to Allah for the Day of Resurrection, thereby rebuking those who continue to harbor doubts regarding their accountability and the inevitable return to their Creator.

translation: And He is Allah, [the only deity] within the heavens and on the earth. He knows your secret and what you make public, and He knows that which you earn.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute Oneness and omnipresence of Allah, asserting that His divinity is acknowledged and manifest throughout the heavens and the earth. It highlights His infinite knowledge, suggesting that since nothing in the hidden depths of the human heart or the open declarations of life escapes His awareness, individuals should live with the constant realization that every action and intention is recorded by the One who sustains all existence.

translation: And no sign comes to them from the signs of their Lord except that they turn away from it.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubbornness of the disbelievers who, despite witnessing clear divine proofs and miraculous signs manifesting the truth of God's message, persist in their arrogance and willful ignorance, choosing to ignore the evidence rather than reflect upon it and accept the guidance provided by their Creator.

translation: They have indeed denied the truth when it came to them, so there will soon reach them the news of what they used to mock.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning that rejecting the manifest truth, which has been presented with clear evidence, is not a matter that will go unaddressed; rather, those who chose to ridicule the divine message will inevitably encounter the harsh reality and consequences of the very things they once treated with disdain and mockery.

translation: Do they not see how many generations We destroyed before them whom We had established in the earth with that which We did not give you? And We sent the heaven upon them in [showers of] rain and made the rivers flow beneath them; then We destroyed them for their sins and brought forth after them another generation.
interpretation: The verse serves as a stern admonition to the disbelievers of the Prophet's time, reminding them that worldly prosperity, vast authority, and bountiful natural resources are not signs of divine favor, but rather tests; when civilizations become arrogant, indulge in transgression, and persist in disobedience despite their immense blessings, God's justice manifests in their total annihilation, proving that material success provides no protection against divine decree when morality and faith are abandoned.

translation: And even if We had sent down to you a writing on a parchment and they had touched it with their hands, those who disbelieve would still say, 'This is nothing but clear magic.'
interpretation: The verse illustrates the persistent state of stubbornness and spiritual blindness inherent in those who reject the truth; it indicates that their disbelief does not stem from a genuine lack of evidence or divine proof, but from an inner arrogance and a refusal to submit to guidance, such that even if they were granted the most undeniable, tangible miracle—like a book descending from the heavens that they could touch—their hearts would remain hardened, leading them to dismiss the supernatural sign as mere sorcery rather than accepting it as the word of God.

translation: And they say, 'Why was there not sent down to him an angel?' But if We had sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided; then they would not be reprieved.
interpretation: The disbelievers were persistently demanding a tangible, supernatural sign like the descent of an angel to confirm the prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him). Allah explains that their request was not born of a sincere search for truth but rather of arrogance and stubbornness. He clarifies that if He were to fulfill their demand by sending an angel, the divine decree for their destruction would have been immediately finalized upon their continued rejection, granting them no further time or opportunity to repent, as the finality of their denial would have been established by witnessing such a manifest miracle.

translation: And if We had made him an angel, We would have made him a man, and We would have covered them with that in which they cover themselves.
interpretation: Allah explains that if He were to send an angel as a messenger to human beings, He would manifest that angel in the form of a man so that they could interact with him and understand his speech, yet this would inevitably lead to the same confusion they already suffer from, as they would still struggle to distinguish the divine message from their own human perceptions and doubts.

translation: And certainly were messengers ridiculed before you, but those who mocked them were encompassed by that which they used to ridicule.
interpretation: This verse serves as a source of solace for the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his followers, reminding them that the mockery and persecution they faced were not unique experiences; rather, the historical pattern of arrogance among disbelievers ensures that their disdain will ultimately return to destroy them, as the divine decree holds that the outcome of their own scorn shall be their downfall and punishment.

translation: Say, 'Travel through the land; then observe how was the end of the deniers.'
interpretation: The verse commands the Prophet to invite people to travel through the earth and study the historical remnants of past nations who rejected divine truth, emphasizing that observing their ruins serves as a clear lesson that disobedience and arrogance inevitably lead to destruction, thereby urging people to reflect on these patterns to avoid meeting a similar fate.

translation: Say, 'To whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and earth?' Say, 'To Allah.' He has decreed upon Himself mercy. He will surely assemble you for the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt. Those who will have lost themselves [that is, lost their own souls] do not believe.
interpretation: Allah commands His Prophet to declare that all existence belongs solely to Him, emphasizing His absolute sovereignty and ownership. By stating that He has decreed mercy upon Himself, Allah assures His creation that His compassion precedes His wrath, serving as a fundamental promise that His actions are guided by benevolence rather than cruelty. The certainty of the Day of Resurrection is presented as an inevitable gathering where truth will be made manifest. The loss referred to for those who do not believe is the ultimate bankruptcy of the soul, where, through their persistent refusal to accept the truth, they have rendered their own essence devoid of value and faith, thereby depriving themselves of the eternal mercy they were invited to accept.

translation: And to Him belongs whatever dwells in the night and the day, and He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse asserts that the entirety of creation, including all living beings and inanimate objects that reside or exist within the cycles of time, belongs exclusively to God. By emphasizing His attributes as the All-Hearing and the All-Knowing, the Qur'an highlights that no movement or stillness, regardless of how hidden or quiet it may be, escapes His divine perception, affirming His absolute sovereignty and omnipresence over all existence.

translation: Say, 'Is it other than Allah I should take as a protector, [He who is] the Creator of the heavens and the earth, while it is He who feeds and is not fed?' Say, 'Indeed, I have been commanded to be the first [among you] who submits [to Allah] and do not ever be of the polytheists.'
interpretation: This verse establishes that Allah alone is the rightful object of worship and devotion because He is the sole Originator of the cosmos and the Provider of all sustenance; to seek patronage or protection from anyone else is a rejection of the logical truth that the Sustainer of all creation does not depend on any created being for His own existence or authority, and therefore, the Prophet is commanded to declare his absolute monotheism as a model for all believers to reject any form of partnership with God.

translation: Say, 'Indeed I fear, if I should disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous Day.'
interpretation: The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, is commanded to declare that he holds a profound reverence and fear for Allah, acknowledging that even for a Messenger, the path to salvation lies in absolute submission to the divine commands; thus, he highlights the gravity of the Day of Judgment, asserting that the prospect of facing God's justice without having fulfilled one's obligations is a terrifying reality that keeps him steadfast in obedience.

translation: He who is spared from the punishment on that Day, [Allah] has surely granted him mercy. And that is the clear triumph.
interpretation: This verse highlights that the ultimate success and true achievement for any human being on the Day of Judgment is not merely the accumulation of worldly possessions or status, but rather being shielded by Allah from the impending retribution. It signifies that salvation from the fire and the attainment of divine grace is the greatest victory one can ever attain, as all other worldly gains pale in comparison to the eternal security and mercy granted by the Creator.

translation: And if Allah should touch you with adversity, there is no remover of it except Him; and if He intends for you good, then there is no repeller of His bounty. He causes it to reach whom He wills of His servants. And He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all occurrences of harm or benefit in a person's life are subject solely to the decree and power of Allah, highlighting that He alone possesses the authority to withhold or bestow blessings, and therefore one should turn exclusively to Him in times of distress and acknowledge His absolute sovereignty over all affairs.

translation: And He is the Subduer over His servants, and He is the Wise, the Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah’s absolute dominion and supreme authority over all creation, indicating that everything is subject to His power and under His perfect control, while simultaneously affirming that His management of the universe is characterized by His profound wisdom and His exhaustive, intimate knowledge of all hidden and manifest matters.

translation: Say, 'What thing is greatest in testimony?' Say, 'Allah is witness between me and you. And this Qur'an was revealed to me that I may warn you thereby and whomever it reaches. Do you truly testify that there are other deities with Allah?' Say, 'I will not testify [so].' Say, 'Indeed, He is but one God, and indeed, I am free of what you associate [with Him].'
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that the ultimate authority and witness to the truth of the Prophet’s message is Allah Himself, whose testimony surpasses all others. By declaring that the Quran is a warning to all whom it reaches, it asserts the universality of the message, challenging the polytheists to abandon their false gods and recognize the absolute oneness of the Creator, while simultaneously distancing the Prophet from their idolatrous practices.

translation: Those to whom We have given the Scripture recognize it as they recognize their own sons. But those who will have lost themselves [that is, lost their own souls] do not believe.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that the people of the Book, specifically the scholars among them, possess an innate and undeniable certainty regarding the truthfulness of the Prophet Muhammad and the Qur'an, based on the clear descriptions and signs contained in their own scriptures. This recognition is as vivid and indisputable as a parent's recognition of their own children. However, despite this absolute clarity and internal testimony of the truth, their persistent rejection stems from a state of spiritual ruin where their worldly desires, arrogance, and prejudices have blinded them to the point where they have effectively forfeited their own souls, rendering them incapable of accepting the guidance that they know in their hearts to be true.

translation: And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie about Allah or denies His verses? Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the extreme gravity of two specific sins: fabricating falsehoods against the Creator—such as falsely attributing laws or partners to Him—and rejecting the manifest signs and guidance He has provided. By framing these actions as the pinnacle of injustice, the Qur'an highlights that such people sever their connection to the ultimate truth, thereby ensuring their own spiritual failure and exclusion from divine prosperity in both this life and the hereafter, as they have effectively blocked themselves from the path of success.

translation: And the Day We will gather them all together, then We will say to those who associated others with Allah, 'Where are your 'partners' whom you used to claim?'
interpretation: On the Day of Resurrection, Allah will assemble all of creation, from the first to the last, and publicly confront the polytheists by asking them to produce the idols, deities, or intercessors they once falsely claimed to be partners to Allah, so that it may become clear to everyone that these entities possess no power, authority, or existence of divinity, leaving the polytheists in a state of utter helplessness and humiliation.

translation: Then their excuse will be only that they will say, 'By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists.'
interpretation: When the polytheists witness the truth on the Day of Resurrection and realize the futility of their past disbelief, they will attempt to deny their association of partners with Allah, hoping to escape His punishment, yet their own limbs and records will bear witness against them, revealing the falsehood of their desperate plea.

translation: See how they lied against themselves, and that which they used to invent has vanished from them.
interpretation: The verse serves as a profound reflection on the ultimate futility of disbelief and polytheism, highlighting that those who fabricate falsehoods against Allah are, in reality, only deceiving themselves and causing their own ruin. By turning away from the truth, they distance themselves from salvation, and when the reality of the Hereafter manifests, all the false deities and man-made ideologies they relied upon will disappear, leaving them unsupported and facing the consequences of their own spiritual dishonesty.

translation: And among them are those who listen to you, but We have placed coverings over their hearts, lest they understand it, and deafness in their ears. And even if they should see every sign, they would not believe in it, to the extent that when they come to you arguing with you, those who disbelieve say, 'This is not but legends of the former peoples.'
interpretation: This verse explains that the obstinacy of the disbelievers is not due to a lack of evidence, but a self-imposed spiritual blindness and deafness; because they persistently chose to reject the truth and mock the message, God sealed their hearts so that they are no longer able to grasp the profound wisdom of the revelation, rendering them incapable of belief regardless of how many miraculous signs they witness.

translation: And they forbid (others) from him and distance themselves from him. And they destroy none except their own selves, but they perceive (it) not.
interpretation: This verse describes the state of the disbelievers who actively discourage others from following the Prophet Muhammad while simultaneously avoiding his teachings themselves. The divine wisdom here highlights a paradoxical self-destruction; by rejecting the source of their own salvation, they are not actually harming the Prophet or the message, but are instead isolating themselves from eternal success, all while remaining oblivious to the fact that their opposition is a form of spiritual suicide.

translation: If you could but see when they are made to stand before the Fire and say, 'Oh, would that we could be returned [to life on earth], and not deny the signs of our Lord and be among the believers.'
interpretation: This verse depicts the state of deep regret and longing experienced by the disbelievers when they are confronted with the reality of the Hellfire, realizing that their rejection of divine truth in the worldly life was a catastrophic error; they plead for a second chance not out of genuine belief, but out of the sheer terror and absolute certainty of their impending punishment, illustrating the tragic futility of seeking repentance after the veil of the unseen has been lifted and the opportunity for trial has passed.

translation: But what they had concealed before has become manifest to them; and even if they were returned, they would certainly revert to that which they were forbidden, and indeed, they are liars.
interpretation: This verse reveals the inherent nature of those who persistently reject the truth: even if they were granted a second chance at life after witnessing the reality of the afterlife, they would inevitably choose to disobey God again. Their inherent corruption and pattern of deception are so deeply rooted that they would immediately return to their previous sinful conduct, proving that their claim of desiring to do good if given another chance is entirely insincere.

translation: And they say, 'There is none but our worldly life, and we will not be resurrected.'
interpretation: This verse portrays the disbelief of those who reject the afterlife, asserting that existence is confined solely to the material life experienced on Earth and denying the possibility of being brought back to life by Allah after death, thus demonstrating their reliance on empirical sensory perception while ignoring the spiritual truth of accountability.

translation: If you could only see when they are made to stand before their Lord! He will say, 'Is this not the truth?' They will say, 'Yes, by our Lord.' He will say, 'Then taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve.'
interpretation: This verse portrays a moment of absolute, undeniable clarity for the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment, where their previous denial of resurrection and accountability is stripped away; by making them affirm the truth of the afterlife before their Lord, Allah demonstrates that their punishment is not an act of injustice, but a direct and inevitable consequence of their conscious choice to reject the truth during their worldly life.

translation: Those who denied the meeting with Allah have certainly lost, until when the Hour comes upon them unexpectedly, they will say, 'Oh, our regret over what we neglected concerning it,' while they bear their burdens on their backs. Unquestionably, evil is that which they bear.
interpretation: This verse portrays the profound remorse of those who rejected the reality of the afterlife when they are suddenly confronted with the Hour of Judgment. Their regret stems from having spent their worldly lives in heedlessness and disbelief, treating the inevitable encounter with their Creator as a falsehood. The imagery of them carrying their 'burdens on their backs' serves as a literal and metaphorical manifestation of their sinful deeds and neglect, emphasizing that the weight of their own choices—the evil they have accumulated—becomes an inescapable punishment that they must personally carry and account for in the hereafter.

translation: And the worldly life is not but amusement and diversion; but the home of the Hereafter is best for those who fear Allah, so will you not then reason?
interpretation: The verse clarifies that the transitory pleasures of this world—such as wealth, status, and sensory enjoyments—are akin to the trivial games of children because they lack lasting substance and purpose. It contrasts this fleeting existence with the afterlife, which is the true, permanent reality. The focus on 'those who fear Allah' (the God-conscious) highlights that the true value of life is found in righteousness and moral conduct, as these are the only investments that yield eternal rewards, urging the intellect to recognize that prioritizing the temporary over the eternal is an irrational choice.

translation: We know indeed that what they say grieves you. Yet, it is not you that they deny, but it is the verses of Allah that the wrongdoers reject.
interpretation: This verse serves as a comforting address from Allah to the Prophet Muhammad, reassuring him that his distress over the polytheists' words is known and understood. It clarifies that their rejection is not born from a genuine belief that he is a liar, as they themselves acknowledged his integrity and truthfulness, but rather from their persistent arrogance and deliberate denial of the manifest signs and divine truths revealed by Allah, which blinds them from accepting the message despite their inner certainty of the Prophet's honesty.

translation: And certainly were messengers denied before you, but they were patient over what they were denied, and they were harmed until Our victory came to them. And none can alter the words of Allah. And there has certainly come to you some information about the messengers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a source of consolation for the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), reminding him that he is not unique in facing rejection or persecution. Allah emphasizes that the path of the prophets is inherently one of trial, requiring steadfast patience ('sabr') in the face of mockery and physical abuse. By linking the Prophet's struggle to the historical precedent of those who came before him, the verse confirms that Allah's promise of divine support and ultimate victory is an immutable law of nature and history, which will inevitably manifest in due time as it did for the messengers of the past.

translation: And if their aversion is difficult for you, then if you are able to seek a tunnel into the earth or a stairway into the sky to bring them a sign, [then do so]. But if Allah had willed, He would have gathered them upon guidance. So never be among the ignorant.
interpretation: The verse serves as a profound consolation to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), emphasizing that his duty is merely to convey the message, not to compel belief. It highlights that the choice to believe rests with the individuals and that Allah, had He willed to coerce mankind into faith, could have easily done so by creating them with an innate nature incapable of disbelief. The command not to be among the ignorant is a reminder to accept the divine wisdom behind human free will, rather than being consumed by the sorrow caused by the stubborn rejection of the disbelievers.

translation: Only those who listen will respond. As for the dead, Allah will resurrect them; then to Him they will be returned.
interpretation: The verse draws a contrast between those who possess living, receptive hearts—who truly listen to the truth and accept it—and those who are spiritually dead, whose hearts are so hardened that they resemble the deceased in their inability to respond to guidance. It serves as a reminder that although the disbelievers may be physically alive, they are spiritually unresponsive, yet they cannot escape the inevitable reality of resurrection and the final accountability before Allah, who has the power to restore life to the dead just as He causes the truth to reach the living.

translation: And they say, 'Why has a sign not been sent down to him from his Lord?' Say, 'Indeed, Allah is able to send down a sign, but most of them do not know.'
interpretation: The disbelievers demanded physical miracles of their own choosing to validate the Prophet's message, yet the verse explains that while Allah possesses the absolute power to manifest any sign, He does not respond to such challenges because the obstinate nature of these people is rooted in ignorance; they fail to realize that if a sign were sent and they still refused to believe, it would only hasten their own destruction, or that the Quran itself is the greatest, all-encompassing miracle that demands intellectual reflection rather than sensory spectacle.

translation: But those who deny Our verses are deaf and dumb within darknesses. Whomever Allah wills - He lets go astray, and whomever He wills - He puts on a straight path.
interpretation: This verse illustrates that those who deliberately reject the truth of divine revelation distance themselves from guidance so thoroughly that they lose the ability to hear the truth or speak it, becoming trapped in a state of spiritual blindness and ignorance. Ultimately, this state of being is a result of Allah's law of causality; those who persist in rejection and arrogance are left to wander in their own confusion, while those who seek the truth with sincerity are granted the divine grace of being firmly established on the straight path.

translation: Say, 'Have you considered: if the punishment of Allah should come to you or the Hour should come to you - is it other than Allah you would invoke, if you should be truthful?'
interpretation: This verse serves as a profound challenge to those who associate partners with Allah, highlighting the natural instinct of human beings to turn exclusively to the Creator during moments of ultimate crisis and unavoidable destruction. By posing this rhetorical question, the Qur'an exposes the hypocrisy of polytheism, demonstrating that when all worldly means and false deities fail to provide security or escape from divine retribution, the heart instinctively recognizes the Oneness of Allah and acknowledges that He alone possesses the power to grant relief or salvation.

translation: Rather, Him alone you call upon, and He removes that for which you supplicated Him if He wills, and you forget what you associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inherent nature of human beings to instinctively turn to the One true God during times of desperate distress and overwhelming calamity, casting aside all false deities and idols they once worshiped; it illustrates that when a person is faced with a hardship that no created being can remove, the mask of polytheism falls away, and the soul naturally recognizes the absolute power and sovereignty of Allah to grant relief, proving that reliance on partners is merely a distraction from the fundamental truth recognized by the human heart.

translation: And We have already sent to nations before you, then We seized them with poverty and hardship that perhaps they might humble themselves.
interpretation: This verse illustrates that Allah sends trials, such as poverty and physical suffering, to past nations not merely as a form of punishment, but as a divine strategy to soften their hearts and incite them toward humility, repentance, and turning back to God in sincere prayer.

translation: Then why, when Our punishment came to them, did they not humble themselves? But their hearts became hardened, and Satan made attractive to them that which they were doing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the tragedy of human arrogance in the face of divine warnings; when people are confronted with the consequences of their transgressions, they often fail to turn to God in sincerity because their hearts have become calloused by persistent sin, creating a state of spiritual blindness where the devil successfully masks their destructive behavior as something noble or justified.

translation: So when they forgot that by which they had been reminded, We opened to them the doors of every thing, until, when they rejoiced in that which they were given, We seized them suddenly, and they were then in despair.
interpretation: This verse warns against the deception of worldly prosperity when it is granted to those who have turned away from God’s guidance; it explains that such abundance is not a sign of divine pleasure, but rather a trial of 'istidraj' (gradual drawing in), where the continued blessings serve to increase their arrogance and distract them further from the truth until their punishment comes unexpectedly, leaving them completely hopeless and cut off from all mercy.

translation: So the last remnant of the people who committed wrong was cut off. And praise to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse signifies the ultimate triumph of divine justice over systemic oppression; when a society persists in tyranny and rejects all calls to truth, God intervenes to eradicate the roots of such corruption, establishing a balance that restores peace to the earth and prompts the believers to acknowledge that such restoration is an act of divine mercy and sovereignty deserving of eternal gratitude.

translation: Say, 'Have you considered: if Allah should take away your hearing and your sight and set a seal upon your hearts, which deity other than Allah could bring them back to you?' Look how We diversify the verses; then they turn away.
interpretation: This verse serves as a profound challenge to human arrogance, reminding individuals that their most essential sensory faculties and cognitive abilities are not self-generated but are gifts from the Creator, which He can revoke at any moment. By questioning who could restore these capabilities if Allah were to withdraw them, the Qur'an aims to dismantle the false sense of self-sufficiency that leads human beings to arrogance and disbelief. The reference to 'turning away' highlights the willful blindness of those who persist in ignoring these signs despite the clear, multifaceted demonstrations of Divine power and grace provided to them.

translation: Say, 'Have you considered: if the punishment of Allah should come to you suddenly or openly, will any be destroyed except the wrongdoing people?'
interpretation: This verse serves as a rhetorical challenge to the polytheists, emphasizing that divine retribution is not an arbitrary act, but a consequence of persistent injustice and disbelief; it asserts that when Allah's punishment arrives—whether unexpectedly or predictably—its target is strictly limited to those who have transgressed against the truth and committed wrong, thereby warning the listeners that their continued rejection of the message places them directly in the category of those destined for destruction.

translation: And We send not the messengers except as bringers of good tidings and warners. So whoever believes and reforms, there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: The verse clarifies that the mission of the prophets is confined to delivering a dual message: hope for those who follow the path of righteousness and warning for those who stray. It emphasizes that salvation is conditional upon two essential pillars: true faith in the heart, which acknowledges the oneness of God, and righteous conduct that manifests in practical deeds. When these two elements are united, the believer is granted divine security, shielding them from the anxieties of the future and the sorrows of the past, as their ultimate destination is marked by peace and divine acceptance.

translation: But those who deny Our verses - the punishment will touch them for their defiantly disobeying.
interpretation: This verse establishes the principle of divine justice: the affliction of punishment is not a random occurrence but a direct consequence of the persistent rejection of divine truth and the deliberate choice to abandon the path of obedience for a life of transgression and corruption.

translation: Say, 'I do not tell you that I possess the depositories of Allah, nor do I know the unseen, nor do I tell you that I am an angel. I only follow what is revealed to me.' Say, 'Is the blind equivalent to the seeing? Then will you not give thought?'
interpretation: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is commanded to clarify his status as a human messenger who possesses no divine powers or supernatural knowledge independent of God. He distinguishes his position from that of a deity or an angel, emphasizing that his entire authority is derived strictly from divine revelation. The comparison between the 'blind' and the 'seeing' serves as a rhetorical challenge to the disbelievers, highlighting that those who fail to recognize the truth of revelation lack spiritual insight, whereas those who follow it possess the clarity of vision necessary to understand the reality of their existence.

translation: And warn by it those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord - for them besides Him there is no protector and no intercessor - that they might become righteous.
interpretation: The verse serves as a reminder that the Quran is a source of guidance for those who possess an active conscience and fear the reality of the afterlife. By emphasizing that no human intercession or external authority will avail a person on the Day of Judgment except by God's permission, the verse urges individuals to prioritize their spiritual integrity and accountability, which in turn inspires them to adopt a lifestyle of piety and God-consciousness.

translation: And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance. Not upon you is anything of their account, and not upon them is anything of your account, so that you were to drive them away and thus become among the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine instruction to the Prophet Muhammad to maintain the dignity and inclusion of sincere believers, regardless of their social or economic status. It emphasizes that a person's worth in the sight of God is determined by their devotion and sincerity in seeking His pleasure, rather than their worldly standing. By commanding the Prophet not to reject those who humble themselves before God, the verse establishes the principle of egalitarianism in faith, reminding the leader that his responsibility is to provide spiritual guidance rather than to judge the past actions or social circumstances of the seekers, as each soul is solely responsible for its own reckoning before God.

translation: And thus We have tested some of them through others, that they might say, 'Is it these whom Allah has favored among us?' Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?
interpretation: Allah explains that He tests people by creating differences in social status, wealth, and worldly circumstances to reveal the true nature of their hearts; those who are arrogant or blind to spiritual truths look at the faithful, who are often among the poor or marginalized, and mockingly question why God would choose to guide them instead of the elite, yet Allah affirms that He possesses perfect knowledge of the hearts of those who are truly grateful and obedient, thereby validating their guidance as a result of their sincerity rather than external worldly measures.

translation: And when those who believe in Our verses come to you, say, 'Peace be upon you. Your Lord has decreed upon Himself mercy: that any of you who does wrong out of ignorance and then repents after that and corrects himself - indeed, He is Forgiving and Merciful.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine reassurance for the believers, highlighting that Allah has made mercy an essential attribute of His dominion; it teaches that since Allah has bound Himself to be merciful, He does not rush to punish those who err out of impulsiveness or lack of knowledge, provided they turn back to Him with sincere repentance and rectify their actions, as His forgiveness is boundless and His mercy encompasses all who strive to reform themselves.

translation: And thus We detail the verses, and so that the way of the criminals may become evident.
interpretation: God clarifies His commandments and signs so that the distinction between the path of faith and the path of the wicked becomes clear, ensuring that those who choose disbelief or transgression do so with full awareness of the consequences and the nature of their actions.

translation: Say, 'I have been forbidden to worship those whom you call upon besides Allah.' Say, 'I will not follow your desires, for I would then have strayed, and I would not be among the [rightly] guided.'
interpretation: The Prophet Muhammad is instructed to firmly declare his dissociation from polytheistic practices, emphasizing that his worship is directed solely to the Creator and that he will never compromise his divine guidance to appease the whims and irrational inclinations of those who reject the truth, as following such subjective desires would lead him away from the path of spiritual rectitude.

translation: Say, 'Indeed, I am on clear evidence from my Lord, and you have denied it. I do not have that for which you are impatient. The decision is only for Allah. He relates the truth, and He is the best of deciders.'
interpretation: The Prophet is instructed to declare that his message is rooted in certain, divine revelation from Allah, which serves as a manifest proof that the disbelievers have rejected despite its clarity. He clarifies that the punishment or the signs they mockingly demand to be hastened are entirely under the jurisdiction of Allah, not under his personal control. The verse emphasizes that all authority to judge between truth and falsehood rests solely with Allah, who provides the ultimate, righteous verdict and is the most excellent of all who can distinguish between right and wrong.

translation: Say, 'If I had that for which you are impatient, the matter would have been decided between me and you; but Allah is most knowing of the wrongdoers.'
interpretation: The Prophet Muhammad is instructed to clarify to the disbelievers who mockingly demand the hastening of divine punishment that he possesses no authority over the timing of such events; rather, if the power to inflict punishment rested in his hands, he would have long since executed the divine judgment upon them for their rejection of the truth, yet he must wait for Allah's predetermined timing, for Allah alone possesses perfect knowledge of who truly deserves retribution and when it is most appropriate to dispense it.

translation: And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them except Him. And He knows what is on the land and in the sea. Not a leaf falls but that He knows it. And no grain is there within the darknesses of the earth and no moist or dry [thing] but that it is [written] in a clear record.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute scope of Divine omniscience, affirming that Allah alone possesses knowledge of the unseen—matters hidden from human perception such as the future or the hidden realities of existence. By contrasting the vastness of the land and sea with the minute detail of a falling leaf or a hidden grain, the Quran illustrates that God's awareness is not merely general but encompasses every infinitesimal occurrence in the universe, asserting that every event is accounted for in a pre-ordained, comprehensive knowledge, often referred to as the 'Preserved Tablet'.

translation: And it is He who takes your souls by night and knows what you have committed by day; then He revives you therein that a specified term may be fulfilled. Then to Him will be your return; then He will inform you about what you used to do.
interpretation: Allah signifies His absolute control over the human soul by comparing the temporary state of sleep to a form of death where the soul is withdrawn, reminding humanity that their daily actions are witnessed by His infinite knowledge. He allows people to 'awaken' each day to continue their allotted lifespan until the appointed time of their final departure, emphasizing that life is a transient cycle leading inevitably to a final accountability where every deed, whether hidden in the night or manifest in the day, will be brought forth for judgment.

translation: And He is the Subjugator over His servants, and He sends over you guardian angels until, when death approaches one of you, Our messengers take his soul, and they do not neglect their duties.
interpretation: Allah emphasizes His absolute sovereignty and control over all creation, noting that He appoints angels to act as custodians and observers who meticulously record every action and word of His servants, ensuring that when the appointed time of death arrives, these celestial emissaries fulfill their mission with precise accuracy, neither delaying nor failing to carry out the decree of Allah by collecting the soul at the exact moment destined.

translation: Then they are returned to Allah, their true Lord. Unquestionably, His is the judgment, and He is the swiftest of accountants.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder to all human beings that regardless of how much autonomy or influence they may possess in this worldly life, their final destination is inevitably back to Allah, who is the sole possessor of absolute truth and sovereignty. It emphasizes that ultimate justice rests entirely with Him, and because of His perfect omniscience and power, He is capable of rendering accounts for all of creation simultaneously and instantly, leaving no deed unrecorded and no injustice unaddressed.

translation: Say, 'Who rescues you from the darknesses of the land and sea [when] you call upon Him imploringly and privately, 'If He should save us from this [crisis], we will surely be among the grateful.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a rhetorical reminder of the inherent human recognition of a Supreme Power during times of extreme peril. Allah instructs the Prophet to confront the disbelievers with their own psychological reality: when they are truly trapped by the overwhelming forces of nature—represented by the 'darknesses' of land and sea—their arrogance vanishes, and they instinctively turn to the Creator in humble supplication. They make solemn promises to be grateful if delivered, highlighting the irony that their hearts naturally incline toward monotheistic devotion when stripped of worldly distractions, only for them to forget this sincerity once they are returned to safety.

translation: Say, 'It is Allah who saves you from it and from every distress; then you still associate others with Him.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a profound indictment of the human tendency to acknowledge God's absolute sovereignty and divine intervention only during moments of extreme trial, yet immediately revert to ingratitude or polytheism once that distress has been lifted, thereby highlighting the inconsistency of the human heart that seeks the Creator in desperation but ignores Him in comfort.

translation: Say, 'He is the [all-]Powerful to send upon you punishment from above you or from beneath your feet or to confuse you with [various] sects and make you taste the violence of one another.' Look how We diversify the signs that they might understand.
interpretation: This verse warns humanity that God possesses the absolute authority to manifest His retribution through cosmic phenomena or natural disasters—represented by what comes from above or beneath—or through the social disintegration of a community, where internal conflict, sectarianism, and mutual aggression lead to the destruction of the social fabric. By showcasing these varied forms of calamity, God urges people to reflect deeply on the consequences of their deeds so that they may attain the wisdom to correct their path and return to righteousness before such divine interventions become inevitable.

translation: And your people have denied it, while it is the truth. Say, 'I am not a manager over you.'
interpretation: God instructs the Prophet Muhammad to address the stubbornness of his people by stating that their rejection of the Quran does not diminish its inherent truth; furthermore, he is commanded to distance himself from responsibility for their disbelief, clarifying that his role is merely to deliver the message clearly, while their account for their choices rests solely with God.

translation: For every news is a fixed time of settlement, and you will come to know.
interpretation: Every divine decree, prophecy, or occurrence ordained by Allah has a designated time and place where it will inevitably materialize and settle. This verse serves as a stern reminder to those who deny the truth that the consequences of their actions and the fulfillment of God's promises are not mere illusions but are scheduled events; when the appointed time arrives, the reality of these matters will be unveiled to them with absolute clarity, leaving no room for doubt or denial.

translation: And when you see those who engage in [offensive] discourse concerning Our verses, then turn away from them until they enter into another conversation. And if Satan should cause you to forget, then do not remain after the reminder with the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse establishes a principle of moral distancing from those who mock or frivolously debate the sacred signs of God. It commands the believer to dissociate from such gatherings as an act of disapproval and self-preservation, ensuring that one does not become desensitized to blasphemy or contribute to the persistence of such discourse. The instruction to leave serves as a form of social sanction, emphasizing that protecting the sanctity of divine revelation outweighs the desire to engage in futile arguments with those who have no intention of seeking the truth, while also reminding the believer that if they happen to linger out of forgetfulness, they must withdraw immediately upon realizing their error to avoid being complicit in the transgression.

translation: And those who fear Allah are not held accountable for them at all, but only for a reminder, that perhaps they will become righteous.
interpretation: The verse indicates that believers are not burdened by the sins or misdeeds of those who mock the signs of Allah, provided they distance themselves from such behavior and do not participate in it; rather, their responsibility is limited to providing counsel and reminding others of the truth so that they might turn away from their transgression and attain piety.

translation: And leave those who take their religion as amusement and diversion and whom the worldly life has deluded. But remind with the Qur'an, lest a soul be given up to destruction for what it earned; it will have besides Allah no protector and no intercessor. And if it should offer every compensation, it would not be taken from it. Those are the ones who are given to destruction for what they have earned. For them will be a drink of scalding water and a painful punishment because they used to disbelieve.
interpretation: The verse commands the Prophet and the believers to distance themselves from those who treat the sanctity of faith as a trivial pastime or a source of mockery, warning that such individuals have been blinded by the ephemeral pleasures of this world. It serves as a stark reminder of the ultimate accountability before God, emphasizing that on the Day of Judgment, no wealth, status, or worldly influence will suffice to save the soul from the consequences of its misdeeds, nor will any intercessor prevail if the person has willfully rejected the truth, leading them to a destiny defined by the bitter fruits of their own disbelief.

translation: Say, 'Do we call upon instead of Allah that which neither benefits us nor harms us and be turned back on our heels after Allah has guided us? [We would then be] like one whom the devils have enticed [wandering] confused upon the earth, while he has companions inviting him to guidance, [calling],
interpretation: This verse presents a rhetorical question highlighting the irrationality of idolatry, illustrating that abandoning the clear truth of monotheism after receiving divine guidance is akin to a man who has lost his way in the desert, bewitched and confused by demonic forces, while his righteous companions desperately call him toward the path of safety. The verse underscores that true guidance resides solely with Allah, and the purpose of human existence is to fully submit one's will and life to the Lord of all the worlds, for seeking any other source for guidance or spiritual benefit is an act of self-abandonment that leads to utter bewilderment.

translation: And [that you] establish prayer and fear Him. And it is He to whom you will be gathered.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the purpose of human existence is to maintain a constant, conscious connection with the Creator through the ritual of prayer, which serves as a spiritual anchor against moral corruption, while simultaneously cultivating a sense of God-consciousness (taqwa) that guides one's actions, all in preparation for the inevitable return to Allah, where every soul will be held accountable for its conduct in this life.

translation: And it is He who created the heavens and the earth in truth. And the day He says, 'Be,' and it is, His word is the truth. And His is the dominion [on] the Day the Horn is blown. [He is] Knower of the unseen and the witnessed; and He is the Wise, the Acquainted.
interpretation: Allah emphasizes His absolute sovereignty and creative power, asserting that the entire universe was brought into existence with a purposeful reality rather than in vain. The verse underscores that the process of creation and resurrection is effortless for Allah; whenever He wills a thing to exist, His command 'Be' manifests it instantly. This establishes that His word is the ultimate truth, and on the Day of Resurrection, all false claims of authority will vanish, leaving His kingship undisputed. By describing Himself as the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, Allah reminds humanity that nothing escapes His awareness, and His actions are governed by perfect wisdom and comprehensive knowledge, ensuring that all outcomes are executed with divine precision.

translation: And mention when Abraham said to his father Azar, 'Do you take idols as deities? Indeed, I see you and your people to be in manifest error.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound intellectual and spiritual confrontation between Prophet Abraham and his father regarding the absurdity of idol worship. Abraham’s question is not merely an inquiry but a sharp rhetorical rebuke, intended to awaken his father's reason by pointing out the fundamental contradiction of creating or shaping objects with one's own hands and then elevating them to the status of divine beings. By declaring them to be in 'manifest error,' Abraham asserts that their deviation from the truth is so obvious and logically inconsistent that it requires no complex proof, urging them to recognize the blindness of their misguided devotion.

translation: And thus We showed Abraham the dominion of the heavens and the earth that he might be among the certain [in faith].
interpretation: Allah bestowed upon Prophet Abraham (peace be upon him) a profound spiritual insight, granting him a clear vision of the hidden realities and the governing laws of the universe. This was not merely a physical sight, but a divine unveiling that allowed his heart to perceive the majesty, order, and sovereignty of the Creator behind every creation. By witnessing the internal logic and the perfect design of the heavens and the earth, Abraham reached the highest level of conviction (yaqin), where his faith became so absolute and unshakable that it transcended all doubt, anchoring his soul firmly in the realization of Allah's Oneness and absolute power.

translation: So when the night covered him [with darkness], he saw a star. He said, 'This is my lord.' But when it set, he said, 'I like not those that disappear.'
interpretation: Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was using a method of intellectual argumentation with his people, who worshipped celestial bodies. By temporarily aligning himself with their perspective and then observing the transient nature of the star as it set, he demonstrated that a true deity cannot be subject to disappearance or decline, thereby guiding his people toward the realization that the Creator must be eternal and unchanging.

translation: And when he saw the moon rising, he said, 'This is my Lord.' But when it set, he said, 'Unless my Lord guides me, I will surely be among the people who are astray.'
interpretation: Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him) utilized a dialectical and educational method in this instance to demonstrate the falsity of worshipping celestial bodies. By observing the moon and initially declaring it his 'Lord' only for it to subsequently disappear, he aimed to lead his people through a logical progression of thought; he showed that that which is subject to movement, change, and setting cannot be divine, as the true Creator is eternal, immutable, and ever-present. His concluding remark emphasizes that true guidance is a divine gift, acknowledging that human reason, while capable of witnessing God's signs, requires Allah's constant light to arrive at the truth and remain steadfast.

translation: And when he saw the sun rising, he said, 'This is my Lord; this is greater.' But when it set, he said, 'O my people, indeed I am free from what you associate with Allah.'
interpretation: Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him) employed a dialectical method of reasoning to guide his people. By initially appearing to align with their observation of the sun—calling it 'Lord' due to its magnitude—he led them to a logical contradiction when the sun eventually disappeared. This demonstration was intended to expose the absurdity of worshipping transient, created celestial bodies, thereby proving that the true Creator must be eternal, self-sustaining, and never subject to the limitations of setting or absence.

translation: Indeed, I have turned my face toward He who created the heavens and the earth, inclining toward truth, and I am not of those who associate others with Allah.
interpretation: This verse represents the declaration of pure monotheism (Tawhid), where the believer renounces all false deities and directs their absolute devotion, worship, and intent solely to the Creator of the universe. It signifies a complete internal and external turning away from polytheism and worldly distractions, anchoring the soul in the innate disposition (Fitra) of recognizing the One True God as the only deserving recipient of worship.

translation: And his people argued with him. He said, 'Do you argue with me concerning Allah while He has guided me? And I fear not what you associate with Him [and would not be harmed] unless my Lord should will something. My Lord encompasses all things in knowledge. Then will you not be reminded?'
interpretation: In this verse, the Prophet Ibrahim addresses the irrationality of his people's polytheism by asserting that his monotheistic belief is rooted in divine guidance, which is superior to their ancestral traditions. He dismisses the power of their idols to cause him harm, clarifying that only the will of Allah—the All-Knowing Creator—determines events. His challenge to them is a rhetorical call for intellectual reflection, urging them to recognize that fearing inanimate objects is illogical when compared to the absolute, all-encompassing knowledge and sovereignty of the One True God.

translation: And how should I fear what you associate with Allah while you do not fear that you have associated with Allah that for which He has not sent down to you any authority? So which of the two parties has more right to security, if you should know?
interpretation: Prophet Ibrahim is posing a rhetorical question to his people to expose the irrationality of their polytheism; he asserts that his monotheistic devotion provides him with true spiritual tranquility and safety, whereas the idolaters live in a state of delusion because they have no divine proof or logical justification for worshipping entities that possess no power to harm or benefit them, ultimately arguing that the one who aligns with the singular, absolute truth of the Creator is the only one who can truly be at peace.

translation: Those who believe and do not mix their belief with injustice - for them is security, and they are [rightly] guided.
interpretation: The verse clarifies that the absolute security from punishment and the state of true guidance belong exclusively to those who maintain their faith in its purity, untainted by the injustice of associating partners with God (shirk), which is the greatest form of oppression against the truth and one's own soul.

translation: And that was Our argument which We gave to Abraham against his people. We raise in degrees whom We will. Indeed, your Lord is Wise and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the profound logic and evidence granted to Prophet Abraham to refute the polytheism of his people were not mere intellectual capabilities, but divine gifts bestowed by Allah. It highlights the divine prerogative of elevating the status of the believers through knowledge, wisdom, and steadfastness in truth, affirming that Allah’s elevation of individuals is always governed by His absolute wisdom, which perceives who is most deserving of such rank, and His omniscience, which encompasses the hidden sincerity and capability of His servants.

translation: And We gave him Isaac and Jacob; all of them We guided. And Noah We guided before; and among his descendants, David and Solomon and Job and Joseph and Moses and Aaron. Thus do We reward the doers of good.
interpretation: The verse illustrates that the prophetic mission and divine guidance are not merely inherited through bloodlines, but are a bestowal from Allah based on His wisdom, specifically rewarding those who achieve the rank of Ihsan—worshipping and acting as if they see Allah, thereby perfecting their faith and deeds.

translation: And Zechariah, John, Jesus, and Elias - all were of the righteous.
interpretation: This verse highlights that these prophets, despite their different times and individual circumstances, shared the fundamental quality of absolute moral integrity and total submission to God, serving as a unified testament to the consistency of divine guidance and the elevated status granted to those who maintain righteousness throughout their lives.

translation: And Ishmael, Elisha, Jonah, and Lot; and all of them We favored over the worlds.
interpretation: God designates these individuals as recipients of divine grace and spiritual exaltation, elevating them above the common people of their time through the bestowal of prophecy, guidance, and unwavering commitment to the truth, thereby establishing them as moral exemplars for humanity regardless of their specific historical contexts.

translation: And among their fathers and their descendants and their brothers - and We chose them and We guided them to a straight path.
interpretation: God Almighty informs us that He selected these noble individuals—the prophets and messengers—along with their virtuous forebears, offspring, and siblings, bestowing upon them the honor of Prophethood and spiritual purity, and guiding them to the path of truth, which is the worship of God alone and the steadfast adherence to His clear, straight religion.

translation: That is the guidance of Allah, by which He guides whom He wills of His servants. But if they had associated others with Allah, then surely would have become worthless to them whatever they were doing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true guidance is a divine favor granted solely by Allah according to His wisdom, and it serves as a stern warning that the gravity of associating partners with God (shirk) is so profound that it invalidates all previous good deeds, rendering a lifetime of worship null and void because the fundamental condition of sincerity and oneness has been violated.

translation: Those are the ones to whom We gave the Scripture, authority, and prophethood. But if the disbelievers deny it, then We have entrusted it to a people who will never deny it.
interpretation: God Almighty affirms that the leadership of the divine message is an established reality that will never be extinguished; if the people of Mecca or any others choose to reject the guidance and the covenant of prophethood, God has prepared others—whether they be the noble Companions or future generations of believers—who possess the faith, sincerity, and steadfastness to uphold the truth, protect the revelation, and fulfill the mission that the deniers have abandoned.

translation: Those are the ones whom Allah has guided, so follow their guidance. Say, 'I ask of you no reward for it. It is but a reminder to the worlds.'
interpretation: The verse commands the Prophet Muhammad and, by extension, his followers to emulate the steadfastness, patience, and unwavering faith of the preceding prophets in the face of adversity, affirming that the divine message is a universal reminder for all of humanity for which no worldly compensation is sought.

translation: And they did not appraise Allah with true appraisal when they said, 'Allah did not reveal to a human being anything.' Say, 'Who revealed the Scripture that Moses brought as light and guidance to the people? You make it into parchments, disclosing [some of] it and concealing much. And you were taught that which you knew not – neither you nor your fathers.' Say, 'Allah [revealed it].' Then leave them in their discourse, amusing themselves.
interpretation: This verse rebukes the disbelievers and polytheists who denied the possibility of divine revelation to human beings, arguing that such a denial stems from a fundamental failure to recognize the majesty, wisdom, and omnipotence of Allah. By claiming that God would not communicate with humanity, they belittle His lordship and ignore the clear historical evidence of the Torah, which was a manifest light and guidance. The verse further highlights the hypocrisy of the People of the Scripture, who manipulated their own sacred texts to suit their worldly desires, concealing the truth while claiming to follow it. The command for the Prophet to 'leave them in their discourse' signifies that since they have rejected the overwhelming evidence of God's sovereignty and His historical communication with prophets, they are merely engaged in vain and frivolous argumentation, and their misguided state is a consequence of their own arrogant insistence on falsehood.

translation: And this is a Book We have revealed, blessed, confirming what was before it, so that you may warn the Mother of Cities and those around it. Those who believe in the Hereafter believe in it, and they are observant of their prayers.
interpretation: The verse highlights the divine authority and purpose of the Qur'an as a continuation of previous scriptures, while specifically tasking the Prophet Muhammad with the mission of inviting the people of Mecca—the spiritual center of the world—and its surrounding regions to the truth, noting that those who truly perceive the significance of the afterlife are the ones who naturally gravitate toward the guidance of this Book and demonstrate their submission through the consistent performance of their ritual prayers.

translation: And you have certainly come to Us alone as We created you the first time, and you have left behind you that which We bestowed upon you. And We do not see with you your 'intercessors' whom you claimed were partners among you. It has all been severed between you, and lost from you is what you used to claim.
interpretation: This verse serves as a profound reminder of the finality and stripping away of worldly attachments upon meeting Allah; it emphasizes that every human being will stand before their Creator entirely alone, stripped of all the material wealth, status, and false divine supports they once relied upon in the worldly life, illustrating the futility of shirk (associating partners with God) and the ultimate abandonment of all illusory protections when the truth of the afterlife is revealed.

translation: Indeed, Allah is the cleaver of the grain and the date seed. He brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living. That is Allah, so how are you deluded?
interpretation: This verse directs the human intellect toward the signs of divine power manifested in the cycle of life and growth, where Allah initiates life from seemingly lifeless matter, such as a dormant seed, and conversely brings forth lifeless matter from living organisms, demonstrating that He alone is the Creator and Sustainer who possesses the absolute authority to orchestrate these complex biological transitions, thereby invalidating any justification for turning away from His worship toward false idols.

translation: [He is] the cleaver of the daybreak and has made the night for rest and the sun and the moon for calculation. That is the determination of the Exalted in Might, the Knowing.
interpretation: God Almighty reveals His absolute power and divine wisdom by managing the cosmic cycles: He initiates the light of dawn to banish darkness, provides the night as a period of tranquility for rest after the toil of the day, and established the celestial orbits of the sun and moon as a precise system for humanity to measure time, seasons, and religious observances, demonstrating that such perfect order is the calculated decree of a Creator who possesses both the limitless strength to sustain the universe and the infinite knowledge to orchestrate its intricate balance.

translation: And it is He who placed for you the stars that you may be guided by them through the darknesses of the land and sea. We have detailed the signs for a people who know.
interpretation: Allah signifies that He created the celestial bodies not merely as ornaments, but as functional navigation tools that enable humanity to traverse vast, featureless landscapes and oceans during the night. By highlighting that these signs are detailed for those who possess knowledge, the verse emphasizes that the utility and complexity of the universe are intended for reflection and intellectual pursuit, serving as an invitation for humans to engage in observation and scientific inquiry to better understand the wisdom behind the design of the cosmos.

translation: And it is He who produced you from a single soul and [gave you] a place of dwelling and a place of storage. We have detailed the signs for a people who understand.
interpretation: This verse highlights the unified origin of humanity, tracing back to Adam, and signifies that the life of every individual is divided between a state of stability and realization, such as life on earth or the womb, and a state of transition and concealment, such as the period spent in the grave or the loins of ancestors, emphasizing that these stages are divine arrangements intended for those who possess the intellectual depth to reflect upon the mysteries of creation and existence.

translation: And it is He who sends down rain from the sky, and We produce thereby the growth of all things. We produce from it greenery from which We produce grains arranged in layers. And from the palm trees – of its emerging fruit are clusters hanging low. And [We produce] gardens of grapevines and olives and pomegranates, similar yet varied. Look at [each of] its fruit when it yields and [at] its ripening. Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.
interpretation: The verse serves as a meditative invitation for the believer to contemplate the divine wisdom and power manifest in the botanical world, where a single source of water gives rise to an immense diversity of life forms, textures, and tastes. By highlighting the complexity of biological growth—from the delicate sprout to the heavy, layered grain and the hanging fruit—the Qur'an directs the human intellect to recognize that such precise design, intentional variation, and life-giving cycles cannot be accidental, but are intentional proofs of a Creator who sustains all existence and provides for His creation.

translation: But they have attributed to Allah partners - the jinn, while He has created them, and they have fabricated for Him sons and daughters without knowledge. Exalted is He and high above what they describe.
interpretation: This verse rebukes the polytheists for their profound ignorance and arrogance in associating the jinn as partners with Allah, despite the fact that Allah is the Sole Creator of those very beings they worship. It further condemns their audacity in falsely inventing offspring for the Almighty—claiming He has sons and daughters—without any basis in truth or revelation, affirming that Allah is transcendently far removed from these blasphemous descriptions and fabrications.

translation: Originator of the heavens and the earth. How could He have a son when He does not have a companion and He created all things? And He is, of all things, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute oneness and transcendence of God by highlighting that procreation, which is a biological necessity for created beings to ensure continuity, is impossible and inapplicable to the Creator, who is the sole Originator of existence and possesses infinite knowledge, thereby rendering the concept of Him having offspring logically and essentially flawed.

translation: That is Allah, your Lord; there is no deity except Him, the Creator of all things, so worship Him. And He is, over all things, Disposer of affairs.
