interpretation: This verse establishes the absolute singularity and sovereignty of Allah, asserting that since He is the unique Creator who brought everything into existence from nothingness, He alone possesses the right to be worshipped, and consequently, all reliance and trust for the administration of one's affairs must be placed solely upon Him, for He is the ultimate guardian and manager of every aspect of His creation.

translation: Vision perceives Him not, but He perceives [all] vision; and He is the Subtle, the Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse signifies the absolute transcendence of Allah, clarifying that while human sight cannot encompass or behold His essence due to the limitations of created faculties and the majesty of the Divine, Allah possesses infinite and perfect knowledge that encompasses all things, including the very sight that attempts to perceive Him; His subtlety lies in His closeness and gentleness in managing the affairs of His creation, while His expertise reflects His encompassing awareness of every detail, hidden or manifest, within the universe.

translation: There have come to you evidences from your Lord. So whoever sees, does so for his own soul, and whoever is blind, does so against it; and I am not a guardian over you.
interpretation: This verse signifies that Allah has provided humanity with clear proofs and intellectual insights through the Qur'an and the guidance of the Prophet, which are sufficient for anyone seeking the truth; the choice to accept this guidance is a personal responsibility where the benefits of faith accrue to the believer and the consequences of rejection fall solely upon the denier, emphasizing that the role of the Prophet is to convey the message clearly rather than to coerce belief or serve as a watchful guardian over the private actions and spiritual outcomes of the people.

translation: And thus do We explain the signs in diverse ways, that they may say, 'You have studied [well],' and that We may make it clear for a people who have knowledge.
interpretation: Allah explains His verses and proofs in various forms and manners so that the truth becomes manifest, leading the stubborn disbelievers to falsely claim that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) learned these revelations from previous scriptures or human teachers, while simultaneously providing clear insight and spiritual understanding to those who possess knowledge and sincere hearts, enabling them to recognize the divine origin of the message.

translation: Follow what has been revealed to you from your Lord; there is no deity except Him; and turn away from the polytheists.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine command for the Prophet Muhammad and, by extension, the believers to hold firmly to the revelation of the Qur'an as the ultimate source of truth, emphasizing the core tenet of monotheism (Tawhid) which asserts that worship is exclusively for Allah, while advising the believer to prioritize this spiritual devotion and avoid the distractions or hostile influence of those who associate partners with God.

translation: And if Allah had willed, they would not have associated others with Him. And We have not made you, [O Muhammad], over them a guardian, nor are you over them a manager of affairs.
interpretation: This verse serves as a profound comfort to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) by emphasizing that the guidance of hearts and the acceptance of faith rest solely with Allah’s will, not the Prophet's personal efforts. It clarifies that his role is restricted to conveying the message clearly, absolving him of the burden of the polytheists' persistent disbelief, as he lacks the divine authority or capacity to compel belief in their hearts, which remains exclusively within the domain of the Creator.

translation: And do not insult those they invoke other than Allah, lest they insult Allah in enmity without knowledge. Thus We have made pleasing to every community their deed. Then to their Lord is their return, and He will inform them about what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse establishes a principle of strategic ethics in preaching and discourse, commanding believers to avoid reviling the false deities of others, even if such deities are illegitimate. The rationale provided is that offensive language directed at false objects of worship will provoke the polytheists to respond with insults against the true God, Allah, out of ignorance and hostility, thereby escalating conflict rather than facilitating guidance. The mention of Allah making every community's deeds 'pleasing' to them suggests that people often become emotionally attached to their cultural and religious traditions, and aggressive confrontation only deepens their stubbornness. Ultimately, the verse redirects the responsibility of judgment to Allah, affirming that all souls will return to Him, where He will justly account for their beliefs and actions, freeing the believer from the need to resort to base insults in the pursuit of truth.

translation: And they swear by Allah their strongest oaths that if a sign came to them, they would surely believe in it. Say, 'The signs are only with Allah.' And what will make you perceive that even if it came, they would not believe?
interpretation: This verse addresses the persistent stubbornness of the polytheists, who claimed they would accept faith if a miracle occurred. Allah informs the Prophet that their oaths are insincere, explaining that belief is a matter of guidance from Allah, and even if their requested signs were manifested, their hearts are so hardened by arrogance and denial that they would persist in their disbelief regardless.

translation: And We will turn away their hearts and their eyes just as they refused to believe in it the first time, and We will leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly.
interpretation: Due to their persistent rejection of the truth despite being presented with clear evidence, God withdraws His divine guidance from them as a form of justice. Consequently, their hearts become incapable of understanding the truth and their insights are dimmed, leaving them trapped in their own arrogance and confusion, where they continue to wander aimlessly without finding the path to righteousness.

translation: And even if We had sent down to them the angels [with the message], and the dead spoke to them, and We gathered together every [created] thing in front of them [in support of the truth], they would not believe unless Allah should will. But most of them, are ignorant.
interpretation: This verse underscores that the refusal of the disbelievers to accept the truth is not due to a lack of empirical evidence or miraculous proofs, but rather a deliberate choice rooted in spiritual blindness and stubbornness; even if they were presented with the most extraordinary supernatural phenomena, such as conversing with the deceased or witnessing the gathering of all creation, their hearts would remain closed unless Allah, in His sovereign will, guides them to faith, noting that their persistent ignorance is a consequence of their refusal to reflect on the signs already provided.

translation: And thus We have made for every prophet an enemy - devils from mankind and jinn, inspiring to one another decorative speech in deception. But if your Lord had willed, they would not have done it, so leave them and that which they fabricate.
interpretation: The verse explains that the presence of opposition to the truth is a recurring phenomenon in the history of Prophethood, designed as a test for the believers; the 'decorative speech' refers to the sophisticated, deceptive rhetoric that the enemies of truth use to mislead others and justify their disbelief, while the phrase 'if your Lord had willed' emphasizes that this struggle occurs within the framework of divine decree, ultimately instructing the Prophet to remain steadfast and leave the outcome of these fabrications to God.

translation: And so that the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter may incline to it and be pleased with it, and that they may commit what they are committing.
interpretation: This verse explains that when God allows the whispers and deceptions of devils to appeal to the hearts of those who reject the afterlife, it serves as a form of trial and a manifestation of divine justice; by letting these individuals find attraction and satisfaction in falsehood, God allows them to fully manifest their chosen path of sin, thereby confirming their responsibility for the deeds they commit before they face their final judgment.

translation: Is it other than Allah I should seek as a judge while it is He who has revealed to you the Book explained in detail? And those to whom We gave the Scripture know that it is sent down from your Lord in truth, so never be among the doubters.
interpretation: The verse serves as a rhetorical assertion of the Prophet Muhammad's singular devotion to divine authority, emphasizing that since Allah has provided a comprehensive and clear revelation, there is no logical or spiritual reason to seek judgment, guidance, or legislation from any other source. By highlighting that those who received previous scriptures recognize the truth of this revelation, the verse encourages the believer to remain steadfast in certainty and rejects any influence of skepticism that might arise from external or opposing ideologies.

translation: And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and in justice. None can alter His words, and He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: The verse confirms that everything Allah has decreed, whether in His revelation of laws or His promises of reward and punishment, is entirely truthful in its information and perfectly just in its rulings, leaving no room for falsehood or inequity. Because His knowledge is absolute and His wisdom is perfect, no one possesses the authority or the ability to change, abrogate, or distort His decrees, as He hears all that is spoken and knows all that has occurred or will occur.

translation: And if you obey most of those upon the earth, they will mislead you from the way of Allah. They follow not except assumption, and they are not but falsifying.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern caution against the fallacy of popular opinion or majority consensus as a benchmark for truth. Allah warns that the majority of mankind often follow subjective whims, conjectures, and unfounded guesses rather than divine guidance or objective reality; therefore, one should seek truth through the revelation of Allah rather than the fleeting trends or societal pressures of the masses.

translation: Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of the [rightly] guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's absolute omniscience regarding the internal state and ultimate choices of His creation, highlighting that He alone possesses the definitive knowledge of who has intentionally turned away from the path of truth and who has sincerely sought and attained guidance, thereby affirming that judgment belongs solely to Him based on His perfect awareness of every heart's true inclination.

translation: So eat of that [meat] upon which the name of Allah has been mentioned, if you are believers in His verses.
interpretation: This command underscores that the consumption of food is an act of worship for the believer; by invoking the name of Allah over the animal, the individual acknowledges that life is a sacred trust granted by the Creator, thereby sanctifying the act of nourishment and distinguishing the believer's lifestyle from those who disregard the divine authority over creation.

translation: And why should you not eat of that upon which the name of Allah has been mentioned, while He has explained in detail to you what He has forbidden you, excepting that to which you are compelled? And indeed, many lead others astray through their own inclinations without knowledge. Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine reprimand against those who impose self-invented prohibitions on food, emphasizing that Allah has clearly defined what is forbidden, leaving no room for human whim to restrict what is lawful. The verse highlights the intellectual and moral error of those who deviate from the clear bounds of revelation to follow their own subjective desires, reminding believers that the true authority to determine lawfulness belongs to Allah alone, who is fully aware of those who overstep these divine boundaries.

translation: And leave what is apparent of sin and what is concealed thereof. Indeed, those who earn sin will be recompensed for what they used to commit.
interpretation: The verse commands the believers to completely abandon sin, whether it is committed openly and publicly or secretly in private, as God is the All-Knowing who encompasses all actions and intentions; therefore, those who persist in transgression—regardless of its nature—will inevitably face a just retribution in the hereafter, proportional to the gravity and frequency of their harmful deeds.

translation: And do not eat of that upon which the name of Allah has not been mentioned, for indeed, it is a grave disobedience. And indeed do the devils inspire their allies [among men] to dispute with you. And if you were to obey them, indeed, you would be associators [of others with Him].
interpretation: This verse establishes that the act of consuming meat slaughtered without invoking Allah's name is a form of defiance against His decree, characterizing it as a moral corruption. It serves as a stern warning that proponents of falsehood—motivated by satanic whispers—will attempt to rationalize or justify such forbidden actions through intellectual sophistry to mislead the believers. Therefore, yielding to these deceptive arguments and prioritizing man-made justifications over the clear commandments of Allah constitutes an act of shirk (polytheism), as it elevates the opinions of creatures above the divine authority of the Creator.

translation: Is he who was dead and We gave him life and provided for him light with which he walks among the people like one who is in darkness, never to emerge from it? Thus it has been made pleasing to the disbelievers what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse presents a metaphorical contrast between the believer and the disbeliever, describing the believer as one who was spiritually dead—lacking guidance and purpose—and then was revived by Allah through faith and the Qur'an. This 'light' represents the clear insight and moral clarity that allows the believer to navigate life with righteousness and understanding among people, whereas the disbeliever remains trapped in the deep darkness of ignorance and disbelief, unable to find a way out because their own wicked actions have been made to appear attractive to them by their lower selves and the influence of evil.

translation: And thus We have placed within every city the greatest of its criminals to conspire therein. But they conspire not except against themselves, and they perceive [it] not.
interpretation: This verse explains a divine law in which those who wield influence and power within a society, and who choose to pursue wickedness and injustice, are allowed to persist in their cunning schemes. This respite serves as a trial for them and a means for their own ultimate downfall, for their deceptive strategies inevitably backfire, causing more harm to their own souls and reputations than to the righteous, even though their arrogance renders them blind to this consequence.

translation: And when a sign comes to them, they say, 'We will never believe until we are given the like of that which the messengers of Allah were given.' Allah is most knowing of where He places His message. There will afflict those who committed crimes humiliation before Allah and severe punishment for what they used to conspire.
interpretation: The verse explains that the arrogance of the disbelievers leads them to demand that prophethood be bestowed upon them as it was to the messengers, out of envy and pride rather than a sincere search for truth; however, God alone possesses the absolute wisdom to choose His messengers based on who is truly qualified, purified in heart, and worthy of bearing the divine trust, and therefore those who oppose this divine decree through deceit and rejection will inevitably face divine retribution and abasement for their obstinacy.

translation: So whoever Allah wants to guide, He expands his breast to [contain] Islam; and whoever He wants to misguide, He makes his breast tight and constricted as though he were climbing into the sky. Thus does Allah place defilement upon those who do not believe.
interpretation: This verse illustrates that guidance is a divine favor that opens the heart to receive the truth with ease and tranquility, while obstinate rejection of faith leads to a state of spiritual suffocation, where the heart becomes so constricted and unable to accept the light of guidance that it feels as overwhelmed and physically strained as a person gasping for breath at extreme altitudes.

translation: And this is the path of your Lord, [leading] straight. We have detailed the verses for a people who remember.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the path Allah has laid out for His servants is the singular, upright way that leads directly to His pleasure and paradise, devoid of any deviation. By clarifying His signs and commands, Allah enables those who possess hearts that reflect and minds that heed advice to understand the truth, recognize the straight path amidst worldly confusion, and maintain their steadfastness upon the faith.

translation: For them is the Home of Peace with their Lord, and He is their Guardian because of what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse signifies that for those who maintain their faith and righteousness, Allah has prepared Paradise—a place of eternal safety, tranquility, and security from all harm and distress. By calling it the 'Home of Peace' with their Lord, it emphasizes that their ultimate sanctuary is found through His proximity and pleasure. Allah acts as their protector and benefactor in the hereafter as a direct consequence and reward for the righteous deeds and obedience they performed during their worldly lives.

translation: And on the Day when He will gather them all together, [He will say], 'O company of jinn, you have misled many of mankind.' And their allies among mankind will say, 'Our Lord, some of us made use of others, and we have reached our term, which You appointed for us.' He will say, 'The Fire is your dwelling place, wherein you will abide eternally, except for what Allah wills. Indeed, your Lord is Wise and Knowing.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the mutual ruin and profound regret experienced by the jinn and their human followers on the Day of Judgment. The jinn led humans astray through temptation and falsehoods, while humans facilitated the jinn's rebellion by obeying them and satisfying their own base desires. By admitting that they 'made use of one another,' they acknowledge that their alliance was a transactional pursuit of worldly pleasure at the expense of their eternal souls. The mention of 'except for what Allah wills' emphasizes that ultimate sovereignty and mercy remain with Allah alone, while the finality of their abode serves as a stern warning against those who trade divine guidance for the transient influence of evil.

translation: And thus We let some of the wrongdoers rule over others as a result of what they used to earn.
interpretation: This verse signifies a form of divine justice where Allah allows corrupt and oppressive people to gain power over one another or face the consequences of their actions through the hands of their own kind, serving as a retribution for their sins and transgressions; it illustrates the universal law that when a society abandons righteousness and embraces injustice, they inevitably fall under the sway of leaders or circumstances that reflect their own moral corruption.

translation: O company of jinn and mankind, did there not come to you messengers from among you, relating to you My verses and warning you of the meeting of this Day of yours? They will say, 'We bear witness against ourselves,' and the worldly life had deluded them, and they will bear witness against themselves that they were disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse depicts the final interrogation of humanity and jinn on the Day of Judgment, where God highlights that they were given every opportunity to reform through messengers chosen from their own kind who clearly communicated divine revelations. Their admission of guilt, acknowledging their own disbelief, serves as a testament to the absolute justice of God; it confirms that their refusal to believe was not due to a lack of guidance, but rather a voluntary surrender to the fleeting, deceptive temptations of the worldly life that blinded them to the ultimate reality of their accountability.

translation: That is because your Lord would not destroy the cities for wrongdoing while their people were unaware.
interpretation: This verse establishes the divine principle of justice, emphasizing that God does not inflict punishment upon a society merely for their errors or lack of belief until He has first sent them messengers and clear signs to alert them, thereby ensuring that no one is held accountable for a state of ignorance they were not given the opportunity to overcome.

translation: And for all are degrees from what they have done, and your Lord is not unaware of what they do.
interpretation: Every soul shall be assigned a status and rank in the afterlife directly corresponding to the quality and quantity of its deeds in this world; as God encompasses all human actions with His perfect knowledge, no act of righteousness or sin goes unnoticed or unrecorded, ensuring that absolute justice is served according to one's conduct.

translation: And your Lord is the Free of need, the possessor of mercy. If He wills, He can do away with you and give succession after you to whomever He wills, just as He produced you from the descendants of another people.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah’s absolute independence from His creation and His boundless mercy, serving as a reminder that humanity’s existence is subject solely to His will. It humbles the arrogant by asserting that Allah has no need for any specific group of people to fulfill His purpose; if He chooses, He can eradicate one generation and replace it with another, just as He brought the current generation into existence from the lineage of previous nations who have long since passed away.

translation: Indeed, that which you are promised is coming, and you will not be able to cause failure [to Allah].
interpretation: This verse serves as a definitive assertion of the inevitability of the Day of Resurrection, emphasizing that Allah's decree is absolute and cannot be evaded; it warns those who deny the afterlife that they possess no power to escape the divine reckoning, as they are entirely within the grasp of the Creator's sovereignty and cannot hinder His will or hide from His judgment.

translation: Say, O my people, work according to your position; indeed, I am working. And you will come to know who will have the [best] outcome of the home. Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning from the Prophet to his people, asserting that he will remain steadfast in his divine mission regardless of their opposition. It challenges the disbelievers to persist in their ways while he persists in his, ultimately placing the matter before God's inevitable judgment. The 'outcome of the home' refers to the afterlife, where the truth will be revealed, and it confirms that those who deny the truth and oppress the believers will ultimately fail, as their worldly power is fleeting and their spiritual end is one of ruin.

translation: And they assigned to Allah from that which He created of crops and livestock a share and said, 'This is for Allah,' by their claim, 'and this is for our partners.' But what was for their 'partners' did not reach Allah, while what was for Allah - this reached their 'partners.' Evil is that which they decide.
interpretation: This verse exposes the spiritual blindness of the polytheists, who sought to validate their idolatry by pretending to honor God while simultaneously serving their false deities. They would designate portions of their produce and animals for both Allah and their idols, yet they displayed their hypocrisy by always prioritizing the needs of their idols; if a portion meant for Allah suffered a loss or deficiency, they would shift it to the idols, but if a portion meant for the idols suffered, they would take from the share designated for Allah to compensate. The verse condemns this behavior as fundamentally irrational and morally corrupt, illustrating how those who associate partners with God inevitably prioritize their worldly whims and false ideologies over the truth of divine sovereignty.

translation: And likewise, to many of the polytheists, their partners have made appearing pleasing the killing of their children in order to bring about their destruction and to cover them with confusion in their religion. And if Allah had willed, they would not have done so. So leave them and that which they fabricate.
interpretation: The verse explains that the idols and demonic figures worshipped by the polytheists successfully deluded them into committing the heinous act of infanticide. This influence was designed not only to destroy the lives of their offspring but also to corrupt their understanding of divine law, causing them to believe that such cruelty was a form of worship. By stating that Allah allowed this to occur as a test of human free will rather than divine mandate, the verse emphasizes that the polytheists bear full responsibility for their own moral collapse and the fabrication of false justifications for their sins.

translation: And they say, 'These animals and crops are restricted; none may eat from them except whom we will,' by their claim. And there are animals whose backs are forbidden, and animals upon which they do not mention the name of Allah - an invention of lies against Him. He will repay them for what they used to invent.
interpretation: The verse condemns the polytheists for arbitrarily enacting religious prohibitions on food and livestock based solely on their own desires and baseless traditions, rather than divine authority. By forbidding certain animals for riding or slaughter and restricting the consumption of crops to specific groups they favored, they attributed these man-made laws to Allah. This is identified as a grave form of falsehood and corruption of faith, for which Allah promises to hold them accountable by punishing them for their audacity in forging lies and attributing their own fabrications to His sacred legislation.

translation: And they say, 'What is in the bellies of these grazing livestock is exclusively for our males and forbidden to our wives. But if it is born dead, then all of them have share therein.' He will recompense them for their description. Indeed, He is Wise and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse exposes the irrationality and unauthorized legal innovations (bid'ah) of the pre-Islamic polytheists, who arbitrarily dictated divine laws regarding their livestock by reserving certain animals for men and forbidding them to women, while simultaneously acknowledging that if an animal was stillborn, everyone could partake of it; God asserts that He will hold them accountable for these fabrications, as He is the only One possessing the wisdom and knowledge to establish religious prohibitions and permissions.

translation: Those who kill their children foolishly without knowledge have lost, and they have forbidden what Allah has provided for them, inventing lies about Allah. They have certainly gone astray and were not guided.
interpretation: This verse highlights the moral and spiritual bankruptcy of those who, driven by ignorance and superstition, committed heinous acts like infanticide and arbitrarily declared lawful sustenance to be forbidden in Allah's name. It emphasizes that these individuals were led astray because they rejected the inherent truth of human life and Divine providence, replacing Allah's guidance with their own false fabrications, thereby forfeiting both their humanity and their path to salvation.

translation: And it is He who causes gardens to grow, [both] trellised and untrellised, and palm trees and crops, [all] varying in food, and olives and pomegranates, similar and dissimilar. Eat of [each of] its fruit when it yields and give its due [zakat] on the day of its harvest. And do not be excessive. Indeed, He does not like the excessive.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's boundless generosity and creative wisdom in providing sustenance for humanity through diverse agricultural products. By commanding the believers to eat from these fruits and then pay the obligatory charity (Zakat) upon harvest, Allah establishes a balance between enjoying His worldly blessings and fulfilling the socio-economic rights of the needy, while the prohibition against extravagance serves as a spiritual and practical warning to maintain moderation and avoid wastefulness in all aspects of consumption and life.

translation: And of the grazing livestock are carriers [of burdens] and those [small enough to be] for slaughter. Eat from what Allah has provided for you and do not follow the footsteps of Satan. Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gratitude owed to Allah for His diverse blessings, specifically the utility of livestock for both heavy labor and sustenance, while simultaneously warning the believer that the path to moral corruption often begins with seemingly small, gradual deviations from divine law—symbolized here as 'footsteps'—which lead one away from the path of obedience and into the trap of an adversary intent on human ruin.

translation: [They are] eight mates: two of the sheep, two of the goats. Say, 'Is it the two males He has forbidden or the two females or that which the wombs of the two females contain? Inform me with knowledge, if you should be truthful.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a rhetorical challenge to the polytheists who arbitrarily prohibited certain livestock for themselves based on superstitious traditions, despite Allah having created them all. By breaking down these animals into pairs of males and females, the verse exposes the absurdity of their claims; it forces them to identify exactly which part of the animal or which sex they allege is forbidden, thereby demonstrating that their dietary restrictions lack any divine foundation, logical consistency, or factual basis.

translation: And of the camels, two, and of the cattle, two. Say, 'Is it the two males He has forbidden or the two females or that which the wombs of the two females contain? Or were you witnesses when Allah enjoined this upon you?' Then who is more unjust than one who invents a lie about Allah to mislead the people without knowledge? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse serves as a logical refutation of the pagan Arabs who arbitrarily prohibited certain livestock for themselves based on superstitious fabrications, while falsely attributing these prohibitions to God. By questioning whether God forbade the male, the female, or the offspring, the verse exposes the absurdity and lack of divine evidence for their religious restrictions; it highlights that their claims were baseless fabrications intended to manipulate others, and emphasizes that those who forge lies against God to control or mislead people are the ultimate transgressors who forfeit divine guidance.

translation: Say, 'I do not find within that which was revealed to me anything forbidden to one who would eat it unless it be a dead animal or blood spilled out or the flesh of swine - for indeed, it is impure - or it be [that slaughtered in] disobedience, dedicated to other than Allah. But whoever is forced [by necessity], neither desiring [it] nor transgressing [its limit], then indeed, your Lord is Forgiving and Merciful.'
interpretation: The verse serves to clarify that the list of forbidden foods in Islam is restricted specifically to those mentioned, refuting the arbitrary prohibitions imposed by the polytheists of Mecca. By defining these specific categories—carrion, spilled blood, swine flesh, and animals sacrificed to idols—Allah demonstrates that His laws are not based on superstition but on spiritual and physical purity; however, He establishes a foundational principle of mercy by allowing the consumption of these items under extreme necessity, provided that one does not seek the forbidden out of defiance or exceed the amount needed to survive, reflecting the divine nature of a Lord who prioritizes the preservation of life.

translation: And to those who are Jews We prohibited every animal of undivided hoof. And of the cattle and the sheep We prohibited to them their fat, except what adheres to their backs or the entrails or what joined with bone. That We repaid them for their injustice. And indeed, We are truthful.
interpretation: God indicates that the strict dietary restrictions imposed upon the Children of Israel—specifically regarding the prohibition of animals with undivided hooves and certain fats—were not original laws of purity, but rather a punitive measure intended as a consequence for their persistent disobedience, rebellion against divine commands, and wrongdoing; thus, these prohibitions served as a symbolic burden or a spiritual correction to discipline them for their moral transgressions.

translation: So if they deny you, say, 'Your Lord is possessor of boundless mercy, but His punishment cannot be averted from the criminal people.'
interpretation: This verse serves as both a comfort and a warning; it encourages the Prophet and the believers to remain steadfast despite rejection, reminding them that Allah's mercy is vast for those who seek it, yet His divine justice and retribution are inescapable for those who persistently choose to commit crimes and reject the truth.

translation: Those who associate partners with Allah will say, 'If Allah had willed, we would not have associated [anything] with Him, nor would our fathers, nor would we have prohibited anything.' Likewise did those before them deny until they tasted Our punishment. Say, 'Do you have any knowledge that you can bring out to us? You follow only assumption, and you do nothing but lie.'
interpretation: The polytheists attempt to justify their idolatry and forbidden innovations by invoking the decree of Allah, wrongly suggesting that their actions are divinely ordained because they were not prevented from doing them. This argument is refuted by the fact that they possess no revealed knowledge or divine proof to support such a claim; rather, they are merely following baseless conjectures and fabricated excuses. Allah points out that this same deceptive logic was employed by past nations who persisted in their denial until they faced catastrophic destruction, serving as a reminder that man is granted the faculty of reason and choice, and thus remains accountable for his beliefs and moral conduct.

translation: Say, 'To Allah belongs the perfect, conclusive argument. Had He willed, He would have guided you all.'
interpretation: This verse asserts that Allah’s evidence for His oneness, His sovereignty, and His laws is complete, undeniable, and sufficient to establish the truth; therefore, no human can claim ignorance or lack of proof on the Day of Judgment, as Allah’s supreme will governs all matters of guidance and the manifestation of truth.

translation: Say, 'Bring forward your witnesses who testify that Allah has prohibited this.' And if they testify, do not testify with them, and do not follow the desires of those who denied Our verses and those who do not believe in the Hereafter, while they equate others with their Lord.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern command to the Prophet Muhammad to challenge the baseless claims of the polytheists regarding divine prohibitions. It instructs that when people invent religious laws or restrictions that God has not ordained, their claims must be met with a demand for factual evidence. The verse emphasizes that since their claims are fabrications stemming from personal desire rather than truth, one must not validate their falsehoods. Furthermore, it highlights that those who reject divine revelation and lack conviction in the afterlife are prone to straying from monotheism, ultimately equating created beings with the Creator, which constitutes the root of their spiritual deviation.

translation: Say, 'Come, I will recite what your Lord has prohibited to you. [He commands] that you not associate anything with Him, and to parents, good treatment, and do not kill your children out of poverty; We provide for you and for them. And do not approach immoralities - what is apparent of them and what is concealed. And do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden [to be killed] except by [legal] right. This has He instructed you that you might use reason.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a foundational ethical manifesto for human society, where God establishes the sanctity of life, the integrity of the family unit, and the purity of individual conduct as inseparable from the central command of pure monotheism. By linking the prohibition of polytheism directly to filial piety and the protection of innocent life, the verse emphasizes that one's relationship with the Creator must necessarily manifest in kindness, social responsibility, and the restraint of destructive impulses, ultimately arguing that adherence to these divine moral boundaries is the true exercise of human intellect and rational development.

translation: And do not approach the orphan's property except in a way that is best until he reaches maturity. And give full measure and weight in justice. We do not charge any soul except with that within its capacity. And when you speak, be just, even if it concerns a near relative. And fulfill the covenant of Allah. This has He instructed you that you may remember.
interpretation: This verse establishes a comprehensive moral and legal framework for human conduct, emphasizing that the protection of the vulnerable, absolute integrity in economic dealings, the necessity of objective truthfulness even against personal interests, and the sacred obligation to keep one's promises are the foundational pillars of a righteous society, all while acknowledging human limitations through the principle that divine accountability is strictly balanced with individual capacity.

translation: And indeed, this is My path, which is straight, so follow it; and do not follow [other] ways, for you will be separated from His way. This has He instructed you that you may become righteous.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine directive establishing the singular, unyielding nature of the path to God. By commanding the followers to adhere strictly to the 'Straight Path'—which represents the totality of the true religion and its moral mandates—God warns against the intellectual and spiritual fragmentation that occurs when individuals pursue diverse, man-made ideologies or innovations. The 'other ways' represent the myriad of worldly distractions and erroneous beliefs that deviate from the ultimate truth; by scattering one's focus across these disparate paths, the seeker loses the unity and clarity of the divine connection. Thus, the adherence to this singular path is presented as a foundational command that fosters spiritual vigilance and Taqwa, allowing the believer to remain focused, disciplined, and protected from the fragmentation of purpose that leads away from the Creator.

translation: Then We gave Moses the Book, completing (Our favor) upon him who did good, and explaining all things in detail, and a guidance and a mercy, that they might believe in the meeting with their Lord.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Torah was bestowed upon Moses as a comprehensive framework for guidance, serving as a perfected manifestation of Allah's benevolence toward those who strive for excellence in their faith and actions. By providing explicit laws and moral principles, the revelation acts as a beacon of mercy that aims to cultivate in the hearts of the people a profound awareness and certainty regarding their ultimate accountability and eventual return to their Creator.

translation: And this is a Book We have revealed, blessed, so follow it and fear Allah, that you may receive mercy.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine command to acknowledge the Quran as a source of immense spiritual blessings and guidance, emphasizing that salvation and the attainment of Allah's mercy are contingent upon actively adhering to its teachings and maintaining a state of God-consciousness, thereby transforming the revelation from a mere text into a practical roadmap for a righteous life.

translation: Or lest you say, 'The Scripture was only sent down to two groups before us, and we were indeed unaware of what they studied.'
interpretation: This verse warns the disbelievers against using the excuse of ignorance or lack of access to divine revelation as a justification for their lack of faith; it clarifies that Allah sent the Quran in a clear, eloquent Arabic tongue directly to the Arabs to ensure that the plea of not understanding or being preoccupied with the traditions of previous nations remains invalid, thereby leaving them without any argument to justify their rejection of the truth.

translation: Or lest you say, 'If only the Scripture had been sent down to us, we would have been better guided than they.' So there has now come to you a clear proof from your Lord, and a guidance and a mercy. Then who is more unjust than one who denies the verses of Allah and turns away from them? We will recompense those who turn away from Our verses with the worst of punishment for their having turned away.
interpretation: Allah rebukes those who claim that had they received a divine scripture like previous nations, they would have been more righteous and guided; He informs them that such an excuse is invalid because the ultimate truth, represented by the Quran, has already been sent to them as a manifest proof and a source of mercy. Therefore, there is no greater state of oppression than rejecting these evident signs and deliberately veering away from them, an act of stubborn arrogance that will inevitably lead to a severe and painful retribution as a consequence of their persistent avoidance of the truth.

translation: Do they wait for anything other than that the angels should come to them, or that your Lord should come, or that some of the signs of your Lord should come? The day that some of the signs of your Lord do come, no good will it do to a person to believe then, if he believed not before, nor earned good (by performing good deeds) through his faith. Say: 'Wait you (all); we (too) are waiting.'
interpretation: The verse serves as a stern warning that the opportunity for repentance and faith is not eternal. It describes a state of spiritual finality where, once the clear, undeniable signs of God's majesty—such as the approach of death, the appearance of the angels, or the onset of the Day of Judgment—become manifest, the trial of earthly life has concluded. At that juncture, the veil is lifted, and faith is no longer a matter of free choice or sincere conviction, but a forced acknowledgment of reality; therefore, a soul that had previously persisted in disbelief or neglected to perform righteous deeds while the door of opportunity remained open will find no spiritual benefit in a sudden, coerced confession of faith.

translation: Indeed, those who have divided their religion and become sects - you are not with them in anything. Their affair is only to Allah, and He will inform them about what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse serves as a declaration of dissociation from those who create factions and splinter groups within the faith, emphasizing that such divisive behavior contradicts the unity of the religion ordained by Allah, and asserting that the final judgment of their actions rests solely with the Creator.

translation: Whoever brings a good deed, for him is ten like it, and whoever brings a bad deed, he will not be recompensed except with its like, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine attribute of boundless generosity and absolute justice, where Allah multiplies the reward for a single act of righteousness by at least tenfold as an act of grace, while maintaining strict fairness by punishing a sin only to the extent of its gravity without any increase, ensuring that no soul is ever treated unjustly in the balance of their deeds.

translation: Say, 'Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path - a correct religion, the way of Abraham, inclining toward truth, and he was not among those who associate others with Allah.'
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that the path of the Prophet Muhammad is the ultimate culmination of divine guidance, which restores the primordial, monotheistic faith originally established by Abraham. By identifying this religion as 'correct' and 'upright,' the text asserts that the Islamic creed is the manifestation of the pure, unadulterated worship of the One God, stripping away the distortions and polytheistic additions that had corrupted religious practice over time, thereby aligning the believer with the true, objective reality of the Creator.

translation: Say, 'Indeed, my prayer, my rites of sacrifice, my living and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a declaration of total dedication and sincerity, asserting that every aspect of a believer's existence—from their formal acts of worship and ritual sacrifices to their daily life and ultimate end—is performed exclusively for the sake of Allah, the Creator and Sustainer of all existence, leaving no room for devotion to anything other than Him.

translation: He has no partner. And of this I have been commanded, and I am the first of the Muslims.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the absolute uniqueness of Allah in His divinity and lordship, rejecting any form of polytheism or associating partners with Him. By declaring that he is the first of the Muslims, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) signifies his complete submission to Allah's command to uphold this monotheistic creed, thereby setting the foundational principle for all who follow him in faith.

translation: Say, 'Is it other than Allah I should desire as a lord while He is the Lord of all things? And every soul earns not [blame] except against itself, and no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you concerning that over which you used to differ.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute Oneness and Sovereignty of Allah, asserting that there is no logical reason for a believer to seek any master or deity other than the Creator of all existence. It establishes the principle of individual moral responsibility, declaring that every person is held accountable solely for their own actions, thereby nullifying the concept of collective or transferred guilt. It serves as a reminder that all worldly disputes and conflicting beliefs will ultimately be resolved through divine judgment when all humanity returns to Allah, who will reveal the objective truth behind their disagreements.

translation: And it is He who has made you successors upon the earth and has raised some of you above others in degrees [of rank] by which He may test you through what He has given you. Indeed, your Lord is swift in penalty; but indeed, He is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: The verse clarifies that the variation in human statuses—such as wealth, power, and social standing—is not intended as a sign of ultimate superiority, but as a deliberate trial to see how each individual fulfills their responsibilities toward others and toward God. By granting some more worldly blessings than others, God tests the gratitude of the prosperous and the patience of the needy, while warning that those who abuse their positions will face swift justice, yet assuring those who repent that His mercy and forgiveness remain accessible to all.

translation: Alif-Lam-Mim-Sad.
interpretation: These disconnected letters serve as a divine challenge to the eloquence of the Arabs, signaling that the Quran is composed of the very same letters they use in their speech, yet they are unable to produce anything comparable to it, thereby highlighting its miraculous nature and divine origin.

translation: This is a Book revealed to you, so let there be no distress in your heart from it, that you may warn thereby, and as a reminder to the believers.
interpretation: The verse serves as a divine reassurance to the Prophet Muhammad, commanding him to convey the message of the Qur'an with absolute confidence and steadfastness, despite the heavy burden of the responsibilities it entails or the opposition he might face from those who reject the truth, emphasizing that the primary purpose of this revelation is to serve as a beacon of caution for the heedless and a source of spiritual reflection and guidance for those who have already accepted faith.

translation: Follow what has been sent down to you from your Lord, and do not follow any protectors besides Him. Little do you take heed.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine command for the believers to adhere exclusively to the guidance provided by Allah through the Qur'an and the Sunnah of His Prophet, cautioning against the deviation of seeking spiritual guidance or absolute allegiance from sources that contradict the word of God, while simultaneously lamenting the human tendency to be forgetful of the ultimate authority and the consequences of disregarding it.

translation: And how many a city have We destroyed, and Our punishment came to it at night or while they were sleeping at midday.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning and a reminder of the fragility of human civilizations, illustrating that divine retribution is not bound by human expectations of time or preparedness; by striking when people are most vulnerable—either in the deep silence of the night or the midday rest—Allah demonstrates that no structure, fortification, or moment of relaxation can grant immunity against the inevitable consequences of persistent disbelief and moral corruption.

translation: And their cry, when Our punishment came to them, was only that they said, 'Indeed, we were wrongdoers.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the inherent nature of human denial in the face of inevitable divine justice; it describes how those who persistently reject the truth and mock the warnings of God throughout their lives eventually reach a moment of inescapable realization where their arrogance crumbles, forcing them to acknowledge their own culpability and transgression only when it is too late for repentance to benefit them.

translation: Then We will surely question those to whom [a message] was sent, and We will surely question the messengers.
interpretation: On the Day of Resurrection, Allah will hold both the communities to whom prophets were sent and the prophets themselves accountable. The nations will be questioned regarding whether they believed in the message delivered to them and how they acted upon it, while the messengers will be questioned regarding how they conveyed the divine revelation and whether they fulfilled the mission entrusted to them by Allah.

translation: Then We will surely relate to them with knowledge, and We were not absent.
interpretation: God affirms that on the Day of Resurrection, He will present a detailed and accurate account of every action humans performed during their worldly lives, as nothing—whether overt or hidden—ever escaped His perfect knowledge or presence, ensuring that His judgment is based on absolute truth and undeniable evidence.

translation: And the weighing [of deeds] that Day will be the truth. So those whose scales are heavy - it is they who will be the successful.
interpretation: The weighing of deeds on the Day of Resurrection will be characterized by absolute justice, where no one will be wronged. The believers who filled their lives with sincere faith and righteous deeds will find their scales heavy with virtue, leading them to attain eternal salvation and the pleasure of Allah.

translation: But those whose scales are light, they are the ones who have lost their souls, for they used to reject Our verses wrongfully.
interpretation: The lightness of the scales signifies the absence of faith and righteous deeds, which represents the ultimate loss, as a person who fails to believe in the truth of God’s signs has effectively squandered their own soul's potential for eternal salvation, choosing instead to suppress and deny the truth in favor of their worldly inclinations.

translation: And We have certainly established you upon the earth and made for you therein ways of livelihood; little are you grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the immense benevolence of Allah towards humanity by preparing the earth as a habitable dwelling place, providing all the essential resources, sustenance, and means of survival necessary for human existence. It serves as a profound reminder that despite the abundance of blessings and the sophisticated mechanisms of providence that allow life to flourish, human beings often fail to recognize the Giver of these gifts, demonstrating a lack of reflection and gratitude for the Divine support that sustains their daily lives.

translation: And We have certainly created you, [O mankind], and given you [human] form. Then We said to the angels, 'Prostrate to Adam'; so they prostrated, except for Iblis. He was not of those who prostrated.
interpretation: Allah recounts the story of human creation, emphasizing the nobility He bestowed upon the human species by shaping them and elevating their status. When He commanded the angels to prostrate to Adam, it was not an act of worship, but a gesture of honor and acknowledgment of the divine spirit breathed into him. The refusal of Iblis signifies the origin of arrogance and disobedience, as he chose to prioritize his perceived elemental superiority over the direct command of his Creator, thereby becoming the archetype of defiance and exclusion from God's mercy.

translation: [Allah] said, 'What prevented you from prostrating when I commanded you?' [Iblees] said, 'I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay.'
interpretation: This verse depicts the moment of Iblees's arrogance, where he attempts to justify his disobedience to Allah's command by using a flawed comparison based on his origin of creation. By claiming superiority through his elemental composition of fire over Adam's composition of clay, Iblees reveals the root cause of his fall: pride, which blinded him to the reality that obedience to the Creator's command is the ultimate measure of status, rather than the substance from which a being was fashioned.

translation: He said, 'Descend from it, for it is not for you to be arrogant therein. So get out; indeed, you are of the debased.'
interpretation: This verse signifies the divine decree of expulsion for Iblis from the high status he once occupied, serving as a definitive consequence of his pride. By commanding him to descend, Allah emphasizes that arrogance is entirely incompatible with a position of honor in His presence, illustrating that the pursuit of self-importance over divine command leads inevitably to spiritual degradation and humiliation.

translation: He said, 'Reprieve me until the day they are resurrected.'
interpretation: When Iblis realized the inevitability of his expulsion and curse, he did not seek repentance but rather exhibited arrogance by demanding a postponement of his punishment. By asking to be granted life until the Day of Resurrection, he aimed to fulfill his vow of tempting and leading the children of Adam astray, seeking to prove his claim that humanity is weak and easily swayed by worldly desires.

translation: He said, 'Indeed, you are of those reprieved.'
interpretation: This verse signifies that Allah granted Iblis a specific delay until the Day of Resurrection, not as a sign of favor or mercy, but as a test for mankind to distinguish those who follow divine guidance from those who succumb to the whispers and temptations of the devil, thereby fulfilling the divine decree regarding human accountability.

translation: He said, 'Because You have put me in error, I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path.'
interpretation: Iblis, acknowledging his expulsion from divine mercy, declares his vengeful intent to block the path of truth, signifying that he will employ every deceptive stratagem, temptation, and doubt to divert humanity from the way of faith and obedience to Allah, making his primary objective the moral and spiritual ruin of those who seek the straight path.

translation: Then I will come to them from before them and from behind them and on their right and on their left, and You will not find most of them grateful [to You].
interpretation: Iblis expresses his determination to systematically waylay and misguide humanity from every possible direction; he plans to make them neglect the afterlife by focusing on worldly affairs in front of them, dwell on past sins or doubts behind them, tempt them with false righteousness on their right, and entice them toward disobedience and sin on their left, ultimately leading them to become ungrateful for Allah's blessings and unmindful of His guidance.

translation: [Allah] said, "Get out of it, disgraced and expelled. Whoever follows you among them - I will surely fill Hell with you, all together."
interpretation: This verse signifies the definitive expulsion of Iblis from the presence and mercy of Allah due to his arrogance and disobedience. It serves as a stern warning to humanity that those who choose to align themselves with the path of the devil, rejecting the guidance of Allah, will share in his ultimate fate of humiliation and punishment in the fire of Hell.

translation: And [We said], 'O Adam, dwell, you and your wife, in Paradise and eat from wherever you will, but do not approach this tree, lest you be among the wrongdoers.'
interpretation: This verse signifies the divine instruction to Adam and Eve, granting them vast freedom and sustenance within Paradise while establishing a specific boundary. The prohibition serves as a test of obedience and restraint; by labeling the transgression as 'wrongdoing' (zulm), the verse emphasizes that disobedience to God's command is an act of injustice against one's own soul, as it disrupts the divine order and leads to the loss of one's privileged state.

translation: Then Satan whispered to both of them to expose to them that which was hidden from them of their private parts. He said, 'Your Lord did not forbid you this tree except that you become angels or become of the immortals.'
interpretation: Satan employed deception by masquerading as a sincere advisor, inciting their natural desire for longevity and elevated status to manipulate them into disobeying God. By suggesting that the fruit held the power to transform them into angelic beings or grant them eternal life, he exploited their human inclination toward growth and perfection, framing the forbidden act as a shortcut to a higher, imperishable existence.

translation: And he swore to them both, 'Indeed, I am to you a sincere advisor.'
interpretation: This verse describes the deception practiced by Iblis upon Adam and Eve, where he used a false oath in the name of Allah to gain their trust. By swearing to them that he was a well-wisher who wanted only their benefit, he manipulated their innocence and desire for eternal life, ultimately leading them to disobey Allah's command, thereby highlighting the cunning nature of Satan in using religious language and feigned sincerity to lead believers into sin.

translation: So he misled them with deception. And when they tasted of the tree, their private parts became apparent to them, and they began to fasten together over themselves from the leaves of Paradise. And their Lord called to them, 'Did I not forbid you from that tree and tell you that Satan is to you a clear enemy?'
interpretation: The verse highlights the cunning nature of Satan’s deception, illustrating how he uses false promises to lead humans into disobedience, and emphasizes that the immediate consequence of violating God's command was the loss of their state of innocence and the realization of their vulnerability, serving as a reminder that yielding to temptation results in shame and serves as evidence of the enmity Satan harbors against humanity.

translation: They said, 'Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the quintessential formula for repentance and spiritual restoration, demonstrating that the realization of one's own shortcomings and the humble admission of sin before God is the essential prerequisite for divine mercy; by acknowledging that their transgression was a harm done primarily to their own souls rather than a slight against God's majesty, Adam and Eve exhibited a profound level of sincerity, which serves as a timeless model for humanity to seek forgiveness through total reliance on God's grace to avoid the ultimate loss of spiritual salvation.

translation: Allah said, 'Descend, being to one another enemies. And for you on the earth is a place of settlement and enjoyment for a time.'
interpretation: This verse marks the beginning of the human experience on earth, following the expulsion of Adam and Eve from Paradise. It signifies that the enmity between humanity and Satan, as well as the potential for conflict among humans themselves, became an inherent reality of earthly life. Simultaneously, it establishes that the earth serves as a temporary dwelling place and a source of provisions for humans, highlighting the transient nature of worldly existence until the appointed time of death and the eventual return to Allah.

translation: He said, 'Therein you shall live, and therein you shall die, and from it you shall be brought forth.'
interpretation: This verse signifies the cyclical journey of the human soul and body in relation to the earth, illustrating that the world is the destined arena for human life, the site of physical death when the spirit departs, and the vessel from which God will resurrect all mankind on the Day of Judgment, highlighting the earth's role as a temporary cradle and a eventual witness to human accountability.

translation: O children of Adam, We have bestowed upon you clothing to conceal your private parts and as adornment. But the clothing of righteousness - that is best. That is from the signs of Allah that perhaps they will remember.
interpretation: Allah reminds humanity that beyond the physical garments He provided to cover their bodies and grant them dignity, there exists a superior form of covering known as the clothing of righteousness (taqwa). This spiritual garment, which involves guarding one's heart and deeds from disobedience, is the ultimate adornment for the soul. Just as physical clothing protects the body from exposure and harsh elements, piety protects the believer from the shame of sin and the severity of Divine punishment, serving as a constant reminder of Allah's grace and the accountability of the human soul.

translation: O children of Adam, let not Satan tempt you as he removed your parents from Paradise, stripping them of their clothing to show them their private parts. Indeed, he sees you, he and his host, from where you do not see them. Indeed, We have made the devils allies to those who do not believe.
interpretation: This verse serves as a profound warning to humanity that Satan’s primary method of deception is the removal of modesty and the corruption of moral boundaries, just as he deceived Adam and Eve to expose their nakedness. It highlights that Satan’s influence operates in the unseen realm, utilizing stealth and psychological manipulation to lead people astray, and emphasizes that the lack of faith acts as a spiritual barrier that leaves a person vulnerable to becoming a companion and ally to the forces of evil.

translation: And when they commit an immorality, they say, 'We found our fathers doing it, and Allah has ordered us to do it.' Say, 'Indeed, Allah does not order immorality. Do you say about Allah that which you do not know?'
interpretation: This verse addresses the human tendency to use ancestral traditions or inherited practices as a justification for actions that contradict divine commands. Allah explicitly rejects the claim that He would ever sanction shameful or immoral behavior, emphasizing that such attributions are grave lies. By challenging them with the question of whether they are speaking about Allah without knowledge, the verse teaches that religious justification cannot be based on blind imitation or unfounded claims, and that moral truth must be rooted in direct revelation rather than the convenient customs of the past.

translation: Say, 'My Lord has enjoined justice.' And set your faces [toward Him] at every place of prostration and call upon Him, sincere to Him in religion. Just as He originated you, so you will return.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the foundation of a believer's conduct is justice and fairness in all affairs. It instructs the believer to maintain complete focus and sincerity toward God during worship, regardless of the physical location. The final phrase serves as a reminder of the cycle of existence: just as God brought humanity into being from nothing, He possesses the power and the inevitable decree to recreate them after death for accountability, highlighting the necessity of living with a consciousness of this eventual return.

translation: A group He has guided, and a group [for whom] error has become deserved. Indeed, they had taken the devils as allies instead of Allah while they think that they are guided.
interpretation: The verse highlights the irony of those who strayed, explaining that their deviation was a consequence of their own choices in befriending malevolent forces, leading them into a state of deep self-deception where they falsely perceive their misguided actions and abandonment of divine guidance as the correct path of righteousness.

translation: O children of Adam, take your adornment at every masjid, and eat and drink, but be not excessive. Indeed, He likes not those who commit excess.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine guideline for moderation in both spiritual and worldly life; it instructs the believer to present themselves with dignity and respect when approaching the house of God, while simultaneously encouraging the enjoyment of worldly provisions such as food and drink, provided that one avoids the spiritual and physical harm caused by wastefulness and gluttony, reminding us that Allah does not favor those who transgress the boundaries of balance in their conduct.

translation: Say, 'My Lord has only forbidden immoralities - what is apparent of them and what is concealed - and sin, and oppression without right, and that you associate with Allah that for which He has not sent down authority, and that you say about Allah that which you do not know.'
interpretation: The verse outlines the fundamental ethical and theological boundaries established by Allah, encompassing all forms of indecent behavior, whether public or private, which degrade human dignity and social morality. It further emphasizes that forbidden acts include not only explicit sins and the unjust transgression against others' rights, but also the intellectual and spiritual vanity of associating partners with the Divine without evidence and the dangerous presumption of attributing religious dictates or descriptions to God without divine knowledge or revelation.

translation: And for every nation is a specified term. So when their time has come, they will not remain behind an hour, nor will they precede it.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of the absolute decree of Allah regarding the lifespan of civilizations and communities. It asserts that every group of people, like every individual, has a preordained period of existence determined by divine wisdom. When the appointed time for a nation's decline or transition arrives, it is governed by an immutable law that cannot be delayed by even a moment, nor can it be hastened. This reflects the sovereignty of Allah over time and history, emphasizing that human efforts, power, or negligence cannot alter the inevitable conclusion ordained for a society once its time has expired.

translation: O children of Adam, if messengers from among you come to you relating to you My verses, then whoever fears Allah and reforms, there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine warning and a promise to all humanity, reminding them that Allah provides guidance through messengers sent from their own kind who communicate His signs. The path to security and peace in both this world and the Hereafter is defined by two conditions: 'taqwa' (God-consciousness), which means abstaining from disobedience, and 'islah' (reforming one's actions), which means rectifying one's conduct and intentions. Those who fulfill these criteria are promised an immunity from the dread of the future and the sorrow of the past, as they have aligned their existence with the truth, thereby securing a state of eternal tranquility.

translation: And those who deny Our verses and are arrogant toward them - those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the root cause of disbelief and eternal punishment is a combination of rejecting the clear proofs of God and the internal disease of pride, which prevents the soul from submitting to the truth even after it has become manifest, thereby sealing the individual's fate in a state of permanent alienation from divine mercy.

translation: And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie about Allah or denies His signs? Those will obtain their portion of what is written, until when Our messengers come to them to take them in death, they will say, 'Where are those you used to invoke besides Allah?' They will say, 'They have departed from us,' and they will bear witness against themselves that they were disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the extreme gravity of fabricating falsehoods against Allah or rejecting His revelations, asserting that such individuals face the ultimate consequence of their actions when their appointed time of death arrives. The interrogation by the angels regarding the false deities they once worshipped serves as a profound moment of realization and humiliation, forcing the disbelievers to acknowledge that their idols are powerless and non-existent, thereby compelling them to testify against their own souls and admit to the truth of their disbelief which they had previously denied.

translation: [Allah] will say, 'Enter among nations which had passed on before you of jinn and mankind into the Fire.' Every time a nation enters, it will curse its sister until, when they have all overtaken one another therein, the last of them will say about the first of them, 'Our Lord, these had misled us, so give them a double punishment from the Fire.' [Allah] will say, 'For each is double, but you do not know.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the ultimate dissolution of the false loyalties and hierarchies formed in worldly life. When the followers and their leaders, who once conspired together in disbelief and transgression, meet in the afterlife, the bond of shared rebellion turns into mutual animosity. The followers realize that their leaders were the primary cause of their straying, and they seek to deflect their own culpability by demanding an extra measure of punishment for those who led them astray. Allah’s decree that 'each is double' signifies that justice is served to both: the leaders are punished for their own disbelief and for the sin of misguiding others, while the followers are punished for their own disbelief and for their willing submission to those who led them away from the truth.

translation: And the first of them will say to the last of them, 'Then you had no favor over us, so taste the punishment for what you used to earn.'
interpretation: This verse depicts the scene of mutual recrimination among the followers of misguidance on the Day of Judgment, where the later generations, who followed the earlier ones in disbelief, will be told by their predecessors that they are equally guilty and possess no superiority or excuse, and thus they must all taste the punishment as a direct consequence of the sins and evil deeds they committed during their earthly lives.

translation: Indeed, those who deny Our verses and are arrogant toward them - the gates of heaven will not be opened for them, nor will they enter Paradise until a camel enters into the eye of a needle. And thus do We recompense the criminals.
interpretation: The verse employs a vivid impossibility—a camel passing through the eye of a needle—to illustrate the total and definitive exclusion of the arrogant deniers from the spiritual realms and Paradise. By linking their pride and rejection of divine truth to this impossible act, the Quran emphasizes that their path to salvation is eternally barred, as their own self-aggrandizement and persistent defiance create an ontological state of incompatibility with the purity and grace of the heavenly domain.

translation: They will have a bed of Fire and, over them, coverings [of fire]. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the complete encompassment of the punishment for those who committed injustice and disbelief; they are surrounded by the Fire from beneath, serving as a mattress for them, and from above, acting as a canopy, signifying that they have no escape or relief from the torment that has entirely surrounded them as a direct consequence of their sins.

translation: But those who believe and do righteous deeds - We charge no soul except with that within its capacity - those are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: Allah emphasizes His boundless mercy and justice by clarifying that He does not burden any human beyond their physical or mental capability, thereby removing any excuse for failing to uphold faith and good deeds; this divine leniency ensures that those who strive sincerely according to their means will be rewarded with an eternal home in Paradise.

translation: And We will remove whatever is in their breasts of resentment, [while] flowing beneath them are rivers. And they will say, 'Praise to Allah, who has guided us to this; and we would never have been guided if Allah had not guided us. Certainly the messengers of our Lord had come with the truth.' And it will be called to them, 'This is Paradise, which you have been made to inherit for what you used to do.'
interpretation: Allah signifies the purification of the hearts of the believers in Paradise, removing all traces of enmity, hatred, or jealousy that might have existed in worldly life, so they may dwell in total peace and brotherly harmony; their subsequent admission that this reward is entirely a result of Allah's grace, while acknowledging that their good deeds were the outward manifestation of their faith that rendered them worthy of this divine inheritance.

translation: And the companions of Paradise will call out to the companions of the Fire, 'We have already found what our Lord promised us to be true. Have you found what your Lord promised to be true?' They will say, 'Yes.' Then an announcer will announce among them, 'The curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers.'
interpretation: This verse depicts the finality of divine justice and the realization of truth in the afterlife. The believers, having reached their destination, confront the inhabitants of Hell not out of malice, but to highlight the absolute fulfillment of Allah’s promises—both the reward of Paradise and the punishment of Hell. The acknowledgment by those in the Fire confirms that they were fully warned and given the truth, leaving them with no excuse. The subsequent proclamation of Allah's curse serves as a definitive separation, establishing that the wrongdoers are those who willfully rejected the truth, thereby separating themselves from divine mercy forever.

translation: Those who hinder people from the path of Allah, seeking to make it crooked, and they are disbelievers in the Hereafter.
interpretation: This verse describes the condition of the unjust who actively work to obstruct the guidance of Allah by distorting the truth, casting doubts, and presenting faith as something distorted or unreasonable, all driven by their fundamental rejection and disbelief in the accountability and eternal life of the Hereafter.

translation: And between them will be a partition, and on [its] elevations are men who recognize all by their mark. And they will call out to the companions of Paradise, 'Peace be upon you.' They have not [yet] entered it, but they long intensely to do so.
interpretation: This verse describes the state of the A'raf (the elevations or heights) on the Day of Judgment, where individuals whose good and bad deeds are equal remain separated from the people of Paradise. These individuals are depicted as recognizing both the believers and the disbelievers by their physical appearances, reflecting their profound state of suspense. Their greeting of peace to the people of Paradise demonstrates their inherent yearning for divine mercy and their hopeful anticipation of finally being admitted into the Garden, signifying that even in their state of uncertainty, they remain inclined toward righteousness and salvation.

translation: And when their eyes are turned toward the companions of the Fire, they will say, 'Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people.'
interpretation: This verse portrays the state of the people of the Heights (Al-A'raf) when they witness the inhabitants of Hell; their prayer reflects a profound fear of being associated with those who committed injustice through disbelief and rebellion, highlighting that even those not destined for punishment recognize the absolute horror of Hell and seek refuge in Allah's mercy to be kept far away from the company of the wicked.

translation: And the companions of the Heights will call to men they recognize by their marks, saying, 'Of no avail to you was your gathering and [all] the pride you used to exert.'
