translation: How can there be a treaty for the polytheists with Allah and His Messenger, except for those with whom you made a treaty at the Sacred Mosque? So as long as they are upright toward you, be upright toward them. Indeed, Allah loves the righteous.
interpretation: This verse serves as a declaration that the polytheists who repeatedly broke their oaths and engaged in treachery have forfeited their moral and legal standing to hold a covenant with the believers, as their actions demonstrate a fundamental lack of sincerity and commitment; however, the exception is made for those specific groups who remained loyal to their agreements at the Sacred Mosque, thereby establishing that righteousness and faithfulness are the true measures by which the believers must evaluate their relationships with others, emphasizing that piety requires upholding one's word so long as the other party remains committed to their obligations.

translation: How [can there be a treaty] while, if they gain dominance over you, they do not respect regarding you any kinship or covenant? They satisfy you with their mouths, while their hearts refuse [to fulfill what they say], and most of them are defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse warns the believers against trusting the hypocrites or those who break their oaths, explaining that their enmity is rooted in their hearts; they use sweet words and empty promises solely to deceive and gain an advantage, but they have no genuine commitment to agreements or moral obligations, revealing that their outward compliance is merely a strategic mask for their inner hostility and rebellion against God's commands.

translation: They have bartered the revelations of Allah for a small price, and have hindered (men) from His way. Evil indeed is what they have been doing.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern condemnation of those who intentionally compromise divine guidance for worldly advantages, emphasizing that by prioritizing transient material gains over the eternal truth of God's message, these individuals not only corrupt their own moral integrity but also become active obstacles preventing others from attaining spiritual salvation, thereby committing a grave transgression that will inevitably lead to their ruin.

translation: They do not observe toward a believer any bond of kinship or covenant of protection; and it is they who are the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the polytheists described have severed all moral and contractual obligations towards believers, demonstrating that their hostility is absolute and devoid of any restraint. Their refusal to honor ties of kinship or formal treaties reveals their deep-seated enmity, thereby confirming their status as those who have exceeded the limits of justice and conduct, rightfully earning the designation of transgressors.

translation: But if they repent, establish prayer, and give zakat, then they are your brothers in religion; and We detail the verses for a people who know.
interpretation: The verse establishes that the bond of faith is the ultimate unifying factor, transcending previous enmities; when those who were once opponents turn toward God through repentance, perform the obligatory prayer, and fulfill the social duty of zakat, they transition from a state of conflict to a state of absolute brotherhood, as their actions demonstrate a genuine commitment to the values and community of Islam.

translation: But if they violate their oaths after their treaty and defame your religion, then fight the leaders of disbelief, for indeed, there are no oaths [binding] for them, so that they might cease.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the sanctity of treaties is contingent upon the other party's adherence to them; when they openly betray their promises and attack the core tenets of the Islamic faith, they forfeit their protected status, and the believers are commanded to confront their leadership directly to dismantle the sources of hostility and aggression, thereby aiming to deter them from their continued oppression and deceit.

translation: Will you not fight a people who broke their oaths and determined to expel the Messenger, and they had begun [the attack upon] you the first time? Do you fear them? But Allah has more right that you should fear Him, if you are [truly] believers.
interpretation: Allah rebukes the believers for their hesitation in confronting those who violated their treaties, betrayed the community, and initiated hostility against the Prophet Muhammad. He reminds them that the fear of human opponents is misplaced when compared to the reverence and fear due to Allah, asserting that true faith is manifested by prioritizing divine command over the intimidation of enemies.

translation: Fight them; Allah will punish them by your hands and will disgrace them and give you victory over them and satisfy the breasts of a believing people.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine assurance to the believers that their engagement in conflict against those who committed aggression against them is not merely a human endeavor but a vessel through which Divine justice is executed; by achieving victory, the believers serve as the instruments of God's retribution, resulting in the public humiliation of the oppressors and the profound psychological healing of the faithful who had previously suffered from the injustice and intimidation inflicted upon them by their enemies.

translation: And He removes the rage in their hearts. And Allah turns in forgiveness to whom He wills; and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse signifies that Allah, through His grace and divine decree, has the power to pacify the souls of the believers after they have faced severe trials or conflicts, effectively removing the bitterness and emotional distress caused by their adversaries. By healing these hearts, Allah grants them internal peace and contentment, demonstrating that He is the ultimate orchestrator of human emotion and destiny, whose wisdom dictates that mercy and guidance are dispensed according to His infinite knowledge of each individual's sincerity and state.

translation: Do you think that you will be left alone while Allah has not yet made evident those among you who strive [for His cause] and who do not take other than Allah, His Messenger, and the believers as confidants? And Allah is Acquainted with what you do.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder that faith is not merely a verbal claim but must be proven through the crucible of trials and tribulations. The phrase regarding the 'confidant' (walija) highlights that true sincerity of faith requires an absolute allegiance to Allah, His Prophet, and the righteous believers, excluding any secret alliances or reliance upon those who oppose the divine message, as these struggles act as a necessary process to manifest the genuineness of a believer's commitment.

translation: It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of Allah, while they bear witness against themselves with disbelief. Those are the ones whose deeds have become worthless, and in the Fire they will abide eternally.
interpretation: The verse establishes a fundamental spiritual incompatibility between the state of polytheism and the guardianship of sacred spaces dedicated to the worship of the One God, asserting that those who openly deny the truth through their disbelief lack the moral and spiritual foundation required to tend to God's houses, and consequently, their external acts of service are rendered void of divine acceptance because their inner rejection of God nullifies the purpose of such devotion.

translation: The mosques of Allah are only to be maintained by those who believe in Allah and the Last Day and establish prayer and give zakah and do not fear except Allah, for it is expected that those will be among the [rightly] guided.
interpretation: The verse establishes that the true patronage and maintenance of the houses of God are not defined by physical construction alone, but by the spiritual qualification of the inhabitants; specifically, those who possess a sincere faith manifested through outward obedience and, most importantly, a heart that is exclusively tethered to the awe of the Creator, rendering them immune to worldly pressures or fear of anyone other than Allah in the fulfillment of His commands.

translation: Have you made the giving of water to the pilgrims and the maintenance of the Sacred Mosque equal to [the deeds of] one who believes in Allah and the Last Day and strives in the cause of Allah? They are not equal in the sight of Allah. And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: The verse clarifies that physical services performed for the Kaaba, even if virtuous in nature, cannot be equated with the superior rank of faith (iman) combined with righteous actions and striving (jihad) in the path of Allah. The Divine scale prioritizes the sincerity of heart and the depth of one's commitment to the faith over outward rituals or services when those services are detached from the foundation of true belief in Allah and the afterlife.

translation: Those who have believed, emigrated, and striven in the cause of Allah with their wealth and their lives are greater in rank in the sight of Allah. And it is those who are the attainers of success.
interpretation: This verse underscores that the true hierarchy of honor in the sight of God is not based on worldly status, lineage, or material wealth, but on the depth of one's commitment to faith through active sacrifice. By pairing belief with the difficult actions of migration and the expenditure of one's resources and life, the verse establishes that success is defined as achieving divine approval, a state reached only by those who prioritize their spiritual principles above their personal comfort and worldly possessions.

translation: Their Lord gives them good tidings of mercy from Him, and approval, and gardens for them wherein is enduring pleasure.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the ultimate reward for the believers who strive in the way of Allah is not merely the physical comforts of Paradise, but the profound spiritual honor of receiving direct affirmation from their Creator, which grants them tranquility, His eternal pleasure, and a state of permanent bliss that is never interrupted or diminished.

translation: Abiding therein forever; indeed, with Allah is a great reward.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine assurance to the believers, highlighting that the ultimate recompense for their faith and righteous deeds is an eternal residence in Paradise, a reward that is vast, incomparable, and everlasting, rooted in the infinite grace and generosity of Allah.

translation: O you who have believed, do not take your fathers or your brothers as allies if they have preferred disbelief over belief. And whoever does so among you - then it is those who are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the bond of faith is the foundational loyalty in Islam, transcending even the closest biological ties. Allah instructs believers that blood relations should not supersede the commitment to truth and divine guidance. If family members choose to persist in disbelief and actively oppose the faith, believers must prioritize their allegiance to Allah and His message, as choosing the support of disbelieving kin over the community of the faithful constitutes a grave injustice against one's own soul and the religion of truth.

translation: Say: If your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your spouses, your kinsfolk, the wealth you have acquired, the commerce you fear may slacken, and the dwellings you love are dearer to you than Allah and His Messenger and struggling in His cause, then wait until Allah brings about His command. And Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.
interpretation: This verse serves as a litmus test for the sincerity of a believer's faith, clarifying that the love for Allah and His Messenger must transcend all worldly attachments. It warns that when human emotions, family ties, and material comforts become prioritized over divine commandments and the pursuit of righteousness, the individual enters a state of spiritual rebellion. The warning to 'wait' is an invitation to reflect on the grave consequences of choosing fleeting worldly interests over the eternal rewards of divine obedience, signaling that such a preference effectively severs one from the path of divine guidance.

translation: Allah has already given you victory in many regions and [even] on the day of Hunayn, when your great number pleased you, but it did not avail you at all, and the earth was wide for you but then grew constrained, and you turned back, fleeing.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine reminder to the believers that victory comes solely from Allah's support, not from military numbers or material strength. By highlighting the Battle of Hunayn, where the Muslims felt confident due to their large numbers, Allah teaches that arrogance and reliance on worldly means lead to failure, as their vast ranks could not prevent their initial retreat when they lost sight of humble dependence on the Creator.

translation: Then Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers and sent down soldiers you did not see and punished those who disbelieved. And that is the recompense of the disbelievers.
interpretation: After the initial panic and disruption among the believers during the battle, Allah granted them a sense of inner peace and steadfastness that allowed them to regain their composure and remain firm in faith. He supported them with celestial forces—angels—that were invisible to the human eye, which turned the tide of the battle in their favor. This intervention was not only a manifestation of divine mercy for the believers but also a direct consequence for the disbelievers, whose arrogance and rejection of the truth led them to experience a humiliating defeat and painful chastisement, serving as a manifestation of the inevitable worldly outcome for those who stubbornly oppose God.

translation: Then Allah will accept repentance after that from whom He wills, and Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: This verse signifies that Allah’s mercy is expansive and constantly available to His servants, indicating that the door of repentance remains open for those who genuinely turn back to Him, regardless of their past transgressions, as His divine essence is defined by infinite forgiveness and overwhelming compassion.

translation: O you who have believed, indeed the polytheists are unclean, so let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram after this, their year. And if you fear privation, Allah will enrich you from His bounty if He wills. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse establishes a prohibition for polytheists to enter the sacred precincts of the Kaaba, signifying that their spiritual impurity—stemming from their association of partners with Allah—renders them unfit to frequent the house dedicated exclusively to His pure worship. The directive serves to purify the sanctuary from the presence of idolaters, while simultaneously reassuring the believers that the potential economic loss resulting from the cessation of trade with these groups will be compensated by Allah's grace, as His wisdom encompasses the needs of His servants and His knowledge ensures provision according to what is most beneficial for them.

translation: Fight those who do not believe in Allah or in the Last Day and who do not consider unlawful what Allah and His Messenger have made unlawful and who do not adopt the religion of truth from those who were given the Scripture - [fight them] until they give the jizyah willingly while they are humbled.
interpretation: This verse establishes the political and legal framework for the relationship between the Islamic state and the People of the Scripture who reject the authority of the Islamic governance, stipulating that they must pay the jizyah—a tax for protection and exemption from military service—as a manifestation of their submission to the state's sovereignty and a symbol of their acknowledgment of the new order established by the Prophet.

translation: The Jews say, 'Ezra is the son of Allah,' and the Christians say, 'The Messiah is the son of Allah.' That is their statement from their mouths; they imitate the saying of those who disbelieved before [them]. May Allah destroy them; how are they deluded?
interpretation: This verse highlights the absurdity and falsehood of the claims made by Jews and Christians regarding the divine sonship of Ezra and Jesus, respectively, describing their words as mere unsubstantiated utterances that mimic the polytheistic beliefs of previous generations who attributed offspring to the Divine, thus prompting a rebuke against those who persist in such fabrications despite the clear evidence of Allah's oneness.

translation: They have taken their scholars and monks as lords besides Allah, and [also] the Messiah, the son of Mary. And they were not commanded except to worship one God; there is no deity except Him. Exalted is He above whatever they associate with Him.
interpretation: The verse explains that the people of the Book committed shirk by granting their religious leaders the authority to declare things lawful or unlawful contrary to God's law. By obeying these leaders in acts of disobedience to Allah and elevating the Messiah to a divine status, they effectively worshipped them as lords, disregarding the core divine command to recognize Allah as the sole legislator and object of worship.

translation: They want to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah refuses except to perfect His light, although the disbelievers dislike it.
interpretation: The disbelievers seek to suppress the guidance and truth of Islam through their verbal opposition and false propaganda, but their efforts are utterly futile because Allah has decreed the triumph and spread of His faith; no matter how much those who reject the truth resist, the divine light of revelation will inevitably prevail and reach its completion.

translation: It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to manifest it over all religion, although the polytheists dislike it.
interpretation: The verse affirms that Allah commissioned His Messenger, Muhammad, with the Quran and a complete way of life to ensure that this divine truth prevails over all other ideologies and systems of belief. This ultimate triumph occurs through the inherent strength of the message's logic and its eventual historical dominance, serving as an immutable promise from Allah that, regardless of the resistance or animosity shown by those who associate partners with God, the light of Islam will persist and overcome all opposing falsehoods.

translation: O you who have believed, indeed many of the scholars and the monks devour the wealth of people unjustly and avert [them] from the way of Allah. And those who hoard gold and silver and spend it not in the way of Allah - give them tidings of a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning against religious leaders who exploit their positions to amass wealth through deception and prevent others from following the truth, while simultaneously condemning the act of hoarding wealth without fulfilling the mandatory obligation of charity, emphasizing that earthly accumulation detached from spiritual responsibility leads to severe divine retribution.

translation: On the Day when it will be heated in the fire of Hell and therewith their foreheads and their flanks and their backs will be branded, [it will be said], 'This is what you hoarded for yourselves, so taste what you used to hoard.'
interpretation: The verse illustrates the divine justice wherein the very wealth that people greedily accumulated while neglecting the rights of Allah and the needy becomes the instrument of their punishment, signaling that their obsession with worldly hoarding resulted in a spiritual burden that manifests as physical torment in the afterlife.

translation: Indeed, the number of months with Allah is twelve [lunar] months in the register of Allah [from] the day He created the heavens and the earth; of these, four are sacred. That is the correct religion, so do not wrong yourselves during them. And fight against the disbelievers collectively as they fight against you collectively. And know that Allah is with the righteous [who fear Him].
interpretation: This verse establishes that the cycle of twelve lunar months is a divinely ordained cosmic order instituted at the creation of the universe, and within this system, four months are sanctified during which aggression is prohibited. The command to 'not wrong yourselves' during these sacred months signifies that since the time is divinely honored, committing sins—whether through oppression or violating the sanctity of these months—is more grievous than at other times. Consequently, believers are urged to observe the limits of Allah, and while they are permitted to fight against those who attack them, they must do so with the consciousness that divine support is exclusively reserved for those who remain disciplined, pious, and observant of the moral boundaries set by God.

translation: Indeed, the postponing of sacred months is an increase in disbelief by which those who have disbelieved are led astray, making it lawful one year and unlawful another year to correspond to the number of months which Allah has made unlawful and thus making lawful what Allah has made unlawful. Their evil deeds have been made attractive to them. And Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse condemns the pre-Islamic practice of 'Nasi,' where the Arabs would manipulate the calendar by postponing the sanctity of a sacred month to a later one to accommodate their desire for continuous warfare or raiding. This act was not merely a chronological adjustment but a profound spiritual transgression, as it represented a defiant attempt to subvert divine law to suit human desires, effectively turning the forbidden into the permissible through human authority, which hardened their hearts and blinded them further from the truth of guidance.

translation: O you who have believed, what is [the matter] with you that, when you are told to go forth in the cause of Allah, you adhere heavily to the earth? Are you satisfied with the life of this world rather than the Hereafter? But what is the enjoyment of worldly life compared to the Hereafter except a [very] little.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern admonition to the believers, rebuking them for the tendency of human nature to cling to the comforts of worldly life and manifest lethargy or hesitation when called upon to sacrifice for the sake of higher, spiritual objectives. It highlights the stark disparity between the transient, fleeting pleasures of this world and the eternal, profound rewards of the afterlife, urging the believer to prioritize their ultimate spiritual destination over the temporary allure of material attachment.

translation: If you do not go forth, He will punish you with a painful punishment and will replace you with another people, and you will not harm Him at all. And Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to the believers that if they fail to uphold their responsibility to support the cause of truth and justice by shrinking from the struggle against oppression, they forfeit their status as the chosen instruments of Allah's work; consequently, they will face spiritual and worldly consequences, while Allah—Who is in no need of their assistance—will simply raise up a different, more resolute people to accomplish His purpose, thereby demonstrating that human inaction does not hinder the divine decree.

translation: If you do not help him, Allah has already helped him when those who disbelieved had driven him out, while he was the second of two, when they were in the cave, and he said to his companion, 'Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us.' And Allah sent down His tranquility upon him and supported him with soldiers you did not see and made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest, while the word of Allah is the highest. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine reassurance that the success of the Prophet’s mission does not depend on human effort alone, for Allah granted him victory even when he was at his most vulnerable state, accompanied only by one companion in the cave of Thawr. It highlights the profound companionship of Allah through His 'Sakina' (divine tranquility), which descended to protect and steady the Prophet’s heart, demonstrating that spiritual strength and divine intervention are more powerful than the collective schemes of disbelievers, ensuring that the ultimate supremacy belongs to the truth of Allah’s message over the falsehood of those who oppose it.

translation: Go forth, whether light or heavy, and strive with your wealth and your lives in the cause of Allah. That is better for you, if you only knew.
interpretation: Allah commands the believers to set out for struggle in His cause regardless of their circumstances, whether they find it easy or difficult, or whether they are young and active or old and burdened. It highlights that the sacrifice of one's personal wealth and life for the sake of divine justice is a superior path that ultimately benefits the believer’s soul and status, as worldly comfort is transient compared to the eternal reward of prioritizing the commandments of the Creator over personal ease.

translation: Had it been an immediate gain or a short journey, they would have followed you, but the distance seemed too far to them. Yet they will swear by Allah, 'If we had been able, we would have gone forth with you,' destroying themselves, while Allah knows that they are liars.
interpretation: This verse exposes the hypocrisy of those who sought excuses to avoid the hardship of the expedition to Tabuk; it highlights that their reluctance was driven by their love for comfort and ease, as they would only have participated if the endeavor offered material profit or lacked difficulty, and their subsequent false oaths regarding their inability to join the Prophet only served to further corrupt their own souls by compounding their deceit with perjury.

translation: May Allah forgive you, [O Prophet], why did you give them permission [to stay behind] before it was evident to you who were truthful and [before] you knew the liars?
interpretation: This verse reflects Allah's gentle guidance to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) regarding his decision to excuse those who sought permission to stay behind during the expedition of Tabuk. Allah explains that it would have been more advantageous for the Prophet to refrain from granting immediate permission, as the passage of time and the unfolding of events would have naturally exposed the sincerity of the believers who were genuinely excused and the hypocrisy of the liars who were merely looking for an escape from their duty.

translation: Those who believe in Allah and the Last Day do not ask you for exemption from fighting with their wealth and their lives. And Allah is Knowing of the righteous.
interpretation: The verse indicates that true faith in Allah and the afterlife creates an inherent motivation within the believer to sacrifice for the sake of the truth and the defense of their community, making the seeking of permission to evade such duties contrary to the sincere heart, for the one who possesses genuine piety understands that these sacrifices are a natural expression of their commitment to their faith.

translation: Only those who do not believe in Allah and the Last Day ask your permission [to stay behind], and their hearts have doubted, so they are hesitating in their doubt.
interpretation: This verse indicates that seeking exemption from the obligation of Jihad is a behavioral manifestation of inner hypocrisy, as the refusal to participate stems from a lack of genuine conviction in Allah's promise and the accountability of the afterlife, leaving their souls perpetually unsettled and swinging between conflicting worldly desires and the fear of social exposure.

translation: And if they had intended to go forth, they would have prepared for it some preparation. But Allah disliked their involvement, so He kept them back, and it was said, 'Remain with those who remain.'
interpretation: The verse highlights that their lack of participation in the cause of Allah was not merely a matter of circumstances, but a deliberate choice driven by internal hypocrisy. Allah prevented their movement not by forcing them against their will, but by exposing the insincerity of their intentions, thereby creating conditions that caused them to linger among the passive and weak-willed who had no genuine desire to strive for the truth.

translation: Had they gone forth with you, they would not have increased you except in confusion, and they would have been active among you, seeking to sow sedition among you; and among you are those who listen to them. And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse reveals the hidden treachery of the hypocrites who remained behind during the expedition of Tabuk, explaining that their presence within the ranks of the believers would have been a source of corruption and discord. Their participation would not have strengthened the Muslim army; rather, it would have created disunity and instability, as they would have actively incited conflict and spread falsehoods to weaken the resolve of the community. The mention of 'those who listen to them' warns the believers that there are individuals among them whose hearts are inclined toward the hypocrites' divisive rhetoric, and Allah, in His absolute knowledge, is fully aware of these deceitful individuals and their malicious intentions.

translation: They had already sought sedition before and upset matters for you until the truth came and the command of Allah appeared, while they were averse.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder to the Prophet Muhammad and the believers that the opposition faced from the hypocrites was not a new development; rather, it was the continuation of a long-standing pattern of sabotage, intrigue, and efforts to undermine the mission of Islam. Despite their relentless attempts to create discord and derail the truth through schemes and conspiracies, Allah’s decree ultimately prevailed, ensuring the victory and establishment of the faith, thereby exposing the futility of their hatred and their inability to obstruct the divine will.

translation: And among them is he who says, 'Permit me and do not tempt me.' Unquestionably, into temptation they have fallen. And indeed, Hell will encompass the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse addresses the hypocrites who sought excuses to avoid participating in the battle of Tabuk by claiming that the presence of Byzantine women would lead them into sin, yet in their refusal to obey the Prophet and their hesitation to strive in the cause of God, they had already succumbed to the greatest trial of hypocrisy and disobedience, a spiritual ruin that inevitably leads them to be trapped and consumed by the fire of Hell.

translation: If good comes to you, it distresses them; but if disaster strikes you, they say, 'We took our precaution beforehand,' and turn away, rejoicing.
interpretation: This verse describes the deep-seated hypocrisy of those who harbor hidden enmity toward the believers; they are so consumed by spite that any success or bounty bestowed upon the Prophet and his followers causes them anguish, while any misfortune that befalls the community serves to validate their arrogance, leading them to believe that their own tactical withdrawal or worldly caution was the reason for their own safety, a sentiment that manifests in joy rather than empathy.

translation: Say, 'Never will we be struck except by what Allah has decreed for us; He is our protector.' And upon Allah let the believers rely.
interpretation: This verse establishes the foundational Islamic doctrine of divine decree, emphasizing that a believer's life is governed entirely by the will and wisdom of Allah. It instructs the faithful to find solace and detachment from worldly anxieties by realizing that no harm or benefit can befall them unless it has been preordained by God. By declaring Allah as the ultimate 'Mawla' (protector and master), the believer is encouraged to release the burden of outcomes and place their complete trust and dependence solely in Him, transforming their reliance from external circumstances to a spiritual connection with the Creator.

translation: Say, 'Do you await for us except one of the two best things? While we await for you that Allah will afflict you with punishment from Himself or at our hands. So wait; indeed we, along with you, are waiting.'
interpretation: The verse highlights the fundamental difference in perspective between the believer and the disbeliever regarding the outcome of their struggle. For the believer, there is no possibility of a disadvantageous outcome: either they achieve victory and success in this world, or they attain the status of martyrdom, which is the ultimate success in the hereafter. Conversely, the believer assures the disbeliever that they are destined for divine retribution, which will come either directly through Allah's command—such as natural disasters or divine intervention—or through the victory of the believers over them. The final command to 'wait' serves as a manifestation of the believer’s absolute certainty and unwavering faith in the promise of Allah.

translation: Say, "Spend, willingly or unwillingly; never will it be accepted from you. Indeed, you have been a defiantly disobedient people."
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern declaration to the hypocrites that their outward contributions and charity, regardless of whether they are given voluntarily or under compulsion, are fundamentally rejected by God because their inner state is defined by a persistent rebellion against divine guidance and a lack of sincere faith, which nullifies the spiritual value of any good deed they perform.

translation: And nothing prevents their expenditures from being accepted from them except that they have disbelieved in Allah and in His Messenger and that they come not to prayer except while they are lazy and that they do not spend except while they are unwilling.
interpretation: The verse explains that the reason why the charities and good deeds of the hypocrites are not accepted by Allah is the absence of true faith in their hearts, which renders their outward actions devoid of sincerity; their reluctance in performing prayers and their resentment when giving to charity indicate that these acts are burdens they perform out of social pressure rather than genuine devotion, and since Allah only accepts deeds done with pure faith and voluntary submission, their hypocrisy disqualifies them from any spiritual reward.

translation: So let not their wealth or their children amaze you; Allah only intends to punish them through these things in this worldly life and that their souls should depart [at death] while they are disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse serves as a divine consolation for the believers, explaining that the abundance of wealth and children granted to the disbelievers is not a sign of divine favor or success. Instead, these worldly blessings are meant to be a source of anxiety, preoccupation, and worldly entanglement that distances them from spiritual truth, ultimately leading them to a state of spiritual ruin and a death devoid of faith, thereby increasing their punishment.

translation: And they swear by Allah that they are indeed among you, while they are not among you; but they are a people who are afraid.
interpretation: This verse reveals the deceitful nature of the hypocrites who mask their true beliefs by swearing oaths to belong to the community of believers; their behavior is driven by an intense, paralyzing fear of being exposed or harmed, which compels them to simulate loyalty rather than possessing genuine faith.

translation: If they could find a refuge, or caves, or any place to hide, they would turn towards it with haste, rushing recklessly.
interpretation: This verse portrays the extreme desperation and cowardice of the hypocrites, who are so repelled by the truth and the demands of faith that they would seize any opportunity to escape the presence of the Prophet and the accountability of the divine message, showing that their hearts are filled with such aversion that they would flee towards any shelter, no matter how miserable, rather than face the light of guidance.

translation: And among them are those who criticize you regarding the [distribution of] charities. If they are given from them, they are satisfied; but if they are not given from them, at once they become angry.
interpretation: This verse reveals the hypocrisy of certain individuals who claim to be part of the community but whose loyalty is conditional; their support for the Prophet and the cause of faith is not based on principles or sincerity, but on worldly gain. When they receive a share of the alms, they remain quiet and compliant, but their true colors are exposed the moment their personal greed is not satisfied, proving that their grievances against the leadership were never about justice, but purely about their own material interests.

translation: And if only they had been satisfied with what Allah and His Messenger gave them and said, 'Sufficient for us is Allah; Allah will give us of His bounty, and so will His Messenger; indeed, we are desirous toward Allah,' [it would have been better for them].
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine prescription for inner peace and spiritual contentment, teaching that true believers find their security not in material accumulation, but in the sufficiency of Allah's decree. By acknowledging that every provision—whether spiritual or worldly—comes ultimately from Him, the believer transcends the bitterness of worldly envy or greed, shifting their desire and focus toward the eternal favor of their Creator.

translation: And among them are those who abuse the Prophet and say, 'He is an ear.' Say, 'He is an ear of goodness for you, believing in Allah and believing the believers and a mercy to those who believe among you.' And those who abuse the Messenger of Allah - for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: The hypocrites mocked the Prophet Muhammad, calling him 'an ear' because he would listen to everything he was told and act upon it. Allah corrected them by stating that the Prophet's receptivity is actually a source of grace and truth; he filters information through his faith in Allah and his sincere commitment to the believers, serving as a compassionate guide for those among them who are truly faithful, while warning that those who persist in slandering him will face severe consequences.

translation: They swear by Allah to you to please you; but Allah and His Messenger are more worthy that they should please Him, if they are believers.
interpretation: The verse reveals the hypocrites' habit of using empty oaths to justify their behavior and appease the believers, exposing the inconsistency of their faith; it asserts that true believers prioritize the satisfaction of Allah and His Messenger over the opinion of people, as seeking worldly approval at the expense of divine commands is a sign of a shaky and insincere faith.

translation: Do they not know that whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger, then for him is the fire of Hell, to abide therein eternally? That is the great disgrace.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning against those who deliberately set themselves in opposition to the divine command and the guidance brought by the Prophet; it asserts that such defiance constitutes a fundamental rejection of truth, the ultimate consequence of which is an everlasting state of spiritual and physical alienation from God's mercy in the afterlife, representing the pinnacle of human failure and humiliation.

translation: The hypocrites are apprehensive lest a surah should be revealed about them, informing them of what is in their hearts. Say, 'Mock as you wish; indeed, Allah will bring to light that which you fear.'
interpretation: This verse reveals the deep-seated anxiety of the hypocrites who live in constant fear that the divine revelation will expose their hidden treachery and secret intentions to the Prophet and the believers, and it serves as a stern warning from God that their attempts to conceal their true nature are futile because His omniscient decree will inevitably manifest their hidden malice and bring it into the open for all to see.

translation: And if you ask them, they will surely say, 'We were only conversing and playing.' Say, 'Is it Allah and His verses and His Messenger that you were mocking?'
interpretation: This verse addresses those who hide their hypocrisy behind the excuse of jesting or idle talk when confronted about their mockery of religious matters; it underscores that such serious subjects as Allah, His revelations, and His Prophet are far beyond the scope of trivial banter, and that ridiculing them is a profound act of disbelief that cannot be dismissed as mere lighthearted entertainment.

translation: Do not make excuses; you have disbelieved after your belief. If We pardon a faction of you, We will punish a faction because they were criminals.
interpretation: This verse addresses the hypocrites who mocked the faith during the expedition of Tabuk, asserting that their excuses for their mockery are invalid because their behavior constitutes a definitive act of disbelief that has nullified their previous profession of faith. The divine decree clarifies that while Allah may show mercy to those among them who truly repent or were misled, divine justice will inevitably overtake the core group of persistent criminals who actively incited and engaged in these acts of disbelief.

translation: The hypocrite men and hypocrite women are of one another. They enjoin what is wrong and forbid what is right and close their hands. They have forgotten Allah, so He has forgotten them. Indeed, the hypocrites are the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inherent characteristics of hypocrites, noting that they form a cohesive network of moral corruption by actively promoting vice and suppressing virtue. Their 'closing of hands' symbolizes a deep-seated stinginess and a refusal to contribute to the cause of Allah. By choosing to ignore Allah's guidance and neglect His remembrance, they have effectively cut themselves off from His mercy and divine attention, resulting in a state where they are rightly classified as those who have completely abandoned obedience to God.

translation: Allah has promised the hypocrite men and hypocrite women and the disbelievers the fire of Hell, wherein they will abide eternally. It is sufficient for them. And Allah has cursed them, and for them is an enduring punishment.
interpretation: This verse signifies that Allah has decreed a definitive and inescapable recompense for those who feign belief while harboring disbelief in their hearts, alongside those who openly reject the truth. By stating that Hellfire is 'sufficient for them,' the verse underscores that their own transgressions have earned them a state of complete deprivation from divine mercy, resulting in a state of eternal alienation and a suffering that remains constant and never ceases.

translation: Like those before you who were stronger than you in power and more abundant in wealth and children. They enjoyed their portion of the world, so you have enjoyed your portion as those before you enjoyed theirs, and you engaged in vain talk like they engaged in it. Those are the ones whose deeds have become worthless in this world and the Hereafter, and it is they who are the losers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning that material prosperity, numerical strength, and worldly influence are not evidence of Divine favor, as these were possessed in greater measure by previous nations who rejected the truth. By mirroring their predecessors' focus on transitory worldly pleasures and their practice of mocking or disputing divine revelations, the hypocrites of the Prophet's time effectively nullified the merit of their own actions, rendering their worldly efforts and their hopes for the afterlife futile because they chose the perishable gain over the eternal reality.

translation: Has there not reached them the news of those before them - the people of Noah and 'Aad and Thamud and the people of Abraham and the companions of Madyan and the towns overturned? Their messengers came to them with clear proofs. And Allah would not have wronged them, but they were wronging themselves.
interpretation: The verse serves as a stern admonition to the disbelievers of Mecca, reminding them that the destruction of past nations was not an act of divine injustice or capriciousness, but a direct consequence of their own rejection of clear truth and divine guidance. By persisting in rebellion despite the arrival of messengers armed with undeniable miracles, these civilizations dismantled their own moral and spiritual foundations, thereby inviting the catastrophic punishments that befell them; thus, the destruction was the inevitable harvest of their own persistent defiance against the truth.

translation: The believing men and believing women are allies of one another. They enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong and establish prayer and give zakah and obey Allah and His Messenger. Those - Allah will have mercy upon them. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the bond of faith creates a spiritual and social unity among believers, characterized by mutual support and collective responsibility. By enjoining virtue and forbidding vice, and by maintaining their duties to Allah through prayer, charity, and obedience, believers actively cultivate a righteous society. The promise of divine mercy is the direct outcome of this cohesive commitment to moral integrity and devotion, reflecting that Allah's governance is rooted in His perfect power and ultimate wisdom, ensuring that those who uphold His commandments are brought under His protection and grace.

translation: Allah has promised the believing men and believing women gardens beneath which rivers flow, to abide therein forever, and pleasant dwellings in gardens of perpetual residence; but approval from Allah is greater. That is the great attainment.
interpretation: While the physical delights of Paradise, such as the flowing rivers and the magnificent, pure mansions, are immense rewards for the believers, the verse highlights that the true peak of felicity is the divine pleasure and acceptance of Allah. This spiritual closeness and the realization that their Creator is pleased with them constitutes a joy and a status that surpasses all material pleasures of the afterlife, representing the ultimate success for which every soul should strive.

translation: O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites and be harsh upon them. And their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination.
interpretation: This verse commands the Prophet to adopt a stance of firmness and uncompromising strength against those who openly reject the faith and those who pretend to believe while harboring malice, as their deceit and opposition threaten the spiritual and social integrity of the community of believers.

translation: They swear by Allah that they did not say [anything offensive], but they did indeed utter the word of disbelief and disbelieved after their Islam. They planned that which they could not attain, and they were not resentful except [for the fact] that Allah and His Messenger had enriched them of His bounty. So if they repent, it is better for them; but if they turn away, Allah will punish them with a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter, and they will not have on earth any protector or helper.
interpretation: This verse addresses a group of hypocrites who attempted to deny their blasphemous remarks against the Prophet. Their core resentment stems from the fact that Allah and His Messenger had granted them economic prosperity and success, yet instead of showing gratitude for these blessings, they plotted against the faith. The verse serves as both a stern warning of the inevitable consequence of their persistent betrayal and an open invitation to sincere repentance, emphasizing that their worldly plots are futile against the divine decree and that they possess no power to shield themselves from Allah's judgment.

translation: And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah, saying, 'If He should give us from His bounty, we will surely spend in charity and will surely be among the righteous.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocritical nature of some individuals who make sincere-sounding promises to Allah during times of hardship, pledging that if they were to attain worldly wealth, they would dedicate it to charity and righteous deeds. However, the verse serves as a warning against the inconsistency of human nature, suggesting that such people often fail to honor their commitments once their worldly desires are satisfied, revealing that their initial promises were born of superficial lip service rather than a firm, lasting resolve rooted in true faith.

translation: But when He gave them of His bounty, they were stingy with it and turned away, while they were averse.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the hypocrisy of those who make solemn vows to God in times of hardship, promising that if He grants them wealth or success, they will become righteous and charitable. However, once God answers their prayers and bestows His favor upon them, their hearts harden; they succumb to greed and break their covenants, turning away from obedience to God and showing complete indifference to the commitments they once made.

translation: So He penalized them with hypocrisy in their hearts until the Day they will meet Him, because they failed to fulfill what they promised Allah, and because they used to lie.
interpretation: This verse explains that the consequence of breaking one's covenant with Allah after witnessing His signs is a spiritual hardening; the hypocritical behavior they chose becomes deeply embedded in their hearts as a permanent state, effectively blinding them to truth and preventing repentance until the moment they face God on the Day of Judgment.

translation: Do they not know that Allah knows their secret and their private conversations and that Allah is the Knower of the unseen?
interpretation: This verse serves as a powerful rhetorical admonition, reminding the disbelievers and the hypocrites that their attempts to conceal their true intentions and malicious plots are futile, as the Divine encompassment of knowledge extends to the most hidden depths of the human heart and the most whispered, private communications, affirming that there is no threshold of privacy from the Creator who possesses perfect, absolute, and exhaustive knowledge of everything that is hidden from created beings.

translation: Those who criticize the contributors among the believers concerning [their] charities and [criticize] those who find nothing [to give] except their effort, so they ridicule them - Allah will ridicule them, and they will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning against the hypocrites who mock the believers for their contributions; they insult the wealthy who give generously by accusing them of ostentation, and they mock the poor who have nothing to offer but their meager physical labor, labeling their efforts as insignificant. The divine response reflects the principle of reciprocating action: because they treated the sincere devotion of the believers with derision and contempt, Allah will subject them to a humiliation far greater than the mockery they inflicted, culminating in a severe and agonizing punishment for their lack of sincerity and their malicious interference in the good deeds of others.

translation: Whether you ask forgiveness for them, or do not ask forgiveness for them—if you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, Allah will never forgive them. That is because they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger; and Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.
interpretation: This verse demonstrates that the state of hardened disbelief and rebellion against Allah and His Messenger reaches a point where the person has completely severed their connection to divine grace, rendering the Prophet's intercession ineffective; the mention of 'seventy times' is an idiomatic expression in Arabic indicating a multitude of attempts, emphasizing that even if the Prophet were to intercede repeatedly, the persistent state of defiance and denial displayed by these hypocrites makes them unworthy of forgiveness, as Allah's guidance is withdrawn from those who consciously choose to remain in a state of willful corruption.

translation: Those who remained behind rejoiced at their staying behind the Messenger of Allah and disliked to strive with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah, and they said, 'Do not go forth in the heat.' Say, 'The fire of Hell is more intense in heat,' if they could understand.
interpretation: This verse exposes the hypocrisy and cowardice of those who feigned excuses to avoid the struggle for justice and truth, revealing that their attachment to worldly comfort and fear of hardship blinded them to the ultimate consequence of their choices, as the fleeting heat of a summer day is incomparable to the eternal agony of those who choose ease over divine responsibility.

translation: So let them laugh a little and weep much as recompense for what they used to earn.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to the disbelievers, illustrating the temporary nature of worldly enjoyment compared to the eternal consequences of their actions; it suggests that the fleeting pleasure they experience through their arrogance and defiance in this life will inevitably be transformed into profound, lasting sorrow in the afterlife, where their deeds will be returned upon them in full measure as a just punishment.

translation: If Allah returns you to a group of them and they ask your permission to go out [to battle], say, 'You will not go out with me ever, and you will not fight with me an enemy. Indeed, you were satisfied with sitting the first time, so sit [now] with those who remain behind.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a disciplinary measure against the hypocrites who abandoned the Prophet during a previous expedition. By forbidding them from joining future battles, Allah exposes their lack of sincerity and loyalty. The command for them to remain with the 'khāliffīn'—those who stay behind—is a form of social and spiritual ostracization, indicating that their previous choice to avoid hardship has disqualified them from the honor and blessing of participating in the noble struggle alongside the believers, effectively sealing their exclusion from the inner circle of the faithful due to their persistent treachery.

translation: And do not pray [the funeral prayer] over any of them who has died - ever - or stand at his grave. Indeed, they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger and died while they were defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine prohibition directed at the Prophet Muhammad, and by extension the entire Muslim community, forbidding them from performing funeral rites or showing spiritual honor toward the hypocrites who openly opposed Islam. It signifies that when an individual persists in their rejection of divine truth and passes away in a state of rebellion against God, they have severed their bond with the community of believers; therefore, the outward displays of intercession and mourning reserved for the righteous are no longer applicable to them, as their final state confirms their total rejection of the faith.

translation: And let not their wealth and their children impress you. Allah only intends to punish them through these things in this worldly life and that their souls should depart [at death] while they are disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine consolation to the Prophet and the believers, explaining that the apparent abundance of worldly blessings bestowed upon the disbelievers is not a sign of Allah's pleasure or favor. Instead, these worldly possessions act as a source of continuous anxiety, preoccupation, and conflict for them, ultimately serving as a means of torment that distracts them from truth and leads them to a state of spiritual ruin, ensuring they remain in their disbelief until their final moments.

translation: And when a surah was revealed, enjoining, 'Believe in Allah and fight alongside His Messenger,' the wealthy among them asked your permission [to stay behind] and said, 'Let us be with those who remain.'
interpretation: This verse exposes the hypocrisy of some wealthy individuals among the believers who, despite their resources, shirked the responsibility of defending the faith by seeking excuses to avoid participating in struggle alongside the Prophet, preferring the safety and comfort of staying behind with the weak and those who had no obligation to fight.

translation: They were content to be with those who remained behind, and their hearts have been sealed, so they do not understand.
interpretation: This verse describes a spiritual state of hypocrisy where individuals consciously choose idleness, comfort, and separation from the path of moral and spiritual struggle, leading to a condition where their hearts become impenetrable to the truth; as a consequence of this willful persistence in apathy, God seals their hearts, rendering them incapable of perceiving the reality of faith or grasping the profound wisdom that benefits them in the hereafter.

translation: But the Messenger and those who believed with him fought with their wealth and their lives. It is they who will have the good things, and it is they who are the successful.
interpretation: This verse highlights that true success and ultimate reward are reserved for the Prophet and the believers who demonstrated the sincerity of their faith through concrete action, specifically by sacrificing their material resources and their physical lives for the cause of God. By equating faith with selfless striving, the verse establishes that the path to eternal prosperity and salvation requires both internal conviction and outward dedication, ensuring that those who endure in this struggle are the ones who will attain the abundant blessings of the afterlife.

translation: Allah has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide eternally. That is the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate reward granted by Allah to those who are righteous and obedient, describing their recompense as eternal dwellings of luxury and peace. The mention of gardens with flowing rivers serves as a metaphor for divine grace and abundant provision, emphasizing that the true success and supreme victory lie not in worldly accumulation, but in securing a permanent state of contentment and proximity to Allah in the afterlife, which far surpasses any transient achievements of this world.

translation: And those among the Bedouins who had excuses came to be permitted [to stay behind], while those who lied to Allah and His Messenger sat at home. A painful punishment will strike those among them who disbelieved.
interpretation: This verse exposes the hypocrisy of those who claimed false excuses to avoid the struggle for the cause of truth, contrasting them with the true believers who remained steadfast, and warns that those who persist in their denial and deceit against the Divine message will inevitably face a severe and sorrowful consequence for their insincerity.

translation: There is no blame upon the weak or upon the sick or upon those who do not find anything to spend if they are sincere to Allah and His Messenger. There is no cause for blame against the doers of good. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse establishes that Allah exempts those who are physically incapacitated by weakness or illness, or those who lack the financial means to support the cause of faith, from the duty of physical or material participation in battle, provided their hearts remain sincerely devoted to Allah and His Messenger. It clarifies that such individuals are not sinful for their inability to act, as the criteria for blame or punishment are removed from those who demonstrate righteousness, sincerity, and virtue, thereby emphasizing that Allah judges His servants based on their intentions and their capabilities rather than solely on outward deeds.

translation: Nor is there any blame on those who, when they came to you to provide them with mounts, and you said: 'I can find no mounts for you,' they turned back, their eyes overflowing with tears out of grief that they could find nothing to spend [for the cause of Allah].
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine exoneration for the sincere believers who were physically or financially unable to join the Prophet in battle. Their deep sorrow and the shedding of tears upon realizing they could not contribute to the cause of Allah demonstrate that true faith is measured by the intention and the yearning of the heart rather than just external physical action. It confirms that Allah judges the believers based on their earnest desire and sincere distress when they are prevented by genuine circumstances from doing good.

translation: The path of blame is only against those who ask your permission while they are rich, content to be with those who remain behind. Allah has set a seal upon their hearts, so they do not know.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the moral censure and accountability fall upon those who possess the physical and financial means to join the cause of truth but choose to seek exemptions for selfish comfort. By preferring the company of the idle and the weak-willed, they demonstrate a spiritual decay that leads God to withdraw their ability to perceive the consequences of their choices and the gravity of their negligence, leaving them in a state of willful ignorance regarding their own moral ruin.

translation: They will make excuses to you when you return to them. Say, 'Do not make excuses; we will never believe you. Allah has already informed us of your affairs. And Allah will observe your deeds, and [so will] His Messenger; then you will be taken back to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you of what you used to do.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine warning to those who claim faith outwardly while harboring hypocrisy, indicating that their excuses for failing to accompany the Prophet in battle are known to be false. It emphasizes that their insincerity is not hidden from Allah or His Messenger, and ultimately, they cannot escape the accountability of the Hereafter, where their true intentions and actions will be fully exposed and judged by the One who encompasses all that is hidden and manifest.

translation: They will swear by Allah to you when you return to them that you might leave them alone. So leave them alone; indeed, they are impurity, and their refuge is Hell as recompense for what they used to earn.
interpretation: The verse commands the believers to adopt a stance of total detachment and avoidance towards the hypocrites who deceitfully justify their failure to join the campaign. By labeling the hypocrites as 'rijs' (impurity), the Quran emphasizes that their inner corruption, lack of sincerity, and persistent inclination toward falsehood make them spiritually unclean, rendering any attempt at reconciliation or social indulgence with them harmful to the integrity of the community of faith; thus, their ultimate destination in Hell is a direct consequence of the deliberate and sinful choices they cultivated throughout their lives.

translation: They swear unto you, that you may be pleased with them. But if you are pleased with them, indeed Allah is not pleased with the disobedient people.
interpretation: This verse warns the believers against being deceived by the false oaths of hypocrites who seek to win their favor. It serves as a reminder that the approval of the believers is irrelevant if those individuals remain persistently defiant and rebellious against the commandments of Allah, as divine displeasure is the ultimate judgment that renders the worldly approval of others meaningless.

translation: The Bedouins are stronger in disbelief and hypocrisy and more likely not to know the limits of what Allah has revealed to His Messenger. And Allah is Knowing, Wise.
interpretation: This verse addresses the nature of the desert-dwelling Bedouins who were distant from the centers of revelation and Islamic instruction, noting that their lack of exposure to the Quranic teachings and the refined company of the Prophet made them more prone to stubborn disbelief and duplicity, as their hearts remained hardened by their isolation and lack of understanding regarding the divine laws and religious boundaries established by Allah.

translation: And among the bedouins are those who consider what they spend as a loss and await for you turns of misfortune. Upon them will be a misfortune of evil. And Allah is Hearing, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse describes a group of hypocritical Bedouins who view the compulsory alms or contributions they make for the sake of Allah not as an investment for the afterlife, but as a burdensome financial penalty; their true allegiance lies against the believers, as they wait for the community of faith to face catastrophic turns of events and defeat, yet the divine justice ensures that the very calamities they plot for others will ultimately encompass them, for Allah hears their whispered conspiracies and knows the hidden corruption of their hearts.

translation: And among the bedouins are some who believe in Allah and the Last Day and consider what they spend as means of nearness to Allah and of obtaining the prayers of the Messenger. Unquestionably, it is a means of nearness for them. Allah will admit them into His mercy. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights that faith is not defined by one's societal status or place of residence, but by the sincerity of one's actions and devotion. The Bedouins mentioned here are praised for their genuine intention to transform their material wealth into spiritual capital, viewing their charity not merely as an obligation but as a vehicle for divine closeness and a means to receive the Prophet’s intercessory prayers, which in turn elevates their spiritual state and guarantees them admission into God's boundless grace.

translation: And the foremost, the first of the Emigrants and the Helpers and those who followed them in goodness - Allah is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him, and He has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever. That is the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the immense spiritual status of the earliest Muslims—the Muhajirun who left their homes for the sake of faith, and the Ansar who welcomed and supported them—along with those who follow their footsteps in righteousness. The divine pleasure mentioned reflects a reciprocal state where God accepts their deeds and grants them His proximity, while they find ultimate contentment in His decree and reward, culminating in an eternal life of bliss as the supreme achievement for the human soul.

translation: And among those around you of the bedouins are hypocrites, and [also] from the people of Madinah. They have become accustomed to hypocrisy. You, [O Muhammad], do not know them, [but] We know them. We will punish them twice [in this world]; then they will be returned to a great punishment.
interpretation: The verse highlights the hidden nature of the hypocrites who resided in and around Medina, noting that even the Prophet Muhammad was not initially aware of their true intentions due to their deceptive outward behavior. The promise of being punished twice in this world refers to the humiliation and fear they experience upon the exposure of their secrets, along with the calamities or divine retribution that strikes them, serving as a prelude to the severe, eternal torment awaiting them in the afterlife for their persistent duplicity.

translation: And others have confessed their sins; they had mixed a righteous deed with another that was evil. It is hoped that Allah will turn to them in forgiveness; indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse describes the state of believers who are not perfect; they occasionally fall into sin but maintain their faith and perform righteous deeds. By admitting their shortcomings and repenting, they demonstrate a sincerity that makes them candidates for Allah's divine grace, as their honest acknowledgment of their human frailty invites the encompassing mercy of God.

translation: Take from their wealth a charity by which you cleanse them and purify them, and pray for them. Indeed, your prayer is a source of tranquility for them. And Allah is Hearing, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the act of giving charity (Zakat) serves as a spiritual means for the believer to rid themselves of the impurities of greed and miserliness, while simultaneously elevating their soul toward righteousness. The command for the Prophet to pray for those who give is a divine instruction highlighting that the Prophet's supplications bring peace, reassurance, and spiritual comfort to the hearts of the believers, confirming that his intercession acts as a source of divine mercy and stability for the community of the faithful.

translation: Do they not know that it is Allah who accepts repentance from His servants and takes the charities, and that it is Allah who is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the boundless mercy of Allah, highlighting that His door to repentance remains perpetually open for those who return to Him sincerely, and that He graciously accepts righteous deeds, such as charity, directly from the believer, treating them with honor and kindness as if He receives them Himself before purifying and rewarding them, which serves as a reassurance that no effort toward righteousness goes unnoticed or unappreciated by Him.

translation: And say, 'Work, for Allah will see your deeds, and [so will] His Messenger and the believers. And you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you of what you used to do.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine command for believers to strive earnestly in their righteous actions, emphasizing that their deeds are not hidden but are constantly observed by Allah, His Messenger, and the community of believers. It functions as a reminder that human activity is subject to accountability; the transparency of one's actions in this life is a prelude to the ultimate manifestation of truth in the afterlife, where Allah will reveal the reality of every deed, whether hidden or public, and recompense each soul accordingly.

translation: And others are deferred until the command of Allah: either He will punish them or He will forgive them. And Allah is Knowing, Wise.
interpretation: This verse refers to those believers who committed sins and failed to participate in the expedition or duty mentioned in preceding context, leaving their fate suspended in uncertainty until Allah decides whether to accept their repentance or punish them for their negligence, reflecting His absolute wisdom and knowledge in discerning the state of their hearts and the appropriateness of either mercy or retribution.

translation: And those who built a mosque for causing harm, disbelief, and division among the believers, and as an outpost for those who had previously fought against Allah and His Messenger—they will surely swear, 'We intended nothing but good.' But Allah bears witness that they are indeed liars.
interpretation: This verse exposes the duplicity of the hypocrites who constructed the 'Mosque of Harm' (Masjid al-Dirar) not for the sake of worship, but as a strategic base to undermine the Muslim community, provide shelter to enemies of the Prophet, and cause schisms among the faithful; it highlights that regardless of how noble an act may appear outwardly or what pious justifications are offered by the perpetrators, Allah judges actions based on their true underlying intent, exposing those who mask treacherous schemes behind a facade of religious devotion.

translation: Do not stand within it ever. A mosque founded on righteousness from the first day is more worthy for you to stand in. Within it are men who love to purify themselves; and Allah loves those who purify themselves.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that the value of a place of worship is determined by the sincerity of intention and the purity of those who frequent it, rather than the building itself. By contrasting the hypocrites' mosque, which was built to sow discord, with the mosque built on piety, it establishes that true spiritual sanctity is derived from devotion to God and the inward and outward cleanliness of the believers who gather there.

translation: Is then he who laid the foundation of his building on piety to Allah and His good pleasure better, or he who laid the foundation of his building on an edge of a crumbling precipice, so that it tumbled down with him into the fire of Hell? And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse presents a profound parable comparing the inner state and the ultimate destiny of two types of believers: those who act with sincere devotion and the fear of Allah as their bedrock, ensuring stability and spiritual permanence, versus those whose deeds are built upon hypocrisy, pride, or unstable worldly foundations, which lack spiritual integrity and will inevitably lead to ruin, just as a building constructed on a collapsing cliff must surely fall into the abyss.

translation: The structure which they have built will not cease to be a source of hypocrisy and misgiving in their hearts, unless their hearts are cut into pieces. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: The verse illustrates that the hypocrites' deliberate construction of a structure intended to sow discord and harm the believers will forever remain a cause of inner torment and spiritual corruption for them, as they have severed their connection with truth; this internal unrest will persist within their souls until they experience the finality of death, as it is only through their own destruction or the complete shattering of their hardened hearts that the deceit they harbor will cease, and Allah, in His supreme wisdom and knowledge, allows this outcome as a consequence of their persistent rebellion.

translation: [The believers are] the repentant, the worshippers, the praisers [of Allah], the travelers [for His cause], those who bow and prostrate [in prayer], those who enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and those who observe the limits [set by] Allah. And give good tidings to the believers.
interpretation: This verse delineates the exalted characteristics of the true believers, highlighting that their devotion to Allah is not merely internal but manifests through active worship, a lifestyle characterized by spiritual vigilance, and a firm commitment to upholding divine moral standards within society, all of which serve as the qualifying conditions for receiving the ultimate promise of success and glad tidings from Allah.

translation: It is not for the Prophet and those who have believed to ask forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they were relatives, after it has become clear to them that they are companions of the Hellfire.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the bond of faith supersedes all ties of kinship, including those of blood; therefore, it is impermissible for believers to intercede or seek divine pardon for those who knowingly chose to die in a state of disbelief and hostility toward God, as their final destination in the afterlife has been irrevocably sealed by their persistent rejection of the truth.

translation: And Ibrahim's asking of forgiveness for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him, but when it became clear to him that he was an enemy to Allah, he dissociated himself from him. Indeed, Ibrahim was compassionate and forbearing.
interpretation: The verse clarifies that Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him) had promised his father he would pray for his forgiveness in the hope that he would eventually accept the faith. However, when it became manifest to Ibrahim through divine revelation that his father would die in a state of persistent disbelief and enmity toward Allah, he stopped praying for him entirely. This highlights that a believer's loyalty must ultimately lie with the truth of Allah’s guidance, and even the most tender relationships must be severed if they constitute enmity against the Creator, demonstrating that Ibrahim's soft-hearted nature was balanced by his unwavering commitment to his Lord.

translation: And it is not for Allah to lead a people astray after He has guided them until He makes clear to them what they should avoid. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah's justice is perfect; He does not hold people accountable for error or misguidance unless He has first provided them with clear guidance and established the truth for them through revelation and signs. By clarifying what is forbidden and what leads to harm, Allah removes any excuse for the believers, ensuring that their accountability is based on conscious knowledge rather than ignorance.

translation: Indeed, to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He gives life and causes death, and you have not besides Allah any protector or any helper.
interpretation: This verse establishes the absolute sovereignty of Allah over all existence, emphasizing that since He is the sole Creator who governs the cycles of life and death, He is the only entity deserving of worship and reliance, rendering all other purported sources of aid or authority powerless against His decree.

translation: Allah has already forgiven the Prophet and the Muhajirin (emigrants) and the Ansar (helpers) who followed him in the hour of difficulty after the hearts of a party of them had almost inclined to doubt; then He forgave them. Indeed, He is to them Kind and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's boundless mercy in pardoning the believers, including the Prophet's companions, who experienced a moment of wavering or psychological struggle during the difficult expedition of Tabuk.
