It serves to comfort the believers, teaching that even if hearts are momentarily shaken by the severity of hardship or trial, Allah's grace encompasses those who remain steadfast in their commitment to His cause, ultimately stabilizing their faith and rewarding their eventual perseverance.

translation: And [He also forgave] the three who were left behind, until the earth, despite its vastness, was narrow for them, and their souls were straitened for them, and they realized that there is no refuge from Allah except unto Him. Then He turned to them [in forgiveness] so that they might repent. Indeed, Allah is the Accepting of Repentance, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound spiritual anguish experienced by the three companions who remained behind from the Battle of Tabuk, illustrating that the true essence of repentance is not merely a verbal declaration, but a state of soul-crushing remorse where one feels the walls of the world closing in due to the weight of their own conscience, ultimately leading to the realization that the only path to salvation is to seek refuge in Allah's mercy, a state which Allah rewards with His acceptance and guidance.

translation: O you who have believed, fear Allah and be with those who are true.
interpretation: This verse calls upon the believers to cultivate a constant consciousness of Allah in all their affairs while simultaneously urging them to seek the company of those whose words, intentions, and actions are marked by absolute truthfulness and sincerity, as surrounding oneself with righteous and honest people serves as a vital safeguard for the soul and a catalyst for maintaining steadfastness on the path of faith.

translation: It was not for the people of Madinah and those around them of the bedouins that they remain behind after the Messenger of Allah or prefer themselves over his own life. That is because they are not afflicted by thirst or weariness or hunger in the way of Allah, nor do they tread any ground that enrages the disbelievers, nor do they inflict upon an enemy any infliction but that it is registered for them as a righteous deed. Indeed, Allah does not allow to be lost the reward of the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the reward for the believer in the path of Allah is not limited to the final victory or the outcome of the struggle, but encompasses every moment of difficulty and every action taken for His sake. It teaches that the spiritual value of a deed is found in the endurance of hardship and the intention of upholding the truth, such that even the fatigue or suffering experienced while standing against injustice is recorded as a virtuous act by God, who validates and preserves the efforts of those who strive with excellence and sincerity.

translation: And they do not spend any expenditure, small or large, nor do they cross a valley, but it is recorded for them so that Allah may reward them for the best of what they were doing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the comprehensive nature of divine justice and record-keeping, emphasizing that no deed—regardless of how insignificant it may seem in the eyes of humans—goes unnoticed by Allah. It serves as a consolation for those striving in the path of truth, assuring them that every minor sacrifice and every step taken in pursuit of righteousness is registered in their favor, ensuring that on the Day of Judgment, their reward will be determined by the excellence of their intentions and the highest quality of their actions.

translation: And it is not for the believers to go forth [to battle] all together. For there should separate from every division of them a group [to remain] to obtain understanding in the religion and warn their people when they return to them that they might be cautious.
interpretation: This verse establishes the essential principle that the pursuit of religious knowledge is a collective responsibility that must be balanced with other communal duties; since it is not feasible for every single believer to abandon their societal roles for military mobilization, a dedicated group must instead focus on deep intellectual and spiritual study so that they may act as guides, preserving the integrity of the faith and instructing their community to righteousness upon their return.

translation: O you who have believed, fight those adjacent to you of the disbelievers and let them find in you harshness. And know that Allah is with the righteous.
interpretation: This verse establishes a tactical principle of prioritization in defending the faith, instructing believers to focus their efforts first on the enemies closest to them to neutralize immediate threats, while maintaining a firm and formidable demeanor that discourages aggression, all while being reminded that ultimate victory and support are reserved for those who remain mindful of Allah's commandments.

translation: And whenever a surah is revealed, there are some among them who say, 'Which of you has this increased in faith?' As for those who believe, it increases them in faith, and they rejoice.
interpretation: The verse illustrates how the revelation of the Qur'an serves as a spiritual litmus test: while hypocrites respond with skepticism or mockery to downplay its impact, the believers experience a genuine increase in their conviction and spiritual contentment, finding profound joy and reassurance in the guidance provided by Allah.

translation: But as for those in whose hearts is disease, it has only added wickedness to their wickedness, and they will have died while they are disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse illustrates the spiritual decline of the hypocrites, whose persistent rejection of truth and tendency toward deceit create a cycle of corruption within their hearts; because they chose to harden themselves against divine guidance, every new revelation only serves to further expose their inner impurity and solidify their state of disbelief until their eventual death.

translation: Do they not see that they are tested once or twice every year? Yet they do not repent, nor do they reflect.
interpretation: The verse highlights the spiritual negligence of the hypocrites who, despite being exposed to recurring trials and hardships—whether through divine warnings, worldly calamities, or the uncovering of their plots—remain obstinately attached to their disbelief. Their failure to repent or learn from these recurring tribulations signifies a profound hardening of their hearts, preventing them from recognizing the repeated opportunities provided by Allah to return to the path of guidance and truth.

translation: And whenever a surah is revealed, they look at one another, saying, 'Does anyone see you?' Then they turn away. Allah has diverted their hearts because they are a people who do not understand.
interpretation: The verse illustrates the deep-seated hypocrisy of those who feigned faith while in the company of the Prophet; upon the revelation of a new chapter of the Qur'an that might expose their secrets or rebuke their actions, they would exchange anxious glances to check if any believer was observing their discomfort, and then quickly slip away. Their departure signifies a deliberate spiritual turning away from the truth, which led Allah to seal their hearts and deprive them of divine guidance, as a just consequence of their persistent refusal to comprehend the message or reflect upon the signs presented to them.

translation: There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves, who is distressed by the suffering you endure, full of concern for your well-being, and toward the believers, he is most kind and merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophet Muhammad's profound empathy for his people, illustrating that he is not a distant figure but one deeply connected to the human experience of his followers. His concern for their spiritual and worldly welfare is driven by a genuine love that causes him to feel their pain as his own, acting as a compassionate guide who desires their salvation and ease above all else, which manifests in his gentle and merciful treatment of the believers.

translation: But if they turn away, say, 'Sufficient for me is Allah; there is no deity except Him. On Him I have relied, and He is the Lord of the Great Throne.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine instruction to the Prophet Muhammad, and by extension all believers, to maintain absolute reliance on Allah when faced with rejection or opposition from others. It emphasizes that when a person has fulfilled their duty of conveying the truth and faces worldly turning away or hostility, they should find complete solace and sufficiency in Allah alone. By affirming His unity and declaring Him the Lord of the Great Throne—the seat of His sovereignty and majesty—the believer anchors their heart in the realization that no human response can diminish their security, as their ultimate refuge and reliance are placed upon the Creator of the universe.

translation: Alif-Lām-Rā. These are the verses of the Wise Book.
interpretation: The verse highlights the divine authority and precision of the Qur'an, identifying it as a 'Wise Book' because it contains eternal truths, clear guidance, and laws that perfectly balance human needs, reflecting the profound wisdom of its Creator which transcends the limited intellect of man.

translation: Is it a wonder to the people that We revealed to a man from among themselves, 'Warn the people and give good news to those who believe that they have a position of honor with their Lord'? The disbelievers say, 'Indeed, this is a clear magician.'
interpretation: The verse highlights the stubborn arrogance of the disbelievers who find the concept of divine revelation to a human being impossible to accept. They reject the message not because it lacks truth, but because they disdain that the messenger is a fellow human, choosing instead to label the clear truth as sorcery to justify their refusal to acknowledge their accountability and the noble standing promised to those who maintain their faith.

translation: Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days and then established Himself above the Throne, arranging the matter. There is no intercessor except after His permission. That is Allah, your Lord, so worship Him. Then will you not be reminded?
interpretation: This verse establishes the absolute sovereignty and oneness of Allah, highlighting that He is the sole Creator and Sustainer of the universe, whose authority over all affairs is total and independent. It emphasizes that no being, regardless of their status or closeness to Him, has the power to intercede for anyone on the Day of Judgment without His express authorization, thereby affirming that all hope for salvation and mercy must be directed toward Him alone and that human intellect should naturally lead to the recognition of His divinity and the necessity of sincere worship.

translation: To Him is your return all together. [It is] the promise of Allah [which is] truth. Indeed, He begins the creation and then repeats it that He may reward those who have believed and done righteous deeds in justice. But those who disbelieved will have a drink of scalding water and a painful punishment for what they used to deny.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine assurance of the inevitability of the Day of Resurrection, emphasizing that just as God possessed the power to initiate human life from nothing, He possesses the absolute authority to reconstitute it. It highlights that the cycle of creation is not a purposeless act but a deliberate mechanism established to manifest divine justice, ensuring that individuals receive the ultimate consequences of their worldly actions—rewarding the faithful for their virtues and requiting the deniers for their persistent rejection of the truth.

translation: It is He who made the sun a shining light and the moon a derived light and determined for it phases - that you may know the number of years and account [of time]. Allah has not created this except in truth. He details the verses for a people who know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine precision in the creation of the celestial bodies, explaining that the sun's constant radiance and the moon's changing phases were established as a cosmic clock to regulate human life, commerce, and worship, underscoring that the universe is governed by purposeful, objective truth rather than random chance, intended for those who possess the knowledge and intellect to reflect upon the signs of the Creator.

translation: Indeed, in the alternation of the night and the day and [in] what Allah has created in the heavens and the earth are signs for a people who fear Him.
interpretation: This verse directs the believer to contemplate the constant cycle of time and the vast complexity of the cosmos as tangible evidence of a Creator's absolute power and wisdom, indicating that only those who possess a heart mindful of God—characterized by piety and an awareness of their accountability—will derive spiritual benefit and guidance from observing these natural phenomena.

translation: Indeed, those who do not expect the meeting with Us and are satisfied with the life of this world and feel secure therein, and those who are heedless of Our signs-
interpretation: This verse describes individuals whose hearts are completely attached to the material world, leading them to disregard the reality of the Hereafter and the accountability that accompanies it. Because they have chosen to be content with the transient pleasures of earthly life and find comfort in its false sense of security, they become blind and indifferent to the divine signs manifested in the universe and the revelations of Allah, which eventually leads to their spiritual stagnation and ultimate loss.

translation: Those—their refuge is the Fire, because of what they used to earn.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the eternal abode of the disbelievers and wrongdoers is the Hellfire, which serves as a direct consequence and recompense for the sinful actions and worldly deeds they chose to commit during their lives on earth.

translation: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - their Lord will guide them because of their faith; beneath them rivers will flow in the Gardens of Pleasure.
interpretation: The verse explains that faith serves as a divine light and a path of guidance that leads the believer to eternal felicity; as one consistently aligns their inner belief with outward righteous deeds, Allah grants them deeper insight, clarity, and steadfastness in this life, which ultimately culminates in their entry into the Gardens of Paradise where they will dwell in perpetual bliss and divine grace.

translation: Their call therein will be, 'Exalted are You, O Allah,' and their greeting therein will be, 'Peace.' And the last of their call will be, 'Praise to Allah, Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the state of the believers in Paradise, indicating that their hearts will be so filled with the glorification of Allah and the realization of His perfection that their every utterance will naturally begin with praising Him. The mention of 'Peace' as their greeting signifies a realm completely free from conflict, malice, or harm, while the conclusion of their call—'Praise to Allah, Lord of the worlds'—serves as a final realization that all grace, sustenance, and eternal joy they experience are solely due to the bounty and sovereignty of Allah, bringing their consciousness to a perfect state of gratitude and contentment.

translation: And if Allah were to hasten for the people the evil as He hastens for them the good, their term would have been ended. But We leave those who do not expect the meeting with Us to wander blindly in their transgression.
interpretation: The verse illustrates the divine attribute of patience and mercy; just as humans are quick to ask for what they perceive as good, they are also prone to making hasty, self-destructive prayers in moments of anger or impatience. If Allah were to grant these rash requests for harm as swiftly as He responds to pleas for goodness, humanity would be destroyed by its own impulses. Therefore, Allah allows time for those who deny the afterlife to persist in their arrogance, providing them with a period of respite in which they might yet turn back, even though they continue to drift in their state of moral blindness.

translation: And when affliction touches man, he calls upon Us, whether lying on his side or sitting or standing; but when We remove from him his affliction, he continues [in disobedience] as if he had never called upon Us to remove an affliction that touched him. Thus is made attractive to the transgressors that which they have been doing.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the inconsistency of the human soul when it is in a state of detachment from God; people often turn to their Creator with sincere desperation when faced with hardship, seeking immediate relief, yet once that relief is granted and the trial is lifted, they revert to their former state of negligence or arrogance, acting as if they were never in need. This behavioral pattern is described as a form of self-deception, where their repetitive indulgence in disobedience is made to seem justifiable or insignificant to them, blinding them to the reality of their gratitude and their dependence on the Divine.

translation: And We had already destroyed generations before you when they did wrong, and their messengers had come to them with clear proofs, but they were not to believe. Thus do We recompense the criminal people.
interpretation: This verse serves as a historical warning, asserting that the destruction of past civilizations was not a random occurrence but a direct consequence of their persistent oppression and rejection of divine truth; God emphasizes that despite the clarity of the signs provided by His messengers, these nations chose disbelief out of stubbornness and arrogance, establishing a recurring divine law that accountability and retribution inevitably follow those who consciously choose to transgress against the truth.

translation: Then We made you successors in the land after them, so that We may observe how you behave.
interpretation: God places successive generations on Earth not merely to occupy it, but as a test of their moral and spiritual responsibility, signifying that every civilization is granted a period of authority to manifest their obedience or disobedience to His laws, and their actions will determine their outcome in the hereafter.

translation: And when Our verses are recited to them as clear evidences, those who do not expect the meeting with Us say, 'Bring us a Qur'an other than this or change it.' Say, 'It is not for me to change it on my own accord. I only follow what is revealed to me. Indeed I fear, if I should disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous Day.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubborn arrogance of the disbelievers who, instead of submitting to the manifest truth of the Qur'an, attempted to dictate terms to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) by demanding he alter the message to suit their desires. The Prophet's response establishes his absolute role as a faithful conveyor of Divine Revelation; he is not the author of the scripture but its servant, strictly bound by the words revealed to him by Allah. His refusal to compromise the message, rooted in his fear of Divine accountability, underscores that the Qur'an is immutable, objective truth that cannot be subjected to human whim, social pressure, or personal preference.

translation: Say, 'If Allah had willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made it known to you, for I had remained among you a lifetime before it. Then will you not reason?'
interpretation: The Prophet Muhammad is commanded to challenge the Meccan disbelievers by highlighting his own history among them; he spent forty years of his life in their midst as an ordinary man known for truthfulness, never reciting scripture or composing poetry, which proves that the Qur'an is not a product of his own intellect or literary creation, but rather a direct revelation from Allah that he could only have brought forth by divine will.

translation: And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie about Allah or denies His verses? Indeed, the criminals will not succeed.
interpretation: This verse serves as a rhetorical condemnation of those who reject the truth, emphasizing that the greatest form of injustice—far beyond worldly wrongdoing—is the act of attributing false teachings to God or dismissing the clear signs of His divinity; such individuals are described as 'criminals' because they have fundamentally severed their connection to the ultimate truth, ensuring that they will not attain salvation or the ultimate success in the eternal life.

translation: And they worship other than Allah that which neither harms them nor benefits them, and they say, 'These are our intercessors with Allah.' Say, 'Do you inform Allah of something He does not know in the heavens or on the earth?' Exalted is He and high above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse serves as a critique of the polytheists who direct their worship toward idols or created beings, erroneously believing that these entities possess the power to intercede on their behalf before God. The Qur'an dismisses this claim by rhetorically asking if they possess knowledge of any such intercessors that God Himself is unaware of, thereby emphasizing that God’s omniscience encompasses all existence; since He has declared no such partners or intercessors, any claims to the contrary are mere fabrications born of human ignorance and false theology, rendering their worship both futile and a violation of the divine oneness.

translation: And mankind was not but one community, then they differed. And if not for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been judged between them regarding that over which they differ.
interpretation: Mankind was originally united upon the true religion and natural disposition of monotheism; however, through the intervention of personal desires and worldly attachments, they diverged into conflicting paths. The delay in divine judgment is not due to a lack of awareness of their differences, but rather a manifestation of Allah's decree to grant humanity a period of respite until an appointed time, allowing individuals the opportunity to seek guidance and repent before the final resolution of their affairs.

translation: And they say, 'Why is a sign not sent down to him from his Lord?' Say, 'The unseen belongs only to Allah; so wait, for I am among you with those who wait.'
interpretation: The disbelievers persist in demanding physical miracles of their own choosing to confirm the Prophet's message, yet the Prophet Muhammad is commanded to clarify that absolute knowledge of the unseen—including the timing and nature of divine signs—rests solely with Allah, thereby redirecting their focus from stubborn skepticism to a state of patient anticipation for the ultimate judgment that will distinguish between truth and falsehood.

translation: And when We let the people taste mercy after adversity which has touched them, at once they have a plan concerning Our verses. Say, "Allah is swifter in planning. Indeed, Our messengers record that which you plan."
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning against those who, upon receiving relief and divine favor after a period of hardship, respond with mockery, deception, or arrogance toward the signs of Allah. Rather than expressing gratitude, they attempt to undermine the truth and conspire against the divine message. The verse clarifies that any human attempt to scheme against Allah's truth is futile, for His ability to execute His decree and bring retribution is infinitely faster and more powerful than their deceptive efforts, and every action they take is meticulously recorded by the angels to be accounted for on the Day of Judgment.

translation: It is He who enables you to travel on land and sea, until, when you are in ships and they sail with them by a favorable wind and they rejoice therein, there comes a storm wind and the waves come upon them from everywhere and they assume that they are encircled, they supplicate Allah, [being] sincere to Him in religion, 'If You should save us from this, we will surely be among the thankful.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the inherent human tendency to turn exclusively toward God when faced with imminent destruction or helplessness, revealing how people often ignore the Divine during times of ease and prosperity but recognize His absolute authority when their worldly means of safety are stripped away by the raw power of nature.

translation: But when He saves them, at once they commit injustice upon the earth without right. O mankind, your injustice is only against yourselves, [being merely] the enjoyment of worldly life; then to Us is your return, and We will inform you of what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern reminder of human ingratitude, noting that those who pray sincerely to God in times of distress often revert to arrogance and transgression once they are delivered. The Quranic wisdom here is that the harm of such moral rebellion ultimately circles back to the transgressor themselves, as the fleeting gains and pleasures of worldly life are temporary distractions that obscure the inevitable accountability one faces when returning to their Creator.

translation: The example of the worldly life is but like rain which We have sent down from the sky, so the vegetation of the earth absorbs it—things whereof men and cattle eat—until, when the earth has taken on its adornment and is beautified and its people suppose that they have power over it, there comes to it Our command by night or by day, and We make it as a harvest, as if it had not flourished yesterday. Thus do We explain in detail the signs for a people who give thought.
interpretation: This verse presents a profound metaphor for the ephemeral nature of worldly existence, comparing the rapid growth and sudden decay of vegetation to the human journey. It cautions against the human tendency toward arrogance and the illusion of self-sufficiency, highlighting that at the peak of prosperity and control, man is most vulnerable to the swift intervention of divine decree. The imagery serves to remind believers that the beauty and stability of this world are transient, and that true wisdom lies in reflecting upon these signs to prioritize the eternal over the temporary.

translation: And Allah invites to the Home of Peace and guides whom He wills to a straight path.
interpretation: Allah invites all of humanity to Paradise, which is characterized by peace and safety from all evils, defects, and hardships; however, He grants the success of actually following the guidance toward that path only to those whose hearts are prepared to accept the truth, illustrating that while the invitation is universal, the attainment of guidance is a manifestation of His divine wisdom and favor.

translation: For those who do good is the best reward and extra. No darkness or humiliation will cover their faces. Those are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: The 'best reward' refers to Paradise as the ultimate recompense for the believers, while the 'extra' signifies the supreme grace of beholding the Countenance of Allah, which is the greatest honor granted to the righteous, ensuring their faces remain radiant, untarnished by the gloom of sin or the shame of judgment.

translation: But those who have earned evil deeds - the recompense of an evil deed is its equivalent, and humiliation will cover them. They will have from Allah no protector. It will be as if their faces are covered with pieces of the night, so dark. Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse warns that the ultimate consequence of persisting in sin is a deep, psychological, and spiritual darkness that clings to the human soul. Just as physical darkness obscures vision, the accumulation of sins strips away the light of guidance from a person's heart, leading to a state of profound alienation from Allah where no one can shield them from the inevitable realization of their error, resulting in a state of perpetual despair and loss in the afterlife.

translation: And the Day We will gather them all together, then We will say to those who associated others with Allah, 'Remain in your place, you and your partners.' Then We will separate them, and their 'partners' will say, 'You did not use to worship us.'
interpretation: This verse describes the scene on the Day of Judgment when Allah will confront the polytheists and their false deities. The command to 'remain in your place' signifies a moment of intense judgment and separation, where the false gods—whether they were idols, angels, or pious people—will explicitly disavow any connection to the worship directed toward them. By stating 'You did not use to worship us,' these deities imply that the polytheists were merely following their own whims, desires, and misinterpretations, rather than the actual gods they claimed to serve, highlighting the utter futility and self-deception of shirk (polytheism) when faced with the absolute truth of the afterlife.

translation: Sufficient is Allah as a witness between us and you that we were of your worship unaware.
interpretation: This verse signifies that on the Day of Judgment, when the idols or entities that were worshipped alongside Allah are brought forth, they will deny any knowledge of those who worshipped them. They will declare that Allah is the ultimate witness to the fact that they were completely oblivious to the devotion directed towards them, thereby dissociating themselves from the polytheists and exposing the futility of their misguided worship.

translation: There, every soul will realize what it has put forth, and they will be returned to Allah, their true Lord, and what they used to invent will vanish from them.
interpretation: On the Day of Resurrection, every individual will attain complete awareness and certainty regarding the deeds they performed during their worldly life, facing the consequences of their past actions as they are brought before Allah, the only true Master and Sovereign. In that definitive state of truth, all the false deities, idols, and fabricated justifications they once relied upon will prove to be utterly powerless and will cease to exist or provide any benefit, leaving the soul to account for its reality before its Creator.

translation: Say, 'Who provides for you from the heaven and the earth? Or who controls hearing and sight? And who brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living? And who arranges [every] matter?' They will say, 'Allah,' so say, 'Then will you not fear Him?'
interpretation: The verse employs a rhetorical challenge, compelling the polytheists to acknowledge that Allah alone possesses the exclusive attributes of sovereignty: the provision of sustenance, the creation and regulation of sensory faculties, the power over life and death, and the administration of the entire cosmic order. By forcing them to admit that their own logic dictates the existence of a single, omnipotent Creator, the verse exposes the irrationality of their idolatry and calls them to abandon their heedlessness by adopting a state of God-consciousness (taqwa) that reflects their stated acknowledgement of His lordship.

translation: Such is Allah, your Lord, the Truth. And what can there be after the truth except misguidance? How then are you turned away?
interpretation: This verse serves as a rhetorical ultimatum emphasizing that Allah is the singular, absolute reality and the only source of objective truth; consequently, any belief or path that deviates from His worship and guidance is inherently fallacious and leads to nothing but ruin, prompting a reflective inquiry into why human beings would consciously choose the errors of falsehood over the clarity of divine truth.

translation: Thus has the word of your Lord come to pass upon those who defiantly disobeyed, that they will not believe.
interpretation: This verse signifies that because these individuals persistently chose to reject the truth and continuously rebelled against divine guidance despite receiving clear signs, Allah, in His perfect justice, has sealed their hearts so that they are no longer capable of choosing faith, serving as a consequence for their own voluntary rejection of the truth.

translation: Say, 'Is there of your partners any who begins creation and then repeats it?' Say, 'Allah begins creation and then repeats it, so how are you deluded?'
interpretation: This verse presents a profound rational challenge to the polytheists, compelling them to acknowledge the exclusivity of Allah’s creative power. It highlights that the capability to originate life from nothing is the fundamental proof of lordship, and that the one who performs the first act of creation is logically the only one capable of recreating it, thereby exposing the absurdity and falsity of attributing divine status to idols that have no power to create or restore life.

translation: Say, 'Are there among your partners any who guides to the truth?' Say, 'Allah guides to the truth.' So is He who guides to the truth more worthy to be followed or he who does not guide [anyone] unless he is guided? Then what is [wrong] with you? How do you judge?'
interpretation: This verse serves as a logical refutation of polytheism by challenging the idolaters to identify any of their false deities capable of providing genuine guidance toward the truth. Since only Allah possesses the attribute of knowledge and the ability to guide hearts, it is logically inconsistent and irrational to follow beings that are themselves blind, powerless, and in need of guidance from their Creator. The verse condemns the cognitive dissonance of the polytheists, who abandon the All-Knowing Guide in favor of inanimate objects that lack the capacity to discern or direct anyone.

translation: And most of them follow nothing but conjecture. Indeed, conjecture avails nothing against the truth. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what they do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inherent fallibility of human speculation and opinion when placed in opposition to divine truth. It asserts that subjective beliefs, inherited traditions, or baseless assumptions cannot replace or nullify the objective, absolute truth revealed by Allah, as certainty cannot be attained through mere guesswork. The verse serves as a warning that while humans may attempt to justify their actions through conjecture, they cannot hide their intentions or their reliance on falsehoods from Allah, who possesses comprehensive knowledge of all their deeds and their motivations.

translation: And it was not for this Qur'an to be produced by other than Allah, but it is a confirmation of what was before it and a detailed explanation of the [former] Scripture, about which there is no doubt, from the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse asserts that the Qur'an possesses an inimitable nature that proves it could not have been fabricated by any human being, as it bears the unmistakable hallmark of divine origin. It functions as a corroboration of the foundational truths present in the preceding scriptures—such as the Torah and the Gospel—while simultaneously providing a clear, comprehensive clarification of the eternal laws and guidance that Allah has decreed for humanity, thereby establishing its absolute authority as a definitive revelation free from any falsehood or uncertainty.

translation: Or do they say, 'He has invented it?' Say, 'Then bring a surah like it and call upon whom you can besides Allah, if you should be truthful.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine challenge to the skeptics who claimed that the Prophet Muhammad fabricated the Qur'an. Allah commands the Prophet to invite these disbelievers to produce even a single chapter comparable to the Qur'an in its linguistic eloquence, literary beauty, and profound wisdom. By urging them to seek the assistance of anyone they wish, Allah demonstrates that the Qur'an is inimitable and beyond human capacity, thereby proving its supernatural origin and the authenticity of the Prophet's message.

translation: Rather, they have denied that which they encompass not in knowledge, and whose interpretation has not yet come to them. Thus did those before them deny. Then observe how was the end of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the rejection of the disbelievers towards the Qur'an stems from their hasty judgment and ignorance, as they criticize truths they have not yet comprehended or fully experienced in their ultimate realization. God draws a parallel between their arrogance and the historical pattern of past nations who similarly rejected divine truth without understanding it, ultimately facing destruction due to their persistent injustice and refusal to reflect upon the inevitable consequences of opposing the divine message.

translation: And among them are those who believe in it, and among them are those who do not believe in it. And your Lord is most knowing of the corrupters.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inherent division among people regarding the divine message; while some sincerely accept and find guidance in it, others deliberately reject it out of obstinacy and corruption. By concluding with the divine attribute of being 'most knowing of the corrupters,' God serves as a warning that those who actively propagate falsehood and reject the truth are under His perfect surveillance, and their malicious attempts to disrupt the spread of faith will not go unnoticed or unpunished.

translation: And if they deny you, say, 'For me are my deeds, and for you are your deeds. You are disassociated from what I do, and I am disassociated from what you do.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a directive for the Prophet to maintain firm boundaries in the face of persistent rejection, emphasizing a clear separation of accountability; it underscores that each soul is responsible solely for its own beliefs and actions, releasing the messenger from the burden of their disbelief while simultaneously establishing that he bears no responsibility for their sinful practices.

translation: And among them are those who listen to you. But can you make the deaf hear, even if they do not understand?
interpretation: This verse highlights that the inability of the disbelievers to accept the truth of the Prophet’s message is not due to a lack of sound reaching their ears, but due to a total lack of insight and spiritual comprehension; just as a physically deaf person cannot benefit from verbal instruction, those whose hearts have been hardened by stubbornness and rejection of the intellect are incapable of perceiving the guidance offered to them.

translation: And among them are those who look at you. But can you guide the blind, even though they do not see?
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad, highlighting the futility of trying to guide those whose hearts have been sealed by arrogance and disbelief; just as one cannot force a blind person to perceive what they are fundamentally unable to see, one cannot compel those who have willfully shut their spiritual eyes to recognize the truth of divine revelation.

translation: Indeed, Allah does not wrong the people at all, but it is the people who are wronging themselves.
interpretation: This verse clarifies that Allah is perfectly just and never imposes any suffering or punishment upon His servants without cause; rather, the harm that befalls human beings is a direct consequence of their own choices, rejection of truth, and transgression against the boundaries set by God, which ultimately leads to their own spiritual and worldly ruin.

translation: And on the Day when He will gather them, it will be as if they had not tarried except an hour of a day, recognizing one another. Those will have lost who denied the meeting with Allah and were not guided.
interpretation: The verse highlights the extreme brevity of earthly life when viewed from the perspective of the afterlife, emphasizing that the intense reality of the Resurrection will make one's entire worldly existence seem like a fleeting moment. The mutual recognition among people signifies the restoration of earthly relationships and identities, which serves as a stark reminder of the accountability each soul carries, ultimately underscoring that those who rejected the reality of divine judgment have suffered the ultimate loss by failing to pursue the path of truth and guidance while they had the chance.

translation: And whether We show you some of what We promise them, or We take you in death, to Us is their return; then Allah is a Witness over what they are doing.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine reassurance to the Prophet Muhammad, emphasizing that the ultimate judgment of his opponents is entirely in the hands of Allah. Whether he lives to see their punishment in this life or passes away before witnessing it, their accountability is inevitable because their final return is to their Creator. The verse highlights the attribute of Allah as the All-Seeing Witness who meticulously records every action and intention of those who reject the truth, ensuring that perfect justice will be served either in this world or in the hereafter.

translation: And for every nation is a messenger; so when their messenger comes, it will be judged between them in justice, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah has established a universal divine pattern of justice by sending a messenger to every community as a witness and guide. The 'judgment' referred to signifies that when the message is delivered, the people are held accountable based on their acceptance or rejection of that truth; Allah ensures that no soul is punished for sins it did not commit, nor is any good deed denied its reward, manifesting absolute divine equity in the final resolution of their affairs.

translation: And they say, 'When will this promise be [fulfilled], if you should be truthful?'
interpretation: The disbelievers challenge the messenger by mocking the inevitability of the Day of Judgment, demanding a specific timeframe for its occurrence as a way to deny its reality, under the false assumption that if the Prophet (peace be upon him) cannot provide a precise date, then the promise of resurrection and accountability must be a falsehood.

translation: Say, 'I possess not for myself any harm or benefit except what Allah wills. For every nation is a [specified] term. When their time has come, then they will not remain behind an hour, nor will they precede [it].'
interpretation: The Prophet Muhammad is commanded to clarify his human limitations, affirming that he has no innate power to bring benefit or ward off harm from himself, let alone others, as all authority belongs solely to Allah. This underscores the theological principle that divine decree governs all existence, including the lifespan of every individual and community. By stating that time is fixed and unchangeable, the verse serves to diminish human reliance on the material world and directs it entirely toward the Creator, reminding humanity that their appointed time is beyond their influence or negotiation.

translation: Say, 'Have you considered: if His punishment should come to you by night or by day, for what would the criminals be impatient?'
interpretation: The verse serves as a stern rhetorical challenge to those who mockingly demand the hastening of God's punishment, questioning why they would impatiently seek something that, if it were to arrive suddenly in the darkness of night or the light of day, would bring only catastrophic ruin and leave them with no capacity to evade or endure it.

translation: Then is it, when it has occurred, that you will believe in it? Now? And you were before hastening it.
interpretation: This verse serves as a rhetorical rebuke to those who mockingly challenged the arrival of divine punishment or the Day of Judgment, highlighting the futility of belief once the event has already manifested; it reveals that faith holds no redemptive value when it is compelled by the sheer terror of witnessing the inevitability of the Truth, rather than being an act of sincere conviction chosen before the signs became absolute.

translation: Then it will be said to those who wronged, 'Taste the punishment of eternity! Are you being recompensed except for what you used to earn?'
interpretation: This verse signifies that the eternal punishment in the Hereafter is not an act of injustice or arbitrary cruelty by God, but rather a direct and necessary consequence of the conscious choices and harmful deeds committed by the individuals during their earthly life; it emphasizes the principle of divine justice where the outcome of the soul is perfectly balanced with the nature of its worldly conduct.

translation: And they ask you, 'Is it true?' Say, 'Yes, by my Lord, it is indeed the truth, and you will not be able to escape it.'
interpretation: The verse addresses the persistent questioning of the disbelievers regarding the reality of the promised Resurrection and the divine retribution. Allah commands the Prophet to swear by His Lord that these promises are an absolute, undeniable reality, emphasizing that no amount of human defiance or power can prevent these divine decrees from manifesting, as nothing in the universe is beyond the reach or authority of the Creator.

translation: And if every soul that has wronged had all that is in the earth, it would seek to ransom itself with it. And they will conceal regret when they see the punishment; and it will be judged between them in justice, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the absolute futility of material wealth on the Day of Judgment; even if a transgressor possessed everything existing on Earth, it would hold no value as a means to escape divine retribution. The mention of them concealing their regret signifies a state of profound shock and inner turmoil where the gravity of their loss becomes so overwhelming that their sorrow turns into a silent, internal agony, leaving them unable to articulate their remorse as they face the definitive and impartial justice of God, where every action is weighed with perfect equity.

translation: Unquestionably, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. Unquestionably, the promise of Allah is true, but most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine reminder of Allah's absolute sovereignty over all existence and the certainty of His promise regarding the Resurrection and Judgment. It highlights that the prevailing ignorance or disbelief of humanity does not alter the objective reality of God's dominion or the inevitability of His decreed outcome, urging the believer to anchor their certainty in divine truth rather than the trends of human opinion.

translation: It is He who gives life and causes death, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse establishes the absolute sovereignty of Allah over the cycles of existence, affirming that He alone possesses the power to initiate life and decree the end of it; it serves as a solemn reminder to humanity that their earthly journey is finite and will inevitably conclude with a return to their Creator, where they shall be held accountable for their deeds.

translation: O mankind, there has come to you an instruction from your Lord and healing for what is in the chests and guidance and mercy for the believers.
interpretation: This verse addresses all of humanity, declaring that the Qur'an serves as a divine sermon that counsels people against heedlessness and guides them toward righteous conduct. The description of it as a 'healing for what is in the chests' signifies its power to cure spiritual ailments such as doubt, hypocrisy, arrogance, and envy, cleansing the human heart of corruption. Furthermore, while the entire message is a benefit to all, it specifically functions as a source of divine guidance and mercy for the believers, as they are the ones who accept its truth and implement its teachings, thereby attaining spiritual clarity and salvation.

translation: Say, 'In the bounty of Allah and in His mercy - in that let them rejoice; it is better than what they accumulate.'
interpretation: The verse commands the Prophet to tell the believers that they should derive their true joy and happiness from the guidance of the Qur'an and the faith bestowed upon them by Allah, rather than from worldly wealth and fleeting material possessions, as spiritual sustenance is eternal and far superior to the transient gains of this world.

translation: Say, 'Have you seen what Allah has sent down to you of provision, of which you have made some lawful and some unlawful?' Say, 'Has Allah permitted you [to do so], or do you invent [something] about Allah?'
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern rebuke to those who arbitrarily legislate religious rulings, particularly those who permit or prohibit things based on their own personal desires or cultural customs rather than divine revelation. Allah challenges the audacity of such people by questioning their authority, highlighting that the power to define what is lawful (halal) and what is forbidden (haram) belongs solely to the Creator, and anyone who claims otherwise without a clear mandate from Him is essentially committing a grave act of fabrication and forgery against His name.

translation: And what will be the assumption of those who invent falsehood about Allah on the Day of Resurrection? Indeed, Allah is full of bounty to the people, but most of them are not grateful.
interpretation: This verse serves as a rhetorical warning, questioning the fate of those who fabricate lies against God by attributing partners or false laws to Him; it emphasizes that their expectation of security or reward on the Day of Judgment will be proven futile, contrasting their delusion with the reality of God's abundant grace, which they reject through their persistent ingratitude.

translation: And you do not find yourself in any situation, nor do you recite any part of the Qur'an, nor do you do any deed, but We are witness over you when you are engaged in it. And not absent from your Lord is [so much as] an atom's weight within the earth or within the heaven or [anything] smaller than that or greater, but that it is in a clear record.
interpretation: This verse serves as a profound reminder of Allah’s absolute omnipresence and perfect knowledge, emphasizing that nothing escapes His sight—not the smallest movement, nor the most secret intention, nor the largest endeavor. It assures the believer that they are never alone in their actions, as Allah is an ever-watchful witness who meticulously records every aspect of human life in a clear, divine register, establishing that the entirety of creation is subject to His encompassing awareness and ultimate justice.

translation: Behold! Verily on the friends of Allah there is no fear, nor shall they grieve.
interpretation: This verse describes the state of the righteous believers who have attained nearness to Allah through faith and piety. They are free from the fear of what is to come in the hereafter, as they have secured the pleasure of their Lord, and they are spared from the sorrow of what they have left behind in this worldly life, for Allah has compensated them with the promise of Paradise and His eternal grace.

translation: Those who believed and were conscious of God.
interpretation: This verse describes the believers whose faith is not merely a verbal declaration, but a constant state of God-consciousness, manifested through their diligent efforts to obey His commands and avoid what He has forbidden in all aspects of their lives.

translation: For them are good tidings in the worldly life and in the Hereafter. No change is there in the words of Allah. That is the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the true believers receive divine reassurance and spiritual tranquility in this world—often through righteous visions, the appreciation of others, or the inner peace granted by their faith—and they are promised the ultimate reward of Paradise in the afterlife. It serves as a profound comfort, emphasizing that Allah's promises are immutable and constant, ensuring that the path of the righteous will inevitably culminate in a success that is absolute, enduring, and unparalleled.

translation: And do not let their speech grieve you. Indeed, honor belongs to Allah entirely. He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse serves as a profound consolation to the Prophet Muhammad, reassuring him that the disparaging remarks, mockery, and disbelief of his opponents should not weigh upon his heart, because true power, victory, and honor are not derived from human opinion or worldly consensus, but reside solely with Allah, who hears all their claims and possesses complete knowledge of their hidden intentions and the ultimate reality of their condition.

translation: Unquestionably, to Allah belongs whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth. And those who invoke other than Allah do not [actually] follow [His] 'partners.' They follow only assumption, and they are not but lying.
interpretation: The verse clarifies that absolute ownership and sovereignty over the entire universe belong solely to Allah, debunking the polytheistic belief that idols or deities have any inherent power or status. It highlights that those who worship others alongside Allah are not following any verified truth, divine revelation, or tangible evidence, but are instead governed by baseless conjectures, subjective whims, and fabrications they have invented themselves, rendering their claims completely devoid of reality or authority.

translation: It is He who made for you the night that you may rest therein and the day, giving sight. Indeed in that are signs for a people who listen.
interpretation: The verse highlights Allah's profound mercy in creating a cyclical rhythm for existence; He fashioned the night as a sanctuary of stillness and tranquility to rejuvenate the human body and soul, while He designed the day with light to facilitate vision, activity, and the pursuit of sustenance, thereby presenting undeniable evidence of His wisdom to those who possess the receptive faculty of heart and mind to heed the truth.

translation: They say, 'Allah has taken a son.' Exalted is He; He is the [sustainer of all, free of all] need. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. You have no authority for this. Do you say about Allah that which you do not know?
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern refutation against those who attribute offspring to the Divine, clarifying that such a claim is both logically baseless and inherently contradictory to the nature of God, who is absolute in His independence and sovereignty; by highlighting that all existence is His creation and entirely dependent upon Him, the verse exposes the audacity of making unfounded claims regarding the essence of the Creator, reminding humanity that religious assertions must be grounded in divine authority rather than baseless human conjecture.

translation: Say, 'Indeed, those who invent falsehood about Allah will not succeed.'
interpretation: The verse serves as a definitive warning that whoever attributes lies to Allah—whether by inventing false religious laws, claiming divine attributes for themselves or idols, or falsely attributing speech to Him—will be deprived of salvation, prosperity, and success in both this world and the Hereafter, as their actions are rooted in deep transgression and rebellion against the Truth.

translation: [It is but a brief] enjoyment in this world; then to Us is their return; then We will make them taste the severe punishment because they used to disbelieve.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern reminder that the comforts, status, and pleasures of this worldly life are fleeting and temporary, serving only as a brief provision before the inevitable meeting with the Creator. The transition from earthly enjoyment to divine accountability underscores the gravity of rejecting faith, indicating that the severity of the ultimate punishment is a direct consequence of their persistent denial and refusal to acknowledge the truth of God's signs while they were immersed in worldly distractions.

translation: And recite to them the news of Noah, when he said to his people, 'O my people, if my residence and my reminding of the signs of Allah has become burdensome to you - then I have relied upon Allah. So resolve upon your plan and call upon your partners; then let not your plan be obscure to you. Then carry it out against me and do not give me respite.'
interpretation: In this verse, Prophet Noah demonstrates complete reliance upon Allah and steadfastness in the face of his people's hostility. By challenging them to gather their forces and their idols—whom they falsely associated with God—to conspire against him, he is not merely being bold, but is instead expressing his absolute certainty that no harm can reach him except by the decree of Allah. He is demonstrating that his mission of truth is backed by the Creator of the universe, and therefore, the threats and combined efforts of his disbelieving people are ultimately inconsequential and incapable of thwarting the divine message he was sent to deliver.

translation: But if you turn away, then I have not asked of you any payment; my reward is only from Allah, and I have been commanded to be among the Muslims.
interpretation: The verse clarifies that the Prophet's mission is purely a duty to convey the message of Allah, free from any worldly expectation or personal gain; by emphasizing that his reward lies solely with God, he affirms his sincerity and total reliance on the Divine, while his commitment to being 'among the Muslims' signifies his complete submission to the will of Allah, serving as a model for all believers to maintain integrity and unwavering devotion regardless of the reactions or rejection of others.

translation: But they denied him, so We saved him and those who were with him in the ship, and We made them successors, and We drowned those who denied Our signs. Then see how was the end of those who were warned.
interpretation: The verse serves as a divine testament to the inevitable victory of truth over falsehood; it highlights the principle of divine justice where the persistent rejection of guidance leads to total destruction, while those who uphold the truth are granted the privilege of continuity and stewardship on earth, emphasizing that the tragic end of the disbelievers is a cautionary historical reality for all who witness their fate.

translation: Then We sent after him messengers to their peoples, and they brought them clear proofs, but they were not to believe in that which they had denied before. Thus do We seal the hearts of the transgressors.
interpretation: The verse explains that because those nations persisted in their disbelief and rejected the truth repeatedly despite the arrival of clear signs from successive messengers, their hearts became hardened and sealed by Allah as a consequence of their own initial choice to reject the truth, leaving them unable to accept guidance thereafter.

translation: Then We sent after them Moses and Aaron to Pharaoh and his chiefs with Our signs, but they behaved arrogantly and were a criminal people.
interpretation: This verse highlights the repetitive nature of human arrogance in the face of divine truth; despite the clear evidence and miraculous signs presented by Moses and Aaron, Pharaoh and his elite leadership chose to reject the message out of pride, demonstrating that their opposition was not due to a lack of understanding but rather a conscious, sinful refusal to submit to the authority of their Creator.

translation: But when the truth came to them from Us, they said, 'Indeed, this is clear magic.'
interpretation: When the divine truth was revealed to them through the Prophet, these individuals chose to reject it not because they lacked understanding of its validity, but because their hearts were hardened by arrogance and worldly attachments; by labeling it as 'magic,' they sought to deflect the awe-inspiring impact of the revelation and discredit its divine origin to maintain their status quo and evade the moral accountability that the truth demanded of them.

translation: Moses said, 'Do you say about the truth when it has come to you, 'Is this magic?' But magicians will not succeed.'
interpretation: Moses reprimands his people for their stubborn refusal to acknowledge the clear signs of divine truth, highlighting the irony of labeling God's miraculous evidence as mere trickery; he asserts that those who rely on falsehood and deceit, like magicians, are ultimately doomed to failure and cannot prevail against the manifest reality of God's guidance.

translation: They said, 'Have you come to us to turn us away from that upon which we found our fathers and so that you two may have grandeur in the land? And we are not believers in you.'
interpretation: The people of Pharaoh rejected Moses and Aaron by asserting that their adherence to ancestral tradition was superior to the divine message, accusing the messengers of fabricating a religious narrative merely as a strategic ploy to seize political authority and establish social dominance over the land of Egypt.

translation: And Pharaoh said, 'Bring to me every learned magician.'
interpretation: Pharaoh's command serves as a manifestation of his arrogance and his attempt to combat the divine truth brought by Moses by seeking to undermine it with human deception and trickery, believing that he could match the signs of God through the accumulated craft of his kingdom's elite sorcerers.

translation: And when the magicians came, Moses said to them, 'Throw whatever you are going to throw.'
interpretation: In this verse, Prophet Moses exhibits profound composure and absolute certainty in his mission as a messenger of God; by inviting the magicians to display their craft first, he demonstrates that he is not afraid of their falsehoods and that he is fully prepared to confront their illusions with the manifest Truth that has been revealed to him by Allah, signaling the inevitable triumph of divine guidance over fabricated trickery.

translation: So when they had thrown, Moses said, 'What you have brought is magic. Indeed, Allah will expose its worthlessness. Indeed, Allah does not amend the work of the corrupters.'
interpretation: Moses confidently dismissed the sorcerers' display as mere illusion and artifice, asserting that their falsehood would inevitably be nullified and rendered powerless by Allah's truth, affirming that those who seek to spread corruption through deception are destined for failure as their efforts lack the divine support and moral integrity necessary to endure.

translation: And Allah will establish the truth by His words, even if the criminals dislike it.
interpretation: Allah confirms the truth by manifesting His decree and promises, establishing it firmly in the world so that it prevails over falsehood, regardless of how much the disbelievers and wrongdoers may despise this outcome or attempt to suppress it.

translation: And none believed in Moses except some youths among his people, out of fear of Pharaoh and his chiefs, lest they should persecute them; and indeed, Pharaoh was tyrannical in the land, and indeed, he was of the transgressors.
interpretation: The verse highlights the immense courage required by those few young people who embraced the truth brought by Moses despite the overwhelming climate of terror maintained by the state. Their fear was not a lack of conviction, but a recognition of the brutal reality of Pharaoh's power, which sought to break the resolve of believers through systematic oppression and violent coercion. By describing Pharaoh as 'arrogant' and 'transgressive,' the Quran emphasizes that his cruelty was not merely a political tactic but a manifestation of his unbounded pride and rebellion against the divine order, which inevitably leads to the reckless abuse of power.

translation: And Moses said, 'O my people, if you have believed in Allah, then rely upon Him, if you should be Muslims.'
interpretation: True faith in Allah requires one to demonstrate total reliance upon Him in all affairs, proving that surrender to the Divine will is not merely a verbal claim but an active trust that manifests when a believer relinquishes their own strength to depend solely on the sufficiency and support of their Creator.

translation: And they said, 'Upon Allah we rely. Our Lord, do not make us objects of trial for the wrongdoing people.'
interpretation: The believers invoke Allah to protect them from the oppression of the disbelievers, specifically fearing that if the disbelievers were to gain power over them or witness their defeat, it would solidify the disbelievers in their falsehood and cause them to believe that their own ways are superior, thus becoming a source of tribulation for both the believers and the misguided.

translation: And save us by Your mercy from the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse represents a heartfelt supplication acknowledging that salvation from the tyranny or influence of those who reject the truth is not achieved through human strength alone, but exclusively through the encompassment of Divine mercy, which serves as the ultimate shield for the believers against the spiritual and worldly harm posed by disbelief.

translation: And We inspired Moses and his brother, 'Settle your people in houses in Egypt and make your houses places of worship and establish prayer, and give good tidings to the believers.'
interpretation: God instructed Moses and Aaron to designate specific houses for the Children of Israel to serve as secret places of prayer and worship, as they were living under the oppressive rule of Pharaoh, allowing them to maintain their faith and communal connection to God through constant prayer despite their difficult circumstances.

translation: And Moses said, 'Our Lord, indeed You have given Pharaoh and his establishment splendor and wealth in the worldly life, our Lord, that they may lead others astray from Your way. Our Lord, obliterate their wealth and harden their hearts so that they will not believe until they see the painful punishment.'
interpretation: This invocation from Moses reflects his realization that the worldly luxuries and abundant wealth bestowed upon Pharaoh and his elite had served only to increase their arrogance and distract them and their followers from the path of Allah; thus, he prayed for their destruction and the hardening of their hearts as a form of divine abandonment, recognizing that they had reached a point of such deep-seated stubbornness and rejection of truth that they would only be humbled by the manifestation of the divine torment.

translation: Allah said, 'Your supplication has been answered, so remain on the right path and do not follow the way of those who do not know.'
interpretation: Allah reassures Musa and Harun that their prayer for the destruction of Pharaoh's power has been accepted; however, He commands them to maintain consistency in their righteousness and patience while awaiting the appointed time for His decree to unfold, warning them against succumbing to the haste or ignorance of those who lack faith in the ultimate wisdom of Allah's timing.

translation: And We brought the Children of Israel across the sea, and Pharaoh and his soldiers pursued them in tyranny and enmity until, when drowning overtook him, he said, 'I believe that there is no deity except that in whom the Children of Israel believe, and I am of the Muslims.'
interpretation: When Pharaoh realized that death was inevitable and the divine punishment had caught up with him, he attempted to repent and declare faith, yet this declaration was invalid because it occurred after the certainty of death and the witnessing of the punishment, at which point the door of repentance is closed and faith is no longer accepted.

translation: Now? While you had disobeyed before and were of the corrupters?
interpretation: This verse reflects the finality of the gates of repentance when the reality of divine punishment becomes undeniable. It signifies that faith or regret expressed only at the moment of witnessing inevitable destruction is insufficient, as it lacks the sincerity of conviction; the individual is reminded that their past life was characterized by persistent rebellion and the spreading of moral corruption, making their belated attempt to turn to God a reaction to fear rather than a genuine transformation of the heart.

translation: So today We will save your body that you may be to those who succeed you a sign. And indeed, many among the people, of Our signs, are heedless.
interpretation: God decreed that the physical body of the Pharaoh would be preserved and washed ashore after he drowned, serving as a lasting manifestation of divine power and a cautionary testament to future generations that even the most arrogant tyrants are ultimately powerless against the command of their Creator, yet despite such tangible evidence of the truth, the majority of humanity remains oblivious to the lessons conveyed through these divine signs.

translation: And We had certainly settled the Children of Israel in an agreeable settlement and provided them with good things. And they did not differ until [after] knowledge had come to them. Indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ.
interpretation: The verse underscores that God granted the Children of Israel a blessed and honorable place of residence along with abundant, lawful provisions to facilitate their obedience and gratitude. However, instead of using this knowledge and divine favor as a means to maintain unity and adherence to the truth, they allowed their differences and internal conflicts to arise only after the truth had been made clear to them through revelation. This indicates that their divergence was not due to ignorance or a lack of guidance, but rather a deliberate choice to follow desires and abandon the clear path, a matter that will be definitively settled by God's justice on the Day of Judgment.

translation: So if you are in doubt, [O Muhammad], about that which We have revealed to you, then ask those who have been reading the Scripture before you. The truth has certainly come to you from your Lord, so never be among the doubters.
interpretation: This verse serves as a rhetorical reassurance to the Prophet and his community; it does not imply that the Prophet Muhammad actually harbored doubts, but rather directs those who might be skeptical to consult the people of the previous scriptures—the Torah and the Gospel—whose authentic texts contain prophecies and signs confirming the revelation of the Qur'an and the truthfulness of the Prophet's mission, thereby establishing that the message has arrived from God with undeniable clarity.

translation: And do not be of those who deny the verses of Allah, for then you would be among the losers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a solemn warning to the Prophet and his followers against the spiritual downfall that accompanies the rejection of divine truth; it implies that by choosing to dismiss or deny the clear signs and guidance provided by Allah, an individual effectively severs their connection to salvation, thereby bringing about their own ultimate ruin and deprivation of eternal success.

translation: Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has come into effect will not believe.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who have persisted in their arrogance and disbelief despite the arrival of truth and guidance, leading them to a state where their hearts have become sealed and incapable of responding to faith as a consequence of their own continuous rejection of the divine signs.

translation: And even if every sign should come to them, until they see the painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubbornness of those who deny the truth; it suggests that their rejection is not due to a lack of evidence or signs, but rather an inner obstinacy that will persist until they are confronted with the undeniable reality of God's punishment, at which point it will be too late for them to repent or benefit from belief.

translation: Then why was there not a [single] city that believed so its faith would have benefited it, except the people of Jonah? When they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in worldly life and gave them enjoyment for a time.
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle that divine punishment for a community is usually final once it has been decreed, except in the exceptional case of the people of Prophet Jonah (Yunus). Their story serves as the sole historical precedent where a community genuinely repented and believed before the arrival of the promised torment, leading Allah to lift the impending disgrace from them in this world and grant them a reprieve to continue their lives, highlighting Allah's mercy and the unique response to their sincere collective repentance.

translation: And had your Lord willed, those on earth would have believed, all of them entirely. Then, would you compel the people in order that they become believers?
interpretation: This verse underscores that faith is a matter of divine guidance and individual choice rather than external coercion. It serves as a reminder to the Prophet that his duty is merely to convey the message, not to force belief upon others, as true faith must stem from a sincere internal conviction that cannot be achieved through compulsion.

translation: And it is not for a soul to believe except by permission of Allah, and He will place defilement upon those who will not use reason.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that guidance toward faith is ultimately a divine gift granted by Allah's will; however, this does not imply fatalism, but rather that Allah designates a state of spiritual impurity, confusion, and error specifically for those who deliberately choose to ignore the clear signs of existence and refuse to apply their intellect to reflect upon the truth.

translation: Say, 'Observe what is in the heavens and earth.' But of what avail will be signs or warners to a people who do not believe?
interpretation: The verse commands the Prophet to urge disbelievers to contemplate the cosmic signs of God's creation—such as the celestial bodies, the structure of the heavens, and the fertility of the earth—as evidence of His existence and power. However, it emphasizes that for those who have hardened their hearts and willfully rejected faith, neither these profound natural signs nor the presence of divine messengers will suffice to guide them, because their lack of belief is not due to a lack of evidence, but a lack of willingness to accept the truth.

translation: Do they then await anything except the like of the days of those who passed away before them? Say, 'Then wait; indeed, I am with you among those who wait.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to the disbelievers who persistently reject the truth, reminding them that the patterns of divine justice are immutable; just as God punished previous nations who mocked their messengers and denied the signs of God, the same fate of historical destruction awaits those who currently repeat those same acts of arrogance and disbelief, leaving the Prophet and his followers to observe the inevitable fulfillment of God's decree.

translation: Then We will save Our messengers and those who have believed. Thus, it is an obligation upon Us that We save the believers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine assurance and a universal principle of Allah's justice, confirming that He will never abandon His messengers or those who sincerely believe in Him during times of trial or impending destruction. The repetition of the promise to save the believers emphasizes that this is a binding decree established by Allah out of His grace, guaranteeing that while the wicked face their recompense, those who maintain their faith will be delivered from the consequences of divine retribution and granted ultimate safety.

translation: Say, 'O mankind, if you are in doubt as to my religion - then I do not worship those you worship besides Allah; but I worship Allah, who will take your souls. And I have been commanded to be of the believers.'
interpretation: The Prophet Muhammad is instructed to declare his absolute detachment from polytheistic practices and his unwavering devotion to the Creator. This verse underscores that the true test of faith lies in recognizing the sovereignty of Allah, who possesses the power of life and death, thereby rendering the idols worshipped by others powerless and unworthy of adoration. By professing his commitment to the belief in the One God, he sets a definitive boundary between the truth of monotheism and the error of idolatry, establishing that his submission is exclusively to the authority that governs the human soul.

translation: And [it was said to me], 'Direct your face toward the religion, inclining to truth, and never be of those who associate others with Allah.'
interpretation: The verse commands the believer to devote their entire being, intention, and focus exclusively to the path of pure monotheism, standing firm upon the truth while turning away from all forms of falsehood or idolatry, for such single-minded dedication is the only way to safeguard one's faith against the corruption of polytheism.

translation: And do not invoke besides Allah that which neither benefits you nor harms you, for if you did, then indeed you would be of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern prohibition against shirk (polytheism), emphasizing that all power to provide benefit or cause harm belongs solely to Allah. To seek intercession or aid from idols or entities that possess no divine authority is an act of extreme injustice against one's own soul, as it misplaces worship and devotion, turning away from the Creator who is the only source of true power and sustenance.

translation: And if Allah should touch you with adversity, there is no remover of it except Him; and if He intends for you good, then there is no repeller of His bounty. He causes it to reach whom He wills of His servants. And He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse establishes that Allah is the absolute possessor of power, indicating that both harm and benefit are entirely under His decree.
