It serves to direct the believer's heart away from reliance on created beings, emphasizing that no obstacle can prevent the manifestation of His grace if He has willed it, and no power can remove a trial once He has ordained it, thereby fostering complete dependence, humility, and trust in His divine wisdom and mercy.

translation: Say, 'O mankind, the truth has come to you from your Lord, so whoever is guided is only guided for the benefit of his soul, and whoever goes astray only goes astray against it. And I am not over you a manager.'
interpretation: The verse clarifies that the Prophet Muhammad is merely a conveyer of the divine message rather than a controller or enforcer of people's choices. It highlights the principle of individual accountability, explaining that accepting divine guidance is a voluntary act that benefits the soul, while rejecting it is a self-destructive choice for which the individual bears full responsibility.

translation: And follow what is revealed to you, and be patient until Allah judges; and He is the best of judges.
interpretation: This verse commands the Prophet Muhammad to remain steadfast in adhering to the divine revelation he received, regardless of the opposition or difficulties he faced from his people. It serves as an instruction to maintain patience and perseverance in his mission, trusting entirely in Allah's wisdom and timing, with the reassurance that Allah’s decree is the most just and final outcome for all matters.

translation: Alif-Lam-Ra. [This is] a Book whose verses are perfected and then explained in detail, from [One who is] Wise and Acquainted.
interpretation: The verse asserts the divine perfection of the Qur'an, explaining that its contents are formulated with precise accuracy and wisdom, and subsequently detailed through clear guidance and legal rulings that emanate from the profound knowledge and absolute wisdom of Allah, who understands the nature of His creation perfectly.

translation: That you worship none but Allah. Indeed, I am to you from Him a warner and a bringer of good tidings.
interpretation: The verse clarifies that the core message of all divine revelation is the command to single out Allah alone in worship, free from any partners, while the Prophet serves as a messenger who alerts humanity to the consequences of disobedience through warnings of punishment and encourages them with the promise of eternal reward for those who uphold this monotheistic faith.

translation: And [saying], 'Seek forgiveness of your Lord and repent to Him, [and] He will let you enjoy a good provision for a specified term and give every doer of favor his favor. But if you turn away, then indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a great Day.'
interpretation: This verse establishes that true repentance requires two elements: seeking forgiveness for past sins through Istighfar and firmly turning away from them toward God with a sincere intention to reform. By doing so, God promises both material and spiritual well-being in this life, rewarding every person according to their level of righteousness and spiritual excellence, while simultaneously warning that those who persist in arrogance and disbelief will face the devastating consequences of the Day of Judgment.

translation: To Allah is your return, and He is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse serves as a definitive reminder that all human existence concludes with an inevitable return to the Creator, establishing that accountability and the ultimate resolution of all affairs rest solely with Him. By affirming His absolute power over all things immediately after mentioning the return, the verse emphasizes that no soul can escape His judgment nor can any action be hidden from His omnipotent grasp, thereby urging the believer to live with a constant consciousness of their ultimate meeting with the Divine.

translation: Unquestionably, they turn away their breasts to hide themselves from Him. Unquestionably, even when they cover themselves with their clothing, He knows what they conceal and what they declare. Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts.
interpretation: The verse highlights the futility of the hypocrites' attempts to conceal their inner thoughts and animosity from Allah, asserting that even when they physically contort their bodies or wrap themselves in coverings to hide from the presence or the message of the Prophet, their internal states remain fully transparent to the All-Knowing Creator, who possesses absolute awareness of the deepest secrets and intentions hidden within human hearts.

translation: And there is no creature on earth but that upon Allah is its provision, and He knows its place of dwelling and place of storage. All is in a clear register.
interpretation: This verse serves as a profound affirmation of God's absolute sovereignty and comprehensive providence, asserting that every living being—regardless of how small or hidden—is under the sustenance and care of the Creator. By stating that He knows both the 'dwelling' (the place where a creature resides during its life) and the 'storage' (the place to which it returns after death or the womb from which it emerges), Allah emphasizes that nothing in the entire cosmos exists outside the bounds of His perfect knowledge and sustained decree, thereby reassuring the believer that their life and livelihood are already secured by the One who sustains all of creation.

translation: And it is He who created the heavens and the earth in six days - and His Throne had been upon water - that He might test you as to which of you is best in deed. But if you, O Muhammad, should say, 'Indeed, you will be resurrected after death,' those who disbelieve will surely say, 'This is not but obvious magic.'
interpretation: The verse clarifies that the creation of the universe, with its vast heavens and earth, was not a purposeless act but a deliberate divine plan carried out over six cosmic periods. By establishing His dominion over the primordial state of existence, Allah set the stage for the moral testing of humanity. The purpose of this life is to distinguish those whose actions are most righteous and sincere. Furthermore, the verse highlights the deep-seated denial of the disbelievers; because their worldly perspective is so narrow, they reflexively reject the concept of the afterlife—a profound reality—by labeling the manifest truth of resurrection as mere illusion or sorcery, revealing their inner resistance to accountability.

translation: And if We delay the punishment for them until a reckoned time, they will surely say, 'What restrains it?' Unquestionably, on the Day it comes to them, it will not be averted from them, and they will be enveloped by what they used to ridicule.
interpretation: This verse addresses the arrogance of the disbelievers who mock the delay of God's punishment, mistaking divine respite for divine inability or neglect. It serves as a stern warning that the postponement of judgment is not a cancellation but a period of testing, and when the appointed hour finally arrives, it will be absolute and unavoidable, forcing those who scoffed at the warnings to finally confront the reality of the consequences they once dismissed.

translation: And if We let man taste mercy from Us and then We withdraw it from him, indeed, he is despairing and ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inherent frailty and instability of the human soul when it is detached from spiritual patience; when a person experiences a blessing and it is subsequently removed, their natural reaction is often to fall into absolute despair, forgetting that the blessing was a temporary gift, and to exhibit ingratitude by failing to acknowledge the goodness they previously enjoyed or the divine wisdom behind its withdrawal.

translation: And if We let him taste a favor after a hardship that has touched him, he will surely say, 'The evils have left me.' Indeed, he is exultant and boastful.
interpretation: This verse describes the volatile and superficial nature of the human psyche when stripped of true faith; when God removes a trial and restores prosperity, the ungrateful person foolishly assumes that his misery was merely a temporary misfortune that has now permanently vanished due to his own merit, rather than recognizing it as a divine test. Consequently, he falls into the trap of arrogance and self-conceit, feeling secure from God's decree and boasting of his worldly success without acknowledging the Giver of the grace.

translation: Except for those who are patient and do righteous deeds; those will have forgiveness and great reward.
interpretation: This verse serves as a crucial exception to the preceding context, highlighting that those who manifest steadfastness in the face of adversity and manifest their faith through consistent righteous conduct are shielded from the state of loss. The forgiveness promised is a divine erasure of their past shortcomings, while the great reward signifies an expansive, immeasurable recompense in the hereafter that compensates for the struggles they endured and the virtuous life they upheld.

translation: Then perhaps you would leave out some of what is revealed to you, and your breast becomes constrained by it because they say, 'Why has a treasure not been sent down to him, or an angel come with him?' You are only a warner, and Allah is Disposer of all things.
interpretation: This verse consoles the Prophet Muhammad, comforting him regarding the distress he feels due to the relentless mocking and unreasonable demands of the disbelievers who insist on miraculous signs like physical treasures or accompanying angels. Allah reassures him that his primary obligation is solely to convey the warning, while reminding him that Allah is the ultimate Protector and Guardian over all affairs, implying that the outcome of these people and the defense of the message are entirely under His divine control, thus relieving the Prophet of the burden of their rejection.

translation: Or do they say, 'He has invented it'? Say, 'Then bring ten surahs like it that have been invented, and call upon [for help] whomever you can besides Allah, if you should be truthful.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a supreme challenge issued by Allah to those who doubted the divine origin of the Qur'an, exposing the impossibility of human imitation. By demanding that they produce even ten chapters comparable to the Qur'an's eloquence and spiritual depth—while acknowledging their own claim that it was 'invented'—Allah highlights that if it were truly a human fabrication, they should be able to replicate it. Since they were incapable of matching its unique structure, wisdom, and rhetorical perfection despite their mastery of the Arabic language, this failure serves as definitive proof that the Qur'an is not a work of human invention but a miraculous revelation from the Creator.

translation: If then they do not respond to you, then know that it has been sent down with the knowledge of Allah and that there is no god but He. So, will you be Muslims?
interpretation: This verse serves as a final, definitive challenge to those who deny the Qur'an; by their inability to produce anything comparable to the revealed Word, it becomes manifest that the message originates from the infinite, absolute knowledge of Allah alone, leaving no logical alternative but to surrender in complete submission to His Oneness.

translation: Whoever desires the worldly life and its adornments - We fully repay them for their deeds therein, and they therein will not be deprived.
interpretation: This verse explains the divine justice of Allah regarding those whose sole ambition and focus are restricted to the material gains, status, and pleasures of this world. Allah grants these individuals the rewards for their good deeds—such as maintaining family ties, charity, or honesty—within the span of this worldly life, ensuring they are not cheated of their efforts; however, since they did not seek the afterlife or perform their deeds for the sake of Allah, they possess no reward or share in the eternal life to come.

translation: Those are the ones for whom there is nothing in the Hereafter but the Fire, and what they did there is lost, and what they used to do is invalid.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who dedicate their lives exclusively to worldly gains while rejecting faith and divine guidance will find their efforts fruitless in the ultimate reality of the Afterlife; their worldly deeds, not being grounded in sincerity or belief in God, possess no spiritual weight or merit, rendering them null and void before the judgment of the Almighty.

translation: Is he then who is on a clear proof from his Lord, and a witness from Him recites it, and before it was the Book of Moses, an imam and a mercy? Those believe in it; but whoever disbelieves in it among the factions, the Fire is his promised meeting place. So do not be in doubt about it. Indeed, it is the truth from your Lord, but most of the people do not believe.
interpretation: The verse highlights that the true believer possesses clear insight granted by Allah, supported by the testimony of the Prophet Muhammad (the witness) and the historical validation of the Torah as a precursor. It serves as a stark reminder that belief is a matter of inner guidance and recognition of divine truth, warning that those who reject this manifest light despite its clear evidence choose a path that leads inevitably to the fire of accountability.

translation: And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie about Allah? Those will be presented before their Lord, and the witnesses will say, 'These are the ones who lied against their Lord.' Unquestionably, the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse highlights that the most grave form of injustice is attributing falsehoods to the Creator, which encompasses acts like associating partners with Him, falsely declaring something He forbade as lawful, or claiming revelations that He never sent down. The inevitable consequence for such individuals is a public exposure on the Day of Judgment, where their deceit is laid bare before witnesses—comprising prophets, angels, and perhaps their own deeds—serving as a definitive condemnation of their betrayal of divine truth and their willful rejection of moral accountability.

translation: Those who avert from the way of Allah and seek to make it crooked, and they, concerning the Hereafter, are disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse describes individuals who actively obstruct others from the path of faith and truth, seeking to distort divine teachings by introducing doubts or corrupt interpretations to make the straight path seem complex or flawed; such actions stem from a fundamental denial of accountability in the afterlife, as their rejection of the Day of Judgment is what drives their persistent efforts to hinder the spread of Allah's guidance.

translation: Those were not able to escape on earth, nor did they have any protectors besides Allah. For them, the punishment will be doubled. They were not able to hear, nor did they see.
interpretation: This verse signifies that those who persisted in disbelief and sought to hinder others from the path of God possess no power to elude His divine decree or escape His retribution upon the earth, as they lack any guardians or allies to shield them from His judgment; furthermore, their hearts and minds have become so hardened and veiled by their own stubbornness and attachment to falsehood that they are rendered metaphorically deaf and blind to the truth, unable to perceive the light of guidance or heed the call of reality, which ensures that their ultimate punishment is compounded for both their own denial and their role in leading others astray.

translation: Those are the ones who have lost their own souls, and what they used to fabricate has vanished from them.
interpretation: This verse describes the ultimate state of those who rejected the truth; they have effectively destroyed their own potential for salvation and eternal happiness by distancing themselves from God. On the Day of Judgment, all the false deities, worldly idols, and baseless arguments they manufactured or relied upon to justify their disbelief will disappear, leaving them exposed and destitute, realizing that their worldly efforts were futile and their reliance on falsehood provided no protection.

translation: Undoubtedly, they are, in the Hereafter, the greatest losers.
interpretation: This verse asserts with absolute certainty that those who turned away from truth and persisted in their arrogance will find their ultimate state in the afterlife to be one of profound deprivation, as they have exchanged the eternal bliss of paradise and the pleasure of God for fleeting worldly desires, leaving them with nothing of value to present before their Creator.

translation: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds and humbled themselves before their Lord - those are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: The verse highlights that true success and entry into Paradise are reserved for those who combine sincere faith in their hearts with tangible righteous actions, while simultaneously maintaining a state of profound humility and submissive surrender (ikhbat) to Allah, recognizing His greatness and their own absolute dependence upon Him.

translation: The likeness of the two parties is as the blind and the deaf and the seeing and the hearing. Are they equal in comparison? Will you not then be reminded?
interpretation: Allah illustrates the vast disparity between the disbelievers—who lack spiritual insight and refuse to listen to the truth—and the believers—who possess true perception and heed the divine message—by comparing them to the physically blind and deaf versus those with functioning senses; this comparison serves to awaken the intellect to realize that those who reject the truth are fundamentally deprived of spiritual discernment, making them in no way comparable to those who perceive the reality of their existence and the guidance of their Lord.

translation: And We certainly sent Noah to his people, [saying], 'Indeed, I am to you a clear warner,'
interpretation: This verse highlights the mission of Prophet Noah as a messenger chosen by Allah to guide his people. By describing himself as a 'clear warner,' Noah clarifies that his role is not to force belief upon them but to explicitly and transparently warn them of the consequences of their disbelief and polytheism, ensuring that the message is conveyed with absolute clarity so that no one can claim ignorance of the truth.

translation: That you should worship none but Allah; indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a painful day.
interpretation: This verse signifies the core mission of prophetic guidance, emphasizing that the absolute singularity of worship is the only path to salvation, while the warning of a painful day serves as a compassionate exhortation to turn away from self-destructive falsehoods before the finality of divine accountability arrives.

translation: But the eminent among those who disbelieved among his people said, 'We do not see you but as a man like ourselves, and we do not see you followed except by those who are the lowest of us by immature judgment. And we do not see in you any merit over us; rather, we think you are liars.'
interpretation: The disbelieving elite rejected the prophet's message by relying on superficial social prejudices rather than intellectual merit; they argued that because the prophet was a human being like them and his followers were from the humble or lower social classes, his message must be invalid and motivated by misguided, impulsive thinking, thereby dismissing his divine mission simply because it did not align with their established social hierarchies or aristocratic superiority.

translation: He said, 'O my people, have you considered: if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord and He has given me mercy from Himself but it has been made obscure to you, can we force you to accept it while you are averse to it?'
interpretation: The Prophet Nuh (Noah) is rhetorically questioning his people by highlighting that truth and guidance are gifts from Allah that cannot be coerced upon those who harbor resentment toward them, implying that faith requires a sincere heart and that forcing belief onto those who are stubbornly resistant is both impossible and contrary to the divine wisdom of free will.

translation: And O my people, I ask of you no wealth for it; my reward is but from Allah. And I am not one to drive away those who have believed; indeed, they will meet their Lord, but I see you as a people who are behaving ignorantly.
interpretation: The Prophet Nuh (Noah) asserts his sincerity by clarifying that his call to faith is not driven by any worldly gain, as his ultimate compensation rests solely with Allah. By refusing to cast aside the impoverished believers at the demand of the wealthy elite, he emphasizes that true faith creates a bond of honor that transcends social status, while simultaneously rebuking the elite for their profound ignorance in failing to recognize that every human soul will ultimately stand before their Creator to be judged based on deeds rather than societal position.

translation: And O my people, who would help me against Allah if I drove them away? Will you not then reflect?
interpretation: The prophet Nuh is reasoning with his people by highlighting the inevitability of divine accountability; he argues that if he were to reject the poor and humble believers who followed him—solely to appease the pride of the wealthy disbelievers—he would have no defense or sanctuary from Allah’s judgment, implying that human social status holds no weight before God compared to the sincerity of faith.

translation: And I do not say to you that I have the depositories of Allah, nor do I know the unseen, nor do I say that I am an angel, nor do I say of those whom your eyes look down upon that Allah will never grant them any good. Allah knows best what is within their souls. Indeed, if I were to say such things, I would then be among the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The Prophet Noah emphasizes his human limitations and ethical integrity by refusing to claim divine attributes or exclusive access to the divine treasury. He rejects the elitist arrogance of his opponents who despised the poor believers, asserting that moral worth is known only to God. By acknowledging his own potential for error should he judge others based on outward appearance, he affirms that true righteousness lies in submitting to God's judgment rather than human biases.

translation: They said, 'O Noah, you have disputed with us and have been frequent in your dispute of us. So bring us what you promise us, if you should be of the truthful.'
interpretation: The people of Noah reached the peak of their arrogance and defiance by challenging his prophethood; instead of reflecting on his warnings, they mockingly demanded that he bring upon them the divine punishment he had been threatening them with, as a way to dismiss his message and declare their stubborn disbelief in the face of his persistent efforts to guide them.

translation: He said, 'Only Allah will bring it to you if He wills, and you will not be able to cause failure [to escape].'
interpretation: The Prophet is clarifying that the timing and occurrence of the punishment or the manifestation of signs rests solely with Allah's decree and wisdom, emphasizing that human resistance or attempts to flee are futile against divine power, as no one possesses the capacity to circumvent or frustrate the will of the Creator.

translation: And my advice will not benefit you, although I wished to advise you, if Allah intends to put you astray. He is your Lord, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse signifies that when a community becomes fully entrenched in disbelief and persists in their rejection of truth to the point where Allah seals their hearts and wills for them to remain in misguidance, external counsel loses its efficacy; thus, the Prophet Nuh is explaining that his warnings and efforts at guidance are subject to the divine decree of whether the hearts of the people are still open to receiving the truth, affirming that ultimately all sovereignty belongs to Allah and everyone is destined to return to Him for accountability.

translation: Or do they say, 'He has invented it'? Say, 'If I have invented it, then upon me is my crime, but I am innocent of what you commit.'
interpretation: The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, is instructed by Allah to establish a clear distinction of accountability, asserting that the burden of any falsehood or fabrication rests solely on the one who commits it; he thereby challenges his detractors to recognize that he is absolved of the sins and spiritual transgressions they continue to perpetrate by rejecting the truth.

translation: And it was revealed to Noah that, 'None will believe among your people except those who have already believed, so do not be distressed by what they have been doing.'
interpretation: God comforted Prophet Noah by informing him that his mission of propagation had reached its completion regarding those who were destined for guidance, relieving him of the sorrow and emotional burden caused by the persistent rejection and harmful actions of his disbelieving people, thereby instructing him to focus on the forthcoming decree of divine judgment.

translation: And construct the ship under Our eyes and Our inspiration, and do not address Me concerning those who have done wrong; indeed, they are to be drowned.
interpretation: This verse signifies that Prophet Nuh (Noah) was commanded by Allah to build the Ark under His direct observation and divine guidance, highlighting the necessity of complete obedience to Allah's instructions. By forbidding Nuh from interceding for the wrongdoers, Allah emphasizes that His decree of punishment for those who persisted in disbelief and tyranny had become absolute, signifying that the time for mercy and divine reprieve had passed and the intervention of justice was inevitable.

translation: And he constructed the ship, and whenever the prominent among his people passed by him, they ridiculed him. He said, 'If you ridicule us, then we will ridicule you just as you ridicule.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the unwavering resolve of Prophet Nuh (Noah) as he fulfilled Allah's command to build the ark despite the mockery of his disbelieving people. His response reflects a divine certainty that the tables would inevitably turn; his declaration of ridicule signifies that when the inevitable punishment of the flood arrives, the believers will mock the unbelievers' ignorance and denial, just as the unbelievers mocked the believers' faith in the unseen.

translation: But soon you will know who it is that will receive a punishment that will disgrace him, and on whom will fall a lasting torment.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning that the arrogance of the disbelievers will eventually be shattered by divine retribution, indicating that the consequences of their defiance will be both humiliating in the immediate sense of worldly downfall and eternal in the afterlife, where the punishment will be permanent and inescapable.

translation: Until when Our command came and the oven overflowed, We said, 'Load upon the ship of each creature two mates and your family, except those against whom the word has already gone forth, and those who have believed.' But none had believed with him, except a few.
interpretation: This verse depicts the commencement of the divine decree of the Flood, marked by the miraculous gushing of water from the oven as a sign for Prophet Nuh (Noah), signaling that the time for punishment had arrived; it emphasizes the implementation of Allah's justice by commanding Nuh to preserve the righteous and the animal pairs, while simultaneously highlighting the stark reality that despite his long-term preaching, the number of his followers remained remarkably small, underscoring the stubbornness of his people.

translation: And [Noah] said, 'Board the ship; in the name of Allah is its course and its anchorage. Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful.'
interpretation: When Prophet Noah commanded his people to board the Ark, he instructed them to initiate the journey by invoking the name of Allah, acknowledging that both the movement of the ship through the waves and its final arrival at safety depend entirely on the power and divine decree of the Creator, reflecting a profound state of reliance upon Him as the One whose mercy and forgiveness encompass all who place their trust in Him.

translation: And it sailed with them through waves like mountains, and Noah called to his son who was apart [from them], 'O my son, come aboard with us and do not be with the disbelievers.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the desperate, compassionate plea of a father trying to save his son from the impending divine retribution of the flood. Despite the miraculous nature of the ark navigating through mountainous waves, Noah's paternal instinct compels him to reach out to his son, who remains separated by both physical distance and spiritual obstinacy. The dialogue underscores the tragic barrier that disbelief creates, as Noah offers a final opportunity for salvation through submission to God, warning that being among the disbelievers will inevitably lead to destruction regardless of earthly lineage.

translation: He said, 'I will take refuge on a mountain to protect me from the water.' [Noah] said, 'There is no protector today from the decree of Allah, except for whom He gives mercy.' And the waves came between them, and he was among the drowned.
interpretation: The son of Noah believed that worldly means and physical elevations could save him from the divine decree of the Flood, failing to realize that when Allah's command for destruction arrives, no earthly power or strategic location can offer immunity. His demise serves as a profound lesson that salvation is not a product of human arrogance or reliance on created causes, but is solely contingent upon Allah's mercy and one's adherence to the divine truth that Noah was preaching.

translation: And it was said, 'O earth, swallow your water, and O sky, withhold [your rain].' And the water subsided, and the matter was accomplished, and the ship came to rest on [the mountain of] Judiyy. And it was said, 'Away with the wrongdoing people.'
interpretation: This verse depicts the dramatic conclusion of the Great Flood as a manifestation of divine sovereignty, where nature itself obeys the command of its Creator to cease its destruction, signifying that the trial was finalized and justice served through the salvation of the righteous and the total eradication of the oppressors who rejected the truth.

translation: And Noah called upon his Lord and said, 'My Lord, indeed my son is of my family; and indeed, Your promise is true; and You are the most just of judges.'
interpretation: Noah's plea represents a heartfelt appeal born of natural parental love and a desperate hope for his son's salvation, based on God's promise to save his household. He is not questioning the justice of God's decree, but rather humbly seeking clarification and intercession, trusting that since God's promise is unfailing and He is the ultimate judge, there must be a profound wisdom in the unfolding events that Noah seeks to reconcile with his request.

translation: He said, 'O Noah, indeed he is not of your family; indeed, he is [one whose] work was other than righteous, so do not ask Me that of which you have no knowledge. Indeed, I advise you, lest you be among the ignorant.'
interpretation: Allah informs Noah that his son had severed the bond of faith that truly joins families, making his son's deeds a manifestation of disbelief and corruption; therefore, Noah was warned against pleading for his son's salvation because asking for the pardon of an unbeliever constitutes an attempt to override divine justice, an act of ignorance regarding the absolute nature of Allah's decree.

translation: He said, 'My Lord, I seek refuge in You from asking You that of which I have no knowledge. And unless You forgive me and have mercy upon me, I will be among the losers.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the profound state of humility and repentance of Prophet Nuh after he inadvertently questioned the wisdom of God regarding the fate of his unbelieving son. It serves as a pedagogical model for the believer to acknowledge the limitations of human knowledge when confronted with Divine Decree, teaching that when a person oversteps the boundaries of divine wisdom—even out of paternal love—they must immediately return to God with total submissiveness, seeking His grace and protection to avoid the state of spiritual ruin.

translation: It was said, O Noah, disembark in peace from Us and blessings upon you and upon the nations [descending] from those with you. But other nations We will grant enjoyment, then there will touch them a painful punishment from Us.
interpretation: This verse signifies the divine decree for Prophet Noah and his followers to step out of the Ark onto the purified earth, bestowing upon them safety, security, and spiritual abundance. It establishes that while the initial group of believers is blessed, human history will witness the rise of later generations who will be granted worldly provisions and temporary enjoyment; however, if these subsequent nations turn away from guidance and persist in disobedience, they will inevitably face the consequences of divine justice in the form of severe retribution.

translation: These are reports of the unseen which We reveal to you, [O Muhammad]. You did not know them, neither you nor your people, before this. So be patient; indeed, the [best] outcome is for the righteous.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that the historical narratives shared with the Prophet Muhammad concerning past prophets were not matters of common knowledge or historical record accessible to him or his contemporaries; rather, they serve as a divine proof of his prophethood. By connecting the reception of this hidden knowledge to the command for patience, Allah indicates that the struggle of upholding the truth is inherently difficult, but that the final triumph and ultimate success in this life and the Hereafter are exclusively reserved for those who fear God and maintain their integrity and piety.

translation: And to the people of 'Ad We sent their brother Hud. He said, 'O my people! Worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. You are nothing but inventors of lies.'
interpretation: Hud calls upon his people to abandon their polytheistic practices and direct all acts of worship solely toward the One Creator, arguing that their claims regarding the divinity of idols are baseless fabrications that hold no truth or reality, thereby challenging them to recognize that worshiping anything other than Allah is a departure from the inherent truth.

translation: O my people, I do not ask of you any reward for it; my reward is only from the One who created me. Will you not then use your reason?
interpretation: The Prophet Hud emphasizes that his call to monotheism is entirely selfless and free from any worldly ambition, demonstrating that his sole motivation is the command of his Creator. By invoking his role as a created being before his Lord, he highlights the logical necessity of worshiping the One who fashioned him, urging his people to abandon their idolatrous traditions and exercise the intellectual faculty that distinguishes truth from falsehood.

translation: And O my people, ask forgiveness of your Lord and then repent to Him. He will send [rain from] the sky upon you in showers and increase you in strength added to your strength. And do not turn away, [being] criminals.
interpretation: Prophet Hud commands his people to combine the seeking of forgiveness with sincere repentance, explaining that the outward spiritual purification of the soul—manifested through faith and turning away from idolatry—is the direct catalyst for material blessings, such as abundant rain for sustenance and a collective strengthening of their societal power, warning that continued rebellion against God is not merely a theological error but a criminal act that leads to the inevitable ruin of a civilization.

translation: They said, 'O Hud, you have not brought us any clear proof, and we will not abandon our gods because of what you say, nor are we believers in you.'
interpretation: The people of 'Ad persisted in their arrogance and disbelief by dismissing the divine signs provided by Prophet Hud, choosing instead to prioritize their ancestral traditions and idols over the clear truth of monotheism, thereby blinding themselves to the reality of his message through stubborn adherence to their misguided beliefs.

translation: We say nothing but that some of our gods have possessed you with evil. He said, 'Indeed, I call Allah to witness, and you [too] witness, that I am free from whatever you associate with Allah.'
interpretation: The verse illustrates the deep-seated spiritual blindness of the idolaters, who attributed the Prophet Hud's sound warnings and moral rectitude to a state of mental derangement or a curse inflicted by their false idols, revealing their inability to conceive of a truth that contradicts their ingrained polytheism. In response, Hud performs a solemn, public disavowal of their pantheon, distancing himself completely from their beliefs and invoking Allah as his ultimate witness, which signifies that his message is rooted in absolute divine oneness and that he bears no responsibility for the consequences of their persistent rejection.

translation: Instead of Him; so plot against me all together; then do not grant me any respite.
interpretation: The verse illustrates the Prophet Hud's firm reliance on Allah, showcasing his absolute confidence and lack of fear toward the polytheists. By challenging his people to unite their efforts, schemes, and power against him while declaring that their collective plots will be futile without Allah's permission, he exposes the weakness of their idols and demonstrates that true strength and protection reside solely with the Creator.

translation: Indeed, I have relied upon Allah, my Lord and your Lord. There is no creature but that He holds it by its forelock. Indeed, my Lord is on a straight path.
interpretation: This verse establishes the absolute sovereignty of Allah over all creation; by stating that He holds every creature by its forelock, it signifies that all beings are entirely subject to His control, power, and decree, and that nothing moves or exists outside of His dominion, while His being on a straight path assures the believer that His governance is defined by perfect justice, truth, and wisdom.

translation: But if they turn away, then I have conveyed to you that with which I was sent to you. And my Lord will replace you with another people, and you will not harm Him at all. Indeed my Lord is, over all things, Guardian.
interpretation: This verse serves as a definitive declaration of the Prophet's fulfillment of his mission; having delivered the message clearly, he is no longer accountable for the stubborn rejection of his people. It emphasizes that divine guidance is not dependent on any specific nation or group, as Allah possesses the power to replace those who persist in arrogance with a more obedient community, while reminding the disbelievers that their rejection does not diminish Allah's sovereignty or majesty in the slightest, for He remains the ultimate Protector and Observer over all His creation.

translation: And when Our command came, We saved Hud and those who believed with him, by a mercy from Us; and We saved them from a harsh punishment.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the deliverance of Prophet Hud and his followers was not due to their own strength or ability, but solely a result of Allah's divine mercy, which shielded them from the severe and destructive chastisement that annihilated their oppressors.

translation: And that was 'Aad; they rejected the signs of their Lord and disobeyed His messengers and followed the order of every obstinate tyrant.
interpretation: The verse highlights the moral and spiritual downfall of the people of 'Aad, explaining that their destruction was a direct consequence of their arrogance, their systematic rejection of divine revelation, and their blind allegiance to corrupt leaders who prioritized tyranny and defiance over truth, serving as a timeless warning that societies which abandon moral guidance in favor of oppressive authority inevitably invite their own ruin.

translation: And they were followed in this world by a curse and [likewise] on the Day of Resurrection. Unquestionably, indeed 'Ad denied their Lord. Unquestionably, away with 'Ad, the people of Hud.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the punishment of those who reject the truth is not confined to the transitory life of this world but extends into the eternal afterlife, where the consequence of their disbelief persists as a perpetual state of divine alienation; it serves as a stern reminder of the finality of God's judgment, illustrating that the destruction of 'Ad was not merely a historical tragedy but a lasting warning for humanity that those who persist in arrogance against their Creator forfeit both worldly peace and eternal salvation.

translation: And to Thamud We sent their brother Salih. He said, 'O my people, worship Allah; you have no god other than Him. It is He who produced you from the earth and settled you in it, so ask forgiveness of Him and then repent to Him. Indeed, my Lord is near and responsive.'
interpretation: Prophet Salih urges his people to recognize the singular divinity of Allah by reflecting on their creation from the elements of the earth and the resources provided to them for development, emphasizing that true repentance—a turning away from sin accompanied by a sincere plea for forgiveness—is the path to reconciliation with a Creator who is not distant or indifferent, but present and ready to answer those who call upon Him.

translation: They said, 'O Salih, you were among us a man of hope before this. Do you forbid us to worship what our fathers worshipped? And indeed we are, concerning that to which you invite us, in disquieting doubt.'
interpretation: The people of Thamud are expressing their profound astonishment at Salih's rejection of their ancestral idolatry, noting that before his claim to prophethood, they held him in high esteem and anticipated he would become a leader of great wisdom and influence among them. Their rejection stems from a deep-seated cultural and emotional attachment to the traditions of their forefathers, which they prioritize over his message of monotheism, revealing that their doubt is not merely an intellectual disagreement but a defensive state of mind meant to protect their societal status quo.

translation: He said, 'O my people, have you considered: if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord and He has given me mercy from Himself, who would protect me from Allah if I disobeyed Him? So you would not increase me except in loss.'
interpretation: The Prophet Salih (peace be upon him) is highlighting that his message is rooted in absolute divine certainty and heavenly grace, making it impossible for him to deviate from his mission; he explains that if he were to prioritize their desires over God's commands, he would suffer a total and irrevocable loss of his spiritual standing, meaning that their efforts to dissuade him only bring them further away from truth and closer to their own ruin.

translation: And O my people, this is the she-camel of Allah, a sign to you. So leave her to feed on Allah's earth and do not touch her with harm, or you will be seized by an imminent punishment.
interpretation: The Prophet Salih invokes the sanctity of the miraculous she-camel as a test of obedience for his people; he emphasizes that since the land belongs to Allah and the camel is a divine sign, the people have no authority to restrict its grazing or inflict any harm upon it. By doing so, he warns that their failure to respect this manifestation of divine power will be met with immediate divine retribution, highlighting that their rejection of the sign is equivalent to a direct act of defiance against the Creator.

translation: But they hamstrung her, so he said, 'Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days. That is a promise not to be belied.'
interpretation: When the people of Thamud defied the command of Allah by killing the she-camel, Prophet Salih (peace be upon him) informed them that their arrogance and rebellion had exhausted their respite. The three-day period granted to them was not a chance for repentance, but a definitive countdown to their destruction, serving as a final demonstration of Allah’s justice and the inevitability of His decree, ensuring that they would face the consequences of their disbelief and cruelty exactly as promised without any falsehood.

translation: So when Our command came, We saved Salih and those who believed with him by mercy from Us, and from the disgrace of that day. Indeed, it is your Lord who is the All-Powerful, the Exalted in Might.
interpretation: The verse illustrates the divine principle that Allah grants salvation to His messengers and the faithful during times of collective divine retribution, shielding them from the physical destruction and the accompanying spiritual and social humiliation that befalls the disbelievers, thereby reaffirming His absolute power and sovereignty in executing His decree.

translation: And the blast seized those who had wronged, and they lay prostrate within their homes.
interpretation: This verse depicts the swift and total divine retribution that befell those who defied the message of God, illustrating that their arrogance and oppression were met with a singular, devastating sound that left them lifeless and motionless, signifying that all their worldly strength and fortified dwellings could offer no protection against the inevitable decree of Allah.

translation: As if they had never prospered therein. Verily, Thamud disbelieved in their Lord. Verily, away with Thamud!
interpretation: The verse serves as a profound reflection on the transience of worldly power and the certainty of divine justice, illustrating that the civilization of Thamud was so completely obliterated after their defiance of God’s signs that it appeared as though they had never established homes, enjoyed life, or held authority in those lands, thereby emphasizing that persistent arrogance and rejection of truth lead not only to spiritual ruin but to the total erasure of a people's legacy from the face of the earth.

translation: And certainly did Our messengers come to Abraham with good tidings. They said, 'Peace,' and he said, 'Peace,' and did not delay in bringing a roasted calf.
interpretation: This verse highlights the high moral character and exemplary hospitality of Prophet Abraham, who, upon receiving the angels disguised as guests, immediately prioritized serving them with a prepared meal despite his initial lack of knowledge regarding their true celestial nature. It emphasizes the Islamic virtue of honoring guests with warmth and promptness, as well as the mutual exchange of peace as a foundational greeting between the emissaries of God and the Prophet.

translation: But when he saw their hands did not reach for it, he mistrusted them and felt a sense of fear from them. They said, 'Do not fear; we have been sent to the people of Lot.'
interpretation: The fear Ibrahim felt signifies a natural human instinct and a sign of his discernment, as in ancient customs, a guest who refused to eat from his host's table was viewed as a potential enemy or someone intending harm. His mistrust arose because he realized these visitors were not ordinary men, and their refusal to partake in the food indicated they were supernatural beings, leading him to fear that their arrival might be for the purpose of bringing divine judgment or punishment.

translation: And his wife was standing, so she laughed, and We gave her glad tidings of Isaac, and after Isaac, Jacob.
interpretation: This verse describes the reaction of Sarah, the wife of Abraham, when the angels visited them to announce the destruction of the people of Lot and to bring them news of a child. Her laughter was an expression of amazement and joyful surprise, as she had reached an old age and was previously barren. The glad tidings indicated that God would grant her a son, Isaac, and that his lineage would continue through his own son, Jacob, thereby confirming that she would live long enough to see her grandson and ensure the continuation of the prophetic line.

translation: She said, 'Woe to me! Shall I give birth while I am an old woman and this, my husband, is an old man? Indeed, this is an amazing thing.'
interpretation: Sarah's exclamation of surprise reflects the human limitation of perceiving biological impossibilities as absolute, serving as a backdrop to highlight that Allah's decree transcends natural laws and aging processes; her reaction is not a denial of divine power, but a human expression of awe at the breaking of established patterns of life and fertility.

translation: They said, 'Are you amazed at the decree of Allah? The mercy of Allah and His blessings be upon you, people of the house. Indeed, He is Praiseworthy and Honorable.'
interpretation: The angels were addressing Sarah, the wife of Prophet Ibrahim, to calm her astonishment regarding the announcement of the birth of her son Ishaq in her old age, clarifying that the decree of Allah is absolute and His power is limitless, and they invoked upon her and her household the mercy and blessings of Allah, as they are the chosen ones to receive His divine grace and honor.

translation: When the fear had left Abraham and the glad tidings had reached him, he began to argue with Us concerning the people of Lot.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the compassion and mercy of Prophet Abraham, as he did not immediately rejoice at the news of his own son's birth but instead sought to intercede for the people of Lot out of deep concern for humanity and a desire to see if repentance could yet be found among them before the divine decree of punishment was finalized.

translation: Indeed, Abraham was forbearing, grieving, and oft-turning back [to Allah].
interpretation: This verse characterizes the Prophet Abraham with three fundamental virtues: 'Halim' refers to his immense self-restraint and patience, even when provoked; 'Awwah' denotes his deep empathy and constant expression of grief or sighing in humble prayer and concern for his people; and 'Munib' signifies his state of perpetual repentance and total reliance, constantly returning his heart and focus to Allah in every situation.

translation: O Abraham, give this up. Indeed, the command of your Lord has come, and indeed, there will reach them a punishment that cannot be repelled.
interpretation: These words were addressed to Prophet Abraham by the angels when he began to plead with them to spare the people of Lot from destruction, highlighting that Allah's decree for their punishment was already finalized and inevitable, thereby closing the door for further intercession because justice for their persistence in sin had become mandatory.

translation: And when Our messengers came to Lot, he was distressed for them and felt helpless regarding them, and said, 'This is a distressful day.'
interpretation: When the angels arrived in the form of handsome youths, Prophet Lot felt intense inner turmoil and anxiety, not because he was unwelcoming, but because he was deeply afraid that his perverse and wicked people would attempt to harm his guests, leaving him feeling powerless to protect them from the impending shame and violence.

translation: And his people came to him, rushing towards him, and before this they had been committing evil deeds. He said, 'O my people, these are my daughters; they are purer for you. So fear Allah and do not disgrace me regarding my guests. Is there not among you a man of right conduct?'
interpretation: In this verse, Prophet Lut attempts to divert his people from their abominable behavior toward his guests by offering his own daughters for lawful marriage, emphasizing that this is a purer and more righteous path than the sin they intend to commit. By asking if there is a man of 'right conduct' among them, he is appealing to their innate sense of honor, reason, and moral integrity, highlighting that their actions are not only sinful but also deeply irrational and shameful.

translation: They said, 'You have certainly known that we have no right to your daughters, and indeed, you know what we want.'
interpretation: The people of Lot, in their state of utter moral corruption and arrogance, were asserting to Lot that they had no interest in marital relationships with women, which were the natural and lawful rights of men; they were essentially declaring that their deviant desires were directed exclusively toward men, thereby defying the natural order and the divine law that Lot was sent to uphold.

translation: He said, 'If only I had against you some power or could take refuge in a strong support.'
interpretation: Prophet Lut (Lot) is expressing his human vulnerability and the lack of physical protection he had against the corrupt men of his community, wishing for either personal strength or the support of a powerful tribe or ally to shield him and his guests from their transgression.

translation: They said, 'O Lot, indeed we are messengers of your Lord; they will never reach you. So set out with your family during a portion of the night and let not any among you look back, except your wife; indeed, that which will strike them will strike her. Indeed, their appointment is [for] the morning. Is the morning not near?'
interpretation: The angels reassured Prophet Lot that the people of Sodom, who were intent on harming him, would be unable to cause him any injury, signaling divine protection. By commanding him to leave at night without looking back, they were instructing him to maintain focus and resolve in his departure, emphasizing the finality of the impending divine punishment that would destroy the evildoers. The specific exclusion of his wife highlights that spiritual kinship and the sanctity of one's message take precedence over biological or marital ties, as she had aligned herself with the moral depravity of her people and thus shared in their ultimate fate.

translation: So when Our command came, We turned it [the city] upside down and rained upon it stones of baked clay, layered one after another.
interpretation: This verse depicts the absolute and total annihilation of the people of Lut, signifying that the punishment of Allah, once it descends, is inescapable and transformative, reducing that which was once elevated and proud to utter ruin and baseness, as the raining of inscribed stones indicates a deliberate, sequential, and divinely ordained destruction that leaves no trace of the corruption that previously existed.

translation: Marked by your Lord, and it is not far from the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse warns the disbelievers of Quraysh—and by extension, all who commit injustice—that the same divine punishment which destroyed previous nations, such as the people of Lot, is already prepared and specifically designated for them. It signifies that their destruction is not a distant or impossible event, but rather a looming reality that could overtake them at any moment, as their persistent denial and oppression have brought them into the same spiritual and physical proximity to divine retribution as those who perished before them.

translation: And to Madyan We sent their brother Shu'ayb. He said, 'O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. And do not decrease from the measure and the weight. Indeed, I see you in prosperity, but indeed, I fear for you the punishment of an all-encompassing Day.'
interpretation: The Prophet Shu'ayb reminds his people of the blessings of economic prosperity they are currently enjoying, warning them that if they continue to engage in fraudulent commercial practices—such as cheating in measurements and weights—they risk losing those blessings and inviting divine retribution. He highlights that justice and honesty in worldly dealings are inseparable from the monotheistic worship of Allah, and that persistent defiance of moral limits will eventually lead to a catastrophic judgment that none can escape.

translation: And O my people, give full measure and weight in justice, and do not deprive people of their due, and do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption.
interpretation: Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) enjoins his people to uphold absolute integrity in all their economic dealings, emphasizing that honest transactions are not merely a matter of commercial ethics but a fundamental pillar of social justice, and he warns that undermining the rights of others through fraud or manipulation disrupts the moral and social order, ultimately leading to widespread spiritual and material decay.

translation: That which is left by Allah is best for you, if you are believers. And I am not a guardian over you.
interpretation: The 'remnant of Allah' refers to the lawful profit and blessings that remain after one has fulfilled their duties with honesty and fairness in dealings. It signifies that what Allah permits—obtained through integrity and justice—is far superior in quality and long-term benefit than the greater gains accumulated through fraud, deceit, or short-changing others. The verse emphasizes that true prosperity is found in God's approval rather than in the quantity of illicit acquisitions, and it highlights that the Prophet's role was merely to convey the truth, not to compel belief or watch over the people's every move.

translation: They said, 'O Shu'ayb, does your prayer command you that we should leave what our fathers used to worship or that we should not do with our wealth what we please? Indeed, you are the forbearing, the discerning.'
interpretation: The people of Shu'ayb used sarcasm and irony to mock him, acknowledging his reputation for wisdom and kindness only to belittle his message. By asking if his prayer was the source of his opposition to their idol worship and their corrupt economic practices, they were attempting to frame his religious devotion as an irrational interference in their ancestral traditions and their personal autonomy regarding property, thereby exposing their own attachment to material gain and the status quo over divine guidance.

translation: And O my people, let not your disagreement with me lead you to [the fate of] a state similar to that which struck the people of Noah or the people of Hud or the people of Salih. And the people of Lot are not far from you.
interpretation: Shu'ayb warns his people that their persistence in disbelief and their opposition to his call should not incite them to persist in their stubbornness to the point that it triggers divine punishment, as had happened to previous nations. He reminds them that the destruction of the people of Lot occurred relatively recently in history and in a location known to them, serving as a clear, tangible, and near-at-hand evidence of the inevitable consequences of rejecting the messengers and disobeying God's commandments.

translation: And ask forgiveness of your Lord and repent to Him. Indeed, my Lord is Merciful and Affectionate.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that true repentance requires two distinct steps: first, seeking God’s forgiveness for past sins through humility and acknowledgment, and second, turning back to Him with a firm resolve to align one's future actions with His guidance; this process is supported by the divine attributes of Rahīm, indicating His boundless mercy in overlooking faults, and Wadūd, signifying that He deeply loves those who return to Him, welcoming their reformation with warmth and grace.

translation: They said, 'O Shu'ayb, we do not understand much of what you say, and indeed, we consider you among us as weak. And if not for your family, we would have stoned you [to death]; and you are not to us one respected.'
interpretation: The people of Midian, blinded by their arrogance and immersion in disbelief, were unable to comprehend the profound divine wisdom in the Prophet Shu'ayb's message, dismissing it as incoherent or insignificant; they measured his authority by worldly status and physical power rather than truth, and it was only out of fear of tribal backlash from his kin—not out of respect for him or his message—that they refrained from executing him.

translation: He said, 'O my people, is my clan more respected by you than Allah, while you have put Him behind your backs [in neglect]? Indeed, my Lord is encompassing of what you do.'
interpretation: The Prophet Shu'ayb is rebuking his people for prioritizing the worldly protection and social status afforded by their kinship and clan over their duty and obedience to Allah. By asking if his tribe is more honorable to them than their Creator, he highlights their spiritual arrogance and hypocrisy, noting that they have relegated Allah's commands to insignificance—like an item cast aside behind one's back—while mistakenly believing their own power or alliances can shield them from the divine reckoning, which is inevitable because Allah is fully aware of their secret and public actions.

translation: And O my people, work according to your position; indeed, I am working. You are going to know to whom will come a punishment that will disgrace him and who is a liar. So watch; indeed, I am with you a watcher.
interpretation: The prophet Shu'ayb is delivering a final, stern warning to his people, informing them that since they have chosen to persist in their defiance and arrogance, they should continue their course of action while he maintains his commitment to his faith and mission. The verse serves as a challenge to their skepticism; by invoking the certainty of divine retribution, he forces them to await a future judgment where the truth of his prophecy and the falsehood of their claims will be unambiguously revealed through the unfolding of their destruction.

translation: And when Our command came, We saved Shu'ayb and those who believed with him by mercy from Us, and the blast seized those who had wronged, and they became [corpses] fallen prone within their homes.
interpretation: The verse illustrates the divine principle of justice where God delivers His prophets and the believers who remain steadfast, while simultaneously meting out punishment upon the oppressors. The 'blast' signifies the terrifying sound of divine retribution that left the arrogant sinners lifeless and immobilized in their own dwellings, demonstrating that their material security and perceived power offered them no protection against the inevitable decree of the Almighty.

translation: As if they had not prospered therein; so away with Madyan, just as Thamud were done away with.
interpretation: The verse serves as a stark reminder of the transience of worldly power and luxury, illustrating that even nations who once thrived in wealth and stability can be completely erased as if they never existed, signaling that those who reject divine guidance and persist in oppression are destined for the same inevitable ruin that befell their predecessors.

translation: And We certainly sent Moses with Our signs and a clear authority.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah did not send Moses to Pharaoh and his people without evidence; rather, He provided him with divine miracles and irrefutable proofs, such as the staff and the shining hand, which served as a manifest authority—an undeniable argument that validated his prophethood and compelled the people to recognize the truth he brought from his Lord.

translation: To Pharaoh and his establishment, but they followed the command of Pharaoh, and the command of Pharaoh was not rightly guiding.
interpretation: The verse illustrates the danger of blind obedience to a corrupt authority, highlighting that when a leader lacks divine guidance and moral integrity, those who follow his decrees are led away from truth and into ultimate ruin, for any system built upon arrogance and defiance of God cannot lead humanity toward righteousness or true success.

translation: He will precede his people on the Day of Resurrection and lead them into the Fire; and wretched is the place to which they are led.
interpretation: This verse describes the tragic end of Pharaoh who, having led his followers into arrogance and disbelief during their worldly life, will continue to lead them as they march toward the punishment of Hell in the afterlife, serving as the first to enter the fire and demonstrating that those who follow corrupt leadership into sin will ultimately share in its devastating consequences.

translation: And they were followed in this [world] with a curse, and [so will they be] on the Day of Resurrection. How wretched is the gift which is given.
interpretation: This verse signifies that those who chose to follow Pharaoh and his oppressive ways have brought upon themselves a dual legacy of destruction: they are destined to be cursed and distanced from God's mercy throughout their earthly lives, and this state of condemnation will persist and culminate on the Day of Resurrection, where the 'gift' or recompense they receive—which is the eternal punishment of Hell—serves as the most miserable and debased outcome imaginable for those who turned away from truth.

translation: That is from the tidings of the towns which We relate to you; of them are some that are standing and some that have been mowed down.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine reminder that history is not merely a collection of past events, but a moral lesson concerning the rise and fall of civilizations. By describing some towns as 'standing' (remnants that still exist) and others as 'mowed down' (completely destroyed and leveled like harvested crops), Allah highlights the inevitable consequence of arrogance and disbelief. It signifies that the prosperity or ruin of a society is directly linked to its adherence to divine truth and moral integrity, illustrating that no power on earth can grant permanence once a people have abandoned the path of righteousness.

translation: And We did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves. So their gods which they invoked besides Allah did not avail them at all when the command of your Lord came, and they did not increase them in anything other than ruin.
interpretation: The verse clarifies that the destruction of those who reject the truth is not an act of divine injustice, but a direct consequence of their own choices and persistence in falsehood. When the divine decree of punishment arrived, the false deities they worshiped—and upon whom they relied for protection or intercession—proved to be completely powerless, failing to offer any defense or benefit and only leading them further into profound loss and spiritual destruction.

translation: And such is the seizure of your Lord when He seizes the cities while they are committing wrong. Indeed, His seizure is painful and severe.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine warning to oppressors and those who persist in disbelief and corruption, illustrating that Allah's retribution is not impulsive but follows a pattern of patient respite; however, when His decree for punishment arrives, it is inescapable, absolute, and profoundly agonizing, demonstrating that no amount of worldly power or prosperity can shield a society from the consequences of its moral and spiritual transgressions against the truth.

translation: Indeed in that is a sign for those who fear the punishment of the Hereafter. That is a Day for which the people will be gathered, and that is a Day [which will be] witnessed.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that the events and historical lessons mentioned prior serve as a clear manifestation of Allah’s power and justice for those who maintain a state of God-consciousness, specifically fearing the accountability of the final judgment. It highlights that the Day of Resurrection is an inevitable reality where all of humanity, from the first to the last, will be brought together in a singular, grand assembly that will be observed and attended by all creatures, angels, and prophets, leaving no room for denial or escape from the ultimate accounting.

translation: And We do not delay it except for a limited term.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the respite granted to the disbelievers and the postponement of their inevitable punishment or the final arrival of the Day of Judgment is not an act of negligence by God, but rather a deliberate choice to allow a precisely calculated period of time to pass, during which the decree of God regarding the course of human history and individual testing must be fulfilled exactly as intended.

translation: On the Day it comes, no soul shall speak except by His permission. And among them will be the wretched and the prosperous.
interpretation: This verse signifies the absolute sovereignty of Allah on the Day of Judgment, where the normal order of worldly discourse is suspended, rendering human will subordinate to Divine decree; the categorization into 'wretched' and 'prosperous' serves as an ontological classification based on the eternal outcomes of their deeds, underscoring that destiny on that day is purely a result of God's final judgment rather than individual worldly status.

translation: As for those who were wretched, they will be in the Fire, wherein they will have sobbing and sighing.
interpretation: This verse describes the state of the damned in the afterlife, where the intensity of their suffering manifests physically as sounds of profound anguish; 'zafir' refers to the long, deep exhalation caused by extreme distress, while 'shahiq' refers to the sharp, agonizing inhalation, illustrating that their punishment is an inescapable cycle of intense, agonizing respiratory strain caused by the overwhelming heat and despair of Hell.

translation: Abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills. Indeed, your Lord is a doer of what He intends.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the duration of the inhabitants of Paradise or Hell within their respective dwellings is subject to the absolute will and sovereign power of Allah, signifying that nothing in the entire creation falls outside His control or decree, and He possesses the ultimate authority to execute His will according to His supreme wisdom, regardless of the apparent state of the universe.

translation: And as for those who were prosperous, they will be in Paradise, abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills—a gift uninterrupted.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the bliss of the believers in Paradise is eternal and everlasting, emphasizing that it is a permanent bestowal from Allah that will never be cut off or diminished, despite the mention of a divine exception, which scholars explain signifies Allah's absolute sovereignty and power to alter circumstances, though He has decreed that this state of grace shall endure forever without end.

translation: So do not be in doubt, [O Muhammad], as to what these people worship. They worship not except as their fathers worshipped before. And indeed, We will give them their full portion undiminished.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine reassurance to the Prophet Muhammad, commanding him not to harbor any uncertainty regarding the falsehood of the idols worshipped by the polytheists. It clarifies that their adherence to these practices is merely an act of blind imitation of their ancestors, devoid of divine guidance or intellectual justification. Furthermore, it serves as a stern warning that God will grant them their full, destined share of punishment in the afterlife, precisely measured and without the slightest reduction, as a consequence of their persistent disbelief and refusal to seek the truth.

translation: And We certainly gave Moses the Scripture, but it came under disagreement. And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been judged between them. And indeed, they are, concerning it, in disquieting doubt.
interpretation: The verse highlights the recurring human tendency to dispute divine guidance even when it is clearly revealed; Allah explains that while the truth was made manifest through the Torah, people fragmented into conflicting factions regarding its meaning, yet the only reason they are not immediately punished for this rejection is because Allah has decreed a period of respite until the Day of Judgment, during which their persistent, unsettling skepticism remains a veil over their hearts.

translation: And indeed, your Lord will fully compensate each of them for their deeds. Indeed, He is, of what they do, Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse serves as a solemn assurance that divine justice is absolute and meticulous; every individual, whether their actions were righteous or sinful, will receive the complete and precise recompense they earned during their worldly life, because God possesses comprehensive knowledge of every minute detail of human conduct, leaving nothing hidden from His ultimate judgment.

translation: So remain on a right course as you have been commanded, [you] and those who have turned back with you [to Allah], and do not transgress. Indeed, He is Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse commands the Prophet and the believers to remain steadfast and firm upon the straight path of monotheism and righteous conduct without deviation or excess, emphasizing that the limits set by Allah must not be overstepped through injustice or rebellion, as Allah is an ever-watchful Observer of all actions, whether hidden or manifest.

translation: And do not incline toward those who do wrong, lest the Fire should touch you, and you have no protectors other than Allah, nor would you then be helped.
interpretation: The verse serves as a stern prohibition against seeking support, showing affection, or aligning oneself with oppressors and tyrants who violate the boundaries of Allah, as even a slight inclination toward their ways reflects a compromise of faith that risks spiritual ruin and exposes the believer to the same divine punishment that awaits the oppressors.

translation: And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night. Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds. That is a reminder for those who remember.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that maintaining consistent, obligatory prayers throughout the day serves as a spiritual purification, where the act of performing good deeds acts as a mechanism to expunge the record of minor sins, serving as a vital constant reminder for believers to remain mindful of their purpose and connection to God.

translation: And be patient, for indeed, Allah does not allow to be lost the reward of those who do good.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine assurance that steadfastness in the face of hardship, combined with excellence in conduct and devotion to God, is never in vain; every act of patience and every effort to perform deeds with righteousness is meticulously recorded by Allah, who ensures that the doer will eventually receive their full recompense, whether in this world or in the afterlife.

translation: So why were there not among the generations before you those of enduring wisdom who forbade corruption on the earth, except a few of those We saved from among them? But those who did wrong pursued what they were given to enjoy of luxury, and they were criminals.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern critique of historical societies, highlighting the catastrophic consequence of a society's moral silence. It laments the lack of influential, virtuous leaders—people of 'enduring wisdom'—who possess the moral authority and courage to actively confront and suppress societal corruption. The implication is that when the righteous remain passive or fail to restrain the spread of immorality, the society inevitably descends into ruin, driven by a hedonistic elite who prioritize fleeting worldly luxuries over ethical conduct, ultimately leading to their own destruction as a result of their criminal disobedience.

translation: And your Lord would not have destroyed the cities for wrongdoing while their people were reformers.
interpretation: This verse indicates that God does not inflict destruction upon a society merely for their errors in belief or minor sins as long as the people are actively engaged in mutual correction, upholding justice, and striving to rectify social corruption, as this collective effort to improve prevents the descent into the total moral collapse that warrants divine retribution.

translation: And if your Lord had willed, He could have made mankind one community, but they will not cease to differ.
interpretation: This verse signifies that Allah has endowed human beings with the freedom of choice and the capacity for independent reasoning, which inherently leads to a diversity of opinions, beliefs, and temperaments. The persistent existence of these differences is an integral aspect of the worldly test, intended to encourage humanity to exercise their intellect, engage in dialogue, and fulfill the divine wisdom of mutual acquaintance and striving toward truth amidst varied perspectives.

translation: Except for those on whom your Lord has mercy, and for that He created them. But the word of your Lord is to be fulfilled: 'I will surely fill Hell with jinn and mankind all together.'
interpretation: The verse indicates that Allah created humanity with diverse temperaments and paths; while the majority of people are destined for divergence due to their exercise of free will in choosing disbelief, those who receive Allah's mercy are exempt from this fate, and the final decree of Allah is inevitable as it serves to manifest His justice and the fulfillment of His supreme will regarding the ultimate destination of both those who choose guidance and those who persist in error.

translation: And all that We relate to you of the stories of the messengers is that by which We make firm your heart. And there has come to you, in this, the truth and an instruction and a reminder for the believers.
interpretation: Allah narrates the trials and triumphs of past prophets to the Prophet Muhammad to reassure his heart and strengthen his resolve in the face of adversity, showing him that the path of truth is often difficult but ultimately leads to divine victory, thereby providing a source of spiritual stability, moral guidance, and a reminder of the consistent nature of faith for those who believe.

translation: And say to those who do not believe, 'Work according to your station; indeed, we are working.'
