interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning and a declaration of firm resolve, where Allah commands the Prophet to tell the disbelievers that they may persist in their ways and strategies as much as they are able, for the believers are likewise persistent in their mission and devotion to the truth, and both parties will soon witness the final outcome of their respective actions when the time of reckoning arrives.

translation: And wait; indeed, we are waiting.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning from the believers to the disbelievers, indicating that the final outcome will be decided by Allah; just as the disbelievers are waiting for a misfortune to befall the believers or for their own desires to be realized, the believers are likewise waiting for the divine promise of victory and the punishment of those who reject the truth.

translation: And to Allah belongs the unseen [aspects] of the heavens and the earth, and to Him will be returned the matter, all of it, so worship Him and rely upon Him. And your Lord is not unaware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah, asserting that all knowledge of the unseen realms, hidden from human perception in both the celestial and earthly domains, resides solely with Him. Because all affairs—be they personal, historical, or universal—ultimately culminate in His judgment, the believer is instructed to direct their singular devotion toward Him and place complete trust in His decree. The concluding reminder serves as both a comfort to the righteous and a warning to the heedless, affirming that nothing escapes the divine vigilance and that every action, whether public or secret, is recorded and will be accounted for.

translation: Alif-Lam-Ra. These are the verses of the clear Book.
interpretation: The verse serves as an opening declaration highlighting that the Qur'an consists of signs and revelations that are inherently clear, explicit in their message, and serve to distinguish truth from falsehood, thereby leaving no room for ambiguity for those who seek guidance.

translation: Indeed, We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an that you might understand.
interpretation: God chose to reveal the Qur'an in the Arabic language because it is a clear, eloquent, and precise medium of expression, intended to ensure that the message is fully comprehended and reflected upon by the intellect, thereby leading the recipients to grasp the profound divine truths and guidance contained within it.

translation: We relate to you, [O Muhammad], the best of stories in what We have revealed to you of this Qur'an although you were, before it, among the unaware.
interpretation: God informs the Prophet Muhammad that the narratives contained within the Qur'an are superior to all other historical accounts because they are perfectly preserved revelations that serve a divine purpose of moral instruction and spiritual guidance, confirming that the Prophet had no prior access to these specific historical details, thereby emphasizing the authenticity of his prophethood as coming directly from divine inspiration.

translation: When Joseph said to his father, 'O my father, indeed I saw [in a dream] eleven stars and the sun and the moon; I saw them prostrating to me.'
interpretation: This dream was a divine revelation and a glad tiding signifying that Joseph would attain a position of high status and authority, to which his brothers, represented by the eleven stars, and his parents, represented by the sun and the moon, would eventually show reverence and submission.

translation: He said, 'O my son, do not relate your vision to your brothers or they will contrive against you a plan. Indeed Satan, to man, is a manifest enemy.'
interpretation: Prophet Ya'qub warns his son Yusuf against sharing his dream with his brothers, fearing that their hearts may be overcome by jealousy and the whispers of Satan, who constantly seeks to incite malice and destruction between family members to sever ties of kinship and incite sin.

translation: And thus will your Lord choose you and teach you the interpretation of events and complete His favor upon you and upon the family of Jacob, as He completed it upon your fathers before, Abraham and Isaac. Indeed, your Lord is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: Allah signifies that He will select Joseph for prophecy and convey to him the deep inner meanings and outcomes of dreams and worldly affairs, assuring him that this divine selection is a continuation of the spiritual legacy and blessings bestowed upon his forefathers, Abraham and Isaac, confirming that Allah's orchestration of these events is rooted in His perfect knowledge of what is best for His servants and His supreme wisdom in placing His grace where it is most deserved.

translation: Certainly were there in Yusuf and his brothers signs for those who ask.
interpretation: The story of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) and his brothers serves as a profound manifestation of Allah's divine wisdom and providence, illustrating how patience in the face of injustice and steadfastness in faith lead to ultimate victory and reunion, thereby providing evidence for those who inquire about the lessons inherent in the experiences of the prophets and the complexities of human nature.

translation: When they said, 'Yusuf and his brother are more beloved to our father than we, while we are a group; indeed, our father is in clear error.'
interpretation: The brothers of Yusuf fell into the trap of envy and arrogance, blinding them to the truth; they perceived their father's love for Yusuf as an injustice, failing to realize that Ya'qub’s affection was a reflection of Yusuf's inherent spiritual nobility and integrity, leading them to wrongly accuse their righteous father of misjudgment and loss of wisdom.

translation: Kill Joseph or cast him into some land, so that your father's attention may be exclusively yours, and after that, you will be a righteous people.
interpretation: The brothers of Joseph suggested removing him from his father's presence by either killing him or exiling him to a remote land, believing that by eliminating the competition for their father's affection and devotion, they could secure his undivided attention; they further deluded themselves into thinking that they could commit this grave sin and subsequently repent to restore their moral standing, demonstrating their moral confusion in seeking to achieve righteousness through an act of heinous injustice.

translation: One of them said, 'Do not kill Joseph, but throw him into the bottom of the well; some travelers will pick him up, if you must do something.'
interpretation: The speaker, who was the most sensible among the brothers, aimed to save Joseph's life while still satisfying the brothers' desire to remove him from their father's presence. By suggesting the well, he hoped that Joseph would be discovered and taken away by passing caravans, thereby distancing him from their sight without the guilt and permanent consequence of murder, reflecting a calculated compromise between their malice and the preservation of his life.

translation: They said, 'O our father, why do you not entrust us with Joseph, while indeed we are his sincere well-wishers?'
interpretation: The brothers of Joseph attempted to manipulate their father, Prophet Ya'qub (Jacob), by feigning deep concern and affection for Joseph, using the language of sincerity and protection to mask their underlying jealousy and malicious intent, thereby trying to persuade him that they would look after Joseph while they actually intended to remove him from his father's presence.

translation: Send him with us tomorrow that he may eat well and play, and indeed, we will be his guardians.
interpretation: The brothers of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) used this deceptive language to manipulate their father, Ya'qub (Jacob), into letting Yusuf go with them. By emphasizing that Yusuf would 'eat well and play,' they portrayed their intentions as innocent and fun, while their hidden agenda was to remove him from his father's presence and abandon him in a well to satisfy their deep-seated jealousy.

translation: He said, 'Indeed, it saddens me that you should take him, and I fear that a wolf would eat him while you are of him unaware.'
interpretation: Prophet Ya'qub expressed his deep fatherly concern and dread, knowing his sons were resentful of Yusuf, and he used the fear of a wolf as an indirect way to warn them against neglecting him, while simultaneously betraying the profound sorrow he felt at the mere prospect of being separated from his beloved son.

translation: They said, 'If a wolf should eat him while we are a strong group, then indeed, we would be losers.'
interpretation: The brothers of Joseph argued that it would be illogical and shameful for them to return to their father without their brother, claiming that if a wolf were to consume him despite them being a united, capable, and physically strong band of brothers, they would effectively be rendered weak and incompetent, having failed in the very duty of protection that they had promised their father.

translation: So when they took him and agreed to put him into the bottom of the well, We inspired him: 'You will surely inform them about this affair of theirs while they do not perceive.'
interpretation: God comforted Joseph in his moment of extreme abandonment by revealing to him that his current predicament was not the end of his story, assuring him that a time would come when he would be in a position of power and authority, at which point he would remind his brothers of their betrayal while they would be completely unaware of his true identity.

translation: And they came to their father at nightfall, weeping.
interpretation: The brothers of Yusuf chose to return to their father Ya'qub under the cover of darkness to avoid scrutiny of their faces, as they knew that daylight would reveal the falsehood in their expressions, while their feigned tears were a calculated attempt to manipulate his emotions and validate their deceitful claim regarding Yusuf's fate.

translation: They said, 'O our father, indeed we went racing each other and left Joseph with our possessions, and the wolf ate him. But you would not believe us, even if we were truthful.'
interpretation: The brothers of Joseph utilized the vulnerability of their father's deep love and intuition; they anticipated his inherent skepticism toward their story by explicitly stating he would not believe them, a rhetorical device intended to manipulate him into doubting his own instincts and accepting their fabricated narrative as the only available account of Joseph's disappearance.

translation: And they brought his shirt stained with false blood. He said, 'Rather, your souls have enticed you to something, so patience is most fitting. And Allah is the one sought for help against that which you describe.'
interpretation: Jacob, upon him be peace, perceived that the blood was not from a wolf, as his sons had claimed, because the shirt was not torn, revealing their deceit. By saying 'patience is most fitting,' he chose to endure this profound tragedy with a steadfast soul that does not complain to people, but instead relies entirely on Allah to grant him the strength to bear this loss and to eventually reveal the truth of their treachery.

translation: And there came a company of travelers; they sent their water-drawer, and he let down his bucket. He said, 'Good news! Here is a boy!' And they concealed him as merchandise. And Allah is All-Knowing of what they do.
interpretation: This verse recounts a pivotal moment where the caravaners, acting as intermediaries of divine decree, discovered Prophet Yusuf in the well. The 'good news' expressed by the water-drawer reveals that they viewed Yusuf not as a human being deserving of dignity, but as a valuable commodity to be traded for profit. Their act of concealing him reflects the greed of the human heart that seeks to obfuscate truth for material gain, yet the verse concludes by reminding the reader that Allah is fully aware of their intentions and actions, signaling that despite their secrecy and worldly schemes, the divine plan for Yusuf was already unfolding beyond their limited understanding.

translation: And they sold him for a reduced price, a few silver coins; and they were, concerning him, among those content with little.
interpretation: The brothers of Yusuf, driven by their jealousy and desire to be rid of him, treated him as a mere commodity of little value, selling him to passing travelers for a meager sum because they had no desire for his presence and wished only to see him disappear from their lives forever.

translation: And the man from Egypt who bought him said to his wife, 'Make his stay honorable; perhaps he may benefit us, or we may adopt him as a son.' And thus We established Joseph in the land that We might teach him the interpretation of events. And Allah is predominant over His affair, but most of the people do not know.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the absolute divine decree of Allah, showing that despite the outward circumstances—such as Joseph being sold into slavery—Allah was orchestrating events to place him in a position of power and wisdom. It emphasizes that no human plan or earthly authority can thwart the ultimate will of Allah, who possesses complete dominion and fulfills His purpose, even when human beings are blind to the underlying wisdom behind their trials.

translation: And when he reached his maturity, We gave him judgment and knowledge. And thus do We reward the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse highlights that the attainment of physical and mental maturity serves as a divine threshold for receiving deeper wisdom and spiritual insight, demonstrating that God bestows clear discernment and beneficial knowledge upon those who conduct their lives with excellence, sincerity, and awareness of His presence in all their actions.

translation: And she, in whose house he was, sought to seduce him. She closed the doors and said, 'Come to me.' He said, 'I seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, my master has made good my residence. Indeed, wrongdoers do not succeed.'
interpretation: When the wife of Al-Aziz attempted to entice Prophet Yusuf into committing adultery by locking the doors and inviting him, he adamantly refused, citing his gratitude and loyalty to his master who had treated him with kindness and honor. By saying 'I seek refuge in Allah,' he demonstrated that his ultimate loyalty was to his Creator, acknowledging that one who commits such a grave transgression and violates the trust placed in him by his benefactor will never find true success or prosperity.

translation: And she certainly desired him, and he would have desired her, had he not seen the proof of his Lord. Thus it was that We might divert from him evil and immorality. Indeed, he was of Our chosen servants.
interpretation: The verse indicates that when the wife of Al-Aziz attempted to seduce Joseph, the natural human inclination might have momentarily stirred within him, yet this was instantly quelled by a clear spiritual sign or divine insight from Allah. This 'proof' refers to a firm realization of the sanctity of his moral duty and the fear of God, which fortified his resolve. The verse clarifies that Allah strengthens His truly sincere servants by bestowing upon them inner guidance, thereby protecting them from falling into sin and ensuring their hearts remain pure and untainted by base desires.

translation: And they both raced to the door, and she tore his shirt from the back, and they found her master at the door. She said, 'What is the recompense for one who intended evil for your wife but that he be imprisoned or a painful punishment?'
interpretation: The verse illustrates the intense physical struggle that occurred when Prophet Yusuf attempted to flee from the wife of Al-Aziz. The fact that the shirt was torn from the back serves as irrefutable forensic evidence of Yusuf's innocence and her pursuit, demonstrating that he was running away from her while she was pulling him back. Her immediate attempt to accuse him to her husband was a calculated effort to manipulate the situation and protect her own reputation by shifting the blame onto the one who was actually the victim of her seduction.

translation: He said, 'It was she who sought to seduce me.' And a witness from her own family testified, 'If his shirt is torn from the front, then she has spoken the truth, and he is of the liars.'
interpretation: The witness, who was endowed with wisdom, realized that the nature of the tear in the garment would reveal the reality of the situation; if the shirt were torn from the front, it would imply that the man was moving toward the woman or resisting her in a face-to-face confrontation, but the logic relied upon here suggests that a tear at the front confirms the woman's proactive approach in pursuit of her desire, thereby proving the man's innocence.

translation: But if his shirt is torn from the back, then she has lied, and he is of the truthful.
interpretation: This verse presents a criterion for determining the truth in a situation of false accusation; it dictates that the physical evidence of the torn shirt indicates where the struggle or movement originated. If the garment was torn from the back, it serves as evidence that the accused was fleeing rather than advancing, thereby proving his innocence and exposing the fabrication of his accuser.

translation: So when he saw his shirt torn from the back, he said, 'Indeed, it is of your plan. Indeed, your plan is great.'
interpretation: The husband of the woman realized that Yusuf's shirt being torn from the back served as definitive evidence that he was fleeing from her attempt to seduce him, rather than him being the aggressor. By stating that her 'plan' or 'stratagem' is great, he is acknowledging the profound and dangerous nature of the deception employed to frame an innocent person, highlighting the capacity for manipulative cunning that can arise when someone is driven by uncontrolled desire.

translation: O Joseph, ignore this. And you, [O wife of Aziz], ask forgiveness for your sin. Indeed, you were of the sinful.
interpretation: The verse illustrates the swift transition from a situation of temptation to one of moral accountability, where the ruler advises Joseph to maintain his integrity by setting aside the incident to prevent public scandal, while simultaneously confronting his wife with the necessity of repentance, emphasizing that her deliberate pursuit of an illicit desire constitutes a clear transgression against divine and moral boundaries.

translation: And women in the city said, 'The wife of Al-Aziz is seeking to seduce her slave boy; he has impassioned her with love. Indeed, we see her in clear error.'
interpretation: The women of the city observed the behavior of the wife of Al-Aziz, perceiving that her infatuation with Joseph had surpassed the boundaries of propriety and reason, leading them to criticize her public loss of dignity and moral judgment due to an obsessive, illicit desire that had blinded her to her societal status and the sanctity of her marriage.

translation: And when she heard of their scheming, she sent for them and prepared a banquet for them and gave each one of them a knife, and she said, 'Come out before them.' And when they saw him, they were greatly impressed by him and cut their hands and said, 'Exalted is Allah! This is not a man; this is none but a noble angel.'
interpretation: The verse illustrates the overwhelming effect of Prophet Yusuf's extraordinary beauty upon the women of the city. When Zulaikha invited them to a banquet and presented Yusuf before them, their perception was so stunned by his unparalleled grace and luminescence that they lost all awareness of their surroundings. They were so startled that they accidentally cut their hands with the knives provided for the fruit, reflecting a state of awe where their human judgment was suspended, leading them to falsely conclude that a being of such perfection could not possibly be human, but must be a noble celestial entity.

translation: She said, 'That is the one about whom you blamed me. And I certainly sought to seduce him, but he firmly refused; and if he will not do what I order him, he will surely be imprisoned and will be among the debased.'
interpretation: The woman openly confesses her desire and pursuit of Prophet Yusuf in front of the women she invited, demonstrating that her initial secrecy had vanished, while simultaneously acknowledging Yusuf's absolute moral integrity and resistance to her temptation, which she then attempts to weaponize by threatening him with imprisonment to force him into submission.

translation: He said, 'My Lord, prison is more to my liking than that to which they invite me. And if You do not avert from me their plan, I might incline toward them and [thus] be of the ignorant.'
interpretation: Prophet Yusuf (peace be upon him) demonstrates the pinnacle of moral resolve by recognizing that the safety of physical confinement is preferable to the moral corruption of succumbing to illicit desires. His plea for God’s intervention reflects the realization that human willpower alone is fragile, and true protection against temptation requires divine assistance, as he acknowledges that failing to remain steadfast would result in a loss of spiritual wisdom and ethical judgment.

translation: So his Lord responded to him and averted from him their plan. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: When Prophet Yusuf (peace be upon him) sought refuge in Allah from the seduction of the women of Egypt and chose imprisonment over disobedience, Allah responded to his sincere prayer and protected him from their deceptive schemes. This verse highlights that when a believer turns to Allah with absolute trust and prefers His pleasure over worldly temptations, Allah provides him with divine protection, nullifies the plots of his enemies, and demonstrates that He hears every whisper of the heart and knows the reality of every situation.

translation: Then it appeared to them after they had seen the signs that they should surely imprison him for a time.
interpretation: After the Egyptian officials and the wife of Al-Aziz witnessed clear evidence of Prophet Yusuf's innocence and his virtue, their base desires and fear of social scandal drove them to suppress the truth; they chose to imprison him, even though they knew he was righteous, simply to protect their reputations and silence the reminder of their own moral failings.

translation: And there entered the prison with him two young men. One of them said, 'Indeed, I saw myself pressing wine.' And the other said, 'Indeed, I saw myself carrying upon my head bread, from which the birds were eating. Inform us of its interpretation; indeed, we see you to be of those who do good.'
interpretation: The two young men approached Prophet Yusuf with their dreams because they recognized in his character and conduct a profound sense of righteousness, piety, and benevolence, which led them to believe he possessed a God-given gift of insight and spiritual wisdom capable of deciphering the hidden meanings of their visions.

translation: He said, 'There will not come to you any food that is provided to you, except that I will inform you of its interpretation before it comes to you. That is from what my Lord has taught me. Indeed, I have left the religion of a people who do not believe in Allah, and they, in the Hereafter, are disbelievers.'
interpretation: Joseph here asserts his prophetic insight and divine favor, explaining to his fellow prisoners that his ability to interpret dreams is not a product of sorcery or guesswork, but a specific knowledge granted to him by Allah. By distancing himself from the polytheistic practices and disbelief of the people around him, he establishes that his spiritual purity and monotheistic commitment are the prerequisites for the divine wisdom he possesses, thereby preparing the listeners to recognize the truth of his message before fulfilling their specific request.

translation: And I have followed the religion of my fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. It was not for us to associate anything with Allah. That is from the bounty of Allah upon us and upon the people, but most of the people are not grateful.
interpretation: The speaker, Prophet Joseph, emphasizes that his monotheistic belief is not a personal innovation but a continuation of the pure faith established by his noble ancestors, indicating that true guidance is a legacy of divine revelation that rejects polytheism in all its forms. By acknowledging this faith as a manifestation of Allah’s grace, he highlights that the privilege of guidance is a universal gift meant for all humanity, and the failure of most people to accept this guidance is a failure of gratitude for the spiritual light provided by the Creator.

translation: O my two companions of the prison, are separate lords better or Allah, the One, the Prevailing?
interpretation: Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) uses this rhetorical question to guide his fellow prisoners toward the logical necessity of Tawhid (monotheism); he argues that it is intellectually and spiritually inconsistent to place one's trust in numerous, competing, and powerless deities when one can instead submit to the singular, absolute Creator who possesses total authority over all existence.

translation: You do not worship besides Him except names which you have named, you and your fathers, for which Allah has sent down no authority. Legislation is not but for Allah. He has commanded that you worship not except Him. That is the correct religion, but most of the people do not know.
interpretation: The verse clarifies that the objects of worship designated by polytheists are mere empty names without any divine justification or inherent power, emphasizing that the absolute right to legislate, command, and judge belongs solely to Allah, as He is the Creator and Sustainer who deserves singular devotion through a way of life based on His objective truth rather than ancestral tradition.

translation: O my two companions of the prison, as for one of you, he will serve wine to his master; and as for the other, he will be crucified, and the birds will eat from his head. The matter has been decreed about which you both inquire.
interpretation: Prophet Yusuf (peace be upon him) here interprets the dreams of his fellow prisoners with divine certainty, informing them that one will return to his former position of service to the King, providing him wine, while the other faces execution by crucifixion, an act that serves as a divine judgment that has already been finalized and cannot be altered.

translation: And he said to the one whom he knew would be saved, 'Mention me to your master.' But Satan made him forget the mention [of] his lord, and he remained in the prison for several years.
interpretation: This verse highlights how Yusuf (Joseph), in his human state, sought a means of intercession through someone he believed had influence, but Allah willed for him to remain in prison longer to refine his patience and trust solely in Him, demonstrating that any reliance on others before seeking Allah is a distraction that can delay one's relief.

translation: And the king said, 'Indeed, I see seven fat cows being eaten by seven lean ones, and seven green spikes of grain and others dry. O eminent ones, explain to me my vision, if you should interpret visions.'
interpretation: The king's dream acts as a divine mechanism to initiate a series of events that would eventually bring Prophet Yusuf to power and save Egypt from a catastrophic famine. The imagery of the lean cows consuming the fat ones represents a period of extreme scarcity and drought that would devour the resources and abundance of seven years of prosperity, signaling an impending economic crisis that required the wisdom and divine guidance Yusuf possessed.

translation: They said, '[It is but] a mixture of dreams, and we are not learned in the interpretation of dreams.'
interpretation: The courtiers of the King dismissed his vision as a chaotic jumble of incoherent dreams born from human fancy, admitting simultaneously that they lacked the esoteric knowledge or divine insight required to decipher such symbolic communications.

translation: And the one who was saved from the two, and remembered after a long time, said, I will inform you of its interpretation, so send me forth.
interpretation: This verse portrays a moment of divine guidance where the individual who had previously forgotten the Prophet Yusuf in prison suddenly experiences a breakthrough of memory, prompted by the distress of the King's dream. This recollection signifies that the timing of enlightenment and truth is entirely in God's hands; once the appointed time arrived, the individual was compelled by the necessity of the interpretation to seek out Yusuf, thereby setting in motion the chain of events that would lead to Yusuf's vindication and his rise to a position of authority, proving that worldly delays are often part of a higher, unfolding plan.

translation: O Yusuf, O man of truth, explain to us about seven fat cows which seven lean ones eat, and about seven green spikes and others which are dry, so that I may return to the people, that they may know.
interpretation: The king's messenger acknowledges Yusuf's integrity and profound knowledge, seeking his divinely-inspired insight to interpret a cryptic dream that perplexed the land's scholars. The request serves as a plea for guidance on a matter of state security and survival, recognizing that Yusuf possesses a unique capacity to decode signs that foretell the future of the kingdom's prosperity and impending scarcity.

translation: He said, 'You will plant for seven consecutive years; so what you harvest, leave it in its ears, except for a little from which you will eat.'
interpretation: Yusuf (Joseph) instructs the people of Egypt to practice agricultural diligence and systematic storage during the coming years of abundance, advising them to preserve the harvested grain within its protective husks to prevent spoilage and ensure a sustainable supply for the impending years of famine, demonstrating his divine foresight and administrative wisdom in managing state resources.

translation: Then there will come after that seven difficult years which will consume what you had stored for them, except a little of that which you have preserved.
interpretation: This verse refers to the interpretation of the King's dream by Prophet Yusuf, warning that after a period of prosperity, a severe and prolonged drought will afflict the land, consuming the surplus of previous years, and advising the people to save a portion of their harvest through careful storage and rationing to survive the impending famine.

translation: Then there will come after that a year in which the people will be given rain and in which they will press [olives and grapes].
interpretation: This verse refers to the relief that follows hardship, indicating a period of abundance and prosperity where the earth will yield its fruits in such large quantities that people will be able to press them for oil, juice, and other products, signifying a complete transition from the previous years of famine and scarcity to a time of relief and divine sustenance.

translation: And the king said, 'Bring him to me.' But when the messenger came to him, he said, 'Return to your master and ask him what is the case of the women who cut their hands. Indeed, my Lord is All-Knowing of their plan.'
interpretation: Joseph (peace be upon him) declined to leave prison immediately upon the king's summons, not out of arrogance or defiance, but because he prioritized his dignity and the establishment of his innocence regarding the false accusations brought against him. By asking the king to investigate the incident involving the women and Potiphar’s wife, he ensured that his release would be an acknowledgement of his integrity and purity, rather than merely an act of royal favor, thereby clearing his reputation before assuming any public office.

translation: He said, 'What was the matter with you when you sought to seduce Joseph?' They said, 'Exalted is Allah! We know of no evil about him.' The wife of al-Azeez said, 'Now the truth has become clear. It was I who sought to seduce him, and he is indeed of the truthful.'
interpretation: This verse marks a pivotal moment of divine intervention where the truth, long suppressed by deception and social status, finally emerges through the conscience of the perpetrator herself. By testifying to Joseph's impeccable character and acknowledging her own guilt, the wife of al-Azeez serves as an instrument of justice, proving that true integrity eventually shatters the facade of falsehood, vindicating the righteous despite the pressures of those in power.

translation: That is so he may know that I did not betray him in his absence, and that Allah does not guide the plan of the betrayers.
interpretation: This verse reflects the Prophet Yusuf's emphasis on integrity and transparency, highlighting that his innocence was maintained even when he was not being watched, while affirming the divine law that those who act with deceit and treachery will find their schemes ultimately thwarted by Allah's justice.

translation: And I do not acquit myself. Indeed, the soul is a persistent enjoiner of evil, except those upon whom my Lord has mercy. Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: The verse conveys a profound spiritual humility, where the speaker acknowledges that the human soul, by its innate nature and worldly desires, naturally inclines toward disobedience and harmful impulses. It emphasizes that salvation from this internal corruption is not achieved through one's own perfection or strength of character, but solely through the divine grace and mercy of Allah, which acts as the only shield against the soul's tendency to lead the individual toward transgression.

translation: And the king said, 'Bring him to me; I will appoint him specifically for myself.' And when he spoke to him, he said, 'Indeed, you are today established [in rank] among us and trusted.'
interpretation: The king, upon witnessing Joseph's profound wisdom and insight during the interpretation of his dream, recognized an extraordinary nobility and capability in him that transcended the typical traits of his court advisors, leading the king to realize that Joseph was uniquely qualified to handle the governance of Egypt with absolute integrity and competence.

translation: [Joseph] said, 'Appoint me over the storehouses of the land. Indeed, I am a knowing guardian.'
interpretation: Prophet Joseph (Yusuf), peace be upon him, requested the position of overseer of the state’s resources not out of ambition for power or worldly status, but out of a profound sense of duty and the desire to serve the public good. Recognizing the impending years of famine, he knew that his unique combination of integrity, trustworthiness, and administrative expertise was essential to managing the food supply effectively, preventing mass starvation, and implementing a fair system of distribution that would protect the people from the coming catastrophe.

translation: And thus We established Joseph in the land to settle therein wherever he willed. We touch with Our mercy whom We will, and We do not allow to be lost the reward of those who do good.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine affirmation that steadfastness in righteousness and patience through hardship, as demonstrated by Prophet Joseph, inevitably leads to a position of authority and influence. It illustrates that God bestows His favor and administrative capability upon whom He wills as a manifestation of His mercy, and it functions as a universal promise that those who uphold excellence in their conduct, ethics, and devotion will never see their efforts go unrewarded by the Creator.

translation: And the reward of the Hereafter is better for those who believed and were fearing Allah.
interpretation: The verse highlights that the transient enjoyments of this worldly life, no matter how enticing they may seem, pale in comparison to the eternal and superior recompense awaiting the believers in the afterlife, a reward reserved specifically for those who maintained sincere faith and upheld consciousness of God through righteous deeds and avoidance of sin.

translation: And the brothers of Joseph came and entered upon him; and he recognized them, while they were unaware of him.
interpretation: This verse highlights the dramatic irony of the reunion between Joseph and his brothers in Egypt; Joseph, having attained high status and being matured by years, was easily identified by his character and authority in the eyes of his brothers who did not expect to find their brother whom they had cast into the pit years ago holding such a position of power and dignity, thus causing them to fail in recognizing him despite his immediate recognition of their familiar faces.

translation: And when he had provided them with their provisions, he said, 'Bring me a brother of yours from your father. Do you not see that I give full measure and that I am the best of hosts?'
interpretation: When Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) fulfilled the needs of his brothers by providing them with the grain they sought, he exerted a subtle pressure on them by demanding they bring their younger brother, Benjamin, to him. His assertion that he provides full measure and is the best of hosts serves both as a reminder of his generosity—which he displayed despite their past transgressions—and as a strategic move to ensure their return, thereby facilitating the eventual reunion with his father and younger brother.

translation: But if you do not bring him to me, then there shall be no measure for you from me, nor shall you approach me.
interpretation: This verse reflects the stern ultimatum issued by Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) to his brothers, highlighting the principle of accountability and justice; he conditions the continued provision of sustenance upon their integrity in fulfilling their promise to bring back their younger brother, thereby demonstrating that favors and communal benefits are tied to transparency, honesty, and the fulfillment of trust.

translation: They said, 'We will attempt to persuade his father concerning him, and indeed we will do it.'
interpretation: The brothers of Yusuf intended to deceive their father, Ya'qub, by exerting persistent pressure or using persuasive arguments to convince him to allow them to take Yusuf along with them, expressing their firm resolve to succeed in this manipulative scheme.

translation: And he said to his young men, 'Put their merchandise back into their saddlebags so that they might recognize it when they return to their people, that perhaps they might come back.'
interpretation: Yusuf (peace be upon him) commanded his servants to return the goods the brothers had brought for trade back into their packs secretly, intending to ensure they would return to him, either out of gratitude for his generosity or because they would realize their own coins had been returned, which might prompt them to come back to resolve the confusion and fulfill their need for grain again.

translation: So when they returned to their father, they said, 'O our father, the measure is withheld from us, so send with us our brother [that] we may obtain measure, and indeed, we will be his guardians.'
interpretation: The brothers of Yusuf, having experienced the refusal of the Egyptian governor to provide them with further grain supplies due to the absence of their youngest brother, returned to Ya'qub to report this obstacle. Their plea was framed not merely as a request for food, but as a strategic appeal to their father's concern for their sustenance, coupled with a solemn oath to protect Benjamin, thereby attempting to reassure their father of his safety while simultaneously attempting to convince him to allow Benjamin to accompany them back to Egypt.

translation: He said, 'Should I entrust you with him except as I entrusted you with his brother before? But Allah is the best guardian, and He is the Most Merciful of the merciful.'
interpretation: Prophet Yaqub expresses a profound sense of human caution based on past experience while simultaneously centering his ultimate trust in the divine protection of Allah. By recalling the previous loss of Yusuf, he acknowledges that his children proved untrustworthy in the past, yet he recognizes that worldly precautions are secondary to the decree and care of the Almighty, who alone possesses the power to preserve what He wills, and whose mercy surpasses all human relationships and intentions.

translation: And when they opened their baggage, they found their goods had been returned to them. They said, 'O our father, what [more] could we desire? This is our merchandise returned to us; and we will obtain provisions for our family, and guard our brother, and obtain an extra camel's load; that is an easy measure [to obtain].'
interpretation: The brothers expressed profound astonishment and gratitude upon finding their currency returned, interpreting it as an act of divine favor that removes any obstacle for their return journey. By highlighting their success to their father, they emphasize that their future objectives—securing provisions for their household, ensuring the safety of their younger brother, and obtaining additional grain—are now easily attainable through this unexpected windfall, thereby persuading their father of the feasibility and necessity of returning to Egypt.

translation: He said, 'Never will I send him with you until you give me a promise by Allah that you will bring him back to me, unless you should be surrounded by enemies.' And when they had given their promise, he said, 'Allah, over what we say, is Witness.'
interpretation: Jacob (Ya'qub), peace be upon him, seeks a binding oath from his sons in the name of Allah to ensure the safety and return of Benjamin, recognizing that human efforts have limits when faced with overwhelming external circumstances, and by invoking Allah as the ultimate guardian and witness, he entrusts the outcome of this covenant to the Divine, acknowledging that Allah is the final guarantor of all commitments and the only one whose protection is absolute.

translation: And he said, 'O my sons, do not enter from one gate but enter from different gates; and I cannot avail you against Allah at all. The decision is only for Allah; upon Him I have relied, and upon Him let those who rely [indeed] rely.'
interpretation: Prophet Ya'qub (Jacob) advised his sons to take sensible precautionary measures to avoid attracting the evil eye or causing public suspicion by entering the city together, yet he simultaneously reminded them that these human efforts do not override Allah's decree. His guidance teaches the perfect balance between 'tawakkul' (placing one's ultimate trust in Allah) and 'asbab' (adopting worldly means), demonstrating that a true believer utilizes wisdom and foresight while remaining fully aware that the ultimate outcome rests solely in the hands of the Almighty.

translation: And when they entered from where their father had ordered them, it did not avail them against Allah at all, except for a need in the soul of Jacob which he satisfied. And indeed, he was a possessor of knowledge because of what We had taught him, but most of the people do not know.
interpretation: Jacob's advice for his sons to enter the city through different gates was not intended to override the divine decree of Allah, as no human strategy can avert what God has predestined. Rather, it was a manifestation of Jacob's fatherly care and his innate concern for their safety, rooted in his prophetic foresight and reliance on Allah, which prompted him to take precautionary measures despite knowing that ultimately everything is subject to the will and sovereignty of the Almighty.

translation: And when they entered upon Joseph, he took his brother to himself and said, 'Indeed, I am your brother, so do not despair over what they used to do.'
interpretation: When Joseph was reunited with his younger brother Benjamin, he revealed his true identity to him in private to comfort and reassure him. By saying 'do not despair over what they used to do,' Joseph was consoling his brother, urging him not to be distressed or grief-stricken by the past mistreatment they had suffered at the hands of their other brothers, assuring him that God had turned their adversity into a noble outcome.

translation: And when he had provided them with their provisions, he placed the drinking cup in his brother's bag. Then a caller called out, 'O you [in the] caravan, indeed you are thieves.'
interpretation: Joseph orchestrated this specific action as a divinely inspired stratagem to retain his brother Benjamin with him in Egypt, utilizing the legal customs of the time which dictated that a thief would become the property of the victim, thereby ensuring Benjamin's presence without resorting to overt coercion or revealing his identity prematurely.

translation: They said, while turning toward them, 'What is it that you are missing?'
interpretation: This verse depicts a scene of confrontation where the brothers of Joseph, after being questioned about the missing cup, adopt an air of feigned innocence or surprise, using this rhetorical question to deflect suspicion from themselves and challenge the integrity of those accusing them of theft.

translation: They said, 'We are missing the measuring cup of the king. And for whoever brings it is a camel's load, and I am responsible for it.'
interpretation: This verse portrays the strategic deception employed by the brothers of Yusuf to frame Benjamin, utilizing the official state authority and a promised reward to create a pretext for searching their luggage, thereby manipulating the legal system to enforce their malicious intent of keeping their brother detained.

translation: They said, 'By Allah, you have certainly come to know that we did not come to cause corruption in the land, and we have not been thieves.'
interpretation: The brothers of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) are responding to the accusation of theft by appealing to the brothers' established reputation and character, asserting that their past behavior and known conduct provided clear evidence that they were neither people of mischief nor those who would stoop to thievery, thereby invoking Allah as a witness to the truthfulness of their innocence.

translation: They said, 'What then shall be the recompense of this (theft) if you are lying?'
interpretation: The brothers of Joseph, feeling emboldened and secure in their own perceived integrity, challenged those who accused them of theft by asking what the decreed punishment for the thief should be according to their law, firmly believing that they were innocent and that their accusers were making a false claim.

translation: They said, 'His recompense is that he in whose bag it is found, he himself is the recompense. Thus do we recompense the wrongdoers.'
interpretation: This verse describes the judgment pronounced by Joseph’s brothers according to the law of the Prophet Jacob, which held that a thief should become the property of the one he robbed. By making this declaration, they unknowingly set a condition for themselves that would later lead to the realization of Joseph's divine plan, illustrating that when people inflict injustice upon others, they often inadvertently create the very mechanisms that lead to their own accountability and the administration of divine justice.

translation: So he began with their sacks before the sack of his brother; then he extracted it from the sack of his brother. Thus did We plan for Joseph. He could not have taken his brother within the religion of the king except that Allah willed. We raise in degrees whom We will, and over every possessor of knowledge is one [more] knowing.
interpretation: The verse illustrates that Allah facilitates the fulfillment of His decrees through subtle strategic wisdom, as Yusuf (Joseph) utilized a calculated process of inspection to legally detain his brother under the laws of Egypt without arousing immediate suspicion or violating the brothers' trust. It serves as a profound reminder that human intellect and planning, while significant, are always subordinate to the Divine Will, and that no matter how much knowledge or status a person attains, there is always a higher level of wisdom and authority belonging to Allah.

translation: They said, 'If he has stolen, a brother of his has stolen before.' But Yusuf kept it secret within himself and did not reveal it to them. He said, 'You are worse in position, and Allah is most knowing of what you describe.'
interpretation: When Yusuf's brothers accused Binyamin of theft to shift blame, Yusuf recalled their past betrayal against him, choosing to internalize his pain and disappointment rather than confronting them with their hypocrisy immediately. By stating they were in a worse position, he was subtly rebuking their moral bankruptcy—specifically their past cruelty toward him—while acknowledging that Allah alone truly understands the hidden motives behind their false accusations and deceitful character.

translation: They said, 'O Aziz, indeed he has a father, an aged man, so take one of us in his place. Indeed, we see you to be of those who do good.'
interpretation: The brothers of Joseph recognized the authority and compassion of the Aziz, and in their desperation to fulfill the promise they made to their father regarding Benjamin, they appealed to the Aziz's sense of justice and kindness. By offering themselves as substitutes, they demonstrated a profound shift in their character compared to their earlier jealousy of Joseph; they sought to shield their aged father from the devastating grief of losing another son, demonstrating a protective responsibility and an acknowledgment of the mercy they hoped to receive from the ruler.

translation: He said, 'I seek refuge in Allah from taking anyone except him with whom we found our property. Indeed, we would then be among the wrongdoers.'
interpretation: Joseph, peace be upon him, invokes Allah's protection to uphold the principles of justice and righteousness, asserting that he cannot punish an innocent person for the theft committed by another, as doing so would be a transgression against truth and fairness.

translation: So when they had despaired of him, they withdrew to confer privately. Their eldest said, 'Do you not know that your father has taken from you a solemn pledge by Allah and that before this you failed in your duty regarding Joseph? So I will never leave this land until my father permits me or Allah decides for me, and He is the best of judges.'
interpretation: The verse highlights the profound sense of shame and fear experienced by Joseph's brothers when they realized they could not secure the release of their younger brother Benjamin. Recognizing their previous betrayal of Joseph and the gravity of the covenant they made with their father, Jacob, the eldest brother demonstrates a sense of moral responsibility and resolve. By refusing to return to Canaan without Benjamin, he undergoes a transformation from a past of deceit to a stance of accountability, choosing to remain in Egypt as a self-imposed exile, placing his trust entirely in the decree of Allah to resolve the family crisis.

translation: Return to your father and say, 'Our father, indeed your son has stolen, and we testify only to what we know, and we were not witnesses of the unseen.'
interpretation: The brothers of Yusuf instructed Binyamin's brothers to use these words as a justification for their father Ya'qub. By stating that they only testify to what they witnessed, they aimed to distance themselves from any suspicion of conspiracy, appealing to Ya'qub's sense of reason by presenting the event as an observed fact while simultaneously highlighting their ignorance of the broader, hidden truth behind the situation—an irony, as they were the architects of the deception, yet they framed their report as an honest account based on the physical evidence they had manufactured.

translation: And ask the city in which we were and the caravan in which we came, and indeed, we are truthful.
interpretation: The brothers of Joseph are telling their father, Jacob, to verify their account by inquiring among the people of the city of Egypt and the members of the caravan with whom they traveled, as these objective witnesses can confirm that Joseph was indeed left behind and that their claims are grounded in fact rather than fabrication.

translation: He said, 'Rather, your souls have made something look appealing to you. So patience is most fitting. Perhaps Allah will bring them all to me. Indeed, it is He who is the Knowing, the Wise.'
interpretation: The Prophet Ya'qub (Jacob) displays a profound state of spiritual realization by recognizing that the deceptive whispers of his sons' souls, driven by envy and desire, led them to concoct a false narrative. Despite the deep agony of losing his sons, he chooses 'beautiful patience'—a state of endurance devoid of complaint or despair—grounded in his unwavering certainty that Allah is all-knowing regarding the hidden truth of their actions and infinitely wise in His decree, trusting that the ultimate return of his sons rests solely in the hands of the Almighty.

translation: And he turned away from them and said, 'Oh, my sorrow for Joseph,' and his eyes became white from the grief that he suppressed.
interpretation: The verse illustrates the profound depth of Prophet Ya'qub's (Jacob's) grief over the loss of his son Joseph, showing that despite his noble patience and unwavering faith in God, he was still overcome by natural human sorrow, leading to his physical blindness caused by the intensity of his suppressed internal anguish.

translation: They said, 'By Allah, you will not cease remembering Yusuf until you become weak from illness or you become among the dead.'
interpretation: The sons of Ya'qub expressed their deep frustration and concern regarding their father's persistent and inconsolable grief, urging him to cease his constant lamentation for Yusuf, warning him that such relentless sorrow would inevitably consume his physical health and lead him to an untimely death.

translation: He said, 'I only complain of my suffering and my grief to Allah, and I know from Allah that which you do not know.'
interpretation: Prophet Ya'qub (Jacob) emphasizes that the ultimate refuge for a believer in times of profound emotional distress is God alone, as He is the only One capable of alleviating sorrow; furthermore, his statement reveals his unwavering trust in God's hidden wisdom and his reliance on a divine knowledge that transcends human perspective, which gives him the patience and endurance his sons lack.

translation: O my sons, go and search for Yusuf and his brother, and do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, no one despairs of the mercy of Allah except the disbelieving people.
interpretation: The verse illustrates the deep faith of Prophet Ya'qub (Jacob), who, despite the long separation from his sons, maintains an unwavering trust in Allah's benevolence. He instructs his children to remain persistent in their search, emphasizing that despair is a spiritual sickness incompatible with belief, as a true believer recognizes that Allah's mercy is infinite and capable of reversing any hardship or resolving any loss.

translation: So when they entered upon him, they said, 'O 'Azeez, adversity has touched us and our family, and we have brought goods poor in quality, but fulfill for us the measure and be charitable to us. Indeed, Allah rewards the charitable.'
interpretation: The brothers of Yusuf, not recognizing him, approached him in a state of desperation and humility due to the severe famine. By acknowledging their poverty and offering meager goods, they appealed to the nobility and generosity of the Egyptian official. Their plea reflects the human tendency to seek relief from those in positions of power during times of hardship, while their invocation of divine reward for charity highlights their recognition that ultimate relief and recompense rest with Allah alone.

translation: He said, 'Do you know what you did with Yusuf and his brother when you were ignorant?'
interpretation: Yusuf is addressing his brothers by reminding them of their past actions—specifically the betrayal of throwing him into the well and the deception regarding his brother Benjamin—not to mock them, but to confront them with their past state of spiritual and moral ignorance when they committed such grave sins, thereby paving the way for their acknowledgment of guilt and ultimate repentance.

translation: They said, 'Are you indeed Joseph?' He said, 'I am Joseph, and this is my brother. Allah has certainly favored us. Indeed, he who fears Allah and is patient, then indeed, Allah does not allow to be lost the reward of those who do good.'
interpretation: Joseph acknowledges his identity to his brothers, attributing his high status and reunion with his family not to his own efforts, but to Allah’s grace and mercy, which are granted as a reward for those who maintain God-consciousness through piety and steadfast patience during times of hardship.

translation: They said, 'By Allah, certainly has Allah preferred you over us, and indeed, we have been sinners.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the moment when Joseph's brothers finally acknowledged the divine favor bestowed upon him despite their previous jealousy and plots; their admission is a profound recognition that Joseph's rise to status and wisdom was a direct manifestation of God's will, coupled with a humble confession of their own moral failure and injustice toward him.

translation: He said, 'No reproach on you today, may Allah forgive you; and He is the Most Merciful of the merciful.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the supreme moral excellence of Prophet Yusuf as he addresses his brothers after they had wronged him; by choosing total forgiveness and refusing to hold them accountable for their past betrayal, he demonstrates the prophetic character of mercy, reflecting the divine attribute of compassion and emphasizing that true greatness lies in pardoning those who have caused us harm when we are in a position of power over them.

translation: Take this shirt of mine and cast it over the face of my father; he will become seeing, and bring me your family, all together.
interpretation: Prophet Yusuf (Joseph), moved by divine inspiration and his deep filial piety, instructs his brothers to take his garment as a miraculous means to restore his father Yaqub's (Jacob's) eyesight, which had been lost due to intense grief and constant weeping over Yusuf's disappearance. This act signifies that the garment, having been worn by a Prophet of God, serves as a medium for a divine sign, reflecting the mercy of Allah in alleviating the sorrow of a righteous servant and paving the way for the reunion of the family.

translation: And when the caravan departed, their father said, 'Indeed, I find the scent of Joseph, if you do not think me senile.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the power of Ya'qub's (Jacob's) profound spiritual intuition and his deep-seated yearning for his son, Joseph. Despite the immense passage of time and the hopelessness expressed by those around him, Ya'qub’s faith in Allah remained unshaken. His declaration of smelling Joseph’s scent signifies a miraculous perception granted by Allah, serving as a comfort to his heart and a sign that his patience and reliance on the Divine were about to be rewarded with the relief he had long sought.

translation: They said: 'By Allah, you are indeed in your old error.'
interpretation: The family of Prophet Yusuf, blinded by their long-standing preoccupation with their grief and their lingering resentment or disbelief regarding Ya'qub's unwavering hope for his son's return, mockingly accused him of being stuck in the same deluded state of mind he had maintained for years, failing to recognize that his certainty was born of divine insight and prophetic trust in Allah's promise.

translation: Then when the bearer of the good news arrived, he cast it [the shirt] over his face, and he became seeing. He said, 'Did I not tell you that I know from Allah that which you do not know?'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the triumph of Prophet Ya'qub's (Jacob) unwavering faith and divine intuition over the logical doubts of his children. By casting the shirt of his son Yusuf (Joseph) over his face, which served as a physical medium for a divine miracle, his sight was restored not merely by the fabric itself, but by the will of Allah who honors the patience and trust of His prophets. The subsequent statement of Ya'qub serves as a profound affirmation that those who maintain spiritual closeness to God possess a unique, divinely-granted insight into the unseen reality that transcends human reason and the limitations of physical perception.

translation: They said, 'O our father, ask forgiveness for our sins for us; indeed, we have been sinful.'
interpretation: Recognizing the gravity of their transgression against their brother and the resulting distress caused to their father, the sons of Jacob exhibit genuine contrition by acknowledging their fault directly to him and seeking his intercession, as they understand that his proximity to Allah and his prophetic status make his prayers for their repentance particularly significant in seeking divine pardon.

translation: He said, 'I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the Prophet Ya'qub's response to his sons after they acknowledged their wrongdoing regarding their brother Yusuf; it signifies a compassionate promise of intercession and reliance upon Allah's infinite mercy, illustrating the duty of a believer to guide others toward repentance while maintaining hope in the divine attribute of forgiveness.

translation: And when they entered upon Yusuf, he sheltered his parents and said, 'Enter Egypt, if Allah wills, in security.'
interpretation: Yusuf's gesture of embracing and sheltering his parents signifies his profound filial piety and honor despite his high status as a ruler, while his assurance of safety reflects his reliance on Allah's will, ensuring his family would find not only physical security from the famine but also peace of mind in the company of their son.

translation: And he raised his parents upon the throne, and they fell down before him in prostration. And he said, 'O my father, this is the explanation of my vision of before. My Lord has made it reality. And He was certainly good to me when He took me out of prison and brought you from the bedouin life after Satan had induced [estrangement] between me and my brothers. Indeed, my Lord is Subtle in what He wills. Indeed, it is He who is the Knowing, the Wise.'
interpretation: This verse signifies the ultimate fulfillment of divine destiny, where Yusuf (Joseph) acknowledges that the trials he endured—the betrayal of his brothers, his imprisonment, and his eventual rise to authority—were all orchestrated by God’s infinite wisdom to bring about a beautiful reunion and the elevation of his family. By attributing the resolution of their long-standing conflict to God’s grace rather than human agency, Yusuf highlights the concept of 'Latif' (the Subtle), demonstrating that God achieves His grand designs through hidden, gentle, and often difficult paths, turning the schemes of the envious into a means of honor for the righteous.

translation: My Lord, You have given me [something] of sovereignty and taught me of the interpretation of dreams. Creator of the heavens and earth, You are my protector in this world and in the Hereafter. Cause me to die a Muslim and join me with the righteous.
interpretation: This prayer represents the pinnacle of human humility and spiritual maturity, where Prophet Yusuf, having reached the height of worldly success and authority, acknowledges that all power and knowledge are mere gifts from Allah; he recognizes that since true success is not found in earthly status but in ultimate submission, he petitions his Creator to maintain his spiritual integrity until the moment of death, preferring the company of the righteous in the eternal realm over any temporary worldly gain.

translation: That is from the news of the unseen which We reveal to you, [O Muhammad], and you were not with them when they put together their plan while they were conspiring.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine affirmation of the Prophet Muhammad's truthfulness, asserting that his detailed knowledge of past historical events—specifically the betrayal of Prophet Yusuf by his brothers—was not obtained through human observation or research, but through direct revelation from Allah, thereby confirming that the Quran is a miraculous record of events that occurred far beyond his physical presence or timeframe.

translation: And most of the people, although you strive [for it], are not believers.
interpretation: This verse consoles the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, by clarifying that his deep desire and persistent efforts to guide all of humanity to the truth will not result in universal faith, because the capacity for belief depends on the sincerity of the individual's own heart and their willingness to accept divine guidance, rather than the Prophet's own zeal or external persuasion.

translation: And you do not ask them for it any payment. It is not except a reminder for the worlds.
interpretation: This verse clarifies that the mission of the Prophet Muhammad is purely for the guidance and benefit of humanity, entirely free from any worldly ambition, personal gain, or material compensation, emphasizing that the message of the Qur'an is a universal warning and a divine reminder intended for all people across all times.

translation: And how many a sign within the heavens and the earth do they pass by, while they, therefrom, are turning away.
interpretation: The verse highlights the persistent negligence of human beings toward the manifest signs of God's existence and power scattered across the universe, suggesting that these physical phenomena act as clear proofs of a Creator that are constantly visible to humanity, yet most people choose to remain heedless or willfully ignorant of the divine truth embedded in the natural world.

translation: And most of them do not believe in Allah except while they associate others with Him.
interpretation: This verse highlights a deep-seated spiritual inconsistency wherein individuals may acknowledge the existence and Lordship of Allah, yet simultaneously compromise their monotheistic devotion by directing acts of worship, reliance, or submission toward other entities, thereby rendering their faith incomplete and tainted by polytheism.

translation: Do they then feel secure against the coming of an overwhelming cover of the punishment of Allah, or the coming of the Hour suddenly while they do not perceive it?
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to those who persist in disbelief and arrogance, questioning whether they truly believe themselves safe from a sudden and inescapable divine retribution or the unexpected onset of the Day of Judgment, which will catch them completely unaware and unprepared, leaving them no chance for repentance or amends.

translation: Say, 'This is my way; I invite to Allah with insight, I and those who follow me. And exalted is Allah; and I am not of those who associate others with Him.'
interpretation: The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, is instructed to declare that his path, his mission, and his entire life are dedicated solely to calling people toward the Oneness of Allah. This call is not based on blind emotion or ignorance, but on 'basirah'—a clear, manifest, and firm certainty grounded in revelation and divine evidence. The verse establishes that this clear method of invitation is the defining mark of the Prophet and all those who truly follow his guidance. By dissociating himself from the polytheists, the Prophet emphasizes that this path of pure monotheism is fundamentally incompatible with any form of shirk (idolatry), and he declares Allah’s transcendence above the false attributes ascribed to Him by those who lack this clarity.

translation: And We did not send before you, [O Muhammad], except men to whom We revealed from among the people of cities. Have they not traveled through the earth and observed how was the end of those before them? And the home of the Hereafter is best for those who fear Allah, so will you not then use your reason?
interpretation: This verse addresses the skepticism of the polytheists regarding the humanity of the Prophets, clarifying that Allah purposefully chose human beings from established communities to receive His revelation so they could effectively model guidance for their people. It urges the disbelievers to look at the ruins of past civilizations that rejected divine truth, emphasizing that worldly power is fleeting and that true success is reserved for the God-fearing in the eternal life of the Hereafter, inviting them to reflect logically on these historical lessons.

translation: Until, when the messengers despaired and thought that they were denied, Our victory came to them, and whoever We willed was saved. And Our punishment cannot be averted from the people who are criminals.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound divine wisdom behind the delay of victory for the messengers, highlighting that the point of absolute desperation is often the prelude to God's intervention, testing the believers' steadfastness to its limit until they reach a state of complete reliance on God alone, at which point the promise of aid is fulfilled to demonstrate that ultimate power belongs to Him.

translation: There was certainly in their stories a lesson for those of understanding. Never was the Qur'an a narration invented, but a confirmation of what was before it and a detailed explanation of all things and guidance and mercy for a people who believe.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that the historical accounts of past nations mentioned in the Quran are not merely tales for entertainment, but profound intellectual and spiritual lessons intended for those who possess insight and wisdom. It asserts that the Quran is a divine revelation that validates previous scriptures, provides comprehensive guidance on religious and worldly matters, and acts as a source of mercy and enlightenment for those who have sincere faith, enabling them to recognize the truth and adhere to the path of righteousness.

translation: Alif-Lam-Mim-Ra. These are the verses of the Book; and what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth, but most of the people do not believe.
interpretation: This verse affirms the divine origin and absolute veracity of the Qur'an, highlighting the contrast between the objective reality of the revelation and the subjective rejection by the majority of humanity, who are blinded by their own prejudices and refusal to acknowledge the clear evidence presented to them.

translation: It is Allah who erected the heavens without pillars that you [can] see; then He established Himself above the Throne and subjected the sun and the moon, each running [its course] for a specified term. He arranges [each] matter; He details the signs that you may, of the meeting with your Lord, be certain.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and sovereignty of Allah over the physical universe, demonstrating that the stability of the celestial bodies is maintained by His unseen command rather than visible physical support. By highlighting that all natural phenomena follow a divinely ordained, temporary course, the verse invites the human intellect to reflect on the complexity and order of creation as a rational proof for the existence of an intelligent Designer. Ultimately, this contemplation serves as a gateway to spiritual certainty, teaching the believer that the same Authority who regulates the movements of the sun and moon is the One who will inevitably bring about the Day of Resurrection, requiring of the human being a life lived in conscious awareness of their ultimate accountability to Him.

translation: And within the land are neighboring plots and gardens of grapevines and crops and palm trees, [growing] several from a root or otherwise, watered by one water; but We make some of them exceed others in [quality of] fruit. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reason.
interpretation: The verse serves as a profound metaphor for human diversity and divine wisdom, illustrating that while all human beings share a common origin and are nurtured by the same environmental and spiritual sustenance, their outcomes, characters, and virtues differ vastly due to the varying degrees of internal disposition and the selective grace bestowed by Allah, signifying that true understanding lies in recognizing this diversity as evidence of a Creator who governs the universe with precise and intentional variation.

translation: And if you are astonished, then astonishing is their saying: 'When we have become dust, will we indeed be in a new creation?' Those are the ones who have disbelieved in their Lord, and those will have shackles upon their necks, and those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: The verse highlights the state of those who deny the resurrection by expressing shock at the Prophet Muhammad's message, as they find the idea of returning to life after decomposing into dust intellectually impossible; God responds by noting that this rejection of the afterlife is fundamentally a rejection of His power and authority, which leads to their spiritual enslavement in this life—symbolized by the shackles—and their eventual permanent dwelling in the state of suffering that results from their willful denial of the truth.

translation: And they hasten you to bring about the evil before the good, while there have already passed before them exemplary punishments. And indeed, your Lord is full of forgiveness for the people despite their wrongdoing, and indeed, your Lord is severe in penalty.
interpretation: The verse highlights the stubborn arrogance of the disbelievers who mockingly challenge the Prophet to bring forth divine punishment instead of seeking the blessings of guidance. Allah reminds them that history is filled with the ruins of past nations who dared to defy their messengers, yet Allah, in His immense mercy, delays retribution to allow time for repentance despite their ongoing transgressions, while simultaneously maintaining the certainty of His eventual severe justice for those who persist in their defiance.

translation: And those who disbelieve say, 'Why has a sign not been sent down to him from his Lord?' You are only a warner, and for every people there is a guide.
interpretation: The verse clarifies that the Prophet Muhammad's primary mission was to warn mankind of the consequences of disbelief, rather than to perform miraculous signs solely at the demand of the disbelievers, who often requested them out of stubbornness rather than a genuine desire for truth; furthermore, it affirms that God provides a source of guidance for every nation throughout history, ensuring that no people were left without the message of truth and a means to reach righteousness.

translation: Allah knows what every female bears and what the wombs lose or exceed, and everything with Him is by a measure.
interpretation: Allah alone possesses the absolute and comprehensive knowledge of every biological detail concerning the formation of life within the womb, including the duration of pregnancy, the developmental stages, and the physical characteristics of the fetus, all of which are governed by a precise, divine decree that leaves nothing to chance or uncertainty.

translation: He is the Knower of the unseen and the seen, the Most Great, the Exalted.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah possesses absolute knowledge of everything that is hidden from human perception and everything that is manifest and observable, while also emphasizing His supreme majesty and His transcendence above all His creation, as He is the One who occupies the highest station of power and honor.

translation: It is the same among you whether one conceals his speech or speaks it openly, and whether he is hidden by night or goes forth by day.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's absolute and all-encompassing knowledge, asserting that no human action, thought, or movement—whether hidden in the deepest darkness of night or performed in the full clarity of daylight—is concealed from Him, as He perceives all things with equal clarity regardless of the circumstances of their occurrence.

translation: For him are angels in succession, before and behind him, protecting him by the command of Allah. Indeed, Allah will not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves. And when Allah intends for a people ill, there is no repelling it. And there is not for them besides Him any patron.
interpretation: This verse establishes the divine decree concerning human responsibility and providence. It explains that Allah assigns angels to accompany and guard human beings as a manifestation of His mercy, while simultaneously setting forth a universal law of causality: a nation's prosperity or downfall is inextricably linked to their own choices and moral state. When a community chooses to abandon righteousness and descend into corruption, they forfeit the protection and favor of Allah, leaving them vulnerable to divine justice; once that decree of adversity is set, no power in existence can avert it, as human beings possess no other protector or guardian capable of overriding His will.

translation: It is He who shows you the lightning, causing fear and aspiration, and generates the heavy clouds.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom behind natural phenomena, where the lightning serves as a reminder of Allah's power that inspires both awe through the fear of potential destruction and hope through the anticipation of the life-giving rain that the heavy, water-laden clouds carry to the parched earth.

translation: And the thunder exalts [Allah] with praise, and the angels [as well] from fear of Him, and He sends the thunderbolts and strikes therewith whom He wills while they dispute about Allah; and He is severe in assault.
interpretation: The verse illustrates the absolute majesty and power of the Creator, highlighting that even the most formidable natural phenomena—the thunder and the lightning—exist in a state of constant, conscious submission and glorification of God. This serves as a rebuke to the skeptics who waste their time in futile arguments regarding the existence and nature of the Divine; while they are busy debating, they remain oblivious to the fact that they are constantly surrounded by overwhelming signs of a Power that can manifest its wrath at any moment, reminding humanity that His reach and capability to punish are far beyond human comprehension or resistance.
