translation: To Him alone is the true call, and those whom they call upon besides Him do not respond to them with anything, except like one who stretches his hands toward water so that it may reach his mouth, but it will not reach it; and the call of the disbelievers is only in error.
interpretation: This verse presents a profound metaphor for the futility of polytheism, comparing those who pray to false deities to a thirsty person trying to catch water by merely reaching out toward it with open palms; just as water cannot be grasped by open hands and will never reach the mouth to quench thirst, the invocations directed toward idols or beings other than Allah are inherently incapable of bringing benefit, relief, or salvation, rendering the efforts of the disbelievers entirely vain and misdirected.

translation: And to Allah prostrates whoever is within the heavens and the earth, willingly or by compulsion, and their shadows [as well] in the mornings and the afternoons.
interpretation: The verse indicates that all of creation, whether sentient beings who choose to obey Allah or those compelled by the natural laws governing their physical existence, are in a state of submission to the Divine Will. The mention of shadows lengthening and shortening as they prostrate alongside their owners serves as a profound allegory for the universal subservience of all physical matter to the Creator's design, demonstrating that no entity can escape the overarching authority and sovereignty of Allah.

translation: Say, 'Who is Lord of the heavens and the earth?' Say, 'Allah.' Say, 'Have you then taken besides Him allies who possess not for themselves any benefit or any harm?' Say, 'Is the blind equivalent to the seeing? Or is darkness equivalent to light? Or have they attributed to Allah partners who created like His creation so that the creation seemed similar to them?' Say, 'Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is the One, the Prevailing.'
interpretation: The verse employs powerful rhetorical questions to expose the logical absurdity of polytheism, emphasizing that since Allah alone is the Creator and Sustainer of the entire universe, He is the only One deserving of worship, whereas false deities are impotent entities incapable of benefiting or harming even themselves, making the distinction between truth and falsehood as clear as the difference between sight and blindness or light and darkness.

translation: He sends down rain from the sky, and valleys flow according to their capacity, and the torrent carries a rising foam. And from that which they heat in the fire, desiring ornaments or utensils, comes a foam like it. Thus does Allah present the example of truth and falsehood. As for the foam, it passes away as scum, but that which benefits the people remains on the earth. Thus does Allah present the examples.
interpretation: In this parable, Allah compares truth to the beneficial water and precious molten metals that remain and serve a purpose, while falsehood is likened to the worthless foam that appears prominent and voluminous on the surface but lacks substance, eventually vanishing and leaving nothing of value behind. The verse serves to reassure the believers that while falsehood may appear overwhelming or dominant temporarily, it is inherently ephemeral and will inevitably disappear, whereas the truth—despite any temporary concealment or struggle—is durable and will ultimately persist for the benefit of humanity.

translation: For those who have responded to their Lord is the best [reward], but those who did not respond to Him - if they had all that is in the earth entirely and the like of it with it, they would [attempt to] ransom themselves thereby. Those will have the worst of the account, and their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the resting place.
interpretation: The verse highlights the stark contrast between the believers who readily submit to Allah's guidance and the disbelievers who reject it; while the former receive the ultimate reward of Paradise, the latter will be so consumed by regret on the Day of Judgment that they would offer double the entire earth's wealth as a ransom to escape the punishment they earned through their persistent defiance, yet their efforts will be futile, leading only to a rigorous divine audit of their deeds and an eternal, miserable abode.

translation: Is then he who knows that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth like him who is blind? Only those endowed with intellect will take heed.
interpretation: The verse draws a definitive moral and spiritual distinction between the person of insight who recognizes the divine truth of the revelation and the one who remains spiritually blind; it emphasizes that true wisdom and the ability to grasp the ultimate reality of existence are reserved for those who possess sound intellects and the humility to reflect deeply upon God's signs.

translation: Those who fulfill the covenant of Allah and do not break the contract.
interpretation: This verse describes the essential quality of the pious, highlighting that their relationship with Allah is grounded in complete loyalty and integrity; they honor every obligation they have committed to, whether it is the covenant of faith made with their Creator or the social and ethical contracts made with fellow human beings, ensuring that no trust is ever violated through deceit or betrayal.

translation: And those who join that which Allah has ordered to be joined and fear their Lord and are afraid of the evil of the account.
interpretation: This verse describes the characteristics of the people of intellect who maintain the bonds of kinship, fulfill covenants, and uphold all ties that Allah has commanded to be preserved; they do so out of a deep reverence for Allah and a constant awareness of the Day of Judgment, knowing that their actions will be scrutinized with absolute justice and that any deficiency in their duty could lead to a difficult reckoning.

translation: And those who are patient, seeking the countenance of their Lord, and establish prayer and spend from what We have provided for them secretly and publicly and prevent evil with good - those will have the good consequence of the [final] home.
interpretation: The verse highlights that true believers reach the ultimate success in the Hereafter by combining patience for the sake of Allah with tangible acts of worship, such as consistent prayer and charitable giving. By actively countering harm or negativity with kindness and good deeds, these individuals not only purify their own characters but also transform potential conflicts into opportunities for righteousness, ultimately earning them the eternal bliss and favorable outcome of Paradise.

translation: Gardens of perpetual residence which they will enter, along with those who were righteous among their fathers, their spouses, and their descendants. And the angels will enter upon them from every gate.
interpretation: This verse highlights the continuity of spiritual bonds in the afterlife, illustrating that the reward of Paradise is not merely an individual achievement but a communal blessing where the righteous are reunited with their virtuous loved ones. The entry of angels from every gate signifies an eternal state of honor, safety, and welcoming, reflecting that the inhabitants of these gardens have attained a level of peace where divine protection and angelic companionship are constantly present to celebrate their success.

translation: Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured. And excellent is the final home.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine greeting delivered by the angels to the believers upon their entry into Paradise, highlighting that their eternal reward is a direct consequence of their steadfastness, perseverance in obedience, and patient endurance through the trials and hardships they faced during their worldly life.

translation: And those who break the covenant of Allah after its confirmation, and sever that which Allah has commanded to be joined, and spread corruption on earth - for them is the curse, and for them is the worst home.
interpretation: This verse warns against three destructive behaviors: violating the solemn bond with the Creator, disrupting the ties of kinship and unity that God commanded to be maintained, and engaging in corruption that harms society; these actions constitute a grave violation of the divine order, leading to total estrangement from God’s mercy and a final abode of profound misery and retribution.

translation: Allah extends provision for whom He wills and restricts it. And they rejoice in the worldly life, while the worldly life, in comparison to the Hereafter, is but a brief and fleeting enjoyment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom behind the varying distribution of worldly wealth, emphasizing that financial status is not a criterion of Allah’s favor. It serves as a reminder that the human tendency to find ultimate satisfaction in temporal material gains is a delusion, as the pleasures of this world are merely temporary provisions that pale in insignificance when measured against the eternal reality and enduring rewards of the Hereafter.

translation: And those who disbelieve say, 'Why has a sign not been sent down to him from his Lord?' Say, 'Indeed, Allah leaves astray whom He wills and guides to Himself whoever turns back [to Him].'
interpretation: The disbelievers demanded miracles of their own choosing as a condition for their faith, ignoring the clear truth already presented to them. Allah clarifies that guidance is not granted based on their arbitrary demands, but is instead a divine favor reserved for those whose hearts are sincerely inclined toward repentance and seeking the truth, while those who persist in arrogance and rejection are left to their own straying.

translation: Those who have believed and whose hearts are assured by the remembrance of Allah. Unquestionably, by the remembrance of Allah hearts are assured.
interpretation: The tranquility of the human heart is exclusively found in the remembrance of Allah, because when a person internalizes the greatness of their Creator, acknowledges His control over all affairs, and maintains a constant connection with Him through prayer, invocation, and reflection, their soul ceases its restless searching for worldly fulfillment and attains a state of serene contentment that remains unshaken by external trials or temporal distress.

translation: Those who have believed and done righteous deeds - a good state is theirs and a beautiful place of return.
interpretation: This verse signifies that believers who supplement their faith with virtuous actions are promised a life of eternal joy and tranquility in Paradise, where they will find the ultimate fulfillment of their desires and a blissful, permanent destination that rewards their steadfastness in this worldly life.

translation: Thus have We sent you to a nation before which [other] nations have passed on so you might recite to them that which We have revealed to you, while they disbelieve in the Most Merciful. Say, 'He is my Lord; there is no deity except Him. Upon Him I have relied, and to Him is my return.'
interpretation: God consoles His Prophet by reminding him that sending messengers to nations who reject the truth is a recurring historical pattern, affirming that his duty is solely to convey the message despite their arrogance, and that his reliance must remain exclusively on the Creator who is the only source of authority and the ultimate destination for all.

translation: And if there were a Qur'an by which mountains could be moved, or the earth could be cloven asunder, or the dead could be made to speak, [it would still be this Qur'an]. But the command belongs to Allah entirely. Have those who believe not yet realized that if Allah had willed, He would have guided all of mankind? And those who disbelieve continue to be struck by calamity for what they have done, or it settles near their homes, until the promise of Allah comes. Indeed, Allah does not fail in His promise.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that the Qur'an possesses such profound and overwhelming power that, were it to be manifest in its full reality, it would affect the very fabric of the physical universe—moving mountains, fracturing the earth, and awakening the dead. However, Allah explains that human guidance is not contingent upon such overwhelming miracles, but rather upon His sovereign will; He has chosen not to compel faith through coercion but through the presentation of truth. The ongoing calamities facing the disbelievers serve as a divine warning and a manifestation of justice in this worldly life, demonstrating that the outcome of human actions is entirely in the hands of Allah, who will inevitably fulfill His promise of reckoning.

translation: And indeed, messengers were mocked before you, but I gave respite to those who disbelieved; then I seized them. And how [terrible] was My penalty!
interpretation: God reassures His Prophet by highlighting that the mockery he faces from disbelievers is not a sign of their triumph or divine approval, but rather part of a pattern observed with previous messengers. By granting these disbelievers a period of respite—allowing them to persist in their arrogance and stray further into error—God ensures that when His final retribution comes, it is fully justified and serves as a definitive end to their opposition, leaving no doubt about the severity and inevitable reality of divine justice.

translation: Then is He who is a maintainer of every soul, [knowing] what it has earned, [like any other]? But they have attributed partners to Allah. Say, 'Name them. Or do you inform Him of that which He does not know upon the earth or is it just what is said in words?' Rather, their plotting has been made attractive to those who disbelieve, and they have been averted from the way. And whoever Allah leaves astray - there is no guide for him.
interpretation: This verse presents a profound contrast between the Creator, who is uniquely omniscient and sustains every individual according to their deeds, and the lifeless idols that the polytheists falsely elevate to divinity. Allah challenges the absurdity of their shirk by demanding proof of these partners' existence or authority, clarifying that their adherence to idolatry is not based on divine knowledge or logical evidence, but is merely a facade of empty words crafted by their own deception. By persistently choosing to reject the truth, these individuals have allowed their own internal moral corruption to be presented to them as wisdom, which ultimately results in Allah allowing them to stray further from the path of guidance as a consequence of their own free-willed choices.

translation: For them is a punishment in the life of this world, and the punishment of the Hereafter is harder, and they have no protector against Allah.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern reminder that those who turn away from divine guidance and persist in wrongdoing face a twofold consequence: they experience distress, loss of peace, and worldly repercussions in this life, yet this is only a prelude to a much more severe and agonizing punishment in the afterlife, from which no power or entity can shield them against the decree of Allah.

translation: The likeness of the Paradise which the righteous have been promised: beneath it rivers flow, its fruits are everlasting, and its shade. That is the end of those who were righteous, and the end of the disbelievers is the Fire.
interpretation: Allah illustrates the state of Paradise to make the unseen comprehensible through familiar earthly imagery, describing it as a realm of perpetual sustenance and comfort where the blessings—symbolized by flowing water, constant fruit, and shade—never cease or diminish, contrasting this eternal reward with the finality of the Fire for those who rejected the truth, thereby emphasizing that the ultimate consequence of one's worldly conduct is either everlasting peace or everlasting torment.

translation: Those to whom We have given the Scripture rejoice at what has been revealed to you, but among the [opposing] factions are those who deny part of it. Say, 'I have only been commanded to worship Allah and not associate anything with Him. To Him I invite, and to Him is my return.'
interpretation: The verse highlights the contrast between the righteous among the People of the Scripture, who find spiritual joy and confirmation in the Quran because it aligns with the truth they already possess, and the obstinate factions who selectively reject parts of the revelation based on their prejudices. It serves as a directive for the Prophet to maintain focus on the fundamental core of monotheism—exclusive worship of God—asserting that the ultimate purpose of his mission and the destination of all creation is the return to the Divine Presence, thereby transcending the sectarian disputes of his time.

translation: And thus We have revealed it as an Arabic legislation. And if you should follow their inclinations after what has come to you of knowledge, you would not have against Allah any protector or any defender.
interpretation: The verse serves as a stern warning to the Prophet Muhammad—and by extension, to his followers—that because the Qur'an has been revealed in a clear, eloquent, and definitive Arabic language, it represents the absolute truth and divine authority. To turn away from this guidance to follow the subjective desires and whims of people who reject the truth is not merely a mistake but a betrayal of the knowledge already received, leading to a state where the individual forfeits the protection and support of Allah, leaving them utterly vulnerable to His judgment.

translation: And We have already sent messengers before you and assigned to them wives and descendants. And it was not for a messenger to bring a sign except by permission of Allah. For every term is a record.
interpretation: This verse serves as a consolation to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) by highlighting that he was not the first messenger to lead a human life, as his predecessors also experienced the natural cycle of marriage and parenthood. It underscores the divine authority behind miracles, clarifying that they are not under the control or whims of the messengers themselves, but occur strictly at the command of Allah. Furthermore, it reminds humanity that every event, life span, and divine decree is governed by an unalterable, preordained timing established by Allah, emphasizing that neither delay nor haste can occur outside of His comprehensive knowledge and wisdom.

translation: Allah eliminates what He wills or confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book.
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah possesses absolute sovereign power to abrogate, alter, or confirm the decrees written in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), as He deems appropriate for His creation, while the 'Mother of the Book' remains the foundational, immutable source of all divine knowledge and decree from which nothing is ever erased or changed.

translation: And whether We show you some of what We promise them or We take you in death, your duty is only to convey the message, and upon Us is the reckoning.
interpretation: Allah reassures His Prophet that his responsibility is strictly limited to delivering the message clearly and faithfully, and he should not feel personally burdened or distressed if he does not witness the punishment of the disbelievers during his own lifetime, as the ultimate task of judging their deeds and exacting justice belongs solely to Allah, who will hold them accountable in the hereafter.

translation: Have they not seen that We set upon the land, reducing it from its borders? And Allah judges; there is no adjuster of His command, and He is swift in account.
interpretation: This verse highlights the continuous process of divine decree wherein Allah gradually diminishes the dominion of the disbelievers by expanding the territory of the believers, serving as a reminder that all worldly power is subject to Allah's ultimate authority, which cannot be challenged, reversed, or delayed by any human force, as He holds everyone to account with swift and perfect justice.

translation: And those before them had plotted, but to Allah belongs all the planning. He knows what every soul earns, and the disbelievers will come to know for whom is the ultimate outcome of the home.
interpretation: The verse serves as a stern reminder that while individuals or civilizations may devise elaborate schemes and conspiracies to oppose the truth, their efforts are ultimately futile because Allah’s decree and wisdom encompass and transcend all human strategies. It emphasizes that Allah is fully aware of every action and intention of mankind, and that the final victory and the eternal reward belong solely to those who remained faithful, while those who rejected the truth will ultimately face the consequences of their disbelief when the true nature of the afterlife is unveiled.

translation: And those who disbelieve say, 'You are not a messenger.' Say, 'Sufficient is Allah as Witness between me and you, and [also] whoever has knowledge of the Scripture.'
interpretation: The verse serves as a divine assertion of the Prophet Muhammad's authenticity, directing him to shift the burden of proof from human disbelief to the infallible testimony of Allah and the evidence present within the sacred scriptures of those who preceded him, suggesting that the integrity of his mission is validated both by direct divine revelation and by the confirmation of his character and message found in the genuine, uncorrupted knowledge possessed by the learned followers of previous divine books.

translation: Alif, Lam, Ra. This is a Book which We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], that you might bring mankind out of darknesses into the light by permission of their Lord - to the path of the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: The Almighty describes the Qur'an as a divine light that dispels the darkness of ignorance, polytheism, and disbelief, guiding humanity toward the clarity of faith and truth. By following this guidance, one is led to the path of Allah, who possesses absolute sovereignty and is the only One worthy of all praise, ultimately securing the traveler's transition from the confusion of worldly misguidance to the certainty and peace of His eternal protection.

translation: Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And woe to the disbelievers from a severe punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty of Allah over the entire universe, reminding humanity that because He is the sole owner and sustainer of all existence, true power and authority reside only with Him. By contrasting His total ownership with the status of those who deny His divinity, the verse serves as a stern warning that rejecting the Creator—who sustains one's very existence—leads inevitably to a painful reckoning, as one cannot escape the domain of the One who controls every atom of the heavens and the earth.

translation: Those who prefer the life of this world over the Hereafter and avert [people] from the way of Allah, seeking to make it crooked—those are in extreme error.
interpretation: This verse describes the state of those who allow their material desires and worldly attachments to outweigh their commitment to divine truth, actively working to obstruct others from the path of righteousness by distorting the religion to justify their own transgressions, a state of deep moral and spiritual corruption that distances them completely from the guidance of Allah.

translation: And We did not send any messenger except in the language of his people to state clearly for them, and Allah sends astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: Allah emphasizes that His messengers were sent with the language of their specific people as a means of mercy and clarity, ensuring that the divine message could be understood without ambiguity. The subsequent mention of guidance and misguidance signifies that while the message is made clear through human language, the actual acceptance of truth and the opening of the heart remains a matter of divine decree, which is exercised by Allah with absolute authority and perfect, calculated wisdom.

translation: And certainly We sent Moses with Our signs, [saying], 'Bring your people out from darknesses into the light and remind them of the days of Allah.' Indeed in that are signs for everyone patient and grateful.
interpretation: Allah emphasizes the mission of Prophet Moses to lead his people from the darkness of ignorance, disbelief, and oppression into the light of guidance, faith, and knowledge. Reminding them of the 'days of Allah' refers to reflecting upon the historical events where Allah displayed His power, mercy, and judgment upon nations, serving as lessons for believers. The verse concludes that these historical manifestations and divine interventions are clear evidence for those who possess the dual qualities of sabr (patience during trials) and shukr (gratitude during blessings), as they recognize the consistent patterns of divine wisdom in both adversity and ease.

translation: And mention when Moses said to his people, 'Remember the favor of Allah upon you when He saved you from the people of Pharaoh, who were afflicting you with the worst of torment and were slaughtering your [newborn] sons and keeping your women alive. And in that was a great trial from your Lord.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine reminder to the Children of Israel regarding the immense mercy of Allah in delivering them from the tyrannical reign of Pharaoh. By recounting the specific horrors they endured—the systematic slaughter of their male infants to curb their population and the enslavement of their women—the text emphasizes that their liberation was not merely a historical event but a profound test of faith and gratitude. The 'great trial' mentioned suggests that the transition from a state of oppressed victimhood to one of freedom was designed to see whether the people would remain steadfast in their devotion to God or succumb to arrogance and disobedience once they were secure from their persecutor.

translation: And [remember] when your Lord proclaimed, 'If you are grateful, I will surely increase you [in favor]; but if you deny, indeed, My punishment is severe.'
interpretation: God guarantees that the sincere expression of gratitude—whether through internal acknowledgment of His blessings, vocal praise, or utilizing those gifts in ways that please Him—serves as the primary catalyst for spiritual and material abundance, while deliberate ingratitude or the rejection of His favors invites a painful reckoning, underscoring that our relationship with Divine grace is directly proportional to our acknowledgment of its Source.

translation: And Moses said, 'If you should disbelieve, you and whoever is on the earth entirely - indeed, Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute self-sufficiency of God, asserting that human belief or disbelief does not affect His essence or majesty in the slightest. Moses is reminding his people that their rejection of the truth does not harm Allah, but rather harms themselves, because Allah is inherently praiseworthy and perfect in His attributes regardless of whether His creation acknowledges Him or not.

translation: Has there not reached you the news of those before you - the people of Noah and 'Aad and Thamud and those after them? No one knows them but Allah. Their messengers brought them clear proofs, but they put their hands in their mouths and said, 'Indeed, we disbelieve in that with which you have been sent, and indeed we are, concerning that to which you invite us, in disquieting doubt.'
interpretation: The verse serves as a historical reminder of the recurring pattern of denial displayed by past nations towards their prophets. When Allah’s messengers presented clear signs and truth, these people responded with stubborn arrogance—symbolized by putting their hands in their mouths, which indicates their attempt to silence the messengers or their utter refusal to accept the truth—choosing instead to remain in a state of unsettling and persistent doubt that prevented them from acknowledging the reality of the divine message.

translation: Their messengers said, 'Is there any doubt about Allah, Creator of the heavens and the earth? He invites you that He may forgive you of your sins, and He delays your death to a specified term.' They said, 'You are not but human beings like us. You wish to avert us from what our fathers were worshipping, so bring us a clear authority.'
interpretation: The verse illustrates the fundamental conflict between the prophetic call based on divine revelation and the materialist skepticism of the deniers. The messengers emphasize that the existence of a Creator is an undeniable intuitive truth, highlighting that the primary purpose of the divine message is to grant humanity spiritual cleansing and a reprieve from immediate destruction to reflect on their choices. Conversely, the disbelievers rely on a shallow argument of anthropocentrism—dismissing the message solely because the messengers were fellow humans—and cling to ancestral tradition over empirical truth, ultimately demanding supernatural signs not to gain knowledge, but to sustain their path of resistance.

translation: Their messengers said to them, 'We are only human beings like you, but Allah confers favor upon whom He wills of His servants. It was not for us to bring you evidence except by permission of Allah. And upon Allah let the believers rely.'
interpretation: The messengers emphasize that their humanity does not undermine their divine mission, as prophethood is a gift of grace from Allah rather than an inherent quality of human nature. By clarifying that they cannot produce miracles or authority without Allah's direct mandate, they humble themselves before the Divine, establishing that their power and guidance are entirely dependent on Him, and they encourage their followers to place their ultimate trust in Allah's sovereignty rather than in the messengers' own personal strength.

translation: And why should we not rely upon Allah while He has guided us to our [good] ways? And we will surely be patient against whatever harm you should cause us. And upon Allah let those who rely [truly] rely.
interpretation: The verse highlights that absolute trust in Allah is the natural outcome of recognizing His guidance, which serves as the fundamental light for a believer’s path. By acknowledging that Allah has directed them toward the truth and righteousness, believers find an unshakeable inner strength that renders them indifferent to the hostility of others. This reliance is not a passive resignation but an active commitment to endurance, recognizing that the source of true success and ultimate protection lies solely with the Creator, thereby liberating the heart from the fear of human persecution.

translation: And those who disbelieved said to their messengers, 'We will surely drive you out of our land, or you must return to our religion.' So their Lord inspired to them, 'We will surely destroy the wrongdoers.'
interpretation: The verse illustrates the perennial pattern of arrogance and intimidation displayed by tyrannical authorities throughout history, who attempt to coerce those preaching the truth into submission or exile. The divine response serves as an absolute promise of justice, affirming that the ultimate outcome of oppression is the inevitable downfall of the transgressors, signaling that no earthly authority can hinder the eventual victory of divine truth.

translation: And We will surely cause you to dwell in the land after them. That is for whoever fears standing before Me and fears My threat.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine assurance to the believers that they will eventually inherit the earth and its power after the demise or destruction of those who committed injustice and oppression. The realization of this promise, however, is strictly conditional upon the individual cultivating two essential states of heart: the awe and reverence of standing before Allah for judgment, and the profound fear of the consequences promised to those who deviate from His path, which serves as a moral anchor to ensure that when power is granted, it is exercised with righteousness and accountability.

translation: And they requested victory, and disappointed was every obstinate tyrant.
interpretation: The verse illustrates the final destiny of those who oppressors and reject the truth; when the divine judgment arrives or when the believers seek aid against these tyrants, all those who stubbornly persist in their arrogance and refuse to submit to the truth find their power shattered, their plans thwarted, and their ultimate end marked by complete failure and loss.

translation: Before him is Hell, and he will be given a drink of purulent water.
interpretation: This verse portrays the inevitable destiny of the disbeliever who stubbornly turns away from the truth, depicting a state of absolute wretchedness where their ultimate refuge is the Fire of Hell, accompanied by a humiliating and agonizing torment manifested in the consumption of 'sadid'—a vile mixture of the blood, pus, and filth flowing from the bodies of the inhabitants of Hell, which serves as both a physical punishment and a symbolic degradation for their refusal to accept guidance.

translation: He will gulp it, but he will hardly be able to swallow it. Death will come to him from every side, yet he will not die; and before him is a harsh, relentless punishment.
interpretation: This verse describes the agonizing state of the dwellers of Hell, illustrating that their suffering is designed to be continuous and inescapable; they are forced to consume substances of extreme bitterness and pain that they cannot ingest, and although they experience the crushing intensity of death approaching them from all directions as if they were perishing, their life is sustained solely to ensure they remain conscious and capable of experiencing the severe, unrelenting torment that awaits them.

translation: The example of those who disbelieve in their Lord is [that] their deeds are like ashes which the wind blows forcefully on a stormy day; they are unable to keep [any of] what they earned. That is what is extreme error.
interpretation: This verse presents a profound parable illustrating the futility of good deeds performed by those who lack faith in Allah. Just as ashes, which have no weight or substance, are instantly scattered and rendered useless by a violent storm, the actions of the disbelievers—though they may appear significant in this life—will carry no weight or benefit in the Hereafter because they lack the foundation of sincere belief and submission to the Creator. The 'stormy day' symbolizes the Day of Judgment, where all worldly pretenses are stripped away, leaving the disbeliever empty-handed and devoid of any reward, signifying their profound loss and deviation from the path of ultimate truth.

translation: Do you not see that Allah created the heavens and the earth in truth? If He wills, He can do away with you and bring forth a new creation.
interpretation: This verse serves as a powerful reminder of Allah's absolute sovereignty and the transience of human existence. By highlighting that the creation of the cosmos was founded upon divine truth and purpose, it establishes that the world is not a product of chance but a manifestation of His wisdom. The assertion that Allah could replace humanity with a different creation at any moment underscores man's complete dependence on His grace, emphasizing that our continuity is entirely contingent upon His will, thereby humbling the pride of those who might think they are indispensable or permanent.

translation: And that is not difficult for Allah.
interpretation: This phrase serves as a divine reassurance that the resurrection of mankind or any act of creation is not beyond the reach of Allah’s infinite power, emphasizing that nothing in the heavens or on the earth can ever hinder or frustrate His absolute will.

translation: And they will all appear before Allah; then the weak will say to those who were arrogant, 'Indeed, we were your followers, so can you avail us anything against the punishment of Allah?' They will say, 'If Allah had guided us, we would have guided you. It is all the same for us whether we show intolerance or are patient; we have no place of escape.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the ultimate dissolution of worldly hierarchies and deceptive loyalties on the Day of Judgment. Those who surrendered their moral agency to powerful earthly figures will realize that their leaders possess no divine authority or capacity to intercede. The admission of the arrogant—that their own guidance was contingent upon Allah’s will—signifies a state of absolute existential helplessness, where both complaints and endurance become equally futile because the opportunity for repentance and change has permanently expired.

translation: And Satan will say when the matter has been concluded, 'Indeed, Allah had promised you the promise of truth. And I promised you, but I betrayed you. But I had no authority over you except that I invited you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me; but blame yourselves. I cannot be called to your aid, nor can you be called to my aid. Indeed, I deny your association of me with Allah before. Indeed, for the wrongdoers is a painful punishment.'
interpretation: This verse depicts the scene on the Day of Judgment where Satan disavows his followers, clarifying that his influence was limited to mere suggestion and enticement, leaving the burden of choice and the resulting consequences entirely upon the individuals who chose to follow his path of disobedience over the truth of Allah.

translation: And those who believed and did righteous deeds will be admitted to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding eternally therein by permission of their Lord; their greeting therein will be, 'Peace.'
interpretation: This verse describes the ultimate reward for the believers whose faith was manifested in virtuous deeds, promising them an eternal abode in Paradise where they will experience perfect security and serenity, as signified by the divine greeting of 'Peace' that permeates their environment, indicating that they are free from all harm, fear, and conflict in the presence of their Creator.

translation: Have you not considered how Allah presents an example, [making] a good word like a good tree, whose root is firmly fixed and its branches [high] in the sky?
interpretation: The good word, which is the profession of faith (Tawheed) and every righteous statement, is likened to a deeply rooted tree because belief is firmly established in the believer's heart, while its branches reaching into the sky represent the righteous deeds and pure intentions that ascend to Allah and bring forth continuous spiritual benefits for both the individual and society.

translation: It yields its fruit at all times, by permission of its Lord. And Allah presents examples for the people that perhaps they will be reminded.
interpretation: The verse illustrates the nature of a righteous word or a believer, suggesting that their goodness, wisdom, and beneficial deeds are continuous and ever-present, much like a healthy tree that bears fruit in every season. By comparing spiritual truths to observable physical phenomena, God helps human beings grasp abstract concepts, encouraging them to reflect on the consistency of virtue and to act in ways that produce everlasting spiritual benefit.

translation: And the example of a foul word is like a foul tree, uprooted from the surface of the earth, having no stability.
interpretation: This verse presents a parable contrasting the nature of falsehood and disbelief with the nature of truth; just as a foul, noxious tree lacks deep roots and cannot sustain itself or provide benefit to the earth, the word of disbelief is devoid of any underlying truth, foundation, or moral permanence, making it easily uprooted and incapable of bearing any lasting fruit for the soul.

translation: Allah strengthens those who believe with the firm word in the worldly life and in the Hereafter, and Allah leads astray the wrongdoers, and Allah does what He wills.
interpretation: This verse refers to the divine support granted to the believers, whereby Allah enables them to remain steadfast in their faith and profession of the testimony of truth (the firm word) during the trials of this world and at the moment of questioning in the grave, whereas those who persist in injustice and disbelief are deprived of this divine guidance and left to wander in their error, as Allah possesses absolute sovereignty to execute His decree according to His infinite wisdom.

translation: Have you not considered those who exchanged the favor of Allah for disbelief and settled their people in the home of ruin?
interpretation: This verse refers to the leaders of the Quraysh who rejected the divine blessing of Prophet Muhammad, upon whom be peace, and led their own people into a state of spiritual destruction and eventual defeat in this life and the afterlife by inciting them toward disbelief and conflict against the truth.

translation: Hell, which they will [enter to] burn, and wretched is the settlement.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning regarding the ultimate destination of those who persist in disbelief and transgression, illustrating that their final abode is not merely a place of confinement, but one of intense suffering and fire, emphasizing that the consequence of rejecting divine truth is an eternal state of misery that stands in sharp contrast to the peaceful residence prepared for the righteous.

translation: And they have attributed to Allah rivals [in worship] to mislead [people] from His way. Say, 'Enjoy yourselves, for indeed, your destination is the Fire.'
interpretation: This verse warns against the arrogance of those who set up partners or false deities alongside Allah, driven by their desire to divert others from the path of truth. The command for them to 'enjoy' is an expression of divine irony and a stern warning; it signifies that their worldly gains and fleeting pleasures are inconsequential and temporary, as their ultimate end is the inescapable consequence of their rebellion against the Creator.

translation: Say to My servants who have believed, that they should establish prayer, and spend from what We have provided them, secretly and publicly, before a Day comes in which there will be no exchange nor any friendships.
interpretation: God commands the Prophet to urge the believers to hasten toward performing righteous deeds, specifically establishing regular prayer and giving charity, before the arrival of the Day of Judgment when the opportunity to earn reward or ransom oneself through material wealth or earthly connections will be permanently lost.

translation: And He has subjected for you the sun and the moon, both continuously pursuing their courses, and He has subjected for you the night and the day.
interpretation: God has placed these vast cosmic entities and the rhythmic cycle of time under a state of perpetual service for humanity, ensuring they function with unwavering precision to sustain life, facilitate the passage of time, and provide the necessary conditions for biological survival and global order.

translation: And He gave you from all that you asked of Him. And if you should count the favor of Allah, you could not enumerate them. Indeed, mankind is most unjust and ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the boundless generosity of God, who anticipates and fulfills the needs of humanity even before they are articulated, providing an abundance of sustenance and grace. The inability to count these blessings underscores their overwhelming nature, serving as a reminder that the human tendency toward oppression and ingratitude stems from a failure to acknowledge this constant divine provision and a persistent tendency to overlook the Creator's benevolence in favor of worldly preoccupations.

translation: And remember when Abraham said, 'My Lord, make this city secure and keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols.'
interpretation: Abraham exhibits profound wisdom and humility by recognizing that security, peace, and spiritual steadfastness are not inherent human achievements, but divine gifts; thus, he beseeches Allah to transform the physical location into a sanctuary of safety and to extend his protection over himself and his progeny to ensure their hearts remain firmly anchored in monotheism, acknowledging the ever-present danger of falling into spiritual blindness or the temptation of material and symbolic idolatry.

translation: My Lord, indeed they have led astray many among mankind. So whoever follows me - then he is of me; and whoever disobeys me - indeed, You are Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: Ibrahim expresses that the idols have caused many people to stray from the path of true monotheism, and he declares that his true followers are those who join him in worshiping Allah alone, while he entrusts those who disobey him to Allah's infinite mercy and forgiveness, hoping that they might eventually repent and be guided back to the truth.

translation: Our Lord, I have settled some of my descendants in an uncultivated valley near Your sacred House, our Lord, that they may establish prayer. So make hearts among the people incline toward them and provide for them from the fruits that they might be grateful.
interpretation: Prophet Ibrahim (AS) demonstrates complete reliance upon Allah by leaving his family in the barren desert of Mecca solely for the sake of God's command. His prayer highlights that the primary purpose for human settlement and social stability is the establishment of prayer, which serves as the foundation for spiritual and communal life. By asking that the hearts of people incline toward them, Ibrahim (AS) acknowledges that spiritual magnetism and social unity are blessings bestowed by Allah, transforming a desolate place into a center of human attraction and sustenance, thereby fostering an environment conducive to gratitude.

translation: Our Lord, indeed You know what we conceal and what we declare, and nothing is hidden from Allah in the earth or in the heaven.
interpretation: This verse serves as a profound affirmation of Allah's absolute and all-encompassing knowledge, acknowledging that He possesses full awareness of the innermost intentions, hidden secrets, and overt actions of all creation, leaving nothing beyond His observation or grasp in any part of existence.

translation: Praise to Allah, who has granted to me in old age Ishmael and Isaac. Indeed, my Lord is the Hearer of supplication.
interpretation: Prophet Abraham acknowledges that the birth of his sons, Ishmael and Isaac, at an advanced age was an act of pure grace and miraculous divine favor, emphasizing that Allah's capacity to answer prayers transcends the natural limitations of biology and time, thereby affirming his absolute reliance on the Creator who hears and responds to the sincere calls of His servants.

translation: My Lord, make me an establisher of prayer, and [many] from my descendants. Our Lord, and accept my supplication.
interpretation: The Prophet Ibrahim prays that Allah grants him and his offspring the consistency, sincerity, and perfect observance of prayer, acknowledging that it is the fundamental pillar of faith and the means by which one maintains a constant connection to the Creator, while humbly requesting that Allah accepts this plea and all other prayers as a sign of His mercy.

translation: Our Lord, forgive me and my parents and the believers the Day the account is established.
interpretation: This verse represents a comprehensive supplication taught by Prophet Ibrahim, expressing a profound sense of accountability before Allah. It reflects the believer's recognition of the necessity of Divine mercy for one's own soul, the honor and gratitude owed to parents, and the social bond of brotherhood that unites all believers, as they all stand in collective need of forgiveness on the Day of Resurrection when every individual's deeds will be scrutinized and justice will be administered.

translation: And never think that Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do. He only delays them for a Day when eyes will stare in horror.
interpretation: This verse serves as a profound consolation for the oppressed and a stern warning to the oppressors, clarifying that God's silence or lack of immediate punishment does not stem from ignorance or neglect; rather, it is a deliberate postponement of justice until the Day of Resurrection, where the severity and terror of the divine judgment will cause the eyes of the wrongdoers to remain fixed in eternal, wide-eyed shock as they finally confront the consequences of their earthly transgressions.

translation: Racing ahead, their heads uplifted, their gaze unable to return to them, and their hearts a void.
interpretation: This verse depicts the state of the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment as they rush towards the caller in a state of utter shock, paralyzing fear, and confusion. They are so fixated on the terrifying reality before them that they cannot blink or look away, while their hearts have become completely hollow and empty of all reason, comfort, and hope due to the overwhelming intensity of their dread.

translation: And warn the people of the Day when the punishment will come to them, and those who did wrong will say, 'Our Lord, delay us for a short term; we will answer Your call and follow the messengers.' [But it will be said], 'Had you not sworn before that there would be for you no cessation?'
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning regarding the inevitability of the Day of Judgment, highlighting the regret of those who transgressed during their worldly lives. When faced with the inescapable reality of divine retribution, the wrongdoers will plead for a second chance, promising to believe and obey the prophets they once rejected. However, this plea is countered by a reminder of their past arrogance and their firm, misplaced conviction in this life that their power, state, or existence would never come to an end, illustrating that their current desperation is born not of genuine repentance, but of the sudden, terrifying realization that their worldly confidence was a delusion.

translation: And you dwelt in the dwellings of those who wronged themselves, and it became clear to you how We dealt with them, and We set forth for you the examples.
interpretation: This verse serves as a historical and moral reminder to the believers, highlighting that the remnants and stories of past civilizations—who persisted in disbelief and tyranny—are not merely empty ruins but lessons meant to demonstrate the inevitability of divine justice. By inhabiting the lands or observing the history of those who oppressed their own souls through sin and rebellion, the believers are prompted to reflect on the reality that worldly power and material prosperity offer no protection against God's decree, urging them to avoid repeating the transgressions that led to the ruin of their predecessors.

translation: And they have planned their plan, but with Allah is [recorded] their plan, even if their plan had been [sufficient] to do away with the mountains.
interpretation: The verse illustrates the absolute impotence of human schemes when confronted with the divine decree; it serves as a consolation to the Prophet and the believers, emphasizing that no matter how formidable or destructive the conspiracies of the disbelievers may appear—even to the point of shaking the very foundations of the earth—they remain entirely subject to Allah's ultimate control and are ultimately rendered futile against His will.

translation: So do not think that Allah will fail in His promise to His messengers. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Owner of Retribution.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine reassurance to the believers that the promise of victory, honor, and ultimate justice granted to the messengers of Allah is absolute and immutable; therefore, one must never doubt that Allah will fulfill His decree, for His infinite power and sovereignty ensure that those who transgress against His truth will inevitably face the consequences of their actions in accordance with His perfect justice.

translation: On the Day the earth will be replaced by another earth and the heavens [as well], and all creatures will come out before Allah, the One, the Prevailing.
interpretation: This verse describes the cosmic transformation on the Day of Resurrection, where the current physical laws and the material composition of the heavens and the earth will be fundamentally altered to accommodate the final judgment. The 'new earth' will be a leveled plain without mountains or valleys, crafted specifically for the gathering of all humanity. The phrase 'emerged before Allah' signifies that no one can hide from the Divine presence; every soul will be exposed in its entirety, stripped of worldly influence, before the absolute authority of the One who holds total dominion and irresistible power over all existence.

translation: And you will see the criminals that Day bound together in shackles.
interpretation: This verse describes the state of the disbelievers and sinners on the Day of Resurrection, where they will be humiliated by being bound together in chains and fetters, signifying their lack of freedom, their profound disgrace, and the collective punishment that reflects their mutual influence in disbelief and corruption during their worldly lives.

translation: Their garments will be of liquid pitch, and fire will cover their faces.
interpretation: This verse vividly illustrates the state of the dwellers of the Hellfire, describing how they are clothed in garments made of tar or molten copper, which are highly flammable and cling painfully to the skin, while the intensity of the flames is such that it envelops and consumes their entire countenance, signifying both physical agony and the total disgrace that accompanies their punishment.

translation: That Allah may recompense every soul for what it has earned. Indeed, Allah is swift in account.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute justice of Allah on the Day of Judgment, where every individual—whether their deeds were good or evil—will receive their exact due without injustice. The mention of Allah being 'swift in account' serves as a reminder to the believers of the certainty of accountability, indicating that while the scale of human actions is vast and the number of souls is immense, Allah’s knowledge and power are such that He requires no time or effort to judge them all simultaneously and decisively.

translation: This is a notification for the people so that they may be warned by it, and that they may know that He is but one God, and that those of understanding may take heed.
interpretation: This verse serves as a declaration of the Quran's primary purpose: to awaken the human consciousness through clear guidance that distinguishes truth from falsehood. It emphasizes that the ultimate goal of this revelation is for mankind to internalize the oneness of God as the core reality of existence, thereby ensuring that people of intellect and insight are continuously reminded to reflect deeply on the signs of the Creator and align their lives with His divine path.

translation: Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the Book and a clear Qur'an.
interpretation: These opening disjointed letters serve to challenge the eloquence and literary supremacy of the Arabs, signaling that the divine revelation is composed of the very alphabet they use, yet they are unable to replicate its wisdom and guidance, affirming that the verses which follow are explicitly clear in their truth, guidance, and distinction between right and wrong.

translation: Perhaps those who disbelieve will wish that they had been Muslims.
interpretation: This verse describes the profound regret that disbelievers will experience on the Day of Judgment when they witness the ultimate triumph of the believers and realize the reality of the faith they rejected. It serves as a stark warning about the finality of their choices and the eternal consequences of persisting in disbelief despite the clear guidance provided to them throughout their lives.

translation: Leave them to eat and enjoy themselves and let false hope divert them, for they will soon come to know.
interpretation: This verse is a stern admonition directed at those who are heedless of the afterlife, illustrating that their preoccupation with worldly pleasures and their reliance on long, unfounded aspirations serve only to distract them from their ultimate accountability; it serves as a warning that once the reality of death and the Day of Judgment arrives, they will realize the futility of their worldly focus and face the consequences of their choices.

translation: And We did not destroy any city but that it had a known decree.
interpretation: This verse signifies that Allah has established a fixed term and a preordained limit for every civilization and community. The destruction of nations is not an arbitrary act but occurs precisely when their decreed time has elapsed according to divine wisdom, which takes into account their persistence in disbelief and transgression once the truth has been made clear to them.

translation: No nation can forestall its appointed time, nor can they delay it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the lifespan of every nation, as well as the predetermined moment for its rise, decline, or destruction, is fixed by divine decree; it is a manifestation of Allah’s absolute sovereignty and perfect knowledge, ensuring that no society can hasten its end or postpone its demise even by a single moment beyond the immutable limit set by His wisdom.

translation: And they said, 'O you upon whom the message has been sent down, indeed you are mad.'
interpretation: The disbelievers were attempting to delegitimize the Prophet Muhammad by accusing him of insanity, as a way to dismiss the profound and transformative nature of the Qur'an which they could not logically refute; by labeling him a madman, they hoped to insulate their followers from the influence of his message and maintain the status quo of their ancestral polytheistic traditions.

translation: Why do you not bring the angels to us, if you should be among the truthful?
interpretation: This verse reflects the arrogance and skepticism of the disbelievers who demanded supernatural evidence to validate the Prophet's message, foolishly believing that the descent of angels was the only measure of truth, while ignoring the clear divine signs and logical proofs that had already been presented to them.

translation: We do not send down the angels except with the truth, and they would not then be reprieved.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the descent of angels is governed by divine wisdom and justice, as they appear only to execute God's command or bring about the truth that seals the fate of the disbelievers, leaving no room for further delay or respite once that definitive decree is issued.

translation: Indeed, it is We who sent down the message and indeed, We will be its guardian.
interpretation: God guarantees the preservation of the Qur'an by protecting it from any alteration, corruption, addition, or deletion, ensuring that it remains exactly as it was revealed to the Prophet Muhammad until the end of time.

translation: And We had certainly sent messengers before you among the former peoples.
interpretation: This verse serves as a source of consolation for the Prophet Muhammad, reassuring him that the challenges, rejection, and mockery he faced from his people were not unique occurrences, but rather a recurring pattern experienced by the messengers who came before him, emphasizing that he is part of a long historical tradition of divine guidance despite persistent human resistance.

translation: And there comes not to them any messenger except that they ridicule him.
interpretation: This verse highlights the deep-seated spiritual blindness and persistent arrogance of those who reject the truth; it describes a recurring pattern in human history where individuals become so hardened by their attachment to ancestral falsehoods and worldly desires that their immediate reaction to divine guidance is not inquiry or reflection, but mockery, as a defensive mechanism to insulate their ego against the transformative power of the messenger's message.

translation: Thus do We cause it to enter into the hearts of the criminals.
interpretation: This verse signifies that Allah allows the disbelief and rejection of the truth to permeate the hearts of those who persist in wickedness, effectively sealing their hearts as a consequence of their own persistent denial and moral choices, thereby ensuring that the message of faith finds no path to their guidance.

translation: They do not believe in it, even though the way of the former people has already passed.
interpretation: The verse highlights the persistent state of denial among the disbelievers who reject the truth despite having clear historical precedents. It serves as a reminder that the patterns of the past—where previous nations were destroyed or faced divine judgment for their persistent disbelief—should act as a sobering lesson for the current generation, yet they remain heedless of these inevitable consequences.

translation: And even if We opened for them a gate from the heaven and they continued therein to ascend,
interpretation: This verse illustrates the extreme obstinacy and skepticism of the disbelievers, indicating that even if Allah were to grant them a sensory miracle as profound as ascending into the heavens before their own eyes, they would remain locked in their denial, claiming that their vision was bewitched or that they had been subjected to magic, thereby proving that their rejection is rooted in arrogance rather than a lack of evidence.

translation: They would surely say, 'Our eyes have only been dazzled; rather, we are a people bewitched.'
interpretation: The verse describes the obstinate disbelief of the deniers who, even if they were to witness miraculous signs or be ascended to the heavens, would reject the truth by claiming their perception has been corrupted or deceived through sorcery, as a way to avoid acknowledging the divine reality presented before them.

translation: And We have placed within the heaven great stars and have beautified it for the observers.
interpretation: Allah signifies His supreme power and artistry by adorning the firmament with constellations and celestial bodies, transforming the night sky into a majestic display that invites human intellect to reflect on the grandeur of the Creator, thereby serving as both a visual delight and a testament to divine order.

translation: And We have protected it from every accursed devil.
interpretation: This verse signifies that Allah has fortified the heavens and the cosmic order against the attempts of devils to eavesdrop on the celestial council, ensuring that the divine decree remains secure from their interference and corruption.

translation: Except for one who steals a hearing, and there follows him a clear burning flame.
interpretation: This verse signifies that while the devils attempt to eavesdrop on the celestial council to learn of the unseen, they are immediately pursued and driven away by a visible, piercing projectile of light, which prevents them from acquiring authentic information or corrupting the divine decrees with falsehoods.

translation: And the earth We have spread out, and set thereon mountains firm, and produced therein all kinds of things in due balance.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom in the structural design of the earth, emphasizing that the placement of mountains serves as a stabilizing force for the crust, while the phrase 'in due balance' signifies that everything grown from the earth exists in a state of precise ecological proportion and equilibrium designed to sustain life.

translation: And We have placed therein for you means of livelihood and for those whom you do not provide.
interpretation: God is highlighting His absolute sovereignty and generosity by explaining that He provides the sustenance not only for humans but also for all other creatures—such as animals and livestock—that depend on Him, reminding human beings that even those whom they believe they are supporting or who are under their care are ultimately sustained by the providence and provision of Allah alone.

translation: And there is not a thing but that with Us are its depositories, and We do not send it down except according to a known measure.
interpretation: This verse establishes that all resources, provisions, and phenomena in existence originate from the absolute, infinite divine treasury of Allah, and their manifestation in the physical world is governed by precise, calculated limits determined by His supreme wisdom, ensuring that every element of creation serves its intended purpose without excess or deficiency.

translation: And We have sent the fertilizing winds and sent down water from the sky and given you drink from it. And you are not its retainers.
interpretation: God highlights His immense favor by orchestrating the atmospheric cycle, where winds serve as the agents of pollination for plants and clouds, leading to the descent of life-giving rain. The final clause serves as a reminder of human frailty and dependence, emphasizing that although humans consume this water, they lack the divine power to create it, store it eternally, or guarantee its provision, as its source and distribution are entirely under God’s sovereign control.

translation: And indeed, it is We who give life and cause death, and We are the Inheritor.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah alone is the absolute Sovereign over the cycle of existence, possessing the exclusive power to bestow life upon the created and to decree the end of their worldly journey. By identifying Himself as 'The Inheritor,' Allah emphasizes that He remains the ultimate and eternal Owner of all things; when all worldly possessions, power, and creatures perish and return to dust, He alone subsists, signifying that every human acquisition is temporary and that true possession belongs only to the Creator.

translation: And We already know those who preceded among you, and We already know the later ones.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's absolute and comprehensive knowledge of all human beings, encompassing those who have already passed away and those who are yet to come into existence, acknowledging that nothing in human history or the timeline of souls is hidden from His awareness.

translation: And indeed, your Lord will gather them; indeed, He is Wise and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah’s decree to gather all of humanity on the Day of Resurrection is an inevitable truth rooted in His divine attributes; it reflects that His wisdom ensures every action and individual is accounted for, while His absolute knowledge leaves nothing hidden, ensuring that the resurrection is a manifestation of perfect justice and purpose.

translation: And We certainly created man out of clay from an altered black mud.
interpretation: This verse describes the physical origin of humanity, indicating that God fashioned the first human, Adam, from a mixture of earth and water that was left to undergo chemical and physical changes, resulting in a dark, malleable clay, signifying that the human body originates from humble, earthy materials before receiving the divine breath of life.

translation: And the jinn We created before from scorching fire.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the Jinn race was brought into existence by Allah before the creation of mankind, and their physical essence originates from a smokeless, intense, and penetrating fire that reaches the pores of the skin, emphasizing their distinct metaphysical and elemental nature compared to the clay-based composition of human beings.

translation: And mention when your Lord said to the angels, 'Indeed, I will create a human being out of clay from an altered black mud.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the commencement of the creation of humanity, illustrating Allah's sovereign decree to bring forth a physical being from terrestrial materials that have undergone transformative stages, specifically clay that has dried to a resonant state and dark, moldable mud, marking the transition from inanimate matter to the potential for life, while simultaneously establishing the status of mankind as a distinct creation intended to manifest divine wisdom on Earth.

translation: So when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My spirit, then fall down to him in prostration.
interpretation: This command signifies an honor bestowed upon Adam, representing the unique dignity of humanity. The 'breathing of the spirit' does not imply a physical part of God, but rather signifies the bestowal of consciousness, intellect, and divine purpose, marking the transition of the human form from mere physical clay to a living being capable of knowing its Creator. The command for the angels to prostrate is an act of recognizing this superior potential and the manifestation of God’s creative power in the human being, serving as an acknowledgment of Adam's status as a vicegerent on Earth.

translation: So the angels prostrated, all of them entirely.
interpretation: This act of prostration represents the total submission and absolute obedience of the angels to Allah's command, acknowledging the honor He bestowed upon Adam, thereby establishing the divine hierarchy and the angelic recognition of human potential through the knowledge imparted by the Creator.

translation: Except for Iblis; he refused to be among those who prostrated.
interpretation: This verse highlights the act of disobedience and arrogance committed by Iblis when he refused to follow the command of Allah to prostrate to Adam, revealing that his pride prevented him from acknowledging the honor bestowed upon humanity by the Creator.

translation: [Allah] said, 'O Iblees, what is [the matter] with you that you are not with those who prostrate?'
interpretation: This verse represents a divine inquiry addressed to Iblees, intended not to seek information that Allah does not already possess, but rather to confront him with his act of disobedience and to expose the arrogance in his heart that led him to defy a direct command of his Creator.

translation: He said, 'Never would I prostrate to a human whom You created out of clay from an altered black mud.'
interpretation: Iblis manifests his arrogance and disobedience by attempting to justify his refusal to obey Allah's command through the lens of racial or elemental superiority; he views his own origin of fire as inherently more noble than the human origin of dust, thereby failing to recognize that the value of a creature is determined solely by the command and decree of the Creator rather than the physical substance from which it was fashioned.

translation: Allah said, 'Then get out of here, for you are indeed rejected.'
interpretation: This command signifies the absolute expulsion of Iblis from the proximity of Allah and the high heavens due to his arrogance and disobedience. Being 'rajim' (rejected/accursed) implies that he has been cast away from all divine mercy and goodness, and he is pelted with disgrace, marking his transition from a state of worship to a state of eternal rebellion and enmity toward humanity.

translation: And indeed, upon you is My curse until the Day of Recompense.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the one who has been expelled from the mercy of Allah, specifically Iblis, will remain in a state of perpetual condemnation and distance from Divine grace, receiving the full measure of punishment and alienation until the Day of Judgment, when he and his followers will face their ultimate and eternal reckoning.

translation: He said: 'My Lord, then reprieve me until the day they are resurrected.'
interpretation: Iblis, upon being expelled for his arrogance, requests a respite from death, seeking to remain alive until the end of the world to further his pursuit of misguiding humanity and proving his claim that mankind is unworthy of divine honor.

translation: He said, 'Then indeed, you are of those reprieved.'
interpretation: This verse signifies that Allah granted Iblis a specific delay until the Day of Resurrection, not because Iblis deserved mercy, but as a test for humanity and a fulfillment of Allah's decree, allowing Iblis to continue his path of temptation so that the distinction between those who follow truth and those who follow falsehood may be made manifest.

translation: Until the day of the time well-known.
interpretation: This phrase refers to the Day of Resurrection, the appointed time known only to Allah, at which point the respite granted to Shaytan and the cycle of earthly trials will come to a definitive end, resulting in the final reckoning for all creation.

translation: He said, 'My Lord, because You have put me in error, I will surely make [disobedience] attractive to them on earth, and I will mislead them all.'
interpretation: Iblis here attempts to shift the responsibility for his transgression onto Allah by claiming that his fall from grace was predestined or caused by Him, using this as a justification for his vow to lead humanity astray. His declaration expresses his defiant resolve to beautify sins, worldly desires, and disbelief in the eyes of mankind, actively working to divert them from the path of obedience and righteousness until the Day of Resurrection.

translation: Except for Your servants among them who are sincere.
interpretation: This verse signifies that Satan's influence and ability to lead astray are fundamentally ineffective against those chosen servants of Allah who have purified their hearts, actions, and intentions exclusively for Him, as their total devotion and spiritual clarity shield them from his deception.

translation: He said, 'This is a path toward Me, a straight path.'
interpretation: This verse signifies that the way leading directly to God is characterized by truth, righteousness, and divine guidance, serving as the sole path that reaches His presence and rewards without deviation.

translation: Indeed, you have no authority over My servants, except for those who follow you from among the deviants.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine assurance to the faithful, clarifying that Iblis possesses no inherent power, force, or coercive influence to compel the sincere servants of Allah into sin; his capability is limited strictly to whisperings and enticements, and his actual 'authority' only manifests over those who voluntarily choose to align themselves with his path of disobedience and misguidance.

translation: And indeed, Hell is the promised place for them all.
interpretation: This verse serves as a definitive divine declaration that the entirety of those who followed the path of Satan and rebelled against God's commands will eventually be gathered together in Hell, where the consequences of their disbelief and corruption will be fully realized in a place of collective retribution.

translation: It has seven gates; for every gate is of them a portion designated.
interpretation: The seven gates of Hell represent distinct levels or layers of punishment, each specifically calibrated and allocated to accommodate different groups of sinners according to the gravity and nature of their transgressions, ensuring that every individual receives the precise measure of retribution they earned during their worldly life.

translation: Indeed, the righteous will be within gardens and springs.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate state of those who possessed God-consciousness in this life, describing their eternal abode as lush gardens filled with verdant beauty and flowing springs, which serves as a manifestation of the peace, spiritual rejuvenation, and divine pleasure they have attained in return for their piety and avoidance of sin.

translation: Enter it in peace, secure.
interpretation: This verse signifies that those who enter Paradise are granted a state of eternal tranquility and safety, where they are protected from all forms of fear, grief, harm, or the possibility of expulsion, reflecting the ultimate reward for their faith and righteous deeds.

translation: And We will remove whatever is in their breasts of resentment, [so they will be] brothers, on thrones facing each other.
interpretation: This verse describes the purification of the hearts of the people of Paradise, where God removes all traces of hatred, envy, or ill will that may have existed between them in the worldly life, ensuring that their relationships are rooted in pure brotherhood, peace, and mutual love as they sit together in equality and harmony.

translation: No fatigue will touch them therein, nor will they ever be removed from it.
interpretation: This verse describes the absolute perfection of the dwellers of Paradise, emphasizing that their state of bliss is immune to any form of physical or mental weariness or exhaustion, and that their residency is eternal and secure, free from any possibility of displacement, expulsion, or termination of their stay.

translation: Inform My servants that it is I who am the Forgiving, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine invitation for believers to maintain a balance between hope and fear; by instructing the Prophet to specifically address His servants, Allah emphasizes His personal accessibility, reassuring them that despite their shortcomings and sins, His infinite capacity for forgiveness and compassion is readily available to those who turn to Him in sincerity and repentance.

translation: And indeed, My punishment is the painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning from Allah, highlighting that the torment He inflicts is unmatched in severity and intensity, far surpassing any form of suffering experienced in this world, thereby urging the listeners to abandon disbelief and sin to escape such an inescapable and agonizing consequence.

translation: And tell them about the guests of Abraham.
interpretation: God instructs Prophet Muhammad to relate to his people the account of the angels who visited Abraham in human form, serving as a reminder of how the righteous are honored by God's messengers and a precursor to the divine judgment that was about to befall the people of Lot.

translation: When they entered upon him and said, 'Peace,' he said, 'Indeed, we are fearful of you.'
