interpretation: God Almighty indicates that He has presented various parables, stories, and proofs in the Qur'an to make the truth clear and accessible to every intellect, yet despite this abundant guidance and the variety of methods used to warn and encourage, the majority of humanity persists in their stubborn rejection of the truth, choosing to remain in a state of willful disbelief rather than submitting to the clear signs provided.

translation: And they said, 'We will not believe you until you break forth for us from the earth a spring.'
interpretation: The disbelievers were demanding tangible, supernatural signs as a prerequisite for their belief, essentially attempting to dictate the terms of divine guidance to the Prophet Muhammad; their request reflects a state of arrogance and obstinacy, where they sought to test the power of God rather than opening their hearts to the intrinsic truth and spiritual clarity of the message itself.

translation: Or you have a garden of palm trees and vines and make rivers flow forth in their midst in streams.
interpretation: This verse reflects the skepticism of the disbelievers toward the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), as they were demanding worldly, material miracles—such as the creation of an abundant garden with flowing water—as a condition for their belief, failing to realize that the truth of his message rests on divine revelation rather than the demonstration of worldly luxury or miraculous landscape architecture.

translation: Or you make the sky fall upon us in pieces as you have claimed, or you bring Allah and the angels before us face to face.
interpretation: This verse reflects the arrogance and stubbornness of the disbelievers who, rather than accepting the clear signs and message brought by the Prophet, issued impossible and challenging ultimatums to him, demanding that he manifest the metaphysical reality of Allah and the angels directly, or that he impose supernatural punishment upon them as proof of his truthfulness, demonstrating their underlying desire for immediate worldly gratification over spiritual belief.

translation: Or you have a house of gold, or you ascend into the sky. And we will not believe in your ascension until you bring down to us a book that we may read. Say, 'Exalted is my Lord! Was I anything but a human messenger?'
interpretation: The disbelievers demanded impossible and materialistic miracles from the Prophet Muhammad as a condition for their belief, such as owning a golden house or physically ascending to the heavens, in an attempt to discredit his message. Through this verse, Allah instructs the Prophet to respond by declaring His transcendence and clarifying that his role is that of a human messenger tasked with delivering divine guidance, not a supernatural being capable of performing arbitrary miracles to suit the whims of those who are already determined to reject the truth.

translation: And nothing has prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them except that they said, 'Has Allah sent a human being as a messenger?'
interpretation: The verse highlights a fundamental psychological barrier that hindered the disbelievers from accepting the truth: their inability to reconcile the concept of Divine message with a human messenger. They harbored an elitist or narrow expectation that a messenger should have been an angel or a supernatural being, and by rejecting the humanity of the Prophet, they used it as a pretext to deny the divine guidance he brought, revealing their arrogance and their unwillingness to submit to a message delivered by someone they considered their equal.

translation: Say, 'If there were upon the earth angels walking securely, We would have sent down to them from the heaven an angel as a messenger.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the persistent demand of the polytheists for an angel to be sent as a messenger to them, explaining that it is a fundamental principle of Divine wisdom that the messenger sent to a particular species must be of the same nature as that species so that communication can be effective and the messenger's lifestyle can serve as a relatable, practical example for the people to follow; thus, an angel would only be sent to a community of angels, whereas for humans, a human messenger is necessary to bridge the gap between divine revelation and human capability.

translation: Say, 'Sufficient is Allah as Witness between me and you. Indeed, He is ever, concerning His servants, Acquainted and Seeing.'
interpretation: The Prophet is instructed to declare that Allah is the ultimate and sufficient witness regarding the truth of his message, as He possesses perfect and absolute knowledge of the hidden realities of his servants and sees their inward states and outward actions, ensuring that nothing is concealed from His divine judgment.

translation: And he whom Allah guides is the [rightly] guided; but he whom He sends astray - you will never find for them protectors besides Him. And We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection [fallen] on their faces - blind, dumb and deaf. Their refuge is Hell; every time it subsides, We increase them in blazing fire.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the absolute sovereignty of Allah over the states of guidance and misguidance; those who receive divine favor and guidance are truly directed toward the truth, while those who persist in turning away from Allah and rejecting His signs are abandoned to their own choices, finding no intercessor or helper in the afterlife. Their state of being gathered on their faces, blinded, deafened, and muted, is a symbolic and literal manifestation of their spiritual state in the worldly life, where they refused to see the truth, hear the word of God, or speak justly, resulting in an eternal retribution where the intensity of their punishment is perpetually renewed.

translation: That is their recompense, because they disbelieved in Our verses and said, 'When we are bones and crumbled particles, will we indeed be resurrected as a new creation?'
interpretation: This verse explains that the punishment of the disbelievers is a direct consequence of their rejection of God's signs and their denial of the afterlife, which stems from an arrogant disbelief in the possibility of God recreating a human being after the physical body has completely disintegrated into dust and bone, thereby underestimating the infinite power of the Creator.

translation: Have they not considered that Allah, who created the heavens and the earth, is [the] One who is able to create the likes of them? And He has appointed for them a term, about which there is no doubt. But the wrongdoers refuse [anything] except disbelief.
interpretation: This verse serves as a rhetorical challenge to those who deny the resurrection, directing their attention to the undeniable power of Allah demonstrated in the creation of the vast heavens and the earth; the implication is that the One who possessed the immense power to originate such an expansive and complex universe from nothing certainly possesses the capability to recreate human beings, whose existence is far less complex by comparison. By reminding them of the inevitable, fixed term of their lives, the verse highlights the irrationality of their arrogance, as their persistence in denial is not due to a lack of evidence, but rather an obstinate refusal to accept the truth of their accountability.

translation: Say, 'If you possessed the storehouses of the mercy of my Lord, then you would withhold out of fear of spending,' and man has ever been stingy.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inherent frailty and shortsightedness of human nature, contrasting it with the infinite generosity of Allah. It serves as a reminder that if humans were in control of the limitless resources of divine mercy and provision, their innate tendency toward greed, insecurity, and the fear of scarcity would lead them to withhold those blessings from others. Because human beings lack the absolute trust in God's providence and possess a narrow vision focused on personal preservation, they would restrict the flow of abundance, whereas Allah remains the ultimate, unfailing provider whose giving is not diminished by the needs of His creation.

translation: And We certainly gave Moses nine clear signs, so ask the Children of Israel [about] when he came to them and Pharaoh said to him, 'Indeed I think, O Moses, that you are affected by magic.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the overwhelming proofs provided to Moses to validate his prophethood, which were so evident that they left no room for honest doubt; Pharaoh’s accusation of sorcery was not an expression of genuine confusion, but a defensive act of stubborn arrogance meant to dismiss the undeniable truth and protect his own worldly authority.

translation: He said, 'You have already known that no one has sent these down as clear evidences except the Lord of the heavens and the earth, and indeed I think you, O Pharaoh, are destroyed.'
interpretation: Musa informs Pharaoh that his internal conviction confirms the divine origin of the miraculous signs, as they possess an intrinsic brilliance that exposes the truth; by pointing out that Pharaoh knows this deep down, Musa highlights the hypocrisy of Pharaoh's rejection, characterizing him as 'mathbura'—meaning someone who is effectively doomed or cut off from all goodness due to his persistent denial of manifest truth.

translation: So he intended to drive them from the land, but We drowned him and those with him all together.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the ultimate futility of Pharaoh's pride and power; despite his efforts to banish Moses and the Children of Israel from their land, Allah intervened to demonstrate that sovereignty belongs to Him alone, turning the oppressor's aggressive scheme into his own absolute destruction and proving that no human authority can withstand the divine decree.

translation: And We said after him to the Children of Israel, 'Dwell in the land, and when the promise of the Hereafter comes, We will bring you forth in a gathered assembly.'
interpretation: This verse signifies that after the demise of Pharaoh and his people, Allah granted the Children of Israel the privilege to inhabit the land of the Levant, yet this establishment was not permanent; it was decreed that upon the arrival of the final promised time—the Day of Resurrection—Allah will gather all of them from their various scattered locations to stand together before Him for the final judgment, manifesting His absolute sovereignty over their destiny.

translation: And with the truth We have sent it down, and with the truth it has descended. And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a bringer of good tidings and a warner.
interpretation: The verse confirms that the Qur'an was revealed with absolute truth and established through divine wisdom, containing no falsehood or error. It emphasizes the purpose of the Prophet Muhammad's mission, which is to guide humanity by giving glad tidings of Paradise to those who believe and do righteous deeds, and warning of the consequences of disbelief and disobedience, thereby fulfilling the divine message with integrity and purpose.

translation: And it is a Qur'an which We have separated [by intervals] that you might recite it to the people over a prolonged period, and We have sent it down progressively.
interpretation: God indicates that He did not reveal the Qur'an all at once but divided it into segments to make it easier for the Prophet to recite, teach, and instill into the hearts of the people, allowing them to contemplate its meanings, memorize its passages, and apply its rulings gradually as circumstances and the needs of the emerging community demanded.

translation: Say, 'Believe in it or do not believe. Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it - when it is recited to them, they fall upon their faces in prostration.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the skeptics by stating that their acceptance or rejection of the Qur'an does not affect its inherent truth, as the reality of the message is confirmed by those who truly possess divine knowledge and discernment; when these individuals hear the profound truths of the revelation, their hearts are so deeply moved by the wisdom and majesty of the words that they are compelled to humble themselves entirely before their Creator, recognizing that the message originates from a source beyond human capacity.

translation: And they say, 'Exalted is our Lord! Indeed, the promise of our Lord will surely be fulfilled.'
interpretation: This verse portrays the humble and reverent reaction of the believers when they hear the words of Allah; they glorify Him by declaring His perfection, acknowledging that every promise He has made—whether of reward for the righteous or punishment for the disobedient—is an absolute certainty that will inevitably come to pass, reflecting their unwavering faith in His sovereignty and the finality of the Day of Judgment.

translation: And they fall upon their faces weeping, and it increases them in humble submission.
interpretation: This verse describes the profound impact of the Qur'an on the hearts of the righteous, illustrating that true guidance is evidenced by a physical and spiritual collapse into humility; when they hear the words of Allah, their hearts are so deeply moved by awe and reverence that their bodies follow suit, causing them to prostrate and weep in recognition of Allah's majesty and their own servitude.

translation: Say, 'Call upon Allah or call upon the Most Merciful. Whichever [name] you call - to Him belong the best names.' And do not recite [too] loudly in your prayer, nor recite quietly, but seek between that an intermediate way.
interpretation: The verse instructs the believer that God possesses all the most beautiful and perfect attributes, making the specific name used in supplication secondary to the sincerity of the heart. Furthermore, it establishes a principle of moderation in religious practice, specifically regarding the public or private recitation of the Quran during prayer; one should avoid ostentatious volume that invites pride or excessive quietness that obscures the message, instead choosing a balanced approach that demonstrates both reverence and humility.

translation: And say, 'Praise to Allah, who has not taken a son and has had no partner in [His] dominion and has no [need of an] ally out of weakness; and glorify Him with [great] glorification.'
interpretation: This verse calls upon the believer to declare Allah's absolute perfection by negating any shortcomings, such as having offspring or needing partners, while emphasizing that His sovereignty is complete and independent; it highlights that His greatness is beyond any human dependency, necessitating that believers recognize His supreme majesty and honor Him with sincere and constant praise.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful. [All] praise is [due] to Allah, who has sent down upon His Servant the Book and has not made therein any deviance.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the Qur'an is characterized by absolute integrity, consistency, and clarity, meaning it contains no contradictions, errors, or deviations from the truth, serving as a perfect guide that remains free from any ambiguity or internal conflict.

translation: [He has made it] upright, to warn of severe punishment from Him and to give good tidings to the believers who do righteous deeds that they will have a good reward.
interpretation: The verse clarifies that the revelation is firmly established upon truth and justice, serving a dual purpose: it acts as a decisive warning to those who persist in disbelief that they will face a formidable retribution decreed by God, while simultaneously offering the promise of a magnificent, eternal reward to those whose faith is manifested through consistent righteous conduct.

translation: Abiding therein forever.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the eternal nature of the reward in Paradise, signifying that those who enter it will dwell there permanently without any end, cessation, or the possibility of death or departure, reflecting the ultimate fulfillment of divine grace and the perfection of the believers' recompense.

translation: And to warn those who say, 'Allah has taken a son.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern admonition to those who attribute offspring to the Divine, rejecting the Islamic doctrine of absolute oneness (Tawhid). It highlights the gravity of such a belief, which contradicts the majesty and self-sufficiency of the Creator, whose nature transcends the human limitations of procreation and familial association.

translation: They have no knowledge thereof, nor had their fathers. Grievous is the word that comes out of their mouths; they speak nothing but a lie.
interpretation: This verse rebukes the polytheists for their baseless claim that God has taken a child, emphasizing that neither they nor their ancestors possess any divine evidence or logical proof to support such a notion; the statement is portrayed as an immensely grave and detestable fabrication, demonstrating that their assertions are void of reality and are merely malicious falsehoods invented without foundation.

translation: Then perhaps you would kill yourself through grief over them, [O Muhammad], if they do not believe in this message, and out of sorrow.
interpretation: The verse conveys the intense compassion and profound pain felt by the Prophet Muhammad for the people who persisted in their disbelief; Allah is comforting him, urging him not to consume himself with despair, and reminding him that his role is to convey the message rather than to force belief, as their rejection is a matter of their own choice for which they will be held accountable, not a failure of his prophetic duty.

translation: Indeed, We have made that which is on the earth adornment for it that We may test them as to which of them is best in deed.
interpretation: Allah has embellished the world with various attractions and worldly possessions to serve as a trial for humanity, assessing whether individuals will be deceived by these fleeting pleasures or if they will remain mindful of their purpose, ultimately choosing to perform righteous deeds that are most sincere and correct for the sake of their hereafter.

translation: And indeed, We will make what is upon it a barren dust.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine reminder of the transitory nature of worldly life, illustrating that all the beauty, adornments, and material structures covering the Earth are fleeting and will ultimately be reduced to barren, unproductive soil by Allah’s command, signifying the inevitable end of earthly existence before the Day of Judgment.

translation: Or have you thought that the companions of the Cave and the Inscription were among Our signs a wonder?
interpretation: Allah is addressing the Prophet Muhammad to emphasize that the story of the People of the Cave is not the most extraordinary of His signs. Rather, the creation of the heavens and the earth, the governance of the universe, and the revelation of the Qur'an itself are far greater proofs of His omnipotence, which makes the miraculous sleep and awakening of these youths merely one manifestation of His absolute power over all things.

translation: When those youths sought refuge in the cave, they said, 'Our Lord, grant us from Yourself mercy and facilitate for us our affair in the right way.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the immense reliance of these young believers upon Allah, demonstrating that true guidance and the success of one's affairs are entirely dependent on divine grace, as they sought shelter not just in a physical space, but in the protection and mercy of their Creator when facing the pressure of their society's corruption.

translation: So We cast a cover over their ears in the cave for a number of years.
interpretation: This verse signifies that Allah caused the sleepers of the cave to enter into a deep, supernatural slumber, rendering them unable to hear any external sounds, which acted as a divine shield protecting them from the disturbances of the outside world throughout their long isolation.

translation: Then We awakened them that We might show which of the two factions was most precise in calculating the duration of their stay.
interpretation: God revived the people of the cave from their long sleep to settle the dispute that had arisen among the people who discovered them; while some speculated on the duration of their slumber, God revealed the reality of the time passed to demonstrate His absolute knowledge and power, thereby silencing the conjectures of men with a clear manifestation of His truth.

translation: We relate to you their story in truth. Indeed, they were youths who believed in their Lord, and We increased them in guidance.
interpretation: God affirms that the account of these young men is transmitted with absolute truth, free from any distortion, serving as a lesson for the believers. It highlights that true spiritual maturity is not determined by age but by the strength of one's faith and the steadfastness of their conviction. When these individuals chose to surrender their hearts to the Creator despite the pressures of their society, God responded to their sincerity by fortifying their spirits with deeper insight, inner peace, and divine firmness, demonstrating that those who strive for truth are granted an ever-increasing measure of celestial guidance.

translation: And We gave strength to their hearts when they stood up and said, 'Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth. Never will we call upon any deity besides Him; otherwise, we would have spoken an outrageous falsehood.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine strengthening granted to the Companions of the Cave, illustrating that when individuals sincerely commit to the oneness of God in the face of immense pressure and societal disbelief, God bestows upon them internal resolve, courage, and spiritual firmness that prevents them from faltering or compromising their monotheistic faith.

translation: These, our people, have taken besides Him deities. Why do they not bring for them a clear authority? And who is more unjust than one who invents about Allah a lie?
interpretation: This verse highlights the absurdity and inherent injustice of idolatry, asserting that those who worship beings other than Allah lack any rational proof or divine authorization for their actions. By challenging them to produce clear evidence, it emphasizes that their beliefs are nothing more than baseless fabrications, and those who attribute partners to the Creator engage in the ultimate act of deception and self-wronging against the objective truth of monotheism.

translation: And when you have withdrawn from them and that which they worship other than Allah, then retreat to the cave. Your Lord will spread for you of His mercy and will prepare for you from your affair facility.
interpretation: This verse signifies that when the believers find themselves in an environment of polytheism and corruption from which they cannot physically or morally escape without compromising their faith, it is an act of spiritual preservation to disassociate from such influences. Seeking refuge in the cave serves as a metaphor for divine protection; by distancing oneself from worldly temptations and falsehoods, the heart becomes a sanctuary where God bestows His grace, transforming a difficult state of isolation into a period of inner growth and eased circumstances.

translation: And you would see the sun, when it rose, inclining away from their cave to the right, and when it set, passing them on the left, while they were in an open space within it. That is from the signs of Allah. Whoever Allah guides is the rightly guided, but whoever He leaves astray - never will you find for him a protecting guide.
interpretation: The verse describes a miraculous divine protection granted to the people of the cave, where Allah caused the sun to shift its trajectory so that it would not enter their cave directly during its rising or setting. This arrangement served to regulate the temperature within their dwelling, ensuring they remained in a temperate environment, thus highlighting Allah's absolute power to command nature for the preservation of His righteous servants and demonstrating that those who are granted divine guidance are shielded from all forms of spiritual and physical harm, while those whom He leaves in error are devoid of any protector or true guide to steer them toward salvation.

translation: And you would think them awake, while they were asleep. And We turned them to the right and to the left, while their dog stretched his forelegs at the entrance. If you had looked at them, you would have turned from them in flight and been filled with terror by them.
interpretation: The awe-inspiring state of the Sleepers of the Cave was divinely orchestrated to prevent anyone from approaching or disturbing them, as their appearance—being alive yet motionless with open eyes—was so formidable that it would strike terror into the heart of any human observer, ensuring their long concealment within the cave until the appointed time of their awakening.

translation: And similarly, We awakened them that they might question one another. Said a speaker among them, 'How long have you remained?' They said, 'We have remained a day or part of a day.' They said, 'Your Lord is most knowing of how long you remained. So send one of you with this silver coin of yours to the city and let him look to which is the best of food and bring you provision from it and let him be cautious and let no one be aware of you.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the miraculous nature of the sleepers' awakening and the disorientation they felt regarding the passage of time, serving as a sign of God's power to resurrect and preserve. Their caution in sending one of their own to the city for food reflects the wisdom and prudence believers should exercise when facing potential hostility, emphasizing that reliance on God does not preclude taking practical measures to ensure safety and secrecy when necessary.

translation: Indeed, if they come to know of you, they will stone you or return you to their religion, and you will never succeed then, ever.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to the believers about the intense enmity and intolerance of the disbelievers, highlighting that their primary goal is either to physically eliminate the believers through execution or to forcefully coerce them into abandoning their faith and reverting to disbelief, stressing that succumbing to such pressure would result in the permanent loss of spiritual salvation and ultimate success.

translation: And in this way We made them known to the people so that they might know that the promise of Allah is true and that there is no doubt about the Hour, when they disputed among themselves about their matter. Then they said, 'Construct a building over them; their Lord is most knowing about them.' Those who prevailed in the matter said, 'We will surely build a place of worship over them.'
interpretation: The revelation of the People of the Cave to the inhabitants of that city served as a manifest sign from Allah to rectify the corrupted beliefs of the people, specifically regarding the resurrection of bodies after death, by proving that the divine promise of the afterlife is an absolute reality. The debate that ensued among the people regarding how to commemorate the sleepers illustrates a human tendency to seek tangible memorials for sacred events, even as the ultimate judgment of their status and the sanctity of their resting place remained known only to Allah, while those in power sought to consecrate the site by establishing a place of worship to honor the memory of these faithful believers.

translation: They will say, 'Three, the fourth of them is their dog,' and they will say, 'Five, the sixth of them is their dog'—guessing at the unseen; and they say, 'Seven, and the eighth of them is their dog.' Say, 'My Lord is most knowing of their number. None knows them except a few.' So do not argue about them except with an obvious argument, and do not inquire about them among them from anyone.
interpretation: The verse clarifies that the varying claims regarding the number of the Sleepers of the Cave—whether three, five, or seven—are largely speculative and based on conjectures rather than certain knowledge. God instructs the Prophet Muhammad to dismiss these trivial debates, as the precise count is unimportant and known only to God and a select few. The command to avoid further inquiry signifies that focusing on historical minutiae diverts from the spiritual essence and the moral lesson of the narrative, which serves as a testament to God's power over life and time.

translation: And never say of anything, 'I shall do such and such tomorrow,'
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine instruction to believers not to assert their ability to perform future actions with absolute certainty, as human life and outcomes are entirely subject to the Will of Allah, emphasizing the necessity of relying on God's permission rather than one's own ego or perceived power.

translation: Except that Allah should will it; and remember your Lord when you have forgotten and say, 'Perhaps my Lord will guide me to what is nearer than this in rectitude.'
interpretation: The verse teaches that human beings should always subordinate their intentions and future plans to the will of Allah, acknowledging their own limitation and forgetfulness. By invoking Allah's name after a lapse of memory, the believer restores their connection to the Divine, and by seeking guidance, they express a humble reliance on Allah to lead them toward paths that are more beneficial, righteous, and truthful than their current expectations.

translation: And they remained in their cave for three hundred years and exceeded by nine.
interpretation: This verse clarifies the duration of the stay of the People of the Cave, stating that they remained in their state of deep sleep for three hundred solar years, which corresponds to three hundred and nine lunar years, highlighting Allah's absolute power to preserve them and control time, while also establishing the specific length of their miraculous concealment as a sign for those who reflect on divine omnipotence.

translation: Say, 'Allah is most knowing of how long they remained. He has [knowledge of] the unseen [aspects] of the heavens and the earth. How seeing is He and how hearing! They have not besides Him any protector, and He shares not His legislation with anyone.'
interpretation: This verse establishes the absolute sovereignty of Allah, asserting that His knowledge encompasses all things, including the duration of the Sleepers of the Cave, which remains beyond human grasp. By emphasizing that Allah possesses perfect sight and hearing, the verse highlights that He does not require assistance or testimony from any created being. Furthermore, it serves as a declaration of Divine Unity in governance, affirming that Allah alone possesses the authority to legislate and command, as He is the only true Protector and Sovereign who brooks no partners in His ultimate decree or judgment.

translation: And recite what has been revealed to you of the Book of your Lord. There is no changer of His words, and never will you find in other than Him a refuge.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine directive to the Prophet Muhammad to remain steadfast in conveying the Quran exactly as it was revealed, emphasizing that God’s words are immutable and perfect, possessing an inherent authority that no human or created being can alter, thereby highlighting that absolute sanctuary and reliance must be directed solely toward Allah, as there is no other place of protection or escape from His decree.

translation: And keep yourself patient [by being] with those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening, seeking His countenance. And let not your eyes pass beyond them, desiring adornments of the worldly life, and do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance and who follows his desire and whose affair is ever [in] neglect.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine directive for the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers to prioritize the company of the sincere, humble worshippers who dedicate their lives to seeking God’s pleasure, regardless of their social standing. It warns against being distracted by the glitter and status of the worldly elite who have become alienated from spiritual truth, emphasizing that true companionship should be based on shared devotion to the Divine rather than the superficial allure of material success, as following those driven by fleeting desires leads only to chaos and spiritual ruin.

translation: And say, 'The truth is from your Lord, so whoever wills - let him believe; and whoever wills - let him disbelieve.' Indeed, We have prepared for the wrongdoers a fire whose walls will surround them. And if they call for relief, they will be relieved with water like murky oil, which scalds [their] faces. Wretched is the drink, and evil is the resting place.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has clarified the truth through His revelation, leaving the choice of faith or disbelief to the individual's free will, while simultaneously warning that those who choose to commit injustice by rejecting the truth will inevitably face the consequences of a severe punishment, illustrating that their ultimate end is a state of total confinement and intense suffering that serves as a grim realization of the outcome of their rejection.

translation: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - indeed, We do not allow to be lost the reward of any who did well in deeds.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine assurance that Allah, in His absolute justice and mercy, keeps a meticulous record of every righteous action performed by a believer, guaranteeing that no sincere effort, regardless of its size, will ever be overlooked or go uncompensated; it emphasizes that true excellence in deeds, characterized by sincerity (Ikhlas) and adherence to divine guidance, creates an unbreakable bond between the servant’s diligence and Allah’s bountiful recompense.

translation: Those will have gardens of perpetual residence; beneath them rivers will flow. They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold and will wear green garments of fine silk and brocade, reclining therein on adorned couches. Excellent is the reward, and good is the resting place.
interpretation: This verse describes the ultimate reward for the believers, illustrating that their recompense is not merely a place of rest, but an environment of sublime beauty, honor, and luxury. By mentioning precious metals like gold and fine fabrics like silk and brocade, the Quran uses imagery of worldly grandeur to signify that in Paradise, the righteous are granted a state of eternal dignity and divine favor, where their physical comfort, represented by reclining on adorned couches, reflects a state of complete spiritual peace and permanent security.

translation: And present to them an example of two men: We granted to one of them two gardens of grapevines, and We bordered them with palm trees and placed between them crops.
interpretation: Allah instructs the Prophet Muhammad to present this parable to the people as a reminder of how worldly possessions can become a source of arrogance; it illustrates a scenario where one man is blessed with abundant agricultural wealth—grapevines, date palms, and grain crops—which serves as a test to see whether he will acknowledge the Giver of these blessings or fall into the delusion that his prosperity is a result of his own merit or an inherent guarantee of his status before God.

translation: Each of the two gardens produced its fruit and did not fall short at all, and We caused a river to gush forth through their midst.
interpretation: The verse illustrates the perfection and abundance of God's provision for the owners of these gardens, emphasizing that the earth yielded its produce completely and without any deficit, while the divine blessing of a constant stream of water ensured the continuous vitality and prosperity of the land.

translation: And he had fruit, so he said to his companion while he was conversing with him, 'I am greater than you in wealth and mightier in [number of] men.'
interpretation: The verse illustrates the psychological trap of arrogance born from worldly abundance; the wealthy man mistakenly equates his material possessions and the number of his supporters with true honor and divine favor, failing to realize that these worldly gains are ephemeral and do not reflect one's actual standing in the sight of God.

translation: And he entered his garden while he was unjust to himself. He said, 'I do not think that this will ever perish.'
interpretation: This verse depicts the state of a person who has become intoxicated by their worldly success and material abundance, leading them to fall into the error of arrogance. By attributing the longevity and fruitfulness of their garden solely to their own efforts or the stability of the physical world, they exhibit a profound lack of spiritual foresight, failing to recognize that all worldly possessions are transient and entirely dependent on the will and decree of God.

translation: And I do not think the Hour will occur. And even if I should be brought back to my Lord, surely I will find better than this as a place of return.
interpretation: The speaker expresses a state of arrogance and delusion, fueled by their worldly success and material abundance, which led them to mistakenly believe that their current status is an indicator of divine favor that will persist in the afterlife, despite their explicit denial of the resurrection and the final accounting.

translation: His companion said to him, while he was dialoguing with him, 'Have you disbelieved in He who created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then fashioned you as a man?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the moral struggle between two companions, where the believer rebukes his wealthy but arrogant associate for his ingratitude and denial of the afterlife. By reminding him of his humble biological origins—starting from dust and then a humble drop of fluid—the believer challenges the companion's pride, arguing that a Creator capable of bringing him into existence from nothingness is surely capable of resurrecting him, and thus, disbelief in the face of such evidence is an act of deep folly and ingratitude.

translation: But as for me, He is Allah, my Lord, and I do not associate with my Lord anyone.
interpretation: This verse represents the declaration of pure monotheism (Tawhid), emphasizing that while others may waver in their faith or attach their hopes to worldly possessions or false idols, the believer anchors their entire existence solely in Allah, recognizing Him as the exclusive Sovereign, Creator, and Sustainer, thereby rejecting all forms of polytheism in worship, reliance, and devotion.

translation: And why did you not, when you entered your garden, say, 'What Allah willed [has occurred]; there is no power except in Allah'? If you see me as less than you in wealth and children,
interpretation: The verse highlights the spiritual requirement for a believer to acknowledge that all blessings, success, and prosperity are entirely dependent upon the will and power of Allah, rather than one's own efforts or status. It serves as a corrective lesson in humility, teaching that when witnessing a bountiful blessing, one should offer the praise of 'Masha'Allah' and 'La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah' to protect one's heart from vanity and pride, and to recognize that true authority and strength belong solely to the Creator, regardless of worldly wealth or family stature.

translation: It may be that my Lord will give me something better than your garden, and will send upon it a calamity from the sky, so it becomes a slippery, barren ground.
interpretation: The speaker expresses a firm conviction in the divine decree, acknowledging that worldly possessions are transient and subject to the will of Allah; he warns his companion that his arrogance regarding his wealth could lead to its total destruction, transforming his flourishing garden into a desolate, unproductive landscape as a consequence of his ingratitude and pride.

translation: Or its water becomes sunken [into the earth], so you would never be able to seek it.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the absolute power of Allah over all worldly blessings, warning that He can withdraw resources like water, which is essential for life and cultivation, at any moment. It serves as a profound reminder of human fragility and the dependency of all creation upon the Divine, highlighting that prosperity is not a permanent human right but a fleeting favor that can vanish, leaving people unable to restore what has been taken away.

translation: And his fruits were encompassed [by ruin], so he began to wring his hands over what he had spent on it, while it had collapsed upon its trellises, and he said, 'Oh, I wish I had not associated with my Lord anyone.'
interpretation: The verse illustrates the inevitable regret of those who invest their hearts and resources in worldly gains while neglecting their relationship with God, showing that when divine retribution strikes and those worldly securities are stripped away, the realization of one's arrogance and misplaced priorities leads to a crushing, irreversible remorse that highlights the futility of polytheism and self-reliance devoid of faith.

translation: And there was no company of people for him to aid him other than Allah, nor was he of those who could defend themselves.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute helplessness of those who rely on worldly power, lineage, or false deities instead of Allah; when the divine decree arrives, all human alliances and material defenses prove utterly useless, revealing that true strength and victory reside solely with the Creator, leaving the arrogant soul completely abandoned and unable to repel any harm that Allah has destined for it.

translation: There, the authority belongs to Allah, the Truth. He is the best in reward and the best in final outcome.
interpretation: This verse affirms that on the Day of Judgment, all power, dominion, and sovereignty will belong exclusively to Allah, without any partners or intermediaries. It serves as a reminder to the believers that seeking His pleasure is the most profitable investment, as His reward for obedience is the ultimate gain, and the final consequence of returning to Him—for those who remained steadfast—is the most excellent and everlasting state of well-being.

translation: And present to them the example of the worldly life: it is like rain which We send down from the sky, and the vegetation of the earth mingles with it and [soon] it becomes dry remnants, scattered by the winds. And ever is Allah, over all things, Perfect in Ability.
interpretation: Allah uses the metaphor of rain-fed vegetation to illustrate the fleeting and transient nature of worldly life; just as lush plants quickly bloom and then wither into dust to be carried away by the wind, the joys, wealth, and status of this world are temporary and will inevitably fade, reminding the believer that true value lies only in what is eternal and that God possesses the ultimate power to bring life and cause decay.

translation: Wealth and children are the adornment of the worldly life. But the enduring good deeds are better to your Lord for reward and better for one's hope.
interpretation: God explains that the worldly possessions people take pride in—namely riches and offspring—are merely temporary decorations that provide comfort and status for a short time; however, these things do not last or provide eternal benefit. True success lies in 'the enduring good deeds,' such as prayer, remembrance of God, and righteous actions, because these deeds persist in their value, bring an everlasting reward in the afterlife, and represent the only secure hope that will not disappoint a believer when they meet their Creator.

translation: And [warn of] the Day when We will remove the mountains and you will see the earth prominent, and We will gather them and not leave behind from among them anyone.
interpretation: This verse depicts the terrifying scenes of the Day of Resurrection, where the mountains, which currently anchor the earth and provide stability, will be uprooted and demolished, leaving the surface of the earth flat, barren, and completely exposed, with nothing to hide the people or provide them shade, signifying the absolute manifestation of Allah's power where no soul will be able to escape the gathering and accounting for their deeds.

translation: And they will be presented before your Lord in rows, [and He will say], 'You have certainly come to Us just as We created you the first time. But you claimed that We would never make an appointment for you.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute power and justice of Allah on the Day of Resurrection, where all of humanity is gathered before Him in total submission. The phrase 'just as We created you the first time' serves as a profound reminder that the One who brought human beings into existence from nothingness is fully capable of resurrecting them. Allah confronts the disbelievers with their past denial of the afterlife, highlighting the folly of their arrogance in assuming that their earthly lives would not culminate in a day of accountability, thereby emphasizing that the promise of the hereafter is an undeniable reality they can no longer ignore.

translation: And the record [of deeds] will be placed [open], and you will see the criminals fearful of that within it, and they will say, 'Oh, woe to us! What is this book that leaves nothing small or great except that it has enumerated it?' And they will find what they did present [before them]. And your Lord does injustice to no one.
interpretation: This verse depicts the scene of the Day of Judgment when the register containing every human action is presented; the criminals will be overwhelmed by profound terror and regret, not because of any falsehood in the record, but because they realize with absolute certainty that the record is perfectly exhaustive and accurate, proving that every fleeting thought and action, no matter how trivial, was captured and preserved, thereby confirming that Divine justice is executed with such absolute precision that no person will be held accountable for a sin they did not commit nor be denied the reward for a good deed they performed.

translation: And when We said to the angels, 'Prostrate to Adam,' so they prostrated, except Iblis. He was of the jinn and departed from the command of his Lord. Then will you take him and his descendants as allies other than Me while they are enemies to you? Wretched it is for the wrongdoers as an exchange.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern divine warning against befriending Satan and his progeny, reminding believers that Iblis's refusal to obey God was a calculated act of rebellion born from arrogance. By highlighting that Iblis belongs to the jinn—beings endowed with free will—the verse clarifies that his disobedience was a choice, not an error. God emphasizes the irrationality of taking an avowed enemy as a guardian or confidant, characterizing such a choice as a self-destructive exchange where the believer abandons the protection of the Creator for the destructive influence of an entity committed to human ruin.

translation: I did not make them witness to the creation of the heavens and the earth or to the creation of themselves, and I would not have taken the misguiders as assistants.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the creation of the universe and humanity is a matter solely known to Allah, as no created being was present to witness it. By explicitly stating that He does not take those who lead others astray as helpers or confidants, Allah clarifies that His decree and governance are entirely independent of created influence, underscoring the absolute monotheistic truth that He alone sustains and directs all existence without needing the counsel of those who reject or distort His path.

translation: And the Day He will say, 'Call My 'partners' whom you claimed,' and they will call them, but they will not respond to them. And We will put between them a barrier of destruction.
interpretation: On the Day of Resurrection, Allah will command the polytheists to call upon the false deities they worshipped alongside Him, hoping these idols might intercede for them or save them from His punishment. However, when the idolaters call out, those idols will prove entirely incapable of responding or offering any aid. Allah will then establish a state of eternal separation and ruin between the worshippers and their worshipped, ensuring that the delusions of the worldly life are shattered and the consequences of their disbelief become an inescapable reality of destruction.

translation: And the criminals will see the Fire and will be certain that they are to fall therein, and they will find no escape from it.
interpretation: This verse depicts the moment of absolute certainty when the disbelievers confront the reality of the afterlife; they realize that the punishment is inevitable and inescapable, leading to a state of utter hopelessness as they witness the place they are destined to occupy, realizing that all their earthly denials cannot shield them from the divine decree.

translation: And We have certainly diversified for the people in this Qur'an from every [kind of] example; but man, more than anything, is [prone to] dispute.
interpretation: The verse highlights the infinite wisdom of Allah in presenting the truth through diverse parables, stories, and metaphors within the Qur'an to make guidance accessible to all intellects, yet it characterizes the inherent nature of man as being prone to argumentation and stubborn questioning, often choosing to debate the clear proofs rather than submitting to the manifest truth.

translation: And nothing has prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them and from asking forgiveness of their Lord except that there should come to them the precedent of the former peoples or that the punishment should come to them face to face.
interpretation: The verse highlights the persistent stubbornness of the disbelievers who refuse to accept the truth and seek repentance despite the clear signs of guidance, noting that their arrogance is so profound that they remain unmoved until they witness the same catastrophic destruction that befell past nations or are confronted directly by the punishment of Allah.

translation: And We send not the messengers except as bringers of good tidings and warners. But those who disbelieve dispute by [using] falsehood to [attempt to] invalidate thereby the truth, and they have taken My signs, and that of which they are warned, in mockery.
interpretation: The verse clarifies that the fundamental role of all messengers sent by God is to provide glad tidings of reward for the righteous and warnings of punishment for the transgressors, rather than performing miracles at the whim of the disbelievers. It further highlights the psychological state of those who reject faith: instead of engaging in honest intellectual inquiry, they consciously employ deceptive arguments and fallacious reasoning to discredit the divine truth, while simultaneously resorting to ridicule and mockery of God’s revelations to mask their inability to refute the truth of the message.

translation: And your Lord is the Forgiving, full of mercy. If He were to impose blame upon them for what they earned, He would have hastened the punishment for them. But they have an appointed time from which they will find no escape.
interpretation: The verse highlights the divine attribute of immense patience, explaining that Allah refrains from immediate retribution despite human transgressions due to His vast mercy and forgiveness, while emphasizing that this delay is not an indication of impunity but rather a respite until a definitive, inescapable moment of accountability.

translation: And those cities, We destroyed them when they committed wrong, and We appointed for their destruction a fixed time.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability of divine justice, illustrating that the destruction of past civilizations was not a spontaneous act but a consequence of their persistent injustice and defiance of truth, occurring only after a set period of respite had elapsed, thereby demonstrating that Allah's governance is rooted in wisdom and measured patience rather than arbitrary punishment.

translation: And mention when Moses said to his servant, 'I will not cease traveling until I reach the junction of the two seas, or I will continue for a very long period.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the immense determination and relentless pursuit of knowledge in the character of Moses. By declaring he would not stop even if it meant traveling for ages, he demonstrates that the quest for spiritual wisdom and hidden truths requires profound sacrifice, patience, and unwavering resolve, setting a model for all seekers of knowledge to persevere despite exhaustion or long distances.

translation: But when they reached the junction between them, they forgot their fish, and it took its way into the sea as a tunnel.
interpretation: This verse signifies a divine sign and a turning point in the journey of Prophet Musa and his companion, where the fish—which was intended to be their meal—miraculously came back to life and entered the sea; this event served as the predetermined indicator or marker set by Allah to guide Musa toward the meeting place with the servant of God, al-Khidr.

translation: So when they had passed beyond [the place], he said to his servant, 'Bring us our morning meal. We have certainly suffered from this journey of ours, [much] fatigue.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the human experience of physical exhaustion even in the pursuit of righteous knowledge and divine assignments, as Moses, despite his prophetic status and his quest to meet the servant of God, reached a point of genuine weariness, illustrating that struggle and fatigue are inherent components of the journey toward truth and spiritual growth.

translation: He said, 'Do you remember when we rested by the rock? Indeed, I forgot the fish—and it was none but Satan who made me forget to mention it—and it took its course into the sea, appearing as a wonder.'
interpretation: The verse illustrates the vulnerability of even the righteous to moments of human forgetfulness, highlighting that spiritual distractions or slip-ups can be attributed to the whispers of Satan, while the miraculous revival and departure of the fish into the sea served as a profound sign of divine intervention meant to guide Musa toward his destined teacher.

translation: He said, 'This is what we were seeking.' So they returned, following their footsteps.
interpretation: This verse depicts the realization of Musa and his companion when they found the specific sign they were searching for—the junction of the two seas where the fish would come back to life—signifying that they had reached the destination ordained by Allah to meet the servant of God, Al-Khidr; thus, they retraced their steps to find the place where they had previously rested, acknowledging that the fulfillment of their objective was in accordance with divine guidance.

translation: And they found a servant from among Our servants to whom We had given mercy from Us and had taught him from Us a [certain] knowledge.
interpretation: This verse describes the meeting between Prophet Musa and the mysterious figure known as Al-Khidr, emphasizing that the unique wisdom possessed by this servant was not acquired through conventional human learning or study, but was a direct divine endowment bestowed by Allah, enabling him to perceive the hidden realities and higher purposes behind events that appear contradictory to outward logic or religious law.

translation: Moses said to him, 'May I follow you on [the condition] that you teach me from what you have been taught of sound judgment?'
interpretation: Moses humbly sought the company of Al-Khidr, recognizing that true knowledge is a gift from God and that even a prophet may need guidance in the hidden, esoteric wisdoms that govern the trials and outcomes of human life.

translation: [Moses] said, 'Indeed, with me you will never be able to have patience.'
interpretation: Al-Khidr cautions Moses that the divine wisdom governing his actions is beyond the scope of human reason and external judgment, indicating that the human psyche, limited by its adherence to apparent causes and outward morality, cannot maintain composure when witnessing events that seem contradictory to established religious laws or common logic.

translation: And how can you have patience for what you do not encompass in knowledge?
interpretation: This verse reflects the pedagogical moment in the story of Moses and Khidr, where human foresight, limited by linear logic and visible outcomes, struggles to accept actions that appear inherently contradictory to divine justice or common sense. It highlights the fundamental limitation of human cognition, which judges based on immediate perceptions, contrasting it with the divine wisdom that operates through a deeper, unseen reality that only God, or those granted divine insight, can fully comprehend.

translation: He said, 'You will find me, if Allah wills, patient, and I will not disobey you in any order.'
interpretation: This verse reflects Musa's profound humility and awareness of his own human limitations. By saying 'if Allah wills,' he acknowledges that his ability to remain patient—a virtue that is difficult to sustain when witnessing actions that seem to contradict apparent justice—is entirely dependent upon the support and decree of God, demonstrating that he relies on divine strength rather than his own willpower alone.

translation: He said, 'Then if you follow me, do not ask me about anything until I make mention of it to you.'
interpretation: This verse signifies the necessity of absolute submission and patience in the pursuit of divine knowledge from a master or teacher, emphasizing that spiritual insight often involves events that appear contradictory or confusing to common logic, requiring the student to refrain from impulsive questioning until the teacher deems the moment appropriate to reveal the hidden wisdom behind his actions.

translation: So they both set out, until when they had embarked on the ship, he damaged it. [Moses] said, 'Have you damaged it to drown its people? You have certainly done a grave thing.'
interpretation: The act of damaging the boat represents the divine wisdom behind seemingly destructive occurrences in life; by creating a minor defect in the vessel, Khidr saved the poor owners from a greater injustice, illustrating that God often allows a small, outwardly negative event to prevent a more catastrophic loss that is hidden from human perception.

translation: He said, 'Did I not tell you that you will not be able to have patience with me?'
interpretation: This verse reflects the pedagogical role of Al-Khidr as he reminds Moses that the nature of his actions follows a divine wisdom that transcends human perception, which naturally triggers a sense of impatience or bewilderment in those who judge events solely by their immediate external appearance rather than their underlying spiritual purpose.

translation: He said, 'Do not blame me for what I forgot, and do not make it difficult for me to fulfill my task.'
interpretation: Musa, peace be upon him, seeks to lower the expectations of his companion by acknowledging his human fallibility, specifically forgetfulness. He humbly requests that this natural limitation not be held against him as a breach of their agreement, while also pleading for ease and leniency in the burden of the companionship and the learning process he is about to undertake.

translation: Then they both set out until they met a boy, and he killed him. Moses said, 'Have you killed a pure soul who has not killed anyone? You have certainly done a repulsive thing.'
interpretation: The verse captures the moment of profound moral shock experienced by Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) when witnessing Al-Khidr kill a youth. Moses, bound by the manifest law of justice and the sanctity of human life, judges the act according to the apparent, objective wrongness of taking an innocent life. This highlights the fundamental tension between the limited human perspective, which perceives events through the lens of observable causes and immediate morality, and the divine perspective, which operates through a transcendent, hidden wisdom that may necessitate events that appear inexplicable or even abhorrent within the framework of worldly justice.

translation: He said, 'Did I not say that you would never be able to bear with me patiently?'
interpretation: Musa (Moses) had explicitly agreed to Khidr's condition of remaining silent and not questioning his actions, yet upon witnessing an act that seemed outwardly contrary to the law or logic, he failed to maintain his composure. This verse highlights the profound spiritual gap between ordinary human reasoning, which is bound by the visible and the immediate, and divine wisdom, which operates based on hidden realities that God has granted to His chosen servants.

translation: He said, 'If I should ask you about anything after this, then do not keep me as a companion. You have already obtained an excuse from me.'
interpretation: Musa (Moses) acknowledges the finality of the conditions set by Al-Khidr, admitting that he has exhausted his capacity for patience regarding the inexplicable actions he witnessed. By stating that he would no longer be a companion if he questioned him again, Musa accepts that he has failed to uphold the agreement and is now providing Al-Khidr with a valid, self-imposed justification to end their journey together, as his own curiosity or inability to perceive the hidden wisdom behind the events has made further instruction impossible.

translation: So they both set out, until when they came to the people of a town, they asked its people for food, but they refused to host them. And they found therein a wall about to collapse, so he set it upright. [Moses] said, 'If you wished, you could have taken payment for it.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the stark contrast between human selfishness and divine wisdom; while the townspeople acted with moral failing by denying hospitality, the traveler corrected a structural defect in the wall without expectation of reward, showing that righteous acts should be performed for their own sake and in accordance with hidden purposes known only to Allah, rather than in response to the treatment received from others.

translation: He said, 'This is the parting between me and you. I will inform you of the interpretation of that over which you could not have patience.'
interpretation: Al-Khidr declares that the time for their companionship has concluded because Musa has exhausted his patience regarding the enigmatic actions he witnessed. Al-Khidr then proceeds to reveal the hidden wisdom and divine purposes behind those actions, demonstrating that what appears externally as injustice or corruption can, in reality, be rooted in mercy and foresight known only through direct revelation or profound spiritual insight.

translation: As for the ship, it belonged to poor people who worked at sea, and I intended to cause a defect in it, for there was a king ahead of them who seized every ship by force.
interpretation: Al-Khidr explains that he damaged the boat not out of malice, but as an act of mercy to save the poor owners' livelihood from a tyrant king who was confiscating all sound and seaworthy vessels for his own use, thereby protecting their humble means of survival through a seemingly destructive act.

translation: And as for the boy, his parents were believers, and we feared that he would overburden them with transgression and disbelief.
interpretation: The divine wisdom behind taking the life of the child was a mercy for his believing parents, as Allah in His foreknowledge knew that if the boy had lived to maturity, his inherent nature and actions would have led him into extreme arrogance and disbelief, which would have consequently caused his righteous parents to suffer intense emotional distress, compromise their faith, or be forced into difficult situations due to his influence.

translation: So we intended that their Lord should replace him for them with one better than him in purity and nearer to affection.
interpretation: This verse reveals the divine wisdom behind the actions of Al-Khidr, who killed the young boy. It explains that Allah, in His perfect knowledge of the unseen, knew that the boy would grow up to be a source of trial and disobedience for his righteous parents. Therefore, Allah decreed his death as a mercy to the parents, intending to replace that child with another who would be more obedient, virtuous, and tender-hearted toward them, thereby preserving their faith and strengthening the bonds of kinship through a more righteous lineage.

translation: And as for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city, and there was beneath it a treasure for them, and their father had been righteous. So your Lord intended that they reach maturity and extract their treasure, as a mercy from your Lord. And I did it not of my own accord. That is the interpretation of that about which you could not have patience.
interpretation: This verse demonstrates the divine principle of intergenerational blessings, where the righteous conduct of a parent serves as a protective shield for their children's future even after the parent has passed away. It highlights that worldly setbacks or seemingly mysterious actions orchestrated by God are rooted in a deep, compassionate wisdom intended to preserve the well-being and rights of the vulnerable until they are mature enough to manage their own affairs.

translation: And they ask you, [O Muhammad], about Dhul-Qarnayn. Say, 'I will recite to you a mention of him.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine introduction to the narrative of a righteous king, indicating that the knowledge of his story was not known to the Prophet Muhammad through his own human learning but was being revealed to him by Allah. The response establishes that the account is intended to be a source of wisdom and reminder, highlighting that the details of his historical journey and his interactions with various nations contain significant moral and spiritual lessons for humanity.

translation: Indeed We established him upon the earth, and We gave him the means to everything.
interpretation: God granted Dhul-Qarnayn great authority, power, and the necessary resources—such as knowledge, technology, and strategic insight—to achieve his objectives and traverse the regions of the earth in order to establish justice and fulfill his divinely ordained mission.

translation: Then he followed a way.
interpretation: This phrase describes a strategic pursuit of knowledge or means by Dhul-Qarnayn, signifying that he did not merely possess power but actively sought out the necessary methods, tools, and logical paths to achieve his objectives, illustrating that success in carrying out one's mission requires both divine guidance and the diligent application of worldly resources and rational planning.

translation: Until, when he reached the setting of the sun, he found it [as if] setting in a spring of dark mud, and he found near it a people. We said, 'O Dhul-Qarnayn, either you punish [them] or else you adopt among them [a way of] goodness.'
interpretation: The verse indicates that when Dhul-Qarnayn reached the westernmost point of his journey, it appeared to his vision as though the sun were sinking into a murky or muddy body of water, describing a natural perspective from the observer's location rather than an astronomical reality. Upon encountering this community, Allah granted him authority and divine guidance, presenting him with a choice: to exercise justice by punishing those who persisted in disbelief and wrongdoing, or to treat them with benevolence and invite them toward righteousness, establishing that true leadership involves the responsibility to balance justice and mercy.

translation: He said: 'As for him who does wrong, we shall punish him, and then he will be brought back to his Lord, and He will punish him with a terrible punishment.'
interpretation: The verse clarifies that the initial punishment mentioned is the earthly consequence or worldly retribution for those who transgress against God and His laws, while the ultimate and definitive punishment resides with God in the afterlife, which will be incomparable in its severity and intensity for those who persist in their denial and injustice.

translation: But as for him who believes and does righteousness, he will have as reward the best [reward], and we will speak to him from our command with ease.
interpretation: This verse signifies that for those who combine sincere faith with righteous deeds, Allah promises the ultimate reward of Paradise, and He will facilitate their affairs and deal with them through leniency, kindness, and ease, both in their worldly obligations and in the reckoning of their deeds.

translation: Then he followed a way.
interpretation: This verse refers to Dhul-Qarnayn, describing how he pursued a course or means to achieve his objectives, signifying that he utilized the knowledge, resources, and strategic planning granted to him by Allah to traverse the earth and fulfill his mission of establishing justice and order.

translation: Until, when he reached the rising of the sun, he found it rising on a people for whom We had not provided any shelter against it.
interpretation: This verse describes Dhul-Qarnayn reaching the furthest eastern point of the inhabited world, where the sun rises upon a civilization that lived in a primitive state, lacking architectural structures, mountains, or thick vegetation that could shield them from the intensity of the sun's direct rays, reflecting their exposure to the natural environment.

translation: Thus, and We have encompassed in knowledge all that he possesses.
interpretation: This verse signifies that Allah's divine knowledge is all-encompassing, meaning He is fully aware of everything that Dhul-Qarnayn possessed—including his strength, his armies, his resources, and the means by which he navigated his affairs—nothing of his circumstances or his inner state remains hidden from the Creator.

translation: Then he followed a way.
interpretation: This verse describes Dhul-Qarnayn as someone who actively sought out the means, resources, and knowledge necessary to fulfill the tasks assigned to him by Allah, demonstrating that success in worldly affairs is achieved through planning, preparation, and utilizing the causes provided by God.

translation: Until, when he reached the space between two mountains, he found beside them a people who could hardly understand any speech.
interpretation: The verse describes Dhul-Qarnayn reaching a remote, secluded location where he encountered a primitive or isolated group of people whose lack of linguistic development or unfamiliarity with external languages made communication with them extremely difficult, requiring him to use signs or other unconventional methods to convey meaning.

translation: They said, 'O Dhu al-Qarnayn, indeed Gog and Magog are corrupters upon the earth. So may we assign for you an expenditure that you might make between us and them a barrier?'
interpretation: The people living near the territory of Gog and Magog recognized their inherent nature of corruption and destruction, and because they were unable to repel them, they sought the assistance of Dhu al-Qarnayn. By offering him a financial tribute or tax, they aimed to secure his immense engineering capabilities and authority to construct a physical fortification that would serve as a permanent containment, preventing the chaos caused by these two groups from reaching their lands.

translation: He said, 'That in which my Lord has established me is better, so assist me with strength; I will make between you and them a barrier.'
interpretation: Dhu al-Qarnayn demonstrates humility and recognition of divine favor by attributing his power and authority entirely to Allah, acknowledging that his capabilities are a gift rather than personal merit; he then calls for collective cooperation, teaching that while God provides the resources and strength, it is incumbent upon humanity to exert physical effort and work together to achieve security and protect the vulnerable from harm.

translation: Bring me blocks of iron until, when he had leveled [them] between the two mountain walls, he said, 'Blow,' until when he made it [like] fire, he said, 'Bring me, that I may pour over it molten copper.'
interpretation: Dhu al-Qarnayn utilized advanced engineering knowledge by creating a structural barrier between two mountains. He stacked iron blocks to match the height of the peaks, then commanded the use of bellows to heat the iron until it reached a state of extreme thermal expansion and glow, after which he poured molten copper over it to seal, solidify, and strengthen the iron, effectively creating an impenetrable, smooth, and durable wall that could withstand external pressure.

translation: So they were not able to scale it, nor were they able to make a breach in it.
interpretation: This verse describes the impenetrable nature of the barrier built by Dhu al-Qarnayn, signifying that the tribe of Gog and Magog, despite their immense numbers and destructive power, were rendered completely incapable of climbing over the smooth, towering wall or piercing through its solid foundation, illustrating the divine protection afforded to the oppressed people through the mastery of engineering and the command of Allah.

translation: He said, 'This is a mercy from my Lord; but when the promise of my Lord comes, He will make it level with the ground; and ever is the promise of my Lord true.'
interpretation: Dhu al-Qarnayn attributes the success of constructing the impenetrable barrier not to his own ingenuity or strength, but solely to the grace and mercy of Allah, while simultaneously acknowledging that this worldly construction is temporary; it is destined to collapse and be leveled to the earth on the Day of Resurrection or when the portents of the Hour arrive, emphasizing that human achievements are fleeting compared to the absolute, unwavering truth of Allah's decree.

translation: And We will leave some of them on that day surging over others, and the Horn will be blown, and We will gather them all together.
interpretation: This verse describes the chaotic state of humanity on the Day of Judgment, where people will be in such profound distress and upheaval that they will collide and interact like waves of a turbulent sea, lacking any order or direction, until the final trumpet blast brings all of creation together before Allah for the ultimate reckoning.

translation: And We will present Hell, that Day, to the disbelievers, fully exposed.
interpretation: On the Day of Resurrection, God will manifest Hell in such a tangible and terrifying manner that it will be made visible and manifest before the disbelievers, so that they may witness the reality of the punishment they had previously denied, leaving them with no doubt or escape.

translation: Those whose eyes were behind a veil from My remembrance and they were not able to hear.
interpretation: This verse describes the state of the disbelievers whose hearts were veiled from perceiving the signs of Allah in the universe and whose ears were incapacitated from truly listening to the truth, signifying that their persistent rejection and arrogance resulted in a spiritual blindness and deafness that prevented them from accepting guidance.

translation: Do those who disbelieve think that they can take My servants as protectors instead of Me? Indeed, We have prepared Hell as a lodging for the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning against the folly of those who elevate created beings—whether idols, prophets, or righteous people—to the status of partners with Allah or as intermediaries worthy of worship. It emphasizes that no creature possesses the power to protect or benefit anyone against the will of the Creator. The consequence of this theological error, which misplaces loyalty and worship, is a destined abode in Hell, highlighting that true sovereignty and protection belong to Allah alone, and assigning these divine attributes to others is a fundamental rejection of the truth that leads to spiritual ruin.

translation: Say, 'Shall we inform you of the greatest losers as to their deeds?'
interpretation: This verse serves as a rhetorical warning meant to capture the attention of the audience, highlighting that the ultimate loss is not in worldly wealth or status, but in the vanity of religious effort that is divorced from truth, sincerity, or proper guidance.

translation: Those whose effort is lost in the life of this world, while they think that they are doing good work.
interpretation: This verse describes individuals who exert immense effort and perform deeds with the misguided belief that their actions are righteous and pleasing to God, yet their efforts are ultimately futile because they are devoid of true faith, sincerity, or alignment with divine guidance, leading them to be deluded about the spiritual value of their conduct.

translation: Those are the ones who disbelieved in the verses of their Lord and in their meeting [with Him], so their deeds have become worthless; and We will not assign to them on the Day of Resurrection any importance.
interpretation: The verse indicates that the rejection of Allah's signs and the denial of the inevitable encounter with Him on the Day of Judgment render all worldly deeds void of any spiritual value. Because their core belief, which serves as the foundation for the acceptance of deeds, is absent, their efforts—no matter how grand they may appear—carry no weight or significance in the scales of divine justice on the Day of Resurrection, resulting in their complete loss and insignificance before Allah.

translation: That is their recompense, Hell, because they disbelieved and took My verses and My messengers in ridicule.
interpretation: This verse explains that the ultimate consequence for the deniers is the Fire of Hell, which is a fitting retribution for their two primary transgressions: their rejection of the truth despite clear evidence, and their blatant mockery of the divine signs and the prophets sent to guide them, an act that demonstrates their profound arrogance and lack of respect for the sanctity of God's message.
