translation: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - they will have the Gardens of Paradise as a lodging.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the ultimate reward for those who combine sincere faith in their hearts with virtuous actions in their lives is the highest level of Paradise, which serves as their eternal home and honorable reception from their Lord, highlighting that entry into such a lofty rank is granted only to those who consistently aligned their outward conduct with their inward belief.

translation: Abiding therein eternally, they will not desire any change from it.
interpretation: This verse describes the ultimate contentment of the people of Paradise, illustrating that their state of bliss is so perfect and complete that the human tendency to seek transition or transformation—a common trait in worldly life driven by dissatisfaction or boredom—is entirely removed from their souls, leaving them in a state of eternal, undisturbed satisfaction.

translation: Say, 'If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would be exhausted before the words of my Lord were exhausted, even if We brought the like of it as a supplement.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the infinite nature of Allah's knowledge, wisdom, and creative decrees. By using the metaphor of the entire ocean serving as ink to record the Words of Allah, the Quran emphasizes that His speech and the realities He brings into existence are boundless. Even if the sea were multiplied many times over, it would dry up completely long before His words—encompassing His decrees, knowledge, and perfect attributes—could ever be fully documented or comprehended, highlighting the absolute transcendence of the Divine over the limitations of the created world.

translation: Say, 'I am only a man like you, to whom it has been revealed that your god is one God. So whoever would hope for the meeting with his Lord - let him do righteous work and not associate in the worship of his Lord anyone.'
interpretation: The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, is instructed to emphasize his shared humanity to clarify that his authority comes strictly from Divine revelation, not from any inherent supernatural nature; he serves as a model who demonstrates that the path to salvation and encountering God is attainable for all people through two essential pillars: the performance of righteous deeds performed with sincerity, and the complete devotion of worship exclusively to the One Creator without attributing divinity to any other created being.

translation: Kaf-Ha-Ya-'Ayn-Sad
interpretation: These are abbreviated letters (al-muqatta'at) whose true meaning is known only to Allah, though they are widely understood to serve as a challenge to the eloquence of the Arabs and a testament to the miraculous nature of the Qur'an, which is composed of the same letters they use in their own language yet remains inimitable.

translation: A mention of the mercy of your Lord upon His servant Zakariya.
interpretation: This verse serves as a gentle introduction, inviting the believer to reflect upon the profound divine mercy bestowed upon Prophet Zakariya in his old age, demonstrating that Allah is capable of answering prayers and granting miracles even when human logic suggests otherwise.

translation: When he called to his Lord with a private call.
interpretation: This verse highlights the sincerity and humility of Prophet Zakariyya in his devotion; by calling upon Allah in secret, he demonstrated a profound level of intimacy and trust, showing that he sought an audience with the Creator that was free from the vanity or performance often associated with public declarations, thus teaching the believer that the most profound supplications are those whispered from the depths of the heart.

translation: He said, 'My Lord, indeed my bones have weakened, and my head has flared with white hair, and never have I been, in my supplication to You, my Lord, unhappy.'
interpretation: Prophet Zakariyya (peace be upon him) is expressing his complete frailty and advanced age to Allah, using these physical signs of weakness not to complain, but to emphasize that he is turning to the Only One who can grant him his request despite his human limitations, highlighting that his lifelong habit of calling upon Allah has never resulted in disappointment or exclusion from divine mercy.

translation: And indeed, I fear the successors after me, and my wife has been barren, so give me from Yourself an heir.
interpretation: Zakariya (peace be upon him) felt a profound concern regarding the future of his mission and the preservation of the divine message after his passing, fearing that his kinsmen lacked the piety or capability to uphold the truth. His plea to Allah was not born of mere worldly inheritance, but of a spiritual longing for a successor who would inherit the legacy of prophecy, ensuring that the guidance he carried would not be lost or corrupted by those who were unfit to lead the community in righteousness.

translation: Who will inherit from me and inherit from the family of Jacob, and make him, my Lord, pleasing [to You].
interpretation: Prophet Zakariya is asking Allah for a successor who will inherit not worldly wealth, but the legacy of Prophethood, spiritual knowledge, and the divine wisdom bestowed upon the lineage of Prophet Yaqub, while praying that this heir may possess righteous character and qualities that are entirely acceptable and beloved to Allah.

translation: O Zechariah, indeed We give you good tidings of a boy whose name will be John. We have not assigned to any such name before.
interpretation: This verse signifies that Allah granted Zechariah a son named John, emphasizing that this name was unique and had never been bestowed upon anyone previously, serving as a divine mark of distinction and a miracle to affirm the special status of this child.

translation: He said, 'My Lord, how will I have a son when my wife has been barren and I have reached extreme old age?'
interpretation: Prophet Zakariyya, upon him be peace, was not doubting the omnipotence of Allah, but rather expressing his profound astonishment at the manifestation of a miracle that defied the conventional laws of biology and nature, as he was old and his wife was infertile.

translation: He said, 'Thus it is; your Lord says, It is easy for Me, for I created you before, when you were nothing.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine reassurance to Zakariya, highlighting that the manifestation of miracles—such as the birth of a child to an elderly couple—is fundamentally effortless for the Creator, whose power is absolute and unbound by the natural laws He established; by reminding him of his own initial creation from nothingness, Allah emphasizes that the origination of life is far more complex than the continuation or renewal of it, thereby silencing any human doubt regarding the limitlessness of Divine capability.

translation: He said, 'My Lord, make for me a sign.' He said, 'Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three nights, [being] sound.'
interpretation: God granted Zechariah a miraculous sign as a physical proof of the impending birth of his son, John; this sign was a temporary inability to speak to others despite remaining in perfect health, which served as a call for him to engage in glorification and remembrance of God during this period of silent reflection.

translation: Then he came out to his people from the sanctuary and signaled to them to glorify [Allah] morning and evening.
interpretation: This verse describes Prophet Zakariya (peace be upon him) emerging from his place of prayer after receiving the glad tidings of his son Yahya, communicating through signs that his people should engage in the constant remembrance and glorification of Allah during the earliest and latest parts of the day, as these times are the most significant for spiritual devotion and divine connection.

translation: O Yahya, take the Scripture with determination, and We gave him wisdom while yet a child.
interpretation: This verse signifies that Allah commanded Yahya (John) to firmly uphold the Torah, to adhere strictly to its laws, and to apply its teachings with sincere dedication and strength of will, while simultaneously bestowing upon him divine knowledge, sound judgment, and profound understanding of the faith from his very childhood.

translation: And affection from Us and purity, and he was fearing of Allah.
interpretation: This verse describes the gift of divine mercy and inner spiritual purification bestowed upon the prophet Yahya (John) by Allah, which enabled him to possess a heart full of compassion for His creation and to maintain a state of profound God-consciousness, ensuring that his actions remained untainted by sin and oriented entirely toward righteousness.

translation: And [he was] dutiful to his parents, and he was not a tyrant or disobedient.
interpretation: This verse describes the refined character of Prophet Yahya, emphasizing that his righteousness was not limited to his devotion to God but extended to his conduct toward his parents, characterized by deep kindness, obedience, and humility, while remaining entirely free from the arrogance of a tyrant or the defiance of a rebellious soul.

translation: And peace be on him the day he was born and the day he dies and the day he is raised alive.
interpretation: This verse signifies that Allah grants security and tranquility to the Prophet Yahya (John) across the three critical stages of his existence—his birth, his death, and his resurrection—ensuring that he is protected from the fear, distress, and punishment that typically accompany these transitions, thereby affirming his honored status and safety from divine wrath.

translation: And mention, [O Muhammad], in the Book [the story of] Mary, when she withdrew from her family to a place toward the East.
interpretation: This verse signifies Mary's devotion and her pursuit of seclusion to dedicate herself entirely to the worship of Allah; by physically moving away from the social distractions and worldly concerns of her people toward a place in the East, she sought a space of purity and spiritual focus, marking the beginning of her preparation for the miraculous events that would follow.

translation: And she took, apart from them, a screen. Then We sent to her Our Spirit, and he represented himself to her as a well-proportioned man.
interpretation: The verse describes the moment the angel Jibril (Gabriel) appeared to Maryam (Mary) in human form to deliver the divine decree regarding the birth of Isa (Jesus). By taking a screen, Maryam was seeking privacy to attend to her spiritual purity and modesty; the appearance of the angel in the form of a 'well-proportioned man' was a necessary manifestation to facilitate human communication, testing her faith and obedience while ensuring the message of the impending miraculous conception was conveyed clearly.

translation: She said: 'I seek refuge in the Most Gracious from you, if you are God-fearing.'
interpretation: When Maryam (Mary) saw the angel Jibril (Gabriel) appearing to her in the form of a perfect man, she instinctively sought the protection of Allah, the Most Gracious, to safeguard her chastity and honor. She added the conditional phrase 'if you are God-fearing' as a final appeal to his conscience, hoping that if he truly possessed piety and a sense of duty toward God, he would be deterred from causing her any harm or evil.

translation: He said, 'I am only a messenger from your Lord to give you a pure son.'
interpretation: The angel Jibril, sent by Allah, informs Maryam that he is merely a conduit of divine decree, sent to bestow upon her a son who is purified from sins, endowed with righteousness, and blessed with sanctity, highlighting that this miraculous birth occurs solely by the command and power of Allah rather than through any human agency.

translation: She said, 'How can I have a boy while no man has touched me and I have not been unchaste?'
interpretation: Maryam expresses her astonishment at the news of a child, not out of doubt regarding Allah's power, but out of wonder at the miraculous process by which he would be created, given that she had never been with a man in a lawful marriage, nor had she ever committed any act of immorality, thus maintaining her purity and status as a chaste woman.

translation: He said, 'Thus it is; your Lord says, It is easy for Me, and [We will make him] a sign to the people and a mercy from Us. And it is a matter already decreed.'
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that the birth of Jesus to Mary without a father is not an outcome of natural cause and effect, but a direct manifestation of God's limitless power. By stating that the event is 'easy' for Him, Allah silences human doubt regarding logical impossibility, demonstrating that the laws of nature are subservient to the Divine Will. Furthermore, the event is framed not merely as a miracle, but as a deliberate act of mercy and a foundational sign intended to guide humanity toward the recognition of God’s sovereignty and creative authority.

translation: So she conceived him, and she withdrew with him to a remote place.
interpretation: This verse depicts the moment Maryam (Mary) secluded herself from her people to avoid the inevitable scandal and social scrutiny regarding her pregnancy, choosing a distant, solitary location to endure the pains of childbirth and the weight of her unique divine trial in privacy.

translation: Then the birth pains drove her to the trunk of a palm tree. She said, 'Oh, I wish I had died before this and was in oblivion, forgotten!'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the intensity of Maryam's psychological and physical distress as she faced the miracle of childbirth in solitude. Her cry is not a challenge to divine decree, but rather an expression of human agony and the overwhelming fear of societal scandal, reflecting the immense burden she felt while carrying the responsibility of a miraculous birth in a world that would struggle to comprehend it.

translation: But he called to her from below her, 'Do not grieve; your Lord has provided beneath you a stream.'
interpretation: The verse highlights the divine mercy bestowed upon Maryam (Mary) during her labor in isolation, illustrating how Allah eases the hardships of the righteous by providing sustenance and comfort from sources they did not anticipate, signifying that even in moments of profound loneliness and physical distress, the believer is under the protective care and providence of their Creator.

translation: And shake toward you the trunk of the palm tree; it will drop upon you ripe, fresh dates.
interpretation: This verse signifies that while Allah provides for His servants miraculously, He also teaches them the necessity of taking active, physical steps—no matter how seemingly small or inadequate—as a means to attain their sustenance, demonstrating that reliance on God (Tawakkul) and human effort work in tandem.

translation: So eat and drink and be glad; and if you see any human, say, 'Indeed, I have vowed a fast to the Most Merciful, so I will not speak today to any man.'
interpretation: Allah instructed Maryam to find solace and comfort in the provision He provided, while simultaneously commanding her to observe a vow of silence from worldly discourse. By directing her to tell anyone who approached her that she was fasting, Allah provided her with a divine strategy to protect her from the gossip and disbelief of the people, effectively shifting the burden of defending her purity from her own speech to the miraculous intervention of God, as she would soon rely on her infant son to speak on her behalf.

translation: Then she brought him to her people, carrying him. They said, 'O Mary, you have certainly done a thing unprecedented.'
interpretation: When Maryam returned to her community while carrying the infant Jesus, her people—who were aware of her known piety and chastity—were shocked and bewildered by her situation; they exclaimed that she had committed a grave and monstrous transgression, viewing the appearance of a child without a father as an act of inconceivable deviation from moral standards, not yet aware of the miraculous nature of his birth.

translation: O sister of Aaron, your father was not a man of evil, nor was your mother unchaste.
interpretation: When the people of Maryam saw her returning with a child, they expressed their shock by comparing her to her brother Aaron—who was known for his piety and righteousness—as well as her parents, who were known for their virtue, thereby implying that such an act of bearing a child out of wedlock was entirely inconsistent with the noble lineage and moral upbringing she had received.

translation: Then she pointed to him. They said, 'How can we speak to one who is a child in the cradle?'
interpretation: When the people of Maryam questioned her about the child, she followed Allah's command to remain silent and simply pointed toward the infant 'Isa, thereby signaling that he would be the one to respond on her behalf and vindicate her purity, leaving the people in disbelief because they deemed it impossible for an infant to speak or provide a rational answer.

translation: [Jesus] said, 'Indeed, I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet.'
interpretation: In these words, Prophet Isa (Jesus) declares his true nature and mission upon the start of his speaking in the cradle; by affirming his status as a servant of Allah, he explicitly refutes any claims of divinity, asserting that his miraculous existence, the divine revelation he received, and his prophethood are all gifts bestowed upon him by his Creator, thereby establishing the fundamental principle of monotheism and his own role as a messenger sent to guide humanity.

translation: And He has made me blessed wherever I may be, and has enjoined upon me prayer and charity as long as I remain alive.
interpretation: This verse signifies that Allah has endowed Prophet Isa (Jesus) with the capacity to be a source of benefit, guidance, and goodness to those around him in every place and time, while establishing a constant covenant with him to maintain the pillars of worship and social responsibility—prayer, representing the connection between the servant and the Creator, and Zakat, representing the duty of compassion toward the creation—as long as his life continues, indicating that one's state of blessing is inextricably linked to the steadfast performance of religious obligations.

translation: And [He has made me] dutiful to my mother, and He has not made me a tyrant, miserable.
interpretation: The speaker, Prophet Isa (Jesus), highlights that his righteousness is manifested through his kindness and obedience toward his mother, Maryam, and that his character is defined by humility and submission to Allah, which shields him from the arrogance of tyrants and the spiritual wretchedness that comes from distancing oneself from divine grace.

translation: And peace is on me the day I was born and the day I will die and the day I am raised alive.
interpretation: This verse signifies the divine declaration of safety, security, and mercy bestowed upon the Prophet Isa (Jesus) by Allah throughout the three critical stages of his existence: his entry into this world, his transition through death, and his ultimate resurrection. It serves as an affirmation that he remains under the protection and peace of his Creator, untainted by the tribulations or fear associated with these transitions, ultimately declaring his servitude to Allah and the inherent sanctity of his mission.

translation: That is Jesus, the son of Mary - the word of truth about which they are in dispute.
interpretation: This verse asserts that the previously mentioned narrative concerning Jesus is the absolute, irrefutable truth, standing in stark contrast to the baseless conjectures, fabrications, and conflicting theological debates held by those who doubt his true nature and mission.

translation: It is not for Allah to take a son; exalted is He! When He decrees an affair, He only says to it, 'Be,' and it is.
interpretation: This verse asserts the absolute transcendence of Allah, clarifying that the notion of Him having a child is incompatible with His divine nature and majesty. By describing His creative act as an instantaneous command ('Be' and it is), the verse emphasizes His total sovereignty and infinite power, suggesting that because all existence is brought into being by His simple will, the concept of procreation—which implies a biological or relational necessity—is entirely alien to the Creator, who stands independent of any physical or social limitations.

translation: And indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. That is a straight path.
interpretation: This verse establishes the foundational principle of monotheism, declaring that the Creator of the speaker and the listeners is one and the same, which necessitates that devotion, obedience, and worship be directed exclusively toward Him alone, as this recognition and practice constitute the correct and unwavering path that leads directly to God's pleasure and salvation.

translation: Then the factions differed among themselves, so woe to those who disbelieved from the spectacle of a Great Day.
interpretation: The disagreement among the factions refers to their conflicting opinions regarding the nature of Jesus, with some claiming he is God and others claiming he is the son of God, all of which are falsehoods that deviate from the truth of his servitude to Allah; thus, the warning of a 'Great Day' serves as a reminder that all those who reject the truth and adhere to these fabricated distortions will face severe punishment when they witness the undeniable reality of the Day of Judgment.

translation: How clearly they will hear and see on the Day they come to Us. But the wrongdoers today are in manifest error.
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound regret and sudden realization that the disbelievers will experience on the Day of Resurrection, when their senses—which they previously ignored or misused in worldly life to deny the truth—will become acute and undeniable, revealing the reality they once mocked. Despite their stubborn arrogance in this world, they will find themselves utterly exposed and lost, forced to acknowledge the truth of the afterlife at a time when their realization no longer benefits their souls, emphasizing the tragic consequence of having lived in blatant deviation from the guidance of Allah.

translation: And warn them, [O Muhammad], of the Day of Regret, when the matter will have been decided; and [yet] they are in [a state of] heedlessness, and they do not believe.
interpretation: This verse warns humanity about the inevitable Day of Judgment, a time characterized by deep remorse because the final verdict will have been issued and the opportunity for repentance or change will have passed forever, leaving those who chose to live in persistent ignorance and disbelief facing the consequences of their rejection of the truth.

translation: Indeed, it is We who will inherit the earth and whoever is on it, and to Us they will be returned.
interpretation: This verse serves as a profound reminder of the ultimate transience of human life and possessions; it affirms that all things belong exclusively to Allah, and as the Creator, He remains the sole possessor when all created beings perish and return to Him for judgment, emphasizing that power, ownership, and sovereignty belong only to Him at the end of time.

translation: And mention in the Book [the story of] Abraham. Indeed, he was a man of truth and a prophet.
interpretation: The verse commands the Prophet Muhammad to remind his people of Abraham, highlighting his two most noble qualities: his absolute sincerity and honesty in faith and deeds, which reached the peak of truthfulness, and his status as a prophet chosen by God to receive revelation and guide humanity. This serves to remind the polytheists that the monotheistic religion they claim to follow is the same one held by their righteous forefather, whose integrity and prophethood remain an undisputed standard for all believers.

translation: When he said to his father, 'O my father, why do you worship that which does not hear and does not see and will not benefit you at all?'
interpretation: Ibrahim (peace be upon him) uses a rational and gentle approach to challenge his father's idolatry, highlighting the inherent helplessness of idols by pointing out their lack of sensory perception and power, thereby inviting his father to reflect on the absurdity of devoting worship to objects that can neither provide aid nor ward off harm.

translation: O my father, indeed there has come to me of knowledge that which has not come to you, so follow me, I will guide you to an even path.
interpretation: Prophet Ibrahim addresses his father with profound gentleness and wisdom, using the invitation to follow him not as a display of arrogance, but as a sincere appeal to truth; he emphasizes that the divine revelation and knowledge he has received is a light that can rescue his father from his state of ignorance and guide him toward the straight path of monotheism and spiritual rectitude.

translation: O my father, do not worship Satan. Indeed Satan has ever been, to the Most Merciful, disobedient.
interpretation: Ibrahim (peace be upon him) addresses his father with utmost gentleness and compassion, warning him that following the path of polytheism and straying from the worship of the One God is effectively an act of obedience to Satan, who is the ultimate rebel against the Creator, and therefore, by persisting in this defiance, the father risks distancing himself from the infinite mercy and grace of Allah.

translation: O my father, indeed I fear that there will touch you a punishment from the Most Merciful so that you would be to Satan a companion [in hell].
interpretation: In this verse, Prophet Ibrahim is expressing deep filial compassion mixed with profound spiritual concern for his father. By using the word 'Rahman' (The Most Merciful), he is highlighting the irony and tragedy of his father's situation: that by rejecting the path of the One who is inherently Merciful, he is actively inviting a state of estrangement from that mercy, which inevitably leads to falling under the dominion and misguided companionship of Satan.

translation: He said, 'Have you no desire for my gods, O Abraham? If you do not desist, I will surely stone you, so leave me for a prolonged time.'
interpretation: This verse portrays the confrontation between Prophet Abraham and his father, where the father resorts to threats of physical violence and expulsion as a defense mechanism for his false idols because he lacks logical arguments to counter Abraham's call to monotheism. The father's demand for Abraham to leave him is an expression of his frustration and desire to sever ties rather than engage with the undeniable truth of God's oneness, signaling that his commitment to tradition and idolatry outweighed his willingness to contemplate the reality of the Creator.

translation: [Abraham] said, Peace be upon you. I will ask forgiveness for you of my Lord. Indeed, He is ever gracious to me.
interpretation: This verse reflects the exemplary character of Prophet Abraham, who responded to his father's hostility and threats of violence with profound gentleness, patience, and a prayer for his guidance, demonstrating that the believer's duty is to maintain noble conduct and persistent kindness even when faced with the harshness of those who reject the truth.

translation: And I will withdraw from you and that which you invoke other than Allah and will invoke my Lord; I hope that I will not be unhappy in my invocation to my Lord.
interpretation: Prophet Ibrahim declares his complete detachment from his people's polytheistic practices and false deities, placing his full trust in Allah alone, while expressing his humble confidence that by directing his prayers exclusively to the Creator, he will attain spiritual fulfillment and mercy rather than the misery and disappointment that inevitably follow the worship of powerless beings.

translation: So when he had isolated himself from them and what they worshipped besides Allah, We bestowed upon him Isaac and Jacob, and We made each of them a prophet.
interpretation: When Abraham fulfilled his commitment to abandon the polytheists and their false deities for the sake of Allah, he achieved a state of complete spiritual detachment from falsehood. As a reward for this sincere renunciation and his steadfast devotion, Allah granted him righteous progeny—Isaac and Jacob—who were not only his physical descendants but were also chosen to inherit the mission of prophethood, thereby demonstrating that true abandonment of worldly attachments for Allah's pleasure results in divine blessings and the elevation of one's legacy through faith.

translation: And We bestowed upon them of Our mercy, and We granted them a reputation of honor and truthfulness that would persist on the tongues of those who came after them.
interpretation: This verse signifies that because of the righteous actions and steadfast devotion of the prophets and the righteous, Allah bestows upon them a lasting legacy of praise and high esteem in the hearts and speech of succeeding generations. It indicates that those who remain sincere to their faith are rewarded not only with spiritual blessings in the afterlife but also with an enduring, virtuous influence and a legacy of noble memory that inspires goodness long after their departure from the world.

translation: And mention in the Book, Moses. Indeed, he was chosen, and he was a messenger and a prophet.
interpretation: The verse highlights the high status of Prophet Moses, emphasizing that his sincerity and devotion to God were the foundational qualities that qualified him for his dual role as both a messenger, conveying God's law to the people, and a prophet, receiving direct divine inspiration.

translation: And We called to him from the right side of the Mount and brought him near, confiding.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the extraordinary honor bestowed upon Prophet Musa, signifying that Allah drew him close through a private and intimate revelation. The term 'najiyya' implies a secret or confidential discourse, highlighting the elevated spiritual proximity and direct communication granted to him during his encounter at Mount Sinai, where he was singled out for a unique conversation with the Divine, transcending the ordinary limits of prophetic revelation.

translation: And We bestowed upon him out of Our mercy his brother Aaron as a prophet.
interpretation: This verse highlights that prophethood is a divine favor and a mercy from Allah, bestowed upon whom He wills. By granting Moses his brother Aaron as a companion, Allah provided him with essential support and strength in his mission, demonstrating that Allah addresses the needs of His messengers by providing them with the necessary resources and spiritual companionship to carry out their heavy responsibilities.

translation: And mention in the Book, Ishmael. Indeed, he was true to his promise, and he was a messenger and a prophet.
interpretation: This verse highlights the noble character of Prophet Ishmael, specifically emphasizing his unwavering integrity and reliability. By describing him as 'true to his promise,' the Qur'an underscores that his faithfulness was not merely a casual trait but a foundational aspect of his prophetic identity, serving as an enduring moral example for believers to honor their commitments and remain steadfast in their word regardless of the circumstances.

translation: And he used to enjoin on his people prayer and zakah and was to his Lord pleasing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of leadership and responsibility within one's own household, indicating that true righteousness is not merely a private matter but involves actively guiding those under one's care toward religious obligations, thereby earning the divine approval and pleasure of God through both personal piety and the moral development of one's family.

translation: And mention in the Book, Idris. Indeed, he was a man of truth and a prophet.
interpretation: Allah commands His Messenger to remind his people of the story of the Prophet Idris, describing him as a truthful person who attained the highest level of honesty in his speech and actions, coupled with the status of prophethood, thereby serving as an example for believers to emulate in righteousness and devotion.

translation: And We raised him to a high station.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Prophet Idris, indicating that Allah elevated his status, honor, and rank in both this world and the Hereafter, granting him a position of great proximity and nobility in the sight of the Creator.

translation: Those were the ones upon whom Allah bestowed favor from among the prophets of the descendants of Adam and of those We carried [in the ship] with Noah, and of the descendants of Abraham and Israel, and of those whom We guided and chose. When the verses of the Most Merciful were recited to them, they fell in prostration and weeping.
interpretation: The verse highlights the spiritual state of those whom Allah has chosen and guided; their deep reverence and humility are manifested physically and emotionally whenever they hear the word of God. By falling in prostration and weeping, they demonstrate a profound awareness of the majesty of the Creator and the gravity of His revelations, showing that true guidance leads not to arrogance, but to a heart that softens and humbles itself in total submission to the Divine truth.

translation: But there came after them successors who neglected prayer and pursued desires; so they are going to meet evil.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning about the decline of faith in future generations, highlighting that the primary indicator of spiritual decay is the abandonment or negligence of the ritual prayer, which inevitably leads to the pursuit of transient worldly desires and, ultimately, a state of profound loss and severe consequence in the afterlife.

translation: Except for those who repent, believe, and do righteousness; for they will enter Paradise and will not be wronged at all.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the boundless mercy of Allah, asserting that even those who have committed grave sins are not beyond redemption if they sincerely turn back to God, embrace faith with conviction, and manifest that faith through virtuous deeds. The promise of entry into Paradise and the assurance that they will not be wronged—meaning their good deeds will be rewarded in full without any reduction or injustice—serves as a divine guarantee that genuine repentance effectively erases past transgressions and secures a favorable outcome in the afterlife.

translation: Gardens of perpetual residence which the Most Merciful has promised His servants in the unseen. Indeed, His promise is ever coming.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the reward of Paradise is not merely a metaphor but a tangible, guaranteed reality that awaits those who believed in Allah and His unseen promises while they were still in this world, demonstrating that the certainty of His decree ensures its manifestation as an inevitable truth for the righteous.

translation: They will not hear therein any ill speech or commission of sin—only a saying, 'Peace, peace.' And they will have their provision therein, morning and evening.
interpretation: This verse describes the refined and peaceful atmosphere of Paradise, where the inhabitants are shielded from the vain, harmful, or distracting speech that characterizes worldly interactions. The repetition of 'peace' signifies a state of absolute security and tranquility where every word exchanged between the believers or directed toward them is pure, comforting, and free from discord. The mention of provision 'morning and evening' indicates a perpetual, delightful, and regular bestowal of sustenance, symbolizing that the dwellers of Paradise will experience a constant cycle of abundance and gratification without the anxieties of scarcity or time.

translation: That is the Paradise which We shall grant as an inheritance to those of Our servants who were pious.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that admission into Paradise is not granted arbitrarily, but is the rightful inheritance reserved for those who demonstrated constant God-consciousness and righteousness in their worldly lives; thus, piety serves as the essential condition and the qualifying act that secures one's place in the eternal abode of divine grace.

translation: And we [angels] descend not except by the command of your Lord. To Him belongs that which is before us and that which is behind us and what is in between. And never is your Lord forgetful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute subordination of the angels to the Divine Will, clarifying that their actions and appearances are not spontaneous but occur strictly by God's permission. By stating that God possesses everything past, future, and the present, it underscores His all-encompassing sovereignty and control over time and space, providing comfort to the Prophet Muhammad that divine delays or the timing of revelations are calculated according to God's eternal knowledge and wisdom, rather than any lapse of memory or negligence on the part of the Creator.

translation: [He is] Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, so worship Him and have patience for His worship. Do you know of any name for Him?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that God is the sole Creator and Sustainer of the entire universe, and therefore, He is the only one worthy of worship. The command to 'have patience' in His worship implies that adhering to a life of devotion requires persistence and endurance against the difficulties and temptations of the world. By rhetorically asking if there is any other who shares His name or attributes, the verse asserts the absolute uniqueness and incomparability of God, reinforcing that there is no other deity that possesses His majesty or deserves the devotion of His servants.

translation: And the human being says, 'When I have died, will I be brought forth alive?'
interpretation: The verse depicts the stance of a disbeliever who expresses astonishment and skepticism regarding the possibility of resurrection after death, reflecting their denial of the afterlife and their reliance solely on material evidence that suggests the permanent cessation of life upon expiration.

translation: Does man not remember that We created him before, when he was nothing?
interpretation: This verse serves as a rhetorical reminder to the human being regarding his origins, emphasizing that his very existence is a miracle brought about by God from a state of non-existence; it is meant to humble the skeptic who doubts the possibility of life after death by highlighting that the Creator who brought him into being from absolute nothingness is certainly capable of resurrecting him after he has turned to dust.

translation: So by your Lord, We will surely gather them and the devils, then We will surely bring them to be present around Hell on their knees.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute certainty of the Day of Judgment, swearing by the Lord of the Prophet to highlight that neither the deniers nor their rebellious companions will escape accountability. Being gathered on their knees signifies the ultimate humiliation and the state of helplessness as they await their final judgment, having been stripped of the arrogance and false deities they relied upon in the worldly life.

translation: Then We will surely extract from every sect those of them who were most stubborn against the Most Merciful in transgression.
interpretation: This verse signifies that on the Day of Resurrection, Allah will identify and single out the leaders and the most audacious of the disobedient from every group or sect, bringing them forth to be the first to enter the Fire and receive the severest punishment, as they were the ones who spearheaded the arrogance and rebellion against divine command.

translation: Then We are surely most knowing of those who are most worthy of burning therein.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine assertion that Allah, in His absolute knowledge and justice, perfectly discerns the hearts and deeds of mankind, ensuring that the punishment of Hellfire is meted out with precise accuracy to those who have truly earned it through their persistent disbelief and transgression.

translation: And there is none of you except he will come to it. This is upon your Lord an inevitability decreed.
interpretation: This verse indicates that every human being, whether righteous or wicked, must pass over or approach the bridge (As-Sirat) set over the Hellfire; the righteous will cross it safely by the grace and mercy of Allah, while the wicked will fall into the Fire according to their deeds, fulfilling the divine decree that all must face the reality of the afterlife.

translation: Then We will save those who feared Allah and leave the wrongdoers within it, on their knees.
interpretation: This verse signifies that on the Day of Judgment, after all of humanity is exposed to the intensity of Hellfire, Allah will manifest His mercy by rescuing those who maintained God-consciousness and refrained from sin, while the oppressors and deniers of truth will be left behind in the Fire, humiliated and broken in posture, unable to escape the consequences of their disbelief and tyranny.

translation: And when Our verses are recited to them as clear evidences, those who disbelieve say to those who believe, 'Which of the two parties is better in position and better in assembly?'
interpretation: The disbelievers in Mecca, blinded by their worldly wealth, status, and material splendor, attempted to measure the worth of the believers—who were often among the poor and marginalized—against themselves. By asking which group had a 'better position' (a more luxurious home or higher status) and a 'better assembly' (more prestigious social gatherings and companions), they were expressing a fundamental materialistic arrogance, erroneously equating worldly prosperity with divine favor and righteousness, while failing to realize that true honor in the sight of God is found in faith, piety, and the quality of one's deeds rather than in worldly rank or the company of the elite.

translation: And how many a generation before them have We destroyed who were better in possession and outward appearance.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern admonition to those who pride themselves on material wealth and worldly splendor, reminding them that historical nations, despite possessing far greater riches, luxurious belongings, and impressive outward beauty than the current disbelievers, were nonetheless utterly destroyed by God due to their arrogance and rejection of the truth, indicating that such worldly advantages offer no protection against divine retribution when a society persists in corruption.

translation: Say, 'Whoever is in error - let the Most Merciful extend for him an extension [in time] until, when they see that which they are promised - either punishment [in this world] or the Hour [of Resurrection] - they will come to know who is worst in position and weaker in soldiers.'
interpretation: The verse serves as a stern warning that God grants respite to those who persist in disbelief, allowing them to accumulate more sins and worldly comforts, which acts as a form of gradual ruin. This delay is not an indication of God's approval, but rather a trial that leads them toward an inevitable confrontation with the truth—either through a manifest calamity in this life or the finality of the Day of Judgment. In that moment of reckoning, the arrogance of the disbelievers will vanish, and they will clearly perceive that their perceived strength, wealth, and worldly status were illusory and useless compared to the power and victory of the believers.

translation: And Allah increases those who have been guided in guidance. And the enduring good deeds are better to your Lord for reward and better for final return.
interpretation: Allah grants those who have embraced the truth and acted upon it a deeper insight and a greater ability to perform virtuous deeds, rewarding their sincere devotion with spiritual growth, while emphasizing that the righteous deeds which endure are superior to the fleeting worldly gains, as they serve as the true foundation for one's ultimate outcome and eternal peace in the Hereafter.

translation: Have you seen him who disbelieved in Our verses and said, 'I will surely be given wealth and children'?
interpretation: This verse addresses a specific disbeliever who mocked the concept of the Hereafter by insolently claiming that if there were truly a resurrection and an afterlife, God would grant him even more wealth and children than he possessed in this world, erroneously equating worldly prosperity with divine favor and erroneously assuming that his status in this life would continue in the next life.

translation: Has he looked into the unseen, or has he taken a pledge from the Most Merciful?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical challenge directed at those who confidently claim for themselves or others positions of honor or certainty regarding the afterlife without any basis in divine revelation; it highlights that such claims are groundless because they neither possess direct knowledge of the unseen realm nor hold a binding promise from Allah that guarantees such status, thereby exposing the arrogance and falsehood of their baseless assertions.

translation: No! We shall record what he says, and We shall extend the punishment for him extensively.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning against the arrogant disbeliever who persists in falsehood and defiance; it emphasizes that every word of enmity or denial uttered by such an individual is meticulously recorded by Divine decree, and as a consequence, their period of torment in the afterlife will be progressively increased and prolonged as a just recompense for their continued stubbornness.

translation: And We will inherit from him what he mentions, and he will come to Us alone.
interpretation: This verse addresses the arrogant denier who boasts of his wealth and children, warning him that all the worldly acquisitions he prides himself on—and which he claims he will possess even in the afterlife—will be stripped away, leaving him to return to Allah in the state he was created, stripped of all worldly power, influence, and possessions, to face judgment entirely by himself.

translation: And they have taken besides Allah deities [for worship] that they would be for them [a source of] honor/power.
interpretation: These polytheists mistakenly believed that by worshiping idols or false gods instead of Allah, they would gain dignity, protection, and a source of strength; however, the verse highlights the futility of this belief, as these idols possess no real power to provide support or honor, and they will ultimately disown those who worshiped them on the Day of Judgment.

translation: No! They will deny their worship and will be opponents to them.
interpretation: On the Day of Resurrection, the false deities and idols that people worshipped instead of God will reject the worship directed toward them and will instead declare their disassociation and hostility toward their worshippers, standing as adversaries against them rather than intercessors.

translation: Have you not seen that We have sent the devils upon the disbelievers, inciting them with an intense incitement?
interpretation: This verse signifies that because of the persistent disbelief and stubborn rejection of the truth by these individuals, Allah leaves them to the influence of the devils, who actively push and provoke them into committing more sins and acts of disobedience, thereby accelerating their path toward destruction.

translation: So do not be hasty with them, for We are only counting for them a numbered count.
interpretation: Do not let the delay in the punishment of these disbelievers distress you, O Prophet, for their days and their breaths are being precisely numbered by God, and they are moving steadily toward a predetermined end where their full accountability awaits them, leaving no room for them to escape the inevitable consequence of their rebellion.

translation: On the Day We will gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation.
interpretation: This verse describes the honor bestowed upon the God-fearing on the Day of Resurrection, as they will be brought before Allah not in a state of humiliation or despair, but as an honored delegation, comparable to diplomats or guests arriving with respect and dignity to meet a noble host, highlighting the intimacy and divine favor they receive for their piety.

translation: And We will drive the criminals to Hell in thirst.
interpretation: The verse illustrates the humiliating and painful state of the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment, as they are gathered and forced toward the fire of Hell like thirsty livestock being driven to a watering hole, highlighting their utter helplessness, their intense suffering, and the irony that instead of receiving the refreshing water they desperately crave, they are driven toward the scorching flames of punishment.

translation: They will not possess [the power of] intercession, except he who has taken a covenant with the Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse clarifies that the right to intercede on the Day of Resurrection is not an inherent possession of any creature, but rather a privilege reserved exclusively for those whom Allah has permitted. Taking a covenant with the Most Merciful refers to the affirmation of the oneness of Allah (Tawhid) and the sincere belief in His messengers, which serves as a solemn commitment that qualifies a person for Allah's grace and grants them the authorization to intercede for others by His leave.

translation: And they say, 'The Most Merciful has taken [for Himself] a son.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the deep spiritual error of the polytheists and certain religious groups who attributed offspring to Allah, thereby projecting human limitations, physical needs, and biological dependency onto the Creator, which contradicts His absolute oneness, self-sufficiency, and transcendence beyond all resemblance to His creation.

translation: You have surely brought forth a monstrous thing.
interpretation: This verse signifies the profound disapproval and condemnation of the polytheists' claim that Allah has a child, portraying this assertion as an act of immense gravity, falsehood, and a distortion of the truth that defies the majesty and oneness of the Creator.

translation: The heavens almost rupture therefrom, and the earth splits open, and the mountains collapse in devastation.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the extreme gravity and cosmic shock resulting from the blasphemous claim that God has taken a son, depicting the very fabric of the universe trembling and threatening to disintegrate in reaction to such a profound falsehood against the Majesty of the Creator.

translation: That they attribute a son to the Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the gravity of the false claim that God has offspring, explaining that such an assertion contradicts the absolute oneness and divine majesty of the Creator, as the concept of having a son implies human-like limitations, needs, or companionship which are fundamentally incompatible with the nature of Allah, the Self-Sufficient, who neither begets nor is begotten.

translation: And it is not appropriate for the Most Merciful that He should take a son.
interpretation: This verse asserts the absolute transcendence and uniqueness of Allah, clarifying that the act of having children is a biological necessity rooted in human finitude, mortality, and the need for succession, all of which are attributes of created beings that are entirely incompatible with the nature of the Creator, who is self-sufficient, eternal, and free from any deficiency or resemblance to His creation.

translation: There is no one in the heavens and the earth but that he comes to the Most Merciful as a servant.
interpretation: This verse signifies that every created being, whether they are angels, humans, or jinn, remains fundamentally subject to the absolute sovereignty of Allah; on the Day of Resurrection, all creation will stand before the Almighty in a state of total submission and humbleness, acknowledging His dominion and their own dependency upon Him, as there is no refuge or escape from His authority for any soul.

translation: He has counted them and numbered them exactly.
interpretation: This verse signifies that Allah possesses complete and exhaustive knowledge of every individual creature in existence, encompassing their precise count, their deeds, the span of their lives, and their ultimate destinies, ensuring that nothing, no matter how small or hidden, escapes His divine reckoning and perfect oversight.

translation: And all of them will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection alone.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute individuality of human accountability before God on the Day of Judgment, signifying that no worldly status, wealth, family lineage, or worldly alliances will be of any avail or provide protection, as every soul will face its Creator entirely by itself to account for its own deeds.

translation: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection.
interpretation: This verse indicates that God will instill love and acceptance for the believers in the hearts of His righteous servants on Earth, and will grant them a special love from Himself that reflects their connection to Him through faith and virtuous actions.

translation: So We have only made it easy in your tongue that you may give good tidings thereby to the righteous and warn thereby a people hostile.
interpretation: Allah explains that He revealed the Qur'an in the clear Arabic language of the Prophet Muhammad so that its meanings would be accessible and easy to understand, serving as a medium to deliver glad tidings of paradise to those who guard themselves against evil and a stern warning to those who are stubbornly contentious and deeply argumentative against the truth.

translation: And how many generations have We destroyed before them! Do you perceive any one of them or hear from them a sound?
interpretation: The verse highlights the absolute finality of God's judgment upon past nations who persisted in their denial, emphasizing that their power, pride, and material achievements have been so thoroughly erased from the earth that not a single trace of their presence remains, nor can any faint whisper of their existence be heard, serving as a profound warning to those who follow in their footsteps.

translation: Ta-Ha
interpretation: These are abbreviated letters (al-Muqatta'at) whose precise meaning is known only to Allah, though many scholars interpret them as an indication of the miraculous nature of the Qur'an, which is composed of the same alphabet that the Arabs used in their speech, yet they are unable to produce its like.

translation: We have not sent down to you the Qur'an that you should be distressed.
interpretation: Allah reassures the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that the revelation of the Qur'an and the burden of delivering its message were not intended to cause him misery or overwhelming hardship; rather, it was sent as a source of mercy, guidance, and spiritual fulfillment, signifying that devotion to Allah brings ultimate tranquility to the soul despite the worldly challenges one may face in spreading the truth.

translation: But [it is] a reminder for whoever fears [Allah].
interpretation: The Qur'an serves as a beacon of clarity and a source of divine admonition that only benefits those whose hearts are filled with reverence and awe for their Creator, as their humility and awareness of God remove the veils of arrogance, allowing the light of revelation to penetrate and guide their souls toward righteousness.

translation: A revelation from Him who created the earth and the highest heavens.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is not a human composition but a divine revelation originating from the Creator of the entire universe, highlighting the authority and majesty of the One who brought the vast expanse of the earth and the layered heavens into existence, thereby establishing that His message carries the absolute truth and legislative power over all creation.

translation: The Most Gracious [Allah] rose above the Throne.
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah, the Most Gracious, has established Himself upon the Throne in a manner that befits His majesty and greatness, without comparing it to the physical sitting or seating of created beings, signifying His absolute sovereignty and control over all of creation.

translation: To Him belongs what is in the heavens and what is on the earth and what is between them and what is under the soil.
interpretation: This verse establishes the absolute sovereignty of Allah over the entire universe; by explicitly mentioning everything from the heights of the heavens down to the hidden depths beneath the earth's soil, it signifies that there is no space, known or unknown, that exists outside of His divine ownership, knowledge, and power, thereby affirming that all creatures are merely subjects within His infinite kingdom.

translation: And if you speak aloud, then indeed, He knows the secret and what is [even] more hidden.
interpretation: The verse serves as a reminder of Allah's absolute omniscience, emphasizing that there is no distinction between what a human expresses openly and what they conceal in their heart; He encompasses the whispers of the soul and the deepest, most subtle thoughts that have not yet manifested into intention or action, thus urging the believer to maintain mindfulness of God in both public speech and private contemplation.

translation: Allah - there is no deity except Him. To Him belong the best names.
interpretation: This verse serves as a profound affirmation of Tawhid, declaring that Allah is the only reality worthy of worship, and establishes that His attributes are infinite and perfect, encompassing all possible forms of beauty, majesty, and perfection, thereby calling the believer to know and invoke Him through these sublime names.

translation: Has the story of Moses reached you?
interpretation: This rhetorical question serves as an invitation for the Prophet Muhammad and his followers to reflect upon the narrative of Moses, highlighting that his experiences with trial, struggle, and divine support are foundational lessons that demonstrate the consistent pattern of God's interaction with His messengers and their communities.

translation: When he saw a fire, he said to his family, 'Stay here, for I have perceived a fire. Perhaps I will bring you a torch from it, or find at the fire some guidance.'
interpretation: This verse describes Prophet Musa's reliance on his human instincts when he witnessed a light in the distance during a cold, dark night. By stating he hoped to find 'guidance' at the fire, he was likely referring to finding someone who could provide directions to travelers or offer assistance in the desolate valley of Tuwa, unaware that this fire was a manifestation of divine presence that would mark the beginning of his prophetic mission.

translation: But when he came to it, he was called, 'O Moses!'
interpretation: This moment signifies the profound transition from Musa's ordinary life as a traveler to his divine appointment as a Prophet, as the voice from the tree represents the direct manifestation of God's presence, breaking the silence of the desert to initiate a direct dialogue between the Creator and His chosen servant, thereby marking the start of a transformative mission that would alter the course of history.

translation: Indeed, I am your Lord, so take off your sandals. Indeed, you are in the sacred valley of Tuwa.
interpretation: God commands Moses to remove his sandals as a gesture of profound reverence and submission upon entering a place sanctified by His divine manifestation, signaling that the profane concerns and worldly attachments of his former life must be shed before standing in the presence of the Almighty.

translation: And I have chosen you, so listen to what is revealed.
interpretation: Allah addresses Musa (Moses) to establish the direct connection of divine communication, emphasizing that the command to listen is a prerequisite for receiving the mission of prophethood and the sacred guidance that is about to follow.

translation: Indeed, I am Allah. There is no deity except Me, so worship Me and establish prayer for My remembrance.
interpretation: This verse establishes the foundational principle of Tawhid, declaring that God alone is worthy of worship, and mandates that the act of prayer serves as a vital spiritual instrument to keep the human heart constantly conscious of the Creator's presence.

translation: Indeed, the Hour is coming; I almost conceal it so that every soul may be recompensed according to that for which it strives.
interpretation: God keeps the exact time of the Day of Judgment hidden from all of creation, including the prophets, to ensure that humans live in a state of perpetual vigilance and accountability, acknowledging that their ultimate destiny is determined solely by the sincerity and weight of their deeds in this worldly life.

translation: So do not let one who does not believe in it and follows his desire avert you from it, or you would perish.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to the believer not to be influenced or led astray by those who reject the truth of the afterlife and the Day of Judgment, as their disbelief is rooted in the pursuit of fleeting worldly desires; yielding to their skepticism or following their path of heedlessness will inevitably lead to one's own spiritual ruin and ultimate destruction.

translation: And what is that in your right hand, O Moses?
interpretation: This question is posed by Allah not out of a lack of knowledge, but as a pedagogical device to draw Moses's attention to the object he was holding, preparing him for the miraculous transformation it was about to undergo. By asking him to identify his own staff, Allah establishes a profound contrast between the ordinary nature of the item and the extraordinary divine power that would manifest through it, thereby anchoring Moses's faith and firming his resolve before his mission to Pharaoh.

translation: He said, 'It is my staff; I lean upon it, and I beat down leaves with it for my sheep, and I have other uses for it.'
interpretation: When Allah asked Prophet Moses what he was holding in his hand, Moses replied by describing the object's various practical functions in his daily life, such as aiding his balance while walking, harvesting fodder for his livestock, and serving as a versatile tool for other needs; this response highlights Moses's humility and his honest, straightforward communication with the Divine, as he did not simply answer with 'a staff' but provided a detailed context that reflected his humble profession as a shepherd and his reliance on modest tools before being granted a miraculous sign.

translation: He said, 'Throw it down, O Moses.'
interpretation: This command from Allah to Moses was intended to prepare him for the manifestation of His divine power; by instructing him to cast his staff, Allah demonstrates that the power which transforms the ordinary into the miraculous resides solely with the Creator, thereby setting the stage for the miraculous transformation of the staff into a serpent as a sign of his prophethood.

translation: So he threw it down, and suddenly it was a snake, moving swiftly.
interpretation: This verse depicts the miraculous transformation of Prophet Musa's staff into a living, slithering serpent at the command of Allah, serving as a clear sign of His divine power meant to manifest the truth of Musa's prophethood before Pharaoh and his court.

translation: He said, 'Seize it and fear not; We will restore it to its former state.'
interpretation: In this verse, Allah addresses Moses during his encounter at the burning bush, commanding him to grasp the staff which had transformed into a snake. The command serves as a test of faith and trust in the Divine power; by instructing Moses to take hold of the creature he feared, Allah demonstrates that worldly dangers hold no power against His will and promises that the staff will return to its original form, reassuring Moses that he is under divine protection and that the miraculous signs he is witnessing are tools for his mission.

translation: And draw your hand to your side, it will come forth white without disease - another sign.
interpretation: This verse refers to one of the miracles granted to Prophet Moses, where he was commanded to place his hand into the opening of his garment at his chest; when he withdrew it, it shone with a brilliant, supernatural whiteness that was not a result of leprosy or any affliction, but rather a miraculous manifestation of Allah's power intended to serve as a clear proof of his prophethood for Pharaoh and his people.

translation: That We may show you [some] of Our greatest signs.
interpretation: This verse signifies that Allah chose to manifest profound and miraculous evidences to Prophet Musa (peace be upon him) not merely as a test of faith, but as a strengthening of his resolve and a preparation for his momentous mission to confront the tyranny of Pharaoh, thereby demonstrating the absolute sovereignty and power of the Creator over all physical laws.

translation: Go to Pharaoh, for he has indeed transgressed all bounds.
interpretation: God commands Moses to confront Pharaoh not because He is unaware of Pharaoh's actions, but to initiate the process of delivering the truth to a tyrant who has exceeded all limits of arrogance, tyranny, and rebellion against divine authority, thereby providing him with a final opportunity to repent or face the inevitable consequences of his oppression.

translation: He said, 'My Lord, expand for me my chest [with assurance]'
interpretation: Musa asks Allah to grant him the capacity of heart, patience, and inner peace necessary to bear the heavy burden of prophethood, to confront the tyranny of Pharaoh, and to endure the trials that accompany the mission of conveying the truth.

translation: And ease for me my task
interpretation: This phrase is a heartfelt supplication from Prophet Musa (Moses) asking Allah to remove all obstacles from his path and to grant him facilitation, smoothness, and success in the difficult and momentous mission of conveying the message to Pharaoh, acknowledging that true capability and the unraveling of complexities lie solely in the hands of the Almighty.

translation: And untie the knot from my tongue.
interpretation: Musa (Moses) is beseeching Allah to grant him clarity, eloquence, and ease in his speech so that his message may be delivered clearly and effectively to Pharaoh, removing any impediment or stuttering that might hinder his mission of conveying the divine message.

translation: understand my speech
interpretation: The phrase refers to the supplication of Prophet Musa (Moses) asking Allah to grant clarity, eloquence, and profound comprehension to his audience so that they may truly grasp the essence and the intended meaning of his message, rather than merely hearing the words.

translation: And appoint for me a minister from my family.
interpretation: Musa (Moses) prays to Allah to grant him a helper and supporter from his own kin, specifically his brother Harun (Aaron), who would share in his burden of prophethood and assist him in conveying the divine message, thereby strengthening his resolve and ensuring that his mission is carried out with effective counsel and solidarity.

translation: Harun (Aaron) is my brother.
interpretation: In this verse, Musa (Moses) is beseeching Allah to grant his brother Harun the rank of prophethood and to appoint him as a support and assistant in his mission of conveying the divine message to Pharaoh. It reflects the profound bond of kinship and the recognition that the weight of the prophetic burden requires a trusted, eloquent, and supportive companion to share in the responsibility of upholding the truth and guiding the people.

translation: Strengthen my back through him.
interpretation: This is a supplication by Prophet Musa (Moses) to Allah, asking Him to reinforce and solidify his mission and authority by supporting him with his brother Harun (Aaron), as a back is strengthened by the spine, enabling him to bear the heavy burden of prophethood and the challenges of conveying the message to Pharaoh.

translation: And let him share my task (or mission).
interpretation: Moses is here seeking divine support by asking God to grant his brother, Aaron, the capacity to participate in the prophethood and the heavy responsibility of conveying the message to Pharaoh, recognizing that the weight of such a momentous task is better borne with the assistance of a trusted and capable partner.

translation: That we may exalt You much
interpretation: The verse expresses that the purpose behind the request for divine assistance and the appointment of a partner in ministry is to enable the believer to engage in the constant remembrance, glorification, and proclamation of God's transcendence, ensuring that the heart remains perpetually occupied with His majesty and purity.

translation: And that we may glorify You much.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the ultimate purpose of keeping Allah in remembrance through speech, heart, and action is to maintain a constant awareness of His greatness, which serves as a spiritual anchor for the believer to remain steadfast in obedience and to purify the soul from negligence.

translation: Indeed, You have always been All-Seeing of us.
interpretation: This phrase signifies the complete and perpetual awareness of Allah regarding the state, actions, and inner secrets of His servants, serving as a reassurance that nothing escapes His divine vision and that His providence encompasses them at every moment.

translation: He said, 'You have been granted your request, O Moses.'
interpretation: This response from Allah signifies the total acceptance of Moses's supplications, highlighting the divine favor bestowed upon him and confirming that his earnest prayers, rooted in his mission and concern for his people, have been heard and fulfilled by the Creator.

translation: And indeed, We conferred favor upon you another time.
interpretation: This verse refers to the divine grace bestowed upon Moses when Allah reminded him of the previous time He showed him favor, which was when He inspired his mother to place him in the chest and cast him into the river, protecting him and guiding him back to her, thereby establishing the foundation for his future mission and divine protection.

translation: When We inspired to your mother that which was inspired.
interpretation: This refers to the divine inspiration sent to the mother of Moses, which was a form of heavenly guidance cast into her heart to strengthen her resolve and reassure her that Allah would protect her child, eventually returning him to her after she placed him in the river as a safeguard against the tyranny of Pharaoh.

translation: Put him into the chest and cast it into the river, and the river will throw him onto the bank; there will take him an enemy to Me and an enemy to him. And I bestowed upon you love from Me that you might be brought up under My eye.
interpretation: Allah signifies that He placed a special divine radiance and affection upon Musa that compelled those who saw him, even his enemies like Pharaoh and his wife, to feel an overwhelming sense of love and compassion for him, ensuring that he would be raised under His direct divine protection and watchful care.

translation: When your sister went and said, 'Shall I guide you to someone who will nurse him?' So We returned you to your mother that her eye might be comforted and she might not grieve. And you killed a man, so We saved you from distress and tried you with a severe trial. And you remained for years among the people of Madyan. Then you came here at the decreed time, O Moses.
interpretation: This verse recounts the divine orchestration of Moses's life, highlighting how Allah meticulously managed his upbringing, from his return to his mother to his exile in Madyan, all as part of a profound process of preparation and spiritual refining meant to ready him for his future mission as a prophet.

translation: And I have chosen you for Myself.
interpretation: This expression signifies that Allah Almighty selected Prophet Musa (Moses) specifically to be His own messenger, purifying him from all distractions and preparing him through direct spiritual refinement so that his entire focus, purpose, and loyalty would be dedicated exclusively to His service and the fulfillment of His divine mission.

translation: Go, you and your brother, with My signs and do not slacken in My remembrance.
interpretation: God commands Moses and Aaron to proceed towards Pharaoh with the miracles He provided, while emphasizing that the secret to their success and their source of strength in the face of such a formidable oppressor lies in maintaining a constant, unbroken connection with God through persistent remembrance and prayer, which will fortify their hearts against fear and ensure their steadfastness in the divine mission.

translation: Go, both of you, to Pharaoh, for he has indeed transgressed all bounds.
interpretation: God commands Moses and Aaron to confront Pharaoh not to negotiate with his tyranny, but to deliver a divine warning that his arrogance and claim of godhood have reached their peak, necessitating a direct challenge to his authority as a precursor to the manifestation of God's truth.

translation: And speak to him with gentle speech, that perhaps he may be reminded or fear [Allah].
interpretation: This verse establishes the principle of utilizing gentleness and kindness in da'wah, even when confronting the most arrogant of tyrants, as a soft approach is more likely to penetrate a hardened heart and lead a person to reflect on the truth or awaken a sense of humility before God.

translation: They said, 'Our Lord, indeed we are afraid that he will hasten [punishment] against us or that he will transgress.'
interpretation: Musa and Harun expressed their fear that the Pharaoh might resort to immediate violence or physical oppression against them before they could deliver the message or as a reaction to their divine call, demonstrating that their apprehension was based on the human instinct for self-preservation in the face of a known tyrant, while still acknowledging Allah as their ultimate protector.

translation: He said, 'Do not fear. Indeed, I am with you both; I hear and I see.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine reassurance to Prophet Musa and Harun as they prepared to confront the tyranny of Pharaoh, emphasizing that the Almighty is ever-present with His servants through His infinite knowledge, all-encompassing oversight, and constant protection, ensuring that no action or intention of their oppressor remains hidden from Him and that He will defend His messengers against any harm.

translation: Then go to him and say, 'Indeed, we are the messengers of your Lord, so send with us the Children of Israel and do not torment them. We have come to you with a sign from your Lord. And peace will be upon the one who follows the guidance.'
interpretation: This verse signifies the command of Allah to Moses and Aaron to approach Pharaoh with authority and clarity, explicitly demanding the liberation of the Children of Israel from their enslavement and persecution. By invoking their status as messengers of the Lord, they establish that their demand is not a personal grievance but a divine mandate. The concluding statement acts as a conditional warning and an invitation, establishing that peace, security, and salvation are reserved solely for those who submit to divine revelation and abandon the path of tyranny and arrogance.

translation: Indeed, it has been revealed to us that the punishment will be upon whoever denies and turns away.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine warning that the ultimate consequence for rejecting the truth brought by the prophets and willfully turning away from God's guidance is the affliction of His punishment, emphasizing that accountability is tied directly to one's deliberate refusal to acknowledge the clear message of faith.

translation: He said, 'Who, then, is the Lord of you two, O Moses?'
interpretation: Pharaoh, in his arrogance and claim to divinity, dismisses Aaron's presence and directs his question exclusively to Moses, attempting to frame the divine mission as a personal dispute rather than a fundamental truth, thereby seeking to intimidate Moses by challenging the source of his authority.

translation: He said, 'Our Lord is He who gave everything its creation and then guided [it].'
interpretation: This verse signifies that Allah is the Creator who granted every creature its specific form, structure, and unique characteristics suited for its existence, and subsequently provided it with the instinctual guidance or necessary direction to fulfill its purpose and survive within its environment.

translation: He said, 'Then what is the case of the former generations?'
interpretation: When Pharaoh asked Moses about the fate and status of those who lived before them and did not believe in the messengers, he was essentially questioning their condition to challenge the truth of the message, but Moses replied that their knowledge is recorded with God in a Book, where He neither errs nor forgets, implying that every soul will be held accountable for its deeds and that the past does not serve as an excuse for present disbelief.

translation: He said, 'The knowledge thereof is with my Lord in a Record. My Lord neither errs nor forgets.'
interpretation: Musa clarifies that the precise details, timings, and outcomes of all creation are not haphazard or lost to time; rather, they are firmly documented in the Preserved Tablet (Al-Lawh al-Mahfuz) under Allah’s absolute sovereignty, emphasizing that God’s infinite knowledge is beyond the possibility of error or the fallibility of human memory.

translation: He who has made for you the earth as a bed [spread out] and inserted therein for you roadways and sent down rain from the sky, and We produced thereby categories of various plants.
