interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom in crafting the Earth to be a stable and hospitable cradle for human existence, facilitating ease of movement through natural pathways, and initiating the life cycle of vegetation through the life-giving water of the rain, which serves as a profound sign of Allah's creative power and his meticulous provision for the sustenance of all living beings.

translation: Eat and pasture your livestock. Indeed, in that are signs for people of intellect.
interpretation: God invites humanity to reflect upon the natural order and the sustenance provided for both humans and their animals, pointing out that the intricate balance of the ecosystem and the provision of resources serve as clear manifestations of His wisdom and power for those who possess sound reason and the ability to contemplate the signs of His creation.

translation: From it We created you, and into it We shall return you, and from it We shall bring you out another time.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the cyclical nature of human existence ordained by Allah, serving as a reminder of our origins from the earth, our eventual return to the soil upon death, and our inevitable resurrection on the Day of Judgment, underscoring that every stage of our life and afterlife is entirely under the control and command of the Creator.

translation: And We had shown him Our signs, all of them, but he denied and refused.
interpretation: This verse refers to Pharaoh, who, despite witnessing the manifest miracles and clear proofs of God's power through Moses, deliberately chose to reject the truth out of arrogance, persistent disbelief, and a refusal to submit to the authority of his Creator.

translation: He said, 'Have you come to us to drive us out of our land with your magic, O Moses?'
interpretation: Pharaoh uses a rhetorical question to frame Moses' message of monotheism and liberation as a political threat, accusing him of utilizing sorcery not to convey divine truth, but as a manipulative tool to incite the populace and destabilize his kingdom, thereby attempting to turn public sentiment against Moses by branding his mission as an act of foreign or supernatural aggression.

translation: Then we will surely bring you magic like it, so appoint between us and you an appointment, which we will not fail to keep and neither will you, in a place [which is] neutral.
interpretation: The magicians are expressing their utmost confidence in their skills and their certainty that they can replicate the miracles brought by Moses (peace be upon him) by labeling them as mere magic. They propose a specific time and a neutral, leveled ground—a place that is fair for both sides—to ensure the public witness the contest without any tactical advantage, showcasing their arrogance and their desire for a decisive confrontation to prove the superiority of their craft over the divine message.

translation: He said, 'Your appointment is the day of the festival, and let the people be assembled when the sun has risen.'
interpretation: Musa, peace be upon him, set the day of 'Zinah'—which was a public holiday for the Pharaoh's people—to ensure that the confrontation would take place before the largest possible audience. By choosing the time of the morning (duha), he intended for the truth to be clearly manifested under the brightness of full daylight, leaving no room for the trickery or illusions of the magicians to be hidden, thereby allowing the divine miracle to be witnessed plainly by all who had gathered.

translation: So Pharaoh turned away, and then he gathered his plot and came [forth].
interpretation: This verse illustrates the persistence of Pharaoh in his arrogance and denial; instead of reflecting upon the signs shown by Moses, he actively orchestrated a calculated plan of deception and organized his sorcerers to confront the truth with falsehood, showing that his rejection was not born of ignorance but of a deliberate and collective effort to undermine the divine message.

translation: Moses said to them, 'Woe to you! Do not invent a lie against Allah, lest He exterminate you with a punishment; and indeed, he who invents a lie will fail.'
interpretation: Moses warns the sorcerers that fabricating lies about Allah—such as attributing divine power to idols or falsely claiming revelation—is a grave transgression that will inevitably lead to their total ruin and spiritual disappointment, as those who attempt to deceive others regarding the nature of the Divine will find their schemes undone by the truth of His judgment.

translation: Then they disputed their affair among themselves, and they concealed their private conversation.
interpretation: The verse indicates that the individuals mentioned fell into internal conflict and disagreement regarding the course of action they should take, leading them to hold secret consultations hidden from the public eye, either to plot mischief or to arrive at a consensus without external interference.

translation: They said, 'Indeed, these two are surely magicians who want to drive you out of your land with their magic and do away with your exemplary way.'
interpretation: The sorcerers of Pharaoh attempted to discredit Moses and Aaron by painting them as political subversives rather than messengers of God, accusing them of using supernatural trickery to incite a populist rebellion that would dismantle the established Egyptian social, religious, and political order to replace it with a new ideology.

translation: So resolve upon your plan and come forward in a line, and indeed, successful today is the one who gains the upper hand.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the arrogance and psychological posturing of the magicians of Pharaoh, who sought to intimidate Moses by organizing their forces in a disciplined, unified formation to demonstrate their collective might and supremacy, foolishly believing that worldly dominance and the ability to perform illusions are the true measures of success and validation of one's cause.

translation: They said, 'O Moses, either you throw, or we will be the first to throw.'
interpretation: The sorcerers of Pharaoh, displaying a mix of arrogance and confidence in their craft, challenged Prophet Moses to initiate the contest. By offering him the choice to strike first, they intended to demonstrate their superior mastery of magic, believing that whatever illusion he presented could be easily overshadowed or countered by their own fabricated sorcery.

translation: He said, 'Throw,' and when they threw, they bewitched the eyes of the people and struck terror into them, and they presented a great magic.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the deceptive nature of the sorcerers' work, where they utilized sleight of hand and psychological influence to alter the perception of the observers, making the inanimate ropes and sticks appear as if they were living, slithering snakes, thereby demonstrating that human senses can be manipulated by illusions to perceive falsehood as reality.

translation: And Moses felt within himself a sense of fear.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inherent human nature of the Prophet Moses, who experienced a natural, instinctive apprehension when faced with the sorcerers' deception, which appeared to transform ropes and staffs into moving serpents; it serves to demonstrate that even for the chosen messengers of God, maintaining faith and composure in the face of daunting challenges is a profound struggle, yet his ultimate reliance remained firmly rooted in divine assurance.

translation: We said, 'Do not fear. Indeed, it is you who are superior.'
interpretation: God reassures Moses that he should not fear the magical deceptions of the sorcerers, for the truth he carries and the divine support he possesses will inevitably triumph over their falsehood, establishing his spiritual and moral authority over their artifice.

translation: And throw what is in your right hand; it will swallow up what they have crafted. What they have crafted is but the trick of a magician, and the magician will not succeed wherever he may be.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine reassurance to Moses, demonstrating that the apparent power of the magicians is merely an illusion based on deception, which cannot prevail against the manifest truth provided by God; it underscores the spiritual principle that falsehood, no matter how skillfully portrayed, lacks the inherent validity and support required for ultimate success.

translation: Then the magicians fell down in prostration. They said, 'We have believed in the Lord of Aaron and Moses.'
interpretation: The magicians, having witnessed a miracle that transcended the limits of human sorcery and magic, were instantly humbled by the realization that Moses was a true messenger of God. Their act of immediate prostration signifies the total submission of their hearts to the Divine truth, demonstrating that their faith was born from a profound recognition of God’s absolute power over all creation, which effectively dismantled their previous allegiance to Pharaoh’s false claims of divinity.

translation: He said, 'You believed him before I gave you permission. Indeed, he is your leader who has taught you magic. So I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides, and I will crucify you on the trunks of palm trees, and you will surely know which of us is more severe in punishment and more enduring.'
interpretation: Pharaoh, driven by arrogance and the fear of losing his absolute authority over the people, employs coercive tactics to suppress the truth. He interprets the conversion of the magicians as an act of defiance against his sovereignty rather than a genuine recognition of divine truth. By threatening them with brutal physical mutilation and death, he attempts to preserve his perceived status as the ultimate deity and authority, while challenging the power of Moses’ Lord by claiming that his own capacity for inflicting suffering is more absolute and lasting.

translation: They said, 'Never will we prefer you over what has come to us of clear proofs and [over] He who created us. So decree whatever you will decree. You can only decree [for the sake of] this worldly life.'
interpretation: The magicians, having witnessed the manifest truth of Prophet Musa's miracle, reached a state of spiritual certainty that superseded all fear of worldly punishment. Their declaration signifies that Pharaoh's authority is transient and confined to the physical realm of this life, whereas their newfound faith connects them to the Eternal Creator, rendering any worldly consequence imposed by the tyrant insignificant compared to the salvation of the soul.

translation: Indeed, we have believed in our Lord, that He may forgive us our sins and what You compelled us to do of magic. And Allah is better and more enduring.
interpretation: The magicians who had been brought by Pharaoh to confront Moses acknowledged their belief in the Lord of Moses and Aaron, seeking His forgiveness for their past sins, specifically for the act of sorcery they were coerced into performing under the threat and authority of Pharaoh, while affirming that the reward and punishment from Allah are far superior and more lasting than any worldly gain or fear induced by mortal rulers.

translation: Indeed, whoever comes to his Lord as a criminal, then indeed for him is Hell, in which he will neither die nor live.
interpretation: This verse portrays the state of the disbeliever in the Hereafter as an existence suspended in perpetual agony, where the punishment is so severe and unending that it lacks the finality of death, which would bring relief, yet it is so devoid of the comfort and purpose of true life that it cannot be considered a state of living, illustrating the eternal nature of the suffering faced by those who rejected the truth.

translation: But whoever comes to Him as a believer who has done righteous deeds, for them are the highest ranks.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the ultimate status of the believer in the afterlife is determined by a combination of firm faith in the heart and the active manifestation of that faith through righteous deeds, indicating that those who balance sincerity of belief with consistent good actions will be elevated to the loftiest positions in Paradise, reflecting the divine recognition of their spiritual and moral excellence.

translation: Gardens of perpetual residence beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide eternally. And that is the reward for those who purify themselves.
interpretation: This verse underscores that the attainment of Paradise is the ultimate outcome for those who have cleansed their souls from the impurities of disbelief, shirk, and moral corruption, fulfilling their purpose by aligning their inner state and outward actions with divine guidance and truth.

translation: And We had already inspired to Moses, 'Travel by night with My servants and strike for them a dry path through the sea; you will not fear being overtaken [by Pharaoh] nor be afraid [of drowning].'
interpretation: In this verse, Allah consoles and commands Moses (peace be upon him) to lead the Children of Israel out of Egypt under the cover of darkness to escape the oppression of Pharaoh. By commanding him to strike a path through the sea, Allah demonstrates His absolute sovereignty over nature, transforming a lethal obstacle into a safe passage of dry land, thereby reassuring Moses that he is under divine protection and need not fear the pursuit of the enemy or the perils of the deep, as God's guidance ensures both deliverance from danger and the ultimate defeat of the tyrant.

translation: Then Pharaoh pursued them with his soldiers, and there covered them from the sea that which covered them.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the sudden and overwhelming nature of divine retribution; as Pharaoh and his army relentlessly chased the children of Israel, the sea—which had been a path of salvation for the believers—turned into a mechanism of total destruction for the oppressors, manifesting God's absolute power to submerge the arrogant in the very elements they thought they could control.

translation: And Pharaoh led his people astray, and he did not guide them.
interpretation: This verse highlights the tragic consequence of Pharaoh's tyranny and deception, explaining that he did not merely fail to provide righteous guidance to his subjects, but actively diverted them from the truth and moral rectitude through his falsehoods, ultimately leading them to their ruin both in this world and the Hereafter.

translation: O Children of Israel, We saved you from your enemy, and We made an appointment with you at the right side of the mount, and We sent down to you manna and quails.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder to the Israelites of the manifest favors bestowed upon them by God: first, the liberation from the tyranny of Pharaoh and his army; second, the divine appointment at Mount Sinai where the Torah was revealed to Moses to guide them; and third, the miraculous provision of sustenance, which signifies that God not only secured their freedom but also actively sustained their physical existence in the wilderness, thereby establishing a covenantal relationship that required their gratitude and adherence to His law.

translation: Eat from the good things which We have provided for you, and do not transgress therein, lest My anger should descend upon you; and he upon whom My anger descends has certainly fallen.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine command to consume the wholesome and lawful sustenance provided by Allah with gratitude, while simultaneously warning against the misuse of these blessings—whether through extravagance, ingratitude, or consuming what is forbidden—as such arrogance and violation of divine boundaries inevitably lead to the loss of spiritual guidance and the encounter with God's retribution.

translation: And indeed, I am the Perpetual Forgiver of whoever repents and believes and does righteousness and then continues in guidance.
interpretation: God emphasizes that His forgiveness is not unconditional but is contingent upon a sincere four-step progression: turning away from sin through repentance, affirming faith in the heart, manifesting that faith through righteous deeds, and consistently maintaining that path of truth throughout one's life rather than relapsing into error.

translation: And what made you hasten from your people, O Moses?
interpretation: God is questioning Moses regarding his decision to leave the Children of Israel behind and rush ahead to the appointed place for communion with his Lord, seeking to draw nearer to Him. This indicates that while Moses' intention was rooted in his intense longing and zeal for divine closeness, God, in His wisdom, draws attention to the leadership responsibility inherent in his station, suggesting that even a prophet’s haste—though born of noble intent—is subject to the divine refinement of conduct.

translation: He said, 'They are right behind me, and I hastened to You, my Lord, so that You would be pleased.'
interpretation: When Moses left his people to head toward the mountain for his appointment with God, he was so eager to reach the place of revelation and communion with his Lord that he moved ahead of the people of Israel, explaining to God that his haste was not due to negligence or a desire to abandon his responsibilities, but rather a manifestation of his intense longing to achieve God's approval and reach the spiritual proximity that comes from obedience to His commands.

translation: Allah said, 'Indeed, We have tested your people after you, and the Samiri has led them astray.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine test that befell the Children of Israel during the absence of Prophet Musa. It emphasizes that human belief is subject to trial and that the influence of a corrupt individual, such as the Samiri, was used as a mechanism of affliction to reveal the true state of their faith and their susceptibility to worldly distractions despite the guidance they had previously received.

translation: Then Moses returned to his people, angry and grieved. He said, O my people, did your Lord not promise you a good promise? Then, did the time seem too long for you, or did you intend that wrath from your Lord should descend upon you, so you broke your promise to me?
interpretation: Moses expresses profound frustration and sorrow because his people abandoned their commitment to monotheism and the guidance he brought them, questioning whether they grew impatient during his short absence or if they deliberately courted divine punishment by forsaking their covenant with God and their pledge to follow his teachings.

translation: They said, 'We did not fail our appointment with you by our own will, but we were burdened with heavy loads of the people's ornaments, so we cast them [into the fire]; and thus did the Samiri suggest.'
interpretation: The people of Moses excused their apostasy by claiming they were unable to resist the social pressure and the burden of the gold they brought with them, suggesting that their actions were a result of external circumstances rather than free will, while pointing to the Samiri as the one who orchestrated the event through his deceptive influence and psychological manipulation.

translation: Then he brought out for them a calf, which had a lowing sound, and they said, 'This is your god and the god of Moses, but he forgot.'
interpretation: The Samiri crafted a golden calf that possessed an internal hollow structure, allowing the wind to pass through it and produce a sound resembling the lowing of a cow, which he used to deceive the people. The verse highlights the spiritual blindness of the Israelites, who abandoned the worship of the unseen God for a physical idol, and it notes that Moses forgot—not his mission, but his earlier instruction to his people to await his return—or that the Samiri forgot the truth of God, leading him to lead others into the grave sin of idolatry.

translation: Do they not see that it cannot return to them a word, and it does not possess for them any harm or benefit?
interpretation: This verse highlights the complete incapacity of false deities, such as the golden calf worshipped by the Israelites, to exercise any form of power, agency, or communication. By pointing out that such idols are inanimate objects devoid of life or intelligence, the Quran exposes the absurdity and irrationality of associating partners with God, as these idols are incapable of responding to the prayers of their worshippers or exerting any influence over their lives, whether to avert misfortune or bestow blessings.

translation: And Aaron had already told them before, 'O my people, you are only being tested by it, and indeed, your Lord is the Most Merciful, so follow me and obey my order.'
interpretation: Aaron emphasizes to the Children of Israel that the golden calf was merely a trial sent by Allah to distinguish the believers from the polytheists, warning them that their true allegiance must be to the Most Merciful, who possesses the qualities of mercy and guidance, rather than to a lifeless idol, and he asserts his prophetic authority to restore them to the correct path of monotheism.

translation: They said, 'We will not cease to be devoted to the worship of it until Moses returns to us.'
interpretation: This verse depicts the stubbornness and spiritual instability of the Israelites who, in the absence of Prophet Moses, allowed their previous exposure to idolatry to resurface, choosing to persist in the worship of the golden calf rather than maintaining their covenant with Allah, thereby demonstrating a reliance on physical manifestations of divinity over the unseen truth taught by their messenger.

translation: He said, O Aaron, what prevented you, when you saw them going astray,
interpretation: Musa is addressing his brother Aaron with a stern tone of inquiry, not out of doubt regarding Aaron's piety, but rather to understand why he did not forcefully intervene or follow him into the mountains when he saw the Children of Israel deviate into the worship of the calf, emphasizing the communal responsibility of a leader to actively prevent manifest disobedience and corruption.

translation: Do you not follow me? Have you then disobeyed my order?
interpretation: This verse reflects the rhetorical reproach directed by Aaron towards the Children of Israel, highlighting the gravity of their deviation when they worshipped the calf despite his clear command to remain steadfast upon the worship of Allah alone, illustrating that abandoning the guidance of a prophet constitutes an act of direct rebellion against divine instruction.

translation: He said, 'O son of my mother, do not seize me by my beard or by my head. Indeed, I feared that you would say,
interpretation: Harun was explaining to Musa that his apparent lack of forceful intervention against the Israelites who worshipped the calf was not due to negligence or abandonment of his duty, but rather a strategic decision to avoid causing a deep, irreparable schism among the people, fearing that any physical confrontation or harsh measures might lead to internal conflict that would have broken the unity of the community of Bani Israel during Musa's absence.

translation: He said, 'What is your case, O Samiri?'
interpretation: Musa (peace be upon him) asks this question to reveal the underlying motive and the deliberate nature of the Samiri's transgression, shifting the focus from the act itself to the personal intent and internal state that led him to corrupt the Israelites by crafting the golden calf.

translation: He said, 'I perceived what they did not perceive, so I took a handful [of dust] from the track of the messenger and threw it, and thus did my soul entice me.'
interpretation: The verse illustrates the psychological state of the Samiri after he had misguided the Israelites; he justifies his actions by claiming a special, esoteric perception—having seen the Angel Jibril on his horse—which allowed him to seize a trace of the angel's footprint. This indicates that his transgression was not born of mere ignorance, but was an act of personal inclination and internal desire (the inciting self) that prioritized his own misguided logic over divine revelation, demonstrating how a person may rationalize their corruption by attributing it to an extraordinary experience that no one else witnessed.

translation: [Moses] said, 'Go. Then indeed, it is [decreed] for you in this life to say, No contact. And indeed, you have an appointment [in the Hereafter] which you will not fail to keep. And look at your 'god' to whom you remained devoted - we will surely burn it and then blow it into the sea with a blast.'
interpretation: Moses pronounces a divine judgment upon the Samiri, stripping him of social standing and normalcy; he is condemned to a life of isolation and psychological distress, where he must warn others not to touch him, mirroring the spiritual alienation he created for the Israelites. Simultaneously, Moses demonstrates the futility of the Samiri’s idolatry by destroying the golden calf—a man-made object that holds no divinity—and scattering its ashes into the sea to prove that what humans create to satisfy their desires can be easily annihilated, leaving nothing behind but the consequence of their disbelief.

translation: Your God is only Allah, He than Whom there is no god. He encompasses all things in knowledge.
interpretation: This verse establishes the principle of absolute Monotheism, affirming that the only entity worthy of worship is the Creator who possesses unique attributes. By stating that He encompasses all things in knowledge, the verse emphasizes that God’s awareness is exhaustive, encompassing every detail of the seen and the unseen, leaving nothing outside of His divine cognizance or oversight.

translation: Thus do We relate to you the news of what has passed, and We have given you from Us a reminder.
interpretation: God addresses Prophet Muhammad, informing him that the historical accounts of past nations and prophets are being revealed to him not through human instruction, but through divine revelation, and that the Qur'an serves as a divine reminder containing the criteria for truth, guidance, and spiritual insight that will benefit all of humanity until the end of time.

translation: Whoever turns away from it, he will surely bear a heavy burden on the Day of Resurrection.
interpretation: This verse warns against abandoning the Qur'an, which implies turning away from its guidance, rejecting its truth, or neglecting to follow its commandments and prohibitions; consequently, the sinner will be burdened on the Day of Judgment with the heavy weight of his sins and the consequences of his disregard for the divine message that was revealed for his own salvation.

translation: Abiding eternally therein, and evil it is for them on the Day of Resurrection as a load.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who choose disbelief and follow falsehoods over the guidance of Allah will carry the heavy, burdensome weight of their sins and transgressions on the Day of Judgment; it is a depiction of the psychological and spiritual agony of bearing the consequences of one's own rejection of truth, which will prove to be an unbearable load when they are forced to confront their accountability before God.

translation: The Day the Horn will be blown, and We will gather the criminals, that Day, blue-eyed.
interpretation: This verse describes the terrifying reality of the Day of Judgment, where the blowing of the Trumpet serves as the divine signal for the resurrection of all souls. The description of the criminals as 'blue-eyed'—often interpreted by exegetes as being blinded by intense fear, having faces darkened with misery, or suffering from the physiological effects of extreme dread—signifies the overwhelming humiliation and psychological trauma that will consume those who rejected the truth during their worldly lives, as their outward appearance will mirror the internal turmoil of their eternal loss.

translation: They whisper among themselves, 'You have not stayed [on earth] but ten days.'
interpretation: The people will be whispering to one another on the Day of Resurrection, reflecting on how fleeting and insignificant their life in this world was compared to the eternal nature of the afterlife, to the point that their entire duration on earth seems to them no longer than a mere ten days.

translation: We are most knowing of what they say when the best of them in conduct says, 'You have not remained [in the world] but one day.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's comprehensive knowledge of the discourse of the disbelievers, highlighting the delusion of those among them who, when contemplating the brevity of their earthly life in comparison to the eternal nature of the afterlife, erroneously perceive their time on earth as having been merely a single day, reflecting the transience of worldly existence when viewed from the perspective of eternity.

translation: And they ask you about the mountains, so say, 'My Lord will blow them away with a blast.'
interpretation: This verse indicates that on the Day of Resurrection, the solid and firmly anchored mountains will be pulverized by the command of Allah until they become like scattered dust, signifying the complete transformation of the earth and the absolute power of God to alter the physical laws of the universe when the Hour arrives.

translation: Then He will leave it a level, smooth plain.
interpretation: This verse describes the ultimate transformation of the earth on the Day of Judgment, where God will level all mountains, hills, and valleys, smoothing the entire surface of the planet so that it becomes flat and uniform, devoid of any vegetation, landmarks, or curves, allowing the vision of the gathered humanity to span across a featureless expanse.

translation: You will not see therein any crookedness or unevenness.
interpretation: The verse indicates that the path of the Qur'an and the state of the terrain on the Day of Resurrection are completely uniform, free from any deviation, distortion, or fluctuations in elevation, symbolizing a state of perfect justice, clarity, and absolute balance that leaves no room for confusion or inconsistency.

translation: On that Day, they will follow the Caller who has no crookedness in him, and voices will be hushed before the Most Merciful, so you will not hear except a whisper.
interpretation: On the Day of Resurrection, all creation will submit to the command of the Caller—the angel appointed to summon them to the place of assembly—following his direction without any deviation or hesitation, for the divine decree will be absolute and inescapable; at that moment, the terrifying majesty and overwhelming presence of the Most Merciful will cause all voices to be stilled in reverence and dread, such that nothing remains audible except the faint, hushed sound of footsteps or breath, as hearts are humbled by the manifestation of the Truth.

translation: On that Day, no intercession will benefit except for the one whom the Most Merciful has permitted and whose word He has approved.
interpretation: On the Day of Resurrection, intercession will be restricted solely to those whom Allah has granted permission to intercede and to those whose speech—namely their profession of faith in the oneness of Allah—He has found acceptable, thereby nullifying the false hopes of the polytheists who expected intercession for their idolatry.

translation: He knows what is before them and what is behind them, but they do not encompass Him in knowledge.
interpretation: This verse affirms Allah's absolute encompassment of all things in time and space—both the future that lies ahead of His creation and the past they have left behind—while highlighting the inherent limitation of created beings, whose finite minds are fundamentally unable to fully grasp the infinite essence, attributes, and wisdom of the Creator.

translation: And faces shall be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence. And he will have failed who carries injustice.
interpretation: On the Day of Resurrection, all creation will be overcome by a sense of awe and submissiveness in the presence of Allah, whose life is absolute and who manages all affairs of existence, leading to the utter regret and disappointment of those who burdened themselves with the sin of polytheism or wrongdoing against others, as they will find no merit or excuse to save them from the consequences of their deeds.

translation: But he who does righteous deeds while he is a believer will neither fear injustice nor deprivation.
interpretation: This verse assures the believer that their righteous deeds will be preserved and rewarded in full by Allah, guaranteeing that they will not suffer any reduction of their earned reward (hadm) nor the addition of any sins that they did not commit (zulm), ensuring complete justice in the afterlife.

translation: And thus We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an and have diversified therein the warnings that perhaps they will avoid sin or it may cause them to remember.
interpretation: The verse explains that Allah revealed the Qur'an in the clear Arabic language and structured its warnings in various forms—through stories of past nations, descriptions of the afterlife, and exhortations—to ensure the message reaches the hearts of the people, aiming to instill piety and encourage them to reflect on the truth so that they may return to the path of guidance and mindfulness of their Creator.

translation: So high [above all] is Allah, the Sovereign, the Truth. And, [O Muhammad], do not hasten with the Qur'an before its revelation is completed to you, and say, 'My Lord, increase me in knowledge.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine instruction to the Prophet Muhammad to exercise patience and restraint while receiving revelation, ensuring that he does not rush to recite or memorize parts of the Qur'an before the Angel Gabriel has finished conveying the message, thereby highlighting the importance of divine precision; simultaneously, it establishes the fundamental principle of intellectual humility by commanding the seeker of truth to perpetually ask Allah to expand their understanding and insight.

translation: And We had already taken a promise from Adam before, but he forgot; and We found not in him determination.
interpretation: The verse highlights the inherent human tendency toward forgetfulness and lack of steadfast resolve when faced with temptation or trial. It explains that Adam's disobedience was not rooted in a malicious desire to defy Allah, but rather in a lapse of memory regarding the divine command and a failure to maintain the firm perseverance required to resist the whisperings of the enemy, serving as a reminder of the fragility of the human condition and the necessity of constant mindfulness.

translation: And [mention] when We said to the angels, 'Prostrate to Adam,' and they prostrated, except for Iblees; he refused.
interpretation: This verse recounts the momentous command from Allah to the angels to show honor and recognition of the excellence bestowed upon Adam by prostrating before him. While the angels complied immediately in obedience to their Creator, Iblees demonstrated the first act of defiance through arrogance and pride, refusing to acknowledge the status of the new creation, which became the root cause of his expulsion from divine grace.

translation: Then We said, "O Adam, indeed this is an enemy to you and to your wife. So let him not remove you from Paradise so that you would suffer."
interpretation: Allah warns Adam and Hawwa (Eve) of the enmity of Iblis, highlighting that his ultimate goal is to strip them of the honor, comfort, and state of divine pleasure found in Paradise, thereby plunging them into a life of hardship, toil, and physical exhaustion necessitated by worldly existence.

translation: Indeed, it is [promised] for you not to be hungry therein nor be naked.
interpretation: This verse signifies that within the abode of Paradise, Allah guarantees for the believer a state of perpetual fulfillment and preservation, where the physical burdens and vulnerabilities of worldly life—specifically the necessity of food for survival and the requirement of clothing for protection and decency—are entirely eliminated, replaced by a life of absolute ease, sufficiency, and dignity.

translation: And indeed, you will not be thirsty therein, nor will you be exposed to the sun.
interpretation: This verse signifies that within Paradise, the soul is granted complete relief from the physical hardships of the worldly life; it expresses that the believer will never experience the discomfort of thirst nor the exhausting effects of the sun's heat, indicating a state of eternal comfort, protection, and perfect bodily ease where all basic needs are fulfilled without the toil associated with human existence.

translation: Then Satan whispered to him; he said, 'O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and possession that will not deteriorate?'
interpretation: The verse highlights the deceptive nature of Satan, who used the human desire for permanence and authority as a tool for temptation, promising Adam a state of everlasting life and sovereignty through disobedience, which reveals how transgression is often disguised under the allure of gaining something perceived as beneficial or essential.

translation: Then the two of them ate from it, and their private parts became apparent to them, and they began to fasten together over themselves from the leaves of Paradise. And Adam disobeyed his Lord and erred.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the immediate psychological and physical consequences of disobedience, where the loss of innocence or the state of grace caused Adam and Eve to become conscious of their vulnerability and imperfection. The act of covering themselves with leaves signifies the sudden emergence of shame and the natural human instinct to conceal one's nakedness, while the description of Adam having 'erred' or 'gone astray' does not imply a malicious moral corruption, but rather a lapse in judgment and a failure to resist the temptation that led to a departure from the direct path laid out by God.

translation: Then his Lord chose him and turned to him in forgiveness and guided him.
interpretation: This verse signifies that after Adam (peace be upon him) had slipped and fallen into error, Allah in His infinite mercy and wisdom selected him for prophethood, accepted his sincere repentance, and granted him the divine guidance necessary to lead his life and guide his progeny on the path of truth and obedience.

translation: Allah said, 'Descend from it, all of you, as enemies to one another. Then if there should come to you guidance from Me, whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor suffer [in the Hereafter].'
interpretation: This verse establishes that the earthly life is a testing ground where human beings are prone to conflict due to their carnal desires and the whispers of Satan, but Allah guarantees that those who anchor their existence in His revealed divine guidance will be protected from both the confusion of misguidance in this world and the misery of regret and suffering in the eternal afterlife.

translation: And whoever turns away from My remembrance - indeed, he will have a depressed [i.e., difficult] life, and We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind.
interpretation: The verse explains that the core cause of psychological distress, lack of inner peace, and spiritual emptiness in this worldly life is the abandonment of God's remembrance and guidance; this severance from the Source of existence leads to a life of perpetual anxiety and dissatisfaction, culminating in a state of spiritual blindness in the afterlife where the individual is cut off from God's mercy and light as a consequence of their refusal to recognize Him during their earthly life.

translation: He will say, 'My Lord, why have You raised me up blind while I was endowed with sight?'
interpretation: This verse depicts the state of the one who turned away from God's message during their worldly life; their blindness in the Hereafter is a metaphorical manifestation of their spiritual blindness in the world, where they were given the faculty of sight but chose to ignore the clear signs of God's existence and guidance, leading them to be resurrected in a state of deprivation and helplessness.

translation: Allah will say, 'Thus did Our signs come to you, and you disregarded them; and so this Day, you will be disregarded.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning that the act of turning a blind eye to divine guidance and abandoning the remembrance of God in this world leads to a reciprocal outcome in the afterlife, where the individual will find themselves deprived of God's mercy and recognition, effectively being left to their own neglect as they once neglected the truth.

translation: And thus do We recompense he who transgressed and did not believe in the verses of his Lord; and the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe and more enduring.
interpretation: This verse explains the principle of divine justice, indicating that just as God punishes those who persist in disbelief and exceed the limits of truth in this world, He maintains a greater standard of retribution in the afterlife. The mention that the punishment is 'more enduring' serves as a warning that while worldly consequences for sin are finite and often perceived as immediate, the spiritual consequences in the eternal realm are infinite and far more profound, reflecting the gravity of rejecting divine signs.

translation: Has it not enlightened them how many generations We destroyed before them, among whose dwellings they walk? Indeed, in that are signs for those of intellect.
interpretation: The verse serves as a stern reminder that the physical ruins of civilizations that defied divine guidance remain as visible warnings for the living. By walking through these desolate spaces, the heedless should recognize that the material power and grand structures of the past offered no protection against divine decree when morality and truth were abandoned, thus urging people of reason to reflect on history as a moral compass to avoid the same destructive path.

translation: And if it were not for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been obligatory [to punish them immediately], and [likewise] a specified term.
interpretation: The verse clarifies that the delay of Allah’s punishment for those who disbelieve or persist in wrongdoing is not due to their innocence or the absence of a divine decree, but rather because of a preordained promise from Allah to grant them a respite until an appointed time, thereby demonstrating His patience and allowing for the completion of the trial of human life.

translation: So be patient over what they say and exalt [Allah] with praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting; and during periods of the night [exalt Him] and at the ends of the day, that you may be satisfied.
interpretation: The command for patience in the face of mockery and disbelief is intrinsically linked to the spiritual nourishment of Salah and Dhikr. By establishing a rhythm of constant remembrance throughout the day—from the early dawn before sunrise, through the late afternoon before sunset, into the deep hours of the night, and at the start and end of the day—the believer attains a state of divine contentment and internal tranquility. This serenity serves as a powerful shield for the heart, making the soul impervious to the taunts of the deniers and grounding the believer in the overwhelming certainty of Allah's presence.

translation: And do not extend your eyes toward that by which We have given enjoyment to [some] categories of them, [its being but] the splendor of worldly life by which We test them. And the provision of your Lord is better and more enduring.
interpretation: God instructs the Prophet, and by extension the believers, not to gaze with envy or longing at the worldly luxuries, status, and transient pleasures granted to disbelievers, as these are merely fleeting trials designed to test their gratitude and faith; instead, one should find contentment in the spiritual rewards and the eternal blessings provided by God, which are infinitely more valuable and lasting than the temporary decorations of this world.

translation: And enjoin prayer upon your family and be steadfast therein. We ask not of you provision; We provide for you, and the [best] outcome is for righteousness.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the primary responsibility of a believer is to prioritize spiritual discipline over worldly anxieties, commanding the Prophet and his followers to ensure that their households remain dedicated to the worship of God while maintaining patience in the face of life's hardships. It serves as a divine reassurance that human beings are not tasked with the burden of securing their own sustenance, as God is the sole Provider, emphasizing that true success and a favorable conclusion in both worlds are reserved exclusively for those who maintain God-consciousness and moral integrity.

translation: And they say, 'Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?' Has there not come to them clear proof of what was in the former scriptures?
interpretation: The disbelievers are demanding an external miracle to prove the prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him), ignoring the fact that the Quran itself serves as a manifest and sufficient miracle; it confirms the divine truths revealed in the earlier scriptures, and the mere existence of this Quranic revelation is the ultimate evidence that they are witnesses to the fulfillment of what was promised in the texts of old.

translation: And if We had destroyed them with a punishment before it, they would have said, 'Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger so that we could have followed Your verses before we were humiliated and disgraced?'
interpretation: This verse underscores the infinite wisdom and justice of Allah in establishing the proof against humanity. By sending messengers and revealed scriptures, Allah ensures that no individual can claim ignorance or lack of guidance on the Day of Judgment. The verse reveals the psychological tendency of those who reject the truth: they seek excuses to justify their disbelief, yet they would have been the first to complain had they been punished without receiving a clear divine warning, demonstrating that their rejection is rooted in stubbornness rather than a genuine lack of evidence.

translation: Say, 'Each is waiting; so wait. For you will come to know who are the companions of the sound path and who is guided.'
interpretation: The verse serves as a final decree to the deniers of the truth, commanding the Prophet to invite them to wait for the inevitable outcome of divine judgment. It emphasizes that while the disbelievers rely on their fleeting worldly positions, the ultimate consequence will reveal that the followers of the true, straight path—who have adhered to the guidance of Allah—are the ones who attained success and true direction, while those who rejected it will face the realization of their error.

translation: The time of reckoning for the people has drawn near, yet they are still in a state of heedlessness, turning away.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning that the Day of Resurrection is imminent and approaching rapidly, yet humanity persists in worldly distractions and spiritual negligence, deliberately ignoring the reality of their accountability before Allah despite the clear signs and warnings presented to them.

translation: There comes not unto them a new reminder from their Lord except that they listen to it while they are playing.
interpretation: This verse portrays the spiritual heedlessness and arrogance of the disbelievers, who treat the Divine revelation—which is meant to guide and save them—as a triviality; by listening to the Qur'an with a playful heart and a distracted mind, they demonstrate that they have closed themselves off from the gravity of God's message, choosing worldly amusement over the eternal truth.

translation: Their hearts are distracted. And those who do wrong conceal their private conversation, saying: 'Is this but a human being like you? Will you then approach magic while you are aware?'
interpretation: The verse highlights the state of the disbelievers whose hearts are preoccupied with worldly distractions, leading them to be heedless of the truth. When they gather in secrecy to whisper against the Prophet, their arrogant rejection stems from their inability to accept that a human being could be chosen by God for revelation; consequently, they falsely dismiss his miracles and message as mere sorcery, despite the clear evidence of the truth being manifest before their eyes.

translation: He said, 'My Lord knows every word spoken in the heavens and on the earth, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.'
interpretation: The Prophet is affirming that God's knowledge is absolute and encompasses all things, whether secret or public, throughout the entire universe. By describing Himself as the All-Hearing and the All-Knowing, God assures the believer that no word or intention escapes His awareness, and therefore, one should maintain constant mindfulness of His presence and authority, knowing that nothing said or thought goes unregistered by Him.

translation: Rather, they say, '[It is a] mixture of false dreams; rather, he has invented it; rather, he is a poet. So let him bring us a sign just as the former [messengers] were sent [with signs].'
interpretation: The disbelievers in their obstinacy and rejection of the truth continuously shifted their accusations against the Prophet Muhammad, vacillating between claiming his message was a mere collection of confused, dream-like visions, a fabricated lie, or the imaginative verses of a poet. They demanded physical, miraculous proof—miracles of their own choosing—while ignoring the profound, self-evident truth of the Qur'an itself, demonstrating that their skepticism was not a search for knowledge but a persistent refusal to submit to the divine message despite the clarity of the evidence provided.

translation: Not a town did We destroy before them that believed; so will they believe?
interpretation: This verse serves as a rhetorical rebuke to the disbelievers of Mecca, emphasizing that historically, no civilization that defied the messengers of God and consequently faced divine destruction had ever turned to faith once that destruction was already destined or unfolding. The implication is that since these predecessors did not attain belief even when faced with their demise, the stubborn disbelievers of the Prophet's time are likewise unlikely to accept the truth, as their persistent denial mirrors that of the nations who were destroyed before them.

translation: And We sent not before you except men to whom We revealed [Our message]. So ask the people of the message if you do not know.
interpretation: God clarifies that all His messengers were human beings rather than angels, reinforcing the normality of the prophetic office to ensure they could effectively guide their communities. By directing the disbelievers to 'ask the people of the message'—meaning those who possess knowledge of the previous scriptures—the verse establishes the principle of seeking expertise and referring to authoritative sources of revelation to clarify matters of faith when one is ignorant of the historical truth.

translation: And We did not make them bodies that do not eat food, nor were they immortal.
interpretation: This verse refutes the claims of those who doubted the prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him) on the basis that he was a human who ate food and experienced physical needs. Allah clarifies that all preceding messengers were likewise mortal humans subject to the natural laws of existence, such as the need for sustenance and the inevitability of death, thereby emphasizing that the nature of prophethood does not require one to be an angelic or supernatural being.

translation: Then We fulfilled the promise to them and saved them and whom We willed, and destroyed the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine attribute of fulfilling promises, indicating that Allah grants victory and salvation to His messengers and their righteous followers who remain steadfast in faith, while simultaneously executing His justice upon those who exceeded all bounds in arrogance and denial, serving as a reminder that the ultimate outcome of history favors the believers.

translation: We have certainly sent down to you a Book in which is your honor and eminence; will you not then use your reason?
interpretation: This verse highlights that the Qur'an serves as the ultimate source of nobility and distinction for those who believe in it and follow its guidance, as it elevates their status in this world and the Hereafter, and it addresses the human intellect, urging people to reflect upon the divine wisdom it contains to recognize their true purpose and value.

translation: And how many a city which was unjust have We destroyed, and raised up after it another people.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning and a lesson from history, illustrating that civilizations which persist in tyranny, disbelief, and oppression ultimately face divine destruction. It emphasizes that Allah's authority is absolute; He does not need the continuation of any specific group of people, and He is fully capable of replacing those who choose corruption with a new generation that may be more upright or simply part of His unfolding decree, reminding humanity that power is temporary and accountability is inevitable.

translation: And when they perceived Our punishment, behold, they fled from it.
interpretation: This verse describes a state of sudden panic and realization among those who rejected the truth; as soon as they experienced the tangible onset of divine retribution, their arrogance vanished and was replaced by a desperate, instinctual rush to escape, highlighting that their defiance was merely a product of worldly security and that they are entirely powerless before the reality of God's judgment.

translation: Do not flee, but return to the luxuries in which you were given comfort and to your homes, that you may be questioned.
interpretation: This verse depicts the scene of the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment being mockingly told to return to their worldly lives of arrogance, wealth, and power, which they once enjoyed, to face the reality that their possessions and status cannot shield them from the inevitable accountability for their deeds.

translation: They said, 'Woe to us! Indeed, we were wrongdoers.'
interpretation: This verse depicts the state of those who rejected the truth during their worldly life; when they are finally confronted with the inevitable reality of judgment, they transition from a state of denial to one of profound self-condemnation, acknowledging that their suffering is the direct consequence of their own choices and their refusal to heed the divine guidance.

translation: And that cry of theirs did not cease until We made them like a harvested field, extinguished.
interpretation: This verse portrays the inevitable consequence of those who persist in their arrogance and denial of the truth; when God’s judgment finally falls upon them, they are rendered entirely powerless and lifeless, like crops that have been completely cut down and leveled, signifying that their influence, power, and defiance are utterly silenced and erased from the earth.

translation: And We did not create the heaven and the earth and whatever is between them in play.
interpretation: God clarifies that the creation of the heavens, the earth, and everything contained within them was not an act of vain amusement, entertainment, or pointlessness; rather, it was established upon profound wisdom, absolute truth, and a purposeful design intended to manifest His power, fulfill His justice, and serve as a testing ground for His creation.

translation: Had We wished to take a pastime, We could have taken it from Our presence, if We were to do so.
interpretation: Allah explains that He is far above the concept of having a spouse, child, or any form of amusement; if He had intended to create a reality beyond His own divine nature for the sake of diversion—which is something He does not do—He would have created it from within His own dominion and according to His own absolute will, rather than requiring the existence of worldly beings or companions to fulfill such a purpose.

translation: Rather, We dash the truth against falsehood, and it destroys it, and thereupon it departs. And for you is destruction from that which you describe.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the inevitable triumph of truth over falsehood by using the metaphor of a physical blow to the head; just as a crushing strike leaves the brain incapacitated, the divine truth acts as a potent, undeniable force that exposes and annihilates the hollow arguments of disbelievers, rendering their false claims completely powerless and transient.

translation: And to Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth. And those who are near Him are not prevented by arrogance from His worship, nor do they tire.
interpretation: The verse illustrates the absolute sovereignty of Allah over all beings in the cosmos, highlighting that even the angels, who reside in the highest proximity to His presence, are characterized by two traits: profound humility that prevents any sense of self-importance or pride from hindering their obedience, and an indefatigable devotion that keeps them in constant worship without ever experiencing physical or spiritual exhaustion.

translation: They exalt Him night and day, and they do not slacken.
interpretation: This verse describes the angels, indicating that their constant glorification of Allah is an innate, perpetual state of being that is inherent to their nature, such that they never experience fatigue, weariness, or a moment of distraction from their devotion to their Creator.

translation: Or have they taken gods from the earth who can resurrect the dead?
interpretation: This verse serves as a rhetorical challenge to the polytheists, pointing out the absurdity of their worship by highlighting that the deities they created from the earth possess no power to give life or perform resurrection, thereby emphasizing that only the Creator of the heavens and the earth holds the power to bring the dead back to life.

translation: Had there been within the heavens and earth gods besides Allah, they both would have been ruined. So exalted is Allah, Lord of the Throne, above what they describe.
interpretation: This verse serves as a rational proof for the oneness of God, explaining that the perfect order, balance, and harmony of the universe necessitate a single, unified Will; if multiple deities with independent powers existed, their conflicting desires and decrees would inevitably lead to chaos, contradiction, and the ultimate collapse of the cosmic structure.

translation: He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned.
interpretation: This verse establishes the absolute sovereignty and ultimate wisdom of Allah, affirming that because His actions are rooted in perfect knowledge, divine justice, and complete authority, He is not subject to being held accountable by His creation; conversely, human beings, as subjects of His creation who possess limited understanding, will inevitably be held accountable for their deeds, choices, and responsibilities before Him.

translation: Or have they taken gods besides Him? Say, 'Bring your proof. This is the message of those with me and the message of those before me.' But most of them do not know the truth, so they are averse.
interpretation: Allah commands the Prophet to challenge the polytheists by demanding clear evidence for their worship of false deities, asserting that neither the Quran, which guides those who believe in it, nor the scriptures of the previous prophets contain any sanction for associating partners with God. The verse highlights that the rejection of monotheism stems from a lack of true knowledge and an intentional turning away from the clear, established truth.

translation: And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no deity except Me, so worship Me.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the core essence of the divine message has remained unchanging throughout human history; the fundamental purpose of prophethood is to call humanity toward the singular worship of Allah, stripping away all forms of polytheism and directing all acts of devotion and submission exclusively to the Creator.

translation: And they say, 'The Most Merciful has taken a son.' Exalted is He! Rather, they are but honored servants.
interpretation: This verse refutes the blasphemous claims of those who attribute offspring to Allah, affirming His absolute transcendence and freedom from such human limitations, while clarifying that those whom the polytheists regard as divine beings—such as the angels—are merely honored servants who do not possess any divinity or partnership with God.

translation: They do not precede Him in speech, and they act by His command.
interpretation: This verse describes the absolute obedience and total submission of the angels to Allah, highlighting that they neither initiate speech nor take any action without His prior permission and direct instruction, thus reflecting their state of perfect alignment with the Divine Will.

translation: He knows what is before them and what will be after them, and they cannot intercede except for one whom He approves, and they, from fear of Him, are apprehensive.
interpretation: God possesses absolute and comprehensive knowledge of all events that have occurred in the past and everything that will transpire in the future, meaning nothing is hidden from Him. Furthermore, the angels or any other intercessors occupy a station of total submission and humility; they lack the authority to advocate for any individual on the Day of Judgment unless God has explicitly granted them permission to do so out of His grace, and even then, these intercessors are themselves in a constant state of awe and reverence, profoundly concerned about their own standing before the majesty and greatness of their Creator.

translation: And whoever among them says, 'Indeed, I am a god besides Him' - that one We will recompense with Hell. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse establishes that any being among the creation who arrogantly claims divinity for themselves—defying the absolute oneness of Allah—will face the ultimate consequence of eternal punishment in Hell, as such a claim is the pinnacle of injustice, constituting the most egregious form of transgression against the Creator and the objective truth of existence.

translation: Have those who disbelieved not considered that the heavens and the earth were a joined entity, and We separated them and made from water every living thing? Then will they not believe?
interpretation: The verse highlights the divine act of creation, pointing out that the heavens and the earth originated as a singular, unified mass before Allah separated them into their current distinct states. Furthermore, it emphasizes that all biological life is fundamentally dependent upon water, serving as an undeniable empirical sign of a Creator's design that should compel the disbelievers to acknowledge His power and existence.

translation: And We placed within the earth firmly set mountains, lest it should shift with them, and We made therein paths as passages that they might be guided.
interpretation: Allah explains that He created mountains as stabilizers for the Earth to prevent it from shaking or becoming unstable for its inhabitants, while simultaneously creating mountain passes and natural corridors to facilitate travel and navigation, ensuring that people can move between regions to seek their livelihood and find their way to their destinations, which serves as a manifestation of Allah's mercy and wisdom in ordering the physical world for human benefit.

translation: And We made the sky a protected ceiling, but they, from its signs, are turning away.
interpretation: Allah signifies that the heavens have been established as a secure and guarded canopy for the earth, structured with such precision and stability that it does not collapse. Despite this overwhelming display of creative power, deliberate order, and the undeniable signs of divine governance present within the celestial bodies and the atmosphere, the disbelievers choose to remain indifferent and neglectful, failing to reflect upon these phenomena as evidence of their Creator.

translation: And it is He who created the night and the day and the sun and the moon; all [heavenly bodies] in an orbit are swimming.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and precise design of Allah in the creation of the cosmos, highlighting that the rhythmic alternation of time and the motion of celestial bodies are not random occurrences but are governed by divine laws that keep them moving in perpetual, orderly paths within their respective orbits.

translation: And We did not grant to any human before you immortality; so if you die, are they the ones who will remain forever?
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine consolation to the Prophet Muhammad, reminding him that the cycle of life and death is a universal law that applies to all human beings, including prophets. By highlighting that no predecessor was granted eternal life on earth, God rebukes the disbelievers who awaited the Prophet's death to see his message vanish; it asserts that death is an inevitable end for everyone, and therefore, their hopes of outlasting the truth or escaping accountability through his demise are entirely futile.

translation: Every soul will taste death. And We test you with evil and with good as trial; and to Us you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse establishes that mortality is an inescapable reality for all living beings, serving as a reminder that worldly life is a transient testing ground rather than a final destination. The phrase 'We test you with evil and with good' signifies that God subjects humanity to alternating states of hardship—such as illness, poverty, or distress—and prosperity—such as health, wealth, or success—not to determine the outcome of their lives (as God already knows it), but to manifest the truth of their character through their reactions of patience and gratitude, ultimately leading them back to their Creator to be held accountable for how they navigated these trials.

translation: And when those who disbelieved see you, they take you not except in mockery, saying, 'Is this the one who mentions your gods?' while they, at the mention of the Most Merciful, are disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse highlights the stubborn arrogance of the polytheists, who mocked the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) for challenging their idol worship; their derision was not merely a reaction to his message, but a symptom of their deep-seated refusal to acknowledge the true nature of God's mercy, as they purposefully ignored the mention of the الرحمن (The Most Merciful) in favor of their own fabricated deities.

translation: Man was created of haste. I will show you My signs, so do not impatiently urge Me.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inherent nature of human beings to be hasty, impatient, and eager for results, often desiring things before their appointed time. Allah addresses this tendency by assuring believers that His signs, judgments, and the fulfillment of His promises will inevitably manifest in due course according to His divine wisdom, thereby instructing them to restrain their impatience and place their trust in His timing rather than seeking to hasten what He has decreed.

translation: And they say, 'When will this promise be [fulfilled], if you should be truthful?'
interpretation: The disbelievers are questioning the reality of the Day of Judgment, not out of a genuine desire for knowledge, but as a form of mockery and skepticism; they challenge the Prophet Muhammad and the believers to provide a specific date for the resurrection, thinking that the lack of a defined timeline serves as evidence against its eventual occurrence.

translation: If only those who disbelieved knew [the time] when they will not be able to ward off the Fire from their faces nor from their backs, and they will not be helped.
interpretation: This verse serves as a profound warning, highlighting the helplessness of those who reject the truth. It describes a future reality where, upon encountering the Fire, the disbelievers will find no mechanism of defense or protection. The imagery of the fire surrounding them from both the front and the back emphasizes that there is no escape and no sanctuary; furthermore, the inability to receive aid signifies that their worldly alliances, false deities, or pride will offer them no support against the inescapable consequences of their denial.

translation: Rather, it will come upon them suddenly and bewilder them, and they will not be able to avert it, nor will they be reprieved.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute inevitability and suddenness of the Hour of Judgment, illustrating that it will descend upon the disbelievers at a moment when they are entirely unprepared and heedless. Their state of 'bewilderment' reflects a profound paralyzing shock that strips them of any power to defend against the divine decree or to bargain for a delay, underscoring the finality of their accountability once the reality of the afterlife manifests.

translation: And certainly were messengers ridiculed before you, but those who mocked them were enveloped by that which they used to ridicule.
interpretation: This verse serves as a source of solace for the Prophet Muhammad and the believers, reminding them that the mockery directed toward them by disbelievers is not a new phenomenon, but a historic pattern faced by all previous messengers; it conveys the divine assurance that the consequences of such arrogance will inevitably return to haunt the mockers themselves, as Allah's justice ensures that their derision becomes the very instrument of their downfall and ultimate humiliation.

translation: Say, 'Who can protect you at night or by day from the Most Merciful?' But they are, from the remembrance of their Lord, turning away.
interpretation: The verse serves as a rhetorical challenge to those who deny God's sovereignty, asking them to identify any entity capable of shielding them from His divine decree or punishment should He choose to unleash it upon them. By highlighting that no one can guard them against the will of the Most Merciful, the verse exposes the inconsistency of their hearts: they live in complete reliance on the constant provision and safety that only He grants, yet they simultaneously distance themselves from acknowledging and obeying Him.

translation: Or do they have gods that can defend them against Us? They are unable to help themselves, nor can they be protected from Us.
interpretation: This verse serves as a rhetorical challenge to the polytheists, emphasizing that the idols they worship possess neither the power to prevent Allah's divine decree nor the strength to shield their worshippers from His judgment, highlighting the utter futility of turning to inanimate objects for salvation or protection when they lack even the agency to preserve their own existence.

translation: But We have given these people and their forefathers comforts, until life became long for them. Do they not see that We gradually reduce the land from its borders? Are they the ones who will prevail?
interpretation: The verse highlights the deceptive nature of worldly prosperity and the inevitability of the decline of falsehood. By granting the disbelievers long lives and worldly enjoyments, God is testing them, while the gradual reduction of the land from its borders serves as a metaphor for the shrinking influence of the unjust, the loss of their territory, and the constant encroachment of truth upon falsehood until it eventually overcomes them entirely.

translation: Say, 'I only warn you by revelation.' But the deaf do not hear the call when they are warned.
interpretation: The Prophet is instructed to declare that his message is not of his own invention but originates from divine revelation, yet those whose hearts are hardened by stubborn disbelief are likened to the deaf, as they are incapable of perceiving or responding to the truth even when it is clearly presented to them.

translation: And if a touch of the punishment of your Lord should touch them, they will surely say, 'O woe to us! Indeed, we have been wrongdoers.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the inherent nature of human denial in the face of divine consequences; when the disbelievers experience even a fleeting or minor taste of the affliction they previously mocked or denied, their arrogance instantly collapses into a realization of their own transgression, demonstrating that their obstinacy is not based on genuine doubt, but on a temporary state of heedlessness that vanishes the moment the truth becomes undeniable.

translation: And We will set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul will be treated unjustly at all. And if there is [even] the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it forth. And sufficient are We as accountant.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, Allah will establish perfectly precise standards of justice to weigh the deeds of every individual, ensuring that not a single act—no matter how trivial or microscopic it may seem—is overlooked or misjudged. This absolute precision serves as a reminder that the Divine reckoning is beyond human fallibility, as Allah encompasses all hidden and manifest actions, leaving no room for inequity and providing complete assurance that every effort will be rightfully acknowledged and accounted for.

translation: And We gave Moses and Aaron the Criterion (Furqan) and a light and a reminder for the righteous.
interpretation: This verse highlights that Allah bestowed upon Moses and Aaron three distinct gifts: the 'Criterion' (al-Furqan), which refers to the Torah as a means to distinguish between truth and falsehood; 'light' (diya'), representing the guidance that illuminates the path of faith and removes the darkness of ignorance; and a 'reminder' (dhikr), which serves to keep the believers mindful of their covenant with Allah and the ultimate truths of existence, specifically designed for those who possess taqwa (God-consciousness), as they are the ones who truly benefit from and heed this divine guidance.

translation: Those who fear their Lord unseen, and they are of the Hour apprehensive.
interpretation: The verse highlights the spiritual excellence of the believers who maintain their consciousness of God and piety even when they are alone, away from the eyes of people, coupled with a deep sense of cautious vigilance and profound concern regarding the inevitable occurrence of the Day of Judgment, which drives them to prepare for their meeting with their Creator.

translation: And this is a blessed reminder which We have sent down; so are you then deniers of it?
interpretation: This verse highlights that the Qur'an is a source of abundant goodness, spiritual guidance, and divine light, emphasizing that its message is clearly beneficial for humanity. By calling it a 'blessed reminder,' Allah asserts its intrinsic value and truth, while simultaneously questioning the rationality of those who reject or deny such an obvious and mercy-filled revelation, suggesting that their denial stems from obstinacy rather than a lack of evidence.

translation: And We had certainly given Abraham his sound judgment before, and We were of him well-knowing.
interpretation: This verse highlights that Allah granted Prophet Ibrahim the ability to distinguish between truth and falsehood, and to discern right from wrong, from an early age due to his inherent purity and willingness to seek the truth, proving that his subsequent devotion and prophethood were grounded in a lifetime of wisdom and divine guidance that Allah recognized and validated.

translation: When he said to his father and his people, 'What are these statues to which you are devoted?'
interpretation: Ibrahim (peace be upon him) addresses his father and his community with a question that serves as a subtle, rational refutation of their idolatry, aiming to expose the logical inconsistency of worshipping inanimate objects that lack the power to help, harm, or respond, thereby challenging them to reflect upon the folly of their blind devotion.

translation: They said, 'We found our fathers worshipping them.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the common psychological reliance of polytheists on ancestral tradition as their primary justification for belief, demonstrating how blind adherence to inherited customs and the weight of social conformity often override critical reflection, logic, and the pursuit of objective truth regarding the oneness of God.

translation: He said, 'You were certainly, you and your fathers, in clear error.'
interpretation: Ibrahim (peace be upon him) is highlighting to his people that the polytheism and idol worship they and their ancestors practiced is a state of manifest deviation from the truth, as they have abandoned the clear path of worshipping the One True God and have instead directed their devotion toward powerless statues that neither benefit nor harm them.

translation: They said, 'Have you brought us the truth, or are you just one of those who play/joke?'
interpretation: The people of the Prophet, upon hearing his message, rejected the possibility that it could be a serious divine revelation. They perceived the truth as so far removed from their established customs and ignorance that they framed their skepticism as an accusation of mockery, reflecting their inability to reconcile the gravity of the prophetic message with their own superficial worldview.

translation: He said, 'Rather, your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, who created them, and I, of that, am among the witnesses.'
interpretation: The Prophet Ibrahim refutes the false claims of his people by directing their attention to the celestial and earthly domains, emphasizing that the Creator is the only One who brought these complex structures into existence from nothingness; by affirming his status as a witness, he underscores that this truth is not merely a theoretical claim but a certain reality founded upon clear intellectual evidence and spiritual insight.

translation: And by Allah, I will surely plan against your idols after you have turned and gone away.
