translation: O you who have believed, do not follow the footsteps of Satan. And whoever follows the footsteps of Satan - indeed, he enjoins immorality and wrongdoing. And if not for the favor of Allah upon you and His mercy, not one of you would have been pure, ever, but Allah purifies whom He wills, and Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine warning against the insidious nature of sin, highlighting that Satan does not lead a believer to major transgression all at once, but rather through a gradual process of small, seemingly insignificant steps. It emphasizes that human moral purity is not achieved through one's own independent strength or self-righteousness, but is fundamentally a manifestation of Allah’s grace and guidance, reminding the believer that without Divine intervention and mercy, the soul would remain susceptible to the corrupting influences of evil.

translation: And let not those among you who possess grace and wealth swear not to give to the kindred, the needy, and the emigrants for the cause of Allah. Let them pardon and overlook. Do you not love that Allah should forgive you? And Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: This verse was revealed regarding Abu Bakr as-Siddiq, who swore to stop financially supporting his relative Mistah bin Uthathah after Mistah participated in the false accusations against Aisha. Allah calls upon the believers who are blessed with material abundance and spiritual virtue not to let their anger or personal grievances prevent them from continuing their charitable support to those in need, even if those people have committed personal offenses against them. It emphasizes that the highest form of character is to rise above emotional retaliation by exercising forgiveness and pardon, reminding the believer that if they desire Allah to overlook their own shortcomings and sins on the Day of Judgment, they must mirror that divine mercy by overlooking the faults of others in this life.

translation: Indeed, those who accuse chaste, unaware, believing women are cursed in this world and the Hereafter, and they will have a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse serves as a severe warning against the heinous act of slander and false accusation directed toward chaste women, emphasizing that such behavior is a major sin in Islam because it destroys reputations and compromises the integrity of the family unit; therefore, God imposes a harsh spiritual and social condemnation upon those who propagate such lies, ensuring they are alienated from divine mercy both in this life and the next.

translation: On the Day when their tongues, their hands, and their feet will bear witness against them as to what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the absolute impossibility of concealing one's deeds on the Day of Judgment, as Allah will grant the limbs of the sinner the power of speech to testify truthfully about every action committed in secret or in public, thereby leaving the individual with no argument or excuse to deny their transgressions.

translation: On that Day, Allah will pay them in full their due recompense, and they will know that Allah is the Manifest Truth.
interpretation: On the Day of Resurrection, Allah will fully and precisely execute His judgment upon all people, granting the righteous their reward and the disbelievers their punishment in accordance with His perfect justice; at that moment, every soul will perceive with absolute, undeniable clarity that Allah is the true Sovereign whose existence, power, and authority are self-evident and manifest to all, leaving no room for the doubts or denials that previously existed in the worldly life.

translation: Corrupt women are for corrupt men, and corrupt men are for corrupt women; and good women are for good men, and good men are for good women. Those are innocent of what they say; for them is forgiveness and a noble provision.
interpretation: This verse establishes a divine principle of moral compatibility, asserting that there is a natural affinity between souls of similar character; just as the corrupt are naturally drawn to their own kind, those who are pure and virtuous belong with those who share their righteousness. The verse specifically serves to vindicate the Prophet Muhammad and Aisha from the false accusations leveled against them, declaring that the nature of their pure characters is fundamentally incompatible with the accusations of immorality, thereby confirming their innocence and promising them divine grace and a generous reward in the hereafter.

translation: O you who have believed, do not enter houses other than your own until you ascertain welcome and greet their inhabitants. That is better for you; perhaps you will be reminded.
interpretation: This verse establishes a vital social ethic regarding privacy and the sanctity of the home, commanding believers to seek permission and offer greetings before entering a space that is not their own. By requiring 'isti'nas' (seeking familiarity or consent) and the 'salam' (greeting of peace), the Qur'an protects the inhabitants from intrusion and ensures that no one is caught in a state of vulnerability or discomfort, thereby fostering mutual respect, maintaining modesty, and preventing social friction within the community.

translation: And if you find no one therein, do not enter until permission has been given to you. And if it is said to you, 'Go back,' then go back; it is purer for you. And Allah is Knowing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse establishes the etiquette of privacy and personal boundaries in social interactions, teaching that entering another person's home without explicit permission is forbidden regardless of whether the house is occupied or empty. The command to turn back when denied entry is framed as a moral purification for the believer, emphasizing that respecting the sanctity of others' spaces preserves the dignity of both the visitor and the owner, and that Allah is fully aware of whether one's intentions in seeking entry are respectful or intrusive.

translation: There is no blame upon you for entering houses not inhabited, in which there is convenience for you. And Allah knows what you reveal and what you conceal.
interpretation: This verse grants permission to enter places such as inns, warehouses, or unoccupied buildings intended for public utility or specific services without needing explicit permission from an owner, provided there is a legitimate need and one does not violate the privacy or sanctity of others, reminding believers that God is fully aware of their intentions and hidden motives when accessing such spaces.

translation: Tell the believing men to reduce [some] of their vision and guard their private parts. That is purer for them. Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what they do.
interpretation: This verse establishes the principle of modesty and self-restraint as a fundamental requirement for the spiritual integrity of a believer. By commanding men to lower their gaze, Allah instructs them to refrain from looking at what is forbidden, as the eyes are the gateway to the heart's desires; this outward act of discipline protects the individual from the corruption of the soul and maintains the purity of society by preventing the spread of temptation and illicit behaviors.

translation: And tell the believing women to reduce [some] of their vision and guard their private parts and not expose their adornment except that which [necessarily] appears thereof and to wrap [a portion of] their headcovers over their chests and not expose their adornment except to their husbands, their fathers, their husbands' fathers, their sons, their husbands' sons, their brothers, their brothers' sons, their sisters' sons, their women, that which their right hands possess, or those male attendants having no physical desire, or children who are not yet aware of the private aspects of women. And let them not stamp their feet to make known what they conceal of their adornment. And turn to Allah in repentance, all of you, O believers, that you might succeed.
interpretation: This verse establishes a comprehensive framework for modesty and moral preservation within the Muslim community, directing women to lower their gaze and protect their chastity, which are the foundations of social purity. By commanding them to cover their beauty and adornments—while permitting exceptions for intimate family members and those who naturally lack sexual interest—Allah intends to close the avenues that lead to social corruption and illicit desire. The prohibition against stamping one's feet highlights that even subtle displays intended to draw attention to hidden ornaments are discouraged, emphasizing that the preservation of dignity and the prevention of temptation are divine priorities for both personal integrity and the health of the community at large.

translation: And marry off the unmarried among you and the righteous among your male slaves and female slaves. If they should be poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty, and Allah is all-Encompassing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine command for society to facilitate marriage for those who are single, emphasizing that financial constraints should not be a barrier to establishing families. It provides a spiritual assurance that Allah will bestow prosperity upon those who seek to maintain chastity through marriage, reminding the believers that His provisions are vast and that He is fully aware of the needs and circumstances of His servants, thus encouraging trust in His providence over earthly anxieties about poverty.

translation: And let those who find not the financial means for marriage keep themselves chaste, until Allah enriches them of His bounty. And such of your slaves as seek a writing (of emancipation), give them such writing, if you know that they are good and trustworthy. And give them something yourselves out of the wealth of Allah which He has bestowed upon you. And force not your slave-girls to prostitution, if they desire chastity, in order that you may make a gain in the perishable goods of this worldly life. But if anyone compels them, then Allah, after their compulsion, is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse commands believers to maintain purity through self-restraint and patience when marriage is not feasible, while simultaneously establishing a social obligation to facilitate the emancipation of enslaved individuals who seek their freedom, provided they demonstrate integrity. It explicitly prohibits the exploitation of vulnerable women for prostitution, declaring that such moral corruption is a grave sin, while emphasizing that the responsibility for the transgression lies with the oppressors who coerce them, rather than the victims of that coercion, thereby opening a door of divine mercy for those forced into sin against their will.

translation: And We have certainly sent down to you distinct verses and an example from those who passed on before you and an admonition for those who fear Allah.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine reminder that the Qur'an contains clear guidance through its revelations, illustrative accounts of historical nations whose stories act as mirrors for the present, and profound exhortations designed to awaken the hearts of the righteous, encouraging them to align their actions with piety and avoid the pitfalls that led previous generations to ruin.

translation: In houses which Allah has ordered to be raised and that His name be mentioned therein; exalting Him within them in the morning and the evenings.
interpretation: These houses refer to mosques, which are places designated for the worship of Allah, elevated in status and purity, where believers engage in the remembrance of Allah and constant prayer, acknowledging His absolute oneness and transcendence at the beginning and the end of each day.

translation: [Are] men whom neither commerce nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah and performance of prayer and giving of zakah. They fear a Day in which the hearts and the eyes will [fearfully] turn about.
interpretation: These individuals are described as being so firmly rooted in their devotion that their worldly pursuits and commercial transactions never occupy their hearts or divert their focus from the worship of their Creator, because they maintain a constant awareness of the Day of Judgment, a time of such overwhelming gravity and transformation that even the most resolute hearts and observant eyes will be seized by profound terror and confusion.

translation: That Allah may reward them for the best of what they were doing and increase them [even more] from His bounty. And Allah gives provision to whom He wills without account.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the boundless generosity of Allah, demonstrating that His reward for the believers is not merely a fair exchange for their deeds, but a gracious enhancement; He accepts their sincere efforts, evaluates them by their highest intentions and actions, and then surpasses that value with an additional overflow of divine grace that exceeds human merit, confirming that His provision is limited neither by worldly standards nor by human calculation.

translation: But those who disbelieved - their deeds are like a mirage in a lowland which a thirsty one thinks is water until, when he comes to it, he finds it is nothing but finds Allah before Him, who will pay him in full his due; and Allah is swift in account.
interpretation: This verse presents a profound metaphor for the state of the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment; just as a thirsty traveler in a vast desert sees a glimmering expanse that promises life-giving water only to discover it is an optical illusion of no substance, the disbelievers' worldly deeds—which they performed with pride and expectation of merit—will vanish upon meeting their Creator. They will realize that their efforts were devoid of the true foundation of faith, leaving them spiritually empty, at which point they will encounter the inescapable reality of divine justice where they are held fully accountable for their choices.

translation: Or [they are] like darknesses within an unfathomable sea which is covered by waves, upon which are waves, over which are clouds - darknesses, some of them upon others. When one puts out his hand [therein], he can hardly see it. And he to whom Allah has not granted light - for him there is no light.
interpretation: This verse describes the state of the disbeliever who has rejected the truth, likening their spiritual condition to someone trapped in multiple layers of darkness in the depths of an ocean. Just as one in such depths is completely surrounded by physical darkness and cannot see their own hand, the disbeliever is enveloped by the darkness of their own disbelief, ignorance, and worldly distractions. Because they have willfully turned away from the divine guidance that Allah provides, they find themselves in a state of utter spiritual blindness where they can no longer perceive the light of faith or the path of truth, leaving them completely bereft of any guidance unless Allah chooses to illuminate their hearts.

translation: Do you not see that to Allah prostrates whoever is in the heavens and the earth and the birds with wings outspread? Each has known its prayer and its glorification, and Allah is Aware of what they do.
interpretation: This verse highlights that the entire universe, including all celestial bodies, living creatures, and even birds in flight, is in a constant state of worship and glorification of Allah. It suggests that every entity in existence has been instilled by its Creator with a unique, innate form of devotion and a specific manner of praise that aligns with its own nature and purpose, affirming that nothing in the cosmos is disconnected from the awareness or the command of the Divine.

translation: And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and to Allah is the final destination.
interpretation: This verse establishes that Allah is the absolute Sovereign and sole Owner of all creation, meaning that nothing occurs within the heavens or upon the earth outside of His decree, power, and oversight. By reminding humanity that the final destination is back to Him, the verse serves as an admonition that every soul will inevitably stand before its Creator to account for its deeds, highlighting that ultimate authority rests with Him both in this life and in the eternal hereafter.

translation: Do you not see that Allah drives clouds, then joins them together, then turns them into a heap, and you see the rain emerge from within them? And He sends down from the sky, from mountains within it, hail; He strikes with it whom He wills and averts it from whom He wills. The flash of its lightning almost takes away the eyesight.
interpretation: This verse directs human observation toward the precise atmospheric mechanics orchestrated by Divine power, illustrating the transformative stages of cloud formation, precipitation, and the release of lightning. It serves as a reminder of Allah's absolute sovereignty over the physical laws of nature, highlighting that natural phenomena like the intensity of lightning or the distribution of rain are not mere accidents but deliberate manifestations of His will, capable of bringing both blessing and adversity according to His perfect wisdom.

translation: Allah alternates the night and the day. Indeed in that is a lesson for those who possess vision.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom behind the cyclical nature of time, suggesting that the constant transition from darkness to light and back is not a random occurrence but a deliberate sign meant to awaken the human intellect; by observing this rhythmic change, a reflective person perceives the power and constancy of the Creator, realizing that just as the world undergoes these inevitable shifts, human conditions are also subject to change, which should drive the wise to seek the eternal truths that remain constant beyond the transient nature of worldly life.

translation: And Allah has created every living creature from water. So among them are those that move on their bellies, and among them are those that walk on two legs, and among them are those that walk on four. Allah creates what He wills. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom and power behind the creation of life, establishing that all living organisms share a fundamental biological origin rooted in water. By describing the diverse methods of locomotion—crawling, bipedalism, and quadrupedalism—the Quran points toward the boundless creative capability of God, asserting that the vast biological variety observed in the animal kingdom is not a product of random chance but a manifestation of a deliberate, omnipotent design that sustains and regulates every form of life according to its unique nature.

translation: We have certainly sent down distinct verses. And Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has provided clear, unequivocal revelation to guide humanity, yet the internal orientation of the heart is the deciding factor in who accepts this guidance; therefore, divine guidance is a bestowal granted by Allah to those who demonstrate a sincere inclination toward the truth, leading them to a path that is free of deviation and aligned with His purpose.

translation: And they say, 'We have believed in Allah and in the Messenger, and we obey'; then a party of them turns away after that. And those are not believers.
interpretation: This verse exposes the contradiction of those who profess faith and obedience with their tongues while their actions demonstrate hypocrisy; it teaches that true faith is not merely a verbal claim but must be validated by consistent submission to the commands of Allah and His Messenger, as turning away in disobedience after claiming belief negates the sincerity of that faith.

translation: And when they are invited to Allah and His Messenger to judge between them, behold, a party of them turns away.
interpretation: This verse exposes the hypocrisy of those who claim faith but reject the authority of the Prophet Muhammad; it highlights that their turning away is not due to a search for truth, but rather an act of defiance against divine justice, as they fear a verdict that might conflict with their personal desires or worldly interests.

translation: But if the truth is on their side, they come to him in willing submission.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of those who turn away from God's judgment; when they suspect that the legal or moral outcome will favor their own interests, they rush to accept the divine authority with complete obedience, not out of true faith or submission to the truth, but merely because the verdict aligns with their worldly desires.

translation: Is there disease in their hearts, or have they doubted, or do they fear that Allah will be unjust to them, or His Messenger? Rather, it is they who are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse exposes the psychological state of the hypocrites who refuse to submit to the judgment of Allah and His Messenger. It suggests that their reluctance stems from one of three flaws: either their hearts are corrupted by hypocrisy and disbelief, they lack certainty in the truth of the message, or they harbor a false, paranoid suspicion that divine justice is oppressive. The verse concludes that their refusal is not based on any legitimate grievance or rational doubt, but rather originates from their own inherent injustice and rebellion against the truth.

translation: The only statement of the [true] believers when they are called to Allah and His Messenger to judge between them is that they say, 'We hear and we obey.' And those are the successful.
interpretation: This verse establishes the hallmark of true faith as the immediate, unhesitating, and absolute submission to the divine will; it highlights that a believer’s spiritual integrity is measured by their willingness to bypass personal desires or social pressures in favor of the Prophet’s judgment, asserting that such total surrender to God's law is the only path to achieving ultimate salvation and fulfillment.

translation: And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger and fears Allah and is conscious of Him - it is those who are the attainers of success.
interpretation: This verse establishes that true success in both this life and the hereafter is attained through a synthesis of four components: submission to the divine commands, adherence to the prophetic model, a heart filled with reverence for the Majesty of God, and a state of constant mindful caution that prevents one from violating His prohibitions.

translation: And they swear by Allah their strongest oaths that if you ordered them, they would surely go forth. Say, 'Do not swear; [such] obedience is known. Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with that which you do.'
interpretation: The verse addresses those who claim to be obedient to the Prophet (peace be upon him) through mere verbal pledges and exaggerated oaths. Allah reveals that their claims of readiness to sacrifice are false, as true obedience is demonstrated through consistent, righteous deeds and sincere adherence to commands rather than empty promises, emphasizing that Allah is fully aware of the hypocrisy hidden in their hearts and the insincerity of their outward professions.

translation: Say, "Obey Allah and obey the Messenger; but if you turn away - then upon him is only that [duty] with which he has been charged, and upon you is that with which you have been charged. And if you obey him, you will be [rightly] guided. And there is not upon the Messenger except the clear conveyance."
interpretation: The verse clarifies that the responsibility of the Prophet is limited to conveying the message clearly, and he is not accountable for the deeds of those who reject it. Each individual is responsible for their own obedience or disobedience; therefore, following the Prophet is the sole condition for receiving divine guidance, as he serves only as a messenger tasked with delivering the truth without the power to force belief upon anyone.

translation: Allah has promised those among you who believe and do righteous deeds that He will surely grant them succession upon the earth, just as He granted it to those before them, and that He will surely establish for them their religion which He has preferred for them, and that He will surely substitute for them, after their fear, security, [for] they worship Me, not associating anything with Me. But whoever disbelieves after that - then those are the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine guarantee that moral integrity and steadfast faith are the true foundations for worldly authority; Allah promises that when a community truly embodies the teachings of their faith and remains loyal to the oneness of God, He will transform their state of vulnerability and persecution into one of stability, security, and empowered leadership, provided they uphold their commitment to monotheism and righteous conduct.

translation: And establish prayer and give zakah and obey the Messenger - that you may receive mercy.
interpretation: The verse serves as a divine instruction emphasizing that the path to attaining Allah's mercy lies in a balanced commitment to spiritual devotion through prayer, social responsibility through the mandatory charity of zakah, and the practical application of faith by following the guidance of the Prophet Muhammad, as his example is the definitive expression of how to implement Allah's commandments in daily life.

translation: Never think that the disbelievers are capable of frustrating [Allah] upon the earth. Their refuge is the Fire, and wretched is the destination.
interpretation: Do not let the outward strength or apparent autonomy of those who reject the truth lead you to believe that they can ever escape the reach of Allah’s sovereignty or evade His judgment. No matter how much power they possess on earth, they remain entirely within His grasp, and their ultimate end will be the Hellfire, which serves as the most miserable and final abode for their rebellion.

translation: O you who have believed, let those whom your right hands possess and those who have not [yet] reached puberty among you ask permission of you [at three times]: before the dawn prayer, and when you put aside your clothing [for rest] at noon, and after the night prayer. [These are] three times of privacy for you. There is no blame upon you or upon them beyond these [times], for they circulate among you, some of you, of others. Thus does Allah make clear to you the verses; and Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse establishes a formal system of domestic privacy and manners, requiring dependents and minors to seek permission before entering private chambers during specific times of day when adults are most likely to be in a state of undress or rest. By designating these three specific timeframes, Allah provides a structured approach to preserving modesty within the household, while simultaneously acknowledging that social interaction among family members and servants is necessary and permissible at other times of the day, thereby balancing the need for personal sanctity with the realities of daily cohabitation.

translation: And when the children among you reach puberty, let them ask permission [at all times], as those before them have asked permission. Thus does Allah make clear to you His verses; and Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse establishes that once a child reaches the age of physical maturity, they are no longer exempt from the social regulations governing privacy and modesty within the household. It mandates that they must adopt the same etiquette as adults—specifically the requirement to seek permission before entering private quarters—thereby ensuring that the preservation of dignity and the protection of private space are upheld as fundamental societal values throughout every stage of human development.

translation: And women of post-menstrual age who have no desire for marriage - there is no blame upon them for putting aside their outer garments [outer cloaks] provided they do not display adornment; but to modestly refrain is better for them. And Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse grants a concession to elderly women who have passed the age of childbearing and no longer hold expectations or desires for marriage, allowing them to lay aside their outer garments like the jilbab or shawl, provided they do not use this liberty as a pretext to display jewelry or beauty intended for ornamentation, yet it simultaneously encourages them to maintain modesty as a virtuous act of piety that is more pleasing to Allah, who is fully aware of their intentions and their actions.

translation: There is no blame upon the blind nor any blame upon the lame nor any blame upon the sick nor upon yourselves if you eat from your own houses or the houses of your fathers or the houses of your mothers or the houses of your brothers or the houses of your sisters or the houses of your paternal uncles or the houses of your paternal aunts or the houses of your maternal uncles or the houses of your maternal aunts or [from houses] whose keys you possess or [from the house of] your friend. There is no blame upon you whether you eat together or separately. But when you enter houses, give greetings of peace upon each other—a greeting from Allah, blessed and good. Thus does Allah make clear to you the verses [of ordinances] that you might understand.
interpretation: This verse serves to remove social barriers and apprehensions regarding sharing meals among family members and close friends, establishing that the bonds of kinship and intimacy permit eating in each other's homes without needing explicit permission for every instance. It emphasizes the sanctity of interpersonal relationships and the spirit of communal harmony, while simultaneously teaching etiquette and the importance of invoking Allah's peace upon entering any dwelling, thereby sanctifying social interactions and reinforcing the divine command to maintain ties of love and mutual respect within the community.

translation: The believers are only those who believe in Allah and His Messenger and, when they are with him upon a matter of common interest, do not depart until they have asked his permission. Indeed, those who ask your permission are those who believe in Allah and His Messenger. So when they ask your permission for some affair of theirs, give permission to whom you will among them and ask forgiveness for them of Allah. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse establishes that true faith is characterized by complete submission to the authority and leadership of the Prophet, requiring that believers prioritize their collective duties to the community of faith over their individual concerns. It illustrates the necessity of maintaining discipline and unity by seeking the leader's consultation and approval before leaving communal responsibilities, framing this act of obedience and respect as a manifestation of sincere belief. The command for the Prophet to pray for their forgiveness highlights the mercy inherent in Islamic leadership, acknowledging that while human needs may arise, the bond of brotherhood and the sanctity of communal obligations must be preserved with humility and divine guidance.

translation: Do not make the calling of the Messenger among yourselves as the calling of one another. God already knows those among you who slip away, concealing themselves. So let those who disobey his command beware lest a trial strikes them or a painful punishment strikes them.
interpretation: This verse establishes the unique status of the Prophet, requiring the believers to address him with a level of respect, reverence, and formality that distinguishes his station from that of ordinary individuals. It warns those who attempt to secretly withdraw from his gatherings or disregard his instructions—treating his guidance as if it were a casual suggestion—that such insubordination invites divine displeasure, which may manifest as worldly tribulations or severe consequences in the Hereafter.

translation: Behold, to Allah belongs all that is in the heavens and the earth. He knows what state you are upon; and the Day they are returned to Him, He will inform them of what they have done. And Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse asserts the absolute sovereignty of Allah over the entire cosmos, emphasizing that because He is the sole owner and creator, He possesses perfect, comprehensive knowledge of the conditions and inner states of His servants. The verse serves as a profound reminder that human actions—whether hidden or manifest—are never obscured from Divine sight, and that the ultimate purpose of existence is the inevitable return to Him, where the reality of every deed will be fully unveiled and justly accounted for, underscoring His attribute of Omniscience.

translation: Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His Servant that he may be to the worlds a warner.
interpretation: The verse highlights the majesty of Allah, who exalted His creation by revealing the Qur'an—the 'Criterion' that distinguishes between truth and falsehood—to Prophet Muhammad. This revelation serves as a universal warning to all of humanity and the jinn, urging them to recognize the divine authority, abandon polytheism, and adhere to the guidance that leads to salvation, confirming that the Prophet's mission is not restricted to one people or time, but encompasses all of existence.

translation: He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and who has not taken a son and has not had a partner in dominion and has created each thing and determined it with [precise] determination.
interpretation: This verse establishes the absolute sovereignty and oneness of Allah, emphasizing that His dominion is comprehensive and independent of any external assistance or familial relations. By stating that He has created everything and determined it with precise measurement, it confirms that Allah is not only the Architect of the universe but also the Sustainer who maintains the balance and purpose of every created being according to His divine wisdom and eternal decree.

translation: Yet they have taken besides Him gods who create nothing, while they themselves are created, and possess no power to harm or benefit themselves, and possess no power over death, nor life, nor resurrection.
interpretation: This verse highlights the absurdity of idol worship by demonstrating the utter powerlessness of false deities; since they are created beings themselves, they lack the creative capacity of the Divine, and because they possess no authority over the fundamental cycle of existence—birth, death, and the afterlife—they are entirely unworthy of the worship, supplication, or reverence that belongs exclusively to the Creator who sustains and governs all things.

translation: And those who disbelieved say, 'This is not but a falsehood he has invented, and another people assisted him in it.' But they have committed an injustice and a lie.
interpretation: The disbelievers mockingly claim that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) did not receive divine revelation but instead fabricated the Qur'an with the help of others, such as people from the People of the Book. Allah rejects this accusation, affirming that their claim is a grave injustice against the truth and a baseless, fabricated lie intended to mislead people from the message of monotheism.

translation: And they say, 'Legends of the former peoples which he has written down, so they are dictated to him morning and afternoon.'
interpretation: The disbelievers of Mecca falsely accused Prophet Muhammad of fabricating the Qur'an by copying stories and ancient myths from past nations, claiming that he had others assist him in writing these accounts and dictating them to him at different times of the day, thereby denying its divine origin and attributing its wisdom to human composition.

translation: Say, 'It has been revealed by He who knows [every] secret within the heavens and the earth. Indeed, He is ever Forgiving and Merciful.'
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is not a human fabrication but a revelation from Allah, whose infinite knowledge encompasses all the hidden realities of the universe, and it highlights that despite human errors, Allah's nature is fundamentally defined by His capacity to pardon sins and His profound compassion toward His creation.

translation: And they said, 'What is the matter with this messenger that he eats food and walks in the markets? Why was an angel not sent down to him so he would be a warner with him?'
interpretation: The disbelievers were expressing their skepticism regarding the validity of the Prophet's mission, as they erroneously equated prophethood with supernatural existence. They believed that a true messenger should be an otherworldly being, like an angel, rather than a human who experiences physical needs such as eating or social interactions like walking in markets, failing to realize that a human messenger is necessary to serve as an accessible role model for humanity who can demonstrate how to practically implement divine laws in everyday life.

translation: Or has a treasure been bestowed upon him, or does he have a garden from which he eats? And the wrongdoers say, 'You follow only a man affected by magic.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and stubbornness of the disbelievers who demanded worldly signs, such as immense wealth or paradise-like gardens, as proofs of Prophethood; by dismissing the Prophet as 'bewitched,' they sought to invalidate his message and cast doubt on the divine nature of his revelations, effectively refusing to acknowledge the truth due to their own hardened hearts and preoccupation with material criteria.

translation: Look at how they strike comparisons for you, so they have gone astray and cannot find a way.
interpretation: The verse highlights the absurdity and confusion of those who reject the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) by describing him with contradictory and baseless labels such as a magician, a poet, or one possessed; this intellectual wandering and inability to grasp the truth causes them to lose their path to guidance and prevents them from finding any logical or spiritual justification for their disbelief.

translation: Blessed is He who, if He willed, could have made for you [something] better than that - gardens beneath which rivers flow - and could make for you palaces.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of Allah's absolute power and sovereignty, rebuking the disbelievers who mocked the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) for his lack of worldly wealth or worldly signs of prophethood. It clarifies that the worldly possessions they value are trivial in the sight of Allah, and that He is fully capable of granting His Messenger far superior rewards—such as eternal gardens and magnificent palaces—if He chooses, highlighting that prophethood is a divine selection based on spiritual merit rather than the accumulation of worldly luxury.

translation: But they deny the Hour, and We have prepared for whoever denies the Hour a Blaze.
interpretation: The verse indicates that the underlying cause of the disbelievers' persistent rejection of the truth is their fundamental denial of the Day of Judgment, leading them to disregard accountability; consequently, God declares that He has prepared a fierce, raging fire as a consequence for those who choose to live their lives denying the inevitable reality of resurrection and divine judgment.

translation: When it sees them from a distant place, they will hear its fury and roaring.
interpretation: This verse describes the personification of Hell, illustrating that it possesses a conscious, terrifying rage against the disbelievers. As soon as they come within its sight—even from a great distance—the Fire begins to boil and groan with intense indignation, signaling its readiness to punish those who rejected the truth, thereby intensifying their psychological terror before they even reach it.

translation: And when they are cast into a narrow place therein, bound in chains, they will call out there for destruction.
interpretation: This verse portrays the state of the disbelievers in Hell, where they are crowded together in a confined, distressing space, shackled in chains as a form of extreme humiliation and suffering, leading them to plead for their own annihilation or death, realizing that their punishment is eternal and inescapable.

translation: Do not call today for one destruction, but call for many destructions.
interpretation: This verse depicts the state of the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection when they realize the severity of their punishment; they are told mockingly that crying out for death or annihilation once will not suffice, as their agony is continuous and eternal, making them wish for destruction repeatedly while it remains forever beyond their reach.

translation: Say, 'Is that better or the Garden of Eternity which is promised to the righteous? It will be for them a reward and a destination.'
interpretation: This verse presents a rhetorical contrast intended to provoke reflection, juxtaposing the temporary and fleeting pleasures or punishments of this world against the eternal, unchanging, and blissful reward of Paradise. It emphasizes that for the righteous who have upheld their faith and moral duties, the ultimate destination is not merely a place of rest, but the culmination of their spiritual journey, serving as both a just recompense for their deeds and an everlasting home where they will remain secure in the presence of God's favor.

translation: For them therein is whatever they wish, abiding eternally. It is an obligation upon your Lord that is requested.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute generosity and fulfillment of Allah towards the people of Paradise, affirming that their desires will be met without limit, and that this promise is a binding commitment that Allah has taken upon Himself to honor, ensuring the believers of the certainty of their reward.

translation: And on the Day when He will gather them and that which they worship besides Allah and will say: 'Did you mislead these My servants, or did they themselves stray from the (right) path?'
interpretation: On the Day of Resurrection, Allah will confront the false deities and the idolaters in the presence of everyone to demonstrate the absurdity of polytheism. By asking the idols if they misled the people or if the people strayed on their own accord, Allah highlights that those worshiped besides Him—whether they are inanimate objects, celestial bodies, or saintly figures who never commanded such worship—are innocent of the false adoration directed at them. This question serves to expose the utter falsehood of the idolaters' beliefs and to seal their confusion, as they will realize that their deities have no power to intercede for them or even acknowledge their devotion.

translation: They will say, 'Exalted are You! It was not appropriate for us to take any allies other than You, but You provided comforts for them and their fathers until they forgot the message and became a people ruined.'
interpretation: The verse illustrates the scene on the Day of Judgment where those who were worshipped besides God, such as idols or human figures, exonerate themselves by acknowledging that the responsibility for the idolaters' misguidance lies in their own worldly indulgence; the comforts and prolonged opportunities for pleasure granted by God in this life led them to become preoccupied and negligent of the divine truth, eventually resulting in their spiritual bankruptcy and eternal loss.

translation: So they will deny you in what you say, and you will not be able to avert [punishment] or find help. And whoever among you commits injustice - We will make him taste a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine rebuke to the polytheists, informing them that their false deities, whom they claimed were intercessors or partners of God, will disavow them and reject their claims on the Day of Judgment. The phrase 'you will not be able to avert' signifies that the idolaters will be powerless to ward off the divine punishment that is destined for them, nor will they find any helpers to save them from it. Furthermore, it establishes a universal principle that whoever persists in the greatest injustice—which is polytheism (shirk)—will be made to experience a severe and agonizing retribution, highlighting that human actions carry profound eternal consequences.

translation: And We did not send before you, [O Muhammad], any of the messengers except that they ate food and walked in the markets. And We have made some of you for others a trial - will you have patience? And your Lord is ever Seeing.
interpretation: This verse addresses the skepticism of the disbelievers who questioned why a prophet should be a human who eats and walks in markets, asserting that prophethood necessitates a divine or angelic nature. Allah clarifies that all preceding messengers were humans subject to the same biological needs and societal interactions as everyone else, thereby establishing that humanity is not a barrier to receiving revelation. The phrase regarding people being a trial for one another signifies that the interplay between the privileged and the poor, or the believer and the disbeliever, is a test of one's character, patience, and commitment to the truth, reminding the reader that God is always watching how they respond to these social and spiritual trials.

translation: And those who do not expect the meeting with Us say, 'Why were angels not sent down to us, or [why] do we not see our Lord?' They have certainly become arrogant within themselves and [become] insolent with great insolence.
interpretation: The verse highlights the spiritual blindness and defiance of the disbelievers who, rather than reflecting on the clear signs of God's existence and the truth of His message, make arrogant demands that contradict the nature of divine revelation. Their request to see angels or God Himself is not born of a sincere search for guidance but is an expression of deep-seated pride and rebellion; they seek to impose their own conditions upon the Creator, refusing to acknowledge the truth unless it conforms to their own flawed desires and expectations.

translation: On the Day they see the angels, there will be no glad tidings that Day for the criminals, and they will say, 'Forbidden, totally forbidden.'
interpretation: On the Day of Resurrection, when the polytheists and criminals behold the angels sent to take their souls or to usher them into the Fire, they will realize that the time for mercy and salvation has passed. Their cry of 'hijran mahjuran' is an expression of desperate seeking for protection or a barrier—much like how the Arabs of the past would say these words to ward off an enemy—but it will be of no avail, as they have entered a state where divine protection is withheld from those who rejected the truth.

translation: And We will turn to whatever deeds they did and make them like scattered dust.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, Allah will examine the deeds performed by those who rejected the truth during their worldly life; despite their outward appearance of virtue or activity, these deeds will be rendered null and void—lacking the foundation of faith—and will be scattered and worthless like dust particles dancing in a sunbeam, providing no benefit or weight to the scales of the doer.

translation: The companions of Paradise, on that Day, are better in settlement and better in their resting place.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine reassurance for the believers, contrasting the transient and exhausting struggles of worldly life with the eternal state of the afterlife. It signifies that for those who enter Paradise, their final abode is not only superior in its physical comfort and security but also provides a sense of deep, permanent rest and peace that surpasses any comfort found in the earthly realm, emphasizing that the reward for patience and righteousness is an incomparable state of spiritual and physical tranquility.

translation: And on the Day when the heaven will split asunder with clouds and the angels will be sent down in successive descent.
interpretation: This verse describes the awe-inspiring and terrifying scenes of the Day of Judgment, indicating that the sky will crack open to reveal the divine manifestation of clouds, accompanied by the descent of angels in orderly, grand ranks to carry out God's commands and bear witness to the gathering of humanity for the final reckoning.

translation: True sovereignty on that Day will be for the Most Gracious; and it will be a difficult Day for the disbelievers.
interpretation: On the Day of Resurrection, when all worldly authorities and false powers have vanished, true and absolute dominion will belong exclusively to Allah, the Most Merciful. This day will be characterized by intense severity and hardship for those who denied the truth, as they will face the consequences of their disbelief without any refuge or intercessor to save them from the manifestation of His divine justice.

translation: And the Day when the wrongdoer will bite on his hands [in regret] he will say, 'Oh, I wish I had taken with the Messenger a way.'
interpretation: This verse portrays the profound state of remorse and despair of the disbeliever on the Day of Judgment, illustrating how the one who followed the path of disbelief and rejected the guidance of the Prophet will be overcome by such intense regret that they will figuratively or literally gnaw at their own hands in agony, realizing too late that the only path to salvation and success was the one brought by the Messenger of Allah, which they chose to abandon in favor of worldly pursuits or false idols.

translation: Oh, woe to me! I wish I had not taken this one as a friend.
interpretation: This verse depicts the profound regret of a disbeliever on the Day of Judgment who realizes too late that his intimate companionship with a corrupt influence led him astray from the path of truth, illustrating that human beings will be held accountable for the company they choose to keep in this life, as close friendships deeply impact one's spiritual direction and ultimate moral outcome.

translation: He had led me astray from the message after it had come to me. And ever is Satan, to man, a deserter.
interpretation: This verse describes the profound regret of a person who allowed a bad companion to divert them from the path of guidance and the remembrance of Allah; it emphasizes that Satan acts as a treacherous deceiver who incites humans to sin, only to abandon them and leave them helpless and alone when they face the consequences of their actions in this life and the Hereafter.

translation: And the Messenger will say, 'O my Lord, indeed my people have taken this Qur'an as a thing abandoned.'
interpretation: The Messenger of Allah will complain to his Lord on the Day of Resurrection that his people had forsaken the Qur'an by failing to recite it, refusing to believe in its truth, ignoring its commands and prohibitions, failing to reflect upon its meanings, and neglecting to seek its guidance for the remedies of their spiritual and worldly ailments.

translation: And thus have We made for every prophet an enemy from among the criminals. But sufficient is your Lord as a guide and a helper.
interpretation: This verse serves as a consolation to the Prophet Muhammad and his followers, explaining that the existence of opposition and hostility from wicked people is an inherent challenge faced by all messengers throughout history. It emphasizes that such antagonism is part of a divine trial, and that the believer need not fear or be discouraged, because God provides sufficient guidance to navigate these trials and sufficient support to overcome the schemes of those who reject the truth.

translation: And those who disbelieve say, 'Why was the Qur'an not revealed to him all at once?' Thus [it is] that We may strengthen thereby your heart. And We have spaced it distinctly [in gradual revelation].
interpretation: The verse explains that Allah sent down the Qur'an in stages rather than as a single volume to provide continuous spiritual support and reassurance to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), as the gradual revelation allowed him to face emerging challenges, respond to specific events, and steadily reinforce his faith and the faith of his followers through constant divine guidance.

translation: And they do not come to you with an argument except that We bring you the truth and the best explanation.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine reassurance to the Prophet Muhammad, affirming that no matter what objections, doubts, or false claims the disbelievers raise to challenge his message, God will always provide a response that is not only factually superior and truthful but also rhetorically more eloquent, logically sound, and clearer in its wisdom, thereby silencing all opposition through the sheer clarity of divine revelation.

translation: Those who will be gathered to Hell upon their faces - they are the worst in position and farthest astray in way.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the utter humiliation and profound wretchedness of the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection, as their physical posture of being dragged on their faces serves as a manifestation of their spiritual state in this world, where they persistently chose to deviate from the straight path of divine guidance and turned away from the truth, ultimately leading them to the most miserable destination and the most misguided course of life.

translation: And We certainly gave Moses the Scripture and appointed with him his brother Aaron as an assistant.
interpretation: Allah emphasizes His favor upon Moses by granting him the divine revelation and strengthening his mission by appointing his brother Aaron, who possessed wisdom and eloquence, as a support and helper to share the burden of his prophetic duties and his confrontation with Pharaoh.

translation: Then We said, 'Go both of you to the people who have denied Our signs.' Then We destroyed them completely.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine justice enacted upon those who persistently rejected the truth and the prophetic guidance, demonstrating that when a people deliberately choose to remain blind to clear divine proofs, they eventually face a total and inescapable ruin as a consequence of their own defiance.

translation: And the people of Noah, when they denied the messengers, We drowned them, and We made them a sign for mankind. And We have prepared for the wrongdoers a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse serves as a divine warning, illustrating that the rejection of truth and the messengers of God leads inevitably to ruin in this world and severe consequences in the Hereafter; by citing the fate of Noah’s people, God demonstrates His absolute power to intervene in history, transforming the arrogant who defied Him into a lasting historical monument and cautionary lesson for all subsequent generations who might choose to persist in injustice and disbelief.

translation: And [We destroyed] 'Aad and Thamud and the companions of the well and many generations between them.
interpretation: God reminds humanity that the destruction of previous nations—such as the people of 'Aad, the people of Thamud, and the inhabitants of the well—serves as a divine warning that disobedience and the rejection of messengers lead to inevitable ruin, emphasizing that history is filled with countless other communities that suffered the same fate due to their persistence in disbelief.

translation: And to each We presented examples, and each We ruined with [total] destruction.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern reminder of the consequences faced by those who persistently reject the truth after clear proofs and parables have been presented to them; it highlights the divine justice that follows willful arrogance, confirming that when a people definitively seal their fate through obstinate denial and corruption, God's decree of complete destruction befalls them as a final eradication of their wickedness.

translation: And they have certainly come upon the town which was rained upon with a rain of evil. Have they not seen it? But they do not expect resurrection.
interpretation: The verse highlights the spiritual blindness of the disbelievers who passed by the ruins of the people of Lot, which were destroyed by a rain of stones. Despite physically seeing the visible evidence of divine punishment in the landscape, they failed to heed the lesson or internalize the reality of God's judgment because their hearts were hardened by a fundamental disbelief in the afterlife, leading them to live as if they would never be held accountable for their deeds.

translation: And when they see you, they take you not except in mockery, [saying], 'Is this the one whom Allah has sent as a messenger?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and disbelief of the polytheists, who judged the truth of the Prophet Muhammad's mission based solely on his physical appearance and human nature, failing to recognize that divine selection is based on the purity of the heart and the truth of the message rather than worldly status or outward grandeur.

translation: He almost led us astray from our gods, had we not been steadfast in our devotion to them. And they will come to know, when they see the punishment, who is further astray in path.
interpretation: This verse reveals the blind stubbornness of the polytheists, who viewed their adherence to idol worship as a virtue of patience. They mistakenly believed that staying true to their false deities in the face of the Prophet's message was a form of endurance, when in reality, it was a profound act of ignorance. The verse serves as a stern warning that the true measure of guidance is not found in the persistence of one's traditions, but in the truth of the message, and that all false convictions will be shattered when the reality of Divine judgment becomes manifest.

translation: Have you seen he who has taken as his god his [own] desire? Then would you be responsible for him?
interpretation: This verse addresses the state of an individual who elevates their own whims, desires, and subjective inclinations to the status of a deity that dictates their actions and values, prioritizing these over the guidance of Allah; the question posed to the Prophet Muhammad serves as a rhetorical reminder that he cannot force guidance upon someone whose heart has become enslaved to their own caprice, as true guidance is a matter of submission to the objective truth rather than the ego.

translation: Or do you think that most of them hear or reason? They are not but like livestock. Rather, they are even more astray in [their] way.
interpretation: The verse highlights that those who reject the truth despite receiving clear guidance have rendered their faculties of hearing and intellect useless by refusing to reflect on the signs of God, thereby descending to a state lower than that of animals; while animals are guided by instinct to what is beneficial for them, these individuals have consciously chosen a path that leads them further away from the ultimate purpose of their existence, making their spiritual error more profound than the instinctual limitations of beasts.

translation: Have you not considered your Lord, how He extends the shadow? And if He willed, He could have made it stationary. Then We made the sun for it an indication.
interpretation: The verse draws attention to the subtle and constant divine power manifest in the phenomenon of the shadow; it highlights that the movement of the shadow is not an inherent property of nature but a deliberate act of Allah's creation, illustrating His control over the celestial mechanics by which the sun serves as a constant witness and guide to the shifting existence of light and darkness.

translation: Then We withdraw it unto Ourselves, a gentle withdrawal.
interpretation: This verse refers to the gradual and subtle setting of the shadow, illustrating Allah's complete control over the manifestations of the physical world. Just as He expands the shadow from the sun, He then causes it to diminish or vanish back toward His divine sovereignty in a smooth, effortless, and orderly manner, serving as a sign of His power in the natural cycles of the universe.

translation: And it is He who made the night for you as a garment and sleep as a rest, and He made the day a time for rising.
interpretation: Allah explains that He has designed the rhythm of human life by providing the night to cover people like a garment, offering them concealment and peace, while appointing sleep as a state of stillness that disconnects the soul from the fatigue of the day to restore physical and mental vitality; subsequently, He brings about the daylight to serve as a period of activity and dispersal, where people arise to pursue their livelihoods and fulfill their worldly obligations, demonstrating His perfect administration of creation.

translation: And it is He who sends the winds as heralds of good news before His mercy, and We send down from the sky pure water.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom in the natural order, where Allah uses the winds as a precursor to rain, serving as a sign of His impending mercy. The description of rainwater as 'pure' emphasizes its role in cleansing the earth and restoring life to barren lands, symbolizing the spiritual rejuvenation and life-giving sustenance that Allah bestows upon His creation through His grace.

translation: That We may bring to life thereby a dead land and give it as drink to those We created - many livestock and humans.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom in the distribution of rain as a manifestation of Allah's life-giving power, showing that the water which revives barren, parched earth also serves as a vital sustenance for both the livestock upon which humans depend and for humanity itself, reflecting the interconnectedness of all living beings through the mercy of the Creator.

translation: And We have distributed it among them so that they may remember, but most of the people refuse except to deny.
interpretation: This verse refers to Allah's distribution of rain, water, or His signs and revelations among people in cycles and varying measures, with the intention that they reflect upon His power and grace, and respond with gratitude; yet, despite these repeated manifestations of divine wisdom and mercy, the majority of humanity persists in their stubborn disbelief and rejection of the truth.

translation: And if We had willed, We could have sent into every city a warner.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute divine will and wisdom of Allah in how He distributes His guidance, indicating that while He possesses the power to send an individual messenger to every single settlement on earth, He chose instead to send messengers to specific central hubs to convey the message, thereby testing humanity's ability to seek, verify, and follow the truth rather than relying solely on receiving the message directly at their doorstep.

translation: So do not obey the disbelievers, and strive against them with it a great striving.
interpretation: The instruction to 'strive with it' refers to the Holy Qur'an itself; this means that the believer should utilize the arguments, proofs, values, and guidance contained within the Divine Revelation to counter the ideologies and falsehoods propagated by those who reject the truth, thereby establishing a profound and intellectual form of struggle that upholds the message of God against disbelief.

translation: And it is He who released [simultaneously] the two seas, one fresh and sweet and one salty and bitter, and He placed between them a barrier and prohibiting partition.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom in the natural order where two distinct bodies of water meet without merging, representing the majesty of Allah's creation; spiritually, it serves as a metaphor for the coexistence of different states of purity and impurity within the world, demonstrating that while they may occupy the same space, their inherent qualities remain distinct and bound by divine law.

translation: And it is He who created from water a human being and made him related by lineage and marriage. And ever is your Lord competent.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom in the creation of humanity, illustrating how Allah brought forth mankind from a humble origin—water or fluid—and established complex social structures through biological kinship and the legal bond of marriage, thereby demonstrating His absolute power and His design for human civilization.

translation: And they worship instead of Allah that which neither benefits them nor harms them, and the disbeliever is ever, against his Lord, an assistant [to Satan].
interpretation: The verse highlights the irrationality of polytheism, noting that those who associate partners with Allah direct their worship toward entities completely devoid of power, as they possess no capacity to bestow any benefit or inflict any harm. The description of the disbeliever as an 'assistant' against his Lord refers to his active support for the cause of falsehood and his alliance with Satan in opposing the truth and the path of divine guidance, thereby dedicating his energy and loyalty to everything that contradicts the sovereignty and commands of Allah.

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a bringer of good tidings and a warner.
interpretation: This verse establishes the comprehensive scope of the Prophet's mission, defining his role as a spiritual guide who balances hope and accountability; he brings the promise of divine mercy, Paradise, and success to those who believe and act righteously, while simultaneously serving as a solemn warner who alerts humanity to the consequences of disbelief, moral corruption, and defiance of God's guidance, ensuring that his message serves as both an incentive for virtue and a deterrent against transgression.

translation: Say, 'I do not ask of you for this message any payment - only that whoever wills might take to his Lord a way.'
interpretation: The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, is instructed to declare that he seeks no worldly compensation or personal gain for conveying the divine message; his sole objective is to provide people with the guidance and opportunity to choose the path of faith and devotion that leads to the pleasure and proximity of Allah.

translation: And rely upon the Ever-Living who does not die, and exalt [Allah] with His praise. And sufficient is He to be, with the sins of His servants, Acquainted.
interpretation: The verse commands the believer to place their complete trust and reliance solely upon Allah, who possesses eternal life and is free from death, unlike all created beings who will inevitably perish. Alongside this reliance, the believer is instructed to engage in the constant glorification and praise of Allah, acknowledging His perfection and majesty. The verse concludes by emphasizing that Allah's comprehensive knowledge encompasses every detail of His servants' deeds and sins; He is fully aware of their inner secrets and outward actions, requiring no witness or informer to judge them accordingly.

translation: He who created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days, then established Himself above the Throne - the Most Merciful, so ask about Him one who is knowledgeable.
interpretation: This verse affirms Allah's absolute power and creative sovereignty by explaining that He brought the entire universe into existence in six distinct phases, asserting His authority and majesty by settling upon the Throne in a manner befitting His divinity, and emphasizing that the intricate nature of His creation and His attributes should be sought from those who possess true divine knowledge and spiritual insight.

translation: And when it is said to them, "Prostrate to the Most Merciful," they say, "And what is the Most Merciful? Should we prostrate to that which you order us?" and it increases them in aversion.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubborn arrogance and deliberate ignorance of the disbelievers who, despite being invited to humble themselves before their Creator, respond with mocking questions about the nature of the Merciful, demonstrating that their rejection is not born of a lack of knowledge, but of a hardened heart that finds only greater repulsion in the truth when it is presented to them.

translation: Blessed is He who has placed in the sky great stars and placed therein a [burning] lamp and a luminous moon.
interpretation: The verse highlights the majesty and creative power of Allah by drawing attention to the cosmic order, describing the sky as adorned with vast constellations and celestial bodies that serve as sources of light, illustrating that the universe is not chaotic but structured, purposeful, and a testament to the divine wisdom that provides light and guidance to humanity.

translation: And it is He who has made the night and the day in succession for whoever desires to remember or desires gratitude.
interpretation: This verse indicates that God has created the cycle of day and night as alternating periods so that if someone misses a devotional act or a prayer during one, they can make up for it in the other, and this alternation serves as a reminder of God's power for those who wish to reflect on His signs and offer thanks for His blessings.

translation: And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth easily, and when the ignorant address them [harshly], they say [words of] peace.
interpretation: This verse describes the refined moral character of the true believers, highlighting that their submission to God is manifested in their outward behavior; they possess a humble and composed demeanor, walking with dignity and tranquility rather than arrogance or haste, and when they are confronted by the foolish or those who seek to provoke them, they respond with composure and gentle, reconciliatory speech, choosing to preserve their own spiritual peace rather than descending into the cycle of hostility.

translation: And those who spend the night in adoration of their Lord, prostrating and standing.
interpretation: This verse describes the devout servants of the Most Merciful, highlighting that their primary characteristic during the darkness of the night—when others are heedless or asleep—is their total dedication to Allah through prayer, encompassing both the humility of prostration and the reverent posture of standing, as these acts represent the peak of spiritual devotion and sincerity toward their Creator.

translation: And those who say, 'Our Lord, avert from us the punishment of Hell. Indeed, its punishment is ever adhering.'
interpretation: The believers acknowledge that the torment of Hell is a persistent, inescapable debt that clings to the one who enters it, and because they recognize the severity and permanence of this suffering, they humbly supplicate to Allah to spare them from it, fearing its constant and inseparable nature.

translation: Indeed, it is evil as a settlement and as a residence.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Hellfire, describing it as the most wretched and miserable place for any soul to dwell or remain, emphasizing that it is a permanent abode of ultimate suffering and disgrace that offers no comfort, security, or relief to those who have earned it through their disbelief and transgression.

translation: And [they are] those who, when they spend, do not do so excessively or sparingly, but are ever, between that, justly moderate.
interpretation: This verse highlights the virtue of moderation in financial matters, teaching that a believer's conduct regarding wealth should avoid the extremes of extravagance—which squanders resources on unnecessary desires—and stinginess—which denies oneself and others their rightful needs. By striking a balance, an individual preserves their financial health, maintains their dignity, and fulfills their responsibilities to both themselves and society in a manner that is pleasing to God.

translation: And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity or kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right, and do not commit unlawful sexual intercourse. And whoever should do that will meet a penalty.
interpretation: This verse outlines the three gravest sins that contradict the essence of a believer's faith and the preservation of human society: associating partners with Allah (shirk), taking an innocent life, and engaging in adultery; it serves as a stern warning that these major transgressions lead to severe divine consequences and eternal accountability in the afterlife.

translation: The punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein in humiliation.
interpretation: This verse signifies that for those who commit major sins and persist in them, the divine judgment involves not only the intensity of the retribution being increased but also an eternal state of disgrace and lowliness, emphasizing that the spiritual status they corrupted during their worldly life will be reflected in their profound degradation and eternal shame in the afterlife.

translation: Except for those who repent, believe, and do righteous work. For them, God will replace their evil deeds with good deeds, and God is ever Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: This verse signifies the profound grace of God, explaining that sincere repentance, combined with faith and righteous actions, acts as a catalyst for a spiritual transformation. Beyond merely erasing past sins, God actively converts the record of those transgressions into a record of merits, showing that divine mercy does not just forgive the past but elevates the status of the believer through a complete rectification of their spiritual state.

translation: And whoever repents and does righteousness, then indeed, he turns to Allah with [proper] repentance.
interpretation: This verse signifies that genuine repentance is not merely a verbal expression of regret, but must be coupled with righteous deeds; when a person sincerely corrects their path, they are effectively returning to their true origin and purpose with Allah, thereby aligning their entire existence with the Divine will.

translation: And those who do not witness falsehood, and when they pass by ill speech, they pass by with dignity.
interpretation: This verse describes the refined conduct of the servants of the Most Merciful, highlighting their refusal to participate in or bear witness to false testimony, deception, and sinful gatherings. Furthermore, it characterizes their noble response to triviality and idle talk; rather than engaging with or being affected by such negativity, they maintain their integrity and self-respect by turning away gracefully, prioritizing their spiritual dignity over pointless discourse.

translation: And those who, when reminded of the verses of their Lord, do not fall upon them deaf and blind.
interpretation: This verse describes the refined character of true believers, noting that they do not disregard or ignore the divine revelations when they are presented to them; instead, they approach the verses of Allah with intellectual alertness and spiritual receptivity, actively listening, observing, and contemplating the truth rather than acting as if they are blind to the signs or deaf to the guidance.

translation: And those who say, 'Our Lord, grant us from among our wives and offspring comfort to our eyes and make us an example for the righteous.'
interpretation: The verse describes the believers as those who do not settle for their own individual righteousness; rather, they are deeply concerned with the spiritual well-being of their families, praying that Allah grants them spouses and children whose devotion and virtuous conduct bring them profound joy and peace of mind. Furthermore, their ambition is not limited to personal salvation, but extends to a desire to attain such a high level of piety and exemplary character that they become models and leaders for those who fear Allah, thereby spreading guidance and goodness throughout the community.

translation: Those will be awarded the Chamber for what they patiently endured, and they will be met therein with greetings and peace.
interpretation: The verse highlights that the high status of the 'Chamber' in Paradise is a direct reward for the believers' steadfastness in their faith and their patience in enduring worldly hardships and remaining obedient to Allah. The 'greetings and peace' signify not only the honor bestowed upon them by the angels and by Allah, but also the eternal state of tranquility, security, and the absence of any distress or conflict that awaits them in that sublime dwelling.

translation: Abiding eternally therein; good is the settlement and the residence.
interpretation: This verse describes the state of the believers in Paradise, emphasizing that their stay is permanent and eternal, as they will never be removed from it. The description of Paradise as a 'good settlement and residence' highlights that it is the ultimate place of comfort, honor, and complete satisfaction, free from any of the hardships, decay, or instability associated with worldly dwellings.

translation: Say, 'My Lord would not value you if it were not for your supplication. For you have denied, so it will be inevitable.'
interpretation: The verse clarifies that the intrinsic worth and significance of human beings in the eyes of God are tethered to their acknowledgment of His Lordship through prayer, supplication, and worship. Without the act of turning to God in humility and seeking His guidance—which signifies a recognition of one's dependency on the Creator—a person loses the very essence that grants them spiritual value. By rejecting the truth and denying the divine call, those addressed have invited a state of spiritual alienation and consequence that will inevitably attach itself to them, as the denial they have committed will result in an inescapable punishment.

translation: Ta-Sin-Mim
interpretation: These are abbreviated letters (al-huruf al-muqatta'at) whose true meaning is known only to Allah, yet they serve as a challenge to the eloquence of the Arabs, signaling that this Quran is composed of the very letters they use in their speech, yet they are unable to replicate its miraculous nature.

translation: These are the verses of the clear Book.
