interpretation: This verse serves as a divine promise and a fundamental principle in God's governance of history, affirming that the ultimate outcome of struggle between truth and falsehood will always favor those who were downtrodden and marginalized because of their faith. It denotes that God intends to transform their state of weakness and persecution into one of authority and guidance, ensuring that the righteous will eventually hold the mantle of leadership and possess the earth's resources as a manifestation of divine justice and the inevitable triumph of the oppressed over their oppressors.

translation: And We will establish them in the land and show Pharaoh and Haman and their soldiers through them that which they had been fearing.
interpretation: God promises to empower the oppressed believers by granting them authority and stability in the land, while simultaneously bringing about the downfall of their oppressors, Pharaoh and Haman, by manifesting the very consequences and shifts in power that these tyrants had desperately sought to prevent through their persistent wickedness.

translation: And We inspired to the mother of Moses, 'Suckle him; but when you fear for him, cast him into the river and do not fear and do not grieve. Indeed, We will return him to you and will make him one of the messengers.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the absolute sovereignty of Allah over human affairs and His profound care for the believers; by commanding a mother to cast her infant into the Nile, Allah demonstrates that trust in His divine decree necessitates the abandonment of human anxiety, ultimately revealing that the very act of apparent peril was the exact means by which He preserved the child's life and fulfilled His promise to return him to her, thereby preparing him for his future role as a prophet.

translation: Then the family of Pharaoh picked him up [out of the river] so that he would become to them an enemy and a cause of grief. Indeed, Pharaoh and Haman and their soldiers were deliberate sinners.
interpretation: The verse illustrates the irony of divine providence; by rescuing baby Musa from the river, the household of Pharaoh unknowingly nurtured the very person destined to bring about their downfall and hold them accountable for their transgressions, demonstrating that human schemes cannot circumvent the will and decree of Allah.

translation: And the wife of Pharaoh said, '[He will be] a comfort of the eye for me and for you. Do not kill him; perhaps he may benefit us, or we may adopt him as a son.' And they perceived not.
interpretation: When the wife of Pharaoh saw the infant Musa floating in the basket, her heart was overcome with maternal affection and divine inspiration, leading her to plea for his life by highlighting that his presence would be a source of joy and solace for both of them. In her desire to protect him from the decree of her husband, she proposed that he might serve their interests or eventually become their adopted son, unaware that the very child she was saving would be the catalyst for the ultimate transformation of their kingdom and the downfall of their oppressive regime.

translation: And the heart of the mother of Moses became void. She was about to disclose it, had We not strengthened her heart, that she might remain one of the believers.
interpretation: The verse illustrates the intense psychological struggle experienced by the mother of Moses, whose maternal instinct drove her to near-exposure of the secret of her child's location out of overwhelming grief and anxiety; however, Allah intervened by bestowing upon her divine steadfastness and tranquility, anchoring her heart so that her faith in His promise would triumph over her human fear, thereby transforming her state of agitation into one of patient reliance.

translation: And she said to his sister, 'Follow him.' So she watched him from a distance while they perceived not.
interpretation: The mother of Moses instructed his sister to keep track of his whereabouts after he was placed in the river, showing her maternal concern; she followed him from a distance so as not to draw attention to herself, displaying both caution and trust in God's plan while the people of Pharaoh remained unaware of the significance of the child they had found.

translation: And We had forbidden him from all nursing mothers before, so she said, "Shall I direct you to a household that will rear him for you and be to him sincere?"
interpretation: This verse illustrates the divine providence surrounding the Prophet Moses. By causing the infant Moses to reject all wet nurses, Allah facilitated a means for his biological mother to be reunited with him, ensuring his physical nourishment and emotional security while fulfilling the divine decree that he be raised within the house of Pharaoh, protected and guided by the very hand of destiny.

translation: So We restored him to his mother that she might be comforted and not grieve and that she would know that the promise of Allah is true. But most of the people do not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine orchestration of events in the life of Moses, emphasizing that Allah's promise is absolute and never fails. The restoration of the child to his mother serves as a manifestation of Allah's mercy and power, intended to replace her profound sorrow with peace and certainty. It teaches the believer that even when circumstances appear dire or uncertain, God's decree is moving toward a specific, beneficial outcome, and the ignorance of the masses regarding these divine manifestations does not alter the immutable truth of His word.

translation: And when he reached his maturity and was well-established, We gave him judgment and knowledge. And thus do We reward the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse signifies that when a person reaches the peak of physical and intellectual development, God bestows upon them the capacity for sound judgment, discernment, and profound knowledge. This spiritual and moral maturity is not merely an age-related milestone but a divine gift granted to those who have demonstrated excellence, sincerity, and virtue in their deeds, serving as a manifestation of God's justice in rewarding those who strive for righteousness.

translation: And he entered the city at a time of inattention by its people and found therein two men fighting: one from his faction and one from his enemy. So the one from his faction called for help to him against the one from his enemy, so Moses struck him and [unintentionally] killed him. [Moses] said, 'This is from the work of Satan. Indeed, he is a manifest, misleading enemy.'
interpretation: Moses entered the city when its inhabitants were unaware of his presence, perhaps due to the time of day or their distraction, and he intervened in a dispute between one of his own followers and an Egyptian adversary. When his follower sought his aid, Moses struck the adversary with a blow intended only to fend him off, but it resulted in the man's accidental death. Moses immediately recognized that this unintended outcome, which arose from the escalation of conflict, was an incitement fueled by Satan’s influence, leading to a regrettable consequence that he had not sought or desired.

translation: He said, 'My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself, so forgive me,' and He forgave him. Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the essence of true repentance, where the servant acknowledges their shortcoming and humbles themselves before the Creator, leading to the immediate manifestation of Allah's mercy, confirming that His readiness to pardon those who seek it is rooted in His boundless attribute of mercy.

translation: He said, 'My Lord, for that You have favored me, I will never be an assistant to the criminals.'
interpretation: Musa, peace be upon him, seeks refuge in his Lord by expressing his firm resolve and commitment to righteousness. By acknowledging that his previous mistake was a result of his strength, he pledges never again to provide support or protection to those who transgress against Allah's laws, thereby aligning his future actions entirely with justice and the pleasure of his Creator.

translation: And he became in the city fearful, anticipating; and behold, the one who had sought his help the day before was calling him for help again. Moses said to him, 'Indeed, you are clearly a transgressor.'
interpretation: Moses' remark serves as a sharp moral rebuke, highlighting that the man's recurring involvement in public altercations demonstrated a habitual tendency toward discord and wrongdoing, indicating that the man had not learned from his previous mistake and was instead creating further social instability.

translation: And when he wanted to strike the one who was an enemy to both of them, he said, 'O Moses, do you intend to kill me as you killed a person yesterday? You only want to be a tyrant in the land and do not want to be among the reformers.'
interpretation: The verse depicts the moment when the man who had previously sought Moses' help in a dispute saw him approach again, causing him to panic and misunderstand Moses' intentions as being directed toward him. By accusing Moses of being a 'tyrant' who desires to spill blood and cause disorder, the man attempts to shift the narrative from his own past wrongdoing and conflict to questioning Moses' moral character, failing to recognize that Moses acts out of justice and righteousness rather than personal aggression or oppressive rule.

translation: And there came a man from the farthest end of the city, running. He said, 'O Moses, indeed the eminent ones are conferring among themselves to kill you, so leave [the city]; indeed, I am to you of the sincere advisors.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the divine providence protecting Moses (peace be upon him) through an unexpected human intervention. The man, described as coming from the farthest part of the city, represents a catalyst of guidance and preservation who possessed inside knowledge of the pharaonic conspiracy. His action signifies that when a believer is destined for a great mission, Allah facilitates means of safety and warning, even from the least expected quarters, urging the believer to recognize the necessity of caution and tactical withdrawal when faced with an organized threat that outweighs the current capacity for resistance.

translation: So he departed therefrom, fearing and vigilant. He said, 'My Lord, save me from the wrongdoing people.'
interpretation: This verse describes Prophet Musa leaving the city of Midian in a state of deep apprehension, characterized by a constant watchfulness for any sign of pursuit or danger. His departure was not merely a flight from physical threat, but a turning point where, feeling vulnerable and isolated, he instinctively sought refuge in Allah, recognizing that his only true protection from the oppressive authorities of the time lay in Divine intervention.

translation: And when he directed his attention toward Midian, he said, 'Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the sound way.'
interpretation: When Musa (Moses) left Egypt fearful and without provisions, he turned his journey toward Midian, seeking safety and guidance; his words reflect a state of humble reliance and absolute trust in Allah, acknowledging that while he had made a choice to travel, the ultimate success of reaching his destination and finding the correct path rests entirely upon Divine guidance.

translation: And when he arrived at the well of Midian, he found there a multitude of people watering, and he found aside from them two women who were holding back their flocks. He said, 'What is your situation?' They said, 'We do not water until the shepherds drive away their flocks, and our father is a very old man.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the character of Prophet Musa (Moses) as a man of chivalry and noble conduct, even while he was a weary fugitive in a foreign land. Upon encountering the two women struggling to water their livestock amidst a crowd of men, he did not remain indifferent but chose to intervene. The women's explanation, that they were waiting for the men to finish due to their father's frailty, reveals their modesty and the necessity of their labor, prompting Musa to offer his assistance despite his own exhaustion, thereby demonstrating his innate disposition toward justice and the protection of the vulnerable.

translation: So he watered for them, then retreated to the shade and said, 'My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You would send down to me, in need.'
interpretation: In this verse, Prophet Musa displays the essence of true dependence on Allah; despite having performed an act of kindness and chivalry by assisting the daughters of Shuaib, he does not seek reward or recognition from people. Instead, he immediately turns toward Allah in total humility, acknowledging his absolute poverty and helplessness, thereby teaching that every favor, sustenance, or grace received by a human being is a direct blessing from God, and that a believer must always maintain a state of spiritual neediness before the Creator, regardless of their own actions or status.

translation: Then one of the two women came to him, walking with shyness, and said, 'Indeed, my father invites you that he may reward you for having watered for us.' So when he came to him and related to him the stories, he said, 'Fear not. You have escaped from the wrongdoing people.'
interpretation: The verse highlights the noble character of the daughters of Prophet Shu'ayb, specifically demonstrating that modesty and shyness are not obstacles to necessary communication but rather safeguards of dignity. It also emphasizes the safety and divine protection afforded to Moses after his departure from Egypt, showing how Allah orchestrated his path toward a place of refuge and honorable employment with a righteous man, marking the beginning of a new chapter of his Prophetic training.

translation: One of the two women said, 'O my father, hire him. Indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong and the trustworthy.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the two essential criteria for choosing someone for any task or responsibility: strength, which refers to competence, efficiency, and the ability to perform the job effectively, and trustworthiness, which refers to integrity, honesty, and moral character. The woman’s recommendation demonstrates that a balance of professional capability and personal virtue is the ideal standard for employment or leadership.

translation: He said, 'Indeed, I wish to wed you to one of these two daughters of mine on the condition that you serve me for eight years; but if you complete ten, it will be as a favor from you. And I do not wish to put you in difficulty. You will find me, if Allah wills, from among the righteous.'
interpretation: The verse illustrates the noble character and wisdom of the father, likely Prophet Shu'aib, who seeks to formalize a marriage contract through a transparent agreement. By setting a term of service as a dowry (Mahr), he acknowledges the value of the suitor's labor while graciously offering flexibility in the duration, emphasizing ease over hardship. His inclusion of the phrase 'if Allah wills' reflects his deep humility, acknowledging that human intentions and outcomes are entirely dependent on divine decree, thereby teaching that even the most righteous of men must remain reliant upon God's providence in all worldly affairs.

translation: He said, 'That is between me and you; whichever of the two terms I fulfill, there is no injustice to me, and Allah is a Witness over what we say.'
interpretation: The speaker confirms a binding agreement with a clear choice between two terms of service, establishing that the completion of either period serves as a full discharge of his obligation, thereby shielding him from any further claim or wrongful imposition, while invoking Allah as the ultimate guardian and observer who ensures that the terms of the covenant are honored truthfully by both parties.

translation: And when Moses had completed the term and was traveling with his family, he perceived from the direction of the mount a fire. He said to his family, 'Stay here; indeed, I have perceived a fire. Perhaps I will bring you from it information or a burning brand of the fire that you may warm yourselves.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the human nature of the Prophet Moses as he sought guidance and comfort for his family during a period of exile and hardship; his act of approaching the fire signifies both his role as a protector providing for his kin and the divine appointment that was about to unfold, as the physical fire he sought out was the manifestation of the divine presence through which he would receive his mission as a Messenger.

translation: And when he came to it, he was called from the right side of the valley, in the blessed spot, from the tree: 'O Moses, indeed I am Allah, the Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse recounts the momentous occasion of the first revelation to Prophet Moses, where Allah establishes His absolute sovereignty and divinity. By identifying Himself directly as the Creator and Lord of all existence, Allah transforms a physical encounter into a spiritual manifestation of His presence, signifying that the authority to command and guide mankind originates solely from the One who sustains the entire universe.

translation: And throw down your staff. But when he saw it writhing as if it were a snake, he turned in flight and did not look back. 'O Moses, approach and fear not. Indeed, you are of the secure.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound awe and transformation of Moses when confronted with a direct manifestation of divine power, where the familiar became alien; Allah reassures him to dispel his human fear, affirming that in the presence of the Creator and under His command, the believer finds true safety and protection from all that once seemed terrifying.

translation: Insert your hand into the opening of your garment; it will come out white, without disease, as another sign. And draw in your hand close to yourself to ward off fear. These are two proofs from your Lord to Pharaoh and his establishment; indeed, they have been a people defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: God provides Musa with two supernatural miracles to substantiate his prophethood, instructing him to use them to neutralize the fear in his heart and to serve as irrefutable evidence for the tyrannical Pharaoh and his council, who had become corrupted by their rebellion against divine truth.

translation: He said, 'My Lord, indeed I killed one of them, so I fear that they will kill me.'
interpretation: Moses expresses a profound sense of natural human anxiety regarding the retribution he anticipates after inadvertently causing the death of an Egyptian. This verse highlights that even a prophet, despite his trust in Allah, experiences the psychological burden of human vulnerability and the fear of consequences, which serves as a precursor to his subsequent plea for divine assistance and the strengthening of his mission through the support of his brother Aaron.

translation: And my brother Aaron, he is more eloquent than me in speech, so send him with me as a supporter, verifying me; indeed, I fear that they will deny me.
interpretation: Moses, recognizing his own limitations in articulate speech, humbly asks Allah to appoint his brother Aaron as his partner in the mission to Pharaoh. This request demonstrates Moses' profound wisdom and sincerity, as he prioritizes the clarity and effectiveness of the divine message over his own ego, acknowledging that Aaron’s natural eloquence will serve as a powerful tool to validate his testimony and protect him against the rejection of the people.

translation: He said, 'We will strengthen your arm through your brother and grant you both authority so that they will not reach you. Through Our signs, you and those who follow you will be the predominant ones.'
interpretation: Allah reassures Prophet Moses by promising that He will bolster his mission and provide him with emotional and physical support through his brother Aaron, ensuring their safety from Pharaoh's persecution; furthermore, this verse serves as a divine guarantee that the truth, represented by Moses and his followers, will ultimately triumph over falsehood, proving that those who uphold God's signs are destined to overcome any opposition through spiritual and moral victory.

translation: But when Musa came to them with Our signs as clear evidences, they said, 'This is nothing but invented magic, and we have not heard of this among our forefathers.'
interpretation: The verse illustrates the persistent pattern of stubborn rejection displayed by those who are blinded by arrogance and ancestral tradition, wherein they label clear divine truth as mere fabrication or sorcery simply because it disrupts their established status quo and challenges the inherited beliefs of their ancestors.

translation: And Moses said, 'My Lord is most knowing of who has brought guidance from Him and to whom will be the ultimate outcome of the home. Indeed, wrongdoers do not succeed.'
interpretation: Moses asserts that God alone holds the true knowledge of whose message represents divine guidance and who will ultimately inherit the success and stability of the eternal abode; this is a declaration of trust in divine justice, emphasizing that those who persist in falsehood and oppression will never achieve true prosperity or salvation.

translation: And Pharaoh said, 'O eminent ones, I have not known you to have a god other than me. Then ignite for me, O Haman, [a fire] upon the clay and make for me a tower that I may look at the God of Moses. And indeed, I do think he is among the liars.'
interpretation: Pharaoh's command to build a high tower was an expression of his extreme arrogance and his attempt to mock Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) in front of his subjects. By asking Haman to bake bricks, he intended to physically ascend to the heavens to 'verify' the existence of God, thereby reducing the metaphysical reality of the Creator to a material, testable object. This statement served to deceive his people into believing that his refusal to accept Moses' message was based on rational investigation, while in reality, it was a display of hubris and a psychological tactic to portray Moses as a deceiver who claimed authority from a God that Pharaoh claimed did not exist or could be easily debunked.

translation: And he and his soldiers acted arrogantly in the land without right, and they thought that they would not be returned to Us.
interpretation: This verse illustrates how the Pharaoh and his forces were blinded by their worldly power, leading them to transgress against divine law and manifest pride; their denial of accountability is depicted as the core delusion that caused them to reject the reality of the afterlife and the inevitable reckoning before their Creator.

translation: So We took him and his soldiers and cast them into the sea. So look at how was the end of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a historical reminder that no matter how great the worldly power of a tyrant or his army may seem, it is entirely insignificant when confronted with the decree of Allah, and their ultimate destruction serves as a timeless lesson for all people regarding the inevitable, wretched consequences of arrogance and injustice.

translation: And We made them leaders inviting to the Fire, and on the Day of Resurrection they will not be aided.
interpretation: This verse refers to the leaders of disbelief and falsehood who, through their persistent calls to idolatry and disobedience, became pioneers of evil, leading their followers toward the punishment of Hell. Because they intentionally chose to obstruct the path of God and entice others into sin, their influence will vanish completely on the Day of Judgment, leaving them isolated and devoid of any power, intercession, or divine support to protect them from the consequences of their deeds.

translation: And We caused a curse to follow them in this world, and on the Day of Resurrection, they will be among the despised.
interpretation: The verse illustrates that the rejection of divine truth and persistence in wrongdoing results in a two-fold state of rejection: in this earthly life, they are distanced from God's mercy and favor, living in a state of spiritual alienation, and in the hereafter, they shall be fully exposed and humiliated, marked as those who are cast aside and rejected from the presence of divine honor.

translation: And We certainly gave Moses the Scripture after We had destroyed the former generations as enlightenment for the people and guidance and mercy that they might remember.
interpretation: God granted Moses the Torah as a source of clear insight and divine illumination after the destruction of previous nations who rejected the truth, demonstrating that this revelation serves as a definitive guide and a mercy intended to awaken the hearts and minds of humanity so that they may reflect upon the lessons of the past and return to righteousness.

translation: And you were not on the western side when We decreed to Moses the command, and you were not among the witnesses.
interpretation: Allah emphasizes to Prophet Muhammad that his knowledge of the historical event regarding Moses and his encounter with the divine decree was not attained through personal presence or direct observation, but rather through revelation, thereby affirming that this narrative is a miraculous truth revealed by the Almighty to validate his prophethood.

translation: But We brought forth many generations, and long periods passed over them. And you were not a resident among the people of Madyan, reciting to them Our verses, but We were messengers.
interpretation: The verse serves as a direct affirmation of the Prophet Muhammad's prophethood by highlighting that his detailed knowledge of historical events, such as the experiences of the people of Madyan with Prophet Shu'ayb, could not have been acquired through personal observation or presence; rather, this information was revealed to him solely through divine inspiration, confirming that his source of knowledge is the Almighty who witnessed those past generations.

translation: And you were not at the side of the Mount when We called, but [it is] a mercy from your Lord to warn a people to whom no warner had come before you, that they might remember.
interpretation: The verse clarifies that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) did not witness the divine revelation given to Moses at Mount Sinai firsthand, nor was he present when Allah spoke to him; therefore, his knowledge of these past events serves as a clear sign of his prophethood, bestowed upon him by Allah as a mercy to humanity so that he may warn the Meccans—who had previously received no prophet—calling them to reflect upon the truth and turn back toward guidance.

translation: And if it were not that a disaster should strike them because of what their hands have put forth, and they would say, 'Our Lord, why did You not send us a messenger so that we could have followed Your verses and been among the believers?'
interpretation: Allah explains that His decree of delaying punishment upon the disbelievers is an act of divine wisdom and mercy; He refrains from inflicting immediate retribution for their misdeeds so that they cannot claim on the Day of Judgment that they remained in disbelief due to a lack of divine guidance or a messenger to warn them, thereby leaving them with no excuse for their rejection of the truth.

translation: But when the truth came to them from Us, they said, 'Why was he not given the like of what was given to Moses?' Did they not disbelieve in that which was given to Moses before? They said, 'Two works of magic supporting each other,' and they said, 'Indeed, we are in both of them disbelievers.'
interpretation: The verse highlights the persistent pattern of denial among those who reject the truth. By comparing the revelation given to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) with the signs given to Prophet Moses (peace be upon him), the disbelievers were not seeking genuine enlightenment but were rather searching for excuses to justify their rejection. God reminds them that their ancestors also rejected Moses's miracles by labeling them as sorcery, proving that their current defiance is merely a continuation of their historical habit of stubborn disbelief, as they have consistently chosen to deny divine evidence regardless of the form in which it appears.

translation: Say, 'Then bring a scripture from Allah that is more guiding than both of them that I may follow it, if you should be truthful.'
interpretation: The verse serves as a profound challenge to those who reject both the Torah and the Qur'an while claiming to follow a path of truth; it exposes the falsehood of their position by demanding that if they truly possess a superior source of divine guidance, they should produce it, thereby proving that their rejection is based on stubborn arrogance rather than the presence of a better alternative.

translation: But if they do not respond to you, then know that they only follow their [own] desires. And who is more astray than one who follows his desire without guidance from Allah? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse serves as a profound psychological and spiritual diagnosis of those who reject the truth; it explains that their refusal to accept the divine message is not due to a lack of evidence or intellectual deficiency, but rather because they have chosen to be governed by their personal whims and subjective inclinations rather than objective divine truth, rendering them incapable of being guided as long as they persist in their self-centered defiance.

translation: And We have conveyed the word consecutively to them so that they might take heed.
interpretation: God clarifies that He has systematically and continuously sent down revelations and signs to humanity—layer upon layer—so that they may reflect upon the truth, recognize their purpose in existence, and return to the path of guidance before the time for repentance passes.

translation: Those to whom We gave the Scripture before it, they believe in it.
interpretation: This verse refers to the sincere and fair-minded individuals among the People of the Scripture, such as the Jews and Christians who recognized the truth through their own scriptures and accepted the Qur'an as the fulfillment of the divine prophecies they had previously received, thereby demonstrating their faithfulness and adherence to God's guidance before it was obscured by human alteration.

translation: And when it is recited to them, they say, 'We have believed in it; indeed, it is the truth from our Lord. Indeed we were, [even] before it, Muslims [submitting to Allah].'
interpretation: This verse highlights the inherent receptivity of those whose hearts are prepared for guidance; upon hearing the revelation, their immediate affirmation of its divine truth serves as a testament to their previous state of sincere submission, suggesting that their faith in the Qur'an is not a sudden deviation but the logical culmination of a long-standing orientation of their souls toward the truth of God.

translation: Those will be given their reward twice for what they patiently endured and [because] they avert evil with good, and they spend out of what We have provided them.
interpretation: The verse highlights the multi-faceted nature of true faith, where the believers receive a double reward for their steadfastness in the face of hardship, their refusal to retaliate against wrongdoing with similar malice—opting instead for benevolence—and their commitment to social welfare through the generous expenditure of their wealth for the sake of God.

translation: And when they hear vain talk, they turn away from it and say, 'For us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds. Peace be upon you; we seek not the ignorant.'
interpretation: The verse illustrates the conduct of the believers who maintain their moral and intellectual dignity by refusing to engage in futile, malicious, or ignorant discourse. By choosing to withdraw from such conversations, they demonstrate self-respect and a refusal to be dragged into hostility, signaling that they prioritize their own spiritual growth and accountability over engaging with those who lack wisdom or harbor ill intent.

translation: Indeed, you do not guide whom you like, but Allah guides whom He wills. And He is most knowing of the [rightly] guided.
interpretation: This verse clarifies that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) did not possess the inherent power to instill faith in the hearts of those he loved, such as his uncle Abu Talib, despite his earnest desire for their salvation. It emphasizes that the guidance of the heart—the spiritual illumination that leads one to accept the truth—is a prerogative that belongs solely to Allah. Therefore, the verse serves as a divine reminder that while humans can invite and advise others toward the truth, the actual transformation and turning of the heart toward belief is exclusively in the hands of the Almighty, who acts based on His infinite wisdom regarding who is sincere and worthy of receiving that grace.

translation: And they say, 'If we follow the guidance with you, we will be expelled from our land.' Have We not established for them a safe sanctuary to which are brought the fruits of all things as provision from Us? But most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse addresses the fear of the polytheists of Mecca who argued that embracing Islam would lead to their vulnerability and displacement by surrounding hostile tribes. Allah counters this by reminding them of the divine favor they already possess in Mecca, a sanctuary made secure by His decree where provisions from all over the world are gathered. The interpretation highlights that their fear of earthly loss is unfounded because the One who established their security and provided for them in a barren land is fully capable of protecting them if they choose to follow His path, revealing that their hesitation stems from a lack of true understanding regarding the source of their safety and sustenance.

translation: And how many a city have We destroyed which was ungrateful for its livelihood! And those are their dwellings, which have not been inhabited after them except little; and it is We who are the Inheritors.
interpretation: The verse serves as a historical warning, illustrating that the prosperity of a society is a trial from God. When people become arrogant, waste their resources, and ignore the moral obligations that accompany their wealth, they invite divine retribution. The crumbling, abandoned ruins of past civilizations serve as a reminder that worldly power and material comfort are transient, and ultimately, all things return to the sovereignty of God, who remains the eternal possessor when all human dominion has vanished.

translation: And never would your Lord have destroyed the cities until He had sent to their principal city a messenger reciting to them Our verses. And We would not destroy the cities except while their people were wrongdoers.
interpretation: God establishes a divine principle of justice where He does not hasten to inflict punishment upon a civilization without first providing them with clear guidance through a messenger sent to their central hub, ensuring they understand His commandments and signs; thus, the eventual destruction is not a result of caprice but a consequence of their deliberate persistence in injustice and polytheism after the truth has been made manifest to them.

translation: And whatever thing you have been given, it is only for the enjoyment of the worldly life and its adornment. But what is with Allah is better and more lasting; so will you not use your reason?
interpretation: The verse serves as a profound reminder that the fleeting possessions and pleasures of this world, regardless of how attractive or valuable they may seem, are merely temporary tools designed for a short duration. It urges the believer to elevate their perspective by comparing these transient earthly gains to the eternal, infinite rewards promised by Allah, highlighting that the spiritual and everlasting nature of the Hereafter far outweighs the limited utility of material life, thereby challenging the intellect to prioritize what is permanent over what is perishable.

translation: Is he whom We have promised a good promise which he will meet, like him whom We have provided with the good things of this worldly life, then he will be on the Day of Resurrection among those brought forth to punishment?
interpretation: The verse draws a definitive contrast between the believer who has been promised the eternal reward of Paradise and the disbeliever who enjoys temporary worldly luxuries; it emphasizes that these two categories of people can never be equal, as the former is sustained by a divine guarantee of everlasting bliss, while the latter, despite their fleeting worldly acquisitions, will ultimately face the humiliation and accountability of the afterlife.

translation: And on the Day He will call to them and say, 'Where are My 'partners' whom you used to claim?'
interpretation: This verse depicts the moment of profound humiliation for the polytheists on the Day of Resurrection, where Allah confronts them with a question that serves not to gain information, but to expose the utter falsehood and helplessness of the idols they worshipped. By asking for these 'partners,' Allah strips away the delusions they harbored in the worldly life, forcing them to realize that those whom they invoked as intercessors or divine equals have no power to benefit or protect them, thereby intensifying their regret and realization of their grave error.

translation: Those upon whom the word has come into effect will say, 'Our Lord, these are the ones we led to error. We led them to error just as we were in error. We declare our disassociation before You; it was not us they used to worship.'
interpretation: This verse reveals the ultimate betrayal of the devils and leaders of misguidance toward their followers on the Day of Judgment; they attempt to deflect blame by asserting that their followers' deviant behavior was merely a reflection of their own confusion, and they completely renounce any responsibility for the worship directed toward them, exposing the tragic realization that those who followed human or demonic desires instead of divine guidance were essentially serving their own whims and passions rather than the intended deities.

translation: And it will be said, 'Call upon your partners,' and they will call upon them, but they will not respond to them; and they will see the punishment. If only they had been guided.
interpretation: This verse depicts the final moment of helplessness for the polytheists on the Day of Judgment, where their futile reliance on false deities is exposed; they are commanded to call upon those whom they worshipped besides Allah, only to find that these idols possess no power to answer or assist, leaving them to witness the impending torment with the agonizing realization that they missed the opportunity to follow the path of true guidance while they were in the worldly life.

translation: And on the Day He will call to them and say, 'What answer did you give the messengers?'
interpretation: This verse depicts the scene of the Day of Judgment, where Allah will confront the disbelievers and those who turned away from guidance, questioning them about their response to the messengers sent to them. The intent of this inquiry is not to obtain information, as Allah knows all, but rather to rebuke and expose their persistent arrogance and refusal to accept the truth, thereby establishing proof against them and confirming that they had no valid justification for their denial and disobedience.

translation: But the news will be blinded to them on that Day, so they will not be able to ask one another.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, the gravity and terror of the situation will be so overwhelming that the disbelievers will lose the ability to provide excuses or ask for explanations; their arguments and defenses will vanish, leaving them unable to communicate or inquire as they become completely bewildered and silenced by the magnitude of the truth they previously denied.

translation: But as for he who repented, believed, and did righteousness, it is expected that he will be among the successful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true salvation and success are not merely contingent upon regret, but require a holistic transformation: sincere repentance from past sins, firm belief in God, and the active pursuit of righteous deeds; when these three components align, the individual is placed on the path to divine mercy and eternal prosperity, as the phrasing indicates an assurance of success for those who fulfill these conditions.

translation: And your Lord creates what He wills and chooses; not for them was the choice. Exalted is Allah and high above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse establishes the absolute sovereignty and divine wisdom of Allah, asserting that He alone possesses the authority to create and elect whatever He wills based on His perfect knowledge and purpose. It negates any capacity for human beings or created entities to exercise independent choice or authority in opposition to His decree, emphasizing that human preferences hold no weight against His divine ordinance, and concluding with a declaration of His transcendence far beyond the false deities or partners that polytheists attribute to His essence.

translation: And your Lord knows what their breasts conceal and what they declare.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute omniscience of Allah, affirming that His knowledge is not limited to the observable actions or speech of human beings, but extends to the innermost secrets, intentions, and hidden thoughts harbored within their hearts, meaning that no one can hide anything from Him whether it is manifested outwardly or kept concealed.

translation: And He is Allah; there is no deity except Him. To Him is [due all] praise in the first [life] and the Hereafter. And His is the [final] decision, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse establishes the absolute Oneness of Allah, affirming that He alone deserves worship and total devotion. By declaring that all praise belongs to Him in this world and the next, it reminds the believer that every blessing, whether in the fleeting life of the dunya or the eternal life of the Hereafter, originates from His grace and mercy. Furthermore, the assertion that the final judgment belongs to Him alone emphasizes that human authority is transient and limited, grounding the human soul in the awareness that all existence will inevitably conclude with a return to its Creator to account for its deeds.

translation: Say, 'Have you considered: if Allah should make for you the night continuous until the Day of Resurrection, what deity other than Allah could bring you light? Then will you not hear?'
interpretation: This verse serves as a rhetorical challenge to the polytheists, drawing their attention to the absolute dependency of human existence on the natural cycles governed by Allah. By postulating an eternal state of darkness, the verse highlights that sunlight—the primary source of energy, growth, and survival—is not a mundane entitlement but a recurring act of divine grace. The inability of any false deity to restore light once withheld underscores the impotence of idols and directs the human mind toward the necessity of acknowledging the Sovereign Creator who alone maintains the essential conditions for life.

translation: Say, 'Have you considered: if Allah should make for you the day continuous until the Day of Resurrection, what deity other than Allah could bring you night in which you may rest? Then will you not see?'
interpretation: This verse serves as a rhetorical challenge to those who reject the oneness of God, highlighting the profound mercy embedded in the natural cycle of day and night. By asking who else could provide the relief of darkness for rest if the sun were to remain fixed, Allah prompts the listener to reflect on the divine wisdom that sustains life's biological and spiritual needs, pointing out that humanity is entirely dependent on His providence for the very conditions that allow for physical repose and psychological tranquility.

translation: And out of His mercy He made for you the night and the day that you may rest therein and that you may seek from His bounty and that you may be grateful.
interpretation: God illustrates His boundless mercy by balancing the cycles of existence; the night provides a necessary respite for the physical body to find tranquility and repose after labor, while the day serves as a window of opportunity for human beings to exert effort, pursue their worldly needs, and seek the sustenance and grace provided by the Creator, ultimately inviting the human heart to recognize these divine gifts and respond with heartfelt gratitude.

translation: And the Day He will call them and say, 'Where are My partners whom you used to claim?'
interpretation: On the Day of Resurrection, Allah will question the polytheists by calling out to them, not to receive an answer, but to expose the falsehood of their beliefs and deepen their regret. By asking for the 'partners' they associated with Him in worship, Allah highlights the futility of their idols, which will be unable to provide them with any assistance, protection, or intercession, thereby confirming that these idols were mere illusions and that sovereignty belongs to Allah alone.

translation: And We will extract from every nation a witness and say, 'Produce your proof,' and they will know that the truth belongs to Allah, and lost from them will be that which they used to invent.
interpretation: On the Day of Resurrection, Allah will summon a witness from every community—typically their Prophet—to testify regarding their deeds and their rejection of divine guidance. When these nations are challenged to produce evidence or arguments to justify their polytheism and disbelief, they will find themselves utterly helpless and speechless. The verse emphasizes that at this critical moment, the absolute sovereignty and truth of Allah will become undeniably clear to everyone, causing all the false idols, fabricated deities, and deceptive ideologies they once invented and relied upon to vanish, leaving them with no defense or path to salvation.

translation: Indeed, Qarun was from the people of Moses, but he tyrannized them. And We gave him of treasures whose keys would burden a band of strong men; when his people said to him, 'Do not exult. Indeed, Allah does not like the exultant.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the danger of arrogance and ingratitude when one is blessed with immense material wealth. Qarun's tyranny originated from his failure to acknowledge that his riches were a trust from Allah, leading him to abuse his power against his own kin; the warning of his people serves as a reminder that excessive pride and vanity, which cause one to become boastful and indifferent to the rights of others, are traits that invite the displeasure of the Almighty.

translation: But seek, through that which Allah has given you, the home of the Hereafter; and [yet], do not forget your portion of [this] world. And do good as Allah has done good to you. And desire not corruption in the land. Indeed, Allah does not like corruptors.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine directive for achieving a balanced existence; it instructs the believer to utilize the wealth and blessings bestowed upon them by Allah as a bridge toward the eternal afterlife through charity and righteous deeds, while simultaneously fulfilling their worldly obligations to sustain themselves and their families in a lawful manner. Furthermore, it emphasizes that since Allah has bestowed His grace and favor upon the servant without cause, the servant is duty-bound to extend that same benevolence to others, while strictly abstaining from any behavior that fosters social, moral, or environmental decay, as such actions are inherently antithetical to the pleasure of the Creator.

translation: He said, 'I was only given it because of knowledge I have.' Did he not know that Allah had destroyed before him of generations those who were greater than him in power and greater in accumulation [of wealth]? But the criminals, about their sins, will not be asked.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the arrogance and self-delusion of Qarun, who attributed his immense wealth solely to his own intellect and skill rather than acknowledging the grace of Allah. It serves as a stark reminder that human achievement is transient and that relying on worldly success as proof of one's personal merit or righteousness is a grave error; history is full of powerful civilizations that were destroyed by divine decree, demonstrating that no amount of wealth or strength can offer protection against the inevitable judgment of God, where ultimate accountability rests with Him alone.

translation: So he went out before his people in his adornment. Those who desired the worldly life said, 'Oh, would that we had like what was given to Qarun. Indeed, he is one of great fortune.'
interpretation: The verse highlights the allure of material wealth and the tendency of people to be deceived by outward appearances. When Qarun paraded his immense riches, the worldly-minded among his people felt envy and ignorance, mistakenly believing that his abundance was a sign of true success and Divine favor, rather than a worldly trial that often blinds a person to the realities of the afterlife.

translation: But those who had been given knowledge said, 'Woe to you! The reward of Allah is better for he who has believed and done righteousness. And none are granted it except the patient.'
interpretation: When the people of faith and insight witnessed the worldly splendor displayed by Qarun, they admonished those who coveted it by clarifying that the true value of life lies not in fleeting material wealth, but in the spiritual and eternal reward that Allah reserves for those who combine sincere belief with righteous deeds, noting that achieving this state of contentment and spiritual endurance requires the strength of soul found only in those who patiently persevere against the allure of worldly temptations.

translation: And We caused the earth to swallow him and his home, and there was no company for him to aid him other than Allah, nor was he of those who could defend themselves.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the ultimate futility of relying on worldly wealth and status, demonstrating that when divine retribution descends, no amount of human support or accumulation of possessions can avert the decree of Allah or offer any form of protection against His power.

translation: And those who had envied his position the day before began to say, 'Oh! It is indeed Allah who extends provision to whom He wills of His servants and restricts it! Had not Allah conferred favor upon us, He would have caused it to swallow us. Oh! It is as if the disbelievers do not succeed.'
interpretation: The verse illustrates the fleeting nature of worldly status by depicting the change of heart in those who previously coveted the wealth and position of a rich man, now realizing through his sudden downfall that worldly abundance is not a measure of divine favor but a test of Allah's wisdom, leading them to feel relief and gratitude that they were spared such a fate, thereby acknowledging that true success is found in faith rather than worldly gain.

translation: That home of the Hereafter We assign to those who do not desire exaltedness upon the earth or corruption. And the [best] outcome is for the righteous.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the eternal reward of Paradise is reserved exclusively for those whose hearts are devoid of arrogance and the desire to oppress others, and who abstain from causing harm or disorder in the world, emphasizing that true success in the end belongs only to those who maintain consciousness of God and adhere to His commandments.

translation: Whoever comes with a good deed will have better than it; and whoever comes with an evil deed, then those who do evil deeds will not be recompensed except for what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse establishes the principle of divine generosity and absolute justice; Allah promises to multiply the reward for any righteous act, far exceeding the value of the deed itself, whereas He restricts the punishment for wrongdoing strictly to the measure of the sin committed, ensuring that no soul is burdened beyond the weight of its own transgressions.

translation: Indeed, He who has ordained upon you the Qur'an will certainly restore you to a place of return. Say, 'My Lord is most knowing of who brings guidance and who is in clear error.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine reassurance to the Prophet Muhammad, promising that the same Allah who revealed the Qur'an to him would eventually restore him to his place of origin, which many scholars interpret as a return to Makkah in triumph, or ultimately the eternal abode of Paradise. It emphasizes that Allah is the ultimate judge who knows the truth of every soul's path, serving as a reminder that the struggle between the truth of divine guidance and the falsehood of misguidance is being observed and adjudicated by the All-Knowing Lord.

translation: And you did not expect that the Book would be delivered to you, but it is a mercy from your Lord. So do not be an assistant to the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine reassurance to the Prophet Muhammad, clarifying that his prophethood and the revelation of the Qur'an were not outcomes he had sought or planned for himself, but rather a manifestation of Allah's grace and mercy. It emphasizes that the message is a heavenly gift and a divine favor bestowed upon him. Consequently, the instruction to 'not be an assistant to the disbelievers' serves as a fundamental commandment to remain steadfast in the mission of the truth, forbidding any compromise, cooperation, or alliance with those who reject the message, as doing so would contradict the very sanctity and nature of the mercy that was entrusted to him.

translation: And never let them avert you from the verses of Allah after they have been revealed to you. And invite to your Lord and do not ever be of those who associate others with Allah.
interpretation: This verse serves as a directive to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and by extension to all believers, emphasizing that the truth of the divine revelation should be the sole guiding authority, regardless of the pressures or worldly objections posed by those who reject the faith. It highlights that the mandate of the believer is twofold: to remain steadfast in upholding the Quranic message once it has been made manifest, and to actively propagate the path of God, ensuring that one's loyalty and devotion remain exclusively focused on the oneness of God, thereby distancing oneself entirely from any form of polytheism or spiritual compromise.

translation: And do not invoke with Allah another deity. There is no deity except Him. Everything will be destroyed except His Face. His is the judgement, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse establishes the absolute oneness of Allah and the transience of all created things, emphasizing that worship must be directed solely to Him because all existence, apart from His eternal Essence, is destined for cessation. It asserts that Allah alone possesses supreme sovereignty and authority to govern all affairs, serving as a reminder that every soul will inevitably return to Him to face account for their deeds.

translation: Alif, Lam, Mim.
interpretation: These are abbreviated letters (al-huruf al-muqatta'at) found at the beginning of several Surahs, and their true meaning is known only to Allah; they serve as a miraculous challenge, asserting that the Qur'an is composed of the same letters used in the language of the Arabs, yet they are unable to produce anything comparable to it.

translation: Do the people think that they will be left to say, 'We believe,' and they will not be tried?
interpretation: This verse establishes that faith is not merely a verbal declaration but a spiritual reality that must be authenticated through testing; Allah subjects believers to trials, hardships, and temptations to distinguish the sincere in their faith from those whose claim is superficial, thereby refining their hearts and demonstrating their true commitment to His path.

translation: And We have certainly tried those before them, and Allah will surely make evident those who are truthful, and He will surely make evident the liars.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the hardships and trials encountered by believers throughout history are not mere incidents of suffering, but a divine mechanism to reveal the true nature of faith; by exposing individuals to tribulations, Allah distinguishes between those whose profession of belief is sincere and rooted in genuine conviction, and those whose claims are hollow, thereby manifesting the state of people's hearts in a way that is evident to all.

translation: Or do those who do evil deeds think that they can outrun Us? Evil is what they judge.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to those who persist in disobedience and transgression, clarifying that their assumption of evading divine justice is a profound error in judgment; Allah is Omnipotent and All-Encompassing, meaning that no one who commits wrongdoing can escape His grasp or hide from His reckoning, and their belief that they might avoid accountability is a deluded and wretched perspective that ignores the inevitability of His retribution.

translation: Whoever hopes for the meeting with Allah, then indeed the time appointed by Allah is surely coming. And He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse serves as a source of consolation and motivation for the believers, emphasizing that the ultimate return to Allah is a fixed certainty that should compel a person to prepare through righteous deeds, while assuring them that Allah hears their invocations and knows the sincerity of their intentions, thereby promising that no effort made for His sake will go unrewarded or unnoticed.

translation: And whoever strives only strives for the benefit of his own soul. Indeed, Allah is free from need of the worlds.
interpretation: The command to struggle in the way of Allah is not for the sake of benefiting Allah, as He is perfectly self-sufficient and independent of His creation; rather, this striving is a means by which the individual refines their own soul, earns spiritual elevation, and secures their own ultimate success in the Hereafter.

translation: And those who believe and do righteous deeds - We will surely remove from them their misdeeds and will surely reward them according to the best of what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the immense mercy and justice of Allah, indicating that for those who possess sincere faith followed by righteous actions, Allah will not only erase their previous sins and imperfections as a gesture of His grace, but He will also elevate the value of their good deeds, rewarding them not just for what they did, but granting them the highest recompense based on the best of their intentions and efforts.

translation: And We have enjoined upon man goodness to parents. But if they endeavor to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them. To Me is your return, and I will inform you about what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse establishes that while kindness, obedience, and dutifulness toward parents are among the most emphasized divine commands, this obligation is strictly bounded by the rights of God; therefore, if parents demand that a person commit shirk or deviate from the truth, one must politely decline their command, as loyalty to the Creator takes precedence over human relationships, yet this does not absolve the individual from continuing to treat those parents with worldly compassion and respect.

translation: And those who believe and do righteous deeds - We will surely admit them among the righteous [in Paradise].
interpretation: Allah promises that those who combine sincere faith in their hearts with righteous deeds in their actions will be granted a place among the ranks of the prophets, the truthful, and the martyrs, ensuring that they are resurrected and joined with the company of the pious servants of Allah who have attained His pleasure and eternal paradise.

translation: And of the people are some who say, 'We believe in Allah,' but when they are persecuted for the sake of Allah, they consider the trial of the people as the punishment of Allah. But if victory comes from your Lord, they will surely say, 'Indeed, we were with you.' Is not Allah most knowing of what is within the breasts of all the worlds?
interpretation: This verse describes the condition of hypocrites whose faith is shallow and unstable, lacking the conviction to withstand hardship. When they face difficulty or harm from others due to their professed faith, they equate this human-inflicted suffering with the severity of divine punishment, choosing to abandon their principles to avoid temporal pain. However, when success or material gain arrives for the believers, these individuals opportunistically realign themselves with the community to claim a share in the benefits, unaware that Allah possesses absolute knowledge of the insincerity hidden deep within their hearts.

translation: And Allah will surely make evident those who believed, and He will surely make evident the hypocrites.
interpretation: The verse explains that Allah subjects the believers to trials and tribulations not to gain knowledge of what He already knows, but to manifest and distinguish the true believers from the hypocrites in the sight of everyone, so that the sincerity of faith is proven through observable actions and steadfastness in the face of hardship.

translation: And those who disbelieved said to those who believed, 'Follow our way, and we will bear your sins.' But they will not bear anything of their sins at all. Indeed, they are liars.
interpretation: This verse addresses the arrogance of the disbelievers who attempted to lead the believers astray by offering to take upon themselves the burden of their sins if they followed their path. It serves as a stern divine declaration that on the Day of Judgment, no soul can bear the burdens of another, and the false promises of the disbelievers—who falsely claimed they could absolve others of accountability—will be revealed as mere lies, leaving every individual to account only for their own deeds.

translation: But they will surely carry their own burdens, and other burdens along with their own, and they will surely be questioned on the Day of Resurrection about what they used to invent.
interpretation: The verse clarifies that those who lead others astray by calling them to disbelief and sin will not only be held accountable for their own transgressions, but will also bear the weight of the sins of those they misled, without diminishing the responsibility of the followers themselves. This demonstrates the magnitude of the consequences for the leaders of falsehood, as they are burdened with the corrupting influence they exerted over others, and they shall be held strictly accountable for the fabrications and lies they propagated against God.

translation: And We certainly sent Noah to his people, and he remained among them a thousand years minus fifty years, and the flood seized them while they were wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the extraordinary patience and perseverance of Prophet Noah in his mission to guide his people toward monotheism, enduring centuries of mockery and rejection before the divine decree of punishment was finally executed against those who persisted in their idolatry and oppression.

translation: So We saved him and the companions of the ship, and We made it a sign for the worlds.
interpretation: God narrates how He rescued Prophet Noah and those who believed in him from the catastrophic flood by securing them within the Ark. By preserving the memory of this ship or the event itself, God intended it to serve as an enduring, manifest lesson for all humanity throughout time, demonstrating His power to protect the faithful and execute His divine decree upon the disbelievers.

translation: And [mention] Abraham, when he said to his people, 'Worship Allah and fear Him. That is best for you, if you should know.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the foundational call of Prophet Abraham to his people, urging them to pivot from their self-constructed idols toward the singularity of God. By pairing the command to worship with the concept of taqwa (God-consciousness or piety), Abraham emphasizes that faith is not merely a ritualistic act but an encompassing state of mind that seeks to avoid divine displeasure. His assertion that this path is 'best for you' serves as a rational appeal, suggesting that aligning one's life with the Truth of the Creator provides the ultimate spiritual and existential benefit, transcending the temporary and hollow security found in worldly attachments.

translation: You only worship idols instead of Allah, and you invent a falsehood. Verily, those whom you worship besides Allah have no power to give you provision; so seek provision from Allah, worship Him, and be grateful to Him. To Him you will be brought back.
interpretation: The verse serves as a rational challenge to the polytheists, exposing the futility of their worship by highlighting that their man-made idols possess no power to sustain them. It redirects their focus toward the true Source of all sustenance, emphasizing that gratitude is the only logical response to the Creator who controls their ultimate destiny and to whom they must return for final judgment.

translation: And if you deny, then nations before you have already denied; and there is not upon the Messenger except the clear notification.
interpretation: God consoles His Messenger by reminding him that the rejection he faces from his people is not a unique phenomenon, as previous messengers were also met with disbelief and opposition from their own communities; thus, the Prophet's responsibility is limited solely to conveying the divine message clearly and truthfully, leaving the outcome, the guidance of hearts, and the ultimate judgment of the deniers entirely to God.

translation: Have they not seen how Allah originates creation and then repeats it? Indeed that, for Allah, is easy.
interpretation: The verse calls upon the disbelievers to observe the observable phenomena of life and its constant renewal in the natural world, using these instances as logical evidence that the Creator who brought life into existence from nothing is perfectly capable of restoring it after death, as the exertion of power for Him is not bound by the limitations or degrees of difficulty that human beings experience.

translation: Say, 'Travel through the land and observe how He began creation. Then Allah will produce the final creation. Indeed Allah, over all things, is competent.'
interpretation: Allah commands humanity to reflect upon the origins of life and the physical world through observation and travel, as the complexity and precision evident in the initial stages of creation serve as a clear sign of His omnipotence. By understanding that Allah originated life from nothing, the intellect is led to the logical conclusion that the same Creator possesses the absolute power to resurrect and re-create beings for the afterlife, as the One who initiates is always capable of repeating the process.

translation: He punishes whom He wills and has mercy upon whom He wills, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse establishes the absolute sovereignty and comprehensive justice of Allah, affirming that His actions are governed by His infinite wisdom; those who face punishment are those who have persisted in disbelief and rejected the truth, while those who receive mercy are those whose hearts were receptive to faith and righteousness, ultimately reminding humanity that all existence concludes with a return to their Creator for final reckoning.

translation: And you will not cause failure upon the earth or in the heaven, and you have not besides Allah any protector or helper.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and sovereignty of Allah, asserting that no human being possesses the ability to escape His decree, evade His knowledge, or hinder His will, whether they attempt to hide on earth or ascend into the heavens; consequently, humans are entirely dependent on His mercy, as there is no other authority or entity capable of shielding them from His judgment or providing them with support against His command.

translation: And those who disbelieve in the verses of Allah and the meeting with Him - those have despaired of My mercy, and those will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the consequence of rejecting the signs of Allah and denying the reality of the afterlife is a total severance from divine grace. Because these individuals willfully closed their hearts to the truth and refused to prepare for the encounter with their Creator, they have effectively barred themselves from the hope of His forgiveness and mercy, thereby rendering themselves subject to the inevitable and severe suffering that follows such persistent defiance.

translation: And his people had no answer except that they said, 'Kill him or burn him,' but Allah saved him from the fire. Indeed, in that are signs for a people who believe.
interpretation: The verse highlights the extreme hostility faced by the Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) from those who rejected his monotheistic message, illustrating that when truth confronts falsehood, the disbelievers often resort to brutal force rather than rational argument. By miraculously shielding Ibrahim from the flames, Allah demonstrates His absolute sovereignty over the laws of nature and His protection of those who remain steadfast in faith, serving as a profound lesson for believers that divine intervention will ultimately safeguard the righteous against the oppression of the wicked.

translation: And he said, 'You have taken idols instead of Allah only for the sake of affection among yourselves in the life of this world; then on the Day of Resurrection, you will disown one another and curse one another, and your abode will be the Fire, and you will have no helpers.'
interpretation: The verse reveals that the bond of friendship and social cohesion people forge through idol worship is purely temporal and based on worldly interests, lacking any spiritual foundation. It highlights that such false allegiances will inevitably collapse on the Day of Judgment when the reality of their error becomes clear, causing them to turn against each other in mutual hatred and denial, ultimately leaving them helpless and abandoned in the punishment of Hell.

translation: And Lot believed him, and said, 'Indeed, I will emigrate to my Lord. Indeed, He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.'
interpretation: Lot declared his firm belief in the monotheistic message brought by Abraham, demonstrating that true faith necessitates taking action to protect one's devotion. By stating his intention to emigrate, Lot signaled that he would leave behind his homeland and those who persisted in disbelief, seeking a place where he could worship Allah freely. The verse highlights that the believer’s ultimate migration is always toward Allah, relying on His supreme power to protect him and His divine wisdom to guide him through the hardships of departure and exile.

translation: And We gave him Isaac and Jacob, and placed the prophethood and the Book in his descendants; and We gave him his reward in this world, and indeed, in the Hereafter, he will be among the righteous.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine blessing bestowed upon Abraham, where God granted him righteous offspring who would continue the legacy of prophethood and divine guidance, ensuring that the revelation and spiritual authority remained within his lineage as a recompense for his unwavering devotion, ultimately affirming his high status and inclusion among the virtuous in the eternal life.

translation: And [We sent] Lot when he said to his people, 'Indeed, you commit such an immorality as no one has preceded you with from among the worlds.'
interpretation: Prophet Lot is confronting his people for engaging in the unprecedented sin of homosexuality, emphasizing that their behavior is a grave violation of the natural order established by Allah, which was previously unknown and unpracticed by any other nation in human history.

translation: Do you indeed approach men, and obstruct the path, and commit vice in your assemblies? But the answer of his people was not except that they said, 'Bring us the punishment of Allah, if you should be of the truthful.'
interpretation: The Prophet Lot (Lut) rebukes his people for three distinct transgressions: engaging in unnatural sexual acts, committing highway robbery or preventing others from traveling safely, and displaying shameless, morally corrupt behavior openly in their public gatherings; their defiant reaction, however, was not to heed his warning or repent, but rather to mock his authority by arrogantly challenging him to produce the divine torment he promised, thereby demonstrating the total blindness and stubbornness of their hearts.

translation: He said, 'My Lord, support me against the corrupting people.'
interpretation: This prayer, uttered by Prophet Lot, reflects the desperation of a servant who has exhausted all peaceful means of calling a rebellious society to righteousness and now seeks divine intervention to establish justice against those who persist in spreading corruption, oppression, and moral decay on earth.

translation: And when Our messengers came to Abraham with the good tidings, they said, 'Indeed, we are going to destroy the people of this city. Indeed, its people have been wrongdoers.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine justice inherent in the destruction of Lot's people. The messengers, who were angels, brought Abraham the glad tidings of the birth of his son Isaac, but immediately followed it with the grave news regarding the annihilation of Sodom. This underscores that the destruction was not an act of arbitrary cruelty, but a direct consequence of the inhabitants' persistent oppression and their rejection of moral boundaries, illustrating that when a society collectively abandons righteousness and embraces wickedness, it faces inevitable divine accountability.

translation: He said, 'Indeed, within it is Lot.' They said, 'We are most knowing of who is within it. We will surely save him and his family, except his wife; she is of those who remain behind.'
interpretation: When Ibrahim expressed concern for Lot, who resided in Sodom, the angels reassured him that God's knowledge and decree concerning the fate of the inhabitants were absolute and beyond question. The deliverance of Lot and his believing family members was explicitly ordained, but his wife was exempted from this salvation because she had aligned herself with the moral corruption and disbelief of her people, thereby sealing her fate to perish with the transgressors.

translation: And when Our messengers came to Lot, he was distressed for them and felt helpless for them; and they said, 'Fear not, nor grieve. Indeed, we will save you and your family, except your wife; she is of those who remain behind.'
interpretation: The verse illustrates the intense human anguish and protective concern felt by Prophet Lot upon the arrival of the angels in the form of handsome men, fearing for their safety due to the moral depravity of his people. The angels comforted him by clarifying their divine mission, assuring him that his protection was guaranteed by God, while emphasizing the inevitable exclusion of his wife from this salvation because her internal inclination and loyalty remained with the transgressors who chose to persist in their disbelief and sins.

translation: Indeed, We will bring down upon the people of this city a punishment from the sky because they have been defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine warning that when a society collectively persists in rebellion against God and abandons moral boundaries, they invite a catastrophic divine retribution that descends from the heavens, signifying that their corruption has reached a point where corrective measures or further respite are no longer applicable.

translation: And We have certainly left of it a sign as a clear evidence for a people who use reason.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the ruins or the remnants of the nations destroyed for their defiance of God serve as a tangible lesson for those who possess intellect, as they observe the consequences of past sins and contemplate the truth of the warnings delivered by the prophets, thereby choosing to avoid the path of disbelief that led to such catastrophic outcomes.

translation: And to Madyan We sent their brother Shu'ayb. He said, 'O my people! Worship Allah and hope for the Last Day, and do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption.'
interpretation: Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) calls his people back to the fundamental purpose of their creation: the exclusive worship of Allah, which serves as the foundation for moral conduct. By linking this worship to the 'hope for the Last Day,' he reminds them that true accountability exists beyond their worldly lives, thereby urging them to abandon their destructive economic practices—such as fraud, dishonesty in trade, and the oppression of the weak—which the verse characterizes as 'spreading corruption' that disrupts the social and spiritual order of the land.

translation: But they denied him, so the earthquake seized them, and they became within their home [corpses] fallen prone.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the immediate and catastrophic divine retribution that befell those who rejected their prophet, depicting the total destruction of their physical bodies and their legacy as they were rendered lifeless and motionless, serving as a permanent warning that those who persist in arrogance and disbelief against the truth will face a swift end that leaves them humbled and destroyed in the very places they once felt secure.

translation: And [We destroyed] 'Aad and Thamud, and it has become clear to you from their [ruined] dwellings. Satan had made their deeds pleasing to them and averted them from the path, even though they were endowed with perception.
