Their precise meaning is known only to Allah, but scholars suggest they serve to draw attention to the miraculous, inimitable nature of the Qur'anic text, which is composed of the very letters used in the Arabic language yet remains impossible for humans to replicate.

translation: The revelation of the Book, in which there is no doubt, is from the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse asserts that the Qur'an is definitively the word of Allah, sent down to guide humanity, possessing an inherent truth and clarity that leaves no room for any rational or logical doubt regarding its divine origin, for it emanates from the Creator and Sustainer of all existence whose knowledge encompasses all things.

translation: Or do they say, 'He invented it'? Rather, it is the truth from your Lord, that you may warn a people to whom no warner has come before you, that they might be guided.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine defense against the skeptics who accused the Prophet Muhammad of fabricating the Qur'an; it confirms that the message is an absolute, objective truth sent by the Creator, specifically designed to awaken a generation that had been left without prophetic guidance for a long period, providing them with the necessary light to steer away from error and find the path to spiritual truth.

translation: Allah is He who created the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them in six days; then He established Himself above the Throne. You have not besides Him any protector or any intercessor; so will you not be reminded?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and uniqueness of Allah as the sole Creator and Sustainer of the cosmos. By mentioning the six days of creation followed by His ascension to the Throne, the verse asserts His total dominion over all existence, meaning that His authority is supreme and direct. The concluding rhetorical question serves as a profound call to human consciousness, urging people to recognize that since no one else possesses the power to create or govern the universe, it is irrational and futile to seek support, protection, or intercession from any being other than Him, as all authority ultimately rests with Him alone.

translation: He arranges [each] matter from the heaven to the earth; then it will ascend to Him in a Day, the measure of which is a thousand years according to what you count.
interpretation: This verse signifies that Allah governs and manages all affairs of the universe with absolute authority, decreeing them from the heavens to the earth, after which all these matters and the records of deeds return to His judgment in a timeframe that corresponds to a thousand years of human reckoning, emphasizing the grandeur of His command and the precise, vast scale by which He manages existence.

translation: That is the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah possesses absolute and all-encompassing knowledge, covering everything hidden from human perception—such as the secrets of the hearts, the future, and the unseen realms—as well as everything manifest and observable in the physical world. By coupling this divine omniscience with His titles of 'The Exalted in Might' and 'The Merciful,' the verse emphasizes that His supreme power and authority are not arbitrary or tyrannical, but are perfectly balanced with infinite mercy, ensuring that His governance over all creation is rooted in both sovereign wisdom and profound compassion.

translation: Who perfected everything He created and began the creation of man from clay.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the ultimate designer who fashioned every element of existence with precise purpose and beauty, establishing a grand order in the universe where nothing is superfluous, and specifically highlights that the biological origin of humanity traces back to the earthly elements, symbolizing the bridge between the physical material world and the elevated spirit bestowed upon man.

translation: Then He made his progeny from an extract of a base fluid.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the humility of human origins by describing the biological process of creation; it serves as a reminder to humanity that despite their later pride or worldly status, their physical beginning is derived from a seemingly insignificant fluid, thereby emphasizing that true honor and greatness come only from God and the practice of faith rather than biological or material lineage.

translation: Then He fashioned him and breathed into him from His spirit, and made for you hearing, vision, and hearts; yet little do you give thanks.
interpretation: This verse signifies that human existence is a deliberate divine creation where the physical form is perfected by the infusion of a spiritual essence, elevating humanity above other creations. By gifting the senses of perception and the intellect, God has equipped mankind with the necessary tools to recognize truth and manifest gratitude, yet the verse highlights the common human tendency to overlook these profound blessings and neglect the acknowledgment due to their Creator.

translation: And they say, 'When we are lost within the earth, will we indeed be in a new creation?' Rather, they are, in the meeting of their Lord, disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse highlights the stubborn denial of the disbelievers regarding the reality of the afterlife. By questioning whether they can be reconstructed after their bodies have decomposed and become indistinguishable from the earth, they are essentially expressing a profound doubt in Allah's omnipotence. Their skepticism is not based on intellectual deficiency, but rather on a deep-seated spiritual rebellion; they reject the truth of resurrection because they refuse to acknowledge that they will ultimately stand before their Creator to account for their deeds.

translation: Say, 'The angel of death will take your souls who has been entrusted with you. Then to your Lord you will be returned.'
interpretation: This verse affirms that death is not a random or natural occurrence but a divinely ordained event overseen by a specific angel, identified as the Angel of Death, who acts by Allah's command to extract the soul at its appointed time, serving as a reminder that the transition from this life is an active process of being gathered back to the Creator to face ultimate accountability.

translation: If you could but see when the criminals will hang their heads before their Lord, [saying], 'Our Lord, we have seen and heard, so return us [to the world]; we will work righteousness. Indeed, we are [now] certain.'
interpretation: This verse portrays the state of deep regret and humiliation experienced by those who denied the truth during their worldly life; they witness the reality of the afterlife with their own eyes and hear the truth clearly, leading them to plead for a second chance to perform righteous deeds, yet this realization comes too late as the opportunity for trial and repentance has passed.

translation: And if We had willed, We could have given every soul its guidance, but the word from Me will come into effect: 'I will surely fill Hell with jinn and mankind all together.'
interpretation: God states that while He possesses the absolute power to compel all of humanity to believe and be guided by His will, He has instead chosen to grant human beings free will as a test; consequently, His decree is established that Hell will be populated by those among the jinn and mankind who chose to reject faith and persist in disobedience despite the guidance provided to them.

translation: So taste [the penalty] because you forgot the meeting of this Day of yours; indeed, We have [now] forgotten you. And taste the punishment of eternity for what you used to do.
interpretation: The 'forgetting' mentioned here is not a lapse of memory by God, but rather a metaphorical abandonment where God treats the disbelievers as if they are forgotten, denying them His mercy and assistance in the afterlife because they chose to live their earthly lives as if the Day of Judgment would never occur.

translation: Only those believe in Our verses who, when they are reminded by them, fall down in prostration and celebrate the praise of their Lord, and they are not arrogant.
interpretation: This verse describes the true mark of faith as a profound state of humility; it signifies that the hearts of true believers are so receptive to the Divine truth that the mere mention of God's signs triggers an immediate, reflexive surrender of the ego, manifesting physically through prostration and spiritually through the glorification of God, thereby purging the soul of the pride that prevents one from accepting guidance.

translation: Their sides forsake their beds, to invoke their Lord in fear and hope, and they spend out of what We have provided them.
interpretation: This verse describes the attributes of true believers who dedicate their nights to standing in prayer, distancing themselves from the comfort of their beds to engage in humble supplication to Allah, alternating between the fear of His punishment and the hope for His mercy, while simultaneously demonstrating their sincerity by giving from the sustenance and wealth that Allah has bestowed upon them to help those in need.

translation: And no soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for eyes as reward for what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse underscores the vastness and unimaginable nature of the rewards awaiting the righteous in Paradise, asserting that human imagination and worldly knowledge are fundamentally incapable of conceiving the exquisite delights and spiritual joys prepared for them, which exist beyond the realm of sensory experience as a direct manifestation of divine generosity in response to their virtuous deeds and steadfast devotion.

translation: Is then he who is a believer like he who is a defiantly disobedient? They are not equal.
interpretation: This verse serves as a rhetorical interrogation that highlights the fundamental disparity between the righteous believer and the sinner, asserting that divine justice and moral reality dictate that those who submit to God and follow His guidance cannot be equated with those who abandon His commands and follow their own desires, as their states of being, their paths in life, and their ultimate outcomes in the hereafter are inherently and definitively different.

translation: As for those who have believed and done righteous deeds, for them will be the Gardens of Refuge as a hospitality for what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the eternal reward of Paradise is not merely a manifestation of Allah's mercy, but it is intrinsically linked to the earthly efforts of the believers; the mention of 'hospitality' (nuzulan) highlights that these Gardens are prepared as a welcoming honor for the righteous, emphasizing that their virtuous actions serve as the qualifying cause for their entry into a state of everlasting tranquility and divine pleasure.

translation: But as for those who defiantly disobeyed, their refuge is the Fire. Every time they wish to emerge from it, they are returned into it, and it is said to them, 'Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the absolute permanence and agonizing nature of the punishment in Hell for those who persisted in their disbelief and rebellion against God; it signifies that their rejection of the truth in worldly life was not merely an intellectual disagreement but a form of arrogance that locks them into a state of perpetual return to torment, where every futile attempt to escape serves only to underscore the reality of the judgment they once ridiculed.

translation: And We will surely let them taste the nearer punishment short of the greater punishment that perhaps they will return [to righteousness].
interpretation: God intends for worldly calamities, hardships, and minor afflictions to serve as wake-up calls for those who have strayed, offering them an opportunity to reflect on their actions, repent, and turn back to the path of guidance before facing the ultimate, inescapable consequences of the afterlife.

translation: And who is more unjust than one who is reminded of the verses of his Lord; then he turns away from them? Indeed We, from the criminals, will take retribution.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning against the profound spiritual transgression of willfully ignoring divine truth. It emphasizes that the greatest form of injustice is not merely ignorance, but the deliberate rejection of guidance after it has been clearly presented, marking such individuals as those who have severed their connection with divine mercy and have thus become deserving of inevitable justice.

translation: And We certainly gave Moses the Scripture, so do not be in doubt of his meeting. And We made it a guidance for the Children of Israel.
interpretation: This verse serves to reassure the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) by affirming that the revelation given to Moses is a historical reality, thereby fortifying his resolve; it emphasizes that the divine guidance provided to the Israelites through the Torah is a testament to the consistency of God's message, which should dispel any hesitation the Prophet might have regarding the authenticity of his own divine mission and the truth of the previous scriptures he has inherited.

translation: And We made from among them leaders guiding by Our command when they were patient, and they were certain of Our signs.
interpretation: God designates individuals as spiritual guides and leaders for mankind only after they have attained two fundamental pillars: steadfast patience in enduring the trials of faith and the hardships of worldly life, and an unshakable, experiential certainty in the truth of God's revelations; it is through the synthesis of this profound inner conviction and the outward resilience of patience that they become qualified to lead others toward the divine command.

translation: Indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine reassurance that the ultimate resolution for all human conflicts, disputes, and conflicting belief systems will not be found in the transient world, but will be perfectly settled by Allah on the Day of Judgment, where truth will be made manifest and justice will be rendered absolute.

translation: Does it not guide them [to the truth] how many generations We destroyed before them, [while] they walk among their dwellings? Indeed, in that are signs; then do they not hear?
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern admonition to the disbelievers, drawing their attention to the physical remnants of past civilizations that were annihilated due to their rebellion against God. By observing these ruins, which they pass by or dwell among, they are urged to contemplate the inevitable consequence of arrogance and disbelief, suggesting that the lessons of history are clear evidence for those who possess the auditory faculty of the heart to listen and learn from the past.

translation: Do they not see that We drive water to the barren land and bring forth thereby crops from which their livestock and they themselves eat? Do they not then see?
interpretation: This verse serves as a profound argument for the existence and power of the Creator by drawing attention to the natural phenomenon of rainfall and the subsequent revival of dead, dry land. It invites humans to reflect on the divine system that sustains life, suggesting that if God is capable of bringing a parched, lifeless earth back to vitality through water, He is similarly capable of resurrecting the dead after their demise. The rhetorical question at the end highlights the human tendency to be heedless of these constant manifestations of divine providence, which should naturally lead the observer to recognize and acknowledge the sovereignty of Allah.

translation: And they say, 'When will this victory be, if you should be truthful?'
interpretation: The disbelievers are expressing their skepticism and arrogance by mocking the believers, questioning the reality of the promised divine judgment or the triumph of the truth. By challenging the Prophet and his followers to specify the time of this promised event, they reveal their stubborn denial and their insistence on demanding tangible proof before they would consider believing, even though the delay is merely a test of patience for the believers and a respite for the disbelievers.

translation: Say, 'On the Day of Decision, the faith of those who disbelieved will not benefit them, nor will they be granted respite.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning that the opportunity for repentance and belief is confined to the worldly life. Once the Day of Judgment arrives—described here as the Day of Decision where truth is made manifest—the doors of mercy are closed for those who persisted in denial. At that ultimate moment, belief becomes a compulsory response to the undeniable reality of God's power rather than a voluntary act of faith, and therefore, it is no longer accepted or transformative for the soul.

translation: So turn away from them and wait; indeed, they are waiting.
interpretation: This verse serves as a command to the Prophet Muhammad to disengage from those who stubbornly reject the truth and mock the divine message, placing his trust entirely in God's decree, while recognizing that both the believer and the denier are awaiting the inevitable outcome of divine justice, which will ultimately manifest in the victory of the truth and the consequence of their defiance.

translation: O Prophet, fear Allah and do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine directive to the Prophet Muhammad, reinforcing his commitment to righteousness and cautioning him against yielding to the pressures or advice of those who actively oppose the faith or those who hide their disbelief, emphasizing that God's omniscience and wisdom ensure that His guidance is always the ultimate path to follow.

translation: And follow what is revealed to you, [O Muhammad], from your Lord. Indeed, Allah is ever, with what you do, Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine directive for the Prophet Muhammad to remain steadfast in adhering strictly to the revelation he received, emphasizing that his primary obligation is obedience to God's guidance, while simultaneously reminding the believers that every human action is known to Allah, who possesses complete awareness of both outward deeds and inward intentions.

translation: And rely upon Allah; and sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This command directs the believer to abandon all forms of inner reliance on worldly means, people, or one's own strength, placing absolute trust instead in Allah's wisdom and power, acknowledging that because He is the Creator and Sustainer of all existence, He is the only One truly capable of managing, protecting, and fulfilling the affairs of those who commit their hearts to Him.

translation: Allah has not made for a man two hearts in his interior. Nor has He made your wives whom you declare unlawful (by saying they are like your mothers' backs) your mothers. Nor has He made your adopted sons your (true) sons. That is but a saying from your mouths, but Allah says the truth, and He guides to the (right) way.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine refutation of three erroneous pre-Islamic customs and false beliefs by establishing the principle of biological and legal reality: just as a human body cannot biologically house two hearts to hold contradictory devotions or contradictory truths simultaneously, religious and social laws must be based on objective truth rather than mere verbal assertions or superstitious practices. It emphasizes that human speech and labeling—such as equating a wife to a mother in a divorce oath (zihar) or declaring an adopted child to be a biological offspring—do not alter the ontological reality created by Allah, and that true guidance lies in acknowledging these established realities rather than following hollow ancestral traditions.

translation: Call them by their fathers' names; that is more just in the sight of Allah. But if you do not know their fathers, then they are your brothers in religion and your wards. There is no blame upon you for that in which you have erred, but only for what your hearts intended. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse establishes a crucial social reform in Islam, commanding that individuals be attributed to their biological fathers rather than those who adopted them. This was intended to preserve the clarity of lineages, protect inheritance rights, and prevent the confusion of bloodlines, ensuring that the legal obligations between biological relatives remain intact. By asserting that Allah considers this naming practice the most equitable standard, the verse removes the societal custom of treating adopted children as biological ones regarding lineage, while simultaneously fostering a spirit of brotherhood and mutual support among believers to ensure no one is left without a sense of community or belonging.

translation: The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves, and his wives are their mothers. And blood relatives are closer to each other in the decree of Allah than the believers and the emigrants, except that you may show kindness to your allies. That is inscribed in the Book.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the Prophet Muhammad holds a spiritual and social status over the believers that supersedes their own personal interests, requiring them to love and obey him above all others. By declaring his wives as 'mothers' to the believers, Allah forbids any possibility of marriage to them after the Prophet’s passing and accords them the sanctity and respect due to one's own mother. Furthermore, the verse transitions the structure of inheritance and mutual support from the early bond of brotherhood between emigrants (Muhajirun) and helpers (Ansar) back to the natural ties of kinship, emphasizing that while blood relations are primary in inheritance and responsibility, believers are still encouraged to uphold the noble practice of kindness and generous gifting toward those whom they had previously formed special alliances with, as this duty of mercy is permanently ordained in the divine decree.

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when We took from the prophets their covenant and from you and from Noah and Abraham and Moses and Jesus, son of Mary; and We took from them a solemn covenant.
interpretation: This verse signifies the profound and absolute commitment required of those chosen by Allah to convey His message; it highlights that the prophets, particularly the five messengers of 'ulul 'azm (those of determination), entered into an unbreakable, solemn bond with God to uphold the truth, bear the burden of the divine mission, and lead their communities toward monotheism, a covenant so weighty that its fulfillment defined their lives and the history of human guidance.

translation: That He may question the truthful about their truthfulness; and He has prepared for the disbelievers a painful punishment.
interpretation: God Almighty intends to test the sincerity of the truthful by questioning them, which serves to manifest their integrity, highlight the distinction between their commitment and the deceit of others, and further reward them for their steadfastness in truth while establishing the justification for the agonizing retribution destined for those who persisted in denial.

translation: O you who have believed, remember the favor of Allah upon you when armies came to [attack] you and We sent upon them a wind and armies [of angels] which you did not see. And Allah is ever, of what you do, Seeing.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder to the believers of the Battle of the Trench, emphasizing that when the believers were surrounded by overwhelming odds and human military strength, Allah intervened with unseen supernatural forces—a paralyzing wind and hosts of angels—to secure their victory. The verse underscores that the divine aid provided to the faithful is a manifestation of Allah's constant, all-encompassing surveillance of their circumstances and actions, reassuring them that their steadfastness in faith attracts providential support that transcends physical limitations.

translation: When they came upon you from above you and from below you, and when eyes grew wild and hearts reached the throats, and you assumed about Allah various assumptions.
interpretation: This verse describes the extreme state of fear and anxiety experienced by the believers during the Battle of the Trench, illustrating the overwhelming nature of the trial where the enemy forces surrounded them from all directions, causing even the steadfast to feel a moment of profound psychological distress and uncertainty regarding the eventual outcome of the conflict.

translation: There, the believers were tested and shaken with a severe shaking.
interpretation: This verse refers to the extreme intensity of the hardship and fear experienced by the believers during the Battle of the Trench (Al-Ahzab), where the psychological and physical pressure reached such a pinnacle that their faith was profoundly tried, stripping away all worldly security and leaving them to face a trial that tested the sincerity and resilience of their commitment to Allah.

translation: And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease said, 'Allah and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion.'
interpretation: This verse reveals the internal state of the hypocrites and those with weak faith during moments of trial, as they exposed their deep-seated cynicism by labeling the divine promise of victory and support as a mere deception, reflecting their failure to trust in the ultimate truth of Allah's word when faced with worldly fears and overwhelming opposition.

translation: And when a party of them said, O people of Yathrib, there is no place for you [to stand here], so return. And a faction of them asked permission of the Prophet, saying, Indeed, our houses are unprotected, while they were not unprotected. They intended only to flee.
interpretation: This verse describes the treachery of the hypocrites during the Battle of the Trench. They attempted to demoralize the believers by telling them that Yathrib (Madinah) was indefensible and that they should retreat. Furthermore, they used the excuse that their homes were exposed to enemy attacks and lacked security as a pretext to abandon their posts and escape the danger of battle, despite the fact that their homes were not in any real danger; their true motive was simply to desert the Prophet and avoid the struggle.

translation: And if entry were made upon them from its various quarters, then they were asked for sedition, they would have certainly committed it, and they would not have remained therein except for a little while.
interpretation: This verse portrays the hypocrites of Medina as people who lack inner conviction and commitment to the truth; it suggests that their loyalty to the community of believers is so fragile that if enemy forces were to breach the city walls and demand they betray their faith or abandon their principles to satisfy the aggressors, they would succumb to that temptation immediately and without hesitation, revealing that their presence among the believers was merely a temporary facade driven by opportunistic survival rather than sincere belief.

translation: And they had already made a covenant with Allah before that they would not turn their backs. And a covenant with Allah will be accounted for.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern reminder that those who pledged their loyalty and commitment to Allah—specifically by promising not to flee from the battlefield or abandon their responsibilities—are held morally and spiritually accountable for that oath, emphasizing that human promises made in the name of Allah are not merely social contracts but divine obligations that demand unwavering integrity and consequence.

translation: Say, 'Never will fleeing benefit you if you should flee from death or killing; and then [if you did], you would not be given enjoyment [of life] except for a little.'
interpretation: The verse serves as a reminder that destiny is fixed and unavoidable, meaning that human attempts to evade death through cowardice or flight are futile because every soul has a predetermined time and place to depart this world; therefore, seeking to delay one's end through avoidance of struggle only results in a fleeting, temporary life that lacks the honor and purpose found in facing one's fate with conviction.

translation: Say, 'Who is it that can protect you from Allah if He intends for you an ill or intends for you a mercy?' And they will not find for themselves besides Allah any protector or any helper.
interpretation: This verse serves as a profound reminder of the absolute sovereignty of Allah, asserting that human beings possess no independent power to avert divine decree, whether that decree manifests as hardship or divine grace; it emphasizes that true security, guardianship, and assistance reside solely with Him, rendering any reliance upon worldly beings or false deities completely futile in the face of His judgment.

translation: Allah already knows those among you who hinder others and those who say to their brothers, 'Come to us,' and they do not join the battle except for a few.
interpretation: This verse reveals that Allah is fully aware of the hypocrites who discouraged the believers from fighting in the cause of God, using their influence to persuade others to abandon the ranks of the faithful; their reluctance to engage in conflict exposes the insincerity of their faith and their underlying cowardice, as their actions are driven by a desire to avoid danger rather than a genuine concern for the community's well-being.

translation: Being stingy toward you; then when fear comes, you see them looking at you, their eyes rolling like one being overcome by death. But when fear departs, they lash you with sharp tongues, stingy toward [all] good. Those have not believed, so Allah has rendered their deeds worthless, and ever is that, for Allah, easy.
interpretation: This verse exposes the duplicity of the hypocrites who reveal their true colors through their intense fear and greed; when danger threatens the community, their cowardice manifests as a state of psychological paralysis akin to the throes of death, yet when safety returns, their lack of genuine faith drives them to verbally abuse the believers out of bitterness and covetousness for worldly gains, demonstrating that their lack of sincere belief leads to the total nullification of any outward good deeds they might have performed.

translation: They think the Confederates have not withdrawn, and if the Confederates should come, they would wish they were among the Bedouins asking about your news; and if they were among you, they would not fight except a little.
interpretation: This verse reveals the hypocrisy and cowardice of those who claimed to be Muslims but were terrified of the enemies of Islam; their hearts were so filled with fear that they doubted the defeat of the allied forces and longed to retreat into the desert to hide, fearing that if they were forced to stand with the believers, they would display only the barest minimum of effort due to their lack of faith and resolve.

translation: There has certainly been for you in the Messenger of Allah an excellent pattern for anyone whose hope is in Allah and the Last Day and [who] remembers Allah often.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine directive for believers to model their lives, character, and conduct after the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), as he embodies the highest standard of moral excellence, patience, and devotion to God. The verse emphasizes that one can only truly benefit from this example if they possess a sincere aspiration to attain God's pleasure and are mindful of the impending Day of Judgment, a mindset which is consistently nurtured through the frequent and heartfelt remembrance of Allah.

translation: And when the believers saw the confederates, they said, 'This is what Allah and His Messenger had promised us, and Allah and His Messenger spoke the truth.' And it increased them only in faith and submission.
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound spiritual resilience of the true believers during the Battle of the Trench. When faced with the overwhelming coalition of enemy forces, the believers did not experience fear or despair; instead, they viewed the tribulation as a fulfillment of the divine test that Allah and His Messenger had forewarned them about, recognizing that trial is an inherent part of the path of faith. Their conviction transformed the external threat into a catalyst for inner growth, strengthening their absolute trust in Allah's promise and deepening their surrender to His decree, thereby demonstrating that true belief is solidified rather than shaken by adversity.

translation: Among the believers are men true to what they promised Allah. Among them is he who has fulfilled his vow to the death, and among them is he who awaits, and they have not altered by any alteration.
interpretation: This verse praises those believers who remain steadfast and loyal to their covenant with Allah, whether they have already sacrificed their lives in battle or are waiting for the opportunity to do so; it emphasizes the consistency and unwavering integrity of their faith, highlighting that they have never compromised their principles or deviated from the path of sacrifice they pledged to uphold.

translation: That Allah may reward the truthful for their truthfulness and punish the hypocrites if He wills or accept their repentance. Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse establishes the divine justice that governs the outcome of human character; it highlights that the reward for sincerity is a certainty rooted in God's promise, while the fate of the hypocrites remains within the scope of divine wisdom—allowing for either correction through discipline or restoration through repentance, provided there is a sincere turn toward Him, emphasizing that His mercy and forgiveness are the foundational principles upon which His judgment rests.

translation: And Allah drove back those who disbelieved in their rage, having gained no good. And Allah sufficed the believers in battle, and ever is Allah All-Powerful, Exalted in Might.
interpretation: This verse refers to the retreat of the Confederates (al-Ahzab) from the trench without achieving their objective. It serves as a profound reminder that when the believers remain steadfast and rely solely on Allah, He intervenes to turn the tide of events, sparing them from the destructive consequences of their enemies' hostility. The divine protection mentioned here illustrates that Allah’s decree is supreme and His support is sufficient to overcome even the most formidable military threats, reinforcing the reality that all strength and victory belong to Him alone.

translation: And He brought down those of the People of the Scripture who supported them from their fortresses and cast terror into their hearts, so that some you killed and some you took captive.
interpretation: This verse refers to the aftermath of the Battle of the Trench, specifically targeting the tribe of Banu Qurayzah, who had betrayed their covenant with the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) by siding with the confederates. Their 'fortresses' (siyas) represent the physical protection they relied upon, which became useless when God withdrew His support from them due to their treachery. The casting of terror into their hearts serves as a divine psychological intervention that paralyzed their ability to resist, demonstrating that victory and defeat are ultimately determined by God’s decree, even when human military efforts are involved.

translation: And He caused you to inherit their land, their homes, and their wealth, and a land which you had not trodden. And Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine promise and a reminder of the historical reality where Allah granted the believers authority over the territories, properties, and resources of their enemies who opposed the message, indicating that the expansion of the Islamic community was not merely a result of human endeavor but a manifestation of divine decree, fulfilling the promise that those who uphold the truth will eventually inherit the earth.

translation: O Prophet, say to your wives, 'If you desire the worldly life and its adornment, then come, I will provide for you and give you a gracious release.'
interpretation: This verse represents a divine directive to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to offer his wives a clear choice between remaining in his household, which was characterized by modest living and devotion to the afterlife, and departing to pursue the material comforts and luxuries of the world. It emphasizes that those who seek the path of Allah and His Messenger must prioritize the spiritual rewards of the hereafter over the temporary and fleeting vanities of worldly existence, and it establishes that a separation under such conditions should be handled with dignity, kindness, and without harm.

translation: But if you desire Allah and His Messenger and the Home of the Hereafter, then indeed, Allah has prepared for the doers of good among you a great reward.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine call for the wives of the Prophet to choose between the worldly ornaments and luxury of this life or the proximity to Allah and His Messenger, emphasizing that those who prioritize the spiritual rewards of the hereafter and demonstrate excellence in their conduct and faith are promised a magnificent recompense from Allah, elevating their status and securing their eternal success.

translation: O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you should commit a clear immorality - for her the punishment would be doubled two-fold, and that is easy for Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the elevated status and immense responsibility borne by the wives of the Prophet, asserting that due to their proximity to the Messenger of Allah and their role as role models for the Muslim community, any moral failing on their part carries a greater gravity, and thus warrants a more severe accountability than that of others, demonstrating Allah's absolute justice in holding those with higher status to a higher standard.

translation: And whoever of you is obedient to Allah and His Messenger and does righteousness, We will give her her reward twice, and We have prepared for her a noble provision.
interpretation: This verse highlights that the wives of the Prophet Muhammad, by virtue of their proximity to the Messenger and their unique status, hold a greater responsibility than other women; therefore, their devotion to Allah and their righteous deeds are granted a double reward compared to others, reflecting both the merit of their actions and the honorable nature of their role in the household of Prophethood.

translation: O wives of the Prophet, you are not like anyone among women. If you fear Allah, then do not be soft in speech [to men], lest he in whose heart is disease should covet, but speak with appropriate speech.
interpretation: Allah addresses the wives of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), acknowledging their unique status and role within the Muslim community. By commanding them to avoid softness in speech when interacting with non-mahram men, Allah establishes a preventative measure to protect them from the potential improper desires of those who harbor hypocrisy or moral corruption in their hearts. The instruction to use 'appropriate speech' implies a demeanor that is direct, firm, and devoid of unnecessary gentleness or flirtation, thereby ensuring that the dignity and sanctity of their position are maintained and that they remain beyond reproach.

translation: And abide in your houses and do not display yourselves as [was] the display of the former times of ignorance. And establish prayer and give zakah and obey Allah and His Messenger. Allah intends only to remove from you the impurity [of sin], O people of the [Prophet's] household, and to purify you with [extensive] purification.
interpretation: This verse addresses the wives of the Prophet (peace be upon him) with specific injunctions regarding modesty, stability, and spiritual conduct. The command to abide in their homes is an instruction to prioritize the sanctity and duties of their domestic sphere, serving as a model of dignity and focus. The prohibition against the display of the 'former times of ignorance' signifies a rejection of the vanity and immodesty common in pre-Islamic tribal culture, emphasizing instead the virtue of inner piety. By pairing these social behaviors with the core acts of worship—prayer and zakah—and absolute obedience to Allah and His Messenger, the verse defines the household of the Prophet as a focal point of moral excellence. The concluding declaration is a divine promise to cleanse this household from spiritual pollutants, elevating their status and affirming that their purity is a deliberate act of divine grace designed to set them apart as beacons of righteousness for the entire Muslim community.

translation: And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of Allah and wisdom. Indeed, Allah is ever Subtle and Acquainted with all things.
interpretation: This verse addresses the wives of the Prophet, commanding them to reflect upon and uphold the revelations of the Qur’an and the prophetic wisdom (Sunnah) that were manifest within their homes. It serves as a reminder that the household of the Prophet was a sanctuary of divine guidance, and by meditating on these teachings, they—and by extension, the believers—are encouraged to internalize divine truth, recognizing that Allah’s grace reaches His servants through subtle, hidden ways while He remains fully aware of their inner thoughts and external deeds.

translation: It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should [thereafter] have any choice about their affair. And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly strayed into clear error.
interpretation: This verse establishes the principle of absolute submission to the divine will, emphasizing that once a command is issued by Allah and His Prophet, the role of a believer is to obey without hesitation or seeking alternative options, as true faith requires recognizing that the judgment of the Creator and His Messenger is superior to human personal preference or worldly logic.

translation: And [remember, O Muhammad], when you said to the one on whom Allah bestowed favor and you bestowed favor, 'Keep your wife and fear Allah,' while you concealed within yourself that which Allah was to disclose. And you feared the people, while Allah has more right that you fear Him. So when Zayd had no longer any need for her, We gave her to you in marriage, so that there would not be upon the believers any discomfort concerning the wives of their adopted sons when they no longer have need of them. And ever is the command of Allah accomplished.
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad's internal conflict regarding his marriage to Zaynab bint Jahsh after her divorce from Zayd ibn Harithah. Allah is instructing the Prophet that he should not have allowed the fear of societal criticism—regarding the social custom of viewing adopted sons as biological ones—to prevent him from following a divine decree that aimed to abolish such pre-Islamic practices. By marrying Zaynab, the Prophet was meant to establish a new legal precedent that clearly distinguished adopted children from biological ones, demonstrating that marriage ties formed through adoption were not equivalent to those formed through blood.

translation: There is no blame upon the Prophet concerning that which Allah has ordained for him. [This is] the established way of Allah with those who passed on before. And ever is the command of Allah a destiny predestined.
interpretation: This verse asserts that the Prophet Muhammad is not subject to social constraints or human disapproval when fulfilling what Allah has decreed for him as a religious or legal command. By linking his actions to the 'way of Allah' regarding previous prophets, the Quran establishes that divine ordinances are not subject to human whims or cultural norms, and that these events are part of a divinely decreed, immutable framework that will inevitably unfold according to Allah's ultimate wisdom and plan.

translation: Those who convey the messages of Allah and fear Him and do not fear anyone but Allah. And sufficient is Allah as Accountant.
interpretation: This verse highlights the primary duty of the messengers and those who follow their path in conveying the divine message to humanity; it emphasizes that true faithfulness requires a profound sense of accountability and devotion to Allah alone, such that the fear of God overrides any worldly fear, pressure, or social repercussion, and it reassures the believer that Allah's reckoning is enough to account for all human actions and intentions.

translation: Muhammad is not the father of [any] one of your men, but [he is] the Messenger of Allah and last of the prophets. And ever is Allah, of all things, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse establishes that Muhammad (peace be upon him) is not biologically related to any of the adult men among the believers, thereby abolishing the pre-Islamic customs regarding adoption where an adopted son would hold the same status as a biological son in inheritance and familial laws. Furthermore, it explicitly declares him as the seal of the prophets, signifying that the chain of prophethood is permanently closed with him and no prophet will come after him, confirming that his message is the final and absolute guidance for humanity.

translation: O you who have believed, remember Allah with much remembrance.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine command for believers to make the constant remembrance of Allah a foundational state of their hearts and tongues, signifying that true faith is not merely a static belief but an active, continuous connection with the Creator; by keeping Allah at the forefront of one's consciousness through praise, supplication, and reflection, the believer shields their soul from negligence and sin, ultimately ensuring that their every thought and action remains aligned with divine guidance.

translation: And exalt Him morning and afternoon.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine command for believers to dedicate time at the start and end of the day to the remembrance and glorification of Allah, emphasizing that consistent, habitual acts of worship and reflection on His greatness provide a spiritual foundation that sustains the believer throughout all other affairs of life.

translation: It is He who sends blessing upon you, and His angels [ask forgiveness for you] that He may bring you out of darknesses into the light. And ever is He, to the believers, Merciful.
interpretation: God's blessing upon the believers signifies His outpouring of mercy, honor, and favorable mention in the highest assembly, while the prayers of the angels constitute a continuous intercession for the forgiveness and spiritual elevation of those who follow His path. This divine and celestial support serves as a transformative force, guiding the hearts of the faithful away from the darkness of ignorance, disbelief, and sin, and leading them toward the radiant light of guidance, certainty, and divine proximity, manifesting His profound compassion for those who remain steadfast in their commitment to Him.

translation: Their greeting the day they meet Him will be, 'Peace,' and He has prepared for them a noble reward.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the greeting the believers will receive from Allah—or the greeting exchanged among them upon entering Paradise—is 'Salam' (Peace), signifying an eternal state of safety, security, and the complete absence of any harm, distress, or fear, followed by a generous and honorable recompense that surpasses their deeds in value and magnificence.

translation: O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness, and a bringer of good tidings, and a warner.
interpretation: This verse establishes the multi-faceted mission of the Prophet Muhammad as an authority who will testify to the deeds of his people on the Day of Resurrection, a source of hope and encouragement for the believers who follow the path of righteousness, and a cautioner who warns those who deviate from the truth of the consequences of their disbelief and wrongdoing.

translation: And inviting to Allah, by His permission, and an illuminating lamp.
interpretation: This verse describes the Prophet Muhammad as a beacon of guidance, likening him to a lamp because just as a lamp dispels physical darkness, his message and example dispel the darkness of ignorance and disbelief, providing clarity and direction to those who seek the truth through the light of revelation.

translation: And give good tidings to the believers that they will have from Allah great bounty.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine directive to the Prophet to provide reassurance and joyous news to those who have embraced faith, emphasizing that their reward transcends mere compensation for their deeds, as it encompasses a generous, limitless, and magnificent grace bestowed directly by Allah, which includes both the attainment of His pleasure and the eternal blessings of Paradise.

translation: And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and disregard their annoyance and rely upon Allah. And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine directive for the believer to remain steadfast in faith by refusing to compromise principles under the pressure of those who oppose the truth. By instructing the Prophet and his followers to disregard the harm inflicted by disbelievers and hypocrites, it emphasizes that spiritual resilience is found in detaching one's emotional and strategic reliance from the opinions or hostility of others. Placing absolute trust in Allah acts as the ultimate safeguard, providing a sense of security that renders the opposition of worldly powers inconsequential, as He is the only One whose guardianship and management of affairs are truly sufficient.

translation: O you who have believed, when you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them, then there is not for you any waiting period you should count for them. So provide for them and release them in a graceful manner.
interpretation: This verse establishes that if a marriage contract is concluded but divorce occurs before any physical intimacy or consummation has taken place, the wife is not required to observe the 'Iddah (the mandatory waiting period). The instruction to 'provide for them' refers to the payment of a consolation gift (Mut'ah) as a form of compensation and kindness, and the instruction to release them 'gracefully' emphasizes that the separation should be conducted without causing harm, malice, or disputes, reflecting the high moral standards expected in marital dissolution.

translation: O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful to you your wives to whom you have given their due compensation and those your right hand possesses from what Allah has returned to you [of captives] and the daughters of your paternal uncles and the daughters of your paternal aunts and the daughters of your maternal uncles and the daughters of your maternal aunts who emigrated with you and a believing woman if she gives herself to the Prophet [and] if the Prophet wishes to marry her, [this is] only for you, excluding the [other] believers. We certainly know what We have made obligatory upon them concerning their wives and those their right hands possess, [but this is for you] in order that there will be upon you no discomfort. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse establishes specific legal exemptions and marital privileges for the Prophet Muhammad as a prerogative of his unique status, granting him the right to marry women who meet these criteria, including those who offer themselves to him out of devotion, while simultaneously clarifying that these specific provisions are unique to his prophethood and do not alter the general matrimonial laws imposed upon the rest of the Muslim community, thereby relieving him of any potential difficulty or social constraint in his personal life.

translation: You may defer whom you will of them, and take to yourself whom you will; and if you desire any of those whom you have set aside, there is no blame upon you. That is more likely that they will be content and not grieve, and that they will be satisfied with what you have given them all. And Allah knows what is in your hearts; and Allah is ever Knowing, Forbearing.
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad regarding his domestic affairs, granting him flexibility in managing the rotation of time spent with his wives. It emphasizes that this relaxation of duty is intended to ease their hearts, mitigate their jealousy or sorrow, and ensure their collective contentment with his companionship and provision. Ultimately, it reminds the believers that Allah is fully aware of the true intentions and emotions held within the human heart, and that He handles such matters with divine knowledge and vast patience.

translation: It is not lawful for you [O Muhammad] to take more wives after this, nor to replace them with other wives, even if their beauty were to please you, except those whom your right hand possesses. And God is ever, over all things, an Observer.
interpretation: This verse was revealed as a specific command to the Prophet Muhammad, limiting his marriages as a manifestation of divine favor and distinction for him. It dictates that he was not permitted to marry new women beyond those he already had, nor to divorce any of his existing wives to replace them with others, regardless of how attracted he might be to the beauty of those potential new wives, while exempting those who came into his possession as bondwomen. This regulation served to honor the wives of the Prophet by granting them a unique status and ensuring stability in his household, while simultaneously reminding all that God remains the constant Watcher and Guardian over all affairs.

translation: O you who have believed, do not enter the houses of the Prophet except when you are permitted for a meal, without awaiting its readiness. But when you are invited, then enter; and when you have eaten, disperse without seeking to remain for conversation. Indeed, that was troubling the Prophet, and he is shy of dismissing you, but Allah is not shy of the truth. And when you ask his wives for something, ask them from behind a partition. That is purer for your hearts and their hearts. And it is not for you to harm the Messenger of Allah or to marry his wives after him, ever. Indeed, that would be in the sight of Allah an enormity.
interpretation: This verse establishes divine etiquette for interacting with the Prophet's household, emphasizing that the sanctity of his domestic life must be respected to avoid causing him social discomfort. It sets a precedent for modesty and social boundaries, specifically mandating the use of a barrier when communicating with the wives of the Prophet to maintain purity of heart for all parties involved, while firmly prohibiting any disrespectful conduct or attempts to marry his wives after his passing, categorizing such actions as a grave offense against both the Prophet and the divine order.

translation: Whether you reveal anything or conceal it, indeed Allah is ever, of all things, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse serves as a profound reminder of the absolute omniscience of Allah, emphasizing that nothing in the human heart or manifest actions escapes His divine awareness. It functions as an admonition to the believer, encouraging sincerity in intentions and caution in conduct, as Allah encompasses the seen and the unseen with His perfect knowledge, meaning He will ultimately hold every soul accountable based on what it has truly manifested or kept hidden within its deepest consciousness.

translation: There is no blame upon them concerning their fathers, nor their sons, nor their brothers, nor their brothers' sons, nor their sisters' sons, nor their own women, nor those whom their right hands possess. And fear Allah. Indeed Allah is ever, over all things, Witness.
interpretation: This verse establishes that there is no sin or restriction for women to interact or appear without the hijab before their close male relatives, fellow believing women, and their female slaves. The command to 'fear Allah' at the end serves as a reminder that even in these private allowances, one must maintain modesty and piety, knowing that Allah is constantly watching over all actions and intentions.

translation: Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who have believed, ask [Allah to send] blessing upon him and ask [Allah to grant him] peace, a worthy peace.
interpretation: This verse establishes the exalted status of the Prophet Muhammad by revealing that Allah Himself confers His mercy, praise, and honor upon him in the highest realm, accompanied by the angels who invoke prayers for his continued exaltation. Consequently, Allah commands the believers to follow suit by invoking peace and blessings upon the Prophet as an expression of love, respect, and gratitude for the guidance he brought, acknowledging that by doing so, the believer connects themselves to the divine blessing bestowed upon him.

translation: Indeed, those who abuse Allah and His Messenger - Allah has cursed them in this world and the Hereafter and prepared for them a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse establishes that causing harm to Allah and His Messenger—whether through disbelief, mocking the religion, or acting against the divine commands—is a grave transgression that severs the perpetrator from Allah's mercy, resulting in both spiritual alienation in this life and an everlasting, degrading torment in the afterlife.

translation: And those who harm believing men and believing women for something they did not earn, have certainly borne upon themselves a slander and a manifest sin.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern prohibition against causing any form of physical or verbal harm to innocent believers who have not committed an act justifying such treatment; it emphasizes that falsely accusing or persecuting the righteous is a grave transgression that carries the heavy burden of both defamation and clear, unforgivable sin in the sight of God.

translation: O Prophet, tell your wives and your daughters and the women of the believers to bring down over themselves [part of] their outer garments. That is more suitable that they will be known and not be abused. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse commands believing women to draw their outer garments close to their bodies when they go out in public, serving as a distinct sign of their modesty and dignity. The purpose of this modest dress is to protect them from the harassment or unwanted attention of those who might mistake them for someone of low moral character, thereby ensuring their safety and societal respect while reflecting the divine guidance that balances practical protection with moral integrity.

translation: If the hypocrites, and those in whose hearts is a disease, and the sowers of false rumors in the city do not cease, We will surely incite you against them; then they will not remain your neighbors therein except for a little while.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning from Allah to those elements within the Islamic community of Medina who were actively working to undermine the stability of the state through hypocrisy, moral corruption, and the spreading of destabilizing lies; it signifies that if these individuals persist in their subversive actions, Allah would grant the Prophet the authority and power to expel them, resulting in their inability to continue living in close proximity to the believers for much longer.

translation: Accursed, wherever they are found, they will be seized and slaughtered completely.
interpretation: This verse refers to the hypocrites who actively sowed discord and hostility within the early Muslim community, indicating that because of their persistent treachery and refusal to desist from subversion, they have forfeited their protection and safety, facing severe consequences wherever they might hide due to the gravity of their betrayal against the collective security of the believers.

translation: This is the way of Allah with those who have passed on before, and you will never find in the way of Allah any change.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the laws governing the rise and fall of nations—such as the triumph of truth over falsehood and the consequences of moral decay—are immutable divine constants that have applied to every past civilization and will remain unchanging for all time, as Allah's wisdom and justice are not subject to alteration or inconsistency.

translation: People ask you about the Hour. Say, 'Its knowledge is only with Allah.' And what makes you perceive? Perhaps the Hour is near.
interpretation: The verse clarifies that the specific timing of the Day of Judgment is a mystery known exclusively to Allah, intended to keep humanity in a state of constant mindfulness, preparedness, and moral responsibility, as the uncertainty of its occurrence serves as a reminder that life is fleeting and the encounter with the Divine could happen at any moment.

translation: Indeed, Allah has cursed the disbelievers and prepared for them a Blaze.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning that those who reject the truth and persist in their denial have severed their bond with divine mercy, leading to a state of exclusion from God's grace and the inevitable consequence of a fierce, eternal punishment that has been specifically designated for them as a result of their own deliberate choice to turn away from faith.

translation: Abiding therein forever; they will not find any protector or helper.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the eternal and irreversible nature of the recompense for those who have turned away from faith and truth, highlighting that once they are placed in their final abode, their state becomes permanent and they are completely cut off from any authority or strength that could rescue them or alleviate their suffering, signifying the total absence of hope for intercession or deliverance.

translation: The Day their faces will be turned about in the Fire, they will say, 'Oh, how we wish we had obeyed Allah and obeyed the Messenger.'
interpretation: This verse portrays the profound regret of the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment, as they experience the physical torment of Hellfire. Their realization is centered on the painful awareness that their suffering is the direct consequence of their disobedience; by choosing to reject the guidance of Allah and the counsel of His Prophet during their worldly life, they have deprived themselves of eternal salvation and are now left only with the bitter yearning for a past they can no longer reclaim.

translation: And they will say, 'Our Lord, indeed we obeyed our masters and our dignitaries, and they led us astray from the [right] way.'
interpretation: This verse portrays the regret of those who, in their worldly life, prioritized the influence, guidance, and authority of their leaders, elders, and those they deemed superior, over the guidance of Allah, ultimately realizing that this blind following led them into a state of spiritual ruin and deviation from the path of truth.

translation: Our Lord, give them a double punishment and curse them with a great curse.
interpretation: The followers in this verse invoke God to inflict a twofold retribution upon their leaders who led them astray, specifically requesting that God remove them from His mercy and grace with the utmost intensity, reflecting the deep resentment and realization of betrayal felt by those who were misguided by the arrogance and falsehood of their predecessors.

translation: O you who have believed, be not like those who annoyed Moses; then Allah cleared him of what they said, and he was, in the sight of Allah, distinguished.
interpretation: This verse serves as a moral instruction to the believers to exercise patience, maintain decorum when dealing with their leaders or prophets, and avoid spreading baseless accusations or slander against them, using the vindication of Prophet Moses as a divine precedent that Allah protects the honor of His chosen servants from the falsehoods fabricated against them.

translation: O you who have believed, fear Allah and speak words of appropriate justice.
interpretation: This verse calls upon the believers to cultivate a constant consciousness of Allah in all their affairs, and emphasizes the weight of human speech by commanding them to ensure their words are truthful, direct, and free from falsehood or ambiguity, as integrity in language is a fundamental reflection of a sincere heart and a means to maintain social harmony and personal righteousness.

translation: He will rectify your deeds for you and forgive you your sins. And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly attained a great attainment.
interpretation: The verse implies that the root of all success lies in the alignment of one's actions with Divine guidance; by prioritizing obedience to Allah and His Messenger, a person receives a twofold blessing: their external actions are refined and made effective, and their internal shortcomings are pardoned, leading to a state of spiritual wholeness that constitutes the ultimate victory.

translation: Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they declined to bear it and feared it; but man [undertook to] bear it. Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant.
interpretation: The 'Trust' (al-amanah) refers to the burden of moral responsibility, free will, and the accountability of choosing between obedience and disobedience to God. The heavens, the earth, and the mountains, despite their vastness and power, recognized the immense gravity and potential consequences of such a choice and chose to remain in a state of natural, involuntary submission. Human beings, however, accepted this responsibility, but in their historical tendency toward self-oppression (zulm) by failing to fulfill their duty to their Creator, and their ignorance (jahl) of the ultimate consequences of their actions, they struggle to uphold the sanctity of this divine mandate.

translation: That Allah may punish the hypocrite men and hypocrite women and the polytheist men and polytheist women and that Allah may accept repentance from the believing men and believing women. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse signifies the ultimate manifestation of Divine Justice and Mercy, where the hypocrites and polytheists, who deliberately chose to persist in falsehood and reject the truth despite clear guidance, face the consequences of their rebellion, while those who maintained their faith, though not perfect and prone to human frailty, are encompassed by Allah’s grace, as His nature is to forgive the repentant and show compassion to those who seek His path.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful. [All] praise is [due] to Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth, and to Him belongs [all] praise in the Hereafter. And He is the Wise, the Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse establishes that Allah is the absolute owner and sovereign of everything in existence, and because all perfection, blessings, and manifestations of power originate from Him, He is the only one truly deserving of unconditional praise in this life and the next. By declaring Himself the Wise and the Acquainted, Allah emphasizes that His dominion is not arbitrary; rather, He manages the affairs of His creation with perfect divine wisdom, ensuring that everything in the heavens and the earth unfolds according to a precise and purposeful plan that aligns with His ultimate knowledge of all hidden and manifest realities.

translation: He knows what penetrates into the earth and what emerges from it and what descends from the heaven and what ascends therein; and He is the Merciful, the Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute and comprehensive omniscience of Allah, detailing His awareness of everything that enters the earth—such as seeds, rain, or the deceased—and everything that emerges from it, like plants, minerals, or springs. It further highlights His knowledge of all that descends from the heavens, such as revelation, angels, or provisions, and all that ascends back to them, including deeds, souls, and angels. By concluding the verse with His attributes of being the Merciful and the Forgiving, the Quran reminds the believer that although God possesses such infinite and minute knowledge of all human actions and states, this knowledge is coupled with grace, ensuring that for those who turn to Him in repentance, His mercy and forgiveness precede His judgment.

translation: And those who disbelieve say, 'The Hour will not come to us.' Say, 'Yes, by my Lord, it will surely come to you.' [He is] the Knower of the unseen. Not absent from Him is an atom's weight within the heavens or within the earth or [what is] smaller than that or greater, except that it is in a clear register.
interpretation: This verse serves as a powerful refutation of those who deny the occurrence of the Day of Judgment by highlighting the absolute nature of Divine Omniscience. By swearing by His Lordship, Allah asserts that the inevitable arrival of the Hour is anchored in His perfect knowledge, which encompasses every minute detail of existence. The emphasis on the 'clear register' signifies that nothing in the universe—regardless of how infinitesimal, such as an atom, or how grand—exists outside of Allah's comprehensive awareness and decree, meaning that His ability to resurrect the dead is an inherent consequence of His perfect knowledge and control over every particle of creation.

translation: That He may reward those who believe and do righteous deeds. Those will have forgiveness and noble provision.
interpretation: The verse conveys that Allah grants His servants who combined sincere belief in their hearts with righteous deeds performed by their limbs two distinct gifts: first, the erasure of their sins through divine forgiveness, and second, an honorable, abundant, and everlasting reward in Paradise, emphasizing that their virtuous actions are the direct cause of this generous recompense.

translation: And those who strive against Our verses, seeking to frustrate [Our will] - for them there will be a punishment of a painful torment.
interpretation: This verse indicates that those who exert strenuous efforts to invalidate the truth, hinder the spread of God's signs, and deceive people regarding the divine message—believing they can escape God's judgment—will face a humiliating and severe punishment, specifically described as 'rijz,' which denotes a loathsome and painful form of chastisement reserved for the most persistent rejecters of the truth.

translation: And those who have been given knowledge see that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth, and it guides to the path of the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: The verse highlights that individuals possessing true spiritual and intellectual insight recognize that the Qur'an is the absolute truth originating from God; this realization serves as a divine beacon that leads humanity toward the straight path of the Almighty, who is worthy of all praise and glory in every state.

translation: And those who disbelieve say, 'Shall we point you to a man who tells you that when you have been torn to pieces with complete disintegration, you will indeed be in a new creation?'
interpretation: The disbelievers mockingly suggested that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was insane or deluded for claiming that human bodies, after being reduced to scattered dust and disintegrated into nothingness, could ever be reconstructed into a living form, thus revealing their profound disbelief in the possibility of resurrection and the power of Allah to restore life after death.

translation: Has he fabricated a lie against Allah, or is there madness in him? Rather, those who do not believe in the Hereafter are in the punishment and extreme error.
interpretation: The disbelievers, due to their arrogance and disbelief in the message brought by the Prophet, attempted to dismiss his teachings by accusing him of either intentionally lying to forge a message from God or suffering from mental illness. The verse clarifies that their dismissal is rooted not in reason, but in their rejection of the afterlife, which blinds them to the truth and leads them into a state of severe moral and spiritual deviation, ultimately resulting in their inevitable suffering.

translation: Do they not see what is before them and what is behind them of the heaven and the earth? If We willed, We could cause the earth to swallow them or let fall upon them fragments from the sky. Indeed in that is a sign for every servant who turns back [to Allah in repentance].
interpretation: The verse serves as a profound admonition regarding the absolute sovereignty and power of Allah over all dimensions of existence, highlighting that human beings are encompassed by His dominion in every direction. It suggests that safety and stability are not inherent qualities of the world but are maintained solely by Divine will, and that any perceived security is illusory if one persists in heedlessness. For the soul that turns to Allah with a repentant heart, these cosmic realities become clear signs of His majesty, prompting the believer to seek refuge in His mercy rather than relying on the precariousness of the material world.

translation: And We certainly gave David from Us bounty, 'O mountains, repeat [Our] praises with him, and the birds [as well],' and We made pliable for him iron.
interpretation: God bestowed upon David a profound favor by granting him the miraculous ability to command the inanimate mountains and the birds to join him in glorifying Allah, serving as a manifestation of his prophetic authority over creation, while simultaneously softening hard iron in his hands like wax, allowing him to craft protective armor and tools without the need for a forge, thereby demonstrating God's supreme power to alter the nature of matter to aid His chosen servant.

translation: [And We commanded David], 'Make full coats of mail and calculate [precisely] the links, and work righteousness. Indeed I, of what you do, am Seeing.'
interpretation: God instructs Prophet David to master the craft of armor-making by creating interlocking rings that are neither too tight, which would hinder movement, nor too loose, which would compromise protection, signifying the divine emphasis on professional precision and excellence in one's worldly labor as a form of worship that must be coupled with consistent righteous deeds, under the constant awareness that God witnesses every detail of human conduct.

translation: And to Solomon [We subjected] the wind: its morning journey was a month's distance and its afternoon journey was a month's distance. And We made flow for him a spring of molten copper. And among the jinn were those who worked before him by the permission of his Lord; and whoever deviated among them from Our command, We would make him taste of the punishment of the Blaze.
interpretation: God bestowed upon Solomon extraordinary mastery over the natural and supernatural worlds, granting him control over the wind to facilitate rapid travel, liquefying copper as a miraculous resource for his construction projects, and subjugating the jinn to perform laborious tasks under his authority; this divine authority served as a test of obedience, where any jinn who rebelled against Solomon’s divinely ordained mandate would face immediate and severe celestial retribution, illustrating that all worldly power is ultimately subject to God’s absolute sovereignty and moral judgment.

translation: They made for him what he willed of elevated chambers, statues, basins as large as reservoirs, and fixed cauldrons. [We said], 'Work, O family of David, in gratitude.' And few of My servants are grateful.
interpretation: The verse serves as a divine command for Prophet Solomon’s family to acknowledge the immense blessings of Allah—such as the subjugation of the Jinn who performed elaborate architectural and industrial tasks for them—by embodying gratitude through righteous deeds. It emphasizes that true gratitude is not merely a verbal expression of thanks, but a state of constant devotion and obedience, noting that those who maintain this profound level of appreciative worship are exceedingly rare among humanity.

translation: And when We decreed death for him, nothing indicated to them his death except a creature of the earth eating away his staff. But when he fell, the jinn became clear that if they had known the unseen, they would not have remained in the humiliating punishment.
interpretation: The verse illustrates the inherent limitation of the jinn regarding knowledge of the unseen; despite their perceived power and the human-like assumption that they possess supernatural insight, their failure to perceive the death of Sulaiman (Solomon) while he remained upright on his staff until it was consumed by termites proves that they, like all created beings, are confined to the manifest world and cannot penetrate the divine mysteries of the future or the hidden states of others.

translation: Indeed, there was for [the people of] Saba' in their dwelling place a sign: two [fields of] gardens on the right and on the left. [They were told], 'Eat from the provisions of your Lord and be grateful to Him. A good land [have you], and a forgiving Lord.'
interpretation: This verse highlights how Allah bestowed abundant blessings upon the people of Saba' as a clear sign of His power and grace, manifested in their lush, expansive orchards.
