interpretation: This verse serves as a divine exhortation to the disbelievers to be mindful of both the sins they have committed in the past and the consequences they may face in the future life, urging them to embrace piety as the essential path to attaining Allah's mercy and salvation.

translation: And no sign comes to them from the signs of their Lord except that they turn away from it.
interpretation: This verse highlights the deep-seated spiritual blindness and stubbornness of the disbelievers, indicating that their rejection of the truth is not due to a lack of evidence or clear manifestations of God's power, but rather a willful choice to ignore and turn away from divine guidance whenever it is presented to them.

translation: And when it is said to them, 'Spend from that which Allah has provided for you,' those who disbelieve say to those who believe, 'Should we feed someone whom, if Allah had willed, He would have fed? You are not but in clear error.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the flawed logic of the disbelievers who misused the concept of divine predestination to justify their stinginess and apathy toward the needy. By arguing that the poor would be fed by God directly if He willed it, they attempted to shift their moral responsibility onto the divine will, essentially rejecting the duty of charity as a test of faith and human compassion, while simultaneously mocking the believers for their commitment to social obligation.

translation: And they say, 'When will this promise be, if you should be truthful?'
interpretation: The disbelievers are expressing their skepticism and denial regarding the Day of Resurrection, using a tone of mockery and challenge to demand that the believers produce proof of the time of its occurrence, as they do not believe that such a day will ever come to pass.

translation: They do not await except one blast, which will seize them while they are disputing.
interpretation: The verse illustrates the suddenness and inevitability of the Day of Resurrection, describing how people will be struck by the final trumpet blast while they are deeply engrossed in their worldly affairs, worldly arguments, and mundane business, caught entirely off guard by the finality of their end.

translation: Then they will not be able to make a testament, nor can they return to their people.
interpretation: This verse describes the sudden and overwhelming nature of the Trumpet's blast on the Day of Resurrection, indicating that the event will happen so unexpectedly that human beings will be caught in the midst of their worldly affairs, completely unable to settle their pending debts or finalize last-minute arrangements, and finding themselves irreversibly cut off from the families and homes they once knew.

translation: And the Horn will be blown; and at once from the graves to their Lord they will hasten.
interpretation: This verse depicts the sudden and inevitable moment of resurrection, where the blast of the Trumpet signals the end of the worldly life, compelling all of humanity to emerge from their graves in a state of rapid, unstoppable motion toward the Divine Presence to account for their deeds.

translation: They will say, 'Woe to us! Who has raised us up from our sleeping place?' This is what the Most Gracious had promised, and the messengers spoke the truth.
interpretation: This verse depicts the scene of the Resurrection, where the disbelievers express their profound shock and regret upon being awakened from the silence of their graves, suddenly realizing that the life after death, which they had previously mocked and denied, is an undeniable reality that fulfills exactly what the Prophets had foretold.

translation: It will not be but one blast, and at once they will all be brought present before Us.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the absolute ease with which Allah will resurrect all of humanity at the end of time; it signifies that the command for the final gathering is singular and instantaneous, emphasizing that no soul can escape the inevitable assembly for judgment when the divine decree is executed.

translation: So today, no soul will be wronged at all, and you will not be recompensed except for what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse affirms the absolute justice of God on the Day of Resurrection, clarifying that every individual will be held accountable strictly for their own deeds, without suffering any injustice, reduction of reward for good actions, or increase in punishment for evil ones.

translation: Indeed, the companions of Paradise today are in an occupation, enjoying themselves.
interpretation: The people of Paradise are so deeply engrossed and delightfully occupied with the bliss, bounties, and intimacy they experience in the gardens of eternal joy that they are completely distracted from the concerns, troubles, or worldly memories that might otherwise dampen their perfect state of happiness and contentment.

translation: They and their spouses will be in shade, reclining on adorned couches.
interpretation: This verse describes the state of the people of Paradise, emphasizing their ultimate comfort and honor; by being under the shade, they are protected from any heat or distress, and by reclining on raised, luxurious couches alongside their righteous companions, it signifies that their reward is one of everlasting rest, dignity, and blissful companionship in the presence of their Lord.

translation: They will have therein fruits, and they will have whatever they request.
interpretation: This verse describes the state of the people of Paradise, emphasizing that they are not only provided with an abundance of delicious, ever-available fruits but also possess the absolute authority to have any desire or wish fulfilled the moment they ask for it, reflecting the ultimate fulfillment and limitless generosity of Allah in the afterlife.

translation: (They will have) 'Peace,' a word from a Merciful Lord.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the reward for the righteous in Paradise is a direct, peaceful greeting from Allah, the Most Merciful, confirming their security, status, and the everlasting satisfaction of His grace, which is the ultimate manifestation of divine favor and tranquility.

translation: And [it will be said], 'Stand apart today, you criminals.'
interpretation: This verse depicts the scene of the Day of Judgment, where God commands a definitive separation between the believers and the transgressors. The command is a manifestation of divine justice, signaling the end of the worldly ambiguity where the righteous and the corrupt were mixed; it marks the moment when the criminals are permanently distinguished and isolated from the people of righteousness, preparatory to their segregation into their respective destinations.

translation: Did I not enjoin upon you, O children of Adam, that you should not worship Satan? Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy.
interpretation: God reminds humanity of the primordial covenant and the inherent guidance provided to them, warning against following the promptings of Satan. By choosing to obey or deify the dictates of Satan—which manifests in following desires, sins, and disbelief—humanity willfully disregards the explicit warnings of their Creator, despite Satan's open, enduring, and undeniable hostility toward them.

translation: And that you worship Me; this is a straight path.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the purpose of human existence is the sincere devotion to Allah alone, affirming that following the path of monotheism and obedience to His commands constitutes the only upright and correct way of life that leads to salvation.

translation: And he has already led astray many of you. Did you not then use your reason?
interpretation: The verse serves as a stern reminder of the historical reality that Shaytan has successfully misled countless generations before the present audience, highlighting that his influence is neither new nor restricted to a few. Allah questions the lack of intellectual discernment among those who follow such misguidance, implying that if they had properly applied their faculty of reason to observe the patterns of past destruction and the clear signs of truth, they would have recognized the trap and avoided falling into the same pattern of error.

translation: This is Hell, which you were promised.
interpretation: This verse signifies the moment of ultimate realization for the deniers when the truth of the afterlife, which they once dismissed as mere superstition or a hollow threat, becomes an undeniable reality before their eyes, marking the commencement of their accountability and the manifestation of divine justice.

translation: Enter it today because you used to disbelieve.
interpretation: This verse addresses the inhabitants of the Fire, commanding them to enter the blazing hell as a direct consequence of their persistent rejection of the truth and their denial of Allah's revelations during their life on earth, highlighting that their eternal suffering is a manifestation of the reality they chose to ignore.

translation: This Day, We shall seal up their mouths, and their hands will speak to Us, and their legs will bear witness to what they used to earn.
interpretation: On the Day of Resurrection, God will render the disbelievers unable to speak or deny their sins, as their own limbs—having been granted the faculty of speech by their Creator—will provide an irrefutable testimony regarding the deeds they performed in their earthly life, leaving them no room for falsehood or excuse.

translation: And if We willed, We could have obliterated their eyes, and they would race to the path, but how could they see?
interpretation: This verse highlights the absolute power of Allah over His creation, illustrating that if He had chosen to deprive the disbelievers of their sight, they would have been unable to navigate even the most familiar of paths; it serves as a reminder that human perception and guidance are entirely dependent upon the will and grace of the Creator.

translation: And if We willed, We could have transformed them [into other forms] in their places, and they would not have been able to proceed, nor could they return.
interpretation: This verse serves as a manifestation of divine omnipotence and a stern warning, illustrating that those who persist in disbelief and arrogance are entirely subject to the power of Allah. By stating that He could immobilize them or transform their very nature, Allah highlights their utter helplessness; they lack the strength to advance toward any goal or to retrace their steps toward repentance or their previous state, emphasizing that their rebellion is only permitted because of His forbearance, not because of their own capability.

translation: And he to whom We grant long life - We reverse him in creation; so will they not use reason?
interpretation: This verse serves as a profound reminder of the frailty of human existence, highlighting how God reverses the physical development of a person as they age, transforming their strength into weakness and their intelligence into child-like ignorance, thereby urging humanity to recognize the transience of worldly life and the absolute power of the Creator.

translation: And We did not teach him poetry, nor is it befitting for him. It is not but a message and a clear Qur'an.
interpretation: God clarifies that the Prophet Muhammad was neither a poet nor was the poetic craft suitable for his noble mission, as poetry often involves artifice and imaginative embellishment that contradicts the divine, objective, and truthful nature of the revelation he brought; therefore, the Qur'an remains a distinct, divinely inspired reminder and a luminous guide that speaks the absolute truth without the metaphorical distortion inherent in human poetry.

translation: That it may give warning to any who are alive, and that the word may be justified against the disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse highlights that the Quran serves as a living, dynamic beacon for those whose hearts are alive with faith and reason, enabling them to accept guidance, while simultaneously establishing the divine argument against those who stubbornly persist in their disbelief, making their eventual judgment inevitable as they have consciously chosen to reject the truth after it was made clear to them.

translation: Do they not see that We have created for them from what Our hands have made, livestock, and they are their owners?
interpretation: This verse serves as a profound reminder of Allah's absolute power and His benevolent grace toward mankind; by attributing the creation of livestock to 'His hands,' Allah emphasizes His direct creative act and personal concern for the needs of humanity, thereby highlighting the irony that while humans claim ownership and mastery over these animals, they exist only because the Creator brought them into being and placed them under human service, which should logically lead the observer to acknowledge the greatness of the Provider and submit to Him in gratitude.

translation: And We have tamed them for them, so some of them they ride, and some of them they eat.
interpretation: Allah signifies His grace and absolute control over creation by having made these large, powerful animals submissive to human beings, despite their inherent strength, allowing man to utilize them for transportation and sustenance as a manifest evidence of His divine mercy and sovereignty.

translation: And for them therein are benefits and drinks. Will they not then give thanks?
interpretation: The verse highlights the divine favor granted to humanity through livestock and the natural resources provided within the earth, emphasizing that these provisions are not merely for survival but also serve as multifaceted sources of utility and sustenance, which should evoke a profound sense of gratitude and recognition of the Creator's benevolence in the hearts of those who reflect.

translation: And they have taken besides Allah gods, that they might be helped.
interpretation: The verse highlights the human tendency to seek refuge in false objects of worship or worldly power structures in the hope of gaining victory or relief from difficulties, illustrating the misguided belief that turning away from the Creator can lead to genuine empowerment, whereas in reality, these idols possess no power to aid those who invoke them.

translation: They cannot help them, and they themselves are brought forward as troops for them.
interpretation: The idols or false deities that the polytheists worship are powerless to offer any aid or support to their followers, and ironically, both the idols and the worshippers will be gathered together on the Day of Judgment, where the worshipped will be humiliated alongside their followers to demonstrate their shared impotence and the falsehood of their path.

translation: So let not their speech grieve you. Indeed, We know what they conceal and what they declare.
interpretation: Allah comforts the Prophet Muhammad by reminding him that the insults and fabrications of the disbelievers are known to Him, and that their ultimate accountability rests with the Creator; therefore, their hollow words should not cause the Prophet distress, as their schemes are already laid bare before Allah's divine knowledge.

translation: Does man not consider that We created him from a drop of fluid? Then, behold, he is an open adversary.
interpretation: The verse serves as a rebuke to the human being for their ingratitude and audacity in debating against their Creator; it highlights the irony that a person who was once a humble, insignificant drop of fluid now arrogantly stands in open opposition to Allah, forgetting both their lowly origin and the divine power that brought them into existence.

translation: And he presents for Us an example and forgets his [own] creation, saying, 'Who will give life to bones while they are disintegrated?'
interpretation: The verse highlights the irony of a human being, who was once nothing and brought into existence by Allah, questioning the ability of the Creator to resurrect the dead. By forgetting his own miraculous origin—how he was fashioned from a drop of fluid—the skeptic arrogantly assumes that the decomposition of bones into dust serves as a logical barrier to God's power, failing to realize that the One who initiated life from non-existence can easily restore it once it has returned to dust.

translation: Say, 'He will give them life who produced them the first time; and He is, of all creation, Knowing.'
interpretation: The verse serves as a powerful rebuttal to those who deny the resurrection by pointing to the logical consistency of Divine power; since Allah possessed the capacity to bring human life into existence from nothingness at the beginning, it is logically and essentially simpler for Him to restore that life after it has decayed, as His infinite knowledge encompasses every detail of His creation, ensuring that not a single atom or component of a human being is lost to Him.

translation: He who made for you fire from the green tree, and behold, you kindle from it.
interpretation: This verse highlights the immense power of Allah by drawing a parallel between the life-giving nature of green trees—which are full of moisture and seemingly contrary to the nature of fire—and the potential they hold to produce heat and flames. It serves as a reminder of the Creator's ability to bring forth opposite states from one another, signaling His omnipotence in creation and His capacity to bring about the resurrection after death, just as He extracts fire from the seemingly incompatible green wood.

translation: Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the likes of them? Yes, and He is the Knowing Creator.
interpretation: This verse serves as a rhetorical argument for the reality of the afterlife by appealing to the intellect; it posits that the One who possessed the infinite power and wisdom required to bring the vast, complex universe into existence from nothing is undoubtedly capable of resurrecting human beings, as the creation of the heavens and the earth is a far greater manifestation of His power than the creation of man.

translation: His command is only when He intends a thing that He says to it, 'Be,' and it is.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the absolute power and effortless sovereignty of Allah over all creation, emphasizing that the existence of anything is contingent solely upon His divine will and authoritative word, requiring no external effort, tools, or time-consuming processes, thereby highlighting that once Allah decrees an outcome, it manifests instantly without delay or resistance.

translation: So exalted is He in whose hand is the dominion of all things, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse affirms the absolute perfection, transcendence, and sovereign authority of Allah, declaring that every atom in the universe, visible or hidden, is under His total control and ownership; it serves as a profound reminder that human life is finite and that all creation will inevitably return to their Creator for accountability, thereby highlighting the necessity of recognizing His majesty and preparing for the ultimate encounter with Him.

translation: By those who arrange themselves in ranks.
interpretation: God swears by the angels who organize themselves in rows, ready to execute His commands, indicating the perfect order, discipline, and absolute submission that governs the celestial realm in service to the Divine Will.

translation: And by those who drive [the clouds or the angels who drive the affairs of the universe] with a driving force.
interpretation: This verse refers to the angels who are tasked by Allah with driving the clouds or moving the affairs of the universe according to His command, illustrating the divine order and control over the elements of nature through the execution of celestial beings.

translation: By those who recite the message.
interpretation: These are the angels who descend with the revelation, reciting it upon the hearts and tongues of the prophets, thereby disseminating the divine word and preserving it from alteration or corruption.

translation: Indeed, your God is One.
interpretation: This verse establishes the foundational doctrine of Tawhid, emphasizing that the Creator of the universe is singular in His essence, attributes, and actions, thereby negating any notion of plurality or partnership in divinity and demanding exclusive worship directed solely toward Him.

translation: The Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them and the Lord of the risings.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah is the absolute Sovereign and Creator of the entire universe, including the heavens, the earth, and everything existing between them. By specifying 'the Lord of the risings,' it emphasizes His total control over the celestial movements and the precise order of the cosmos, indicating that He governs the changing positions of the sun, moon, and stars throughout the year, which serves as a manifestation of His unique authority and systematic maintenance of creation.

translation: Indeed, We have adorned the nearest heaven with an adornment of stars.
interpretation: God Almighty declares that He has beautified the lowest heaven—the one visible to humans—with stars, which serve both as an ornament to decorate the night sky and as a manifestation of His creative perfection, reflecting His majesty and power to those who observe the heavens with contemplation.

translation: And as protection against every rebellious devil.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the heavens are fortified by the stars against the approach or eavesdropping of the devils who rebel against the command of Allah, ensuring that the celestial domain remains secure from their corruption and their attempts to steal information from the angelic realm.

translation: They cannot listen to the exalted assembly, and they are pelted from every side.
interpretation: This verse describes the state of the devils who attempt to eavesdrop on the secrets of the heavens; they are prevented from hearing the discourse of the angels in the high realm, and they are repelled by brilliant flames or shooting stars whenever they attempt to ascend, ensuring that the divine decree remains protected and inaccessible to those who seek to corrupt or intercept the truth.

translation: Repelled; and for them is a constant punishment.
interpretation: The verse describes the state of the devils who attempt to eavesdrop on the heavenly council; they are forcefully driven away and distanced from the realm of the angels, and beyond this rejection, they are destined to endure a permanent, everlasting, and uninterrupted torment that never ceases.

translation: Except one who steals a snatch, then there follows him a piercing flame.
interpretation: This verse refers to the devils or Jinn who attempt to eavesdrop on the secrets of the heavens by listening to the conversations of the angels; however, they are immediately pursued and driven away by a bright, shooting star or a piercing meteor that strikes them, preventing them from conveying any true information to their human accomplices on earth.

translation: So ask them, 'Is their creation more difficult or those We have created?' Indeed, We created them from sticky clay.
interpretation: This verse serves as a rhetorical challenge to the disbelievers who deny the possibility of resurrection. Allah instructs the Prophet Muhammad to remind them that their own physical existence—created from a base substance like sticky clay—is no less miraculous than the creation of the vast heavens and earth, or the resurrection of the dead; therefore, it is illogical for them to admit that Allah created them initially but doubt His power to recreate them after they have turned to dust.

translation: Nay, you are amazed, while they mock.
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad, reflecting on his astonishment at the stubbornness of the disbelievers who deny the truth of the resurrection despite the clear signs provided; it highlights the contrast between the Prophet’s sincere wonder at their rejection and their dismissive, arrogant mockery of the divine message.

translation: And when they are reminded, they do not take heed.
interpretation: This verse describes the state of those whose hearts have become hardened to the point that the truth no longer finds a receptive place within them; despite the clear signs and admonitions presented to them, they remain obstinate and willfully ignore the guidance, demonstrating that their lack of response is not due to a failure of communication, but a deliberate choice to remain in negligence.

translation: And when they see a sign, they mock.
interpretation: This verse describes the condition of those whose hearts have been hardened by disbelief; when they are presented with a clear miraculous sign or a proof of God's existence and power, instead of reflecting upon it with humility or seeking guidance, they react with derision and contempt, attempting to diminish the significance of the truth by treating it as a joke or a subject of mockery.

translation: And they said, 'This is nothing but clear magic.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the stubborn denial of the disbelievers who, confronted with the undeniable truth and the miraculous nature of the Quran, chose to dismiss it as mere sorcery to protect their own arrogance and preserve the traditional status quo, effectively labeling anything that challenged their worldview as deception.

translation: What! When we die and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be resurrected?
interpretation: This verse reflects the skepticism of the polytheists regarding the afterlife; it highlights their inability to comprehend how the physical elements of a human body, which have disintegrated into soil and decayed bones, could ever be reconstructed and brought back to life, thereby challenging the absolute power of Allah to initiate a new creation after death.

translation: Or our forefathers of old?
interpretation: This rhetorical question expresses the astonishment and disbelief of the polytheists regarding the concept of resurrection, as they found it irrational that their ancestors, who had long since turned to dust and decayed, could be brought back to life again.

translation: Say, 'Yes, and you will be humbled.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a declaration that those who reject the truth and persist in their arrogance will inevitably face a state of total submission and disgrace, as the reality of their accountability before God will strip away all their worldly pride and defiance.

translation: But it will only be a single shout, and behold, they will be watching.
interpretation: The verse describes the sudden transition from the state of death to the state of resurrection; when the command is given for the final blowing of the trumpet, that single, intense sound will be sufficient to awaken all of humanity from their graves, causing them to emerge in a state of astonishment and clear realization of the reality they once doubted, waiting in terror for the judgment to follow.

translation: And they will say, 'Woe to us! This is the Day of Judgment.'
interpretation: The evildoers will realize with terror that the Day of Resurrection, which they once mocked or denied, has arrived, and they will lament their past negligence, recognizing that this is the moment of final reckoning and accountability from which there is no escape.

translation: This is the Day of Judgement, which you used to deny.
interpretation: This verse signifies the moment when the truth is finally revealed and the final decree is passed, marking the irreversible separation between those who lived in belief and submission to God's guidance and those who persisted in rejection and arrogance; it is the manifestation of the reality that the deniers had mocked throughout their worldly lives, confirming that their skepticism was a grave miscalculation of their eternal destiny.

translation: Gather those who committed injustice, along with their counterparts, and what they used to worship.
interpretation: God commands the angels to assemble the wrongdoers, their like-minded peers who shared their beliefs and deeds, and the false deities they worshipped, so that they may all be gathered together for the reckoning and subsequent punishment.

translation: Besides Allah, then guide them to the path of Hell.
interpretation: This verse is a command directed at the angels or the keepers of Hell to assemble the polytheists who associated partners with Allah, illustrating their state of humiliation and abandonment as they are driven toward their final abode of torment, emphasizing that the false deities they once worshipped are powerless to assist them or alter their destiny.

translation: But stop them; indeed, they are to be questioned.
interpretation: This verse signifies that on the Day of Judgment, the evildoers and those who disbelieved will be halted before the presence of Allah to be interrogated and held accountable for their worldly deeds, their intentions, and their rejection of the truth, leaving no room for escape or evasion from divine justice.

translation: What is the matter with you that you do not help one another?
interpretation: This verse represents a rhetorical challenge posed to the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment, highlighting their utter helplessness and inability to support or defend each other against the divine decree, contrasting their former arrogance and mutual reliance in the worldly life with the absolute isolation and abandonment they experience when facing the truth of their accountability.

translation: Rather, they are this day submissive.
interpretation: This verse signifies that on the Day of Resurrection, the arrogance and defiance of the disbelievers will completely vanish, and they will find themselves utterly humbled and surrendered to the divine decree and the absolute authority of Allah, having no power to resist or deny the reality they once rejected.

translation: And they will approach one another, questioning each other.
interpretation: This verse depicts the inhabitants of Paradise engaging in friendly conversation, where they recall their past lives in the worldly realm and reflect upon the trials they endured, thereby expressing their gratitude to Allah for His guidance and mercy that ultimately led them to such a blissful destination.

translation: They will say, 'Indeed, you used to come at us from the right.'
interpretation: The followers will accuse their leaders of using their positions of power, influence, and deceptive oaths to divert them from the path of truth and righteousness, making their falsehood appear as if it were the right and virtuous way.

translation: They will say, 'Rather, you yourselves were not believers.'
interpretation: This verse depicts the scene of the afterlife where the followers who were led astray will confront their leaders or those who deceived them. The deceivers will retort by stripping the followers of any claim to faith, asserting that their alleged belief was never sincere or firm in their hearts, but rather a facade or a result of superficial conformity, thereby absolving themselves of responsibility for those who chose to follow falsehood out of their own free will and inner inclination toward disbelief.

translation: And we had no authority over you, but you were a transgressing people.
interpretation: The followers of the disbelievers and the followers of the devils will disclaim responsibility for one another on the Day of Judgment; the devils will clarify that they possessed no power to force the disbelievers into their path of disbelief, asserting that the choice to reject the truth and commit sins was entirely the free will of the disbelievers themselves, who were already inclined toward rebellion and arrogance against God.

translation: So the word of our Lord has come into effect against us; indeed, we will taste [the punishment].
interpretation: This verse reflects the moment of ultimate realization by the disbelievers when they acknowledge the absolute truth of Allah's decree and warning that they had previously denied, accepting that the promised torment is now an unavoidable reality that they must experience as the consequence of their earthly choices.

translation: So we led you astray, indeed we ourselves were astray.
interpretation: This verse depicts the scene of the people of Hell acknowledging their own accountability for their misguided state. It reveals that the leaders of disbelief, who claimed to invite others to their ways, will admit that they were not guided themselves, thereby dismantling the excuses of their followers who claimed they were merely following the path of their predecessors.

translation: For indeed, on that Day, they will be partners in the punishment.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the wicked individuals who associated partners with Allah and those who led them astray will share in the agony of the Hereafter, as their collective misguidance and shared defiance of truth result in a unified experience of torment where neither the leader nor the follower can escape the burden of their common destination.

translation: Thus do We deal with the criminals.
interpretation: This verse serves as a declaration of divine justice, asserting that the catastrophic consequences faced by those who reject the truth and persist in wrongdoing are not arbitrary; rather, they are a consistent and established law of God, ensuring that arrogance and disbelief inevitably lead to humiliation and loss as a just requital for their rebellion against the divine guidance.

translation: Indeed, when it was said to them, 'There is no deity but Allah,' they were arrogant.
interpretation: The verse highlights that the underlying cause of their rejection of the truth was not a lack of intellectual clarity, but rather an inflated sense of self-importance that prevented them from submitting to the oneness of Allah and the authority of His messengers, as pride acts as a spiritual veil that makes the heart resist humbling itself before the Creator.

translation: And they say, 'Are we to leave our gods for a mad poet?'
interpretation: The disbelievers of the Quraysh expressed their profound rejection and mockery of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) by dismissing his call to monotheism as an absurd abandonment of their ancestral traditions; they falsely accused him of madness and poetic fabrication to justify their stubborn refusal to abandon their idols, thereby revealing that their hostility was rooted in a psychological inability to break free from the established cultural norms they blindly inherited.

translation: Rather, he has come with the truth and confirmed the messengers.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) did not bring anything of his own invention, but rather he arrived with the absolute Truth from God, thereby validating the fundamental message of monotheism and divine law that all previous prophets had conveyed before him.

translation: Indeed, you will be tasters of the painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse serves as a direct and definitive warning to those who persist in disbelief and transgression, affirming that the experience of divine punishment is an inevitable reality they will undergo, emphasizing the inescapability of the consequences resulting from their rejection of the truth.

translation: And you will not be recompensed except for what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse establishes the principle of absolute divine justice, affirming that the reward or punishment a person receives in the hereafter is a direct consequence and manifestation of their own deeds in this life, meaning that every individual’s destiny is shaped entirely by their own actions and choices rather than arbitrary judgment.

translation: Except for the chosen servants of Allah.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the servants of Allah who have been purified of worldly attachments, sins, and the whispers of Satan are exempt from the general condemnation or the influence of evil, as their hearts are exclusively devoted to the sincere worship and remembrance of Allah, thereby securing His protection and guidance.

translation: Those will have a known provision.
interpretation: The verse indicates that the faithful, who are devoted to Allah and seek His pleasure, have been promised a specific and assured reward in Paradise—a provision that is not subject to cessation, scarcity, or deprivation, but is instead perfectly suited to their needs and honors their service to the Divine.

translation: And fruits, and they will be honored.
interpretation: This verse highlights the immense rewards bestowed upon the people of Paradise, where they are provided with an abundance of delicious fruits, not merely for sustenance but as a mark of the high status, reverence, and continuous favor they receive from Allah, ensuring their comfort and dignity are upheld in every aspect of their existence.

translation: In gardens of pleasure.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the righteous will reside in the gardens of Paradise, which are filled with every type of everlasting delight, comfort, and blessing, free from any distress, sorrow, or imperfection, as a reward for their faith and virtuous deeds in the worldly life.

translation: On thrones, facing one another.
interpretation: This verse describes the state of the dwellers of Paradise as they recline upon elevated couches or thrones in a position of perfect equality, peace, and mutual affection, signifying that there is no enmity, malice, or social hierarchy among them, as they all share in the eternal honor and joy of being in the presence of their Lord.

translation: Circulated among them will be a cup from a flowing spring.
interpretation: This verse describes the refined hospitality in Paradise, where the inhabitants are served by attendants with vessels of pure, delicious wine that flows freely from a pristine, inexhaustible source, emphasizing the constant state of ease and luxury provided to the righteous without any of the intoxicating or harmful side effects associated with worldly drinks.

translation: White, delicious to the drinkers.
interpretation: This verse describes the wine of Paradise, indicating that it is pure in color, visually appealing, and free from the foulness, bitterness, or intoxication associated with worldly wine, providing only pleasure and refreshment to those who consume it.

translation: No bad effect is there in it, nor will they be intoxicated from it.
interpretation: This verse describes the wine of Paradise, emphasizing that unlike the wine of this world which causes physical illness, headaches, or the loss of mental faculties and sobriety, the wine provided to the dwellers of Paradise is pure, wholesome, and free from any side effects that could disrupt their enjoyment or state of consciousness.

translation: And with them will be women limiting [their] glances, with beautiful, large eyes.
interpretation: This verse describes the companions of the believers in Paradise, emphasizing their modesty and exclusive devotion to their spouses; by 'limiting their glances,' it signifies that they look only at their husbands with affection and loyalty, while their 'large, beautiful eyes' serve as a metaphor for their exquisite purity and captivating grace, reflecting the perfect bliss and tranquility found in the presence of one's beloved in the afterlife.

translation: As if they were hidden eggs.
interpretation: This verse describes the purity, delicacy, and preservation of the women of Paradise, likening their untarnished and protected skin to the color and texture of an egg that has been kept hidden from exposure to dust, wind, or sunlight, symbolizing their pristine beauty and high status.

translation: Then they will approach one another, questioning each other.
interpretation: This verse describes the scene among the inhabitants of Paradise as they engage in conversation, reflecting back upon their worldly lives and the difficulties they faced in remaining steadfast in their faith, thereby highlighting the culmination of their shared perseverance and the communal joy they experience in the afterlife.

translation: A speaker among them will say, 'Indeed, I had a companion [on earth].'
interpretation: In this verse, Allah describes the scene of a believer in Paradise who recalls his life on earth and remembers a close acquaintance—a non-believer—who used to mock his faith and dispute the reality of the afterlife, highlighting how the influence of such companions was a test of one's conviction.

translation: He said, 'Are you indeed of those who confirm [the truth]?'
interpretation: This verse reflects a tone of skepticism or wonder from the person addressed, questioning whether the recipient truly believes in the reality of the afterlife or the specific truth being presented, highlighting the psychological distance often found between those who hold deep faith and those who demand empirical proof for metaphysical concepts.

translation: What! When we die and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be raised up and recompensed?
interpretation: This verse reflects the skepticism of the polytheists regarding the afterlife; they expressed astonishment and doubt at the possibility of resurrection after their bodies have completely decayed into dust and bones, finding the concept of standing before God for judgment and receiving their due reward or punishment to be illogical or impossible.

translation: He will say, 'Will you look down?'
interpretation: The speaker—identified by scholars as a believer in Paradise—will ask his companions to look down into the depths of Hell to witness the state of those who were once his companions in the worldly life but chose disbelief, highlighting the stark contrast between the reward of the righteous and the punishment of the wrongdoers.

translation: Then he will look down and see him in the midst of the Hellfire.
interpretation: The verse describes a believer in Paradise who, upon reflecting on the state of his companions in the worldly life, asks about a specific person who once doubted the resurrection. He is then granted a vision by Allah to look into the depths of Hell, where he perceives that former companion enduring the punishment, thereby confirming the justice of Allah and the consequence of the arrogance and disbelief that the individual once held.

translation: He said, 'By Allah, you almost brought me to ruin.'
interpretation: In this verse, the believer is addressing his companion in the Hereafter, acknowledging that the companion’s persistent invitations to disbelief and worldly distraction were so influential that they nearly caused him to succumb to error and perish spiritually, highlighting the profound impact that companions have on one's faith and the necessity of being cautious regarding one's social circles.

translation: And if not for the favor of my Lord, I would have been among those brought [into Hell].
interpretation: The verse acknowledges that the speaker's escape from the punishment of the fire is not due to his own merit, but rather solely by the grace and guidance of Allah, which shielded him from the corruption and error that lead one to be present among the condemned.

translation: Are we then not to die?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical question posed by the people of Paradise who, in their state of eternal bliss and joy, recall the life of the world and find it difficult to believe that they will never again experience the sting of death, thereby confirming that their current state of existence is permanent, absolute, and beyond the reach of any further termination or change.

translation: Except for our first death, and we will not be punished.
interpretation: This verse reflects the desperate sentiment of the disbelievers who, having dismissed the reality of the afterlife throughout their worldly lives, attempt to minimize the gravity of death by claiming it is a singular, final event, thereby denying the possibility of a resurrection or subsequent reckoning for their earthly deeds.

translation: Indeed, this is the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the ultimate success, which transcends all worldly achievements and fleeting gains, is attaining the pleasure of Allah and securing a place in Paradise, as this represents the absolute peak of human salvation and eternal prosperity.

translation: For the like of this let the workers work.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine exhortation directed at those who strive, urging them to direct their labor, devotion, and virtuous deeds toward achieving the eternal bliss of Paradise and the pleasure of Allah, rather than exhausting their efforts in pursuit of the fleeting, transient ornaments of this worldly life.

translation: Is that better as a lodging or the tree of Zaqqum?
interpretation: This rhetorical question serves as a severe warning, contrasting the eternal, peaceful dwellings prepared for the righteous in Paradise with the horrific, tormenting nature of the Zaqqum tree, which grows in the heart of Hellfire and serves as the only source of sustenance for its inhabitants, highlighting the stark choice between divine reward and inescapable punishment.

translation: Indeed, We have made it a trial for the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse indicates that this specific entity or reality is appointed by Allah as a test and a means of exposure for the unjust; their refusal to submit to the truth or their arrogance in the face of divine signs leads them into further disbelief, thereby confirming their moral corruption and hastening their deserved consequences.

translation: It is a tree that emerges from the depths of Hellfire.
interpretation: This verse metaphorically describes the Zaqqum tree as an entity that originates from the very heart and foundation of the Fire, signifying that its existence is intrinsically linked to the torment of the inhabitants of Hell, making its bitter fruit and horrific nature a central part of their eternal punishment.

translation: Its fruit clusters are as if they were the heads of devils.
interpretation: This imagery serves as a hyperbolic depiction of the terrifying and hideous appearance of the fruit of the Zaqqum tree, utilizing the concept of 'the heads of devils'—which are associated in the Arab imagination with everything repulsive and frightening—to convey to the human mind the extreme repugnance and unsettling nature of the sustenance provided to the inhabitants of Hell, emphasizing that even the visual appearance of their food is a source of torment and dread.

translation: Then indeed, they will be eating from it and filling with it their bellies.
interpretation: This verse describes the torment of the people of Hellfire, illustrating the intensity of their hunger and the wretchedness of their sustenance; specifically, it refers to their consumption of the Zaqqum tree, which is so repugnant and burning that it fills their stomachs not to nourish them, but to further punish their inner organs, signifying that their suffering is both internal and external, continuous and inescapable.

translation: Then, indeed, they will have upon it a mixture of scalding water.
interpretation: After the inhabitants of Hell have been served their initial refreshments, their drink will be blended with a mixture of boiling water that is intensely hot, causing their insides to be scorched and further intensifying their agony as a direct consequence of their persistence in disbelief and transgression.

translation: Then, indeed, their return will be to the Hellfire.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern reminder that all those who persist in disbelief, arrogance, and transgression against the divine commands will ultimately face their final destination in the Fire of Hell, as there is no refuge or escape from the accountability that follows this worldly life.

translation: Indeed, they found their fathers astray.
interpretation: This verse explains that the reason for the disbelief of those who reject the truth is their blind imitation of their ancestors, as they chose to follow the corrupted traditions and misguided paths of those who came before them without using their own reason or seeking divine guidance.

translation: And they are rushing in their footsteps.
interpretation: This verse describes the state of those who were given the scriptures and the truth but chose to follow their desires and imitate the actions of their predecessors in misguidance, showing how they eagerly and blindly persist in the same errors that led the previous generations to destruction.

translation: And certainly, most of the ancients went astray before them.
interpretation: The verse serves as a historical reminder and a sobering reality check for the contemporaries of the Prophet Muhammad, illustrating that deviation from the truth is not a new phenomenon; rather, it has been the persistent pattern of the majority of past nations who disregarded the guidance of their messengers, thereby emphasizing that numbers and tradition are no guarantee of righteousness.

translation: And indeed, We sent among them warners.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine mercy and the continuity of God's guidance, explaining that throughout history, Allah has never left His creation without messengers to remind them of the truth, warn them against the consequences of disbelief, and guide them toward the path of righteousness to establish a clear proof against those who choose to ignore the divine message.

translation: So observe how was the end of those who were warned.
interpretation: This verse serves as a profound directive to contemplate the historical consequences faced by those who rejected the truth and disregarded the warnings of the messengers, emphasizing that persistence in arrogance and denial inevitably leads to a devastating downfall, thereby acting as a cautionary lesson for all who follow in their footsteps.

translation: Except the chosen servants of Allah.
interpretation: This verse indicates that there is a group of believers whom Allah has purified and refined, protecting them from the deceptions of Satan and the allure of worldly desires, which ensures their immunity from the path of evil and keeps them steadfast in sincere devotion and obedience to Him.

translation: And Noah had certainly called Us, and how excellent were We to respond.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's attribute of being the All-Hearing and All-Responsive. When Prophet Noah, peace be upon him, faced the overwhelming denial and oppression of his people for centuries and finally called upon his Lord for relief and justice, Allah responded by saving him and the believers in the Ark and delivering his promise of divine judgment against the disbelievers. It serves as a reminder to the believers that Allah is near to those who sincerely invoke Him and that His help is certain and perfect in its timing and manner.

translation: And We saved him and his family from the great distress.
interpretation: This verse refers to the divine deliverance of Prophet Noah and his followers from the overwhelming calamity of the Flood, illustrating that when believers face extreme persecution or life-threatening hardship, Allah provides a path of salvation, thereby validating the truth of their message and rewarding their steadfastness in the face of inevitable destruction.

translation: And We made his descendants the ones remaining.
interpretation: This verse signifies that Allah ensured the survival and continuation of the human race specifically through the lineage of Prophet Nuh (Noah), meaning that after the great flood, all subsequent generations of humanity are descendants of those who were saved with him in the Ark, rendering his progeny the sole survivors and the source of all future mankind.

translation: And We left for him [favorable mention] among the later generations.
interpretation: This verse signifies that Allah decreed that the righteous legacy, honorable reputation, and the beautiful message of the prophet mentioned in the preceding context would be preserved and cherished by successive generations of believers until the end of time, ensuring that his example remains a source of guidance and inspiration.

translation: Peace be upon Noah among the worlds.
interpretation: This verse signifies that Allah granted Prophet Noah a legacy of eternal praise and noble remembrance among all generations and nations throughout history, ensuring that his name is associated with honor, righteousness, and the successful propagation of the divine message until the end of time.

translation: Thus do We reward the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse signifies that God's justice and benevolence are consistent and established; just as He grants success, protection, and spiritual elevation to those who perfect their faith and deeds through sincerity and excellence in their worship and conduct, He will unfailingly bestow the same divine grace upon anyone who follows that path of excellence.

translation: He is indeed one of Our believing servants.
interpretation: This phrase serves as a divine attestation to the sincerity and depth of the individual's faith, signifying that they have attained a rank of excellence in their submission to God, characterized by an unwavering trust and consistent righteous conduct that manifests their true status as a beloved servant of the Creator.

translation: Then We drowned the others.
interpretation: This verse signifies the ultimate consequence of divine justice for those who persisted in their arrogance and disbelief despite clear warnings, marking the final stage of their destruction as a historical lesson for all humanity regarding the fate of those who reject the truth.

translation: And indeed, among those who followed his way was Abraham.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the Prophet Abraham was counted among the followers of the methodology and creed of Noah, characterized by the sincere devotion to the oneness of God, the rejection of polytheism, and the dedication to guiding humanity toward the truth with patience and steadfastness.

translation: When he came to his Lord with a sound heart.
interpretation: A sound heart, or Qalb-i-Salim, signifies a heart that is completely free from polytheism, doubt, and spiritual diseases such as pride, envy, and arrogance, being purely dedicated to Allah with total sincerity, devotion, and steadfast faith, which is the ultimate condition for success on the Day of Judgment.

translation: When he said to his father and his people, 'What is it that you worship?'
interpretation: Prophet Ibrahim (AS) initiates a dialogue with his family and community by questioning the rationality of their idol worship, intending to stir their intellects and expose the absurdity of directing devotion toward objects that possess no power to hear, see, or benefit them.

translation: Is it falsehood as gods other than Allah that you desire?
interpretation: This rhetorical question serves as a severe rebuke from the Prophet Ibrahim to his people, highlighting the absolute absurdity and spiritual deception involved in abandoning the Creator of the universe to worship idols that possess no power, knowledge, or inherent divinity, thereby exposing the irrationality of their desires which prioritize temporary worldly gratification and ancestral traditions over the eternal truth of monotheism.

translation: Then what is your thought about the Lord of the worlds?
interpretation: This verse serves as a profound rhetorical challenge to humanity, urging them to reflect on the nature and attributes of Allah; it implies that if one truly contemplates His absolute power, infinite mercy, and wisdom, they would realize the gravity of their actions and the necessity of placing complete trust, hope, and sincerity in Him alone, rather than associating partners with Him or doubting His promise.

translation: And he cast a look at the stars.
interpretation: This verse refers to Prophet Ibrahim, who looked at the stars to contemplate the vastness of Allah's creation and the wisdom behind their orderly movement, using the celestial bodies as a means to reason that the One who created such magnificent systems is the only One worthy of worship, distinct from the transient objects his people mistakenly deified.

translation: And he said, 'Indeed, I am ill.'
interpretation: Prophet Ibrahim said this as a clever strategy to excuse himself from participating in the polytheistic festivities of his people, intending to use their absence while they attended these rites to break their idols and demonstrate the impotence of their false gods.

translation: Then they turned away from him, retreating.
interpretation: This verse describes the physical act of turning one's back and moving away from a messenger or a divine message, symbolizing a deliberate rejection of the truth and a refusal to listen, highlighting the arrogance of those who choose to distance themselves from guidance.

translation: Then he turned to their gods and said, 'Will you not eat?'
interpretation: Prophet Ibrahim, peace be upon him, approached the idols that his people worshipped with food placed before them, questioning them in a manner of mockery and profound irony to expose their lifelessness and inability to benefit or harm themselves, thereby demonstrating to his people the absurdity of worshipping inanimate objects that cannot even consume food despite being presented with it.

translation: What is the matter with you that you do not speak?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical challenge posed by Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) to his people, who worshipped idols. By asking why they do not speak, he highlights the absurdity and inherent lifelessness of their idols, demonstrating that if these objects were truly divine or possessed any power, they would be able to defend themselves or respond to his inquiries, thus exposing the intellectual bankruptcy of polytheism.

translation: Then he turned upon them, striking them down with [his] right hand.
interpretation: This verse describes Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him) entering the temple of the idols after the people had left for their festival, where he proceeded to destroy the false deities with his hands, physically demonstrating their utter inability to defend themselves or do anything to prevent their own destruction, thereby exposing the futility of worshipping inanimate objects that have no power to harm or benefit.

translation: Then they came towards him, rushing.
interpretation: This verse describes the condition of those who were seeking Prophet Lut (Lot), peace be upon him, as they approached his house in a state of intense eagerness and haste, driven by their corrupt desires to commit sin with the guests who were actually angels sent by God.

translation: He said, 'Do you worship that which you [yourselves] carve?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the absurdity and inherent contradiction of idolatry, as Prophet Ibrahim challenges his people for directing their worship and devotion toward objects that they have physically crafted with their own hands, thereby elevating the created work above the Creator who gave them the ability to carve in the first place.

translation: And Allah created you and that which you do.
interpretation: This verse affirms the doctrine of divine decree and creation, asserting that all human actions, whether they be intentions, movements, or outcomes, originate from the power and pre-ordainment of Allah, as He is the Creator of both the human agent and the very acts they perform, while human beings remain accountable for their choices through their own acquisition of those deeds.

translation: They said, 'Construct for him a structure and cast him into the burning fire.'
interpretation: This verse recounts the desperate and hostile response of the idolaters who, unable to refute the truth of Prophet Ibrahim's message, resorted to extreme violence by constructing a massive furnace to incinerate him, demonstrating how worldly arrogance and stubborn denial often lead people to commit heinous acts against the messengers of God.

translation: So they intended a plan against him, but We made them the lowest.
interpretation: This verse demonstrates the absolute sovereignty of Allah, illustrating that no matter the magnitude of a scheme devised by oppressors to harm a believer, it is ultimately rendered futile and self-defeating by His divine decree, resulting in the humiliation and downfall of the conspirators.

translation: And he said, 'Indeed, I will go to my Lord; He will guide me.'
interpretation: This verse reflects Prophet Ibrahim's (Abraham) reliance and trust in Allah as he prepared to leave his people and their idolatry, signifying that true guidance is found only through turning sincerely to the Creator and distancing oneself from sources of disbelief, with the firm conviction that Allah will lead the seeker to the path of truth and righteousness.

translation: My Lord, grant me [a child] from among the righteous.
interpretation: This is a profound supplication uttered by Prophet Ibrahim, expressing his deep spiritual desire to be blessed with righteous offspring who would continue his legacy of faith, devotion, and obedience to Allah, emphasizing that the true value of progeny lies not in their number or worldly status, but in their character and adherence to the path of piety.

translation: So We gave him the good tidings of a forbearing boy.
interpretation: This verse signifies that in response to Prophet Ibrahim's supplication for a righteous offspring, Allah granted him the joyous news of a son who would be characterized by his exceptional patience, mildness of temper, and steadfastness in the face of trials, reflecting the high moral quality of forbearance that would define his character.

translation: And when he reached with him [the age of] exertion, he said, 'O my son, indeed I have seen in a dream that I [must] slaughter you, so see what you think.' He said, 'O my father, do as you are commanded. You will find me, if Allah wills, of the steadfast.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the pinnacle of submission and absolute obedience to the Divine Will, showcasing the profound bond of faith and mutual trust between Ibrahim and his son Isma'il; the father approaches his son not with command but with consultation out of mercy, while the son demonstrates immediate, unquestioning acceptance of Allah's decree, proving his spiritual fortitude and commitment to patience in the face of the ultimate trial.

translation: And when they had both submitted (to the command of Allah) and he laid him down on his forehead (for the sacrifice).
interpretation: This verse depicts the profound level of faith attained by both Ibrahim and his son Ismail; when they both reached a state of total surrender to the divine will, Ibrahim prepared his son for the sacrifice by laying him face down, demonstrating that true faith is realized through absolute obedience even when it requires the ultimate act of sacrifice.

translation: And We called to him, 'O Abraham,'
interpretation: This verse signifies the moment of divine intervention where Allah addresses Prophet Abraham directly to halt the sacrifice of his son, emphasizing the profound honor of being called upon by God and the immediate transition from a trial of extreme devotion to one of divine relief and mercy.

translation: You have fulfilled the vision. Indeed, We thus reward the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse signifies that Ibrahim (peace be upon him) demonstrated true sincerity in his submission to God's command by preparing to sacrifice his son, thereby proving that his love for his Creator surpassed all worldly attachments; consequently, God accepted his devotion as an act of absolute righteousness, establishing a divine precedent that those who act with excellence and unwavering obedience are granted ease and deliverance after their trials.

translation: Indeed, this is clearly a manifest trial.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the command given to Prophet Ibrahim to sacrifice his son was a distinct and unambiguous test of his absolute devotion, obedience, and surrender to the will of Allah, manifesting his sincerity in faith by prioritizing God's instruction over his deepest natural human affection.

translation: And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice.
interpretation: This verse refers to the moment when Allah accepted the devotion of Prophet Ibrahim and his son Ismail, substituting the impending sacrifice of the son with a magnificent ram. It signifies that the true essence of the trial was the profound submission and complete obedience of both the father and the son to the command of Allah, proving that faith is demonstrated through total surrender to the Divine will, which ultimately resulted in the preservation of the son's life and the establishment of a sacred ritual for future generations.

translation: And We left for him [favorable mention] among the later generations.
interpretation: This verse signifies that God bestowed upon the prophet an enduring legacy of praise and honor, ensuring that his exemplary life, righteous deeds, and steadfast faith in the face of trials continue to be remembered, celebrated, and emulated by succeeding generations of believers throughout history.

translation: Peace be upon Abraham.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine declaration of security and honor bestowed upon Prophet Abraham, signifying that he is shielded from all harm, anxiety, and the tribulations of the Hereafter, while also bestowing upon him a legacy of everlasting praise and remembrance among all nations who follow the path of truth.

translation: Thus do We reward the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse signifies that God's justice and generosity are consistent for those who perform acts of excellence—whether in their worship of God or their treatment of His creation—ensuring that their sincerity and efforts are met with divine favor and a recompense that transcends the standard measure of their deeds.

translation: Indeed, he is of Our believing servants.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the individual being referred to has attained a distinguished status in the sight of Allah, characterized by a profound state of faith that permeates his actions and character, establishing him as one of the chosen few who have truly internalized the essence of submission and devotion to the Creator.

translation: And We gave him the good tidings of Isaac, a prophet from among the righteous.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine favor bestowed upon Prophet Abraham as a reward for his patience and submission to God's command to sacrifice his son; the glad tidings of the birth of Isaac, who would himself attain the noble status of prophethood, served as a comforting assurance and an honor, signifying that God grants those who remain steadfast in their faith not only worldly blessings but also righteous descendants who carry forward the prophetic mission.

translation: And We blessed him and Isaac. And among their descendants is the doer of good and the clearly unjust to himself.
interpretation: God bestowed His divine blessings upon Abraham and his son Isaac, a lineage that became a fountainhead of prophecy and righteousness; however, this verse clarifies that nobility of descent does not guarantee individual salvation, as the descendants are divided between those who perform righteous deeds and those who commit clear acts of injustice against their own souls by disobeying God.

translation: And We certainly conferred favor upon Moses and Aaron.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine grace bestowed upon Moses and Aaron by selecting them for the momentous task of prophethood, providing them with clear signs, supporting them against their adversaries, and granting them victory through the revelation of the Torah, thereby emphasizing that their success and status were not achieved by their own power alone but by the sustained, benevolent intervention of Allah.

translation: And We saved them and their people from the great affliction.
interpretation: This verse refers to the divine rescue of Prophet Moses and Prophet Aaron, along with the Children of Israel, from the brutal tyranny, enslavement, and impending destruction imposed upon them by Pharaoh and his army, illustrating God's intervention to deliver the righteous from overwhelming oppression.

translation: And We gave them victory, so they were the victors.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the triumph of the believers is not merely a product of their own efforts, but is fundamentally secured by divine intervention, confirming that Allah establishes His support for those who remain steadfast in truth, ensuring their eventual dominance over their oppressors.

translation: And We gave them the clear Scripture.
interpretation: The verse indicates that God bestowed upon Moses and Aaron a Book—the Torah—that is characterized by absolute clarity, serving as a definitive guide that distinguishes truth from falsehood and provides a comprehensive framework for the religious and legal obligations of their people.

translation: And We guided them to the straight path.
interpretation: This verse indicates that God provided Musa and Harun with clear divine guidance and a focused methodology that leads directly to His pleasure and salvation, reinforcing that success in conveying the message and upholding the truth is dependent upon God's constant support and direction.

translation: And We left for them [favorable mention] among the later generations.
interpretation: This verse signifies that God ensured the legacy of the prophets and their followers would endure in history, such that subsequent generations would remember them with honor, praise, and respect, thereby immortalizing the impact of their righteous conduct and adherence to the divine message.

translation: Peace be upon Moses and Aaron.
interpretation: This verse signifies a divine declaration of security, honor, and well-being bestowed by Allah upon Moses and Aaron, confirming their elevated status as righteous messengers who were protected from all harm and distress, while also serving as a comforting assurance of their legacy of truth and steadfastness.

translation: Indeed, thus do We reward the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse signifies that God's justice and generosity are consistent for those who perfect their worship and conduct, as He grants them ease, guidance, and honor in both this world and the hereafter as a direct consequence of their sincerity and devotion in performing righteous deeds.

translation: Indeed, they were of Our believing servants.
interpretation: This phrase affirms the spiritual status of the Prophets mentioned in the preceding context, highlighting that their greatness was rooted in their sincere devotion to Allah and their unwavering faith, serving as a testament that true nobility in the sight of God is attained through genuine belief and faithful servitude.

translation: And indeed, Elias was among the messengers.
interpretation: This verse affirms the prophethood of Ilyas (Elias), situating him within the noble line of messengers sent by Allah to guide humanity. It highlights his status as a chosen servant entrusted with the divine message, emphasizing that his mission was consistent with the message of all preceding prophets who called their people to the oneness of Allah and the abandonment of idolatry.

translation: When he said to his people, 'Will you not fear Allah?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the role of a prophet as a caller to righteousness, emphasizing that the primary barrier preventing people from accepting the truth is their lack of God-consciousness, or taqwa; by questioning their state of fear, the speaker is inviting them to reflect on their accountability before the Creator, which serves as the essential foundation for reforming one's character and actions.

translation: Do you call upon Ba'l and forsake the best of creators?
interpretation: In this verse, the Prophet Elias (peace be upon him) reproaches his people for their polytheism, pointing out the illogical nature of abandoning the worship of Allah, the supreme Creator who brought everything into existence, to instead worship an inanimate idol named Ba'l which has no power to create, benefit, or harm, thereby highlighting the utter absurdity of shirk (associating partners with Allah).

translation: Allah is your Lord and the Lord of your first forefathers.
interpretation: This verse establishes the universality of Allah’s Lordship across all generations, reminding the polytheists that the same God who sustains them today is the same God who sustained their ancestors, thereby invalidating any claim that their ancestral customs or idols hold any divine authority over their current lives.

translation: But they denied him, so indeed, they will be brought forward [for punishment].
interpretation: The verse conveys that because the people rejected their messenger and refused to believe in the truth he brought, they have inevitably sealed their fate; they will be seized and compelled to appear before Allah on the Day of Judgment to face the consequences of their disbelief and account for their stubborn opposition to the divine message.

translation: Except the chosen servants of Allah.
interpretation: This verse signifies that those who have been purified and chosen by Allah through their sincere devotion and firm faith remain protected from the influence of Satan and the path of disbelief, as their hearts are entirely dedicated to the obedience of their Creator, rendering them immune to the temptations that lead others astray.

translation: And We left for him [favorable mention] among the later generations.
interpretation: God granted the prophets, such as Abraham or Noah, a lasting legacy of praise, honor, and righteous remembrance that continues to circulate among the nations that come after them, ensuring that their message and virtuous character remain an inspiration for believers throughout history.

translation: Peace be upon Elias.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine salutation of peace bestowed upon the Prophet Elias (Ilyas), confirming his high status, his steadfastness in faith, and the protection he enjoys from Allah as a reward for his unwavering commitment to his prophetic mission and his struggle against polytheism.

translation: Indeed, thus We reward the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse signifies that God’s standard of justice and grace is consistent, ensuring that those who perform acts of righteousness, sincerity, and excellence—both in their worship of God and their treatment of His creation—will inevitably receive a divine recompense that reflects His appreciation of their virtue, confirming that goodness is never lost or unrewarded by the Creator.

translation: Indeed, he is among Our believing servants.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the individual being mentioned has attained the highest status of faith through their sincere submission, steadfast devotion, and total reliance on God, marking them as one of the chosen elite who are distinguished by their profound spiritual closeness to the Divine.

translation: And indeed, Lot was among the messengers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine affirmation of Lot's status as a chosen prophet, highlighting that his mission was not an isolated event but part of the continuous, sacred chain of messengers sent by God to call humanity toward monotheism and moral righteousness, thereby validating his authority and the truth of his message to his people.

translation: When We saved him and his family, all of them.
interpretation: This refers to the divine rescue of Prophet Lut (Lot) and his righteous family from the impending destruction of their people, signaling that the protection of God encompasses those who remain steadfast in faith even when surrounded by widespread corruption and disbelief.

translation: Except an old woman among those who remained behind.
interpretation: This verse refers to the wife of Prophet Lot, who did not accompany the believers when they were commanded to leave the city of Sodom before its destruction; instead, she chose to remain behind with the transgressors who denied the truth, thereby sharing in their ruin due to her betrayal and disobedience to the messenger.

translation: Then We destroyed the others.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine warning, illustrating that the destruction of previous disbelieving nations was not an isolated incident but a recurring pattern of justice; it signifies that those who persist in arrogance and rejection of the truth after clear signs have been provided will inevitably face the same consequence of divine annihilation, confirming that God's law regarding the overthrow of the corrupt is absolute and unchanging throughout history.

translation: And indeed, you pass by them in the morning.
interpretation: The verse serves as a stern reminder to the people of Mecca as they travel on their trade routes, passing by the desolate, ruined dwellings of past civilizations that were destroyed for their disbelief. Allah highlights that these remnants are visible signs—observed at dawn—intended to provoke reflection on the inevitable consequences of rejecting divine guidance and to serve as a cautionary lesson for those currently persisting in arrogance.

translation: And by the night; will you not then use your reason?
interpretation: The verse invites the human intellect to contemplate the phenomena of the night, such as the darkness that brings rest, the movement of the celestial bodies, and the alternation of light and shadow, as clear signs of an All-Knowing Creator, suggesting that a mind capable of reflecting on these orderly natural systems should inevitably recognize the existence and majesty of Allah.

translation: And indeed, Yunus was among the messengers.
interpretation: This statement serves to affirm the prophethood of Yunus (Jonah) and his elevated status among those chosen by Allah to convey His message, emphasizing that his mission was an essential part of the chain of divine guidance sent to mankind, regardless of the trials he faced.

translation: When he fled to the laden ship.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Prophet Yunus (Jonah), peace be upon him, at the moment he departed from his people in a state of anger, choosing to board a fully loaded ship. The 'fleeing' described signifies his unauthorized departure from the land where he was commanded to stay and convey the message of Allah, leading him to face the trial of the sea and the subsequent swallowing by the whale as a consequence of his hasty decision before waiting for divine permission.

translation: So he cast lots, and he was among those who were losers.
