interpretation: God highlights the immense favor and divine responsibility bestowed upon the Children of Israel, noting that by granting them revealed guidance, wisdom in discernment, and a lineage of prophets, He elevated their status among contemporary nations to serve as a testimony of His bounty; this preference was not an unconditional endowment but a charge to uphold righteousness, illustrating that true superiority in the sight of God is measured by adherence to His revelation and the gratitude shown for His provisions.

translation: And We gave them clear proofs of the matter; yet they did not differ until after knowledge had come to them, out of envy among themselves. Indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ.
interpretation: The verse indicates that the division and disagreement among the people did not arise from a lack of guidance or hidden truth, but rather from the corruption of the soul and the presence of malice. Despite being provided with clear evidence and divine knowledge, they chose to dissent against the truth deliberately, driven by worldly jealousy and the desire to oppress one another. This highlights that human conflict often stems from personal agendas and arrogance rather than genuine confusion, and it reassures the believers that ultimate justice and the resolution of all disputes belong solely to God, who will reveal the truth and settle all accounts on the Day of Judgment.

translation: Then We put you, [O Muhammad], on an ordained way concerning the matter [of religion]; so follow it and do not follow the inclinations of those who do not know.
interpretation: God established a clear and divine path of laws and religious guidance for the Prophet Muhammad, commanding him to adhere strictly to this revealed truth and to remain steadfast against the influence, desires, and irrational opinions of those who lack knowledge of God’s revelation and divine wisdom.

translation: Indeed, they will not avail you at all against Allah. And indeed, the wrongdoers are allies of one another, but Allah is the ally of the righteous.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine assurance to the Prophet and the believers that worldly alliances, wealth, or power held by those who transgress against God are entirely futile and cannot offer any protection or intercession when faced with the judgment of the Almighty. It highlights a clear distinction between the base loyalty found among those who persist in injustice—who rely on each other to further their worldly desires—and the noble guardianship of Allah, who exclusively protects and guides those who maintain piety and consciousness of Him.

translation: This is a source of insight for mankind, and a guidance and a mercy for a people who are certain in faith.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an serves as a clear proof and intellectual enlightenment that allows human beings to discern between truth and falsehood, acting as a divine light that leads those who possess firm, unwavering conviction toward spiritual salvation and the encompassing grace of God.

translation: Or do those who commit evil deeds think We will make them like those who have believed and done righteous deeds - [make them] equal in their living and their dying? Evil is what they judge.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute impossibility of moral equivalence in the divine court. It asserts that God’s justice dictates a fundamental distinction between the righteous and the wicked, both in their worldly experiences—where the believer finds peace and guidance even in hardship—and in their transition into the afterlife, where the believer is granted divine grace and eternal reward, while the transgressor faces the consequences of their deeds. The verse concludes that any assumption suggesting both groups will share the same fate is a deeply flawed and illogical judgment.

translation: And Allah created the heavens and the earth in truth and so that every soul may be recompensed for what it has earned, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: The creation of the universe is not a chaotic or purposeless event; rather, it is founded upon ultimate divine justice and wisdom. Allah has structured existence as a grand stage where human actions possess real consequences, ensuring that on the Day of Judgment, every individual will be held accountable and rewarded or punished with absolute precision, devoid of any injustice, partiality, or loss of merit.

translation: Have you seen him who takes as his god his own desire, and Allah has sent him astray due to knowledge and has set a seal upon his hearing and his heart and put over his vision a veil? So who will guide him after Allah? Then will you not be reminded?
interpretation: This verse warns against the spiritual corruption of those who prioritize their own whims and personal desires over the guidance of Allah, effectively making their own passions the object of their worship. When a person willfully persists in following their desires despite knowing the truth, Allah leaves them to wander in their own confusion, sealing their senses so that they can no longer perceive the guidance or truth that would lead to their salvation.

translation: And they say, 'There is not but our worldly life; we die and live, and nothing destroys us except time.' And they have of that no knowledge; they are only assuming.
interpretation: This verse highlights the denial of the afterlife by the polytheists and materialists who believe that existence is confined to the worldly life. They attribute the cycle of life and death to the passage of time or natural laws rather than to a Creator who initiates life and causes death. The Qur'an rejects this belief as a groundless conjecture, emphasizing that their claim lacks any scientific or spiritual foundation and is merely a product of their own baseless assumptions and superficial observation.

translation: And when Our verses are recited to them as clear evidences, their argument is nothing except that they say, 'Bring back our forefathers, if you should be truthful.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the obstinate nature of those who reject the truth; when confronted with clear, divine proofs of the afterlife and resurrection, they do not engage with the evidence provided. Instead, they respond with unreasonable demands and mockery, essentially challenging the power of God to reverse death, revealing that their rejection is rooted in arrogance and a refusal to submit rather than a genuine lack of intellectual conviction.

translation: Say, 'It is Allah who gives you life, then causes you to die; then He will assemble you for the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt, but most of the people do not know.'
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty of Allah over the cycle of human existence, asserting that life and death are entirely under His divine command. By reminding humanity of the certainty of the Day of Resurrection, it highlights that human ignorance or denial of the afterlife does not invalidate the immutable truth of accountability, which remains an inevitable destiny decreed by the Creator.

translation: And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. And the day the Hour appears - that Day the falsifiers will lose.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the absolute sovereignty over all existence belongs solely to Allah, underscoring that any human claim to power or autonomy is transient and deceptive. The mention of the 'falsifiers' refers to those who denied the truth, relied on vanity, or propagated falsehoods during their worldly lives; on the Day of Judgment, their efforts will be revealed as hollow, leading to their ultimate spiritual bankruptcy and loss when they encounter the reality they once chose to ignore.

translation: And you will see every nation kneeling; every nation will be called to its record [and told], 'Today you will be recompensed for what you used to do.'
interpretation: On the Day of Resurrection, all communities will be seen humbled and kneeling in anticipation of the divine judgment, acknowledging their absolute helplessness before Allah. Each nation will be presented with the comprehensive record of their deeds, testifying to their earthly conduct, and they will be reminded that this final judgment is the inevitable outcome of their past choices, ensuring that every soul is requited according to its actions without injustice.

translation: This is Our record which speaks about you in truth. Indeed, We were recording what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse signifies that on the Day of Resurrection, God will present a comprehensive and precise record of every human being's deeds, gathered and preserved by the recording angels throughout their earthly lives. This account serves as an undeniable and truthful testimony, leaving no room for denial or justification, as it perfectly captures all actions, intentions, and behaviors that were previously concealed or forgotten, thereby justifying the divine judgment that follows.

translation: As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, their Lord will admit them into His mercy. That is the clear triumph.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the ultimate success and the highest achievement for a believer is not merely the attainment of worldly comfort, but the entry into the expansive and encompassing mercy of Allah, which denotes being granted Paradise and eternal contentment, marking a victory that is manifest and undeniable because it secures the soul's salvation and proximity to the Creator forever.

translation: But as for those who disbelieved, [it will be said], 'Were not My verses recited to you? But you were arrogant and were a people of criminals.'
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, the disbelievers will be confronted with the reality of their rejection; they will be reminded that God's signs and proofs were clearly presented to them through His messengers and scriptures, yet they chose to reject the truth out of pride and arrogance, persisting in their state of disbelief and transgression until they met their end.

translation: And when it was said, 'Indeed, the promise of Allah is truth and the Hour [is coming] - no doubt about it,' you said, 'We know not what is the Hour. We assume only assumption, and we are not convinced.'
interpretation: This verse exposes the intellectual dishonesty and stubborn arrogance of the disbelievers who, despite being presented with clear evidence regarding the reality of resurrection and the afterlife, choose to mask their rejection behind an affectation of uncertainty and skeptical doubt, thereby attempting to dismiss the accountability of the Hereafter under the pretense that they lack sufficient knowledge to be certain of its occurrence.

translation: And the evil consequences of what they did will appear to them, and they will be enveloped by that which they used to ridicule.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, the true nature of their sinful deeds—which they previously justified or ignored in worldly life—will become starkly apparent to the disbelievers. This realization will manifest as a tangible punishment, proving that the divine warnings and the afterlife they once mocked were not mere myths, but absolute truths that have now surrounded them from every direction, leaving them no escape from the mockery they once directed toward the truth.

translation: And it will be said, 'Today We will forget you, just as you forgot the meeting of this Day of yours, and your refuge is the Fire, and for you there are no helpers.'
interpretation: This verse signifies that God will deal with the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment as if He has forgotten them, mirroring how they ignored and neglected the reality of this inevitable meeting during their worldly lives; thus, He will leave them to their fate in the Fire, stripping them of any mercy, recognition, or assistance, which serves as a divine justice commensurate with their intentional disregard for the afterlife.

translation: That is because you took the verses of Allah in mockery, and the worldly life deluded you. So this day they will not be brought out from it, nor will they be asked to repent.
interpretation: The verse explains that the permanent torment and exclusion from mercy are the direct consequences of the human choice to treat divine guidance with arrogance and ridicule, while allowing the fleeting pleasures of worldly existence to create a false sense of security that blinds the soul to the reality of the afterlife. It signifies that the time for correction and opportunity for turning back to God has concluded, leaving the disbelievers in a state of eternal stagnation where no further excuses or efforts at reconciliation will be accepted.

translation: So all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth, Lord of all the worlds.
interpretation: This verse establishes that all forms of praise, gratitude, and perfection belong exclusively to Allah, who is the creator, sustainer, and absolute sovereign of everything in the physical heavens, the earth, and all existence beyond human perception, thereby grounding the believer's worship in the recognition of His comprehensive lordship over every realm of reality.

translation: And to Him belongs all majesty within the heavens and the earth, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true greatness, supreme power, and absolute authority reside solely with Allah, as He is the Creator and Sustainer of the entire universe, and all beings are subordinate to His divine will and wisdom in all His decrees.

translation: Ha-Mim.
interpretation: These are abbreviated letters (al-huruf al-muqatta'at) whose precise meaning is known only to Allah, though many scholars suggest they serve as a challenge to the eloquence of the Arabs, signifying that the Qur'an is composed of the same letters they use, yet they are unable to produce anything comparable to it.

translation: The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse serves as a formal declaration of the divine origin of the Quran, emphasizing that it descends directly from Allah, who combines absolute power that executes His will without opposition and perfect wisdom that places everything in its proper place, thereby affirming that the guidance contained within the Book is infallible and beyond human imitation.

translation: We did not create the heavens and the earth and that which is between them except in truth and for a specified term. But those who disbelieve, from that of which they are warned, are turning away.
interpretation: The creation of this vast universe is not a frivolous or purposeless act; rather, it is established upon absolute truth, wisdom, and justice, designed to lead to a calculated end at an appointed time. The warning given to the disbelievers is rooted in this ultimate reality, yet they remain heedless and willfully ignore the clear signs and warnings presented to them, choosing to turn away from the truth that holds the key to their final destiny.

translation: Say, 'Have you considered those you invoke besides Allah? Show me what they have created from the earth, or do they have partnership in the heavens? Bring me a scripture before this, or some remnant of knowledge, if you should be truthful.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a rational challenge to the polytheists, compelling them to present empirical evidence for the divinity of their idols. By demanding proof of any creative act performed by their deities regarding the earth, or any evidence of their shared authority over the celestial realms, Allah dismantles the foundation of their polytheism. The verse further emphasizes that true guidance must be supported by revealed scriptures or established, verifiable knowledge transmitted from earlier traditions, thereby exposing their religious practices as being based purely on conjecture and ancestral imitation rather than divine truth or objective reality.

translation: And who is more astray than he who calls upon instead of Allah those who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, and they, of their invocation, are unaware.
interpretation: This verse highlights the extreme folly and spiritual blindness of those who worship idols, statues, or created beings, as these entities lack the capacity to hear, understand, or answer the supplications directed toward them. The verse emphasizes that these false objects of worship are not only unable to fulfill any request but are entirely unconscious of the prayers of those who seek them, marking a state of profound delusion for the idolater who wastes their devotion on entities that offer nothing in return and remain indifferent to their plight.

translation: And when the people are gathered, they will be enemies to them, and they will be deniers of their worship.
interpretation: This verse describes the state of idols and false deities on the Day of Resurrection, asserting that those things which were worshipped besides God will disavow their followers and express enmity toward them, rejecting the claim that they ever accepted or sanctioned the worship offered to them by those individuals.

translation: And when Our verses are recited to them as clear evidences, those who disbelieve say of the truth when it has come to them, This is obvious magic.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubborn arrogance of the disbelievers who, despite seeing the manifest truth and the undeniable light of divine revelation, choose to dismiss it as mere sorcery. Their rejection is not based on a lack of understanding or evidence, but rather on a deep-seated resistance to truth, leading them to mischaracterize the miracle of the Qur'an as deception to maintain their own disbelief and justify their deviation from the right path.

translation: Or do they say, 'He has invented it'? Say, 'If I have invented it, then you have no power to protect me from Allah. He is most knowing of what you discuss. Sufficient is He as Witness between me and you, and He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.'
interpretation: The verse serves as a declaration of the Prophet's sincerity, asserting that he would not dare fabricate lies against Allah, as he alone would bear the devastating consequences of such a transgression without any possibility of intercession from his critics. By invoking Allah as the ultimate Witness, the verse shifts the burden of judgment away from the skeptics and reminds them that while their malicious discourse is fully documented by the Almighty, the door to divine mercy remains open for those who choose to seek it.

translation: Say, 'I am not something original among the messengers, nor do I know what will be done with me or with you. I only follow that which is revealed to me, and I am not but a clear warner.'
interpretation: The Prophet Muhammad is commanded to clarify that his mission is not an unprecedented event in human history, as other messengers have come before him with similar guidance. Regarding the concern of destiny, he acknowledges that he possesses no hidden knowledge of his own personal fate or the specific outcomes for his people in the afterlife, as such matters reside solely with Allah. This verse emphasizes the Prophet's role as a humble messenger whose authority is derived strictly from divine revelation, rather than personal claim to knowledge of the unseen, establishing that his purpose is to deliver a transparent warning to humanity.

translation: Say, 'Have you considered: if it is from Allah and you have disbelieved in it while a witness from the Children of Israel has testified to the like of it and believed, while you were arrogant?' Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: The verse serves as a powerful rhetorical challenge to the disbelievers of Quraysh, highlighting the inconsistency of their rejection by pointing to an objective, scholarly witness. It signifies that the truth of the Prophet Muhammad's message was corroborated by the scriptures and traditions held by the learned among the Children of Israel, who recognized in the Qur'an the same divine origin as their own revelations. By dismissing this scholarly testimony and choosing pride over intellectual integrity, the disbelievers condemned themselves to spiritual blindness, as Allah withholds His guidance from those who willfully choose arrogance and injustice over the clear evidence of the truth.

translation: And those who disbelieved said to those who believed, 'If it were good, they would not have reached it before us.' And since they are not guided by it, they will say, 'This is an ancient falsehood.'
interpretation: This verse exposes the arrogant logic of the disbelievers who equate worldly status or priority in receiving a message with divine truth, falsely assuming that if the Qur'an were truly beneficial, they—as the self-proclaimed elite—would have been the first to embrace it; because they refuse to accept the guidance offered to them, they resort to the dismissive tactic of labeling the eternal message as outdated myths or archaic fabrications to justify their own stubborn rejection.

translation: And before it was the Book of Moses as a guide and a mercy. And this is a Book confirming [it] in an Arabic tongue to warn those who have done wrong and as good tidings to the doers of good.
interpretation: The verse clarifies that the Qur'an serves as a divine confirmation and a linguistic completion to the previous revelations given to Moses. By being revealed in Arabic, it bridges the gap between the historical legacy of the Torah and the final message for humanity, establishing a standard of accountability for the unjust and providing a promise of divine grace and reward for those who uphold righteousness in their faith and actions.

translation: Indeed, those who have said, 'Our Lord is Allah,' and then remained on a right course - there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse signifies that those who sincerely affirm the oneness of Allah and maintain steadfastness in their faith and righteous conduct throughout their lives are granted divine tranquility and protection, ensuring that they will experience no apprehension regarding their future in the afterlife nor sorrow for what they have left behind in the worldly life.

translation: Those are the companions of Paradise, abiding eternally therein as a reward for what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse establishes the divine justice of Allah by affirming that entering Paradise and attaining eternal life within it is not a matter of arbitrary selection, but a direct consequence and recompense for the righteous deeds, sincere faith, and steadfastness in obedience that the believers performed during their worldly life.

translation: And We have enjoined upon man, toward his parents, good treatment. His mother carried him with hardship and gave birth to him with hardship, and his gestation and weaning period is thirty months. [He grows] until, when he reaches his maturity and reaches [the age of] forty years, he says, 'My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents and to work righteousness of which You will approve and make righteous for me my offspring. Indeed, I have repented to You, and indeed, I am of the Muslims.'
interpretation: This verse establishes that the peak of human maturity and intellectual clarity is reached at the age of forty, serving as a critical threshold where one should earnestly seek Allah's guidance to express gratitude for His blessings, commit to virtuous deeds that please Him, and ensure the righteousness of their descendants, as this milestone represents the transition into full moral accountability and the time to solidify one's devotion and submission to the Divine path.

translation: Those are the ones from whom We will accept the best of what they did and overlook their misdeeds, among the companions of Paradise - a promise of truth which they had been promised.
interpretation: This verse signifies that Allah, in His boundless mercy, evaluates the believers based on their most virtuous deeds while forgiving their shortcomings, ensuring their inclusion among the inhabitants of Paradise as a fulfillment of the truthful promise He made to His righteous servants.

translation: But the one who says to his parents, 'Uff to you! Do you promise me that I will be brought forth when generations have already passed away before me?' while they call upon Allah for help [saying], 'Woe to you! Believe! Indeed, the promise of Allah is truth,' but he says, 'This is not but legends of the former people.'
interpretation: This verse portrays a soul blinded by arrogance and disbelief, characterized by its utter disrespect for the foundations of life and guidance—the parents—and its rejection of the hereafter. The individual's insolence manifests as a denial of the afterlife by dismissing it as a mere collection of ancient myths, reflecting a heart so deeply entrenched in materialism that it refuses to heed the warnings of the truth, despite the desperate pleas of those who care most for its ultimate salvation.

translation: Those are the ones upon whom the word has come into effect, among nations which had passed on before them of jinn and mankind. Indeed, they were the losers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning that those who persist in disbelief and rejection of the truth will meet the same fate as the misguided nations of jinn and humans that preceded them, as God's decree of punishment has been irrevocably established for those who choose to squander their own souls by turning away from divine guidance, ultimately rendering them the true losers who have forfeited both their earthly potential and their eternal reward.

translation: And for all are degrees from what they have done, and that He may fully compensate them for their deeds, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: The verse indicates that human beings will be assigned varying ranks in the Hereafter, which are not determined by chance or favoritism but are direct consequences of their own earthly actions. Allah emphasizes divine justice, asserting that every individual will receive the precise recompense they have earned, ensuring that no good deed goes unrewarded and no soul is burdened with a punishment it did not deserve, thereby affirming the absolute fairness of the Creator in His judgment.

translation: And the Day those who disbelieved are exposed to the Fire [it will be said], 'You exhausted your pleasures during your worldly life and enjoyed them, so this Day you will be awarded the punishment of [extreme] humiliation for what you used to be arrogant upon the earth without right and for what you used to defiantly disobey.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern reprimand to the disbelievers who prioritized the transient luxuries and hedonistic pleasures of this world over their spiritual duties, effectively 'consuming' their share of goodness in this life rather than preparing for the hereafter; consequently, their punishment of humiliation is a direct, ironic recompense for their worldly pride, where they falsely elevated themselves above others and disregarded divine truth through their continuous transgression.

translation: And mention the brother of 'Aad, when he warned his people in the curved sand-hills - and warners had already passed on before him and after him - saying, 'Do not worship except Allah. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a terrible Day.'
interpretation: This verse recounts the mission of the Prophet Hud, who was sent to the people of 'Aad. The mention of 'his brother' serves to highlight his close kinship and common lineage with them, emphasizing that his call was out of genuine compassion and concern for their welfare rather than a desire for power or personal gain. By reminding them of the prophets who preceded him and those who followed, he points to a consistent message of monotheism that has been the cornerstone of divine guidance throughout history. His warning is a reflection of a sincere heart seeking to shield his own people from the inevitable consequences of their arrogance and defiance against their Creator, underscoring the gravity of rejecting the truth when it is clearly presented.

translation: They said, 'Have you come to us to turn us away from our gods? Then bring us what you promise us, if you should be of the truthful.'
interpretation: The disbelievers, gripped by their blind adherence to ancestral traditions and arrogance, challenged the messenger by mockingly demanding that he hasten the divine punishment he had warned them of, revealing their disbelief in his message and their stubborn refusal to abandon their idol worship despite the clear signs he presented.

translation: He said, 'The knowledge is only with Allah, and I convey to you that with which I was sent, but I see you are a people behaving ignorantly.'
interpretation: The Prophet Hud here redirects the focus of his people from demanding signs or knowledge of the unseen—which belongs solely to Allah—to the core of his mission, which is the message of Tawhid. By accusing them of ignorance, he is emphasizing that their stubbornness, arrogance, and lack of spiritual insight into the obvious signs of creation constitute a profound moral and intellectual deficiency, rather than a mere lack of information.

translation: And when they saw it as a cloud approaching their valleys, they said, 'This is a cloud bringing us rain!' Rather, it is that which you were impatient for - a wind, within it a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse illustrates the irony of human perception when faced with divine warning; those who had persistently demanded that the punishment be hastened upon them were blinded by their own materialistic expectations, interpreting the very instrument of their destruction—a dark, approaching storm—as a sign of mercy and life-giving rain, only to realize too late that the phenomenon was the fulfillment of their own defiant challenges.

translation: Destroying everything by the command of its Lord, so that they became such that nothing could be seen except their dwellings. Thus do We recompense the criminal people.
interpretation: The verse illustrates the absolute nature of divine retribution when it descends upon a people who have persisted in disbelief and arrogance; the destruction is so total and final that their civilizations, once bustling with life, are reduced to mere silent ruins, serving as a bleak testament to the futility of rebelling against the Creator's decree.

translation: And We had certainly established them in such as We have not established you, and We endowed them with hearing, and sight, and hearts; but their hearing, and their sight, and their hearts availed them nothing at all, for they were denying the signs of Allah, and they were enveloped by what they used to ridicule.
interpretation: The verse serves as a profound warning to humanity that material prosperity, technological advancement, and sensory faculties are not signs of divine favor in and of themselves. It illustrates that when a civilization rejects the truth and mocks the signs of God, their physical and mental capacities—which were intended to lead them to faith—become liabilities rather than assets. Because they chose to ignore the clear evidence of Allah's sovereignty, their faculties of perception failed to guide them toward salvation, ultimately leaving them defenseless against the very consequences they had once treated with arrogant mockery.

translation: And We have already destroyed what surrounds you of cities, and We have diversified the signs so that they might return.
interpretation: The verse serves as a stern admonition to the disbelievers of Mecca, highlighting that the physical ruins of previous civilizations—which were destroyed due to their persistence in disbelief—stand as clear, observable evidence that divine retribution is an inevitable consequence of rejecting the truth; by presenting these warnings in various forms, God aims to stir the conscience and intellect of the people so that they may abandon their falsehood and repent before they meet a similar fate.

translation: Then why did those whom they took besides Allah as deities to bring them closer to Him not help them? But they vanished from them; and that was their falsehood and what they were fabricating.
interpretation: This verse serves as a rebuke to the polytheists who worshipped idols under the false pretense that these images would act as intermediaries or drawing-closer agents to God. The Quran exposes the futility of this belief by pointing out that when these individuals faced reality or divine reckoning, their supposed deities failed to provide any assistance, proving that the entities they worshipped were mere fabrications with no actual power, and their reliance on them was a deceptive lie that led them further into delusion.

translation: And when We directed toward you a few of the jinn, listening to the Qur'an. And when they attended it, they said, 'Listen quietly.' And when it was concluded, they went back to their people as warners.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the transformative power of the Qur'an, showing that its divine guidance is not limited to humans but also encompasses the jinn. When these jinn encountered the recitation, they recognized its profound authority, which compelled them to observe respectful silence and subsequently take on the responsibility of conveying this message of warning and guidance to their own kin, signifying the universal nature of the revelation.

translation: They said, 'O our people, indeed we have heard a Book revealed after Moses, confirming what was before it which guides to the truth and to a straight path.'
interpretation: The Jinn acknowledge that the Qur'an is a divine revelation that aligns with the fundamental truths found in the Torah, emphasizing that its primary purpose is to provide clear guidance toward the objective truth and a direct, unswerving path of righteousness that leads to God.

translation: O our people, respond to the Caller of Allah and believe in Him; He will forgive you of your sins and protect you from a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse represents the call of the believing Jinn to their own kin, urging them to embrace the message of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) by accepting the invitation to monotheism. The promise of forgiveness for their sins and salvation from a severe punishment serves as an encouragement, emphasizing that sincere faith and obedience to Allah's messenger are the only paths to spiritual protection and eternal security.

translation: And whoever does not respond to the Caller of Allah will not escape upon the earth, and he will have no protectors besides Him. Those are in clear error.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that evading the call to truth is a futile act, as no human has the power to escape the ultimate authority and judgment of Allah, nor can anyone find refuge or intercessors to shield them from His divine decree, leaving those who persist in turning away in a state of manifest and profound deviation from the path of salvation.

translation: Have they not seen that Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and was not wearied by their creation, is able to give life to the dead? Yes, indeed, He is over all things competent.
interpretation: The verse employs a rational argument by analogy to address those who doubt the resurrection of the dead. By highlighting the creation of the vast, complex heavens and earth, Allah demonstrates that the power required to initiate existence from nothing is infinitely greater than the power required to restore life after death. Since God was not exhausted or overwhelmed by the immense task of bringing the entire universe into being, He is logically and inherently capable of resurrecting human beings, proving that His omnipotence is absolute and beyond human limitations.

translation: And on the Day when those who disbelieved will be exposed to the Fire, [it will be said], 'Is this not the truth?' They will say, 'Yes, by our Lord.' He will say, 'Then taste the punishment because you used to disbelieve.'
interpretation: This verse depicts the moment of ultimate realization for the disbelievers when the reality of the afterlife, which they denied in their worldly life, is presented before them as an inescapable fact. Their forced admission of the truth serves as a final witness against their own souls, confirming that the suffering they are about to experience is not an arbitrary act of cruelty, but a direct and logical consequence of their deliberate rejection of divine guidance and the truth during their time on earth.

translation: So be patient, [O Muhammad], as were those of determination among the messengers and do not be impatient for them. It will be—on the day they see what they are promised—as though they had not remained [in the world] except an hour of a day. [This is] notification. And will [any] be destroyed except the defiantly disobedient people?
interpretation: The verse commands the Prophet to mirror the steadfast endurance of the most resolute messengers who faced intense rejection and hardship without faltering. It serves as a reminder that the timeline of worldly life, no matter how long it feels or how persistent the defiance of the disbelievers may be, is insignificant when measured against the eternity of the Hereafter. By stating that the disbelievers will view their entire earthly existence as a mere hour upon facing their fate, the Quran emphasizes that justice is inevitable and that the ultimate destruction awaiting the wicked is a consequence of their own persistent rebellion against divine guidance.

translation: Those who disbelieve and avert from the way of Allah - He will waste their deeds.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the spiritual efficacy and ultimate reward of any worldly actions performed by disbelievers are nullified in the sight of God; because they actively reject the truth and hinder others from following the path of guidance, their efforts—regardless of how seemingly virtuous or productive they may appear in a worldly context—lack the foundation of faith necessary to be accepted, ultimately leaving them without any merit or spiritual gain in the hereafter.

translation: But those who believe, do righteous deeds, and believe in what has been sent down upon Muhammad—and it is the truth from their Lord—He will remove from them their misdeeds and improve their state of mind.
interpretation: The verse highlights the transformative power of divine guidance, suggesting that when a person fully embraces the truth revealed to Prophet Muhammad with sincere faith and righteous conduct, God facilitates an inner purification that erases past transgressions and brings harmony, peace, and rectitude to their heart and affairs.

translation: That is because those who disbelieved followed falsehood, while those who believed followed the truth from their Lord. Thus does Allah present to the people their comparisons.
interpretation: The verse explains that the fundamental divergence between the two groups—the disbelievers and the believers—stems from their choice of allegiance: one group adheres to falsehood, which has no foundation or endurance, while the other adheres to the truth revealed by their Lord, which is stable and eternal. Through these contrasting examples, Allah demonstrates the state and destiny of each group, clarifying that the spiritual path one chooses determines their final outcome in both this life and the hereafter.

translation: So when you meet those who disbelieve [in battle], strike [their] necks until, when you have inflicted slaughter upon them, then secure their bonds, and either confer favor afterwards or ransom [them] until the war lays down its burdens. That [is the command]. And if Allah had willed, He could have taken vengeance upon them [Himself], but [He ordered armed struggle] to test some of you by means of others. And those who are killed in the cause of Allah - never will He waste their deeds.
interpretation: This verse establishes the rules of engagement during active warfare, emphasizing that the command to strike the enemy is specifically within the context of combat to achieve victory and weaken their power, after which the focus shifts to containment and mercy through either unconditional release or ransom, reflecting that the purpose of such struggle is not mere killing but a divine test of human character, endurance, and justice in the face of conflict.

translation: He will guide them and set their affairs in order.
interpretation: This verse signifies that Allah will lead the believers to the paths of goodness and truth, while simultaneously rectifying their internal states and external conditions, ensuring that their hearts are tranquil and their worldly and otherworldly affairs are settled in the best possible manner.

translation: And He will admit them into Paradise, which He has made known to them.
interpretation: This verse signifies that Allah will grant the believers an intuitive and divine guidance that leads them directly to their specific dwellings and honors within Paradise as if they had known them beforehand, ensuring they experience a sense of familiarity, comfort, and immediate belonging upon their arrival.

translation: O you who have believed, if you support Allah, He will support you and plant firmly your feet.
interpretation: This verse establishes a reciprocal relationship between the believer and the Divine: when individuals dedicate their efforts, resources, and sincere intentions to upholding the message of truth and justice, they essentially advocate for the cause of God. In return, God provides them with spiritual aid, strength of heart, and unwavering resolve, ensuring that their moral and physical footing remains stable even amidst the tribulations and challenges of life.

translation: But as for those who disbelieve, for them is destruction, and He will lead their deeds to nothing.
interpretation: This verse signifies that those who reject the truth and persist in their disbelief will find their worldly efforts and intentions devoid of any spiritual weight or benefit in the afterlife, as their rejection of the divine path renders their actions futile and lacking the foundational sincerity required for acceptance by God.

translation: That is because they disliked what Allah has revealed, so He rendered their deeds worthless.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the foundation of one's deeds being accepted by God is the sincerity of the heart and the acceptance of His guidance; therefore, whoever possesses hatred or rejection in their heart toward the revelation of Allah—whether it concerns the laws, the message of monotheism, or the prophetic guidance—effectively nullifies the value of their own actions, as their inward rebellion renders their outward works devoid of the spiritual merit necessary for salvation.

translation: Have they not traveled through the earth and observed how was the end of those before them? Allah destroyed them, and for the disbelievers is something similar.
interpretation: The verse serves as a historical and spiritual exhortation, urging those who deny the truth to contemplate the ruins of past civilizations that defied divine guidance. By observing the physical remains of nations that were destroyed due to their arrogance and disbelief, people are meant to realize that the laws governing moral decay and divine retribution are constant. The declaration that 'for the disbelievers is something similar' underscores that the patterns of history are cyclical; those who persist in the same patterns of corruption and denial as their predecessors will inevitably face the same ultimate ruin, as Allah's justice does not favor any group over another.

translation: That is because Allah is the protector of those who have believed and because the disbelievers have no protector.
interpretation: This verse establishes a fundamental spiritual reality: the believers are granted a special bond of support, guidance, and triumph through their connection with Allah, who serves as their guardian and advocate, whereas those who reject the truth are left to their own devices, devoid of divine assistance or any true defender to shield them from the ultimate consequences of their disbelief.

translation: Indeed, Allah will admit those who have believed and done righteous deeds to gardens beneath which rivers flow, but those who disbelieve enjoy themselves and eat as grazing livestock eat, and the Fire will be a residence for them.
interpretation: The verse draws a stark contrast between the ultimate end of the believers, whose lives are marked by purposeful righteousness and the reward of eternal bliss, and the disbelievers, whose existence is characterized by a mindless, materialistic pursuit of temporary worldly pleasures, likened to the instinctual consumption of livestock, leading them ultimately to a state of spiritual ruin and divine retribution.

translation: And how many a city which was stronger than your city which has driven you out have We destroyed, and there was no helper for them.
interpretation: This verse serves as a profound consolation to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and a warning to the disbelievers of Makkah; it highlights that the persecutors' worldly power and defiance against the truth are temporary, reminding them that historical empires far more formidable than theirs were utterly annihilated by God's decree when they rejected the truth, and that no human authority or alliance could offer them protection or salvation when divine retribution arrived.

translation: Is he who is upon a clear proof from his Lord like him to whom the evil of his deed has been made attractive while they follow their [own] desires?
interpretation: This verse presents a sharp contrast between two types of people: those who live their lives guided by the divine guidance and absolute truth revealed by God, and those who are blinded by their own whims, desires, and worldly passions. It illustrates that when a person follows their base inclinations, they begin to perceive their evil actions as righteous or beneficial, effectively shutting their hearts to the light of faith. The rhetorical question emphasizes that these two paths are fundamentally incompatible, as the person of insight walks in the light of certainty, while the person of desire wanders in the darkness of self-deception, unable to distinguish between truth and falsehood.

translation: The description of the Garden which the righteous have been promised is that therein are rivers of water incorruptible, rivers of milk of which the taste never changes, rivers of wine delicious to those who drink, and rivers of clarified honey; in it they will have every kind of fruit and forgiveness from their Lord. Is this like those who will abide forever in the Fire, and be given to drink boiling water that cuts up their bowels?
interpretation: The verse employs a vivid metaphorical contrast to illustrate the stark difference between the eternal bliss of the righteous and the harrowing punishment of the inhabitants of Hell, highlighting that true success lies in the pleasure of God and that the pleasures of Paradise are not only pure and everlasting but reflect a spiritual perfection that stands in complete, agonizing opposition to the destructive and relentless physical torment of those who have rejected divine guidance.

translation: And among them are those who listen to you, until when they depart from you, they say to those who were given knowledge, 'What has he said just now?' Those are the ones whom Allah has sealed their hearts and who follow their [own] desires.
interpretation: The verse describes the hypocrites who attend the Prophet's gatherings with hearts devoid of sincerity or intent to understand, acting out of mockery and arrogance; because they willfully turned away from the truth to indulge their base desires, Allah rendered their hearts incapable of perceiving or accepting divine guidance, leaving them lost in their own confusion and stubborn ignorance.

translation: And those who are guided - He increases them in guidance and gives them their righteousness.
interpretation: This verse signifies that faith is a dynamic and cumulative process; when a person genuinely seeks the truth and takes the initiative to follow divine guidance, God responds by fortifying their heart with further enlightenment and clear understanding. Simultaneously, God grants them the ability to act upon that guidance, bestowing upon them the state of piety and God-consciousness which acts as a protective shield against wrongdoing, thereby enabling them to fulfill their duties and ascend further in their spiritual journey.

translation: Are they waiting for anything except the Hour to come upon them suddenly? But its portents have already come. So how will they be reminded when it actually reaches them?
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning that the signs of the Day of Judgment have already manifested, yet people persist in their heedlessness, waiting for a surprise event that will leave no room for repentance or reflection once it arrives, as the time for learning from warnings expires the moment the reality of the end begins.

translation: So know, [O Muhammad], that there is no deity except Allah and ask forgiveness for your sin and for the believing men and believing women. And Allah knows of your movement and your resting place.
interpretation: This verse establishes the foundational duty of monotheism (Tawhid) as the prerequisite for all spiritual growth, directing the Prophet and his followers to ground their faith in the absolute oneness of God. By pairing the command to acknowledge God's unity with the command to seek forgiveness—both for oneself and for the collective community—the verse emphasizes that true realization of God's sovereignty must manifest in humility, repentance, and empathetic concern for others. It serves as a reminder that every action taken during one's active life and every moment of stillness is witnessed by the Divine, grounding the believer's moral accountability in the continuous presence of an All-Knowing Creator.

translation: And those who have believed say, 'Why has a Surah not been sent down?' But when a precise Surah is revealed and fighting is mentioned therein, you see those in whose hearts is disease looking at you with a look of one swooning unto death. And more appropriate for them is destruction.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the state of hypocrisy, wherein individuals profess faith but possess hearts weakened by doubt and cowardice. When the command for jihad or struggle in the path of truth is revealed, their fear of losing worldly safety or their lives reveals the instability of their faith. Their physical reaction—the look of one experiencing the throes of death—signifies the intense inner conflict and dread they feel when faced with the necessity of sacrifice, contrasting their outward claims of devotion with the reality of their compromised spiritual commitment.

translation: Obedience and good words. And when the matter is determined, if they had been true to Allah, it would have been better for them.
interpretation: This verse underscores that true faith is not merely a verbal claim but must be accompanied by active obedience and honorable conduct; it warns that when faced with decisive tests or the command for struggle, those who genuinely align their hearts with sincerity toward Allah will find that their commitment yields the greatest spiritual benefit, whereas inconsistency in times of resolution reveals a lack of integrity in their previous professions of faith.

translation: So would you perhaps, if you turned away, cause corruption on earth and sever your ties of kinship?
interpretation: This verse serves as a rhetorical reprimand directed at those who turn away from the path of Allah and the commands of His messenger, highlighting that abandoning divine guidance inevitably leads to moral decay and social disintegration; when people disregard the sacred bounds set by God, they naturally revert to the primitive behavior of the Age of Ignorance, prioritizing personal power and base desires over justice and communal harmony, which results in widespread corruption and the destruction of the natural bonds of family and society.

translation: Those are the ones whom Allah has cursed, so He deafened them and blinded their vision.
interpretation: This verse describes the spiritual consequence of persistently rejecting the truth and choosing corruption over guidance; by hardening their hearts against the message of God, these individuals lose the inner capacity to hear the call of righteousness or perceive the signs of divine truth, effectively blinding and deafening their souls to spiritual reality as a result of their own deliberate deviation.

translation: Do they not then reflect on the Qur'an, or are there locks upon their hearts?
interpretation: The verse serves as a profound rhetorical inquiry into the spiritual state of those who fail to engage deeply with the divine message; it suggests that the failure to contemplate the Qur'an is not merely an intellectual shortcoming, but a symptom of a spiritual obstruction—a metaphorical lock—that prevents the light of guidance from penetrating the heart and allowing the soul to perceive the truth.

translation: Indeed, those who reverted to disbelief after guidance had become clear to them, Satan enticed them and prolonged hope for them.
interpretation: This verse explains that the cause of apostasy after having recognized the truth is the psychological manipulation by Satan, who beautifies evil actions to the soul and distracts the individual with long-term worldly aspirations, causing them to neglect the inevitable reality of the afterlife and lose their firm grasp on the clarity of divine guidance.

translation: That is because they said to those who disliked what Allah has revealed, 'We will obey you in some matters,' and Allah knows their secrets.
interpretation: This verse reveals the duplicity of the hypocrites who secretly conspired with the disbelievers and opponents of the revelation. By promising to obey those who rejected Allah's message in certain matters, they attempted to appease the enemies of the faith while maintaining a facade of belief. The verse serves as a reminder that although these individuals believed their clandestine agreements were hidden from the Muslim community, Allah possesses absolute knowledge of their true intentions, hidden agendas, and secret alliances, and will hold them accountable for their betrayal.

translation: How will it be when the angels take their souls, striking their faces and their backs?
interpretation: This verse describes the severe state of the disbelievers at the moment of their death, where the angels of punishment approach them with harshness and violence, striking their faces and their backs as a form of painful retribution for their disbelief, reflecting the transition from their earthly rebellion to the commencement of their divine judgment.

translation: That is because they followed what angers Allah and disliked His pleasure, so He rendered their deeds worthless.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the corruption of one's inner state and the deliberate choice to pursue sinful actions that contradict the divine will inevitably lead to the nullification of all spiritual efforts, as these individuals prioritize their own misguided desires over the pursuit of Allah's approval, thereby disqualifying themselves from any reward.

translation: Or do those in whose hearts is a disease think that Allah will not expose their grudges?
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to the hypocrites who conceal animosity and hatred against the believers in their hearts; it emphasizes that they are deeply mistaken if they believe their true intentions are hidden from Allah, for He will inevitably expose their inner malice and reveal their true characters through trials and life events that bring their secrets to light.

translation: And if We willed, We could show them to you, and you would know them by their marks; but you will surely know them by the tone of their speech. And Allah knows your deeds.
interpretation: This verse indicates that although Allah possesses the power to explicitly reveal the identities of the hypocrites to the Prophet Muhammad through visual physical signs, He chose instead to reveal them through the subtle linguistic cues and the underlying hostile or insincere tone in their discourse, serving as a test for the believers to exercise discernment and wisdom in recognizing the true nature of those who oppose the faith.

translation: And We will surely test you until We make evident those who strive among you [for the cause of Allah] and the patient, and We will test your affairs.
interpretation: The verse indicates that Allah subjects human beings to trials and tribulations not to acquire new knowledge of their nature, as He already possesses perfect knowledge of all things, but to manifest their hidden qualities in the tangible world, thereby establishing evidence of their sincerity and endurance for the sake of His reward and judgment.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and avert others from the way of Allah and oppose the Messenger after guidance has become clear to them – they will never harm Allah at all, and He will render their deeds worthless.
interpretation: This verse warns those who knowingly reject the truth and actively work to hinder others from following the divine path that their rebellion is ultimately futile; because their hostility cannot diminish Allah's sovereignty, He nullifies the value of any outwardly good deeds they might perform, as their underlying rejection of faith strips those actions of any spiritual benefit or divine reward.

translation: O you who have believed, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and do not invalidate your deeds.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine command for believers to maintain the integrity of their worship and righteous actions; it cautions against acts of disobedience, showing off (riya'), or falling back into disbelief, as these behaviors strip one's good deeds of their spiritual value and merit in the eyes of God, ultimately rendering them fruitless in the afterlife.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieved and averted [people] from the way of Allah and then died while they were disbelievers - never will Allah forgive them.
interpretation: This verse serves as a final decree regarding those who deliberately reject the divine message and actively obstruct others from following the path of truth until their final breath. By persisting in their denial until death, they sever the connection to Allah's mercy, as repentance is a door that remains open only during one's lifetime; once death arrives in a state of disbelief, the opportunity for divine forgiveness is permanently sealed because the individual has consciously chosen to reject the only means of salvation provided by God.

translation: So do not weaken and call for peace while you are superior; and Allah is with you and will never deprive you of [the reward of] your deeds.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine command for believers to maintain their resolve and dignity during times of conflict, forbidding them from initiating peace out of fear, weakness, or exhaustion when they hold the upper hand in truth and faith. It reassures the believers that God’s support is their ultimate strength and guarantees that no act of patience, struggle, or righteousness performed in His cause will go unrewarded or be diminished, as their eternal recompense is secure with Him.

translation: The life of this world is only play and amusement. And if you believe and fear Allah, He will give you your rewards and will not ask you for your wealth.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the transient and deceptive nature of worldly life, suggesting that it is akin to a temporary diversion that should not be the primary focus of a believer's existence. The contrast drawn between worldly pursuits and spiritual devotion indicates that true value lies in faith and righteousness, which are the means to attain eternal reward, while the mention of wealth serves to reassure the believer that God does not demand their material possessions for His own benefit, but rather invites them to invest their hearts and actions into a permanent afterlife.

translation: If He should ask you for them and press you, you would withhold, and He would bring out your grudges.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inherent human tendency toward attachment to worldly possessions, indicating that if Allah were to demand all of one's wealth, the pressure would lead individuals to reveal the hidden resentment, stinginess, and malice dormant within their hearts, thus exposing the lack of sincere devotion and the weakness of their faith when faced with the complete surrender of material comforts.

translation: Here you are, those invited to spend in the cause of Allah, yet among you are those who withhold. And whoever withholds only withholds [benefit] from himself; and Allah is the Free of need, while you are the needy. And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people; then they will not be the likes of you.
interpretation: The verse serves as a stern reminder that charitable spending for the sake of Allah does not diminish one's wealth but rather acts as a spiritual investment for the donor's own ultimate benefit. It clarifies that Allah is independent of the creations' contributions, meaning He does not require our charity to sustain His sovereignty; rather, the act of giving is a necessity for the believer to purify the soul and demonstrate sincerity. By warning that those who turn away from this duty will be replaced by a people more obedient and generous, the verse emphasizes that the opportunity to serve the divine cause is a privilege, and if the current community fails to uphold its responsibilities, God's mission will continue through those who prove themselves more worthy and steadfast.

translation: Indeed, We have granted you, [O Muhammad], a clear conquest.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, which Allah describes as a 'clear conquest' because it paved the way for the peaceful spread of Islam, the eventual liberation of Makkah, and the consolidation of the Muslim state, demonstrating that divine victory is not always through immediate battle but through strategic outcomes that serve the ultimate mission of the message.

translation: That Allah may forgive for you what preceded of your sin and what will follow and complete His favor upon you and guide you to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to convey that Allah has granted him a comprehensive forgiveness covering his past and future, signifies the completion of his spiritual and legislative perfection through the message of Islam, and confirms his divine guidance on the path of truth that leads directly to Allah’s pleasure.

translation: And that Allah may help you with a mighty victory.
interpretation: This verse signifies that Allah grants the believers a profound and honorable triumph that is fortified by His power, ensuring that their message prevails and their dignity is restored, leaving no room for the enemies of the truth to undermine or overcome the divine victory granted to His servants.

translation: It is He who sent down tranquility into the hearts of the believers that they would increase in faith along with their [present] faith. And to Allah belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth, and ever is Allah Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights that inner peace and spiritual serenity are divine gifts bestowed upon the believers by Allah, which serve to fortify their conviction and deepen their spiritual commitment, especially during times of uncertainty or trial. By mentioning His control over the vast forces of the heavens and the earth, Allah reassures the faithful that He possesses absolute power to support them, while His attributes of being All-Knowing and All-Wise ensure that every challenge they face is ordained with perfect purpose and timing.

translation: That He may admit the believing men and the believing women to gardens beneath which rivers flow to abide therein eternally and remove from them their misdeeds - and ever is that, in the sight of Allah, a great attainment.
interpretation: The verse highlights that the ultimate success for the believers is not merely the attainment of paradise and its everlasting pleasures, but the divine forgiveness of their past sins, as the complete removal of one's shortcomings is a prerequisite for achieving the perfection and peace of the Hereafter in the presence of the Almighty.

translation: And [that He may] punish the hypocrite men and hypocrite women, and the polytheist men and polytheist women - those who assume about Allah an assumption of evil. Upon them is a misfortune of evil; and Allah has become angry with them and has cursed them and prepared for them Hell, and evil it is as a destination.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the root cause of the punishment for these groups is their malicious assumption regarding Allah, which refers to their doubt in His sovereignty, their disbelief that He would grant victory to His Prophet, or their suspicion that He would abandon the believers to falsehood; such an evil mindset reflects a corrupted heart that denies Divine wisdom, leading to the enactment of the very destruction they presumed would befall the believers, while the wrath and curse of Allah signify their complete isolation from His mercy and their ultimate ruin in the eternal fire.

translation: And to Allah belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth. And ever is Allah Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty of Allah over all existence, affirming that every creature, element, and force—whether seen or unseen—serves as a manifestation of His power and an instrument of His will. By framing these forces as 'soldiers,' the verse underscores that the entire universe is organized and governed by His command, ensuring that no event occurs outside of His divine decree. The description of Him as 'Exalted in Might' ensures that His authority cannot be challenged, while 'Wise' guarantees that every action or occurrence orchestrated by His forces is perfectly placed, purposeful, and aligned with His ultimate justice and order.

translation: Indeed, We have sent you as a witness and a bringer of good tidings and a warner.
interpretation: God Almighty affirms the status of Prophet Muhammad as a comprehensive guide for humanity; he serves as a witness over his nation regarding their deeds and adherence to divine truth, an announcer of glad tidings of paradise for the believers who follow the path of righteousness, and a warner against the consequences of disbelief and corruption, thereby establishing his role as the final link between the Creator and His creation to guide them toward their ultimate salvation.

translation: That you may believe in Allah and His Messenger, and may assist him and honor him, and exalt Him morning and afternoon.
interpretation: The verse commands believers to uphold their faith in Allah and support His Messenger by defending the truth, upholding the religion, and honoring the Prophet through absolute reverence and obedience, while continuously remembering Allah and declaring His perfection at the start and end of each day to maintain a constant spiritual connection with Him.

translation: Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you, [O Muhammad] - they are actually pledging allegiance to Allah. The hand of Allah is over their hands. So he who breaks his word only breaks it to the detriment of himself. And he who fulfills that which he has covenanted with Allah - He will give him a great reward.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the pledge of loyalty given to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is equivalent to a pledge made to Allah Himself, as the Prophet acts as His messenger and representative. The phrase 'the hand of Allah is over their hands' metaphorically denotes Allah’s presence, support, and oversight during the covenant, emphasizing that He is the ultimate witness and partner in this bond. Therefore, breaking the oath is not merely a betrayal of the Prophet, but a spiritual transgression against Allah that brings harm upon the oath-breaker, while upholding the covenant invites divine favor and an immense reward in the hereafter.

translation: Those of the bedouins who remained behind will say to you, 'Our possessions and our families occupied us, so ask forgiveness for us.' They say with their tongues what is not within their hearts. Say, 'Then who could prevent Allah at all if He intended for you harm or intended for you benefit? Rather, ever is Allah, with what you do, Acquainted.'
interpretation: This verse exposes the hypocrisy of the desert Arabs who sought excuses to avoid the struggle in the path of God by claiming worldly preoccupations hindered them, while their hearts lacked sincere faith; it serves as a stern reminder that their worldly attachments are ultimately powerless to shield them from the divine decree of either harm or benefit, as God encompasses all their secret motives and outward actions with perfect knowledge.

translation: Nay, you thought that the Messenger and the believers would never return to their families, and that was made fair-seeming in your hearts, and you thought an evil thought, and you became a ruined people.
interpretation: This verse addresses the hypocrites who remained behind during the expedition of Hudaibiyah, assuming that the Muslims would be annihilated by the Quraysh and never return. Their lack of faith in Allah's promise led them to succumb to the whispers of Satan, who made their cynical disbelief appear rational and desirable to them; consequently, they were spiritually ruined, having bartered their guidance for a hollow certainty of destruction that reflected their own corrupt and treacherous inner state.

translation: And whoever does not believe in Allah and His Messenger - then indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers a Blaze.
interpretation: This verse establishes that rejection of faith in Allah and the divine message brought by His Messenger results in a severe consequence, as those who deliberately choose to deny the truth after it has become clear to them will face the fire of Hell which has been specifically prepared as a dwelling for those who persist in their disbelief.

translation: And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse establishes the absolute sovereignty of Allah over the entire universe, emphasizing that His authority is not subject to any external law or accountability. The statement that He forgives or punishes whom He wills signifies that His decisions are rooted in His infinite wisdom and justice, ensuring that His mercy remains accessible to those who seek it through repentance while asserting His power to hold the defiant accountable, ultimately revealing that His attribute of forgiveness and mercy is the encompassing reality of His divine governance.

translation: Those who remained behind will say when you set out toward the spoils to take them, 'Let us follow you.' They wish to change the words of Allah. Say, 'Never will you follow us. Thus did Allah say before.' Then they will say, 'Nay, you envy us.' But they were not understanding except a little.
interpretation: The verse highlights the opportunistic nature of those who refused to join the Prophet and the believers in the expedition of Khaybar. When they saw the promise of wealth and spoils, they sought to join the mission not for the sake of faith, but for worldly gain. Their desire to 'change the words of Allah' refers to their attempt to disregard the divine decree that restricted the spoils of Khaybar solely to those who had participated in the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah. By accusing the believers of jealousy, they reveal their shallow understanding, as they project their own material greed onto the believers, failing to realize that the restriction was a matter of divine command and justice, not human malice.

translation: Say to those of the bedouins who were left behind, 'You will be called to [face] a people of great military might; you will fight them or they will [choose to] submit. And if you obey, Allah will give you a good reward; but if you turn away as you turned away before, He will punish you with a painful punishment.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a test of sincerity for the bedouin tribes who previously evaded military duty. Allah informs them that they will be summoned to engage in a severe battle against a formidable foe, which serves as a trial to distinguish those who truly believe and seek Allah's reward from those who are hesitant or hypocritical. By framing the outcome as either combat or the enemy's submission, Allah underscores the gravity of the call to jihad, emphasizing that their obedience is the path to divine grace, while repeating their past patterns of betrayal will inevitably lead to severe earthly and spiritual consequences.

translation: There is no blame upon the blind nor any blame upon the lame nor any blame upon the sick [for remaining behind in battle]. And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger - He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow; but whoever turns away - He will punish him with a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse establishes that individuals with physical disabilities such as blindness, lameness, or chronic illness are exempt from the religious obligation of Jihad, as the lack of physical capability removes the duty of participation. The verse then emphasizes that true success is contingent upon the sincere obedience to the commands of Allah and the guidance of the Prophet, which leads to the reward of Paradise, while those who knowingly reject or turn away from this obedience forfeit that mercy and face the consequence of their defiance.

translation: Certainly was Allah pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you, [O Muhammad], under the tree, and He knew what was in their hearts, so He sent down tranquility upon them and rewarded them with an imminent conquest.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine approval of the Companions who swore an oath of loyalty to the Prophet Muhammad at Hudaybiyyah. It underscores that Allah's satisfaction was based on His perfect knowledge of their internal sincerity, devotion, and steadfast faith during a time of uncertainty, which prompted Him to bestow upon them spiritual peace and the subsequent triumph at Khaybar as a manifestation of His grace.

translation: And many spoils of war which they will take; and Allah is Exalted in Might, Wise.
interpretation: This verse signifies that Allah promises the believers abundant rewards and spoils as a consequence of their perseverance and obedience in challenging times. It underscores that Allah's decree is backed by His absolute power to grant victory and His profound wisdom in determining the timing and distribution of these gains, ensuring that everything occurs according to a calculated and divine plan for the benefit of the faithful.

translation: Allah has promised you many spoils which you will obtain, so He has hastened this for you and restrained the hands of people from you, that it may be a sign for the believers and that He may guide you to a straight path.
interpretation: The verse conveys that Allah grants His believers immediate successes as a preview and a source of strength, demonstrating His divine protection by preventing their enemies from harming them, thereby reinforcing the faith of the believers and confirming that obedience to His commands is the only sure path to sustained success and spiritual righteousness.

translation: And [there are] others [victories] which you have not yet been able to achieve, but Allah has already encompassed them; and Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine reassurance to the believers, promising that beyond the immediate successes or spoils they have secured, there are future conquests and spiritual or material gains already decreed and protected by God’s knowledge and power. It emphasizes that human inability to reach certain objectives does not imply failure if God has ordained them, as His comprehensive encompassment ensures that all destined outcomes are firmly within His control, reflecting His absolute ability to bring about whatever He wills at the appropriate time.

translation: And if those who disbelieve had fought you, they would have turned their backs [in flight]; then they would not find a protector or a helper.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine reassurance to the believers, emphasizing that the disbelievers' power is ultimately hollow and destined for defeat; it suggests that even if the disbelievers were to engage in battle, their lack of true conviction and spiritual support from God would inevitably lead them to flee in disgrace, finding no one to defend them from the consequences of their actions or to provide them the victory they seek.

translation: This is the way of Allah which has occurred before, and you will never find in the way of Allah any change.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that the laws governing the rise and fall of nations and the divine retribution for those who reject the truth are immutable and constant, reflecting the absolute wisdom and unchanging justice of Allah, which means that the historical outcomes of the past—where arrogance and denial led to inevitable destruction—will remain the same for those who follow in those same footsteps in the future.

translation: And it is He who withheld their hands from you and your hands from them within the valley of Makkah after He had let you overcome them. And ever is Allah, of what you do, Seeing.
interpretation: Allah reminds the believers of His favor in preventing a violent confrontation during the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, despite the Muslims having gained the upper hand. He emphasizes that this restraint was a divine act of mercy to preserve the sanctity of the Sacred Mosque and to allow for a peaceful outcome that ultimately led to the conquest of Makkah, demonstrating that Allah is fully aware of the intentions and actions of His servants.

translation: They are the ones who disbelieved and obstructed you from al-Masjid al-Haram while the sacrificial animals were prevented from reaching their place of slaughter.
