interpretation: This verse was revealed regarding Khawla bint Tha'labah, who came to the Prophet (peace be upon him) disputing the harsh treatment of her husband, Aws ibn al-Samit, after he pronounced zihar upon her. It serves as a profound reassurance that Allah is intimately aware of the private struggles, grievances, and prayers of His servants, emphasizing that no matter how isolated or desperate a person may feel in their distress, their voice is never unheard by the Divine, who possesses absolute knowledge of every detail of their circumstance.

translation: Those among you who pronounce Zihar against their wives (calling them as their mothers), they cannot be their mothers. Their mothers are only those who gave birth to them. And indeed, they utter an ill word and a lie. And verily, Allah is Pardoning, Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse invalidates the pre-Islamic practice of Zihar, a form of divorce where a husband would declare his wife to be equivalent to his mother to forbid her to himself. Allah clarifies that no verbal decree or false analogy can change the fundamental biological reality of motherhood, which is restricted solely to the woman who gives birth. By labeling such statements as reprehensible and false, the verse emphasizes the sanctity of the marital bond and protects women from such degrading linguistic abuse, while simultaneously opening a door of mercy through divine forgiveness for those who committed this grave error before it was strictly forbidden.

translation: And those who pronounce zihar regarding their wives then wish to retract what they said, then the expiation is the freeing of a slave before they touch one another. That is what you are instructed; and Allah is, with what you do, Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse establishes a severe spiritual and social regulation regarding the pre-Islamic practice of 'zihar' (where a man equates his wife to his mother to effectively divorce her). It mandates that if a husband wishes to reconcile after making such a statement, he must perform the act of manumission—freeing a slave—as an expiation for his rash oath before he can resume marital intimacy. This serves as a divine mechanism to discourage impulsive, damaging speech while providing a clear path of repentance and rectification that honors the sanctity of the marriage bond.

translation: But he who does not find [a slave to free] must fast for two months consecutively before they touch one another; and he who is unable [to fast] must feed sixty poor persons. That is to establish your faith in Allah and His Messenger; and these are the limits [set by] Allah. And for the disbelievers is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse outlines the progressive penance required for violating the sanctity of marital relations during the fasting state, emphasizing that these rulings are ordained by Allah to solidify the believer's commitment and obedience to divine law, while warning that those who knowingly transgress these sacred boundaries and reject His commandments will face severe retribution.

translation: Indeed, those who oppose Allah and His Messenger will be humbled as those before them were humbled. And We have certainly sent down verses of clear evidence. And for the disbelievers is a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse asserts that those who act in defiance and hostility toward the commands of Allah and the guidance of His Messenger will inevitably face ignominy and failure, just as the arrogant nations of the past who resisted Divine Truth were brought to ruin. The humiliation of the disbelievers is a direct consequence of their rejection of the manifest proofs and clear signs that have been revealed to clarify the path of righteousness, serving as a warning that turning away from Divine wisdom results in both temporal defeat and an everlasting, degrading torment.

translation: On the Day when Allah will resurrect them all and inform them of what they did. Allah has kept account of it, while they have forgotten it. And Allah is, over all things, Witness.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute nature of divine omniscience, contrasting human forgetfulness with the infallible record-keeping of God. It serves as a reminder that every action, no matter how small or seemingly insignificant, is meticulously documented in a divine ledger, even if the person who committed the deed has long since banished it from their memory. The mention of Allah as the ultimate Witness emphasizes that there is no escape from accountability, as the truth of one's existence is held in the constant, encompassing awareness of the Creator, who sees and preserves the reality of all things that occur within the universe.

translation: Do you not see that Allah knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth? There is no private conversation of three but He is the fourth of them, nor of five but He is the sixth of them—and no less than that and no more except that He is with them [in knowledge] wherever they are. Then He will inform them of what they did on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed Allah is, of all things, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute omniscience and omnipresence of Allah, asserting that His knowledge encompasses every secret whisper and private gathering. His 'being with them' signifies His total awareness, encompassing surveillance, and perfect observation of every individual's actions and intentions, ensuring that nothing is hidden from Him. This serves as a reminder to the believer that they are never truly alone, and that every deed—whether public or deeply concealed—is recorded and will be brought to light for divine judgment on the Day of Resurrection.

translation: Have you not seen those who were forbidden from private conspiracy, then they return to that which they were forbidden and conspire in sin, aggression, and disobedience to the Messenger? And when they come to you, they greet you with a greeting that Allah does not greet you with and say within themselves, 'Why does Allah not punish us for what we say?' Sufficient for them is Hell, which they will [enter to] burn, and wretched is the destination.
interpretation: This verse addresses the hypocrites who persisted in their secret, malicious plotting despite being forbidden from it, showing their deep-seated rebellion and lack of true faith. Their defiance is highlighted by their mockery of the Prophet Muhammad through distorted greetings and their arrogant skepticism, as they falsely believe that if they were truly wrong, divine punishment would befall them immediately. The verse serves as a warning that their worldly defiance will ultimately lead to an inevitable and severe consequence in the afterlife, where their deeds will be met with the eternal torment of Hell, proving that Allah's delayed punishment is not an indication of their innocence but rather a respite that leads to their greater ruin.

translation: O you who have believed, when you hold private conversation, do not converse about sin and aggression and disobedience to the Messenger; but converse about righteousness and piety. And fear Allah, to whom you will be gathered.
interpretation: This verse serves as a moral guideline for interpersonal communication, specifically targeting secret counsels or private gatherings. Allah instructs the believers to shun conspiracies or whisperings that involve wrongdoing, hostility towards others, or defiance of the Prophet's teachings, as such actions corrupt the soul and foster division within the community. Instead, believers are commanded to utilize their private dialogues for constructive purposes, focusing on acts of goodness, virtue, and God-consciousness. The verse concludes with a reminder of the inevitable accountability in the afterlife, suggesting that even our hidden intentions and private discussions are under the divine observation of Allah, before whom all people will eventually stand for judgment.

translation: Private conversation is only from Satan, that he may grieve those who have believed, but he will not harm them at all except by permission of Allah. And upon Allah let the believers rely.
interpretation: This verse addresses the behavior of those who whisper secretly among themselves with the intent of spreading fear or sowing discord among the believers. It reveals that such malicious whisperings are inspired by Satan to create anxiety and distress in the hearts of the faithful, yet these plots have no real power to inflict harm unless Allah allows it. The verse ultimately directs the believers to remain steadfast in their faith and place their complete trust in Allah, for His protection is superior to any human or satanic scheme.

translation: O you who have believed, when you [wish to] privately consult the Messenger, present before your consultation a charity. That is better for you and purer. But if you find not [the means] - then indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse serves as a spiritual discipline for the believers, teaching them that seeking the company of the Prophet for private counsel is a privilege that requires a manifestation of sincerity and detachment from worldly attachment; by giving charity, the believers demonstrate that their desire for his guidance outweighs their love for wealth, while the subsequent dispensation for those unable to pay highlights that Allah measures the intent of the heart and the capability of the individual rather than the material value of the offering.

translation: Are you afraid to offer charity before your private consultation? If you do not do it and Allah forgives you, then establish prayer, give zakat, and obey Allah and His Messenger; and Allah is All-Aware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine leniency for the believers who were initially commanded to offer charity before speaking privately with the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), acknowledging the financial burden this placed on them. By relieving them of this obligation, Allah redirects their focus toward the fundamental pillars of faith—prayer, obligatory charity (zakat), and obedience—emphasizing that true piety is measured by adherence to these core duties rather than the ritual of private donations, all while reminding them that their actions and intentions are fully known to Him.

translation: Have you not considered those who make allies of a people with whom Allah has become angry? They are neither of you nor of them, and they swear to untruths while they know [they are lying].
interpretation: This verse addresses the hypocrites who oscillate between the believers and the disbelievers, seeking to deceive both sides. Their behavior reveals their lack of genuine faith in either party, as they cultivate alliances with those who have earned Allah's displeasure—the Jews—while outwardly claiming membership with the Muslims. By swearing false oaths to protect their duplicitous position despite knowing they are lying, they demonstrate that their primary allegiance is to their own worldly security rather than divine truth.

translation: Allah has prepared for them a severe punishment; indeed, it is evil what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute justice of Allah, stating that He has decreed a painful and rigorous retribution for those who persistently committed grave sins and rejected the truth, highlighting that their ultimate suffering is a direct and logical consequence of the wicked deeds, corruption, and defiance they willfully chose to engage in throughout their worldly lives.

translation: They have made their oaths a shield, so they diverted [people] from the way of Allah, and for them is a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: The verse highlights the hypocrisy of those who use sworn oaths as a deceptive barrier or cover to conceal their true intentions and facilitate their opposition to the faith, thereby misleading others and preventing them from embracing the truth; consequently, they are destined for a punishment that serves as a fitting disgrace for their act of betrayal and deceit.

translation: Neither their wealth nor their children shall avail them at all against Allah. They are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern reminder that material possessions and familial lineages, which are often used as sources of pride or protection in this world, become entirely ineffective and powerless when facing the divine judgment of Allah. It emphasizes that the true weight in the hereafter is carried by faith and righteous deeds, and that those who reject the truth and persist in disbelief seal their fate to dwell in the Hellfire forever, where no worldly influence can intervene to change their destiny.

translation: On the Day when Allah will resurrect them all, they will swear to Him as they swear to you, and they will think that they stand on something. Verily, it is they who are the liars.
interpretation: This verse describes the state of the hypocrites on the Day of Resurrection, where their habit of deceit persists even before their Creator. Despite the overwhelming reality of the afterlife, they will attempt to justify their past conduct by swearing oaths to Allah just as they falsely swore to the believers in worldly life, clinging to the delusional belief that their hollow claims or fabricated justifications hold some value. The verse serves as an ultimate refutation, emphasizing that their arrogance and persistence in falsehood lead them to a state of profound self-deception, as they are ultimately proven to be the ones who truly betrayed the truth.

translation: Satan has overcome them and made them forget the remembrance of Allah. Those are the party of Satan. Unquestionably, the party of Satan are the losers.
interpretation: The verse indicates that when a person continuously gives in to the whispers of Satan, he effectively allows Satan to gain complete dominance over his heart and actions. This state of spiritual subjugation leads the individual to become indifferent to the commandments of Allah and detached from His remembrance. By abandoning the path of God, these individuals align themselves with Satan's group, and their ultimate end is an irreversible state of loss because they have traded eternal salvation for the fleeting temptations of worldly desires.

translation: Indeed, those who oppose Allah and His Messenger—those will be among the most humbled.
interpretation: This verse asserts that anyone who chooses to defy the commandments of Allah and reject the guidance brought by His Messenger will ultimately face degradation, spiritual ruin, and a state of lowliness both in this world and the Hereafter, as they have set themselves against the Source of all power and truth, leading inevitably to their own defeat and insignificance.

translation: Allah has written, 'I will surely overcome, I and My messengers.' Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine assurance and a definitive decree that the ultimate victory belongs to Allah and those who carry His message. It signifies that despite any temporary setbacks, opposition, or persecution faced by the messengers and the believers, the truth will inevitably prevail through divine intervention because Allah is omnipotent, possessing the absolute power to enforce His will, and He is the Almighty, whose sovereignty cannot be defeated or challenged by any created being.

translation: You will not find a people who believe in Allah and the Last Day loving those who oppose Allah and His Messenger, even if they were their fathers or their sons or their brothers or their kindred. Those – He has decreed within their hearts faith and supported them with spirit from Him. And We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally. Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. Those are the party of Allah. Unquestionably, the party of Allah – they are the successful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the bond of faith is the ultimate criteria for loyalty in Islam, transcending even the strongest ties of blood and kinship. It declares that genuine believers cannot hold affection for those who actively wage war against Allah's laws and His Messenger, as true faith necessitates an unwavering commitment to the principles of God. By placing the love of Allah above earthly relationships, the believer demonstrates that their heart has been fortified with divine guidance and spiritual strength, leading to the ultimate reward of God's pleasure and eternal residence in Paradise, which defines the true success of those who belong to the party of Allah.

translation: Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth exalts Allah, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that every single element of the creation, whether animate or inanimate, possesses a form of consciousness or natural disposition that causes it to declare the glory and perfection of Allah, testifying to His oneness and majesty; furthermore, this constant act of glorification acknowledges that Allah possesses absolute power, which He exercises with perfect wisdom and precision in all His decrees and creations.

translation: It is He who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture from their homes at the first gathering. You did not think they would leave, and they thought that their fortresses would protect them from Allah; but Allah came at them from where they had not expected and cast terror into their hearts so they destroyed their houses by their own hands and the hands of the believers. So take warning, O people of vision.
interpretation: This verse serves as a profound reminder that human reliance on worldly defenses, such as fortresses or strategic positions, is futile when faced with the decree of the Divine. It illustrates how Allah subverts the expectations of the arrogant, stripping them of their perceived security and leaving them to dismantle their own structures of power, both physically and metaphorically. The command to 'take warning' instructs those with insight to recognize that true security resides solely in submission to Allah, rather than in the material fortifications or earthly alliances that people erroneously trust to prevent inevitable outcomes.

translation: And had Allah not decreed for them exile, He would have punished them in this world, and for them in the Hereafter is the punishment of the Fire.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Banu Nadir tribe, explaining that their expulsion from their homes was a mercy from Allah to spare them from a more immediate and destructive punishment in this world, such as death or total annihilation at the hands of the believers, while simultaneously serving as a warning that this worldly consequence does not absolve them from the ultimate and eternal retribution of Hellfire in the afterlife.

translation: That is because they opposed Allah and His Messenger; and whoever opposes Allah, then indeed Allah is severe in penalty.
interpretation: The verse explains that the harsh punishment inflicted upon those who resisted the truth is a direct consequence of their active defiance and hostility toward the divine commands and the mission of the Prophet; it serves as a warning that because Allah is the ultimate source of power and authority, any attempt to wage war against His path or obstruct His guidance is a futile endeavor that will inevitably lead to a severe and inescapable requital.

translation: Whatever you have cut down of (the) palm trees or left them standing on their roots, it was by permission of Allah and so that He might disgrace the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine justification for the strategic actions taken by the Muslims against the Banu Nadir tribe during the siege. By clarifying that the felling of the date palms was done under Allah’s command, the verse absolves the believers of any perceived moral guilt regarding the destruction of property. Furthermore, it highlights that the primary purpose behind this command was to demoralize and expose the hypocrisy and weakness of the transgressors who had broken their covenant, demonstrating that their reliance on their fortifications and wealth was futile against the decree of Allah.

translation: And what Allah restored to His Messenger from them - you did not spur for it any horses or camels, but Allah gives His messengers power over whom He wills, and Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the spoils of war acquired without active military engagement, such as the property of the Banu Nadir, belong exclusively to Allah and His Messenger to be distributed as He wills, because the Muslims did not have to undergo the hardship of fighting or traveling to seize them; rather, it was Allah who caused the enemy to surrender through divine decree, demonstrating His absolute authority and power over all matters.

translation: For the poor emigrants who were expelled from their homes and their properties, seeking bounty from Allah and [His] approval and supporting Allah and His Messenger, [there is also a share]. Those are the truthful.
interpretation: This verse honors the Emigrants (Muhajirun) who sacrificed everything they owned and left their homelands solely to seek the pleasure and grace of Allah, confirming their sincerity by actively supporting the Prophet and the religion of Islam through their steadfast dedication and willingness to give up their worldly comforts for the sake of their faith.

translation: And those who had settled in the Home and in faith before them love those who migrated to them and find not any want in their breasts of what they were given and prefer them over themselves, even though they were in poverty. And whoever is saved from the stinginess of his soul - it is those who are the successful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound spiritual bond of brotherhood among the Ansar in Medina. It praises them for their genuine lack of envy toward the Muhajirun regarding the wealth or status they received from the Prophet, and specifically commends their extreme altruism, where they sacrificed their own needs to provide for their brothers despite their own personal struggle and poverty, illustrating that true success lies in overcoming the selfish greed inherent in the human soul.

translation: And those who came after them, saying, 'Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith and put not in our hearts any resentment toward those who have believed. Our Lord, indeed You are Kind and Merciful.'
interpretation: This verse establishes the ideal spiritual bond between generations of believers, emphasizing that true faith requires a heart cleansed of envy, hatred, and grudge. By asking God to forgive those who came before them and to purify their own intentions, the believers acknowledge the continuity of the community of faith and recognize that the absence of malice toward one's fellow believers is a fundamental prerequisite for divine mercy and the preservation of communal harmony.

translation: Have you not considered those who practice hypocrisy, saying to their brothers who have disbelieved among the People of the Scripture, 'If you are expelled, we will surely leave with you, and we will not obey, in regard to you, anyone ever; and if you are fought, we will surely aid you.' But Allah testifies that they are liars.
interpretation: This verse exposes the duplicity of the hypocrites who formed secret alliances with the disbelievers of Medina, such as the Banu Nadir, by offering false assurances of loyalty and military support. Allah reveals their inherent cowardice and deceit, confirming that their promises were empty rhetoric driven by political convenience rather than genuine conviction or bravery, as they would never actually risk their lives or safety to honor these treacherous oaths when faced with real conflict.

translation: If they are expelled, they will not leave with them, and if they are fought, they will not help them. And even if they were to help them, they would surely turn their backs in flight; then they would not be helped.
interpretation: This verse exposes the inherent cowardice and hypocrisy of the hypocrites, asserting that their promises of loyalty to their allies are empty; when faced with the reality of persecution or conflict, their supposed courage will dissolve, and their alliances will fail to provide them with any protection or victory because they lack true conviction and divine support.

translation: You are indeed more fearful in their hearts than Allah. That is because they are a people who do not understand.
interpretation: This verse addresses the hypocrites of Medina, highlighting that their hearts were filled with a greater fear and awe of the physical power and presence of the believers than they were of Allah's punishment or majesty. This irrational state of fear arises because they lack true spiritual insight and understanding; they are focused solely on immediate worldly consequences rather than recognizing the absolute authority of the Creator, which blinds them to the reality that fearing anything other than Allah is a consequence of their ignorance of His true nature.

translation: They will not fight you all together except within fortified cities or from behind walls. Their violence among themselves is severe. You think they are united, but their hearts are divided. That is because they are a people who do not reason.
interpretation: The verse highlights the inherent cowardice and internal discord of those who reject the truth. Despite their outward appearance of strength and collective organization, they are fundamentally fractured by mutual enmity and lack of true understanding. Their refusal to engage in open, direct combat—preferring the safety of fortifications—reflects a lack of genuine conviction, and their internal hostility towards one another renders their unity merely superficial, proving that their worldly strategies are devoid of the wisdom that comes from divine guidance.

translation: Like the case of those before them shortly; they tasted the consequence of their conduct, and they will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse serves as a historical and spiritual reminder that the pattern of divine justice is consistent throughout time; just as previous disbelievers faced the immediate worldly repercussions of their sins, those who persist in opposing the truth will similarly suffer the spiritual and temporal fallout of their actions in this life, which acts as a precursor to the definitive and agonizing punishment they will encounter in the Hereafter.

translation: [The hypocrites are] like Satan when he says to man, 'Disbelieve.' But when he disbelieves, he says, 'Indeed, I am disassociated from you. Indeed, I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the ultimate treachery of evil forces: they incite individuals to abandon faith and commit sins, promising support or justification for their actions, but the moment the person falls into transgression, the deceiver abandons them entirely. It serves as a warning that those who lead others astray will never accept responsibility for their followers' misdeeds on the Day of Judgment; instead, they will feign piety and claim innocence, leaving their victims to face the full consequences of their actions alone before Allah.

translation: So the outcome for both of them was that they will be in the Fire, abiding eternally therein. And that is the recompense of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning that the ultimate consequence for those who incite others to disbelief or commit grave transgressions is eternal punishment in Hell, illustrating that divine justice is absolute and that those who persist in oppression and disobedience against God forfeit their place in Paradise, receiving instead the recompense fitting for their chosen path of injustice.

translation: O you who have believed, fear Allah. And let every soul look to what it has put forth for tomorrow - and fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do.
interpretation: This verse serves as a profound call for self-reflection and spiritual accountability, urging believers to constantly evaluate their actions and intentions as investments for the afterlife, realizing that every deed is being recorded and will be presented on the Day of Judgment, a day for which one must prepare through piety and consistent awareness of God's presence.

translation: And do not be like those who forgot Allah, so He made them forget themselves. Those are the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: The verse warns that abandoning the remembrance of Allah and failing to fulfill His rights leads to a spiritual blindness where a person loses sight of their own true interests, purpose, and moral integrity; by neglecting their Creator, they become estranged from their own soul, ultimately leading them to pursue temporary desires that lead to their own ruin and persistent disobedience.

translation: The companions of the Fire and the companions of Paradise are not equal. The companions of Paradise are the successful ones.
interpretation: This verse serves as a definitive moral contrast, establishing that the dwellers of Hell, who chose disbelief and disobedience, and the dwellers of Paradise, who embraced faith and righteous conduct, occupy fundamentally different stations that can never be equated. The ultimate triumph belongs exclusively to those in Paradise, because their success is eternal, based on the attainment of Allah's pleasure and the realization of salvation, whereas the state of those in the Fire is one of permanent loss and failure.

translation: Had We sent down this Qur'an upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled and split asunder from the fear of Allah. And these parables We present to the people that perhaps they will reflect.
interpretation: This verse employs a powerful rhetorical metaphor to illustrate the profound weight, majesty, and transformative authority of the Qur'an. By suggesting that even an inanimate, immovable object like a mountain would be moved to humility and disintegration if it were burdened with the gravity of Allah's word, the verse serves as a spiritual critique of the human heart that remains hardened or indifferent to the revelation. It emphasizes that the message of the Qur'an is so monumental that its true reception requires a level of consciousness and spiritual receptivity that transcends the physical nature of creation, inviting believers to recognize the immense sanctity of the divine discourse and to allow their own hearts to be softened and transformed by its wisdom.

translation: He is Allah, other than whom there is no deity, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed. He is the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.
interpretation: This verse establishes the absolute Oneness of Allah and highlights His unique attributes, affirming that He alone possesses perfect knowledge of all things—both that which is hidden from human perception and that which is manifest—while simultaneously emphasizing that His governance over the entire universe is rooted in a boundless mercy that encompasses all creation.

translation: He is Allah, other than whom there is no deity, the Sovereign, the Pure, the Perfection, the Bestower of Faith, the Overseer, the Exalted in Might, the Compeller, the Superior. Exalted is Allah above whatever they associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse serves as a profound declaration of Allah's absolute oneness and His divine attributes. By listing these names, the Quran emphasizes that Allah alone possesses true sovereignty, absolute holiness, and total perfection. He is the ultimate source of peace, safety, and security for His creation, overseeing all affairs with complete authority. The mention of His power and superiority is intended to humble the human heart, leading it to recognize that any entity or concept partners associate with Him—whether material wealth, ego, or worldly idols—is infinitely inferior and beneath the majesty of the Creator, who is far beyond the limitations of human perception or polytheistic corruption.

translation: He is Allah, the Creator, the Inventor, the Fashioner; to Him belong the best names. Whatever is in the heavens and earth is exalting Him. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse presents the multifaceted nature of Allah's creative power, moving from the act of bringing existence from nothingness to the intentional design and specific shaping of all entities. It emphasizes that because He possesses these supreme attributes, all of creation exists in a state of continuous acknowledgement and glorification of His perfection, reflecting His sovereign authority combined with profound purpose in every aspect of the universe.

translation: O you who have believed, do not take My enemies and your enemies as allies, extending to them affection while they have disbelieved in what came to you of the truth, having driven out the Messenger and yourselves [only] because you believe in Allah, your Lord. If you have come out for Jihad in My cause and seeking My pleasure, [do not take them as allies]. You confide in them affection, while I am most knowing of what you have concealed and what you have declared. And whoever does that among you has certainly strayed from the soundness of the way.
interpretation: This verse serves as a fundamental directive for the believers to establish a clear distinction between the community of faith and those who actively wage war against Allah and His Messenger. It emphasizes that true loyalty, love, and secrecy should never be extended to those who reject the truth and persecute believers for their faith. The interpretation highlights that the ultimate test of a believer's sincerity lies in their allegiance; since Allah knows the innermost secrets of the heart, any attempts to secretly align with the enemies of the faith—while claiming to be a follower—constitute a complete deviation from the straight path and a betrayal of the divine covenant of faith.

translation: If they capture you, they will be your enemies and will stretch out their hands and their tongues against you with evil, and they wish that you would disbelieve.
interpretation: This verse warns the believers against the hidden enmity of those who feign friendship while harboring deep-seated hatred; it emphasizes that if these hypocrites or adversaries were to gain power over the believers, they would not hesitate to inflict physical harm and verbal abuse, driven by their core desire to see the believers abandon their faith and fall into disbelief.

translation: Neither your relatives nor your children will benefit you; on the Day of Resurrection, He will judge between you, and Allah is All-Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, earthly ties and kinship will carry no weight in shifting the scales of justice; rather, the ultimate separation will occur based on the truth, wherein every individual shall be judged solely by their own deeds and faith, for Allah observes the hidden realities of every action, ensuring that no one is unjustly burdened or favored.

translation: There has already been for you an excellent pattern in Abraham and those with him, when they said to their people, 'Indeed, we are disassociated from you and from whatever you worship other than Allah. We have denied you, and there has appeared between us and you animosity and hatred forever until you believe in Allah alone,' except for the saying of Abraham to his father, 'I will surely ask forgiveness for you, but I have not, for you, [power to do] anything against Allah. Our Lord, upon You we have relied, and to You we have returned, and to You is the destination.'
interpretation: This verse establishes the principle of 'al-wala wal-bara' (loyalty and disavowal), instructing believers to emulate Prophet Abraham and his followers by completely distancing themselves from polytheism and those who practice it. It highlights that the core of this disavowal is centered on the exclusive worship of Allah, and while believers are commanded to maintain this firm stance, the exception made by Abraham regarding his father serves as a reminder that divine guidance is ultimately in Allah's hands, and believers must entrust their affairs solely to Him while remaining steadfast in their monotheistic commitment.

translation: Our Lord, do not make us a trial for the disbelievers and forgive us, our Lord. Indeed, it is You who are the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: The believers are supplicating to Allah to protect them from being subjected to the dominance or persecution of the disbelievers, lest the disbelievers perceive their own falsehood as truth due to their temporary worldly success over the believers, or that the believers themselves might be tempted by the disbelievers' lifestyle; they acknowledge Allah's ultimate authority and wisdom in all decrees, seeking His mercy to remain steadfast in their faith.

translation: There has certainly been for you in them a good example for anyone who hopes in Allah and the Last Day. And whoever turns away - then indeed, Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: The verse establishes the prophets and righteous believers as exemplary models for the faithful, emphasizing that imitating their steadfastness in faith and their dissociation from falsehood is a practical manifestation of one's hope for divine reward; furthermore, it warns that turning away from this guidance harms only the individual, as Allah is entirely independent of His creation's devotion and is inherently worthy of all praise regardless of whether people believe or disbelieve.

translation: It may be that Allah will grant affection between you and those you have held as enemies among them. And Allah is All-Powerful, and Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: This verse serves as a hopeful promise that the hostility between the believers and their disbelieving enemies is not necessarily permanent; rather, through the guidance and decree of Allah, hearts can be softened and reconciled, turning enmity into kinship and mutual regard, as Allah possesses the infinite power to change human hearts and the boundless mercy to forgive past transgressions.

translation: Allah only forbids you from those who fight you because of religion and expel you from your homes and aid in your expulsion - [forbids you] from making allies of them. And whoever makes allies of them, then it is those who are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse serves as a legal boundary for the Muslim community regarding their social and political dealings with non-Muslims; it specifies that the prohibition of maintaining friendly, supportive, or protective alliances is strictly limited to those enemies who have actively engaged in physical aggression, religious persecution, and the forced displacement of believers. By explicitly naming those who wage war and conspire to expel Muslims from their homes, the Qur'an clarifies that the prohibition is rooted in the hostility and injustice of the opposing party's actions rather than their religious identity alone, thus labeling those who seek patronage or loyalty from such active oppressors as 'wrongdoers' who have crossed the bounds of justice.

translation: O you who have believed, when the believing women come to you as emigrants, examine them. Allah is most knowing of their faith. And if you know them to be believers, then do not return them to the disbelievers; they are not lawful [wives] for them, nor are they lawful [husbands] for them. But give the disbelievers what they have spent. And there is no blame upon you if you marry them when you have given them their compensation. And hold not to marriage bonds with disbelieving women, but ask for what you have spent and let them ask for what they have spent. That is the judgment of Allah; He judges between you. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse establishes a legal framework for dealing with women who emigrate from disbelieving lands to the community of believers, emphasizing that faith is the defining bond of relationships. By commanding the examination of these women, Allah establishes that religious allegiance supersedes previous social or marital ties, rendering existing marriages to disbelievers void and prohibiting the return of these women to a state where their faith might be compromised. The instruction to settle financial dues ensures justice and clarity in dissolving past unions, while the prohibition against maintaining marital ties with disbelieving spouses reflects the essential incompatibility of different belief systems in establishing a cohesive and protected household in Islam.

translation: And if anything from your wives has passed from you to the disbelievers and you have an opportunity [for retaliation], then give those whose wives have gone the equivalent of what they had spent. And fear Allah, in whom you are believers.
interpretation: This verse establishes a ruling for a specific historical context where Muslim women would leave their husbands to join the disbelievers in Mecca or elsewhere. God instructs the Muslim community that if they gain spoils or find themselves in a position of victory over the enemy, they must compensate the Muslim men whose wives deserted them, ensuring they are repaid the dowry or wealth they originally spent on those wives from the collective gains of the community. This served as a means of social justice and economic security for the believers, emphasizing the preservation of individual rights within the framework of faith and the fear of God.

translation: O Prophet, when the believing women come to you pledging to you that they will not associate anything with Allah, nor will they steal, nor will they commit unlawful sexual intercourse, nor will they kill their children, nor will they bring forth a slander they have invented between their arms and legs, nor will they disobey you in what is right - then accept their pledge and ask forgiveness for them of Allah. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse establishes the essential criteria for spiritual and moral conduct expected of believing women, emphasizing the renunciation of polytheism, criminal behavior, and social indecency. By commanding the Prophet to accept this oath, Allah highlights that salvation is rooted in a covenant of righteous action and obedience to divine guidance, while simultaneously offering the comforting assurance of His mercy and readiness to forgive past shortcomings for those who genuinely commit to this virtuous path.

translation: O you who have believed, do not make allies of a people with whom Allah has become angry; they have despaired of the Hereafter just as the disbelievers have despaired of [the inhabitants of] the graves.
interpretation: This verse warns the believers against forming loyalties or alliances with those who have rejected the truth and earned Allah's displeasure, as their hearts are so entrenched in disbelief that they have completely lost hope in the resurrection and the reward of the afterlife, mirroring the hopelessness of the deniers of old who do not believe that the dead in their graves will ever be brought back to life.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful. Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth exalts Allah, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse indicates that all creation, animate and inanimate, declares the perfection of Allah and His freedom from any deficiency, acknowledging His absolute sovereignty and majesty. This universal glorification serves as a testament to the order and purpose infused into the cosmos, reflecting that every atom in existence operates under the decree of an Almighty Creator whose wisdom governs all affairs, ensuring that nothing occurs without a precise and calculated reason.

translation: O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do?
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern divine reprimand to the believers against hypocrisy and the misalignment between one's outward speech and inward actions, emphasizing that a person's credibility and spiritual integrity are anchored in the consistency of their deeds with their claims, as claiming virtues or commitments one does not practice invites the displeasure of Allah.

translation: Great is hatred in the sight of Allah that you say what you do not do.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern condemnation of hypocrisy, highlighting the moral inconsistency between one's words and actions; it warns that claiming virtues or commitments while failing to embody them in practice is an act of deep deception that incurs the severe displeasure of God, as it undermines the integrity of one's faith and character.

translation: Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in a row as though they are a [single] structure joined firmly.
interpretation: This verse highlights the necessity of unity, discipline, and steadfastness in the pursuit of righteous goals; it implies that when believers act in complete harmony and collective purpose, their strength and resolve become impenetrable and solid like a well-constructed building, reflecting an internal cohesion that pleases God.

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when Moses said to his people, 'O my people, why do you harm me while you certainly know that I am the messenger of Allah to you?' And when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate. And Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.
interpretation: This verse illustrates that the persistent rejection and intentional turning away from the truth by the people of Moses, despite their clear recognition of his prophetic status, caused them to lose the ability to accept guidance. Allah’s act of making their hearts deviate is a consequence of their own initial choice to incline towards falsehood, demonstrating that when a person stubbornly persists in corruption and disobedience, Allah withdraws the light of guidance from their hearts as a fitting outcome for their willful abandonment of the truth.

translation: And remember when Jesus, son of Mary, said: 'O Children of Israel! I am the messenger of Allah to you, confirming the Torah that came before me and bringing glad tidings of a messenger who will come after me, whose name shall be Ahmad.' But when he came to them with clear signs, they said: 'This is manifest sorcery.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the continuity of the divine message by highlighting that Jesus did not come to abolish the previous revelations but to confirm the Torah, while simultaneously preparing his followers for the arrival of Prophet Muhammad, referred to here by his name 'Ahmad.' It illustrates the tragic irony of human stubbornness, where even in the face of unmistakable divine miracles, those whose hearts are hardened by prejudice and attachment to worldly power will choose to dismiss the truth as mere deception rather than submit to the guidance presented to them.

translation: And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie about Allah while he is being invited to Islam? And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse highlights the gravity of persisting in falsehood and arrogance when the truth of Islam is presented, emphasizing that those who willfully fabricate lies against God despite receiving the invitation to guidance have severed themselves from divine direction because their own persistent injustice and spiritual blindness prevent them from receiving it.

translation: They want to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah will perfect His light, although the disbelievers dislike it.
interpretation: The verse illustrates the futility of the efforts made by those who oppose the truth of Islam; their attempts to undermine the message of Allah through falsehood and malicious speech are as ineffective as trying to blow out the sun with one's breath, as Allah's divine guidance is destined to spread and prevail regardless of their hostility.

translation: It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to manifest it over all religion, although the polytheists dislike it.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah sent Prophet Muhammad with the perfect guidance of the Quran and the true way of life of Islam, ensuring that this message will ultimately prevail and dominate over all other ideologies and false beliefs through its clear evidence, rational strength, and eventual widespread acceptance, a reality that remains constant despite the persistent opposition and hatred of those who associate partners with God.

translation: O you who have believed, shall I guide you to a transaction that will save you from a painful punishment?
interpretation: Allah addresses the believers with a rhetorical question meant to stir their interest and focus their attention on the ultimate path to salvation; He metaphorically compares righteous deeds and sincere faith to a profitable trade, emphasizing that by investing their efforts, wealth, and devotion in His cause, they will secure a divine profit that protects them from the agonizing consequences of misguidance and sin.

translation: You believe in Allah and His Messenger and strive in the cause of Allah with your wealth and your lives. That is best for you, if you should know.
interpretation: The verse highlights that the highest manifestation of sincere faith is the willingness to sacrifice one's worldly possessions and physical life to uphold the truth and support the cause of Allah, asserting that the spiritual rewards and eternal consequences of this sacrifice far outweigh any temporary material gains or worldly comfort.

translation: He will forgive you your sins and admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow and pleasant dwellings in gardens of perpetual residence. That is the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse highlights that the ultimate success for a believer lies in the transition from spiritual purification through the forgiveness of sins to the physical and eternal reward of paradise. The mention of 'pleasant dwellings' signifies that Allah provides not just entry into the gardens, but also a state of comfort, security, and beauty that fulfills the deepest desires of the soul, marking the highest level of triumph one can achieve in existence.

translation: And another [favor] that you love - victory from Allah and an imminent conquest; and give good tidings to the believers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine promise to the believers that, in addition to the salvation from punishment mentioned previously, they will be granted tangible rewards in this world, specifically the triumph over their enemies and the swift opening of new lands for the message of Islam, which should serve as a source of immense joy and motivation for those who possess true faith.

translation: O you who have believed, be supporters of Allah, as when Jesus, the son of Mary, said to the disciples, 'Who are my supporters for Allah?' The disciples said, 'We are supporters of Allah.' And a faction of the Children of Israel believed and a faction disbelieved. So We supported those who believed against their enemy, and they became dominant.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine call for believers to embody the same level of commitment and active defense of the truth that the disciples of Jesus (Isa) displayed. By likening the believers to the 'helpers' of Jesus, Allah emphasizes that supporting His cause—by upholding His law and spreading His message—results in divine empowerment, ensuring that those who remain steadfast in their faith ultimately prevail over their adversaries, whether through manifest victory in this world or through the everlasting triumph of their spiritual integrity.

translation: Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth is exalting Allah, the Sovereign, the Pure, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse signifies that all creation, through its very existence and natural order, declares the perfection and transcendence of Allah. By identifying Him as the Sovereign, the Pure, the All-Mighty, and the All-Wise, the verse asserts that His creation serves as a testimony to His absolute authority, His freedom from any defect or partner, His irresistible power, and the profound wisdom inherent in every aspect of His decree and governance.

translation: It is He who has sent among the unlettered a Messenger from themselves reciting to them His verses and purifying them and teaching them the Book and wisdom - although they were before in clear error.
interpretation: Allah signifies that the mission of Prophet Muhammad is a manifestation of His immense mercy, as he was sent to a society devoid of scripture and divine guidance to elevate them through the recitation of Quranic revelation, which cleanses their souls from the filth of polytheism and moral corruption, educates them in the laws of the divine scripture, and grants them the deep wisdom necessary to understand the purpose of existence, effectively transitioning them from a state of manifest deviation and spiritual blindness into a state of divine enlightenment and clarity.

translation: And [He sent Him to] others of them who have not yet joined them. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the prophetic mission of Muhammad (peace be upon him) was not limited to his contemporary companions, but extends to all those who would embrace the faith from subsequent generations until the Day of Judgment, indicating that the divine guidance and the call to Islam are universal, eternal, and sustained by the absolute power and profound wisdom of Allah.

translation: That is the bounty of Allah, which He grants to whom He wills, and Allah is the Possessor of great bounty.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all forms of worldly and spiritual blessings, including guidance, success, and virtue, are gifts bestowed by Allah according to His divine wisdom and absolute will, and it serves as a reminder that no one can attain such grace through their own efforts alone without the generous providence of the Creator.

translation: The example of those who were entrusted with the Torah and then did not take it on is like that of a donkey who carries volumes of books. Wretched is the example of the people who deny the verses of Allah. And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern reprimand to those who possess divine knowledge but fail to apply it in their lives or live according to its guidance. By likening such people to a donkey burdened with heavy books, the Qur'an emphasizes that the mere possession, recitation, or physical preservation of sacred texts is meaningless if the heart remains unmoved and the intellect refuses to implement the truth contained within. True scholarship and faith are defined not by the information one carries, but by the transformation of character and the adherence to the divine commandments that such knowledge necessitates.

translation: Say, 'O you who are Jews, if you claim that you are allies of Allah, excluding the [rest of] people, then wish for death, if you should be truthful.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a logical challenge to the Jews of Medina who claimed a unique and exclusive relationship with Allah, positioning themselves as His beloved people above all others. Allah instructs the Prophet Muhammad to demand a practical demonstration of their sincerity: if they truly believed they were God’s chosen favorites and were assured of a reward in the afterlife, they should have no fear of death and instead long for it as a means to return to their Lord. Since their hearts were attached to the worldly life, their reluctance to face death exposes the falsehood of their claim and proves that their faith did not provide the spiritual comfort of a true connection with their Creator.

translation: But they will never wish for it, ever, because of what their hands have put forth. And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse asserts that the deniers of the truth will never genuinely desire death to face God, despite their claims of being favored by Him, because they are profoundly aware of the wicked deeds they have committed and the severe consequences awaiting them; God, in His omniscience, is fully cognizant of their internal corruption and their external transgressions.

translation: Say, 'Indeed, the death from which you flee - indeed, it will meet you. Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you about what you used to do.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a profound reminder that human attempts to escape or postpone the inevitable arrival of death are futile because it is an appointment decreed by God that will certainly overtake every individual, regardless of their efforts to hide from it or seek security elsewhere. The transition from life to death is merely the prelude to being brought back before the Creator, who possesses absolute knowledge of everything hidden and manifest; therefore, the true significance of life lies in the reality that every deed, whether secret or public, will be brought to light and accounted for before the Almighty.

translation: O you who have believed, when [the adhan] is called for the prayer on the day of Jumu'ah [Friday], then proceed to the remembrance of Allah and leave trade. That is better for you, if you only knew.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine command emphasizing the sanctity and priority of the Friday congregational prayer. By instructing believers to leave behind their worldly transactions and economic pursuits the moment the call to prayer is heard, Allah establishes that the spiritual obligation of collective worship and the remembrance of God takes precedence over material gain. It serves as a reminder that true prosperity and ultimate benefit are found in prioritizing the commands of the Creator over the temporary distractions of worldly commerce.

translation: And when the prayer has been concluded, disperse within the land and seek from the bounty of Allah, and remember Allah often that you may succeed.
interpretation: This verse establishes that worldly pursuit and spiritual devotion are not mutually exclusive; once the communal obligation of Jumu'ah prayer is fulfilled, believers are encouraged to return to their daily economic activities and social responsibilities with the intention of seeking God's provision, while simultaneously maintaining a state of constant mindfulness (dhikr) of Allah to ensure that their worldly efforts are spiritually grounded and lead to ultimate success.

translation: But when they see a transaction or a diversion, they disperse toward it and leave you standing. Say, 'What is with Allah is better than diversion and than a transaction, and Allah is the best of providers.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine reprimand to the believers who allowed the fleeting allure of worldly commerce and entertainment to distract them from the spiritual priority of the Prophet's sermon during Friday prayer. It emphasizes that while seeking provision through trade is permissible, prioritizing material gain over the obligatory remembrance of Allah is a grave error, as the eternal rewards and blessings bestowed by the Creator far surpass any temporary profit found in worldly affairs.

translation: When the hypocrites come to you, [O Muhammad], they say, 'We testify that you are the Messenger of Allah.' And Allah knows that you are His Messenger, and Allah testifies that the hypocrites are liars.
interpretation: The verse highlights the hypocrisy of those who profess faith outwardly while their hearts remain devoid of sincere belief. Even though their statement that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah is factually true, their declaration is branded as a lie because it does not reflect the truth of their inner convictions; they say with their tongues what they do not believe in their hearts, effectively using the truth as a mask for their disbelief.

translation: They have taken their oaths as a shield, so they averted [people] from the way of Allah. Indeed, it was evil that they were doing.
interpretation: This verse describes hypocrites who use false oaths and deceptive claims of faith as a protective covering to conceal their disbelief and corruption, thereby deceiving others and obstructing them from the path of righteousness; the verse emphasizes the moral gravity of their actions by characterizing their conduct as profoundly evil, as they intentionally manipulate divine truth to facilitate worldly harm and misguidance.

translation: That is because they believed and then disbelieved, so their hearts were sealed, and they do not understand.
interpretation: The verse indicates that the hardening of the hearts and the loss of spiritual insight are not arbitrary actions by God, but rather a direct consequence of the individual's choice to abandon faith after having embraced it, which leads to a state of moral and spiritual insensitivity where they lose the capacity to discern the truth.

translation: And when you see them, their figures please you; and if they speak, you listen to their speech. They are as if they were pieces of timber propped up. They think every shout is against them. They are the enemy, so beware of them. May Allah destroy them; how are they deluded?
interpretation: The verse describes the hypocrites as possessing outwardly impressive appearances and eloquent speech that may deceive the observer, yet they lack true inner substance, faith, or integrity, rendering them like hollow, useless timber leaning against a wall. Their deep-seated inner anxiety and guilt manifest as constant paranoia, where they interpret any sudden noise or call as a threat against their own deception, highlighting that despite their deceptive exterior, they are the true spiritual enemies of the believers who must be approached with extreme caution and discernment.

translation: And when it is said to them, 'Come, the Messenger of Allah will ask forgiveness for you,' they turn their heads aside, and you see them averting their faces while they are arrogant.
interpretation: This verse highlights the deep-seated hypocrisy and arrogance of the disbelievers, illustrating how their pride serves as a barrier to their salvation. By physically turning away from the Messenger's call, they demonstrate a complete rejection of divine guidance, showing that their hearts are hardened by vanity to the point where they prefer their own misguided status over the opportunity for repentance and reconciliation with Allah.

translation: It is all the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them; never will Allah forgive them. Indeed, Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.
interpretation: This verse indicates that for those who have intentionally chosen the path of hypocrisy and persistent rebellion against divine truth, the intercession of the Prophet serves no purpose. Their hearts have become so hardened and sealed by their own deliberate rejection of faith that the path of divine guidance is no longer accessible to them, as God's law of retribution dictates that those who reject the light after it has been made clear to them forfeit the capacity for repentance and forgiveness.

translation: They are the ones who say, 'Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they desert him.' And to Allah belong the depositories of the heavens and the earth, but the hypocrites do not understand.
interpretation: The verse exposes the deceptive strategy of the hypocrites who sought to weaken the Muslim community by cutting off their financial resources, wrongly assuming that their material support was the sole source of the believers' survival. Through this, Allah reveals their profound spiritual ignorance, reminding them that all provision originates from Him alone, and that true power lies in divine sustenance rather than the limited wealth that mortals can withhold or grant.

translation: They say, 'If we return to Al-Madinah, the more honored will surely expel therefrom the more humble.' But honor belongs to Allah, His Messenger, and the believers, but the hypocrites do not know.
interpretation: The hypocrites believed that worldly status, wealth, and influence were the true measures of honor, and they arrogant assumed that because they possessed these, they held the upper hand over the believers. In response, this verse clarifies that true honor is a spiritual reality granted by Allah, rooted in faith and obedience to Him and His Messenger. The outward strength of the hypocrites is deceptive and hollow, as true power resides with those who are devoted to the Truth, rendering the claims of the hypocrites manifestations of their own ignorance regarding the nature of divine dignity and success.

translation: O you who have believed, let not your wealth and your children divert you from the remembrance of Allah. And whoever does that - then those are the losers.
interpretation: Allah commands the believers not to let the distractions of worldly possessions, such as wealth and offspring, occupy their hearts and time to the extent that they neglect the worship and remembrance of Allah, which is the ultimate purpose of their existence; those who prioritize these worldly attachments over their spiritual obligations are considered the true losers because they have sacrificed their eternal felicity for the sake of temporary, fleeting benefits.

translation: And spend out of that which We have provided for you before death comes to one of you, and he says, 'My Lord, if only You would delay me for a brief term so I would give charity and be among the righteous.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern exhortation for believers to hasten in performing acts of charity and righteousness while they still possess life and health, warning them against the procrastination of the soul that realizes its error only when the certainty of death arrives, at which point the opportunity for repentance and worldly deeds is irrevocably lost, leaving the individual in a state of desperate but futile regret as they plead for a second chance that cannot be granted.

translation: But Allah will never delay a soul when its time has come. And Allah is Acquainted with what you do.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of the absolute decree of death, emphasizing that the span of a person's life is firmly fixed by Allah's knowledge and command; once that appointed moment arrives, it cannot be postponed by even a single instant, reflecting the sovereignty of God over all life and the importance of being prepared for the inevitable through one's deeds, as He is fully aware of every action performed throughout one's existence.

translation: Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth is exalting Allah. To Him belongs dominion, and to Him belongs praise, and He is over all things competent.
interpretation: The verse conveys that every atom of creation, whether in the celestial realms or upon the earth, is engaged in a perpetual state of glorifying and declaring the perfection of its Creator, as this universal resonance serves as a testimony to His absolute sovereignty, infinite grace, and omnipotence which governs and sustains the entire structure of existence.

translation: It is He who created you, and among you is the disbeliever, and among you is the believer. And Allah, of what you do, is Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has granted human beings the capacity for free will and the ability to choose their own paths. By stating that He created humanity and then acknowledging the existence of both believers and disbelievers, Allah highlights that while He is the Creator of all souls and their faculties, He has given people the agency to exercise their reason and conscience. He is fully aware of every choice, action, and inner inclination, and He observes all deeds with perfect knowledge, ensuring that every individual is held accountable for the path they have chosen to follow.

translation: He created the heavens and the earth in truth and formed you and perfected your forms; and to Him is the [final] destination.
interpretation: This verse underscores that the universe was brought into existence by Allah with a deliberate, wise purpose rather than through randomness, and that human beings in particular were crafted with intentional care and structural perfection, emphasizing that after this life of purpose, every individual will inevitably return to their Creator to face the consequences of their deeds.

translation: He knows what is within the heavens and the earth and knows what you conceal and what you declare. And Allah is Knowing of that within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute omniscience of Allah, highlighting that His knowledge is not limited to the visible, physical universe or outward human actions, but extends to the deepest, most hidden secrets of the human soul. By explicitly mentioning 'what is in the breasts,' the verse serves as a divine reminder that intentions, hidden doubts, and unspoken thoughts are as transparent to God as external words or actions, thereby underscoring the necessity of spiritual sincerity and inward righteousness before Him.

translation: Has there not reached you the news of those who disbelieved before, so they tasted the consequence of their affair, and for them is a painful punishment?
interpretation: This verse serves as a historical reminder and a warning to the believers and disbelievers alike, emphasizing that the rejection of divine truth carries inevitable repercussions. By highlighting that past generations faced earthly catastrophes or spiritual ruin as a direct consequence of their defiance against God, the Quran underscores the principle of divine justice, indicating that current actions will lead to similar outcomes in both this life and the afterlife if the path of arrogance and disbelief is maintained.

translation: That is because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs, but they said, 'Shall human beings guide us?' So they disbelieved and turned away. And Allah dispensed [with them], and Allah is Free of need, Praiseworthy.
interpretation: The verse explains that the cause of the disbelievers' destruction is their arrogance in rejecting guidance simply because it was brought to them by fellow human beings, as they deemed themselves superior or expected messengers to be of a different nature, leading them to turn away from the truth despite the clear evidence provided by Allah, who remains entirely independent of their faith and whose worthiness of all praise is inherent regardless of their denial.

translation: Those who disbelieve have claimed that they will never be resurrected. Say, 'Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected; then you will surely be informed of what you did. And that, for Allah, is easy.'
interpretation: The verse serves as a definitive refutation of the skeptics who deny life after death by asserting that the resurrection is an absolute certainty confirmed by an oath upon the Creator. It highlights that the process of bringing life back from the dead is not a complex task for the Almighty, as His power is absolute and the re-creation of existence is as effortless for Him as the initial creation, ensuring that every individual will eventually be held accountable for their earthly deeds.

translation: So believe in Allah and His Messenger and the Light which We have sent down; and Allah is All-Aware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse commands the believers to place their complete faith in Allah, His Messenger Muhammad (peace be upon him), and the Qur'an, which is described as 'the Light' because it illuminates the path of truth and guidance, dispelling the darkness of ignorance and disbelief, while simultaneously reminding mankind that Allah is fully cognizant of all their deeds, intentions, and hidden secrets, and He will hold them accountable for their actions accordingly.

translation: On the Day He will assemble you for the Day of Assembly - that is the Day of Deprivation. And whoever believes in Allah and does righteousness - He will remove from him his misdeeds and admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever. That is the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse portrays the Day of Resurrection as a moment of profound revelation where the scales of worldly choices are settled; it is named 'the Day of Deprivation' because those who traded eternal salvation for fleeting worldly pleasures will realize with intense regret that they were swindled, having lost the ultimate reward while gaining nothing of lasting value, whereas those who maintained faith and performed righteous deeds will find their past shortcomings erased and their ultimate desire fulfilled in the everlasting gardens of Paradise.

translation: But those who disbelieved and denied Our verses - those are the companions of the Fire, abiding eternally therein. And wretched is the destination.
interpretation: This verse underscores the severe spiritual and eternal consequences of willful rejection of divine truth, emphasizing that those who persist in denying the clear signs of God ultimately choose a path that leads to self-exclusion from His mercy, resulting in a state of eternal deprivation and suffering in the afterlife as a reflection of their conscious choice to turn away from guidance.

translation: No disaster strikes except by permission of Allah. And whoever believes in Allah - He will guide his heart. And Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: When a believer experiences adversity, they realize that it occurred by Allah’s decree and wisdom, which leads them to accept His will with patience and contentment; consequently, Allah strengthens their faith, grants them tranquility, and guides their heart to recognize the hidden grace and ultimate purpose behind the trial.

translation: And obey Allah and obey the Messenger; but if you turn away - then upon Our Messenger is only the clear notification.
interpretation: This verse serves as a fundamental directive for believers to submit to the authority of Allah and the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), emphasizing that true guidance is found in following the divine revelation and the Prophet's exemplary conduct; it also establishes the nature of the Prophetic mission, clarifying that the Prophet is responsible only for delivering the message clearly, while the accountability for acceptance or rejection rests entirely upon the individuals who hear it.

translation: Allah - there is no deity except Him, and upon Allah let the believers rely.
interpretation: This verse establishes the foundation of Islamic monotheism by affirming that Allah is the only being worthy of worship, and it follows this truth with the practical requirement of faith: total reliance and trust in Him alone, as He is the sole possessor of power and control over all affairs.

translation: O you who have believed, indeed, among your wives and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them. But if you pardon and overlook and forgive - then indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse serves as a cautionary guidance to believers, warning that emotional attachments to spouses and children can sometimes lead a person to neglect their religious duties, compromise their moral integrity, or commit sins in order to satisfy the worldly demands or whims of their loved ones. It highlights that such influence acts as a form of enmity by diverting one from the path of righteousness, yet it balances this warning with the command to exercise forgiveness and forbearance, emphasizing that choosing reconciliation and mercy over retaliation—especially when family members have caused one to stumble—aligns with the divine attribute of Allah’s infinite compassion.

translation: Your wealth and your children are but a trial, and Allah has with Him a great reward.
interpretation: The verse serves as a reminder that worldly attachments such as wealth and offspring are tests designed by Allah to reveal the true state of a believer's heart; those who prioritize their duties to God over the temptations or distractions presented by these worldly blessings will find that the eternal rewards waiting for them in the Hereafter far exceed any temporary comfort or emotional fulfillment found in this life.

translation: So fear Allah as much as you are able and listen and obey and spend; it is better for your selves. And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul - it is those who will be the successful.
interpretation: The verse commands believers to exercise piety and devotion to the limits of their capacity, emphasizing that religious duty is not an impossible burden but one scaled to human capability. It links the act of charitable spending to the spiritual struggle against internal greed, teaching that true salvation and success are attained by those who conquer the covetousness of their own hearts, thereby purifying their intentions and ensuring their own ultimate benefit in the hereafter.

translation: If you loan Allah a goodly loan, He will multiply it for you and forgive you. And Allah is Most Appreciative and Forbearing.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to spend their wealth in the cause of Allah—whether through charity, supporting the needy, or funding righteous endeavors—viewing such acts as a loan to the Almighty. The divine promise of 'multiplying' this contribution signifies that Allah rewards the giver manifold in this life and the hereafter, while the mention of 'forgiving' highlights that such selfless acts act as a spiritual cleanser, erasing sins and demonstrating that Allah recognizes the sincerity of His servants by rewarding them abundantly for what they offer, while overlooking their shortcomings through His inherent forbearance.

translation: Knower of the unseen and the seen, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse affirms the absolute divine attribute of comprehensive knowledge, emphasizing that God encompasses everything that is hidden from human perception and all that is manifest and observable in the physical world. By pairing this infinite knowledge with His supreme power and perfect wisdom, the verse assures the believer that every event occurring in the universe is managed with profound purpose and authority, leaving nothing outside of His deliberate control or sagacious arrangement.

translation: O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them for [the commencement of] their waiting period and keep count of the waiting period, and fear Allah, your Lord.
