Do not turn them out of their [husbands'] houses, nor should they [themselves] leave [during that period] unless they are committing a clear immorality. And those are the limits [set by] Allah. And whoever transgresses the limits of Allah has certainly wronged himself. You know not; perhaps Allah will bring about after that a [different] matter.
interpretation: This verse establishes the legal framework for the beginning of the divorce process, mandating that it be initiated at a time when the woman is in a state of purity and has not yet started her waiting period (iddah), so that the count is clear and unambiguous. It further highlights the sanctity of the marital home during this waiting phase, explicitly forbidding the husband from expelling his wife and the wife from leaving, as staying together serves as a crucial final opportunity for reflection, communication, and potential reconciliation, which Allah may facilitate through a change of heart or circumstances.

translation: And when they have reached their term, then either retain them in kindness or part from them in kindness; and call to witness two just men from among you, and keep the testimony upright for Allah. That is an admonition for him who believes in Allah and the Last Day. And whoever fears Allah, He will appoint for him a way out.
interpretation: This verse establishes a divine framework for marital ethics, emphasizing that the end of a legal waiting period should not be a moment of injustice or exploitation. Allah commands that if a husband chooses to reconcile, it must be done with genuine kindness and honor, rather than as a means to exert control. If he chooses to divorce, he must do so without causing harm or bitterness, ensuring that the rights and dignity of the woman are preserved. The requirement to call witnesses serves as a safeguard for truth and accountability, elevating the act of witnessing to a sacred duty performed for the sake of Allah. Ultimately, the verse provides a profound spiritual promise: for those who navigate the complexities of life and interpersonal conflict with mindfulness of God (taqwa), Allah guarantees a pathway through every difficulty, granting them relief, wisdom, and a successful resolution that leads to both worldly peace and spiritual salvation.

translation: And He provides for him from where he does not expect. And whoever relies upon Allah - then He is sufficient for him. Indeed, Allah will accomplish His purpose. Allah has already set for everything a [decreed] extent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of true reliance on God (Tawakkul) by highlighting that when a person sincerely entrusts their affairs to the Creator, God ensures their needs are met through avenues beyond human foresight or logical planning. It serves as a profound reminder that human effort is bounded by finite capability, while God’s decree is absolute, irresistible, and perfectly measured, providing comfort to the believer that every outcome is governed by divine wisdom and timing rather than mere coincidence.

translation: And those who no longer expect menstruation among your women - if you are in doubt, then their period is three months, and [also for] those who have not menstruated. And for those who are pregnant, their term is until they give birth. And whoever fears Allah - He will make for him of his matter ease.
interpretation: This verse establishes the waiting period (Iddah) for women who do not menstruate, whether due to age or because they have not yet begun, setting it at three months to ensure the absence of pregnancy. It further mandates that pregnant women complete their waiting period upon delivery, regardless of the time elapsed. The concluding promise serves as a divine reassurance that those who uphold God's laws and act with piety will find relief and facilitate in all their worldly and spiritual affairs.

translation: That is the command of Allah, which He has sent down to you; and whoever fears Allah, He will remove from him his misdeeds and grant him a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the rulings established by Allah are not merely suggestions but divine imperatives intended for the benefit of humanity, and it underscores that the path to spiritual rectification and eternal success lies in God-consciousness (taqwa), which acts as a catalyst for both the cleansing of one's past transgressions and the attainment of immense, unearned divine favor in the hereafter.

translation: Lodge them where you dwell according to your means and do not harm them to straiten them. And if they are pregnant, spend on them until they deliver their burden. Then if they suckle for you, give them their rewards, and consult among yourselves in kindness; but if you disagree, then another woman shall suckle for him.
interpretation: This verse establishes the social and financial responsibilities of a husband toward his wife during the waiting period (Iddah) following a revocable divorce, emphasizing that he must provide adequate housing and maintenance commensurate with his wealth, while strictly forbidding any form of psychological or physical harassment intended to pressure the woman; it further guarantees the rights of a pregnant divorced woman to support, secures payment for mothers who breastfeed their children, and provides a framework for mutual consultation and mediation to resolve disputes regarding the child's care.

translation: Let a man of wealth spend from his wealth, and he whose provision is restricted - let him spend from what Allah has given him. Allah does not charge a soul except [according to] what He has given it. Allah will bring about, after hardship, ease.
interpretation: This verse establishes a principle of justice and compassion in financial obligations, specifically regarding the maintenance of families and dependents, by tying the duty of spending to one's actual capacity. It relieves those in poverty from the impossible burden of providing beyond their means, while simultaneously offering a profound promise of divine comfort, assuring the believer that temporal difficulties are transient and will be followed by relief and prosperity ordained by God.

translation: And how many a city was insolent toward the command of its Lord and His messengers, so We took it to severe account and punished it with a terrible punishment.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern admonition, illustrating that nations throughout history who arrogantly defied the divine laws and rejected the guidance brought by the messengers did not escape the consequences of their rebellion; rather, they were subjected to a swift and rigorous divine reckoning, highlighting that worldly power and societal persistence in sin offer no protection against the inevitable manifestation of God's justice.

translation: So it tasted the consequence of its conduct, and the end of its affair was ruin.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the inevitable outcome for those who reject the truth and persist in disbelief; they will eventually experience the bitter consequences of their sinful actions in this life and the next, leading to a state of total loss where they are deprived of God's mercy and success.

translation: Allah has prepared for them a severe punishment. So fear Allah, O you who have understanding, those who have believed. Allah has certainly sent down to you a Reminder.
interpretation: The verse serves as a stern warning to those who persist in disbelief and rejection of the truth, assuring them of a grievous consequence for their actions. It then pivots to address the people of intellect—those possessing sound judgment and reflective hearts—who have embraced faith, urging them to maintain consciousness of Allah. By identifying the Qur'an as 'a Reminder' (dhikr), Allah emphasizes that this divine revelation serves as a light to steer the believers away from the paths of destruction, reminding them of their purpose and the eternal reality that lies beyond their worldly existence.

translation: A Messenger who recites to you the distinct verses of Allah, so that He may bring forth those who believe and do righteous deeds from the depths of darkness into the light. And whoever believes in Allah and does righteousness, He will admit him into gardens beneath which rivers flow, to abide therein forever; Allah has indeed granted him an excellent provision.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that the primary objective of the Messenger's mission is to guide humanity out of the darkness of ignorance, polytheism, and moral corruption into the light of divine guidance, faith, and knowledge. By following this guidance and coupling faith with righteous deeds, the believer is promised a profound transformation in the afterlife, where Allah rewards their sincere commitment with eternal paradise, signifying that true success and sustenance lie in the favor of the Creator rather than the transient gains of the worldly life.

translation: It is Allah who has created seven heavens and of the earth, the like of them. [His] command descends among them so that you may know that Allah is over all things competent and that Allah has encompassed all things in knowledge.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that the complexity and vastness of the universe, encompassing both the celestial realms and the terrestrial strata, serve as a profound manifestation of Allah's absolute authority and infinite wisdom; by witnessing the systematic governance of the cosmos, believers are intended to internalize that God’s power remains unconstrained by any boundaries and His consciousness permeates every detail of existence, leaving nothing outside the scope of His divine awareness.

translation: O Prophet, why do you forbid [yourself from] what Allah has made lawful for you, seeking the approval of your wives? And Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: This verse serves as a gentle divine counsel to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) regarding a personal matter where he had sworn off something permissible—specifically honey or a specific wife—out of a desire to please his spouses. The interpretation highlights that the Prophet, while being the recipient of revelation, was nonetheless a human subject to personal dilemmas, and Allah reminds him that he should not deprive himself of what has been decreed as pure and lawful by God simply to satisfy the human expectations or jealousy of his family, emphasizing that God's law takes precedence over personal concessions, while simultaneously reassuring the Prophet of divine forgiveness and mercy.

translation: Allah has already ordained for you the dissolution of your oaths. And Allah is your protector, and He is the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.
interpretation: Allah indicates through this verse that He has legislated a legal mechanism through expiation (kaffarah) for those who have sworn oaths and then found it better to act otherwise, thereby relieving them of the burden of their commitment while acknowledging His sovereign authority as the ultimate guardian who governs human affairs with perfect knowledge of human needs and profound wisdom in His ordinances.

translation: And when the Prophet confided to one of his wives a statement, and when she reported it [to another] and Allah made it known to him, he made known part of it and ignored a part. And when he informed her about it, she said, 'Who told you this?' He said, 'I was informed by the Knowing, the Acquainted.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the Prophet Muhammad's character in dealing with a breach of confidence among his household; by choosing to confront his wife only partially about what she had disclosed and overlooking the rest, he demonstrates the prophetic quality of wise forbearance, prioritizing the preservation of family harmony and the dignity of others over exercising his full right to reproach.

translation: If you both repent to Allah, then indeed your hearts have inclined, but if you cooperate against him, then indeed Allah is his protector, and Gabriel and the righteous among the believers and the angels, moreover, are [his] assistants.
interpretation: The verse serves as a stern admonition to the two wives of the Prophet (SAW) who conspired to cause him distress, warning them that their inclination toward wrongdoing has been exposed to Allah. It emphasizes that despite their alliance against him, the Prophet (SAW) is divinely supported by Allah, Jibril (Gabriel), the righteous believers, and the legions of angels, making their opposition futile and ultimately harmful only to themselves.

translation: If he were to divorce you, his Lord might replace you with wives better than you, submissive, believing, devout, repentant, worshipping, traveling, previously married and virgins.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern admonition to the wives of the Prophet (peace be upon him) regarding their duty to maintain the sanctity of his household and support his mission; it underscores that Allah is not dependent on any specific individuals for the success of His Prophet, and that He possesses the power to replace those who fail to uphold the necessary standards of piety and character with others who embody the qualities of sincere submission, faith, and devotion.

translation: O you who have believed, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is people and stones, over which are [appointed] angels, harsh and severe; they do not disobey Allah in what He commands them but do what they are commanded.
interpretation: The verse serves as a divine mandate for believers to take active responsibility for the spiritual and moral upbringing of their families, emphasizing that the primary duty of a guardian is to shield their dependents from the consequences of disobedience to Allah by teaching them righteousness and patience; it simultaneously warns that the severity of the Hereafter is an inescapable reality governed by executioners who possess absolute strength and unwavering obedience to the Divine Will, underscoring that no amount of personal connection or intercession will exempt those who have neglected their duty of faith and piety from the inevitable accountability of the afterlife.

translation: O you who have disbelieved, make no excuses this Day. You will only be recompensed for what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern declaration on the Day of Judgment, indicating that the time for repentance, excuses, or seeking justification for one's disbelief and worldly transgressions has come to an end. It emphasizes the absolute justice of God, clarifying that the punishment or outcome a person faces is not arbitrary but is the direct, inevitable consequence of the deeds they intentionally chose to perform throughout their earthly life.

translation: O you who have believed, repent to Allah with sincere repentance. Perhaps your Lord will remove from you your misdeeds and admit you into gardens beneath which rivers flow [on] the Day when Allah will not disgrace the Prophet and those who believed with him. Their light will proceed before them and on their right; they will say, 'Our Lord, perfect for us our light and forgive us. Indeed, You are, over all things, competent.'
interpretation: This verse is a direct call from Allah to the believers to return to Him through an honest and sincere repentance that leaves no room for relapse into sin; it promises that such a pure return will not only wipe away past transgressions and secure entry into Paradise, but will also grant them a divine light that illuminates their path on the Day of Resurrection, reflecting their faith and guidance when others are shrouded in darkness, while simultaneously revealing their humble reliance on God's grace to sustain that light until they reach their eternal reward.

translation: O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites and be harsh upon them. And their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet to confront those who openly reject the truth and those who hide their disbelief with firm conviction and uncompromising resolve, emphasizing that the stance against such individuals must be robust and unwavering, for their ultimate consequence for choosing falsehood is the final abode of fire, which serves as a fitting and miserable end for their persistent opposition to divine guidance.

translation: Allah sets forth an example for those who disbelieve: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot. They were under two of Our righteous servants, but they betrayed them, so they did not avail them at all against Allah, and it was said, 'Enter the Fire with those who enter.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a profound warning that no proximity to the righteous—even marriage to a Prophet—can intercede for a person if they choose disbelief and betrayal. It emphasizes that salvation is an individual responsibility based on personal faith and righteous deeds, illustrating that lineage, social status, or noble associations are rendered void in the sight of God when the heart is devoid of true belief.

translation: And Allah presents an example of those who believed: the wife of Pharaoh, when she said, 'My Lord, build for me near You a house in Paradise and save me from Pharaoh and his deeds and save me from the wrongdoing people.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a profound testament that true belief in Allah is not contingent upon one's earthly surroundings or the company one is forced to keep; despite living in the opulent palace of a tyrant who claimed divinity, the wife of Pharaoh prioritized her spiritual connection to Allah above all else, demonstrating that internal faith and the desire for closeness to the Creator can remain pure and unshaken even in the most hostile environments.

translation: And Mary, the daughter of Imran, who guarded her chastity, so We breathed into it through Our spirit, and she believed in the words of her Lord and His scriptures, and she was of the devoutly obedient.
interpretation: This verse highlights the unique spiritual status of Maryam by emphasizing her physical and moral purity, as well as her profound faith in the divine revelation, illustrating that her miraculous motherhood was a result of her exemplary piety and unwavering submission to the commands and books of God.

translation: Blessed is He in whose hand is dominion, and He is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse establishes the absolute sovereignty of Allah, asserting that all power, authority, and control over the universe belong exclusively to Him, while emphasizing His infinite capability to execute His will over every aspect of existence without limitation or obstacle.

translation: He who created death and life to test you [as to] which of you is best in deed - and He is the Exalted in Might, the Forgiving.
interpretation: God created the state of non-existence known as death and the state of existence known as life not for their own sake, but as a crucible to discern which human beings will achieve the highest quality of conduct, defined by sincerity to God and correctness according to His law; He then supports this testing process with His supreme power that none can overcome, while simultaneously maintaining a vast mercy that overlooks the shortcomings of those who strive to perform well.

translation: He who created seven heavens in layers. You do not see in the creation of the Most Merciful any inconsistency. So return [your] vision [to the sky]; do you see any rifts?
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine invitation for humanity to contemplate the perfect engineering of the cosmos, asserting that the universe is characterized by profound harmony, precision, and logical order; the absence of 'inconsistency' or 'rifts' underscores that Allah's creation is devoid of accidental errors, flaws, or structural imbalance, reflecting the absolute perfection of the Creator’s design.

translation: Then cast your eyes again and again; your sight will return to you humbled while it is weary.
interpretation: This verse serves as a profound call to observe the perfection and order of the creation, implying that no matter how intensely or repeatedly a human looks for flaws, imperfections, or lack of purpose in the cosmos, their gaze will eventually fail to find any. The sight returns 'humbled' because it cannot penetrate the divine wisdom behind the creation, and 'weary' because of the exhaustive and futile effort expended in trying to find a contradiction or a disorder in the flawless system established by the Creator.

translation: And We have certainly decorated the nearest heaven with lamps and have made them as missiles for the devils and have prepared for them the punishment of the Blaze.
interpretation: The verse illustrates the dual purpose of the celestial lamps (stars): they serve as a source of beauty and light for the earthly realm, while also acting as instruments of divine defense to ward off devils who attempt to eavesdrop on the celestial council, and the mention of the 'Blaze' serves as a reminder of the ultimate accountability awaiting those who deviate from divine guidance.

translation: And for those who disbelieved in their Lord is the punishment of Hell, and wretched is the destination.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern declaration of the ultimate consequence for those who persistently reject the oneness of Allah and the truth of His revelation, emphasizing that the fire of Hell is the inevitable and most terrible final abode for anyone who chooses to turn away from the path of faith, highlighting that their denial was not merely an intellectual disagreement but an act of defiance against the Creator who sustained their very existence.

translation: When they are cast into it, they will hear from it a roaring breath as it boils.
interpretation: This verse describes the horrifying state of Hell, where its intensity is so great that it makes a loud, terrifying sound like the braying of a donkey or the gasping of someone in extreme distress, reflecting the violent agitation and fury of the fire as it seethes with the souls of those cast within it.

translation: It almost bursts with rage. Every time a group is thrown into it, its keepers ask them, 'Did no warner come to you?'
interpretation: The verse illustrates the intense, personified fury of Hellfire, indicating that its rage is a reflection of the Divine anger against those who rejected the truth, and the question posed by the keepers is not one of ignorance but a rhetorical interrogation meant to emphasize that the inhabitants of Hell were given every opportunity to believe through the warnings of the Prophets but chose to persist in their disbelief, thus sealing their own fate through their defiance.

translation: They will say, 'Yes, a warner had certainly come to us, but we denied him and said, 'Allah has not sent down anything; you are not but in great error.'
interpretation: This verse portrays the moment of deep regret and painful realization by the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment, as they admit that they were not ignorant of the truth or devoid of guidance, but rather chose to reject the messengers and the divine revelations out of arrogance and obstinacy, ultimately accusing those who brought them the truth of being astray while they themselves were the ones wandering in profound misguidance.

translation: And they will say, 'If only we had been listening or reasoning, we would not be among the companions of the Blaze.'
interpretation: The verse illustrates the deep remorse of the disbelievers in the Hereafter, as they realize that their suffering is the direct consequence of their refusal to use the faculties of hearing and intellect that God bestowed upon them to reflect on the truth; they acknowledge that had they truly listened to the guidance with a receptive heart and contemplated the signs of existence with a sound mind, they would have accepted the faith that saves from the agony of the fire.

translation: So they will acknowledge their sins, but far removed is the blazing fire from the people of righteousness.
interpretation: This verse signifies that when the disbelievers face the reality of the afterlife, they will explicitly admit to the sins they committed and the truth of the message they rejected; however, this late admission will not benefit them, as their denial of the truth in the worldly life has earned them a deserved distance from mercy and condemned them to the eternal punishment of the blazing fire.

translation: Indeed, those who fear their Lord unseen will have forgiveness and a great reward.
interpretation: This verse highlights that the true test of faith and sincerity lies in fearing Allah even when one is alone, away from the eyes of people, and without any worldly witness; because those who maintain their devotion and refrain from sinning in private—despite their human weaknesses—are those who have achieved a state of genuine consciousness of the Divine, and thus, they are promised the erasure of their shortcomings and a magnificent recompense in the hereafter.

translation: And keep your speech secret or public; indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts.
interpretation: God is emphasizing His absolute omniscience, clarifying that there is no distinction in His knowledge between what a person whispers in secret and what they declare openly; He perceives the hidden intentions, thoughts, and feelings residing in the hearts of His creation as clearly as He perceives their outward actions and speech.

translation: Does He who created not know, while He is the Subtle, the Acquainted?
interpretation: This verse serves as a rhetorical argument highlighting the impossibility that a Creator would be unaware of His creation; it affirms that God’s profound knowledge extends to the most hidden and minute details of all things, just as His gentleness and subtlety in action are matched by His absolute awareness of everything He has brought into existence.

translation: It is He who made the earth subservient for you, so walk among its slopes and eat of His provision; and to Him is the resurrection.
interpretation: Allah emphasizes His boundless favor upon humanity by preparing the earth as a stable and hospitable dwelling place, ensuring that its terrain is manageable for travel, agriculture, and settlement; this serves as a divine call for humans to actively pursue their worldly needs through diligent labor while remaining mindful that this life is a temporary journey leading inevitably to a final return to the Creator for ultimate accountability.

translation: Have you felt secure that He who is in the heaven would not cause the earth to swallow you when suddenly it sways?
interpretation: This verse serves as a profound admonition from Allah, challenging the arrogance of those who feel secure from His punishment. It draws attention to the instability of the earth—which humans perceive as firm and solid—reminding them that it is entirely under the command of the Creator. If He were to command the earth to open and swallow them, it would be as unstable and shifting as a stormy sea, demonstrating that the only true security lies in submission to Allah, as His power encompasses the heavens and the earth alike.

translation: Or do you feel secure that He who is in the heaven will not send against you a storm of stones? Then you would know how [severe] was My warning.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning from Allah to those who persist in disbelief and arrogance, challenging them to consider whether they are truly safe from His power. By referencing His authority in the heavens, Allah highlights His absolute sovereignty and ability to unleash natural calamities upon those who deny His signs, emphasizing that the delayed punishment is not a sign of His weakness but a period of respite before the ultimate accountability.

translation: And those before them had already denied, and how [terrible] was My reproach.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern reminder that the inhabitants of Mecca were not the first to reject the truth; history is replete with nations that refused to believe in their messengers. Allah is rhetorically asking the listeners to reflect upon the fate of those ancient peoples, emphasizing that His denial and punishment of their falsehoods were inescapable and devastating, thereby warning that current deniers should expect a similar outcome if they persist in their defiance.

translation: Have they not seen the birds above them with wings outspread and sometimes folded in? None holds them up except the Most Merciful. Indeed He is, of all things, Seeing.
interpretation: This verse directs the human intellect to observe the precise laws of nature governing the flight of birds as a clear manifestation of Allah's sovereignty and care. The act of spreading and folding wings is a physical process, but the verse emphasizes that the very ability of these creatures to defy gravity and remain aloft is sustained solely by Allah's divine decree and constant oversight, serving as a reminder that all physical phenomena are ultimately reliant on His power.

translation: Or who is it that could be an army for you to aid you other than the Most Merciful? The disbelievers are not but in delusion.
interpretation: This verse serves as a rhetorical challenge to the disbelievers, exposing the vanity of their reliance on false deities or worldly power; it emphasizes that there is no source of protection or victory apart from Allah, and that those who believe otherwise are merely blinded by a deceptive sense of security that will ultimately fail them.

translation: Or who is it that could provide for you if He withheld His provision? But they have persisted in insolence and aversion.
interpretation: This verse serves as a rhetorical challenge to the disbelievers, highlighting their total dependency on the Creator. It emphasizes that if Allah were to withhold the means of sustenance—whether through rain, the growth of crops, or the capability to earn—no other being has the power to provide it. The phrase 'persisted in insolence and aversion' characterizes their rejection as a deliberate, stubborn turning away from the clear truth despite their constant reliance on the very source they choose to deny.

translation: Is one who walks prone on his face better guided, or one who walks upright on a straight path?
interpretation: The verse employs a vivid metaphor to contrast the behavior of the disbeliever, whose vision is restricted to the earthly and mundane, stumbling blindly through life without moral direction, against the believer, who follows the clear, balanced path of divine guidance with clarity of purpose and spiritual stability.

translation: Say, 'It is He who has produced you and made for you hearing and vision and hearts; little are you grateful.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a profound reminder of the innate human faculties—the capacity to listen, observe, and comprehend—which are not merely biological functions but divine endowments intended to lead the individual toward the recognition and worship of their Creator, highlighting the tragic disconnect between the magnitude of these blessings and the scarcity of human gratitude for them.

translation: Say, 'It is He who has dispersed you throughout the earth, and to Him you will be gathered.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of the divine wisdom behind human existence on Earth, indicating that God is the one who created humanity and spread them across the globe to populate it and fulfill their roles as stewards. It simultaneously shifts the focus toward the inevitable return to the Creator, underscoring that earthly life is a temporary station and that all people will eventually be brought together before God to be held accountable for their actions and beliefs.

translation: And they say, 'When will this promise be [fulfilled], if you should be truthful?'
interpretation: The disbelievers are asking about the timing of the Day of Judgment in a mocking manner, intending to deny its occurrence by questioning its delay, rather than seeking genuine knowledge, thereby revealing their arrogance and lack of belief in the prophecy.

translation: Say, 'The knowledge is only with Allah, and I am only a clear warner.'
interpretation: The Prophet Muhammad is commanded to clarify that he does not possess independent knowledge of the Unseen, specifically regarding the timing of the Hour, as such knowledge belongs exclusively to Allah. His role is strictly defined as a messenger sent to provide a manifest warning to humanity, emphasizing that his authority lies in delivering the divine message clearly rather than claiming divine attributes or hidden omniscience.

translation: But when they see it approaching, the faces of those who disbelieved will be distressed, and it will be said, 'This is what you used to call for.'
interpretation: When the disbelievers witness the punishment of the Hereafter drawing near and confronting them, the reality of their rejection manifests as profound shame and terror upon their faces, serving as a bitter confrontation where they are reminded that this inevitable consequence is the very judgment they once mockingly challenged to occur.

translation: Say, 'Have you considered: whether Allah should destroy me and those with me or have mercy upon us, who can protect the disbelievers from a painful punishment?'
interpretation: The verse serves as a challenge to the disbelievers, highlighting the futility of their wish for the Prophet's downfall; even if their desire were granted and the believers were removed, it would not provide them with any sanctuary or escape from the inevitable divine retribution that awaits their rejection of the truth.

translation: Say, 'He is the Most Merciful; we have believed in Him, and upon Him we have relied. And you will come to know who it is that is in clear error.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a declaration of faith and trust in Allah as the source of infinite mercy, positioning the believer's firm reliance on God against the arrogance of the disbelievers, while issuing a prophetic challenge that the ultimate truth regarding who is truly misguided and lost will be laid bare and proven beyond doubt as their consequences unfold.

translation: Say, 'Have you considered: if your water was to become sunken [into the earth], then who could bring you flowing water?'
interpretation: This verse serves as a profound challenge to human arrogance and self-sufficiency, compelling the observer to recognize the fragility of their existence by considering the sudden disappearance of a vital resource like fresh water deep underground, thereby illustrating that the continuity of life's essential provisions is entirely dependent upon the sovereign mercy and power of the Creator rather than human ingenuity or control.

translation: Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe.
interpretation: The letter Nun is one of the detached letters found at the beginning of certain chapters, the precise meaning of which belongs to Allah alone; the oath taken by the pen refers to the instrument used by angels, prophets, and scholars to record divine knowledge, the decrees of destiny, and human wisdom, highlighting the supreme importance of writing as the primary means by which knowledge is preserved, transmitted, and established as evidence against or for humanity.

translation: By the grace of your Lord, you are not a madman.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine consolation to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in response to the false accusations made by the polytheists of Mecca, who sought to discredit his message by labeling him possessed or insane. Allah confirms that the Prophet's sound intellect, noble character, and the guidance he received through revelation are absolute proofs that he is far removed from any form of madness, emphasizing that his prophethood is a blessing and a manifestation of divine grace that transcends human folly.

translation: And indeed, for you is a reward uninterrupted.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine reassurance to the Prophet Muhammad, confirming that his reward for conveying the message of Islam, enduring the hardships of his mission, and maintaining his noble character is eternal, continuous, and will never be withheld, diminished, or ended, as it is a gift from Allah that remains firm and infinite.

translation: And indeed, you are of a great moral character.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine affirmation of Prophet Muhammad's impeccable conduct, highlighting that his behavior, personality, and mannerisms were perfectly aligned with the highest standards of ethics, compassion, and patience as ordained by Allah, making him the ultimate role model for humanity in all aspects of life.

translation: So you will see and they will see.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine reassurance to the Prophet Muhammad, promising that the truth regarding the triumph of the message and the reality of the Hereafter will soon become manifest, both to him and to the disbelievers who mocked him, as the consequences of their disbelief and the validity of his prophethood will be revealed in a way that leaves no room for doubt.

translation: Which of you is afflicted with madness.
interpretation: This verse serves as a rhetorical challenge directed at the disbelievers who accused the Prophet Muhammad of being possessed or insane; it highlights the irony of their claim by asserting that it is actually the disbelievers themselves who are blinded by their stubborn denial and lack of reason, thereby suffering from the true spiritual madness of rejecting clear divine guidance.

translation: Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of the [rightly] guided.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of God's absolute omniscience regarding the inner state and final destination of every human soul; it emphasizes that while humans may judge based on outward appearances or personal biases, God alone possesses the perfect knowledge to distinguish between those who have truly abandoned the path of truth and those who have sincerely sought guidance, ensuring that justice and divine decree are applied with unerring precision.

translation: So do not obey the deniers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine directive to the Prophet and, by extension, all believers to remain firm in their faith and moral convictions, explicitly forbidding any compromise or concession to those who reject the truth, as yielding to their influence would lead to the corruption of the message and the straying from the path of righteousness.

translation: They wish that you would compromise so they might compromise [with you].
interpretation: The verse exposes the psychological tactics of the disbelievers who desire that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) soften his stance regarding the truth of the message and abandon his uncompromising principles of monotheism in order to reach a superficial agreement that would compromise his divine mission.

translation: And do not obey every habitual swearer, despicable.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine warning against placing one's trust in or following individuals who habitually resort to oaths to gain credibility or deceive others. It characterizes such people as 'mahin' (despicable or base), implying that their constant need to swear oaths suggests a lack of inner integrity, moral weakness, and a reliance on falsehood, thus making them unworthy of being taken as role models, advisors, or leaders.

translation: A slanderer, going about with gossip.
interpretation: This verse describes a person who engages in backbiting and disparaging others behind their backs through gestures, facial expressions, or words, while also actively walking among people to spread malicious rumors and incite conflict between individuals to break their bonds of friendship.

translation: A preventer of good, an aggressor, a sinner.
interpretation: This verse describes a person who stubbornly blocks goodness and blessings from reaching others, frequently transgresses the limits set by God in his dealings, and persists in committing acts of disobedience and sin, reflecting a character rooted in selfishness, hostility, and a lack of moral accountability.

translation: A cruel person, and moreover, an illegitimate intruder.
interpretation: This verse describes an individual who combines extreme arrogance and harshness with a lack of noble lineage or genuine belonging, implying that his wickedness is not just an inherent defect in his character, but is further exacerbated by his status as an outsider who has usurped a position he does not rightfully hold.

translation: Because he possesses wealth and children.
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance of a disbeliever who relies solely on his worldly possessions and offspring to gain status or deflect the truth, mistakenly believing that such worldly abundance serves as a sign of God's approval or a shield against accountability in the Hereafter.

translation: When Our verses are recited to him, he says, 'Legends of the former peoples.'
interpretation: This verse describes the arrogant state of the disbeliever who, upon hearing the divine revelations of the Qur'an, dismisses them as mere fairy tales or outdated folklore inherited from ancient generations, thereby closing his heart to the truth and failing to recognize the divine origin of the message.

translation: We will brand him upon the snout.
interpretation: This verse serves as a metaphor for the profound humiliation and disgrace that will befall the stubborn disbeliever, likening his debasement to the branding of an animal, signifying that his pride will be stripped away and replaced by an indelible mark of shame that everyone will recognize.

translation: Indeed, We have tried them as We tried the companions of the garden, when they swore to cut its fruit in the morning.
interpretation: This verse serves as a cautionary parable regarding the arrogance of those who rely solely on their own efforts and earthly resources while excluding God's will. By using the example of the 'companions of the garden'—who greedily resolved to harvest their crops early in the morning to deny the poor their share—the Qur'an highlights that prosperity is a divine test. Their oath reflects a state of heedlessness, illustrating that when humans become blinded by their wealth and fail to acknowledge the sovereignty of the Creator, they risk losing the very blessings they sought to secure, as the subsequent destruction of the garden serves as a reminder that all success is subject to God's permission and remembrance.

translation: And they did not say, 'If Allah wills.'
interpretation: The verse refers to the owners of the garden who, in their arrogance and greed, resolved to harvest their crops early the next morning while firmly intending to deprive the poor of their due right, intentionally omitting the phrase 'Insha'Allah' (If Allah wills), thereby displaying a lack of reliance on Allah and a disregard for His absolute sovereignty over their wealth and outcomes.

translation: Then there visited it a visitation from your Lord while they were asleep.
interpretation: This verse describes the sudden and divine destruction that descended upon the garden of the sinful owners mentioned in Surah Al-Qalam, illustrating that punishment can strike precisely when people feel most secure in their worldly possessions and negligence, serving as a reminder that human efforts are fragile and entirely subject to the sovereign will and decree of Allah.

translation: And it became like the harvested field (or like the charred remains of a night-darkened landscape).
interpretation: The verse illustrates the swift and total destruction of the garden that the owners had relied upon; the imagery of 'sarim' signifies that the garden was stripped bare as if it had been completely harvested or devastated by fire, leaving nothing behind, thereby highlighting the sudden reversal of fortune for those who were arrogant and unmindful of God's power over their sustenance.

translation: Then they called out to one another in the morning.
interpretation: The verse illustrates the haste and state of confusion of the people of the garden as they realized they had lost their harvest due to their arrogance and refusal to acknowledge the rights of the poor, signifying that their attempt to execute their scheme in secret was thwarted by divine intervention, forcing them to confront their failure immediately upon the break of dawn.

translation: Set out early to your field if you are going to harvest.
interpretation: This verse recounts the story of the owners of a garden who conspired to harvest their fruits early in the morning, secretly and selfishly, intending to exclude the poor from their share. The instruction is a metaphorical depiction of their greedy resolve and premature haste, reflecting a human tendency to prioritize worldly gain while arrogantly ignoring the dependence on God’s will and the moral obligation of charity.

translation: So they set off, whispering among themselves.
interpretation: The owners of the garden departed in the early morning, speaking in hushed and secretive tones to one another so that no poor person might hear of their plans and come to ask for a share of their harvest, driven by their stinginess and their desire to deprive the needy of their rightful portion.

translation: That no poor person shall enter upon you today therein.
interpretation: This verse reflects the intention of the owners of the garden who conspired to harvest their fruits early in the morning so that they could exclude the poor from receiving their customary portion, revealing their stinginess and their desire to prevent those in need from benefiting from their provisions.

translation: And they went out in the morning, having the power to prevent [the poor from their due].
interpretation: This verse describes the mindset of the owners of the garden who set out early with a firm resolve and sense of capability to harvest their crops, specifically intending to exclude the poor and needy from receiving the customary share of their produce, reflecting a state of arrogance and miserliness that ultimately led to their downfall.

translation: Then when they saw it, they said, 'Indeed, we are lost.'
interpretation: When the owners of the garden arrived at their destination and witnessed that their crop had been completely destroyed and turned into ashes, they realized that they had been misguided in their arrogant assumption that they could prevent the poor from their rights, and they acknowledged that they had strayed from the path of gratitude and obedience to Allah, leading to their own ruin.

translation: Rather, we have been deprived.
interpretation: This expression reflects the profound sense of despair and realization felt by those who worked hard and cultivated the land, only to find their efforts come to nothing due to a divine decree, signifying that true success and provision are entirely dependent on God's bounty rather than human exertion alone.

translation: The most moderate of them said, 'Did I not tell you, why do you not exalt Allah?'
interpretation: The most balanced and virtuous among the group rebuked his companions for their negligence, pointing out that their failure to glorify Allah and acknowledge His grace was the very reason they were afflicted with this calamity, as hearts that remain heedless of divine remembrance are prone to arrogance and eventual loss.

translation: They said, 'Exalted is our Lord! Indeed, we were wrongdoers.'
interpretation: When the individuals realized their error and the consequences of their transgression, they acknowledged the absolute perfection and transcendence of God, thereby confessing that the fault lay entirely with their own souls for having deviated from the truth and acted unjustly against their own selves by ignoring the divine guidance.

translation: Then they turned to one another, blaming each other.
interpretation: This verse describes the state of the people of the Garden after they realized their arrogance and greed had caused the destruction of their bounty; in their desperation and regret, they began to deflect responsibility, accusing one another of being the ones who encouraged the decision to prevent the poor from their share, revealing the inherent discord and cowardice of those whose hearts are tethered to worldly accumulation.

translation: They will say, 'Woe to us! Indeed, we were transgressors.'
interpretation: This verse depicts the moment of realization for the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment when they finally comprehend the gravity of their rebellion against divine truth. By acknowledging themselves as 'taghin' (transgressors), they admit that they had knowingly exceeded all bounds and abandoned the path of moderation and obedience, leading to their profound regret and despair as they face the consequences of their arrogance and defiance.

translation: Perhaps our Lord will substitute for us [something] better than it; indeed, we are toward our Lord desirous.
interpretation: This verse reflects the humble resignation and optimistic hope of the believers who, having lost worldly possessions or facing deprivation, turn their hearts entirely toward Allah, trusting that His compensation—whether in this life or the Hereafter—is superior to what they have lost, and reaffirming that their ultimate aspiration and longing are directed solely toward His pleasure.

translation: Such is the punishment; and the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if they only knew.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning that the worldly calamities or punishments faced by those who turn away from truth are merely reflections of a temporary nature, whereas the retribution in the afterlife is far more severe, encompassing and eternal, highlighting that if the disbelievers truly grasped the magnitude of the consequences awaiting them, they would refrain from their arrogance and disbelief.

translation: Indeed, for the righteous are Gardens of Bliss with their Lord.
interpretation: This verse signifies that those who shielded themselves from disbelief and disobedience through piety will be rewarded by Allah with eternal gardens filled with various forms of refined pleasure, honor, and delight, specifically placed in close proximity to His mercy and grace as a mark of their high status and His divine contentment.

translation: Shall We then treat those who submit (to Allah) like those who are guilty (of disbelief and sin)?
interpretation: This rhetorical question emphasizes the absolute justice of Allah, asserting that it would be inconsistent with His divine wisdom and equity to equate those who have surrendered their will to His commandments with those who have rebelled against Him and persisted in transgression, as such parity would negate the distinction between moral rectitude and wickedness.

translation: What is the matter with you? How do you judge?
interpretation: This rhetorical question serves as a severe reprimand to those who deviate from logic, justice, and divine revelation in their reasoning; it highlights the absurdity of their distorted perceptions and biased judgments that contradict both sound intellect and the clear signs provided by God.

translation: Or do you have a scripture in which you study?
interpretation: This rhetorical question serves as a rebuke to the polytheists, challenging them to produce any divinely revealed authority or heavenly book that supports their false claims of polytheism or their assertion that they will be granted salvation or special status in the afterlife, thereby highlighting that their beliefs are based on mere conjecture rather than truth.

translation: Indeed, you have in it whatever you choose.
interpretation: This verse signifies that within the realm of Paradise, the souls of the righteous are granted absolute fulfillment of their desires; whatever they contemplate, imagine, or yearn for will immediately manifest before them, as the limitations of worldly cause and effect are removed, and the divine promise of ultimate contentment is realized through the mere exercise of their will.

translation: Or do you have oaths from Us, extending until the Day of Resurrection, that you will have whatever you judge?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical challenge directed at the disbelievers who presume they will receive the same blessings as the righteous in the Hereafter, rebuking them by highlighting that they possess no divine covenant or valid scriptural promise granting them the authority to determine their own outcome or secure a reward they have not earned.

translation: Then ask them, which of them will guarantee that for such a claim?
interpretation: The verse serves as a rhetorical challenge directed at the polytheists who invented false associations with Allah or claimed a share of divine authority; it demands that they produce a verifiable proof or a spokesperson who can rightfully guarantee the validity of their unfounded assertions, highlighting that they possess no evidence or divine mandate to support their fabrications.

translation: Or have they partners who have ordained for them a religion to which Allah has not given permission? And had it not been for the decisive word, it would have been judged between them. And indeed, the wrongdoers will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse presents a rhetorical challenge to those who invent religious laws or practices without divine authority, highlighting the absurdity of their claims by asking them to produce their partners or intercessors who could justify such fabrications if they are truthful in their assertions, thereby exposing their lack of evidence and the baselessness of their innovations in faith.

translation: On the Day when the shin will be bared and they will be invited to prostrate, but they will not be able to do so.
interpretation: This verse describes the severity and terror of the Day of Resurrection, where 'baring the shin' is an idiomatic expression in Arabic signifying the intensity of a difficult situation or the unveiling of a great matter, indicating that the reality of the divine decree will be revealed in a way that exposes the true nature of everyone’s deeds, leaving the disbelievers overwhelmed by fear and unable to prostrate as they were once invited to do in this life, thereby manifesting their regret and inability to seek salvation once the time for accountability has arrived.

translation: Their eyes will be cast down, humiliation will cover them, for they were invited to prostrate while they were sound.
interpretation: The verse describes the state of the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment, showing that their current state of degradation and downcast eyes is a direct consequence of their arrogance in the worldly life; they were repeatedly called to humble themselves before Allah through prayer and prostration while they were healthy, capable, and free from hardship, yet they stubbornly refused to comply.

translation: So leave Me alone with those who deny this discourse. We will lead them on by degrees from where they do not know.
interpretation: God instructs the Prophet to refrain from debating the disbelievers who reject the Qur'an, as He will handle their punishment personally. The meaning of leading them on by degrees (istidraj) signifies that God will grant them consecutive blessings and material worldly successes despite their denial, which will cause them to become more arrogant and heedless. This process ensures that they remain unaware that their temporary prosperity is actually a path leading them toward their eventual destruction and divine reckoning.

translation: And I will give them respite; indeed, My plan is firm.
interpretation: God grants the disbelievers a period of delay and worldly comfort, not out of love or approval, but as a deliberate strategy to allow them to increase in their transgression, ensuring that when His retribution eventually arrives, it is inescapable and complete, demonstrating the absolute strength and precision of His divine decree.

translation: Or do you ask of them a payment, so that they are burdened by debt?
interpretation: This verse rhetorically challenges the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) by highlighting that he does not demand any worldly compensation or financial reward from his people for conveying the message of Allah, thereby removing any excuse they might have to turn away, as their refusal cannot be attributed to the financial burden of his mission.

translation: Or do they possess the knowledge of the unseen, so that they record it?
interpretation: This verse serves as a rhetorical challenge to the polytheists, questioning whether they have attained direct, divine knowledge of the unseen realm—such as the details of the afterlife, God's decrees, or the hidden truths of existence—that would entitle them to write down or legislate their own false religious claims and assertions as if they were established facts or divinely inspired scriptures.

translation: So wait patiently for the command of your Lord, and be not like the companion of the fish, when he called out while he was filled with distress.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine counsel to the Prophet Muhammad to remain steadfast and patient in fulfilling his mission, even when faced with hardships or when the fulfillment of God's promise seems delayed. It explicitly references the Prophet Yunus (Jonah) as a cautionary example, urging the Prophet not to repeat the haste or impatience that led Yunus to leave his people before receiving divine permission, which subsequently resulted in his confinement within the belly of the whale. The mention of him being 'filled with distress' highlights the internal struggle and exhaustion of a soul burdened by its situation, serving as a reminder that one must endure the trials appointed by God without faltering or seeking premature relief.

translation: Had it not been that a favor from his Lord overtook him, he would have been cast onto the desolate shore while he was condemned.
interpretation: This verse signifies that if Allah had not bestowed His mercy and divine grace upon Prophet Yunus by accepting his repentance and rescuing him from the belly of the whale, he would have been expelled onto the barren land in a state of disgrace and rebuke for having left his people before receiving the divine command to do so.

translation: Then his Lord chose him and made him among the righteous.
interpretation: This verse signifies that after Prophet Yunus (Jonah) was delivered from the depths of the whale and turned back to Allah in sincere repentance, Allah bestowed upon him His special favor, purified his spirit, and elevated his status to that of the truly righteous, demonstrating that Allah's mercy and forgiveness restore the believer to a state of spiritual excellence and closeness to Him.

translation: And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes when they hear the message, and they say, 'Indeed, he is mad.'
interpretation: The verse indicates the intensity of the hatred and malice harbored by the disbelievers toward the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) upon hearing the Qur'an; they looked at him with such fierce, envious, and malevolent stares that it was as if they intended to harm him physically or cause him to stumble and fall, while simultaneously attempting to discredit his divine message by baselessly labeling him as insane.

translation: And it is nothing but a reminder for the worlds.
interpretation: This verse asserts that the Qur'an serves as a universal source of guidance, admonition, and remembrance for all humanity and jinnkind, transcending barriers of time, culture, and geography, as it contains the essential truths and moral principles necessary for every individual to align their life with the will of the Creator.

translation: The Inevitable Reality.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Resurrection, which is called 'Al-Haqqah' because its occurrence is an absolute certainty that cannot be avoided, and because it is the day when the truth of everyone's deeds will be fully manifested and realized, bringing about the final judgment for all of creation.

translation: The Inevitable Reality.
interpretation: The verse refers to the Day of Resurrection, which is called 'Al-Haqqah' because it is a truth that must inevitably occur, leaving no room for doubt, and it is the day when the consequences of every individual's actions will be fully manifested and realized.

translation: And what can make you know what the Inevitable Reality is?
interpretation: This verse employs a rhetorical structure intended to instill awe and emphasize the gravity of the Day of Judgment; by posing this question, Allah underscores that the true nature, terror, and magnitude of this inevitable event are far beyond the scope of human imagination or comprehension, thereby urging the listener to reflect deeply upon its certainty.

translation: The people of Thamud and 'Ad denied the Striking Calamity.
interpretation: The verse highlights the stubbornness of these ancient nations who rejected the promise of the Day of Resurrection, referred to as 'al-Qari'ah' (the Striking Calamity), because it would shatter the hearts of mankind with its terrifying intensity and divine judgment, serving as a warning that those who deny the inevitable truth of the afterlife will face the same ruin as those who preceded them.

translation: As for Thamud, they were destroyed by the overwhelming blast.
interpretation: The verse explains that the people of Thamud were eradicated because they transgressed the bounds of rebellion against Allah and His messenger, and were punished by an intense, overpowering sound or earthquake that surpassed their capacity to endure, signaling the absolute authority of divine retribution over those who persistently reject the truth.

translation: As for ‘Aad, they were destroyed by a screaming, violent wind.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the absolute power of Allah in executing His judgment upon the rebellious people of ‘Aad, demonstrating that while they relied on their physical strength and architectural prowess, they were ultimately brought to ruin by an atmospheric force they could neither resist nor escape, serving as a reminder that human arrogance is fleeting against the divine decree.

translation: He imposed them upon them for seven nights and eight days in succession, so you would see the people therein fallen as if they were hollow trunks of palm trees.
interpretation: The verse illustrates the devastating and annihilating power of the wind sent upon the people of 'Ad, describing how they were relentlessly battered for an extended period until their physical state resembled decaying, hollow date palm trunks—uprooted and empty—symbolizing that their previous arrogance and stature were reduced to lifeless debris due to their rejection of divine truth.

translation: So do you see any remnant of them?
interpretation: This rhetorical question emphasizes the absolute and total annihilation of those who rejected the truth before the people of Makkah, serving as a stern warning that their defiance will ultimately lead to a similar state of utter erasure and nonexistence.

translation: And Pharaoh, and those before him, and the overturned cities committed sin.
interpretation: This verse serves as a historical warning, grouping Pharaoh, the nations preceding him who rejected their messengers, and the people of Lot—whose cities were overturned—as entities that collectively transgressed against the divine laws, thereby emphasizing that the ultimate consequence of pride and disbelief is inevitable destruction.

translation: But they disobeyed the messenger of their Lord, so He seized them with a terrible seizure.
interpretation: This verse highlights the gravity of rebelling against divine guidance; when a people persistently reject the truth brought by a messenger, they exhaust the limits of divine patience, resulting in a sudden and overwhelming punishment that serves as both a consequence of their arrogance and a final settling of accounts for their moral corruption.

translation: Indeed, when the water overflowed, We carried you in the sailing ship.
interpretation: This verse refers to the time of Prophet Nuh (Noah), explaining that when the floodwaters rose excessively and covered the earth to punish the disbelievers, Allah saved the believers—your ancestors—by instructing them to board the Ark, which signifies Allah's mercy in preserving the lineage of humanity through the righteous who obeyed His command amidst the widespread destruction.

translation: That We might make it a reminder for you, and [that] a conscious ear might grasp it.
interpretation: Allah signifies that He preserved the accounts of past nations in the Qur'an so that they serve as a didactic lesson for the believers, emphasizing that only those who listen with attentive hearts and a sincere intent to understand and apply the divine message are capable of truly retaining and benefiting from its wisdom.

translation: And when the Horn is blown with a single blast,
interpretation: This verse describes the commencement of the Day of Resurrection, where a single, definitive sound from the Trumpet acts as the cosmic signal for the sudden termination of worldly life and the simultaneous gathering of all creation for the final judgment, highlighting the absolute authority of Allah and the inevitability of the afterlife.

translation: And the earth and the mountains are lifted and levelled with a single crushing.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, the physical structure of the world will be utterly transformed by the command of Allah, as the earth and its massive mountains are uprooted from their foundations and struck against each other until they are crushed into dust, signalling the complete dissolution of the material world to prepare for the final reckoning.

translation: So on that Day, the Event will have come to pass.
interpretation: This verse refers to the inevitable occurrence of the Day of Resurrection, emphasizing its certainty and the absolute reality with which it will manifest, signaling the end of the worldly life and the beginning of the ultimate judgment for all of creation.

translation: And the heaven will split asunder, for that day it is frail.
interpretation: This verse describes the terrifying dissolution of the cosmic order on the Day of Resurrection, where the firmament, despite its immense strength and stability, will lose its structural integrity and become brittle and flimsy, signaling the collapse of the physical universe as it surrenders to the absolute command of Allah.

translation: And the angels will be on its edges, and eight [angels] will bear the Throne of your Lord above them that Day.
interpretation: This verse describes the awe-inspiring scene on the Day of Resurrection, where the majesty of God’s sovereignty becomes manifest; the presence of the angels at the boundaries of the heavens signifies their complete subjugation and presence in the divine presence, while the detail of the eight angels bearing the Throne emphasizes the immense power and sublime status of the Divine Throne, which is held up not by need, but as a demonstration of the honor and strength granted to these created beings by their Creator.

translation: On that Day, you will be brought forth; not a secret of yours will be hidden.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of the absolute transparency of the Day of Judgment, where every hidden intention, secret action, and concealed thought of a person will be laid bare before Allah, leaving no possibility for denial or concealment, as the divine omniscience encompasses every detail of human existence.

translation: Then as for he who is given his record in his right hand, he will say, 'Here, read my record!'
interpretation: This verse depicts the moment of extreme triumph and joy for the believer on the Day of Judgment; when they receive their book of deeds in their right hand, they are so overcome with happiness and confidence in their salvation that they beckon others to witness their success and read the account of their righteous life.

translation: Indeed, I was certain that I would meet my account.
interpretation: The speaker expresses a profound realization of the afterlife, reflecting the state of the believer who lived their worldly life with the constant awareness that every action, thought, and intention would eventually be scrutinized by Allah, which served as a guiding force for their moral conduct and spiritual accountability.

translation: He will be in a pleasant life.
interpretation: This verse describes the state of the believer in the Hereafter, indicating that their life will be characterized by complete contentment and satisfaction, where every desire is fulfilled, their soul is at peace, and they are surrounded by the eternal pleasures of Paradise.

translation: In a lofty Paradise.
interpretation: This verse describes the status and nature of the Garden of Paradise, emphasizing that its rank is elevated and its station is sublime, indicating both its physical height in the heavens and its high spiritual honor where the believers shall reside in peace and majesty.

translation: Its clusters [of fruit] will be low in reach.
interpretation: This verse describes the ease and comfort bestowed upon the dwellers of Paradise, indicating that the fruits hanging from the trees will be so conveniently positioned and low-hanging that they can be gathered effortlessly by those reclining or resting, without the need for standing, climbing, or any form of exertion.

translation: Eat and drink in satisfaction for what you put forth in the days past.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the believers in Paradise are told to enjoy the bounties and eternal rewards of their surroundings as a direct recompense for the righteous deeds, patience, and acts of obedience they performed during their worldly life, which is described here as 'days past' to emphasize its fleeting nature compared to the eternal life they have now entered.

translation: But as for he who is given his record in his left hand, he will say, 'Oh, I wish I had not been given my record.'
interpretation: This verse depicts the profound state of remorse and despair felt by the wicked on the Day of Judgment, when they realize the gravity of their sins recorded against them. The wish to not have received the book signifies a desperate, futile desire for non-existence or oblivion to escape the shame and the inevitable punishment that follows the exposure of their worldly deeds.

translation: And I did not know what my account is.
interpretation: This verse depicts the state of utter bewilderment and profound regret experienced by the disbeliever on the Day of Resurrection upon receiving their record of deeds; it highlights the complete absence of preparation and the sudden, overwhelming realization of the gravity of one's accountability before God, leaving the individual in a state of hopeless confusion regarding their ultimate fate.

translation: Oh, I wish it had been the end.
interpretation: This verse reflects the profound and final regret of the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection when they witness their fate, expressing a desperate wish that their death in the worldly life had been the absolute end of their existence, meaning they would have remained in the void of non-existence rather than facing the eternal reckoning and the consequences of their deeds.

translation: My wealth has not availed me at all.
interpretation: This verse depicts the moment of ultimate regret for the disbeliever who relied solely on worldly possessions, realizing as they face the reality of the afterlife that no amount of gathered wealth, status, or material power can offer protection against the decree of Allah or serve as a substitute for faith and righteous deeds.

translation: My power has gone from me.
interpretation: This verse describes the ultimate state of helplessness and regret experienced by the disbeliever on the Day of Judgment, where all the worldly influence, authority, wealth, and worldly connections they once relied upon vanish, leaving them completely stripped of any power or defense to save themselves from the consequences of their deeds.

translation: Seize him and shackle him.
interpretation: This verse depicts the severe humiliation and punishment of the disbeliever in the Hereafter, where the angels are commanded to seize him forcibly and bind his hands to his neck with iron collars as a manifestation of divine justice for his arrogance and rejection of the truth during his earthly life.

translation: Then into the Hellfire, he will be cast.
interpretation: This verse signifies the ultimate consequence for the individual who has transgressed against divine guidance and ignored the truth; it describes a state of total envelopment and searing intensity where the soul experiences the painful, inevitable result of its earthly rebellion against its Creator.

translation: Then into a chain whose length is seventy cubits insert him.
interpretation: This verse describes the severe and inescapable punishment of the disbelievers in the Hereafter, where they will be bound with an unimaginably long and heavy chain. The specific length of seventy cubits signifies an immense and crushing restriction, emphasizing that the condemned person will be completely overpowered and unable to flee from the consequences of their disbelief and corruption on earth.

translation: Indeed, he used to not believe in Allah, the Most Great.
interpretation: This verse underscores that the root cause of the individual's spiritual downfall and ultimate punishment is the absence of true faith and reverence for the majesty of Allah, as the rejection of His supreme authority and oneness serves as the fundamental barrier to righteousness and eternal success.

translation: And he does not encourage the feeding of the poor.
interpretation: The verse highlights a profound moral failing characterized by a lack of compassion and social responsibility; it describes a person who is not only stingy with their own wealth but also actively refuses to promote or facilitate the act of charity, demonstrating a heart hardened against the suffering of the destitute and a disregard for the communal obligation to support those in need.

translation: So there is no devoted friend for him here this Day.
interpretation: This verse highlights the absolute isolation of the disbeliever on the Day of Judgment, where no worldly connections, family ties, or influential friendships—which one might have relied upon for protection or intercession during life—will possess any authority or capability to offer help, showing that salvation depends solely on one's personal faith and deeds.

translation: And no food except from Ghislin.
interpretation: Ghislin refers to the viscous, foul-smelling fluids, pus, and bloody discharge that flows from the bodies of the inhabitants of Hell, which serves as the only sustenance for those who rejected the truth and lived in arrogance, emphasizing the ultimate degradation and the wretched state of those who refused to purify their souls in the worldly life.

translation: None eat it except the sinners.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Zaqqum tree in Hell, emphasizing that the sustenance of the Hellfire is exclusively reserved for those who intentionally persisted in their sinful rejection of the truth and arrogance against the commands of Allah, highlighting that their earthly disobedience is met with a fittingly painful and corrupting punishment in the afterlife.

translation: So I swear by what you see.
interpretation: Allah is swearing by all the visible things in the universe, including the signs of His creation and power that human beings can observe with their physical sight, to emphasize the truth of the message conveyed by His Messenger.

translation: And [of] that which you do not see.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the vast expanse of existence is not limited to the tangible, sensory realm perceived by human sight, but encompasses a comprehensive hidden dimension—including the divine realm, the angels, the jinn, and the unseen metaphysical realities—which remains veiled from human eyes as a test of faith in the unseen.

translation: Indeed, it is a word [conveyed by] a noble messenger.
interpretation: This verse establishes the divine origin and authoritative nature of the Qur'an by affirming that the message being recited is not a human fabrication but a revelation conveyed by an honorable and trustworthy messenger, Jibril (Gabriel), who faithfully delivers the word of Allah to the Prophet Muhammad without alteration or error.

translation: And it is not the word of a poet; little do you believe.
interpretation: This verse asserts that the Qur'an does not bear the hallmarks of poetic composition, which is characterized by imaginative flights, subjective emotionalism, and stylistic ornamentation intended for entertainment or praise. Instead, the Qur'an presents a message of objective truth, divine guidance, and moral law, distinguishing it fundamentally from the creations of human poets. The latter part of the verse serves as a rebuke to the skeptics, pointing out that their hesitation to accept the message arises not from a lack of clear evidence, but from an inherent weakness in their faith and a reluctance to submit to the divine truth contained within the revelation.

translation: And neither is it the word of a soothsayer; little is it that you remember.
interpretation: This verse asserts that the message of the Qur'an does not originate from the chaotic or speculative utterances of a fortuneteller or a psychic, but rather represents a coherent, divinely inspired truth, emphasizing that the failure of the disbelievers to recognize this is due to their neglect of deep reflection and their failure to heed the profound signs presented before them.

translation: A revelation from the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse affirms the divine origin of the Qur'an, emphasizing that its message is not a product of human imagination or earthly invention, but rather a direct communication from the Creator and Sustainer of all existence, designed to provide comprehensive guidance and truth to all of humanity.

translation: And if he had fabricated against Us some of the sayings
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute purity and divine authority of the Qur'anic revelation by stating that if the Prophet Muhammad had dared to attribute false words to God, Allah would have taken severe punitive measures against him, specifically by seizing him by the right hand and severing his life artery, thereby demonstrating that the message delivered is entirely authentic and beyond any human fabrication.

translation: We would have seized him by the right hand.
