interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the essence of all divine revelations and religious obligations is the unification of worship for Allah alone, free from any form of polytheism or hypocrisy, while maintaining a firm uprightness in faith, as this specific orientation of the heart combined with the practical implementation of prayer and charity constitutes the fundamental, immutable, and perfect path of life that leads to salvation.

translation: Indeed, they who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists will be in the fire of Hell, abiding eternally therein. Those are the worst of creatures.
interpretation: This verse describes the ultimate state of those who willfully rejected the truth brought by the messengers despite possessing previous scripture or clear signs of God's oneness. Their status as the 'worst of creatures' stems from their deliberate choice to turn away from the light of guidance after it had become manifest to them, leading them to commit the greatest injustice against their own souls and the truth, which results in their permanent exclusion from God's mercy.

translation: Indeed, they who have believed and done righteous deeds - those are the best of creatures.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the standard for moral excellence and ultimate superiority in the sight of God is not based on lineage, status, or worldly acquisition, but rather on the combination of sincere inner conviction (faith) and the consistent outward manifestation of that faith through virtuous deeds, which together elevate the human being to the highest rank of creation.

translation: Their reward with their Lord is gardens of perpetual residence beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever. Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. That is for whoever has feared his Lord.
interpretation: The verse highlights that the ultimate recompense for those who maintain God-consciousness is a state of eternal bliss and divine satisfaction, where the bond of mutual pleasure between the Creator and the believer becomes the pinnacle of their reward, signifying that true salvation is achieved not just by deeds, but through the profound reverence and awe of God that governs one's life.

translation: When the earth is shaken with its [final] earthquake.
interpretation: This verse describes the onset of the Day of Judgment, portraying the earth as being violently convulsed and upheaved to its utmost capacity, symbolizing the profound, cataclysmic transition from the transitory worldly life to the eternal state of existence where all secrets hidden within the earth and the hearts of men will be exposed.

translation: And the earth throws out its burdens.
interpretation: This verse depicts a scene from the Day of Judgment, indicating that the earth will eject everything hidden within it—whether these are the corpses of the dead from the beginning of time or the vast mineral and hidden treasures it contains—as it prepares to yield all that it has held to be presented before Allah.

translation: And man will say, 'What is [the matter] with it?'
interpretation: This verse depicts the state of confusion and terror of human beings on the Day of Resurrection when they witness the earth shaking, splitting, and undergoing violent transformations, causing them to cry out in alarm at the sudden and unprecedented nature of these cosmic upheavals.

translation: On that Day, it will report its news.
interpretation: On the Day of Resurrection, the earth will bear witness to everything that was done upon its surface, whether good or evil, by speaking out by the command of Allah as a definitive testimony for or against its inhabitants.

translation: That your Lord has commanded her.
interpretation: This verse signifies that Allah has inspired or decreed for the earth to carry out His divine command on the Day of Judgment, compelling it to yield up all that is contained within it, whether it be the dead, their deeds, or the secrets they held, as the earth serves as a witness to everything that transpired upon its surface.

translation: On that Day, people will emerge in separate groups to be shown the results of their deeds.
interpretation: This verse describes the state of humanity on the Day of Resurrection, where they will emerge from their graves in varied groups—separated based on their beliefs and actions—moving toward the place of gathering to finally witness the manifestations of their worldly deeds, receiving either reward or punishment for what they have earned.

translation: So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine assurance of absolute justice, conveying that no action, regardless of how minute or seemingly insignificant it may be in the eyes of the world, escapes the record of God; every act of goodness performed by a person will be revealed to them and rewarded in the afterlife, highlighting the importance of every choice one makes and the comprehensive nature of divine accountability.

translation: And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine assurance that absolute justice will be served in the afterlife, highlighting that no action, no matter how insignificant or hidden it may seem, escapes the sight of the Almighty, and that every individual will be confronted with the consequences of their deeds on the Day of Judgment.

translation: By the panting runners.
interpretation: God swears by the horses that charge into battle with such speed and intensity that they produce a distinct panting sound from their chests, emphasizing the majesty of the creatures created by God and the power manifested through their swift movement in the pursuit of righteous endeavors.

translation: And by the chargers that strike fire with their hooves,
interpretation: This verse refers to the warhorses that gallop with such intensity and speed that sparks of fire are produced when their hooves strike the hard rocks, serving as an oath by Allah to emphasize the power, swiftness, and zeal of those engaged in the cause of righteousness.

translation: And those that charge at dawn.
interpretation: This verse refers to the horses of the warriors of Allah, which rush toward the enemy forces at the break of dawn, taking them by surprise and striking terror into their hearts before they have the chance to prepare for battle.

translation: And thereby, they stir up dust.
interpretation: This verse describes the powerful and swift movement of horses in the heat of battle, highlighting how their rapid charge kicks up clouds of dust that obscure the horizon, symbolizing both the intensity of the struggle and the overwhelming force of the believers as they advance toward their goal.

translation: And thereby penetrate the center of the gathering.
interpretation: This verse describes the swift and sudden arrival of the horses of the Mujahideen into the heart of the enemy's formation, splitting their ranks and creating confusion through their sheer speed and surprise, signaling the momentum and decisive impact of the believers in the face of conflict.

translation: Indeed, mankind is ungrateful to his Lord.
interpretation: The verse highlights a inherent tendency in the human soul to focus on worldly trials while remaining oblivious to the countless divine blessings bestowed upon it, often resulting in a state of ingratitude where one complains excessively about difficulties while neglecting to acknowledge the sustaining favor of the Creator.

translation: And indeed, he is to that a witness.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the human being is fully aware of his own ingratitude toward his Lord and his obsession with worldly desires, for his own conscience and his actions serve as undeniable evidence against him that he cannot conceal on the Day of Judgment.

translation: And indeed, he is, in love of wealth, intense.
interpretation: This verse highlights the deep-seated, natural human inclination toward material possessions and worldly gains, suggesting that this overwhelming attachment often blinds a person to the higher spiritual truths and the ultimate reality of the Hereafter.

translation: Does he not know when that which is in the graves is scattered and brought forth?
interpretation: This verse serves as a rhetorical awakening intended for the heedless human being, reminding them that the concealment of their deeds within the silent graves is only temporary; when the Day of Resurrection arrives, Allah will command the earth to cast out everything it contains, forcing every individual to face the reality of their earthly actions and the inevitable accountability that follows.

translation: And that which is in the breasts is made manifest.
interpretation: On the Day of Resurrection, all the hidden secrets, intentions, beliefs, and concealed deeds that were harbored within human hearts during their worldly life will be brought out, exposed, and laid bare before Allah for ultimate judgment.

translation: Indeed, their Lord, on that Day, is fully Aware of them.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that on the Day of Resurrection, God’s omniscience is absolute and inescapable; He possesses total knowledge of every hidden intention, secret action, and the true state of every soul, meaning that no one can conceal their deeds or escape the divine justice that will be administered based on His perfect awareness of their reality.

translation: The Striking Calamity.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Resurrection, which is named 'Al-Qari'ah' because it strikes the hearts of mankind with intense fear and terror due to the overwhelming nature of the events that will unfold on that day.

translation: The Striking Calamity.
interpretation: It refers to the Day of Resurrection, which is named as such because it strikes the hearts of people with its extreme terrors, and it strikes the enemies of Allah with His punishment and wrath.

translation: And what can make you know what the Striking Calamity is?
interpretation: This rhetorical question is intended to highlight the immense magnitude and terrifying nature of the Day of Resurrection, indicating that its significance is beyond human comprehension and far exceeds any worldly catastrophe, thereby instilling a sense of awe and urgency in the heart of the listener.

translation: The day when mankind will be like moths dispersed.
interpretation: This imagery describes the state of humanity on the Day of Resurrection, where people will be in a state of utter confusion, helplessness, and agitation, rushing aimlessly in every direction like moths or locusts that scatter in chaos when they are disturbed or drawn toward a light, reflecting their lack of direction and intense fear as they arise from their graves.

translation: And the mountains will be like wool, teased/fluffed out.
interpretation: This verse depicts the terrifying transformation of the earth on the Day of Resurrection, where the solid, immovable mountains, despite their massive size and stability, will become weightless, scattered, and shredded like carded wool being blown about by the wind, indicating the total dissolution of the physical laws and the terrestrial structure of the world as humanity enters the afterlife.

translation: Then as for him whose scales are heavy [with good deeds]
interpretation: The verse signifies that on the Day of Judgment, the individual whose record of righteous deeds, faith, and obedience to Allah outweighs their sins will find salvation, as their spiritual merit has achieved the necessary weight to merit entry into Paradise and escape the consequences of their shortcomings.

translation: He shall be in a life that is pleasing.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the believer who attains Paradise will experience a state of absolute contentment and satisfaction, where every aspect of their existence is agreeable, serene, and devoid of any distress or imperfection, reflecting the ultimate reward for a life lived in righteousness and obedience to God.

translation: But as for him whose scales are light
interpretation: This verse refers to the individual whose righteous deeds are insufficient or outweighed by their sins on the Day of Judgment, indicating that their lack of faith and good works results in a loss of spiritual merit, leaving them in a state of deficiency before the justice of God.

translation: Then his refuge will be an abyss.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the individual whose good deeds are light in the scale of justice will have his final destination in the blazing fire of Hell, which serves as a mother that embraces him and brings him down into its deepest depths, signifying both his ultimate containment and the severity of his punishment.

translation: And what can make you know what it is?
interpretation: This verse serves to magnify the gravity and intensity of the reality being described, indicating that the true nature of the impending event is so profound, terrifying, and beyond ordinary human comprehension that it cannot be grasped or fully understood through human intellect alone.

translation: A scorching fire.
interpretation: This verse describes the nature of the Hellfire, emphasizing that its heat is intense, overwhelming, and extreme, designed as a manifestation of divine justice for those who rejected the truth and persisted in their disobedience.

translation: The rivalry in worldly increase diverts you.
interpretation: The verse highlights the human tendency to be preoccupied and distracted from the ultimate purpose of life—preparing for the hereafter—by an insatiable desire to accumulate and boast about worldly possessions, status, and numbers, which ultimately prevents one from focusing on spiritual growth and devotion to God.

translation: Until you visited the graveyards.
interpretation: This verse signifies that human preoccupation with the accumulation of worldly gains and the desire for status continues unabated until death overtakes individuals, at which point they are brought to their final resting places in the graves and come to realize the true, transient nature of their worldly pursuits.

translation: No! You are going to know.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning and a call to reflection, emphasizing that the reality of the afterlife and the consequences of one's actions in this world will become undeniably clear to every individual. It signifies a transition from worldly heedlessness and denial to a state of absolute certainty where the truth of Allah's judgment manifests, leaving no room for doubt or excuse for those who persisted in their arrogance.

translation: Again, you will come to know.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning and a rhetorical rebuke, emphasizing that the truth regarding the reality of the afterlife and the consequences of their worldly deeds will be made undeniably manifest to the disbelievers when they face their ultimate accountability, moving from the state of heedless denial to one of inescapable certainty.

translation: No! If you only knew with certain knowledge.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern rebuke to those who are preoccupied with the distractions of worldly life, emphasizing that if they possessed true, absolute certainty regarding the inevitable reality of the afterlife—much like seeing it with their own eyes—they would never have allowed themselves to be diverted from their ultimate purpose and would have lived their lives in total preparation for the encounter with their Creator.

translation: You will surely see the Hellfire.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning and a definitive certainty regarding the afterlife, asserting that those who persist in negligence or disbelief will inevitably be confronted with the reality of Hell, compelling them to witness with their own eyes the consequences of their worldly choices that they previously chose to ignore or deny.

translation: Then you will surely see it with the eye of certainty.
interpretation: This verse signifies that on the Day of Resurrection, the truth of Hellfire, which was previously known through revelation and faith, will become an undeniable, direct, and sensory reality that removes any remaining doubt, moving the soul from the certainty of knowledge to the absolute certainty of vision.

translation: Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the pleasure.
interpretation: This verse signifies that every individual will be held accountable for the various bounties and blessings bestowed upon them by Allah in this worldly life, including health, security, provisions, and comfort, as to whether they utilized these gifts in obedience to their Creator or in ways that displeased Him.

translation: By the time.
interpretation: God swears by the passage of time—the eras and the fleeting moments of human life—to emphasize that humanity is in a state of inevitable loss, for every second that passes brings a person closer to the end of their life, and without faith and righteous deeds, this time is spent in ultimate waste and spiritual ruin.

translation: Indeed, mankind is in loss,
interpretation: Human beings are perpetually immersed in a state of deficiency and decline, as they exhaust the limited capital of their lives and existence in this world without investing in the righteous deeds and spiritual growth necessary to secure their eternal well-being in the hereafter.

translation: Except for those who have believed and done righteous deeds and advised each other to truth and advised each other to patience.
interpretation: This verse serves as the path of salvation from the inherent loss of humanity, establishing that one must possess four essential qualities to be successful: sincere belief in Allah, the manifestation of that faith through good works, the mutual encouragement of others toward truth and righteousness, and the mutual reinforcement of steadfastness and endurance in the face of life's difficulties and the challenges of upholding the faith.

translation: Woe to every backbiter, defamer.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning and a declaration of impending destruction for those who habitually malign others, whether through verbal insults and gossiping or through physical gestures and body language intended to mock and belittle people behind their backs.

translation: Who collects wealth and counts it repeatedly.
interpretation: The verse criticizes the person who is obsessed with the continuous accumulation and counting of worldly possessions, suggesting that such a person is so preoccupied with their material hoard that they believe their wealth will guarantee them immortality or protection from the consequences of their deeds.

translation: He thinks that his wealth will make him immortal.
interpretation: This verse exposes the delusion of the arrogant person who believes that accumulating worldly riches and status provides a shield against death, reflecting a lack of spiritual insight into the transient nature of life and the inevitability of meeting one's Creator.

translation: No! He will surely be cast into the Crusher.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern reprimand to the one who gathers wealth and counts it, asserting that his worldly hoarding will not save him, but rather he will be thrown into the 'Hutamah'—a terrifying fire that aggressively crushes and consumes everything cast into it, symbolizing the ultimate destruction of the greed and arrogance that blinded him in this life.

translation: And what can make you know what is the Crushing One?
interpretation: This verse serves to magnify the severity and terrifying nature of the Crushing One (al-hutamah), which is a name for Hellfire, by indicating that its true reality and intensity are beyond human comprehension and far exceed any standard of punishment known to the created mind.

translation: The fire of Allah, kindled [to a blaze].
interpretation: This verse describes the hellfire as being uniquely attributed to Allah to emphasize its intensity and inescapable nature, signifying that it is a fire ignited by His command, which will consume everything in its path and cannot be extinguished by any means known to humanity, serving as a manifestation of His supreme judgment against those who persist in arrogance and transgression.

translation: Which mounts directed at the hearts.
interpretation: This verse describes the nature of the hellfire mentioned in the preceding context, highlighting that its intensity and reach are not confined to the physical body alone; rather, it penetrates deep into the inner essence of human beings, reaching the seat of their intentions, beliefs, and hidden emotions, thereby reflecting the totality of the suffering that corresponds to the internal state of those who harbored malice and arrogance.

translation: Indeed, it is closed in upon them.
interpretation: This verse describes the state of the fire of Hell, indicating that its gates are firmly shut and bolted, ensuring that no one trapped within can ever escape or find a way out, as a manifestation of their eternal containment and the total hopelessness of their situation.

translation: In extended columns.
interpretation: This verse describes the condition of the Hellfire, where the doors or the punishment itself are held within tall, towering columns or chains that confine the inhabitants, emphasizing the inescapability and the crushing nature of their imprisonment.

translation: Have you not considered, [O Muhammad], how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant?
interpretation: This verse serves as a rhetorical reminder to the Prophet and his people of a historical event that occurred in the year of his birth, where Allah protected the sanctity of the Kaaba by destroying the army of Abraha, who intended to demolish it with war elephants; this signifies that Allah is the ultimate Protector of His House and that He will always triumph over those who commit aggression against sacred truths and divine signs.

translation: Did He not make their plot go astray?
interpretation: This verse refers to the miraculous protection of the Prophet Muhammad and his companions against the schemes of the disbelievers of Quraysh, illustrating that Allah effectively rendered their malicious efforts and strategic conspiracies against the truth futile, causing them to be lost and ineffective, just as He did with the People of the Elephant who sought to destroy the Kaaba but were instead destroyed themselves by divine decree.

translation: And He sent against them birds in flocks.
interpretation: This verse refers to the divine intervention against the army of the Elephant, where Allah unleashed groups of birds that carried stones of baked clay to destroy the invaders. This signifies that no matter how powerful or organized human forces may appear in their arrogance, they are ultimately powerless against the command and the retributive power of Allah, who protects His sacred sites by means beyond human comprehension.

translation: Striking them with stones of baked clay.
interpretation: This verse refers to the divine retribution brought upon the companions of the elephant, where Allah sent flocks of birds that pelted them with hardened clay stones, which obliterated them like chewed-up straw, serving as a manifestation of His supreme power and protection of His sacred house.

translation: And He made them like eaten straw.
interpretation: This verse describes the destruction of the companions of the Elephant who sought to demolish the Kaaba. By likening them to 'eaten straw,' Allah portrays their total humiliation and devastation, illustrating how those who defy His sanctity are reduced to fragments of chaff or remnants of fodder that have been consumed and trampled upon by livestock, leaving them utterly powerless and devoid of any honor.

translation: For the accustomed security of the Quraysh.
interpretation: This verse establishes a reminder of the immense favor bestowed upon the tribe of Quraysh by Allah, highlighting that their social cohesion, safe travels, and economic prosperity—facilitated by their protected status as custodians of the Sacred House—were not due to their own strength but were divine gifts intended to cultivate gratitude and recognition of the Provider who sustained them.

translation: For their accustomed security in the caravan of winter and summer.
interpretation: The verse highlights the divine blessing upon the Quraish, who were granted the safety and privilege to conduct their mercantile journeys to Yemen in the winter and Syria in the summer without fear, a security established by Allah so that they might continue their trade, sustain their livelihood, and maintain their status as the custodians of the Sacred House.

translation: Let them, therefore, worship the Lord of this House [the Ka'bah].
interpretation: This command directs the Quraish to acknowledge the divine favor of being granted safety and provision in the sacred sanctuary of Makkah by dedicating their exclusive worship and devotion to Allah alone, Who is the Lord and Creator of the Ka'bah, rather than associating partners with Him who possess no power to provide or protect.

translation: Who has fed them, [saving them] from hunger and made them safe from fear.
interpretation: This verse highlights the two fundamental pillars of human stability and societal well-being granted by God to the Quraish, which are physical sustenance and psychological security; by ensuring both their provisions and their protection from external threats, God invites them to acknowledge His lordship and respond with gratitude and exclusive worship, as these blessings are the essential foundation upon which all other aspects of life are built.

translation: Have you seen the one who denies the Recompense?
interpretation: This verse serves as a rhetorical address to the Prophet, intended to incite reflection on the character and mindset of those who reject the fundamental truth of accountability in the afterlife. By questioning whether the listener has observed such a person, it directs attention toward the moral degradation that inevitably follows the denial of divine judgment, signaling that one who lacks belief in ultimate justice will inevitably disregard the rights of others and become hardened in their conduct toward the vulnerable.

translation: For that is the one who drives away the orphan
interpretation: This verse describes a person who lacks true faith by highlighting their cruel treatment of the vulnerable, specifically the orphan; it emphasizes that one's attitude toward those in need is a direct reflection of their sincerity in belief and their recognition of the Day of Judgment.

translation: And he does not encourage the feeding of the poor.
interpretation: This verse highlights that the person who denies the religion is characterized by a heart devoid of compassion and altruism; they are not only miserly in their own charity, but they also fail to advocate for or support the social responsibility of ensuring that the vulnerable and needy are fed, reflecting a total lack of empathy and communal concern.

translation: So woe to those who pray.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who are negligent in their prayers, whether by delaying them beyond their prescribed times, performing them without sincerity, or neglecting the humble presence of heart (khushu') and the essence of devotion, thereby turning an act of worship into a mere ritual devoid of meaning and respect for the Creator.

translation: Those who are heedless of their prayer.
interpretation: This refers to individuals who neglect their prayers by delaying them beyond their prescribed times, failing to observe their proper requirements and pillars, or performing them without focus, sincerity, and presence of heart, ultimately treating their worship as a trivial matter rather than a profound connection with their Creator.

translation: Those who show off.
interpretation: This verse describes individuals who perform acts of worship or good deeds not for the sake of Allah, but to seek praise, recognition, or validation from people, thereby nullifying the sincerity required for their actions to be accepted in the sight of God.

translation: And they withhold common kindness.
interpretation: This verse characterizes the hypocrites who, in their extreme stinginess and lack of faith in the afterlife, refuse to lend even the simplest, most mundane household items to their neighbors, thereby demonstrating a complete absence of communal empathy and a failure to fulfill the basic rights of those around them.

translation: Indeed, We have granted you, [O Muhammad], the Al-Kawthar (the Abundant Good).
interpretation: God Almighty bestowed upon the Prophet Muhammad a vast and endless bounty, which refers specifically to the river in Paradise known as Al-Kawthar, and more broadly encompasses the great abundance of prophetic knowledge, spiritual virtues, and the eternal legacy of his message that will continue to benefit humanity until the end of time.

translation: So pray to your Lord and sacrifice.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to devote his outward worship and gratitude exclusively to Allah by performing the prayer and offering the sacrifice as a physical manifestation of his sincerity and thanksgiving for the abundant blessings bestowed upon him.

translation: Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine consolation to the Prophet Muhammad, assuring him that those who hate him and mock his message are the ones who are truly deprived of all goodness, remembrance, and the blessings of posterity, while the Prophet's legacy and influence will continue to flourish and endure through eternity.

translation: Say, 'O disbelievers,'
interpretation: This verse serves as a definitive declaration of separation between the path of monotheism and the path of idolatry, instructing the Prophet to establish a clear and uncompromising stance that his devotion to the One God is fundamentally incompatible with the polytheistic practices and beliefs of those who reject the truth.

translation: I do not worship what you worship.
interpretation: The verse serves as an unequivocal declaration of religious dissociation, asserting that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers remain firm in their absolute monotheism (Tawhid) and cannot participate in the polytheistic practices or deities that the disbelievers of Quraysh associate with Allah, establishing that there is no compromise or middle ground between the worship of the One true God and the veneration of idols.

translation: Nor are you worshippers of what I worship.
interpretation: This verse signifies an absolute declaration of the fundamental irreconcilability between the monotheistic worship of Allah, which is pure and directed solely toward Him, and the polytheistic practices of the idolaters, emphasizing that the nature, intent, and object of worship in Islam are completely distinct and incompatible with the rituals of those who associate partners with God.

translation: And I will not be a worshipper of what you worship.
interpretation: This verse serves as a definitive declaration of disassociation from the polytheistic practices of the idolaters, emphasizing that the Messenger's act of worship is fundamentally distinct from theirs both in its object and its essence; while they worship idols fabricated by human desires and tradition, he worships the One True God, and this total divergence confirms that there can be no compromise or intersection between the religion of Tawhid (monotheism) and the practice of Shirk (polytheism).

translation: Nor are you worshippers of what I worship.
interpretation: This verse serves as a definitive declaration of the fundamental incompatibility between the monotheistic devotion of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and the polytheistic practices of the idolaters. It emphasizes that the object of the Prophet's worship—Allah, the One, the Eternal, who has no partners—is entirely distinct from the idols and false deities that the disbelievers invoke, signifying that there is no common ground in their respective concepts of divinity.

translation: To you is your religion, and to me is my religion.
interpretation: This verse serves as a definitive declaration of disassociation from the polytheism practiced by the disbelievers, emphasizing that there can be no compromise in matters of creed; it establishes a clear boundary asserting the absolute distinction between the truth of monotheism and the falsehood of idolatry, signaling a finality in religious allegiance where the believer remains steadfast in their worship of the One God, leaving the opponents to the consequences of their own misguided paths.

translation: When the help of Allah comes and the victory,
interpretation: This verse announces the divine promise of the final triumph of Islam, indicating that when Allah grants His support to the Prophet and his companions, resulting in the conquest of Makkah and the widespread acceptance of the faith, it serves as a sign that the mission of conveying the message is nearing its completion and that the believers should respond to this success by increasing their devotion, glorifying their Lord, and seeking His forgiveness.

translation: And you see the people entering into the religion of Allah in multitudes.
interpretation: This verse signifies the ultimate triumph of the Islamic message, where the hearts of the people are opened by divine guidance, leading them to embrace the faith not as isolated individuals, but in massive, successive waves, marking the fulfillment of Allah's promise to establish His religion and the widespread acknowledgement of the truth after a period of struggle and hardship.

translation: So exalt [Him] with praise of your Lord and ask forgiveness of Him. Indeed, He is ever Accepting of repentance.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad and the believers to respond to the completion of tasks and the attainment of victory by increasing in glorification, gratitude, and humility. By praising Allah and seeking His forgiveness, the believer acknowledges that any success achieved is through divine grace and simultaneously admits to the shortcomings inherent in human effort, thereby maintaining a state of spiritual purification and proximity to the Merciful.

translation: May the hands of Abu Lahab be ruined, and ruined he is.
interpretation: This verse serves as a declaration of the total failure and loss of Abu Lahab, both in his efforts to oppose the Prophet Muhammad and in his ultimate fate, signifying that his hostile actions against the message of Islam have resulted in his own spiritual and worldly destruction, leaving him with nothing but ruin.

translation: His wealth and what he has earned will not avail him.
interpretation: This verse signifies that neither the vast wealth gathered throughout one's life, nor the worldly status, influence, or achievements acquired through effort, can offer any protection or intercession against the divine decree of punishment, as all worldly possessions become utterly worthless when facing the inescapable reality of the afterlife.

translation: He will enter a Fire to burn with flames.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine decree concerning the ultimate fate of the disbeliever who actively opposes the truth, signifying that he will be encompassed by a blazing, intense fire that will consume him as a direct consequence of his arrogance and hostility toward God's message.

translation: And his wife [as well] - the carrier of firewood.
interpretation: This verse refers to the wife of Abu Lahab, Umm Jamil, who was known for her intense hostility toward the Prophet Muhammad. The description of her as the 'carrier of firewood' signifies that she used to gather thorny branches and place them in the path of the Prophet to harm him, symbolizing the burdens of sin and malicious gossip she carried, which will ultimately manifest as fuel for the fire in the afterlife.

translation: Around her neck is a rope of twisted fiber.
interpretation: This verse describes the wretched state of the wife of Abu Lahab, who used to gather thorns and sharp branches to spread in the path of the Prophet Muhammad, as a metaphor for the weight of her sins and the humiliation she will suffer in the afterlife, signifying that the very means by which she sought to harm others will become the instrument of her own torment and disgrace.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful. Say, 'He is Allah, [who is] One,'
interpretation: This verse establishes the doctrine of absolute monotheism (Tawhid), asserting that Allah is unique in His essence, attributes, and actions, possessing no partners, equals, or rivals, and being indivisible in His divinity.

translation: Allah is the Eternal Refuge.
interpretation: This verse signifies that Allah is the ultimate objective to whom all creation turns for their needs, the One who is absolute and self-sufficient, requiring nothing from others while all beings are perpetually dependent upon Him for their existence and sustenance.

translation: He neither begets nor is He begotten.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute uniqueness and transcendence of God, clarifying that He is not subject to the biological processes or dependencies of creation; He does not produce offspring, nor did He originate from a predecessor or an external source, affirming His eternal and self-existent nature.

translation: And there is none comparable to Him.
interpretation: This verse asserts the absolute uniqueness and incomparability of Allah, declaring that He has no equal, no peer, no likeness in His essence, His attributes, or His actions, thereby negating any possibility of partnership or similarity between the Creator and His creation.

translation: Say, I seek refuge in the Lord of daybreak.
interpretation: The command to seek refuge in the Lord of daybreak signifies turning exclusively to Allah as the Creator who splits the darkness of night to bring forth the light of dawn, thereby placing one's protection and reliance in His power to dispel all forms of evil, harm, and obscurity that might afflict a person's life or spiritual well-being.

translation: From the evil of that which He created
interpretation: This phrase serves as a comprehensive plea for protection against all forms of harm and malevolence originating from any of Allah's creations, whether they be animate beings such as humans, jinn, or animals, or inanimate forces like diseases, natural disasters, and harmful occurrences, acknowledging that while Allah created all things, He alone possesses the authority to shield and guard His servants from the potential evils residing within those creations.

translation: And from the evil of the darkness when it settles.
interpretation: This verse invokes Allah's protection from all manifestations of evil that emerge or intensify in the darkness of night, whether they are physical dangers, malevolent spirits, or internal whispers of anxiety and despair that tend to afflict the human soul when it is isolated in the gloom.

translation: And from the evil of those who blow on knots.
interpretation: This verse refers to practitioners of black magic, specifically those who tie knots in strings or ropes and blow upon them while reciting incantations to inflict harm, discord, or illness upon others; it serves as a prayer for divine protection against the insidious and secret efforts of sorcerers who aim to disturb the lives of believers.

translation: And from the evil of an envier when he envies.
interpretation: This verse warns against the destructive nature of envy, specifically directing the seeker of refuge to protect themselves from the person who harbors ill-will and malicious desire for another's blessings to be removed, especially when that person acts upon their envy by speaking or behaving in a way that inflicts harm on the object of their jealousy.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful. Say, 'I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind,'
interpretation: The command to seek refuge in the Lord of mankind highlights that Allah is the Sole Sustainer, Sovereign, and Protector of all human beings, and that true safety and security can only be attained by turning directly to Him, the Creator who possesses total authority over His creation.

translation: The Sovereign of mankind.
interpretation: This attribute emphasizes that Allah is the absolute Owner and true King of all people, possessing complete authority, decree, and governance over their affairs, lives, and ultimate destiny, thereby mandating that they submit to His laws and seek refuge only in His domain.

translation: The God of mankind
interpretation: This phrase affirms that Allah is the sole deity worthy of worship for all of humanity, possessing absolute sovereignty, authority, and divinity over them, and that every human being is obligated to submit to Him alone as their true Lord and Protector.

translation: From the mischief of the whisperer (the Shaytan) who withdraws (when Allah is remembered).
interpretation: This verse warns the believer against the subtle, persistent whispers of Satan, who constantly attempts to instill doubts, evil suggestions, and sinful inclinations into the human heart. The description 'the one who withdraws' signifies that whenever a person remembers Allah, seeks His refuge, or mentions His name, the devil retreats and loses his power, highlighting that constant remembrance of Allah is the most effective shield against psychological and spiritual corruption.

translation: Who whispers into the breasts of mankind.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Devil, who stealthily casts evil suggestions, doubts, and sinful temptations into the hearts and minds of human beings, exploiting their internal thoughts to incite them toward disobedience or away from the remembrance of God, while remaining unseen and undetectable to their physical senses.

translation: From among the jinn and mankind.
interpretation: This phrase identifies the sources of whisperings and temptation that mislead the human heart, affirming that these negative influences are not limited to invisible beings like the jinn, but also originate from human beings who incite others toward evil through their words, actions, and deceptive philosophies.
